Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Fully Self-Enlightened One.

Vinayapiṭake

The Vinaya Piṭaka

Pācittiyapāḷi

The Pācittiya Pāḷi

5. Pācittiyakaṇḍaṃ

5. The Pācittiya Section

1. Musāvādavaggo

1. The Chapter on False Speech

1. Musāvādasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The Training Rule on False Speech

Ime [T 2.0153] kho panāyasmanto dvenavuti pācittiyā

Venerables, these ninety-two Pācittiya rules

Dhammā uddesaṃ āgacchanti.

come up for recitation.

1. Tena [P 4.0001][M 0.0001][V 0.0001] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena hatthako sakyaputto vādakkhitto hoti. So titthiyehi saddhiṃ sallapanto [V 0.0002] avajānitvā paṭijānāti, paṭijānitvā avajānāti, aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, sampajānamusā bhāsati, saṅketaṃ katvā visaṃvādeti. Titthiyā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma hatthako sakyaputto amhehi saddhiṃ sallapanto avajānitvā paṭijānissati, paṭijānitvā avajānissati, aññenaññaṃ paṭicarissati, sampajānamusā bhāsissati, saṅketaṃ katvā visaṃvādessatī”ti!

1. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the monk Hatthaka, the Sakyan prince, was a debater. While conversing with the sectarians, having denied, he would admit, and having admitted, he would deny; he would cover one matter with another; he would speak a deliberate falsehood; and having made an appointment, he would break it. The sectarians complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed can the monk Hatthaka, the Sakyan prince, while conversing with us, admit after having denied, and deny after having admitted; cover one matter with another; speak a deliberate falsehood; and having made an appointment, break it?”

Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ titthiyānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū yena hatthako sakyaputto tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā hatthakaṃ sakyaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, āvuso hatthaka, titthiyehi saddhiṃ sallapanto avajānitvā paṭijānāsi, paṭijānitvā avajānāsi, aññenaññaṃ paṭicarasi, sampajānamusā bhāsasi, saṅketaṃ katvā visaṃvādesī”ti? “Ete kho, āvuso, titthiyā [M 0.0002] nāma yena kenaci jetabbā; neva tesaṃ jayo [T 2.0154] dātabbo”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma hatthako sakyaputto titthiyehi saddhiṃ sallapanto avajānitvā paṭijānissati, paṭijānitvā [P 4.0002] avajānissati, aññenaññaṃ paṭicarissati, sampajānamusā bhāsissati, saṅketaṃ katvā visaṃvādessatī”ti!

The monks heard those sectarians complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Then those monks approached the monk Hatthaka, the Sakyan prince; having approached, they said this to the monk Hatthaka, the Sakyan prince: “Is it true, friend Hatthaka, that while conversing with the sectarians, having denied, you admit, and having admitted, you deny; you cover one matter with another; you speak a deliberate falsehood; and having made an appointment, you break it?” “Friends, these sectarians must be defeated by any means whatsoever; victory should not be given to them.” Those monks who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed can the monk Hatthaka, the Sakyan prince, while conversing with the sectarians, admit after having denied, and deny after having admitted; cover one matter with another; speak a deliberate falsehood; and having made an appointment, break it?”

Atha kho te bhikkhū hatthakaṃ sakyaputtaṃ anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā hatthakaṃ sakyaputtaṃ paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, hatthaka, titthiyehi saddhiṃ sallapanto avajānitvā paṭijānāsi, paṭijānitvā avajānāsi, aññenaññaṃ paṭicarasi, sampajānamusā bhāsasi, saṅketaṃ katvā visaṃvādesī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, titthiyehi saddhiṃ sallapanto avajānitvā paṭijānissasi, paṭijānitvā avajānissasi, aññenaññaṃ paṭicarissasi, sampajānamusā bhāsissasi, saṅketaṃ katvā visaṃvādessasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

Then those monks, having reproached the monk Hatthaka, the Sakyan prince, in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having had the community of monks assembled, questioned the monk Hatthaka, the Sakyan prince: “Is it true, Hatthaka, that while conversing with the sectarians, having denied, you admit, and having admitted, you deny; you cover one matter with another; you speak a deliberate falsehood; and having made an appointment, you break it?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “How indeed could you, worthless man, while conversing with the sectarians, admit after having denied, and deny after having admitted; cover one matter with another; speak a deliberate falsehood; and having made an appointment, break it! This, worthless man, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:”

2. “Sampajānamusāvāde pācittiya”nti.

2. “For deliberate false speech, there is a Pācittiya offense.”

3. Sampajānamusāvādo nāma visaṃvādanapurekkhārassa vācā, girā, byappatho, vacībhedo, vācasikā viññatti, aṭṭha anariyavohārā – adiṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhaṃ meti, assutaṃ sutaṃ meti, amutaṃ mutaṃ [V 0.0003] meti, aviññātaṃ viññātaṃ meti, diṭṭhaṃ adiṭṭhaṃ meti, sutaṃ assutaṃ meti[T 2.0155], mutaṃ amutaṃ meti, viññātaṃ aviññātaṃ meti.

3. Deliberate false speech means: the speech, utterance, expression, verbal utterance, or verbal communication of one who intends to deceive; and the eight ignoble expressions: saying of what was not seen, ‘It was seen by me’; of what was not heard, ‘It was heard by me’; of what was not sensed, ‘It was sensed by me’; of what was not cognized, ‘It was cognized by me’; and saying of what was seen, ‘It was not seen by me’; of what was heard, ‘It was not heard by me’; of what was sensed, ‘It was not sensed by me’; of what was cognized, ‘It was not cognized by me’.

Adiṭṭhaṃ nāma na cakkhunā diṭṭhaṃ. Assutaṃ nāma na sotena sutaṃ. Amutaṃ nāma na ghānena ghāyitaṃ, na jivhāya sāyitaṃ, na kāyena phuṭṭhaṃ. Aviññātaṃ nāma na manasā viññātaṃ. Diṭṭhaṃ nāma cakkhunā diṭṭhaṃ. Sutaṃ nāma sotena sutaṃ. Mutaṃ nāma ghānena ghāyitaṃ, jivhāya sāyitaṃ, kāyena phuṭṭhaṃ. Viññātaṃ nāma manasā viññātaṃ.

‘Unseen’ means not seen with the eye. ‘Unheard’ means not heard with the ear. ‘Unsensed’ means not smelled with the nose, not tasted with the tongue, not touched with the body. ‘Uncognized’ means not cognized with the mind. ‘Seen’ means seen with the eye. ‘Heard’ means heard with the ear. ‘Sensed’ means smelled with the nose, tasted with the tongue, touched with the body. ‘Cognized’ means cognized with the mind.

4. Tīhākārehi “adiṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhaṃ me”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa – pubbevassa hoti “musā bhaṇissa”nti, bhaṇantassa hoti “musā bhaṇāmī”ti, bhaṇitassa hoti “musā mayā bhaṇita”nti.

4. For one who speaks a deliberate falsehood, saying of what was not seen, ‘It was seen by me,’ an offense of Pācittiya is incurred in three ways: beforehand, he has the thought, ‘I will speak falsely’; while speaking, he has the thought, ‘I am speaking falsely’; and after having spoken, he has the thought, ‘A falsehood has been spoken by me’.

Catūhākārehi [M 0.0003] “adiṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhaṃ me”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa – pubbevassa hoti “musā bhaṇissa”nti, bhaṇantassa hoti “musā bhaṇāmī”ti, bhaṇitassa hoti “musā mayā bhaṇita”nti, vinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ.

For one who speaks a deliberate falsehood, saying of what was not seen, ‘It was seen by me,’ an offense of Pācittiya is incurred in four ways: beforehand, he has the thought, ‘I will speak falsely’; while speaking, he has the thought, ‘I am speaking falsely’; after having spoken, he has the thought, ‘A falsehood has been spoken by me’; and having set aside his view.

Pañcahākārehi “adiṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhaṃ me”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa – pubbevassa hoti “musā bhaṇissa”nti, bhaṇantassa hoti “musā bhaṇāmī”ti, bhaṇitassa hoti “musā mayā bhaṇita”nti, vinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ, vinidhāya khantiṃ.

For one who speaks a deliberate falsehood, saying of what was not seen, ‘It was seen by me,’ an offense of Pācittiya is incurred in five ways: beforehand, he has the thought, ‘I will speak falsely’; while speaking, he has the thought, ‘I am speaking falsely’; after having spoken, he has the thought, ‘A falsehood has been spoken by me’; having set aside his view; and having set aside his acceptance.

Chahākārehi [P 4.0003] “adiṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhaṃ me”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa – pubbevassa hoti “musā bhaṇissa”nti, bhaṇantassa hoti “musā bhaṇāmī”ti, bhaṇitassa hoti “musā mayā bhaṇita”nti[T 2.0156], vinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ, vinidhāya khantiṃ, vinidhāya ruciṃ.

For one who speaks a deliberate falsehood, saying of what was not seen, ‘It was seen by me,’ an offense of Pācittiya is incurred in six ways: beforehand, he has the thought, ‘I will speak falsely’; while speaking, he has the thought, ‘I am speaking falsely’; after having spoken, he has the thought, ‘A falsehood has been spoken by me’; having set aside his view; having set aside his acceptance; and having set aside his inclination.

Sattahākārehi “adiṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhaṃ me”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa” – pubbevassa hoti “musā bhaṇissa”nti, bhaṇantassa hoti “musā bhaṇāmī”ti, bhaṇitassa hoti “musā mayā bhaṇita”nti, vinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ, vinidhāya khantiṃ, vinidhāya ruciṃ, vinidhāya bhāvaṃ.

For one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, saying, 'I have seen,' regarding what has not been seen, there is an offense of pācittiya by way of seven factors: beforehand, he has the thought, 'I will speak a falsehood'; while speaking, he has the thought, 'I am speaking a falsehood'; after having spoken, he has the thought, 'A falsehood has been spoken by me'; concealing his view, concealing his approval, concealing his liking, and concealing his intention.

5. Tīhākārehi “assutaṃ sutaṃ me”ti…pe… amutaṃ mutaṃ meti…pe… aviññātaṃ [V 0.0004] viññātaṃ meti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa – pubbevassa hoti “musā bhaṇissa”nti, bhaṇantassa hoti “musā bhaṇāmī”ti, bhaṇitassa hoti “musā mayā bhaṇita”nti.

5. By way of three factors, for one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, saying, 'I have heard,' regarding what has not been heard... and so on... saying, 'I have sensed,' regarding what has not been sensed... and so on... saying, 'I have known,' regarding what has not been known, there is an offense of pācittiya: beforehand, he has the thought, 'I will speak a falsehood'; while speaking, he has the thought, 'I am speaking a falsehood'; after having spoken, he has the thought, 'A falsehood has been spoken by me'.

Catūhākārehi…pe… pañcahākārehi…pe… chahākārehi…pe… sattahākārehi “aviññātaṃ viññātaṃ me”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa – pubbevassa hoti “musā bhaṇissa”nti, bhaṇantassa hoti “musā bhaṇāmī”ti, bhaṇitassa hoti “musā mayā bhaṇitanti, vinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ, vinidhāya khantiṃ, vinidhāya ruciṃ, vinidhāya bhāvaṃ.

By way of four factors... and so on... by way of five factors... and so on... by way of six factors... and so on... by way of seven factors, for one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, saying, 'I have known,' regarding what has not been known, there is an offense of pācittiya: beforehand, he has the thought, 'I will speak a falsehood'; while speaking, he has the thought, 'I am speaking a falsehood'; after having spoken, he has the thought, 'A falsehood has been spoken by me'; concealing his view, concealing his approval, concealing his liking, and concealing his intention.

6. Tīhākārehi “adiṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhañca me sutañcā”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe… tīhākārehi “adiṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhañca me mutañcā”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe… tīhākārehi “adiṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhañca me viññātañcā”ti [T 2.0157] sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa [M 0.0004]…pe… tīhākārehi adiṭṭhaṃ “diṭṭhañca me sutañca mutañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi adiṭṭhaṃ “diṭṭhañca me sutañca viññātañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi adiṭṭhaṃ “diṭṭhañca me sutañca mutañca viññātañcā”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe….

6. By way of three factors, for one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, saying, 'I have both seen and heard,' regarding what has not been seen, there is an offense of pācittiya... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has not been seen, saying, 'I have both seen and sensed'... and so on... By way of three factors, for one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, saying, 'I have both seen and known,' regarding what has not been seen, there is an offense of pācittiya... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has not been seen, saying, 'I have seen, heard, and sensed'... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has not been seen, saying, 'I have seen, heard, and known'... and so on... By way of three factors, for one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, saying, 'I have seen, heard, sensed, and known,' regarding what has not been seen, there is an offense of pācittiya... and so on.

Tīhākārehi assutaṃ “sutañca me mutañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi assutaṃ “sutañca me viññātañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi assutaṃ “sutañca me diṭṭhañcā”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe… tīhākārehi assutaṃ “sutañca me mutañca viññātañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi assutaṃ “sutañca me mutañca diṭṭhañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi assutaṃ “sutañca me mutañca viññātañca diṭṭhañcā”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe….

By way of three factors, regarding what has not been heard, saying, 'I have both heard and sensed'... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has not been heard, saying, 'I have both heard and known'... and so on... By way of three factors, for one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, saying, 'I have both heard and seen,' regarding what has not been heard, there is an offense of pācittiya... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has not been heard, saying, 'I have heard, sensed, and known'... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has not been heard, saying, 'I have heard, sensed, and seen'... and so on... By way of three factors, for one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, saying, 'I have heard, sensed, known, and seen,' regarding what has not been heard, there is an offense of pācittiya... and so on.

Tīhākārehi amutaṃ “mutañca me viññātañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi amutaṃ “mutañca me diṭṭhañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi amutaṃ “mutañca me sutañcā”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe… tīhākārehi amutaṃ “mutañca me viññātañca diṭṭhañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi amutaṃ “mutañca me viññātañca sutañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi amutaṃ “mutañca me viññātañca diṭṭhañca sutañcā”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe….

By way of three factors, regarding what has not been sensed, saying, 'I have both sensed and known'... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has not been sensed, saying, 'I have both sensed and seen'... and so on... By way of three factors, for one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, saying, 'I have both sensed and heard,' regarding what has not been sensed, there is an offense of pācittiya... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has not been sensed, saying, 'I have sensed, known, and seen'... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has not been sensed, saying, 'I have sensed, known, and heard'... and so on... By way of three factors, for one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, saying, 'I have sensed, known, seen, and heard,' regarding what has not been sensed, there is an offense of pācittiya... and so on.

Tīhākārehi [V 0.0005] aviññātaṃ “viññātañca me diṭṭhañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi aviññātaṃ “viññātañca me sutañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi aviññātaṃ “viññātañca me mutañcā”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe… tīhākārehi aviññātaṃ “viññātañca me diṭṭhañca sutañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi aviññātaṃ “viññātañca me diṭṭhañca mutañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi aviññātaṃ “viññātañca me diṭṭhañca sutañca mutañcā”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti [T 2.0158] pācittiyassa…pe….

By way of three factors, regarding what has not been known, saying, 'I have both known and seen'... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has not been known, saying, 'I have both known and heard'... and so on... By way of three factors, for one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, saying, 'I have both known and sensed,' regarding what has not been known, there is an offense of pācittiya... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has not been known, saying, 'I have known, seen, and heard'... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has not been known, saying, 'I have known, seen, and sensed'... and so on... By way of three factors, for one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, saying, 'I have known, seen, heard, and sensed,' regarding what has not been known, there is an offense of pācittiya... and so on.

7. Tīhākārehi diṭṭhaṃ “adiṭṭhaṃ me”ti…pe… sutaṃ “assutaṃ me”ti…pe… mutaṃ “amutaṃ me”ti…pe… viññātaṃ “aviññātaṃ me”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe….

7. By way of three factors, for one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, regarding what has been seen, saying, 'I have not seen'... and so on... regarding what has been heard, saying, 'I have not heard'... and so on... regarding what has been sensed, saying, 'I have not sensed'... and so on... regarding what has been known, saying, 'I have not known,' there is an offense of pācittiya... and so on.

8. Tīhākārehi diṭṭhaṃ “sutaṃ me”ti…pe… tīhākārehi diṭṭhaṃ “mutaṃ [T 2.0159] me”ti…pe… tīhākārehi diṭṭhaṃ “viññātaṃ me”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti [M 0.0005] pācittiyassa…pe… tīhākārehi diṭṭhaṃ “sutañca me mutañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi diṭṭhaṃ “sutañca me viññātañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi diṭṭhaṃ “sutañca me mutañca [P 4.0004] viññātañcā”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe….

8. By way of three factors, regarding what has been seen, saying, 'I have heard'... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has been seen, saying, 'I have sensed'... and so on... By way of three factors, for one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, saying, 'I have known,' regarding what has been seen, there is an offense of pācittiya... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has been seen, saying, 'I have both heard and sensed'... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has been seen, saying, 'I have both heard and known'... and so on... By way of three factors, for one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, saying, 'I have heard, sensed, and known,' regarding what has been seen, there is an offense of pācittiya... and so on.

Tīhākārehi sutaṃ “mutaṃ me”ti…pe… tīhākārehi sutaṃ “viññātaṃ me”ti…pe… tīhākārehi sutaṃ “diṭṭhaṃ me”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe… tīhākārehi sutaṃ “mutañca me viññātañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi sutaṃ “mutañca me diṭṭhañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi sutaṃ “mutañca me viññātañca diṭṭhañcā”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe….

By way of three factors, regarding what has been heard, saying, 'I have sensed'... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has been heard, saying, 'I have known'... and so on... By way of three factors, for one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, saying, 'I have seen,' regarding what has been heard, there is an offense of pācittiya... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has been heard, saying, 'I have both sensed and known'... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has been heard, saying, 'I have both sensed and seen'... and so on... By way of three factors, for one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, saying, 'I have sensed, known, and seen,' regarding what has been heard, there is an offense of pācittiya... and so on.

Tīhākārehi mutaṃ “viññātaṃ me”ti…pe… tīhākārehi mutaṃ “diṭṭhaṃ me”ti…pe… tīhākārehi mutaṃ “sutaṃ me”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe… tīhākārehi mutaṃ “viññātañca me diṭṭhañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi mutaṃ “viññātañca me sutañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi mutaṃ “viññātañca me diṭṭhañca sutañcā”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe….

By way of three factors, regarding what has been sensed, saying, 'I have known'... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has been sensed, saying, 'I have seen'... and so on... By way of three factors, for one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, saying, 'I have heard,' regarding what has been sensed, there is an offense of pācittiya... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has been sensed, saying, 'I have both known and seen'... and so on... By way of three factors, regarding what has been sensed, saying, 'I have both known and heard'... and so on... By way of three factors, for one who knowingly speaks a falsehood, saying, 'I have known, seen, and heard,' regarding what has been sensed, there is an offense of pācittiya... and so on.

Tīhākārehi viññātaṃ “diṭṭhaṃ me”ti…pe… tīhākārehi viññātaṃ “sutaṃ me”ti [V 0.0006] …pe… tīhākārehi viññātaṃ “mutaṃ me”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe… tīhākārehi viññātaṃ “diṭṭhañca me sutañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi viññātaṃ “diṭṭhañca me mutañcā”ti…pe… tīhākārehi viññātaṃ “diṭṭhañca me sutañca mutañcā”ti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe….

For one who speaks a deliberate falsehood about what was cognized by three conditions, saying, 'I have seen,'... For one who speaks a deliberate falsehood about what was cognized by three conditions, saying, 'I have heard,'... For one who speaks a deliberate falsehood about what was cognized by three conditions, saying, 'I have sensed,' there is the incurring of a pācittiya offense... For one who speaks a deliberate falsehood about what was cognized by three conditions, saying, 'I have both seen and heard,'... For one who speaks a deliberate falsehood about what was cognized by three conditions, saying, 'I have both seen and sensed,'... For one who speaks a deliberate falsehood about what was cognized by three conditions, saying, 'I have seen, heard, and sensed,' there is the incurring of a pācittiya offense...

9. Tīhākārehi diṭṭhe vematiko diṭṭhaṃ nokappeti, diṭṭhaṃ nassarati[T 2.0160], diṭṭhaṃ pamuṭṭho hoti…pe… sute vematiko sutaṃ nokappeti, sutaṃ nassarati, sutaṃ pamuṭṭho hoti…pe… mute vematiko mutaṃ nokappeti, mutaṃ nassarati, mutaṃ pamuṭṭho hoti…pe… viññāte vematiko viññātaṃ nokappeti, viññātaṃ nassarati, viññātaṃ pamuṭṭho hoti… viññātañca me diṭṭhañcāti…pe… viññātaṃ pamuṭṭho hoti viññātañca me sutañcāti…pe… viññātaṃ pamuṭṭho hoti; viññātañca me mutañcāti…pe… viññātaṃ pamuṭṭho hoti; viññātañca me diṭṭhañca sutañcāti…pe… viññātaṃ pamuṭṭho [M 0.0006] hoti; viññātañca me diṭṭhañca mutañcāti…pe… viññātaṃ pamuṭṭho hoti; viññātañca me diṭṭhañca sutañca mutañcāti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

9. By three conditions: regarding what was seen, one is doubtful, does not believe what was seen, does not recollect what was seen, is forgetful of what was seen... Regarding what was heard, one is doubtful... is forgetful of what was heard... Regarding what was sensed, one is doubtful... is forgetful of what was sensed... Regarding what was cognized, one is doubtful, does not believe what was cognized, does not recollect what was cognized, is forgetful of what was cognized. One is forgetful of what was cognized, and says, 'I have both cognized and seen,'... one is forgetful of what was cognized, and says, 'I have both cognized and heard,'... one is forgetful of what was cognized, and says, 'I have both cognized and sensed,'... one is forgetful of what was cognized, and says, 'I have both cognized, seen, and heard,'... one is forgetful of what was cognized, and says, 'I have both cognized, seen, and sensed,'... one is forgetful of what was cognized, and says, 'I have cognized, seen, heard, and sensed'—for one who speaks a deliberate falsehood, there is the incurring of a pācittiya offense.

10. Catūhākārehi…pe… pañcahākārehi…pe… chahākārehi…pe… sattahākārehi…pe… viññātaṃ pamuṭṭho hoti, viññātañca me diṭṭhañca sutañca mutañcāti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa – pubbevassa hoti “musā bhaṇissa”nti, bhaṇantassa hoti “musā bhaṇāmī”ti, bhaṇitassa hoti “musā [T 2.0161] mayā bhaṇita”nti, vinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ, vinidhāya khantiṃ, vinidhāya ruciṃ, vinidhāya bhāvaṃ.

10. By four conditions... by five conditions... by six conditions... by seven conditions... for one who is forgetful of what was cognized and speaks a deliberate falsehood, saying, 'I have cognized, seen, heard, and sensed,' there is the incurring of a pācittiya offense. Beforehand, for him, there is the thought, 'I will speak a falsehood'; while speaking, there is the thought, 'I am speaking a falsehood'; after having spoken, there is the thought, 'I have spoken a falsehood'—having set aside view, having set aside acceptance, having set aside inclination, having set aside intention.

11. Anāpatti davā bhaṇati, ravā bhaṇati davāya bhaṇati, ravāya bhaṇati (syā.). “Davā bhaṇati nāma sahasā bhaṇati. Ravā bhaṇati nāma ‘aññaṃ bhaṇissāmī’ti aññaṃ bhaṇati”. Ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

11. There is no offense for one who speaks hastily, for one who speaks mistakenly. 'Speaking hastily' means speaking quickly. 'Speaking mistakenly' means, intending to say one thing, one says another. For one who is insane, for the first offender.

Musāvādasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The first training rule on false speech is concluded.

2. Omasavādasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Training Rule on Scornful Speech

12. Tena [T 2.0162] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme[V 0.0007]. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū pesalehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ bhaṇḍantā bhaṇḍentā (itipi) pesale bhikkhū omasanti – jātiyāpi, nāmenapi, gottenapi, kammenapi, sippenapi, ābādhenapi, liṅgenapi, kilesenapi, āpattiyāpi; hīnenapi akkosena khuṃsenti vambhenti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū pesalehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ bhaṇḍantā pesale bhikkhū [P 4.0005] omasissanti – jātiyāpi, nāmenapi, gottenapi, kammenapi, sippenapi, ābādhenapi, liṅgenapi, kilesenapi, āpattiyāpi; hīnenapi akkosena khuṃsessanti vambhessantī”ti!

12. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. Now at that time, the monks of the group of six, while quarreling with the virtuous monks, verbally assaulted the virtuous monks—by birth, by name, by clan, by work, by craft, by illness, by appearance, by defilement, by offense; they reviled and disparaged them with inferior abuse. Those monks who were of few desires… they criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: 'How is it that the monks of the group of six, while quarreling with the virtuous monks, would verbally assault the virtuous monks—by birth, by name, by clan, by work, by craft, by illness, by appearance, by defilement, by offense; how could they revile and disparage them with inferior abuse?'

Atha kho te bhikkhū chabbaggiye bhikkhū anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, pesalehi [M 0.0007] bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ bhaṇḍantā pesale bhikkhū omasatha – jātiyāpi…pe… hīnenapi akkosena khuṃsetha vambhethāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, pesalehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ bhaṇḍantā pesale bhikkhū omasissatha – jātiyāpi…pe… hīnenapi akkosena khuṃsessatha vambhessatha[T 2.0163]! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

Then those monks, having rebuked the monks of the group of six in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One… 'Is it true, monks, that while quarreling with the virtuous monks, you verbally assault the virtuous monks—by birth… with inferior abuse you revile and disparage them?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… 'How could you, worthless men, while quarreling with the virtuous monks, verbally assault the virtuous monks—by birth… with inferior abuse revile and disparage them! This, worthless men, is not for the faith of the faithless…' Having rebuked them and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks:

13. “Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, takkasilāyaṃ takkasīlāyaṃ (ka.) aññatarassa brāhmaṇassa nandivisālo nāma balībaddo balivaddo (sī.), balibaddo (syā.) ahosi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, nandivisālo balībaddo taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – “gaccha tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, seṭṭhinā saddhiṃ sahassena abbhutaṃ karohi – mayhaṃ balībaddo sakaṭasataṃ atibaddhaṃ pavaṭṭessatī”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, so brāhmaṇo seṭṭhinā saddhiṃ sahassena abbhutaṃ akāsi – mayhaṃ balībaddo sakaṭasataṃ atibaddhaṃ pavaṭṭessatīti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, so brāhmaṇo sakaṭasataṃ atibandhitvā nandivisālaṃ balībaddaṃ yuñjitvā etadavoca – “gaccha, kūṭa añcha kūṭa (sī. syā.), vahassu, kūṭā’ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, nandivisālo balībaddo tattheva aṭṭhāsi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, so brāhmaṇo sahassena parājito pajjhāyi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, nandivisālo balībaddo taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – “kissa tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, pajjhāyasī”ti? ‘Tathā hi panāhaṃ, bho, tayā sahassena parājito”ti. ‘Kissa pana maṃ tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, akūṭaṃ kūṭavādena pāpesi? Gaccha tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, seṭṭhinā saddhiṃ dvīhi sahassehi abbhutaṃ karohi – “mayhaṃ balībaddo sakaṭasataṃ atibaddhaṃ pavaṭṭessatī”ti. “Mā ca maṃ akūṭaṃ kūṭavādena pāpesī”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, so brāhmaṇo seṭṭhinā [T 2.0164] saddhiṃ dvīhi sahassehi abbhutaṃ akāsi – “mayhaṃ balībaddo sakaṭasataṃ atibaddhaṃ pavaṭṭessatī”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, so brāhmaṇo [V 0.0008] sakaṭasataṃ atibandhitvā nandivisālaṃ balībaddaṃ yuñjitvā etadavoca – “accha, bhadra, vahassu, bhadrā”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, nandivisālo balībaddo sakaṭasataṃ atibaddhaṃ pavaṭṭesi.

13. Once upon a time, monks, in Takkasilā, a certain brahmin had an ox named Nandivisāla. Then, monks, the ox Nandivisāla said to that brahmin: ‘Go, brahmin, make a wager with the merchant for a thousand, saying: “My ox will set in motion one hundred carts tied together.”’ Then, monks, that brahmin made a wager with the merchant for a thousand, saying: ‘My ox will set in motion one hundred carts tied together.’ Then, monks, that brahmin, having tied one hundred carts together and yoked the ox Nandivisāla, said this: ‘Go, you crooked one! Pull, you crooked one!’ Then, monks, the ox Nandivisāla stood right there. Then, monks, that brahmin, having lost the thousand, was downcast. Then, monks, the ox Nandivisāla said to that brahmin: ‘Why, brahmin, are you downcast?’ ‘Because, sir, I have been made to lose a thousand by you.’ ‘But why, brahmin, did you address me, who am not crooked, with the word “crooked”? Go, brahmin, make a wager with the merchant for two thousand, saying: “My ox will set in motion one hundred carts tied together.” But do not address me, who am not crooked, with the word “crooked”.’ Then, monks, that brahmin made a wager with the merchant for two thousand, saying: ‘My ox will set in motion one hundred carts tied together.’ Then, monks, that brahmin, having tied one hundred carts together and yoked the ox Nandivisāla, said this: ‘Go on, good one! Pull, good one!’ Then, monks, the ox Nandivisāla set in motion the one hundred carts tied together.

jā. 1.1.28 nandivisālajātakepi, tattha pana manuññasaddo dissati “Manāpameva [M 0.0008] bhāseyya, nā, manāpaṃ kudācanaṃ;

Manāpaṃ bhāsamānassa, garuṃ bhāraṃ udabbahi;

Dhanañca naṃ alābhesi, tena ca, ttamano ahūti.

One should speak only what is pleasant, never what is unpleasant. For the one who spoke pleasantly, he carried the heavy burden; he also caused him to gain wealth, and by that, he was pleased.

“Tadāpi [P 4.0006] me, bhikkhave, amanāpā khuṃsanā vambhanā. Kimaṅgaṃ pana etarahi manāpā bhavissati khuṃsanā vambhanā? Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe…. “Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

Monks, even then, reviling and disparaging were unpleasant to me. How much more so now would reviling and disparaging be pleasant? This, monks, does not lead to the faith of the faithless… and so on…. And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

14. “Omasavāde pācittiya”nti.

14. There is an offense entailing expiation for scornful speech.

15. Omasavādo nāma dasahi ākārehi omasati – jātiyāpi, nāmenapi, gottenapi, kammenapi, sippenapi, ābādhenapi, liṅgenapi, kilesenapi, āpattiyāpi, akkosenapi.

15. Scornful speech means scorning in ten ways: by birth, by name, by lineage, by occupation, by craft, by illness, by physical characteristic, by defilement, by offense, or by insult.

Jāti nāma dve jātiyo – hīnā ca jāti ukkaṭṭhā ca jāti. Hīnā nāma jāti – caṇḍālajāti, venajāti, nesādajāti, rathakārajāti, pukkusajāti. Esā hīnā nāma jāti. Ukkaṭṭhā nāma jāti – khattiyajāti, brāhmaṇajāti. Esā ukkaṭṭhā nāma jāti.

Birth means two kinds of birth: a low birth and a high birth. A low birth means the birth of a caṇḍāla, a veṇa, a nesāda, a rathakāra, or a pukkusa. This is called a low birth. A high birth means the birth of a khattiya or a brahmin. This is called a high birth.

Nāmaṃ nāma dve nāmāni – hīnañca nāmaṃ ukkaṭṭhañca nāmaṃ[T 2.0165]. Hīnaṃ nāma nāmaṃ – avakaṇṇakaṃ, javakaṇṇakaṃ, dhaniṭṭhakaṃ, saviṭṭhakaṃ, kulavaḍḍhakaṃ, tesu tesu vā pana janapadesu oññātaṃ avaññātaṃ hīḷitaṃ paribhūtaṃ acittīkataṃ, etaṃ hīnaṃ nāma nāmaṃ. Ukkaṭṭhaṃ nāma nāmaṃ – buddhappaṭisaṃyuttaṃ, dhammappaṭisaṃyuttaṃ, saṅghappaṭisaṃyuttaṃ, tesu tesu vā pana janapadesu anoññātaṃ anavaññātaṃ ahīḷitaṃ aparibhūtaṃ cittīkataṃ, etaṃ ukkaṭṭhaṃ nāma nāmaṃ.

Name is of two kinds: a low name and a superior name. A low name is a name such as Avakaṇṇaka, Javakaṇṇaka, Dhaniṭṭhaka, Saviṭṭhaka, Kulavaḍḍhaka, or any name that is considered base, despised, loathed, scorned, and disrespected in various regions—this is called a low name. A superior name is a name associated with the Buddha, the Dhamma, or the Saṅgha, or any name that is not considered base, not despised, not loathed, not scorned, and is respected in various regions—this is called a superior name.

Gottaṃ nāma dve gottāni – hīnañca gottaṃ ukkaṭṭhañca gottaṃ. Hīnaṃ nāma gottaṃ – kosiyagottaṃ, bhāradvājagottaṃ, tesu tesu vā pana janapadesu oññātaṃ avaññātaṃ hīḷitaṃ paribhūtaṃ [V 0.0009] acittīkataṃ, etaṃ hīnaṃ nāma gottaṃ. Ukkaṭṭhaṃ nāma gottaṃ – gotamagottaṃ, moggallānagottaṃ, kaccānagottaṃ, vāsiṭṭhagottaṃ, tesu tesu vā pana janapadesu anoññātaṃ anavaññātaṃ ahīḷitaṃ aparibhūtaṃ cittīkataṃ, etaṃ ukkaṭṭhaṃ nāma gottaṃ.

Lineage is of two kinds: low lineage and superior lineage. Low lineage is the Kosiyagotta, the Bhāradvājagotta, or that which in various regions is considered base, despised, loathed, scorned, and disrespected; this is called low lineage. Superior lineage is the Gotamagotta, the Moggallānagotta, the Kaccāyanagotta, the Vāsiṭṭhagotta, or that which in various regions is not considered base, not despised, not loathed, not scorned, and is respected; this is called superior lineage.

Kammaṃ nāma dve kammāni – hīnañca kammaṃ ukkaṭṭhañca kammaṃ. Hīnaṃ nāma kammaṃ – koṭṭhakakammaṃ, pupphachaḍḍakakammaṃ, tesu tesu vā pana janapadesu oññātaṃ avaññātaṃ hīḷitaṃ paribhūtaṃ acittīkataṃ, etaṃ hīnaṃ nāma kammaṃ. Ukkaṭṭhaṃ nāma kammaṃ – kasi, [M 0.0009] vaṇijjā, gorakkhā, tesu tesu vā pana janapadesu anoññātaṃ anavaññātaṃ ahīḷitaṃ aparibhūtaṃ cittīkataṃ. Etaṃ ukkaṭṭhaṃ nāma kammaṃ.

Occupation is of two kinds: low occupation and superior occupation. Low occupation is the work of a mason, the work of a flower-sweeper, or that which in various regions is considered base, despised, loathed, scorned, and disrespected; this is called low occupation. Superior occupation is agriculture, trade, cattle-tending, or that which in various regions is not considered base, not despised, not loathed, not scorned, and is respected; this is called superior occupation.

Sippaṃ nāma dve sippāni – hīnañca sippaṃ ukkaṭṭhañca [P 4.0007] sippaṃ[T 2.0166]. Hīnaṃ nāma sippaṃ – naḷakārasippaṃ, kumbhakārasippaṃ, pesakārasippaṃ, cammakārasippaṃ, nahāpitasippaṃ, tesu tesu vā pana janapadesu oññātaṃ avaññātaṃ hīḷitaṃ paribhūtaṃ acittīkataṃ. Etaṃ hīnaṃ nāma sippaṃ. Ukkaṭṭhaṃ nāma sippaṃ – muddā, gaṇanā, lekhā, tesu tesu vā pana janapadesu anoññātaṃ anavaññātaṃ ahīḷitaṃ aparibhūtaṃ cittīkataṃ, etaṃ ukkaṭṭhaṃ nāma sippaṃ.

Craft is of two kinds: low craft and superior craft. Low craft is the craft of a reed-worker, the craft of a potter, the craft of a weaver, the craft of a leather-worker, the craft of a barber, or that which in various regions is considered base, despised, loathed, scorned, and disrespected; this is called low craft. Superior craft is computation by finger-signs, calculation, writing, or that which in various regions is not considered base, not despised, not loathed, not scorned, and is respected; this is called superior craft.

Sabbepi ābādhā hīnā, apica madhumeho ābādho ukkaṭṭho.

All illnesses are low, but indeed, the illness of diabetes is superior.

Liṅgaṃ nāma dve liṅgāni – hīnañca liṅgaṃ ukkaṭṭhañca liṅgaṃ. Hīnaṃ nāma liṅgaṃ – atidīghaṃ, atirassaṃ, atikaṇhaṃ, accodātaṃ, etaṃ hīnaṃ nāma liṅgaṃ. Ukkaṭṭhaṃ nāma liṅgaṃ – nātidīghaṃ, nātirassaṃ, nātikaṇhaṃ, nāccodātaṃ. Etaṃ ukkaṭṭhaṃ nāma liṅgaṃ.

Appearance, so-called, is of two kinds: inferior appearance and superior appearance. Inferior appearance, so-called, is being too tall, too short, too dark, or too fair; this is called inferior appearance. Superior appearance, so-called, is being not too tall, not too short, not too dark, and not too fair; this is called superior appearance.

Sabbepi kilesā hīnā.

All defilements are inferior.

Sabbāpi āpattiyo hīnā. Apica, sotāpattisamāpatti ukkaṭṭhā.

All offenses are inferior. But indeed, the attainment of stream-entry is superior.

Akkoso nāma dve akkosā – hīno ca akkoso ukkaṭṭho ca akkoso. Hīno nāma akkoso – oṭṭhosi, meṇḍosi, goṇosi, gadrabhosi, tiracchānagatosi, nerayikosi; natthi tuyhaṃ sugati, duggati yeva tuyhaṃ pāṭikaṅkhāti, yakārena vā bhakārena vā, kāṭakoṭacikāya vā, eso hīno nāma akkoso. Ukkaṭṭho [T 2.0167] nāma akkoso – paṇḍitosi, byattosi[V 0.0010], medhāvīsi, bahussutosi, dhammakathikosi, natthi tuyhaṃ duggati, sugatiyeva tuyhaṃ pāṭikaṅkhāti, eso ukkaṭṭho nāma akkoso.

Reviling, so-called, is of two kinds: inferior reviling and superior reviling. Inferior reviling, so-called, is to revile saying: ‘You are a camel, you are a ram, you are an ox, you are a donkey, you are an animal, you are a hell-dweller; there is no good destination for you, only a bad destination is to be expected for you,’ or to revile with the letter ‘ya’ or with the letter ‘bha,’ or with reference to the male or female organ; this is called inferior reviling. Superior reviling, so-called, is to revile saying: ‘You are wise, you are accomplished, you are intelligent, you are learned, you are a Dhamma-preacher; there is no bad destination for you, only a good destination is to be expected for you’; this is called superior reviling.

16. Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena hīnaṃ vadeti, caṇḍālaṃ venaṃ nesādaṃ rathakāraṃ pukkusaṃ – “caṇḍālosi, venosi, nesādosi, rathakārosi, pukkusosī”ti bhaṇati vadetīti uddeso. bhaṇatīti vitthāro (vajirabuddhi), āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

16. If a fully ordained one, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks to one of an inferior class with an inferior reviling, to a caṇḍāla, a vena, a nesāda, a rathakāra, a pukkusa, saying: ‘You are a caṇḍāla, you are a vena, you are a nesāda, you are a rathakāra, you are a pukkusa,’ for every utterance there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno [M 0.0010] upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, khattiyaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ – “caṇḍālosi, venosi, nesādosi, rathakārosi, pukkusosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

If a fully ordained one, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks to one of a superior class with an inferior reviling, to a khattiya, a brāhmaṇa, saying: ‘You are a caṇḍāla, you are a vena, you are a nesāda, you are a rathakāra, you are a pukkusa,’ for every utterance there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo ukkaṭṭhena hīnaṃ vadeti, caṇḍālaṃ venaṃ nesādaṃ rathakāraṃ pukkusaṃ – “khattiyosi, brāhmaṇosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

If a fully ordained one, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks to one of an inferior class with a superior reviling, to a caṇḍāla, a vena, a nesāda, a rathakāra, a pukkusa, saying: ‘You are a khattiya, you are a brāhmaṇa,’ for every utterance there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo ukkaṭṭhena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, khattiyaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ – “khattiyosi, [P 4.0008] brāhmaṇosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

If a fully ordained one, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks to one of a superior class with a superior reviling, to a khattiya, a brāhmaṇa, saying: ‘You are a khattiya, you are a brāhmaṇa,’ for every utterance there is an offense of pācittiya.

17. Upasampanno [T 2.0168] upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena hīnaṃ vadeti, avakaṇṇakaṃ [V 0.0011] javakaṇṇakaṃ dhaniṭṭhakaṃ saviṭṭhakaṃ kulavaḍḍhakaṃ – “avakaṇṇakosi, javakaṇṇakosi, dhaniṭṭhakosi, saviṭṭhakosi, kulavaḍḍhakosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

17. If a fully ordained one, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks to one with an inferior name with an inferior reviling, to an Avakaṇṇaka, a Javakaṇṇaka, a Dhaniṭṭhaka, a Saviṭṭhaka, a Kulavaḍḍhaka, saying: ‘You are an Avakaṇṇaka, you are a Javakaṇṇaka, you are a Dhaniṭṭhaka, you are a Saviṭṭhaka, you are a Kulavaḍḍhaka,’ for every utterance there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, buddharakkhitaṃ dhammarakkhitaṃ saṅgharakkhitaṃ – “avakaṇṇakosi, javakaṇṇakosi, dhaniṭṭhakosi, saviṭṭhakosi, kulavaḍḍhakosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

If a fully ordained one, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks to one with a superior name with an inferior reviling, to a Buddharakkhita, a Dhammarakkhita, a Saṅgharakkhita, saying: ‘You are an Avakaṇṇaka, you are a Javakaṇṇaka, you are a Dhaniṭṭhaka, you are a Saviṭṭhaka, you are a Kulavaḍḍhaka,’ for every utterance there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo ukkaṭṭhena hīnaṃ vadeti, avakaṇṇakaṃ javakaṇṇakaṃ dhaniṭṭhakaṃ saviṭṭhakaṃ kulavaḍḍhakaṃ – “buddharakkhitosi, dhammarakkhitosi, saṅgharakkhitosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

If a fully ordained one, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks to one with an inferior name with a superior reviling, to an Avakaṇṇaka, a Javakaṇṇaka, a Dhaniṭṭhaka, a Saviṭṭhaka, a Kulavaḍḍhaka, saying: ‘You are a Buddharakkhita, you are a Dhammarakkhita, you are a Saṅgharakkhita,’ for every utterance there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo ukkaṭṭhena ukaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, buddharakkhitaṃ dhammarakkhitaṃ saṅgharakkhitaṃ – “buddharakkhitosi, dhammarakkhitosi, saṅgharakkhitosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

If a fully ordained one, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks to one with a superior name with a superior reviling, to a Buddharakkhita, a Dhammarakkhita, a Saṅgharakkhita, saying: ‘You are a Buddharakkhita, you are a Dhammarakkhita, you are a Saṅgharakkhita,’ for every utterance there is an offense of pācittiya.

18. Upasampanno [T 2.0169][M 0.0011] upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena hīnaṃ vadeti, kosiyaṃ bhāradvājaṃ – “kosiyosi, bhāradvājosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

18. If a fully ordained one, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks to one of an inferior clan with an inferior reviling, to a Kosiya, a Bhāradvāja, saying: ‘You are a Kosiya, you are a Bhāradvāja,’ for every utterance there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, gotamaṃ moggallānaṃ kaccānaṃ vāsiṭṭhaṃ – “kosiyosi, bhāradvājosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

If a fully ordained one, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks to one of a superior clan with an inferior reviling, to a Gotama, a Moggallāna, a Kaccāna, a Vāsiṭṭha, saying: ‘You are a Kosiya, you are a Bhāradvāja,’ for every utterance there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo ukkaṭṭhena hīnaṃ vadeti, kosiyaṃ bhāradvājaṃ – “gotamosi, moggallānosi, kaccānosi, vāsiṭṭhosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

If a fully ordained one, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks to one of an inferior clan with a superior reviling, to a Kosiya, a Bhāradvāja, saying: ‘You are a Gotama, you are a Moggallāna, you are a Kaccāna, you are a Vāsiṭṭha,’ for every utterance there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo ukkaṭṭhena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, gotamaṃ moggallānaṃ kaccānaṃ vāsiṭṭhaṃ – “gotamosi, moggallānosi, kaccānosi, vāsiṭṭhosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

If a fully ordained one, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks to one of a superior clan with a superior reviling, to a Gotama, a Moggallāna, a Kaccāna, a Vāsiṭṭha, saying: ‘You are a Gotama, you are a Moggallāna, you are a Kaccāna, you are a Vāsiṭṭha,’ for every utterance there is an offense of pācittiya.

19. Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena hīnaṃ vadeti, koṭṭhakaṃ pupphachaḍḍakaṃ – “koṭṭhakosi, pupphachaḍḍakosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

19. If a fully ordained one, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks to one of an inferior occupation with an inferior reviling, to a stone-breaker, a flower-refuse-remover, saying: ‘You are a stone-breaker, you are a flower-refuse-remover,’ for every utterance there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, kassakaṃ vāṇijaṃ gorakkhaṃ – “koṭṭhakosi, pupphachaḍḍakosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

If a fully ordained one, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks to one of a superior occupation with an inferior reviling, to a farmer, a merchant, a cowherd, saying: ‘You are a stone-breaker, you are a flower-refuse-remover,’ for every utterance there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno [V 0.0012] upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo [T 2.0170] ukkaṭṭhena hīnaṃ vadeti, koṭṭhakaṃ pupphachaḍḍakaṃ – “kassakosi, vāṇijosi, gorakkhosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or humiliate another fully ordained person, addresses an inferior person with a high abuse—a storekeeper or a flower-refuse-remover—saying, 'You are a farmer; you are a merchant; you are a cowherd.' For every utterance, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo ukkaṭṭhena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, kassakaṃ vāṇijaṃ gorakkhaṃ – “kassakosi, vāṇijosi, gorakkhosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or humiliate another fully ordained person, addresses a superior person with a high abuse—a farmer, a merchant, or a cowherd—saying, 'You are a farmer; you are a merchant; you are a cowherd.' For every utterance, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

20. Upasampanno [M 0.0012] upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena hīnaṃ vadeti, naḷakāraṃ kumbhakāraṃ pesakāraṃ cammakāraṃ nahāpitaṃ – “naḷakārosi, kumbhakārosi, pesakārosi, cammakārosi, nahāpitosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

20. A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or humiliate another fully ordained person, addresses an inferior person with a low abuse—a reed-worker, a potter, a weaver, a leather-worker, or a barber—saying, 'You are a reed-worker; you are a potter; you are a weaver; you are a leather-worker; you are a barber.' For every utterance, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, muddikaṃ gaṇakaṃ lekhakaṃ – “naḷakārosi, kumbhakārosi, pesakārosi, cammakārosi, nahāpitosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or humiliate another fully ordained person, addresses a superior person with a low abuse—an accountant, a calculator, or a scribe—saying, 'You are a reed-worker; you are a potter; you are a weaver; you are a leather-worker; you are a barber.' For every utterance, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo ukkaṭṭhena hīnaṃ vadeti, naḷakāraṃ kumbhakāraṃ pesakāraṃ cammakāraṃ nahāpitaṃ – “muddikosi, gaṇakosi, lekhakosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or humiliate another fully ordained person, addresses an inferior person with a high abuse—a reed-worker, a potter, a weaver, a leather-worker, or a barber—saying, 'You are an accountant; you are a calculator; you are a scribe.' For every utterance, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo [T 2.0171] ukkaṭṭhena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, muddikaṃ gaṇakaṃ lekhakaṃ – “muddikosi, gaṇakosi, lekhakosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or humiliate another fully ordained person, addresses a superior person with a high abuse—an accountant, a calculator, or a scribe—saying, 'You are an accountant; you are a calculator; you are a scribe.' For every utterance, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

21. Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena hīnaṃ vadeti, kuṭṭhikaṃ gaṇḍikaṃ kilāsikaṃ sosikaṃ apamārikaṃ – “kuṭṭhikosi, gaṇḍikosi, kilāsikosi, sosikosi, apamārikosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

21. A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or humiliate another fully ordained person, addresses an inferior person with a low abuse—a leper, one with boils, one with a skin disease, a consumptive person, or an epileptic—saying, 'You are a leper; you are one with boils; you are one with a skin disease; you are a consumptive person; you are an epileptic.' For every utterance, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

Upasampanno [V 0.0013] upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, madhumehikaṃ – “kuṭṭhikosi, gaṇḍikosi, kilāsikosi, sosikosi, apamārikosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or humiliate another fully ordained person, addresses a superior person with a low abuse—a diabetic—saying, 'You are a leper; you are one with boils; you are one with a skin disease; you are a consumptive person; you are an epileptic.' For every utterance, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo ukkaṭṭhena hīnaṃ vadeti, kuṭṭhikaṃ gaṇḍikaṃ kilāsikaṃ sosikaṃ apamārikaṃ – “madhumehikosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or humiliate another fully ordained person, addresses an inferior person with a high abuse—a leper, one with boils, one with a skin disease, a consumptive person, or an epileptic—saying, 'You are a diabetic.' For every utterance, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

Upasampanno [M 0.0013] upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo ukkaṭṭhena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, madhumehikaṃ – “madhumehikosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or humiliate another fully ordained person, addresses a superior person with a high abuse—a diabetic—saying, 'You are a diabetic.' For every utterance, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

22. Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena hīnaṃ vadeti, atidīghaṃ atirassaṃ atikaṇhaṃ accodātaṃ [T 2.0172] – “atidīghosi, atirassosi, atikaṇhosi, accodātosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

22. A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or humiliate another fully ordained person, addresses an inferior person with a low abuse—one who is excessively tall, excessively short, excessively dark, or excessively pale—saying, 'You are excessively tall; you are excessively short; you are excessively dark; you are excessively pale.' For every utterance, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, nātidīghaṃ nātirassaṃ nātikaṇhaṃ nāccodātaṃ – “atidīghosi, atirassosi, atikaṇhosi, accodātosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or humiliate another fully ordained person, addresses a superior person with a low abuse—one who is not too tall, not too short, not too dark, or not too pale—saying, 'You are excessively tall; you are excessively short; you are excessively dark; you are excessively pale.' For every utterance, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo ukkaṭṭhena hīnaṃ vadeti, atidīghaṃ atirassaṃ atikaṇhaṃ accodātaṃ – “nātidīghosi, nātirassosi, nātikaṇhosi, nāccodātosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or humiliate another fully ordained person, addresses an inferior person with a high abuse—one who is excessively tall, excessively short, excessively dark, or excessively pale—saying, 'You are not too tall; you are not too short; you are not too dark; you are not too pale.' For every utterance, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo ukkaṭṭhena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, nātidīghaṃ nātirassaṃ nātikaṇhaṃ [P 4.0009] nāccodātaṃ – “nātidīghosi, nātirassosi, nātikaṇhosi, nāccodātosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or humiliate another fully ordained person, addresses a superior person with a high abuse—one who is not too tall, not too short, not too dark, or not too pale—saying, 'You are not too tall; you are not too short; you are not too dark; you are not too pale.' For every utterance, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

23. Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena hīnaṃ vadeti, rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṃ dosapariyuṭṭhitaṃ mohapariyuṭṭhitaṃ – “rāgapariyuṭṭhitosi, dosapariyuṭṭhitosi, mohapariyuṭṭhitosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

23. A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or humiliate another fully ordained person, addresses an inferior person with a low abuse—one assailed by lust, assailed by hatred, or assailed by delusion—saying, 'You are assailed by lust; you are assailed by hatred; you are assailed by delusion.' For every utterance, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

Upasampanno [V 0.0014] upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, vītarāgaṃ vītadosaṃ vītamohaṃ – “rāgapariyuṭṭhitosi[T 2.0173], dosapariyuṭṭhitosi, mohapariyuṭṭhitosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or humiliate another fully ordained person, addresses a superior person with a low abuse—one free from lust, free from hatred, or free from delusion—saying, 'You are assailed by lust; you are assailed by hatred; you are assailed by delusion.' For every utterance, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo ukkaṭṭhena hīnaṃ vadeti, rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṃ dosapariyuṭṭhitaṃ mohapariyuṭṭhitaṃ [M 0.0014] – “vītarāgosi, vītadososi, vītamohosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or humiliate another fully ordained person, addresses an inferior person with a high abuse—one assailed by lust, assailed by hatred, or assailed by delusion—saying, 'You are free from lust; you are free from hatred; you are free from delusion.' For every utterance, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo ukkaṭṭhena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, vītarāgaṃ vītadosaṃ vītamohaṃ – “vītarāgosi, vītadososi, vītamohosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to make ashamed another fully ordained person, speaks to a superior person with a superior reviling, to one free from lust, free from hatred, or free from delusion, saying: 'You are free from lust, you are free from hatred, you are free from delusion.' For every utterance, there is the falling into an offense of pācittiya.

24. Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena hīnaṃ vadeti, pārājikaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ thullaccayaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ pācittiyaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ pāṭidesanīyaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ dukkaṭaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ – “pārājikaṃ ajjhāpannosi, saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpannosi, thullaccayaṃ ajjhāpannosi, pācittiyaṃ ajjhāpannosi, pāṭidesanīyaṃ ajjhāpannosi, dukkaṭaṃ ajjhāpannosi, dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpannosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

24. A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to make ashamed another fully ordained person, speaks to an inferior person with an inferior reviling, to one who has fallen into a pārājika offense, a saṅghādisesa offense, a thullaccaya offense, a pācittiya offense, a pāṭidesanīya offense, a dukkaṭa offense, or a dubbhāsita offense, saying: 'You have fallen into a pārājika offense, you have fallen into a saṅghādisesa offense, you have fallen into a thullaccaya offense, you have fallen into a pācittiya offense, you have fallen into a pāṭidesanīya offense, you have fallen into a dukkaṭa offense, you have fallen into a dubbhāsita offense.' For every utterance, there is the falling into an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, sotāpannaṃ – “pārājikaṃ ajjhāpannosi…pe… [T 2.0174] dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpannosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to make ashamed another fully ordained person, speaks to a superior person with an inferior reviling, to a stream-enterer, saying: 'You have fallen into a pārājika offense... you have fallen into a dubbhāsita offense.' For every utterance, there is the falling into an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo ukkaṭṭhena hīnaṃ vadeti, pārājikaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ…pe… dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ – “sotāpannosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to make ashamed another fully ordained person, speaks to an inferior person with a superior reviling, to one who has fallen into a pārājika offense... or a dubbhāsita offense, saying: 'You are a stream-enterer.' For every utterance, there is the falling into an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo ukkaṭṭhena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, sotāpannaṃ – “sotāpannosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to make ashamed another fully ordained person, speaks to a superior person with a superior reviling, to a stream-enterer, saying: 'You are a stream-enterer.' For every utterance, there is the falling into an offense of pācittiya.

25. Upasampanno [V 0.0015] upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena hīnaṃ vadeti, oṭṭhaṃ meṇḍaṃ goṇaṃ gadrabhaṃ tiracchānagataṃ nerayikaṃ – “oṭṭhosi, meṇḍosi, goṇosi, gadrabhosi, tiracchānagatosi, nerayikosi, natthi tuyhaṃ sugati, duggati yeva tuyhaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

25. A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to make ashamed another fully ordained person, speaks to an inferior person with an inferior reviling, to one who is a camel, a ram, an ox, a donkey, an animal, or a hell-being, saying: 'You are a camel, you are a ram, you are an ox, you are a donkey, you are an animal, you are a hell-being. There is no good destination for you; only a bad destination is to be expected for you.' For every utterance, there is the falling into an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno [M 0.0015] upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, paṇḍitaṃ byattaṃ medhāvi bahussutaṃ dhammakathikaṃ – “oṭṭhosi, meṇḍosi, goṇosi, gadrabhosi, tiracchānagatosi, nerayikosi; natthi tuyhaṃ sugati, duggati yeva tuyhaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to make ashamed another fully ordained person, speaks to a superior person with an inferior reviling, to one who is wise, competent, intelligent, learned, or a Dhamma-speaker, saying: 'You are a camel, you are a ram, you are an ox, you are a donkey, you are an animal, you are a hell-being. There is no good destination for you; only a bad destination is to be expected for you.' For every utterance, there is the falling into an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo [T 2.0175] ukkaṭṭhena hīnaṃ vadeti, oṭṭhaṃ meṇḍaṃ goṇaṃ gadrabhaṃ tiracchānagataṃ nerayikaṃ – “paṇḍitosi, byattosi, medhāvīsi, bahussutosi, dhammakathikosi, natthi tuyhaṃ duggati, sugati yeva tuyhaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to make ashamed another fully ordained person, speaks to an inferior person with a superior reviling, to one who is a camel, a ram, an ox, a donkey, an animal, or a hell-being, saying: 'You are wise, you are competent, you are intelligent, you are learned, you are a Dhamma-speaker. There is no bad destination for you; only a good destination is to be expected for you.' For every utterance, there is the falling into an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo ukkaṭṭhena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, paṇḍitaṃ byattaṃ medhāviṃ bahussutaṃ dhammakathikaṃ – “paṇḍitosi, byattosi, medhāvīsi, bahussutosi, dhammakathikosi, natthi tuyhaṃ duggati, sugati yeva tuyhaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to make ashamed another fully ordained person, speaks to a superior person with a superior reviling, to one who is wise, competent, intelligent, learned, or a Dhamma-speaker, saying: 'You are wise, you are competent, you are intelligent, you are learned, you are a Dhamma-speaker. There is no bad destination for you; only a good destination is to be expected for you.' For every utterance, there is the falling into an offense of pācittiya.

26. Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo evaṃ vadeti, “santi idhekacce caṇḍālā venā nesādā rathakārā pukkusā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dukkaṭassa.

26. A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to make ashamed another fully ordained person, speaks thus, saying: 'There are here certain outcastes, bamboo workers, hunters, chariot makers, and scavengers.' For every utterance, there is the falling into an offense of dukkaṭa.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo evaṃ vadeti, “santi idhekacce khattiyā, brāhmaṇā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dukkaṭassa.

A fully ordained person, wishing to revile, wishing to disparage, wishing to make ashamed another fully ordained person, speaks thus, saying: 'There are here certain warriors and brahmins.' For every utterance, there is the falling into an offense of dukkaṭa.

27. Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo evaṃ [P 4.0010] vadeti, “santi idhekacce avakaṇṇakā javakaṇṇakā dhaniṭṭhakā saviṭṭhakā kulavaḍḍhakā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Santi idhekacce buddharakkhitā dhammarakkhitā [T 2.0176] saṅgharakkhitā”ti bhaṇati [V 0.0016] …pe…. “Santi idhekacce kosiyā bhāradvājā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Santi idhekacce gotamā moggallānā kaccānā vāsiṭṭhā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Santi idhekacce koṭṭhakā pupphachaḍḍakā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Santi idhekacce kassakā vāṇijā gorakkhā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Santi idhekacce naḷakārā kumbhakārā [M 0.0016] pesakārā cammakārā nahāpitā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Santi idhekacce muddikā gaṇakā lekhakā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Santi idhekacce kuṭṭhikā gaṇḍikā kilāsikā sosikā apamārikā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Santi idhekacce madhumehikā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Santi idhekacce atidīghā atirassā atikaṇhā accodātā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Santi idhekacce nātidīghā nātirassā nātikaṇhā nāccodātā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Santi idhekacce rāgapariyuṭṭhitā dosapariyuṭṭhitā mohapariyuṭṭhitā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Santi idhekacce vītarāgā vītadosā vītamohā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Santi idhekacce pārājikaṃ ajjhāpannā…pe… dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpannā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Santi idhekacce sotāpannā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Santi idhekacce oṭṭhā meṇḍā goṇā gadrabhā tiracchānagatā nerayikā, natthi tesaṃ sugati, duggatiyeva tesaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dukkaṭassa.

27. If a fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or make ashamed another fully ordained person, says thus: 'Here there are some named Avakaṇṇaka, Javakaṇṇaka, Dhaniṭṭhaka, Saviṭṭhaka, Kulavaḍḍhaka...' ... 'Here there are some named Buddharakkhita, Dhammarakkhita, Saṅgharakkhita...' ... 'Here there are some of the Kosiya clan, of the Bhāradvāja clan...' ... 'Here there are some of the Gotama clan, of the Moggallāna clan, of the Kaccāna clan, of the Vāsiṭṭha clan...' ... 'Here there are some who work with stone-mortars, some who sweep up flower-refuse...' ... 'Here there are some farmers, merchants, cowherds...' ... 'Here there are some reed-workers, potters, weavers, leather-workers, barbers...' ... 'Here there are some who count by cracking their knuckles, calculators, scribes...' ... 'Here there are some with leprosy, with boils, with skin diseases, with consumption, with epilepsy...' ... 'Here there are some with diabetes...' ... 'Here there are some who are excessively tall, excessively short, excessively dark, excessively fair...' ... 'Here there are some who are not excessively tall, not excessively short, not excessively dark, not excessively fair...' ... 'Here there are some overcome by lust, overcome by hatred, overcome by delusion...' ... 'Here there are some free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion...' ... 'Here there are some who have incurred a pārājika offense... who have incurred a dubbhāsita offense...' ... 'Here there are some who are stream-enterers...' ... 'Here there are some who are camels, rams, oxen, donkeys, animals, denizens of hell; for them there is no good destination, only a bad destination is to be expected for them,' for every utterance, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred.

28. Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo [T 2.0177] evaṃ vadeti, “santi idhekacce paṇḍitā byattā, medhāvī bahussutā dhammakathikā, natthi tesaṃ duggati, sugatiyeva tesaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dukkaṭassa.

28. If a fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or make ashamed another fully ordained person, says thus: 'Here there are some who are wise, competent, of penetrating wisdom, of great learning, and Dhamma speakers; for them there is no bad destination, only a good destination is to be expected for them,' for every utterance, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred.

29. Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo evaṃ vadeti, “ye nūna caṇḍālā venā nesādā rathakārā pukkusā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dukkaṭassa…pe….

29. If a fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or make ashamed another fully ordained person, says thus: 'Whoever they are, they are surely of the caṇḍāla class, of the bamboo-worker class, of the hunter class, of the leather-worker class, of the flower-refuse-sweeper class,' for every utterance, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo evaṃ vadeti, “ye nūna paṇḍitā byattā medhāvī bahussutā dhammakathikā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dukkaṭassa.

If a fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or make ashamed another fully ordained person, says thus: 'Whoever they are, they are surely wise, competent, of penetrating wisdom, of great learning, and Dhamma speakers,' for every utterance, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred.

30. Upasampanno upasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo evaṃ vadeti, “na mayaṃ caṇḍālā venā nesādā rathakārā pukkusā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Na mayaṃ paṇḍitā byattā [V 0.0017] medhāvī bahussutā dhammakathikā, natthamhākaṃ duggati, sugatiyeva amhākaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā”ti bhaṇati. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya dukkaṭassa.

30. If a fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or make ashamed another fully ordained person, says thus: 'We are not of the caṇḍāla class, not of the bamboo-worker class, not of the hunter class, not of the leather-worker class, not of the flower-refuse-sweeper class...' ... 'We are not wise, not competent, not of penetrating wisdom, not of great learning, not Dhamma speakers; for us there is no bad destination, only a good destination is to be expected for us,' for every utterance, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred.

31. Upasampanno [M 0.0017] anupasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo hīnena hīnaṃ vadeti,…pe… hīnena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti…pe… ukkaṭṭhena hīnaṃ vadeti…pe… ukkaṭṭhena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, paṇḍitaṃ byattaṃ medhāviṃ bahussutaṃ dhammakathikaṃ – “paṇḍitosi, byattosi, medhāvīsi, bahussutosi, dhammakathikosi, natthi tuyhaṃ duggati, sugatiyeva tuyhaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā”ti [T 2.0178] bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dukkaṭassa.

31. If a fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or make ashamed an unordained person, addresses a low person with low terms... addresses a high person with low terms... addresses a low person with high terms... addresses a high person with high terms; and says to one who is wise, competent, of penetrating wisdom, of great learning, and a Dhamma speaker: 'You are wise, you are competent, you are of penetrating wisdom, you are of great learning, you are a Dhamma speaker; for you there is no bad destination, only a good destination is to be expected for you,' for every utterance, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred.

Upasampanno anupasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo evaṃ vadeti, “santi idhekacce caṇḍālā venā nesādā rathakārā pukkusā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Santi idhekacce paṇḍitā byattā medhāvī bahussutā dhammakathikā, natthi tesaṃ duggati, sugatiyeva tesaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dukkaṭassa.

If a fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or make ashamed an unordained person, says thus: 'Here there are some of the caṇḍāla class, of the bamboo-worker class, of the hunter class, of the leather-worker class, of the flower-refuse-sweeper class...' ... 'Here there are some who are wise, competent, of penetrating wisdom, of great learning, and Dhamma speakers; for them there is no bad destination, only a good destination is to be expected for them,' for every utterance, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred.

Upasampanno anupasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo evaṃ vadeti, “ye nūna caṇḍālā venā nesādā rathakārā pukkusā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Ye nūna paṇḍitā byattā medhāvī bahussutā dhammakathikā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dukkaṭassa.

If a fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or make ashamed an unordained person, says thus: 'Whoever they are, they are surely of the caṇḍāla class, of the bamboo-worker class, of the hunter class, of the leather-worker class, of the flower-refuse-sweeper class...' ... 'Whoever they are, they are surely wise, competent, of penetrating wisdom, of great learning, and Dhamma speakers,' for every utterance, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred.

Upasampanno anupasampannaṃ khuṃsetukāmo vambhetukāmo maṅkukattukāmo evaṃ vadeti, “na mayaṃ caṇḍālā venā nesādā rathakārā pukkusā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Na mayaṃ paṇḍitā byattā medhāvī bahussutā dhammakathikā, natthamhākaṃ [P 4.0011] duggati, sugatiyeva amhākaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā”ti bhaṇati. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya dukkaṭassa.

If a fully ordained person, wishing to revile, disparage, or make ashamed an unordained person, says thus: 'We are not of the caṇḍāla class, not of the bamboo-worker class, not of the hunter class, not of the leather-worker class, not of the flower-refuse-sweeper class...' ... 'We are not wise, not competent, not of penetrating wisdom, not of great learning, not Dhamma speakers; for us there is no bad destination, only a good destination is to be expected for us,' for every utterance, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred.

32. Upasampanno upasampannaṃ na khuṃsetukāmo na vambhetukāmo na maṅkukattukāmo, davakamyatā hīnena hīnaṃ vadeti, caṇḍālaṃ venaṃ nesādaṃ rathakāraṃ pukkusaṃ – “caṇḍālosi, venosi, nesādosi, rathakārosi[T 2.0179], pukkusosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dubbhāsitassa.

32. If a fully ordained person, not wishing to revile, not wishing to disparage, not wishing to make ashamed another fully ordained person, but with the intention of jesting, addresses a person of low birth with low terms, saying to one of the caṇḍāla class, the bamboo-worker class, the hunter class, the leather-worker class, or the flower-refuse-sweeper class: 'You are of the caṇḍāla class, you are of the bamboo-worker class, you are of the hunter class, you are of the leather-worker class, you are of the flower-refuse-sweeper class,' for every utterance, a dubbhāsita offense is incurred.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ na khuṃsetukāmo na vambhetukāmo na maṅkukattukāmo, davakamyatā hīnena [V 0.0018] ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, khattiyaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ – “caṇḍālosi, venosi, nesādosi, rathakārosi, pukkusosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dubbhāsitassa.

A fully ordained one, not wishing to revile, not wishing to disparage, and not wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks out of a desire for jest, reviling a person of high birth with a term of low birth. To a khattiya or a brahmin, he says: 'You are a caṇḍāla, you are a vena, you are a nesāda, you are a rathakāra, you are a pukkusa.' For every utterance, there is an offense of wrong speech.

Upasampanno [M 0.0018] upasampannaṃ na khuṃsetukāmo na vambhetukāmo na maṅkukattukāmo, davakamyatā ukkaṭṭhena hīnaṃ vadeti, caṇḍālaṃ venaṃ nesādaṃ rathakāraṃ pukkusaṃ – “khattiyosi, brāhmaṇosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dubbhāsitassa.

A fully ordained one, not wishing to revile, not wishing to disparage, and not wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks out of a desire for jest, reviling a person of low birth with a term of high birth. To a caṇḍāla, a vena, a nesāda, a rathakāra, or a pukkusa, he says: 'You are a khattiya, you are a brahmin.' For every utterance, there is an offense of wrong speech.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ na khuṃsetukāmo na vambhetukāmo na maṅkukattukāmo, davakamyatā ukkaṭṭhena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, khattiyaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ – “khattiyosi, brāhmaṇosī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dubbhāsitassa.

A fully ordained one, not wishing to revile, not wishing to disparage, and not wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks out of a desire for jest, reviling a person of high birth with a term of high birth. To a khattiya or a brahmin, he says: 'You are a khattiya, you are a brahmin.' For every utterance, there is an offense of wrong speech.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ na khuṃsetukāmo na vambhetukāmo na maṅkukattukāmo, davakamyatā hīnena hīnaṃ vadeti…pe… hīnena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti…pe… ukkaṭṭhena hīnaṃ vadeti…pe… ukkaṭṭhena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, paṇḍitaṃ byattaṃ medhāviṃ bahussutaṃ dhammakathikaṃ – “paṇḍitosi, byattosi, medhāvīsi, bahussutosi, dhammakathikosi, natthi tuyhaṃ duggati, sugati yeva tuyhaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dubbhāsitassa.

A fully ordained one, not wishing to revile, not wishing to disparage, and not wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks out of a desire for jest, reviling a person of low birth with a term of low birth... (and so on)... reviling a person of high birth with a term of low birth... (and so on)... reviling a person of low birth with a term of high birth... (and so on)... reviling a person of high birth with a term of high birth. To one who is wise, competent, intelligent, learned, or a Dhamma-speaker, he says: 'You are wise, you are competent, you are intelligent, you are learned, you are a Dhamma-speaker. There is no bad destination for you; only a good destination is to be expected for you.' For every utterance, there is an offense of wrong speech.

33. Upasampanno upasampannaṃ na khuṃsetukāmo na vambhetukāmo na [T 2.0180] maṅkukattukāmo, davakamyatā evaṃ vadeti, “santi idhekacce caṇḍālā venā nesādā rathakārā pukkusā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Santi idhekacce paṇḍitā byattā medhāvī bahussutā dhammakathikā, natthi tesaṃ duggati, sugati yeva tesaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dubbhāsitassa.

33. A fully ordained one, not wishing to revile, not wishing to disparage, and not wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks thus out of a desire for jest. He says: 'There are here some caṇḍālas, venas, nesādas, rathakāras, and pukkusas.'... (and so on)... He says: 'There are here some who are wise, competent, intelligent, learned, and Dhamma-speakers. There is no bad destination for them; only a good destination is to be expected for them.' For every utterance, there is an offense of wrong speech.

Upasampanno upasampannaṃ na khuṃsetukāmo na vambhetukāmo na maṅkukattukāmo, davakamyatā evaṃ vadeti, “ye nūna caṇḍālā venā nesādā rathakārā pukkusā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Ye nūna paṇḍitā byattā medhāvī bahussutā dhammakathikā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dubbhāsitassa.

A fully ordained one, not wishing to revile, not wishing to disparage, and not wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks thus out of a desire for jest. He says: 'Whoever they are, they are surely caṇḍālas, venas, nesādas, rathakāras, and pukkusas.'... (and so on)... He says: 'Whoever they are, they are surely wise, competent, intelligent, learned, and Dhamma-speakers.' For every utterance, there is an offense of wrong speech.
