Upasampanno upasampannaṃ na khuṃsetukāmo na vambhetukāmo na maṅkukattukāmo, davakamyatā evaṃ vadeti, “na mayaṃ caṇḍālā venā nesādā rathakārā pukkusā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Na mayaṃ paṇḍitā [V 0.0019] byattā medhāvī bahussutā dhammakathikā, natthamhākaṃ duggati, sugatiyeva amhākaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā”ti bhaṇati. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya dubbhāsitassa.

A fully ordained one, not wishing to revile, not wishing to disparage, and not wishing to humiliate another fully ordained one, speaks thus out of a desire for jest. He says: 'We are not caṇḍālas, venas, nesādas, rathakāras, or pukkusas.'... (and so on)... He says: 'We are not wise, competent, intelligent, learned, or Dhamma-speakers. There is no bad destination for us; only a good destination is to be expected for us.' For every utterance, there is an offense of wrong speech.

34. Upasampanno [M 0.0019] anupasampannaṃ na khuṃsetukāmo na vambhetukāmo na maṅkukattukāmo, davakamyatā hīnena hīnaṃ vadeti…pe… hīnena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti…pe… ukkaṭṭhena hīnaṃ vadeti…pe… ukkaṭṭhena ukkaṭṭhaṃ vadeti, paṇḍitaṃ byattaṃ medhāviṃ bahussutaṃ dhammakathikaṃ – “paṇḍitosi[T 2.0181], byattosi, medhāvīsi, bahussutosi dhammakathikosi, natthi tuyhaṃ duggati; sugati yeva tuyhaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dubbhāsitassa.

34. A fully ordained one, not wishing to revile, not wishing to disparage, and not wishing to humiliate an unordained person, speaks out of a desire for jest, reviling a person of low birth with a term of low birth... (and so on)... reviling a person of high birth with a term of low birth... (and so on)... reviling a person of low birth with a term of high birth... (and so on)... reviling a person of high birth with a term of high birth. To one who is wise, competent, intelligent, learned, or a Dhamma-speaker, he says: 'You are wise, you are competent, you are intelligent, you are learned, you are a Dhamma-speaker. There is no bad destination for you; only a good destination is to be expected for you.' For every utterance, there is an offense of wrong speech.

Upasampanno anupasampannaṃ na khuṃsetukāmo na vambhetukāmo na maṅkukattukāmo, davakamyatā evaṃ vadeti, “santi idhekacce caṇḍālā venā nesādā rathakārā pukkusā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Santi idhekacce paṇḍitā byattā medhāvī bahussutā dhammakathikā, natthi tesaṃ duggati, sugati yeva tesaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dubbhāsitassa.

A fully ordained one, not wishing to revile, not wishing to disparage, and not wishing to humiliate an unordained person, speaks thus out of a desire for jest. He says: 'There are here some caṇḍālas, venas, nesādas, rathakāras, and pukkusas.'... (and so on)... He says: 'There are here some who are wise, competent, intelligent, learned, and Dhamma-speakers. There is no bad destination for them; only a good destination is to be expected for them.' For every utterance, there is an offense of wrong speech.

Upasampanno anupasampannaṃ na khuṃsetukāmo na vambhetukāmo na maṅkukattukāmo, davakamyatā evaṃ vadeti, “ye nūna caṇḍālā venā nesādā rathakārā pukkusā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Ye nūna paṇḍitā byattā medhāvī bahussutā dhammakathikā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dubbhāsitassa.

A fully ordained one, not wishing to revile, not wishing to disparage, and not wishing to humiliate an unordained person, speaks thus out of a desire for jest. He says: 'Whoever they are, they are surely caṇḍālas, venas, nesādas, rathakāras, and pukkusas.'... (and so on)... He says: 'Whoever they are, they are surely wise, competent, intelligent, learned, and Dhamma-speakers.' For every utterance, there is an offense of wrong speech.

Upasampanno anupasampannaṃ na khuṃsetukāmo na vambhetukāmo na maṅkukattukāmo, davakamyatā evaṃ vadeti, “na mayaṃ caṇḍālā venā nesādā rathakārā pukkusā”ti bhaṇati…pe…. “Na mayaṃ paṇḍitā byattā medhāvī bahussutā dhammakathikā, natthamhākaṃ duggati, sugati yeva amhākaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā”ti bhaṇati, āpatti vācāya, vācāya dubbhāsitassa.

A fully ordained one, not wishing to revile, not wishing to disparage, and not wishing to humiliate an unordained person, speaks thus out of a desire for jest. He says: 'We are not caṇḍālas, venas, nesādas, rathakāras, or pukkusas.'... (and so on)... He says: 'We are not wise, competent, intelligent, learned, or Dhamma-speakers. There is no bad destination for us; only a good destination is to be expected for us.' For every utterance, there is an offense of wrong speech.

35. Anāpatti [T 2.0182] atthapurekkhārassa, dhammapurekkhārassa, anusāsanipurekkhārassa, ummattakassa, khittacittassa, vedanāṭṭassa, ādikammikassāti.

35. There is no offense for one who has the meaning as his aim, for one who has the text as his aim, for one who has instruction as his aim, for one who is insane, for one whose mind is distracted, for one who is afflicted by pain, or for the first offender.

Omasavādasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The second training rule on contemptuous speech is finished.

3. Pesuññasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Training Rule on Divisive Speech

36. Tena [T 2.0183][P 4.0012][V 0.0020] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhūnaṃ [M 0.0020] bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ pesuññaṃ upasaṃharanti; imassa sutvā amussa akkhāyanti, imassa bhedāya; amussa sutvā imassa akkhāyanti, amussa bhedāya. Tena anuppannāni ceva bhaṇḍanāni uppajjanti, uppannāni ca bhaṇḍanāni bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattanti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhūnaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ pesuññaṃ upasaṃharissanti, imassa sutvā amussa akkhāyissanti, imassa bhedāya; amussa sutvā imassa akkhāyissanti, amussa bhedāya! Tena anuppannāni ceva bhaṇḍanāni uppajjanti, uppannāni ca bhaṇḍanāni bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattantī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū chabbaggiye bhikkhū anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ pesuññaṃ upasaṃharatha, imassa sutvā amussa akkhāyatha, imassa bhedāya, amussa sutvā imassa akkhāyatha, amussa bhedāya? Tena anuppannāni ceva bhaṇḍanāni uppajjanti, uppannāni ca bhaṇḍanāni bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattantī”ti? “Saccaṃ[T 2.0184], bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, bhikkhūnaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ pesuññaṃ upasaṃharissatha! Imassa sutvā amussa akkhāyissatha, imassa bhedāya! Amussa sutvā imassa akkhāyissatha, amussa bhedāya! Tena anuppannāni ceva bhaṇḍanāni uppajjanti, uppannāni ca bhaṇḍanāni bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattanti. Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya. Pasannānaṃ vā bhiyyobhāvāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

36. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the monks of the group of six conveyed divisive speech to monks who were quarreling, disputing, and engaged in arguments; having heard from this one, they reported it to that one for the purpose of division from this one; having heard from that one, they reported it to this one for the purpose of division from that one. Because of this, quarrels that had not yet arisen arose, and quarrels that had arisen grew and spread extensively. Those monks who were of few wishes… criticized, scorned, and disparaged them, saying: “How can the monks of the group of six convey divisive speech to monks who are quarreling, disputing, and engaged in arguments? Having heard from this one, they report it to that one for the purpose of division from this one; having heard from that one, they report it to this one for the purpose of division from that one! Because of this, quarrels that had not yet arisen arise, and quarrels that had arisen grow and spread extensively!” Then those monks, having rebuked the monks of the group of six in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, monks, that you convey divisive speech to monks who are quarreling, disputing, and engaged in arguments? Having heard from this one, you report it to that one for the purpose of division from this one; having heard from that one, you report it to this one for the purpose of division from that one? And because of this, quarrels that had not yet arisen arise, and quarrels that had arisen grow and spread extensively?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “Worthless men, how can you convey divisive speech to monks who are quarreling, disputing, and engaged in arguments? Having heard from this one, you report it to that one for the purpose of division from this one! Having heard from that one, you report it to this one for the purpose of division from that one! Because of this, quarrels that had not yet arisen arise, and quarrels that had arisen grow and spread extensively. This, worthless men, is not for the inspiration of the uninspired or for the increase of the inspired… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule in this way:”

37. “Bhikkhupesuññe pācittiya”nti.

37. “Divisive speech concerning a monk is an offense entailing expiation.”

38. Pesuññaṃ nāma dvīhākārehi pesuññaṃ hoti – piyakamyassa vā bhedādhippāyassa vā. Dasahākārehi pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – jātitopi, nāmatopi, gottatopi, kammatopi, sippatopi, ābādhatopi, liṅgatopi, kilesatopi, āpattitopi, akkosatopi.

38. Divisive speech occurs for two reasons: from a desire for affection or with the intention to cause division. One conveys divisive speech on ten grounds: regarding birth, name, clan, occupation, craft, illness, physical characteristics, defilement, an offense, or abuse.

Jāti [V 0.0021] nāma dve jātiyo – hīnā ca jāti ukkaṭṭhā ca jāti. Hīnā nāma jāti – caṇḍālajāti venajāti nesādajāti rathakārajāti pukkusajāti[M 0.0021]. Esā hīnā nāma jāti. Ukkaṭṭhā nāma jāti – khattiyajāti brāhmaṇajāti. Esā ukkaṭṭhā nāma jāti…pe….

Birth is of two kinds: low birth and superior birth. Low birth is birth as a caṇḍāla, a veṇa, a nesāda, a rathakāra, or a pukkusa. This is called low birth. Superior birth is birth as a khattiya or a brāhmaṇa. This is called superior birth… and so on.

Akkoso nāma dve akkosā – hīno ca akkoso ukkaṭṭho ca akkoso. Hīno nāma akkoso – oṭṭhosi, meṇḍosi, goṇosi, gadrabhosi, tiracchānagatosi, nerayikosi; natthi tuyhaṃ sugati; duggati yeva tuyhaṃ pāṭikaṅkhāti, yakārena vā bhakārena vā kāṭakoṭacikāya vā. Eso [T 2.0185] hīno nāma [P 4.0013] akkoso. Ukkaṭṭho nāma akkoso – paṇḍitosi, byattosi, medhāvīsi, bahussutosi, dhammakathikosi; natthi tuyhaṃ duggati; sugati yeva tuyhaṃ pāṭikaṅkhāti. Eso ukkaṭṭho nāma akkoso.

Abuse is of two kinds: low abuse and superior abuse. Low abuse is this: “You are a camel, you are a ram, you are an ox, you are a donkey, you are an animal, you are a hell-being; there is no good destination for you; only a bad destination should be expected by you,” or by abuse with the ‘ya’ syllable, the ‘bha’ syllable, or concerning the male and female organs. This is called low abuse. Superior abuse is this: “You are wise, you are competent, you are intelligent, you are learned, you are a speaker of the Dhamma; there is no bad destination for you; only a good destination should be expected by you.” This is called superior abuse.

39. Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘caṇḍālo veno nesādo rathakāro pukkuso’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

39. If a fully ordained monk, having heard from a fully ordained monk, conveys divisive speech to another fully ordained monk, saying, “So-and-so says of you, ‘He is a caṇḍāla, a veṇa, a nesāda, a rathakāra, a pukkusa,’” for every utterance, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘khattiyo brāhmaṇo’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

If a fully ordained monk, having heard from a fully ordained monk, conveys divisive speech to another fully ordained monk, saying, “So-and-so says of you, ‘He is a khattiya, a brāhmaṇa,’” for every utterance, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘avakaṇṇako javakaṇṇako dhaniṭṭhako saviṭṭhako kulavaḍḍhako’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

If a fully ordained monk, having heard from a fully ordained monk, conveys divisive speech to another fully ordained monk, saying, “So-and-so says of you, ‘His name is Avakaṇṇaka, Javakaṇṇaka, Dhaniṭṭhaka, Saviṭṭhaka, Kulavaḍḍhaka,’” for every utterance, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘buddharakkhito dhammarakkhito saṅgharakkhito’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

If a fully ordained monk, having heard from a fully ordained monk, conveys divisive speech to another fully ordained monk, saying, “So-and-so says of you, ‘His name is Buddharakkhita, Dhammarakkhita, Saṅgharakkhita,’” for every utterance, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘kosiyo bhāradvājo’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

If a fully ordained monk, having heard from a fully ordained monk, conveys divisive speech to another fully ordained monk, saying, “So-and-so says of you, ‘He is of the Kosiya clan, of the Bhāradvāja clan,’” for every utterance, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Upasampanno [T 2.0186][V 0.0022] upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘gotamo moggallāno kaccāno vāsiṭṭho’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

If a fully ordained monk, having heard from a fully ordained monk, conveys divisive speech to another fully ordained monk, saying, “So-and-so says of you, ‘He is of the Gotama clan, of the Moggallāna clan, of the Kaccāna clan, of the Vāsiṭṭha clan,’” for every utterance, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Upasampanno [M 0.0022] upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘koṭṭhako pupphachaḍḍako’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

If a fully ordained monk, having heard from a fully ordained monk, conveys divisive speech to another fully ordained monk, saying, “So-and-so says of you, ‘He is a granary-keeper, a flower-remover,’” for every utterance, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘kassako vāṇijo gorakkho’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says you are a farmer, a merchant, or a cowherd.' For every utterance, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘naḷakāro kumbhakāro pesakāro cammakāro nahāpito’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says you are a reed-worker, a potter, a weaver, a leather-worker, or a barber.' For every utterance, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘muddiko gaṇako lekhako’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says you are an accountant, a reckoner, or a scribe.' For every utterance, there is an offense of pācittiya.

40. Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘kuṭṭhiko gaṇḍiko kilāsiko sosiko apamāriko’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

40. A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says you are a leper, one with boils, one with skin disease, one with a wasting disease, or an epileptic.' For every utterance, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno [T 2.0187] upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘madhumehiko’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says you are a diabetic.' For every utterance, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘atidīgho atirasso atikaṇho accodāto’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says you are too tall, too short, too dark, or too fair.' For every utterance, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘nātidīgho [V 0.0023] nātirasso nātikaṇho nāccodāto’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says you are not too tall, not too short, not too dark, or not too fair.' For every utterance, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘rāgapariyuṭṭhito dosapariyuṭṭhito mohapariyuṭṭhito’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says you are overcome by lust, overcome by aversion, or overcome by delusion.' For every utterance, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno [M 0.0023] upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says you are without lust, without aversion, or without delusion.' For every utterance, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘pārājikaṃ ajjhāpanno, saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpanno, thullaccayaṃ ajjhāpanno, pācittiyaṃ ajjhāpanno[T 2.0188], pāṭidesanīyaṃ ajjhāpanno, dukkaṭaṃ ajjhāpanno, dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpanno’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says you have committed a pārājika offense, a saṅghādisesa offense, a thullaccaya offense, a pācittiya offense, a pāṭidesanīya offense, a dukkaṭa offense, or a dubbhāsita offense.' For every utterance, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘sotāpanno’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says you are a stream-enterer.' For every utterance, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘oṭṭho meṇḍo goṇo gadrabho tiracchānagato nerayiko, natthi tassa sugati, duggatiyeva tassa pāṭikaṅkhā’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says you are a camel, a ram, an ox, a donkey, an animal, a hell-being; for you there is no good destination, only a bad destination is to be expected.' For every utterance, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo taṃ ‘paṇḍito byatto medhāvī bahussuto dhammakathiko, natthi tassa duggati, sugati yeva tassa pāṭikaṅkhā’ti bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says you are wise, accomplished, intelligent, learned, a Dhamma-speaker; for you there is no bad destination, only a good destination is to be expected.' For every utterance, there is an offense of pācittiya.

41. Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo ‘santi idhekacce caṇḍālā venā nesādā rathakārā, pukkusā’ti bhaṇati, na so aññaṃ bhaṇati, taññeva bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya dukkaṭassa.

41. A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says, "There are here certain outcastes, bamboo-workers, hunters, leather-workers, and refuse-removers," and he is not speaking of anyone else; he is speaking only of you.' For every utterance, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Upasampanno [V 0.0024] upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo ‘santi idhekacce khattiyā brāhmaṇā’ti bhaṇati, na so aññaṃ bhaṇati, taññeva bhaṇatī’ti. Āpatti [T 2.0189] vācāya, vācāya dukkaṭassa…pe….

A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says, "There are here certain nobles and brahmins," and he is not speaking of anyone else; he is speaking only of you.' For every utterance, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo ‘santi idhekacce paṇḍitā byattā medhāvī bahussutā dhammakathikā, natthi tesaṃ duggati, sugati yeva tesaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā’ti bhaṇati, na [M 0.0024] so aññaṃ bhaṇati, taññeva bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya dukkaṭassa.

A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says, "There are here certain wise, accomplished, intelligent, learned, and Dhamma-speakers; for them there is no bad destination, only a good destination is to be expected," and he is not speaking of anyone else; he is speaking only of you.' For every utterance, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo ‘ye nūna caṇḍālā venā nesādā rathakārā pukkusā’ti bhaṇati, na so aññaṃ bhaṇati, taññeva bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya dukkaṭassa.

A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says, "They are surely outcastes, bamboo-workers, hunters, leather-workers, and refuse-removers," and he is not speaking of anyone else; he is speaking only of you.' For every utterance, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo ‘ye nūna paṇḍitā byattā medhāvī bahussutā dhammakathikā’ti bhaṇati, na so aññaṃ bhaṇati, taññeva bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya dukkaṭassa.

A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says, "They are surely wise, accomplished, intelligent, learned, and Dhamma-speakers," and he is not speaking of anyone else; he is speaking only of you.' For every utterance, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati – “itthannāmo ‘na mayaṃ caṇḍālā venā nesādā rathakārā pukkusā’ti bhaṇati, na so aññaṃ bhaṇati, taññeva bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya dukkaṭassa.

A fully ordained person, having heard the speech of a fully ordained person, conveys divisive speech to a fully ordained person, saying: 'So-and-so says, "We are not outcastes, bamboo-workers, hunters, leather-workers, or refuse-removers," and he is not speaking of anyone else; he is speaking only of you.' For every utterance, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati [T 2.0190] – “itthannāmo ‘na mayaṃ paṇḍitā byattā medhāvī bahussutā dhammakathikā, natthamhākaṃ duggati, sugati yeva amhākaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā’ti bhaṇati, na so aññaṃ [P 4.0014] bhaṇati, taññeva bhaṇatī”ti. Āpatti vācāya, vācāya dukkaṭassa.

A fully ordained one, having heard the speech of a fully ordained one, conveys slanderous speech to a fully ordained one, saying: 'So-and-so says, "We are not wise, not skilled, not intelligent, not learned, not Dhamma-speakers. For us there is no bad destination; only a good destination is to be expected by us." He does not speak of another; he speaks only of you.' For every utterance, an offense of wrong conduct is incurred.

42. Upasampanno upasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati; āpatti vācāya, vācāya pācittiyassa.

42. A fully ordained one, having heard the speech of a fully ordained one, conveys slanderous speech to a fully ordained one; for every utterance, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

Upasampanno [V 0.0025] upasampannassa sutvā anupasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

A fully ordained one, having heard the speech of a fully ordained one, conveys slanderous speech to one who is not fully ordained; an offense of wrong conduct is incurred.

Upasampanno anupasampannassa sutvā upasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

A fully ordained one, having heard the speech of one who is not fully ordained, conveys slanderous speech to a fully ordained one; an offense of wrong conduct is incurred.

Upasampanno anupasampannassa sutvā anupasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

A fully ordained one, having heard the speech of one who is not fully ordained, conveys slanderous speech to one who is not fully ordained; an offense of wrong conduct is incurred.

43. Anāpatti napiyakamyassa, nabhedādhippāyassa, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

43. There is no offense for one not intending to endear himself, for one not intending to cause division, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Pesuññasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The third training rule on slanderous speech is concluded.

4. Padasodhammasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Training Rule on Teaching the Dhamma Word by Word

44. Tena [T 2.0191][M 0.0025] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū upāsake padaso dhammaṃ vācenti. Upāsakā bhikkhūsu agāravā appatissā asabhāgavuttikā viharanti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū upāsake padaso dhammaṃ vācessanti! Upāsakā bhikkhūsu agāravā appatissā asabhāgavuttikā viharantī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū chabbaggiye bhikkhū anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, upāsake padaso dhammaṃ vācetha; upāsakā bhikkhūsu agāravā appatissā asabhāgavuttikā viharantī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, upāsake padaso dhammaṃ vācessatha! Upāsakā bhikkhūsu agāravā appatissā asabhāgavuttikā viharanti! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya pasannānaṃ vā bhiyyobhāvāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

44. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus were teaching the Dhamma to lay followers word by word. The lay followers became disrespectful, irreverent, and their conduct was unsuitable towards the bhikkhus. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes... criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: 'How is it that the group-of-six bhikkhus are teaching the Dhamma to lay followers word by word? The lay followers have become disrespectful, irreverent, and their conduct is unsuitable towards the bhikkhus!' Then those bhikkhus, having rebuked the group-of-six bhikkhus in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One... 'Is it true, Bhikkhus, that you teach the Dhamma to lay followers word by word, and that the lay followers have become disrespectful, irreverent, and their conduct is unsuitable towards the bhikkhus?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... 'How is it, foolish men, that you teach the Dhamma to lay followers word by word? The lay followers have become disrespectful, irreverent, and their conduct is unsuitable towards the bhikkhus! This, foolish men, is not for the confidence of the faithless, nor for the increase of the faithful...' And so, Bhikkhus, this training rule should be set forth in this way:

45. “Yo pana bhikkhu anupasampannaṃ padaso dhammaṃ vāceyya pācittiya”nti.

45. “Whatever bhikkhu should teach one who is not fully ordained the Dhamma word by word, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

46. Yo [V 0.0026] panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

46. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind... ‘Bhikkhu’ means: ...in this context, this is the bhikkhu who is intended.

Anupasampanno nāma bhikkhuñca bhikkhuniñca ṭhapetvā avaseso anupasampanno nāma.

‘One who is not fully ordained’ means: setting aside a bhikkhu and a bhikkhunī, the remainder is called ‘one who is not fully ordained’.

Padaso [T 2.0192] nāma padaṃ, [P 4.0015] anupadaṃ, anvakkharaṃ, anubyañjanaṃ.

‘Word by word’ means: by phrase, by subsequent phrase, by letter, by syllable.

Padaṃ nāma ekato paṭṭhapetvā ekato osāpenti. Anupadaṃ nāma pāṭekkaṃ paṭṭhapetvā ekato osāpenti. Anvakkharaṃ nāma “rūpaṃ anicca”nti vuccamāno, “ru”nti opāteti. Anubyañjanaṃ nāma “rūpaṃ anicca”nti vuccamāno, “vedanā aniccā”ti saddaṃ nicchāreti.

‘By phrase’ means: having started together, they finish together. ‘By subsequent phrase’ means: having started separately, they finish together. ‘By letter’ means: when ‘rūpaṃ aniccaṃ’ (form is impermanent) is being said, one prompts with ‘ru’. ‘By syllable’ means: when ‘rūpaṃ aniccaṃ’ is being said, one utters the sound ‘vedanā aniccā’ (feeling is impermanent).

Yañca [M 0.0026] padaṃ, yañca anupadaṃ, yañca anvakkharaṃ, yañca anubyañjanaṃ – sabbametaṃ padaso padaso dhammo (itipi) nāma.

Whatever is by phrase, and whatever is by subsequent phrase, and whatever is by letter, and whatever is by syllable—all this is called ‘word by word’.

Dhammo nāma buddhabhāsito, sāvakabhāsito, isibhāsito, devatābhāsito, atthūpasañhito, dhammūpasañhito.

‘Dhamma’ means: what is spoken by the Buddha, spoken by a disciple, spoken by a sage, spoken by a deity, connected with the meaning (commentary), or connected with the text (Pāli).

Vāceyyāti padena vāceti, pade pade āpatti pācittiyassa. Akkharāya vāceti, akkharakkharāya āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should teach’ means: if one teaches by the phrase, for every phrase an offense of pācittiya is incurred. If one teaches by the letter, for every letter an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

47. Anupasampanne anupasampannasaññī padaso dhammaṃ vāceti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anupasampanne vematiko padaso dhammaṃ vāceti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anupasampanne upasampannasaññī padaso dhammaṃ vāceti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

47. If one teaches the Dhamma word by word to one who is not fully ordained while perceiving them as not fully ordained, an offense of pācittiya is incurred. If one teaches the Dhamma word by word to one who is not fully ordained while being in doubt, an offense of pācittiya is incurred. If one teaches the Dhamma word by word to one who is not fully ordained while perceiving them as fully ordained, an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

Upasampanne anupasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Upasampanne vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Upasampanne upasampannasaññī, anāpatti.

In the case of one who is fully ordained, if one teaches while perceiving them as not fully ordained, an offense of wrong conduct is incurred. In the case of one who is fully ordained, if one teaches while being in doubt, an offense of wrong conduct is incurred. In the case of one who is fully ordained, if one teaches while perceiving them as fully ordained, there is no offense.

48. Anāpatti ekato uddisāpento, ekato sajjhāyaṃ karonto[T 2.0193], yebhuyyena paguṇaṃ ganthaṃ bhaṇantaṃ opāteti, osārentaṃ opāteti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

48. There is no offense when causing them to learn together, when making a communal recitation together, when one prompts someone reciting a text that is mostly fluent, when one prompts someone who is finishing, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Padasodhammasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.

The fourth training rule, on teaching the Dhamma word by word, is concluded.

5. Sahaseyyasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Training Rule on Sleeping Together

49. Tena [T 2.0194][V 0.0027] samayena buddho bhagavā āḷaviyaṃ viharati aggāḷave cetiye. Tena kho pana samayena upāsakā ārāmaṃ āgacchanti dhammassavanāya. Dhamme bhāsite therā bhikkhū yathāvihāraṃ gacchanti. Navakā bhikkhū tattheva upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ upāsakehi saddhiṃ muṭṭhassatī, asampajānā, naggā, vikūjamānā, kākacchamānā seyyaṃ kappenti. Upāsakā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhadantā muṭṭhassatī asampajānā naggā vikūjamānā kākacchamānā seyyaṃ kappessantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ upāsakānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti [P 4.0016] vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhū anupasampannena [M 0.0027] sahaseyyaṃ kappessantī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū te navake bhikkhū anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhū anupasampannena sahaseyyaṃ kappentī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā anupasampannena sahaseyyaṃ kappessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

49. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Āḷavī at the Aggāḷava shrine. Now at that time, lay followers would come to the monastery to listen to the Dhamma. When the Dhamma had been spoken, the elder bhikkhus would go to their respective dwellings. The junior bhikkhus, however, right there in the assembly hall, together with the lay followers, with lapsed mindfulness, without clear comprehension, naked, groaning, and snoring loudly, lay down to sleep. The lay followers complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: ‘How indeed can the venerable sirs, with lapsed mindfulness, without clear comprehension, naked, groaning, and snoring loudly, lay down to sleep?’ The bhikkhus heard those lay followers complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhus who were of few wants… they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: ‘How indeed can bhikkhus arrange to sleep together with one who is not fully ordained?’ Then those bhikkhus, having rebuked those junior bhikkhus in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One… ‘Is it true, bhikkhus, that bhikkhus arrange to sleep together with one who is not fully ordained?’ ‘It is true, Blessed One.’ The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… ‘How indeed, bhikkhus, can those worthless men arrange to sleep together with one who is not fully ordained? This, bhikkhus, is not for the inspiring of faith in the uninspired… And so, bhikkhus, you should set forth this training rule in this way:

“Yo pana bhikkhu anupasampannena sahaseyyaṃ kappeyya pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever bhikkhu should sleep together with one who is not fully ordained, it is an offense of expiation.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

Thus this training rule was laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

50. Atha [T 2.0195] kho bhagavā āḷaviyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena kosambī tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena kosambī tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā kosambiyaṃ viharati badarikārāme. Bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ rāhulaṃ etadavocuṃ – “bhagavatā, āvuso rāhula, sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ – ‘na anupasampannena sahaseyyā kappetabbā’ti. Seyyaṃ, āvuso rāhula, jānāhī”ti. Atha kho āyasmā rāhulo seyyaṃ alabhamāno vaccakuṭiyā seyyaṃ kappesi. Atha kho bhagavā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya yena vaccakuṭi tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ukkāsi. Āyasmāpi rāhulo ukkāsi. “Ko etthā”ti? “Ahaṃ, bhagavā, rāhulo”ti. “Kissa tvaṃ, rāhula, idha nisinnosī”ti? Atha kho āyasmā rāhulo bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ [V 0.0028] kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, anupasampannena dirattatirattaṃ sahaseyyaṃ kappetuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

50. Then the Blessed One, having dwelt in Āḷavī for as long as he wished, set out on a journey towards Kosambī. Wandering on tour by stages, he in due course arrived at Kosambī. There, the Blessed One dwelt in Kosambī at the Badarikā monastery. The bhikkhus said this to the venerable Rāhula: ‘Friend Rāhula, a training rule has been laid down by the Blessed One: “One should not sleep together with one who is not fully ordained.” Friend Rāhula, find a sleeping place.’ Then the venerable Rāhula, not finding a sleeping place, lay down to sleep in the privy. Then the Blessed One, having risen towards dawn, approached the privy; having approached, he cleared his throat. The venerable Rāhula also cleared his throat. ‘Who is there?’ ‘I am Rāhula, Blessed One.’ ‘Rāhula, why are you sitting here?’ Then the venerable Rāhula reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus: ‘I allow, bhikkhus, to sleep together with one who is not fully ordained for two or three nights. And so, bhikkhus, you should set forth this training rule in this way:

51. “Yo pana bhikkhu anupasampannena uttaridirattatirattaṃ sahaseyyaṃ kappeyya, pācittiya”nti.

51. “Whatever bhikkhu should sleep together with one who is not fully ordained for more than two or three nights, it is an offense of expiation.”

52. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

52. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever, of whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhu’ means… in this context, this is the bhikkhu who is intended.

Anupasampanno nāma bhikkhuṃ ṭhapetvā avaseso anupasampanno nāma.

‘One not fully ordained’ means: setting aside a bhikkhu, the remainder is called ‘one not fully ordained’.

Uttaridirattatirattanti [T 2.0196][M 0.0028] atirekadirattatirattaṃ.

‘For more than two or three nights’ means exceeding two or three nights.

Sahāti [P 4.0017] ekato.

‘Together’ means in one place.

Seyyā nāma sabbacchannā, sabbaparicchannā, yebhuyyenacchannā, yebhuyyena paricchannā.

A lodging means that which is completely roofed, completely enclosed, mostly roofed, or mostly enclosed.

Seyyaṃ kappeyyāti catutthe divase atthaṅgate sūriye, anupasampanne nipanne, bhikkhu nipajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Bhikkhu nipanne, anupasampanno nipajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ubho vā nipajjanti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Uṭṭhahitvā punappunaṃ nipajjanti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should sleep’ means: on the fourth day, after the sun has set, if, when one who is not fully ordained is lying down, the bhikkhu lies down, there is an offense of expiation. If, when a bhikkhu is lying down, one who is not fully ordained lies down, there is an offense of expiation. Or if both lie down, there is an offense of expiation. If, having gotten up, they lie down again and again, there is an offense of expiation.

53. Anupasampanne anupasampannasaññī uttaridirattatirattaṃ sahaseyyaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anupasampanne vematiko uttaridirattatirattaṃ sahaseyyaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anupasampanne upasampannasaññī uttaridirattatirattaṃ sahaseyyaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

53. If he sleeps together with one who is not fully ordained for more than two or three nights, perceiving them as not fully ordained, there is an offense of expiation. If he sleeps together with one who is not fully ordained for more than two or three nights, being in doubt, there is an offense of expiation. If he sleeps together with one who is not fully ordained for more than two or three nights, perceiving them as fully ordained, there is an offense of expiation.

Upaḍḍhacchanne upaḍḍhaparicchanne, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Upasampanne anupasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Upasampanne vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Upasampanne upasampannasaññī, anāpatti.

In a place that is half-roofed and half-enclosed, there is an offense of wrong conduct. If he sleeps with one who is fully ordained, perceiving them as not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong conduct. If he sleeps with one who is fully ordained, being in doubt, there is an offense of wrong conduct. If he sleeps with one who is fully ordained, perceiving them as fully ordained, there is no offense.

54. Anāpatti [V 0.0029] dvetisso rattiyo vasati, ūnakadvetisso rattiyo vasati, dve rattiyo vasitvā tatiyāya rattiyā purāruṇā nikkhamitvā puna vasati, sabbacchanne, sabbaaparicchanne, sabbaparicchanne sabbaacchanne vasati, sabbaacchanne sabbaaparicchanne, (sī.), yebhuyyena acchanne, yebhuyyena aparicchanne, anupasampanne nipanne bhikkhu nisīdati, bhikkhu nipanne anupasampanno [T 2.0197] nisīdati, ubho vā nisīdanti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

54. There is no offense: if one stays for two or three nights; if one stays for less than two or three nights; if, having stayed for two nights, one leaves before dawn on the third night and then stays again; in a place that is completely roofed but completely unenclosed; in a place that is completely enclosed but completely unroofed; in a place that is mostly unroofed or mostly unenclosed; if, when one who is not fully ordained is lying down, a bhikkhu sits; if, when a bhikkhu is lying down, one who is not fully ordained sits; if both are sitting; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Sahaseyyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The fifth training rule on sleeping together is finished.

6. Dutiyasahaseyyasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Second Training Rule on Sleeping Together

55. Tena [T 2.0198] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā anuruddho kosalesu [M 0.0029] janapade ettha ambaṭṭhasuttādiṭīkā oloketabbā sāvatthiṃ gacchanto sāyaṃ aññataraṃ gāmaṃ upagacchi. Tena kho pana samayena tasmiṃ gāme aññatarissā itthiyā āvasathāgāraṃ paññattaṃ hoti. Atha kho āyasmā anuruddho yena sā itthī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ itthiṃ etadavoca – “sace te, bhagini, agaru, vaseyyāma ekarattaṃ āvasathāgāre”ti. “Vaseyyātha, bhante”ti. Aññepi addhikā yena sā itthī tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ itthiṃ etadavocuṃ – “sace te, ayye, agaru vaseyyāma ekarattaṃ āvasathāgāre”ti[P 4.0018]. “Eso kho ayyo samaṇo paṭhamaṃ upagato; sace so anujānāti, vaseyyāthā”ti. Atha kho te addhikā yenāyasmā anuruddho tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavocuṃ – “sace te, bhante, agaru, vaseyyāma ekarattaṃ āvasathāgāre”ti. “Vaseyyātha, āvuso”ti. Atha kho sā itthī āyasmante anuruddhe saha dassanena paṭibaddhacittā ahosi. Atha kho sā itthī yenāyasmā anuruddho tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavoca – “ayyo, bhante, imehi manussehi ākiṇṇo na phāsu viharissati. Sādhāhaṃ, bhante, ayyassa [T 2.0199] mañcakaṃ abbhantaraṃ paññapeyya”nti. Adhivāsesi kho āyasmā anuruddho tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho sā itthī āyasmato anuruddhassa mañcakaṃ abbhantaraṃ paññapetvā alaṅkatappaṭiyattā gandhagandhinī yenāyasmā anuruddho tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavoca – “ayyo, bhante, abhirūpo dassanīyo pāsādiko, ahaṃ camhi abhirūpā dassanīyā pāsādikā. Sādhāhaṃ, bhante, ayyassa pajāpati bhaveyya”nti. Evaṃ vutte āyasmā anuruddho tuṇhī ahosi. Dutiyampi kho…pe… tatiyampi kho sā itthī āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavoca – “ayyo, bhante, abhirūpo [V 0.0030] dassanīyo pāsādiko, ahañcamhi abhirūpā dassanīyā pāsādikā. Sādhu, bhante, ayyo mañceva paṭicchatu sampaṭicchatu (syā.) sabbañca sāpateyya”nti. Tatiyampi kho āyasmā anuruddho tuṇhī ahosi. Atha kho sā itthī sāṭakaṃ nikkhipitvā āyasmato anuruddhassa purato caṅkamatipi tiṭṭhatipi nisīdatipi seyyampi kappeti. Atha kho āyasmā anuruddho indriyāni okkhipitvā taṃ itthiṃ neva olokesi napi ālapi. Atha kho [M 0.0030] sā itthī – “acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho! Bahū me manussā satenapi sahassenapi pahiṇanti. Ayaṃ pana samaṇo – mayā sāmaṃ yāciyamāno – na icchati mañceva paṭicchituṃ sabbañca sāpateyya”nti sāṭakaṃ nivāsetvā āyasmato anuruddhassa pādesu sirasā [T 2.0200] nipatitvā āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavoca – “accayo maṃ, bhante, accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ yāhaṃ evamakāsiṃ. Tassā me, bhante, ayyo accayaṃ accayato paṭiggaṇhātu āyatiṃ saṃvarāyā”ti. “Taggha tvaṃ, bhagini, accayo accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ yā tvaṃ evamakāsi. Yato ca kho tvaṃ, bhagini, accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ [P 4.0019] paṭikarosi, taṃ te mayaṃ paṭiggaṇhāma. Vuddhi hesā, bhagini, ariyassa vinaye yo accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikaroti āyatiñca saṃvaraṃ āpajjatī”ti.

55. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the Venerable Anuruddha, while traveling in the Kosalan country on his way to Sāvatthī, approached a certain village in the evening. And at that time, in that village, a lodging-house had been prepared by a certain woman. Then the Venerable Anuruddha approached that woman; having approached, he said this to that woman: “Sister, if it is not a burden to you, may we stay one night in the lodging-house?” “You may stay, venerable sir.” Other travelers also approached that woman; having approached, they said this to that woman: “Madam, if it is not a burden to you, may we stay one night in the lodging-house?” “This venerable ascetic arrived first; if he consents, you may stay.” Then those travelers approached the Venerable Anuruddha; having approached, they said this to the Venerable Anuruddha: “Venerable sir, if it is not a burden to you, may we stay one night in the lodging-house?” “You may stay, friends.” Then that woman, upon seeing the Venerable Anuruddha, became infatuated with him. Then that woman approached the Venerable Anuruddha; having approached, she said this to the Venerable Anuruddha: “Venerable sir, the venerable one will not dwell comfortably, being crowded by these people. I beg you, venerable sir, let me prepare a couch for the venerable one inside.” The Venerable Anuruddha consented through silence. Then that woman, having prepared a couch for the Venerable Anuruddha inside, adorned and perfumed herself, and approached the Venerable Anuruddha; having approached, she said this to the Venerable Anuruddha: “Venerable sir, the venerable one is handsome, good-looking, and pleasing, and I too am handsome, good-looking, and pleasing. I beg you, venerable sir, let me be the venerable one’s wife.” When this was said, the Venerable Anuruddha remained silent. For a second time… for a third time, that woman said this to the Venerable Anuruddha: “Venerable sir, the venerable one is handsome, good-looking, and pleasing, and I too am handsome, good-looking, and pleasing. I beg you, venerable sir, may the venerable one accept me and all my property.” For a third time, the Venerable Anuruddha remained silent. Then that woman, having removed her lower garment, walked, stood, sat, and lay down in front of the Venerable Anuruddha. Then the Venerable Anuruddha, having cast down his senses, neither looked at that woman nor spoke to her. Then that woman thought: “Oh, how wonderful! Oh, how marvelous! Many men send for me with a hundred or a thousand. But this ascetic, though I myself entreat him to accept me and all my property, does not wish it.” Having put on her lower garment and bowed with her head at the feet of the Venerable Anuruddha, she said this to the Venerable Anuruddha: “Venerable sir, a transgression has overcome me, according to my foolishness, my delusion, my unskillfulness, in that I acted in such a way. May the venerable one accept my transgression as a transgression, for the sake of future restraint.” “Indeed, sister, a transgression has overcome you, according to your foolishness, your delusion, your unskillfulness, in that you acted in such a way. And because you, sister, having seen the transgression as a transgression, make amends according to the Dhamma, we accept it from you. For this is growth in the discipline of the Noble One, sister: that one who, having seen a transgression as a transgression, makes amends according to the Dhamma and undertakes restraint in the future.”

Atha kho sā itthī tassā rattiyā accayena āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā, āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho taṃ itthiṃ āyasmā anuruddho dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho sā itthī – āyasmatā anuruddhena dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā – āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante! Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – cakkhumanto rūpāni [T 2.0201] dakkhantīti, evamevaṃ ayyena anuruddhena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, taṃ bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsikaṃ maṃ ayyo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

Then that woman, after that night had passed, having satisfied and gratified the Venerable Anuruddha with her own hands with excellent hard and soft food, paid homage to the Venerable Anuruddha, who had finished his meal and removed his hand from the bowl, and sat down to one side. To that woman seated to one side, the Venerable Anuruddha instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened her with a talk on the Dhamma. Then that woman—having been instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened by the Venerable Anuruddha with a talk on the Dhamma—said this to the Venerable Anuruddha: “Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! Just as, venerable sir, one might set upright what was overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or point out the way to one who was lost, or hold an oil lamp in the darkness, thinking, ‘Those with eyes will see forms,’ in just the same way, the Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by the Venerable Anuruddha. I, venerable sir, go for refuge to that Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Sangha of bhikkhus. May the venerable one remember me as a lay female follower who has gone for refuge from this day forth for as long as life lasts.”

Atha kho āyasmā anuruddho sāvatthiyaṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā anuruddho mātugāmena sahaseyyaṃ kappessatī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, anuruddha, mātugāmena [V 0.0031] sahaseyyaṃ kappesī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti[M 0.0031]. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, anuruddha, mātugāmena sahaseyyaṃ kappessasi! Netaṃ, anuruddha, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

Then the Venerable Anuruddha, having gone to Sāvatthī, informed the monks of this matter. Those monks who were of few desires... criticized, scorned, and disparaged him, saying: “How indeed could the Venerable Anuruddha arrange to lie down together in the same lodging with a woman?” Then those monks, having criticized the Venerable Anuruddha in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One... “Is it true, reportedly, Anuruddha, that you arranged to lie down together in the same lodging with a woman?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him... “How indeed, Anuruddha, could you arrange to lie down together in the same lodging with a woman? This, Anuruddha, is not for the confidence of the unconfident... And so, monks, you should set forth this training rule in this way:

56. “Yo pana bhikkhu mātugāmena sahaseyyaṃ kappeyya pācittiya”nti.

56. “Whatever monk should arrange to lie down together in the same lodging with a woman, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

57. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

57. Whatever: means whatever kind... Monk: ... in this context, this is the monk who is intended.

Mātugāmo nāma manussitthī, na yakkhī yakkhinī (ka.), na petī, na tiracchānagatā; antamaso tadahujātāpi dārikā, pageva mahattarī.

A woman means a human female, not a female yakkha, not a female peta, not a female animal—even a girl born on that very day, how much more so an older one.

Sahāti ekato.

Together: means in one place.

Seyyā nāma sabbacchannā, sabbaparicchannā, yebhuyyenacchannā, yebhuyyena paricchannā.

A lodging is one that is completely roofed, completely enclosed; or mostly roofed, mostly enclosed.

Seyyaṃ [P 4.0020] kappeyyāti atthaṅgate sūriye, mātugāme nipanne bhikkhu nipajjati, āpatti [T 2.0202] pācittiyassa. Bhikkhu nipanne mātugāmo nipajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ubho vā nipajjanti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Uṭṭhahitvā punappunaṃ nipajjanti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

“Should one arrange to lie down together” means: after the sun has set, if a woman is lying down and a monk lies down, it is an offense of pācittiya. If a monk is lying down and a woman lies down, it is an offense of pācittiya. Or if both lie down, it is an offense of pācittiya. If, having gotten up, they lie down repeatedly, it is an offense of pācittiya.

58. Mātugāme mātugāmasaññī sahaseyyaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Mātugāme vematiko sahaseyyaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Mātugāme amātugāmasaññī sahaseyyaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

58. If, with a woman, one perceives her as a woman and arranges to lie down together, it is an offense of pācittiya. If, with a woman, one is doubtful and arranges to lie down together, it is an offense of pācittiya. If, with a woman, one perceives her as not a woman and arranges to lie down together, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Upaḍḍhacchanne upaḍḍhaparicchanne, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yakkhiyā vā petiyā vā paṇḍakena vā tiracchānagatitthiyā vā sahaseyyaṃ kappeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Amātugāme mātugāmasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Amātugāme vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Amātugāme amātugāmasaññī, anāpatti.

If one arranges to lie down together in a place that is half-roofed and half-enclosed, it is an offense of wrong-doing. If one arranges to lie down together with a female yakkha, a female peta, a eunuch, or a female animal, it is an offense of wrong-doing. With a non-woman, if one perceives her as a woman, it is an offense of wrong-doing. With a non-woman, if one is doubtful, it is an offense of wrong-doing. With a non-woman, if one perceives her as a non-woman, there is no offense.

59. Anāpatti [V 0.0032] sabbacchanne sabbaaparicchanne, sabbaparicchanne sabbaacchanne anāpatti sabbaacchanne sabbaaparicchanne, (sī.), yebhuyyena acchanne, yebhuyyena aparicchanne, mātugāme nipanne bhikkhu nisīdati[M 0.0032], bhikkhu nipanne mātugāmo nisīdati, ubho vā nisīdanti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

59. There is no offense if the place is completely roofed but completely unenclosed; completely enclosed but completely unroofed; mostly unroofed and mostly unenclosed; if a woman is lying down and a monk is sitting; if a monk is lying down and a woman is sitting; or if both are sitting; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Dutiyasahaseyyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The sixth, the Second Training Rule on Lying Down Together, is finished.

7. Dhammadesanāsikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Training Rule on Teaching the Dhamma

60. Tena [T 2.0203] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā udāyī sāvatthiyaṃ kulūpako hoti, bahukāni kulāni upasaṅkamati. Atha kho āyasmā udāyī pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena aññataraṃ kulaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Tena kho pana samayena gharaṇī nivesanadvāre nisinnā hoti, gharasuṇhā āvasathadvāre nisinnā hoti. Atha kho āyasmā udāyī yena gharaṇī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā gharaṇiyā upakaṇṇake dhammaṃ desesi. Atha kho gharasuṇhāya etadahosi – “ki nu kho so samaṇo sassuyā jāro udāhu obhāsatī”ti?

60. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the Venerable Udāyī was a frequenter of families in Sāvatthī; he approached many families. Then the Venerable Udāyī, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, approached a certain family. At that time, the householder's wife was sitting at the entrance to the residence, and the daughter-in-law was sitting at the entrance to the inner room. Then the Venerable Udāyī approached the householder's wife; having approached, he taught the Dhamma near her ear. Then this thought occurred to the daughter-in-law: 'Is that ascetic my mother-in-law’s secret lover, or is he perhaps jesting with her?'

Atha kho āyasmā udāyī gharaṇiyā upakaṇṇake dhammaṃ desetvā yena gharasuṇhā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā gharasuṇhāya upakaṇṇake dhammaṃ desesi. Atha kho gharaṇiyā etadahosi – “kiṃ nu kho so samaṇo gharasuṇhāya jāro udāhu obhāsatī”ti[P 4.0021]? Atha kho āyasmā udāyī gharasuṇhāya upakaṇṇake dhammaṃ desetvā pakkāmi. Atha kho gharaṇī gharasuṇhaṃ etadavoca – “he je, kiṃ te eso samaṇo avocā”ti? “Dhammaṃ me, ayye, desesi”. “Ayyāya pana kiṃ avocā”ti? “Mayhampi dhammaṃ desesī”ti. Tā [T 2.0204] ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyo udāyī mātugāmassa upakaṇṇake dhammaṃ desessati! Nanu nāma vissaṭṭhena vivaṭena dhammo desetabbo”ti?

Then the Venerable Udāyī, having taught the Dhamma near the ear of the householder's wife, approached the daughter-in-law; having approached, he taught the Dhamma near the daughter-in-law's ear. Then this thought occurred to the householder's wife: 'Is that ascetic the daughter-in-law’s secret lover, or is he perhaps jesting with her?' Then the Venerable Udāyī, having taught the Dhamma near the daughter-in-law's ear, departed. Then the householder's wife said this to the daughter-in-law: 'Hey you, what did that ascetic say to you?' 'Lady, he taught me the Dhamma.' 'But what did he say to you, lady?' 'He taught me the Dhamma also.' They complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: 'How indeed could the Venerable Udāyī teach the Dhamma near a woman’s ear! Should not the Dhamma be taught clearly and openly?'

Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tāsaṃ itthīnaṃ ujjhāyantīnaṃ khiyyantīnaṃ vipācentīnaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā udāyī mātugāmassa dhammaṃ desessatī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū [M 0.0033] āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, udāyi, mātugāmassa dhammaṃ desesī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi [V 0.0033] nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, mātugāmassa dhammaṃ desessasi. Netaṃ moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

The monks heard those women complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those monks who were of few desires... complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: 'How indeed could the Venerable Udāyī teach the Dhamma to a woman!' Then those monks, having rebuked the Venerable Udāyī in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One... 'Is it true, reportedly, Udāyī, that you teach the Dhamma to a woman?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him... 'How indeed, O foolish man, could you teach the Dhamma to a woman? This, foolish man, is not for the confidence of the unconfident... And so, monks, you should set forth this training rule in this way:

“Yo pana bhikkhu mātugāmassa dhammaṃ deseyya pācittiya”nti.

“Should any monk teach the Dhamma to a woman, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

In this way, this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.

61. Tena kho pana samayena upāsikā bhikkhū passitvā etadavocuṃ – “iṅghāyyā dhammaṃ desethā”ti. “Na, bhaginī, kappati mātugāmassa dhammaṃ desetu”nti. “Iṅghāyyā chappañcavācāhi dhammaṃ desetha, sakkā ettakenapi dhammo aññātu”nti. “Na, bhaginī, kappati mātugāmassa dhammaṃ desetu”nti. Kukkuccāyantā na desesuṃ. Upāsikā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā amhehi yāciyamānā dhammaṃ na desessantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tāsaṃ upāsikānaṃ [T 2.0205] ujjhāyantīnaṃ khiyyantīnaṃ vipācentīnaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mātugāmassa chappañcavācāhi dhammaṃ desetuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

61. Now at that time, female lay disciples, upon seeing the monks, said this: 'We ask you, venerable sirs, please teach the Dhamma.' 'Sisters, it is not allowable to teach the Dhamma to a woman.' 'We ask you, venerable sirs, please teach the Dhamma with five or six words; it is possible to know the Dhamma even with just that much.' 'Sisters, it is not allowable to teach the Dhamma to a woman.' Being scrupulous, they did not teach. The female lay disciples complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: 'How is it that the venerable ones, though requested by us, will not teach the Dhamma?' The monks heard those female lay disciples complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this context, having given a discourse on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: 'I allow, monks, that the Dhamma be taught to a woman with five or six words. And so, monks, you should recite this training rule in this way:

“Yo pana bhikkhū mātugāmassa uttarichappañcavācāhi dhammaṃ deseyya, pācittiya”nti.

Should any monk teach the Dhamma to a woman with more than five or six words, it is an offense of expiation.

Evañcidaṃ [P 4.0022] bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

In this way, this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.

62. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū – “bhagavatā anuññātaṃ mātugāmassa chappañcavācāhi dhammaṃ desetu”nti te aviññuṃ purisaviggahaṃ upanisīdāpetvā mātugāmassa uttarichappañcavācāhi dhammaṃ desenti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū aviññuṃ purisaviggahaṃ upanisīdāpetvā mātugāmassa uttarichappañcavācāhi dhammaṃ desessantī”ti!

62. Now at that time, the monks of the group of six, thinking, 'It has been allowed by the Blessed One to teach the Dhamma to a woman with five or six words,' had an unintelligent man sit nearby and taught the Dhamma to a woman with more than five or six words. Those monks who were of few wishes... complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: 'How indeed could the monks of the group of six, having had an unintelligent man sit nearby, teach the Dhamma to a woman with more than five or six words!'

Atha [M 0.0034] kho te bhikkhū chabbaggiye bhikkhū anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, aviññuṃ purisaviggahaṃ upanisīdāpetvā mātugāmassa uttarichappañcavācāhi dhammaṃ desethā”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi [V 0.0034] buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, aviññuṃ purisaviggahaṃ upanisīdāpetvā mātugāmassa uttarichappañcavācāhi dhammaṃ desessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha [T 2.0206] –

Then those monks, having rebuked the monks of the group of six in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One... 'Is it true, monks, as is said, that you, having had an unintelligent man sit nearby, teach the Dhamma to a woman with more than five or six words?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... 'How indeed, O foolish men, could you, having had an unintelligent man sit nearby, teach the Dhamma to a woman with more than five or six words? This, foolish men, is not for inspiring faith in the faithless... And so, monks, you should recite this training rule in this way:

63. “Yo pana bhikkhu mātugāmassa uttarichappañcavācāhi dhammaṃ deseyya, aññatra viññunā purisaviggahena, pācittiya”nti.

63. Should any monk teach the Dhamma to a woman with more than five or six words, except in the presence of an intelligent man, it is an offense of expiation.

64. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

64. ‘Should any’ refers to whoever, of whatever kind... and so on. ‘Monk’ refers to... and so on... the monk who is meant in this context.

Mātugāmo nāma manussitthī; na yakkhī na petī na tiracchānagatā; viññū, paṭibalā subhāsitadubbhāsitaṃ duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ ājānituṃ.

A woman means a human female; not a female yakkha, not a female peta, not a female animal; one who is intelligent and capable of understanding what is well-spoken and ill-spoken, what is coarse and not coarse.

Uttarichappañcavācāhīti atirekachappañcavācāhi.

'With more than five or six words' means with words exceeding five or six.

Dhammo nāma buddhabhāsito, sāvakabhāsito, isibhāsito, devatābhāsito, atthūpasañhito, dhammūpasañhito.

Dhamma means that which is spoken by the Buddha, spoken by a disciple, spoken by a sage, spoken by a deity, connected with the meaning, or connected with the text.

Deseyyāti padena deseti, pade pade āpatti pācittiyassa. Akkharāya deseti, akkharakkharāya āpatti pācittiyassa.

If one teaches by the word, for every word there is an offense of expiation. If one teaches by the syllable, for every syllable there is an offense of expiation.

Aññatra viññunā purisaviggahenāti ṭhapetvā viññuṃ purisaviggahaṃ. Viññū nāma purisaviggaho, paṭibalo hoti subhāsitadubbhāsitaṃ duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ ājānituṃ.

'Except for an intelligent man' means excluding an intelligent man. An intelligent man is one who is capable of understanding what is well-spoken and ill-spoken, and what is coarse and not coarse.

65. Mātugāme mātugāmasaññī uttarichappañcavācāhi dhammaṃ deseti, aññatra viññunā purisaviggahena, āpatti pācittiyassa. Mātugāme vematiko uttarichappañcavācāhi dhammaṃ deseti, aññatra viññunā purisaviggahena, āpatti pācittiyassa. Mātugāme amātugāmasaññī uttarichappañcavācāhi dhammaṃ deseti, aññatra viññunā purisaviggahena, āpatti pācittiyassa.

65. If, in the case of a woman, perceiving her as a woman, one teaches the Dhamma with more than five or six words—except in the presence of an intelligent man—there is an offense of expiation. If, in the case of a woman, one is in doubt, and teaches the Dhamma with more than five or six words—except in the presence of an intelligent man—there is an offense of expiation. If, in the case of a woman, perceiving her as not a woman, one teaches the Dhamma with more than five or six words—except in the presence of an intelligent man—there is an offense of expiation.

Yakkhiyā [M 0.0035][V 0.0035] vā petiyā vā paṇḍakassa vā [P 4.0023] tiracchānagatamanussaviggahitthiyā vā uttarichappañcavācāhi [T 2.0207] dhammaṃ deseti, aññatra viññunā purisaviggahena, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Amātugāme mātugāmasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Amātugāme vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Amātugāme amātugāmasaññī, anāpatti.

If one teaches the Dhamma with more than five or six words to a female yakkha, or a female peta, or a paṇḍaka, or a female animal in human form—except in the presence of an intelligent man—there is an offense of wrongdoing. In the case of a non-woman, if one perceives her as a woman, there is an offense of wrongdoing. In the case of a non-woman, if one is in doubt, there is an offense of wrongdoing. In the case of a non-woman, if one perceives her as a non-woman, there is no offense.

66. Anāpatti viññunā purisaviggahena, chappañcavācāhi dhammaṃ deseti, ūnakachappañcavācāhi dhammaṃ deseti, uṭṭhahitvā puna nisīditvā deseti, mātugāmo uṭṭhahitvā puna nisīdati tasmiṃ deseti, aññassa mātugāmassa deseti, pañhaṃ pucchati, pañhaṃ puṭṭho katheti, aññassatthāya bhaṇantaṃ mātugāmo suṇāti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

66. There is no offense: if an intelligent man is present; if one teaches the Dhamma with five or six words; if one teaches the Dhamma with fewer than five or six words; if one stands up, sits down again, and then teaches; if the woman stands up and sits down again, and one teaches her; if one teaches another woman; if one asks a question; if, having been asked a question, one answers; if a woman listens while one is speaking for the benefit of another; for one who is insane; for the first-doer.

Dhammadesanāsikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.

The seventh training rule on teaching the Dhamma is finished.

8. Bhūtārocanasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Training Rule on Announcing an Actual Attainment.

67. pārā. 193 Tena [T 2.0208] samayena buddho bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā sandiṭṭhā sambhattā bhikkhū vaggumudāya nadiyā tīre vassaṃ upagacchiṃsu. Tena kho pana samayena vajjī dubbhikkhā hoti – dvīhitikā setaṭṭhikā salākāvuttā, na sukarā uñchena paggahena yāpetuṃ. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “etarahi kho vajjī dubbhikkhā – dvīhitikā setaṭṭhikā salākāvuttā, na sukarā uñchena paggahena yāpetuṃ. Kena nu kho mayaṃ upāyena samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṃ vassaṃ vaseyyāma, na ca piṇḍakena kilameyyāmā”ti? Ekacce evamāhaṃsu – “handa mayaṃ, āvuso, gihīnaṃ kammantaṃ adhiṭṭhema. Evaṃ te amhākaṃ dātuṃ maññissanti. Evaṃ mayaṃ samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṃ vassaṃ vasissāma, na ca piṇḍakena kilamissāmā”ti. Ekacce evamāhaṃsu – “alaṃ, āvuso, kiṃ gihīnaṃ kammantaṃ adhiṭṭhitena? Handa mayaṃ, āvuso, gihīnaṃ dūteyyaṃ harāma. Evaṃ te amhākaṃ dātuṃ maññissanti. Evaṃ mayaṃ samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṃ vassaṃ vasissāma, na ca piṇḍakena kilamissāmā”ti. Ekacce evamāhaṃsu – “alaṃ, āvuso; [M 0.0036] kiṃ gihīnaṃ kammantaṃ adhiṭṭhitena! Kiṃ gihīnaṃ dūteyyaṃ haṭena! Handa mayaṃ, āvuso, gihīnaṃ aññamaññassa uttarimanussadhammassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsissāma [T 2.0209] – ‘asuko bhikkhu paṭhamassa jhānassa [P 4.0024] lābhī, asuko bhikkhu dutiyassa jhānassa lābhī, asuko bhikkhu tatiyassa jhānassa lābhī, asuko bhikkhu catutthassa jhānassa [V 0.0036] lābhī, asuko bhikkhu sotāpanno, asuko bhikkhu sakadāgāmī, asuko bhikkhu anāgāmī, asuko bhikkhu arahā, asuko bhikkhu tevijjo, asuko bhikkhu chaḷabhiññoti. Evaṃ te amhākaṃ dātuṃ maññissanti. Evaṃ mayaṃ samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṃ vassaṃ vasissāma, na ca piṇḍakena kilamissāmā”ti. Eso yeva kho, āvuso, seyyo, yo amhākaṃ gihīnaṃ aññamaññassa uttarimanussadhammassa vaṇṇo bhāsito”ti.

67. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Vesālī in the Great Wood, in the Hall with the Peaked Roof. Now at that time, many monks who were acquaintances and companions had entered the rains residence on the bank of the Vaggumudā River. At that time, the Vajjī country was afflicted by famine, a time of hardship, with white bones scattered about, and where sustenance was distributed by lots; it was not easy to subsist by gleaning with bowl in hand. Then this thought occurred to those monks: 'At present, the Vajjī country is afflicted by famine, a time of hardship, with white bones scattered about, and where sustenance is distributed by lots; it is not easy to subsist by gleaning with bowl in hand. By what means can we dwell in unity, harmony, and without dispute, spending the rains comfortably without being exhausted by alms gathering?' Some said: 'Come, friends, let us manage the work of householders. Then they will think to give to us. Thus we will dwell in unity, harmony, and without dispute, spending the rains comfortably without being exhausted by alms gathering.' Others said: 'Enough, friends! What is the use of managing the work of householders? Come, friends, let us act as messengers for householders. Then they will think to give to us. Thus we will dwell in unity, harmony, and without dispute, spending the rains comfortably without being exhausted by alms gathering.' Still others said: 'Enough, friends! What is the use of managing the work of householders? What is the use of having acted as messengers for householders? Come, friends, let us speak to the householders in praise of one another's superhuman states: "Such-and-such a monk is an obtainer of the first jhāna, such-and-such a monk is an obtainer of the second jhāna, such-and-such a monk is an obtainer of the third jhāna, such-and-such a monk is an obtainer of the fourth jhāna, such-and-such a monk is a stream-enterer, such-and-such a monk is a once-returner, such-and-such a monk is a non-returner, such-and-such a monk is an arahant, such-and-such a monk possesses the three true knowledges, such-and-such a monk possesses the six higher knowledges." Then they will think to give to us. Thus we will dwell in unity, harmony, and without dispute, spending the rains comfortably without being exhausted by alms gathering.' And they agreed upon this proposal: 'This indeed is the best course, friends, that we speak to the householders in praise of one another's superhuman states.'

Atha kho te bhikkhū gihīnaṃ aññamaññassa uttarimanussadhammassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsiṃsu – “asuko bhikkhu paṭhamassa jhānassa lābhī…pe… asuko bhikkhu chaḷabhiñño”ti. Atha kho te manussā – “lābhā vata no, suladdhaṃ vata no, yesaṃ no evarūpā bhikkhū vassaṃ upagatā, na vata no ito pubbe evarūpā bhikkhū vassaṃ upagatā, yathayime bhikkhū sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā”ti. Te na tādisāni bhojanāni attanā bhuñjanti, mātāpitūnaṃ denti puttadārassa denti dāsakammakaraporisassa denti mittāmaccānaṃ denti ñātisālohitānaṃ denti yādisāni bhikkhūnaṃ denti. Na tādisāni khādanīyāni sāyanīyāni pānāni attanā khādanti sāyanti pivanti attanā pivanti (syā. ka.) mātāpitūnaṃ denti puttadārassa denti dāsakammakaraporisassa denti mittāmaccānaṃ denti ñātisālohitānaṃ denti[T 2.0210], yādisāni bhikkhūnaṃ denti. Atha kho te bhikkhū vaṇṇavā ahesuṃ pīṇindriyā pasannamukhavaṇṇā vippasannachavivaṇṇā.

Then those monks spoke to the householders in praise of one another's superhuman states: 'Such-and-such a monk is an obtainer of the first jhāna... such-and-such a monk possesses the six higher knowledges.' And those people said: 'It is a gain for us, indeed! It is well-gained by us, indeed, that such monks have entered upon the rains in our vicinity! Never before, indeed, have such monks entered upon the rains in our vicinity as these monks who are virtuous and of good qualities.' The kind of staple foods they gave to the monks, they did not eat themselves, nor did they give to their mothers and fathers, children and wives, servants, workers, and men, friends and colleagues, or kinsmen and relatives. The kind of hard foods, soft foods, and beverages they gave to the monks, they did not eat, taste, or drink themselves, nor did they give to their mothers and fathers, children and wives, servants, workers, and men, friends and colleagues, or kinsmen and relatives. Then those monks became of good complexion, with plump faculties, with serene facial complexions, and with exceptionally clear skin complexions.

68. Āciṇṇaṃ kho panetaṃ vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū vassaṃvuṭṭhā temāsaccayena senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena vesālī tena pakkamiṃsu. Anupubbena yena vesālī mahāvanaṃ kūṭāgārasālā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Tena kho pana samayena disāsu vassaṃvuṭṭhā bhikkhū kisā honti lūkhā dubbaṇṇā [M 0.0037] uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajātā dhamanisanthatagattā. Vaggumudātīriyā pana bhikkhū vaṇṇavā honti pīṇindriyā pasannamukhavaṇṇā vippasannachavivaṇṇā. Āciṇṇaṃ kho panetaṃ buddhānaṃ bhagavantānaṃ āgantukehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ paṭisammodituṃ. Atha kho bhagavā vaggumudātīriye bhikkhū etadavoca [P 4.0025] – “kacci, bhikkhave, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ, kacci samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṃ vassaṃ vasittha, na ca piṇḍakena kilamitthā”ti? “Khamanīyaṃ bhagavā, yāpanīyaṃ bhagavā. Samaggā ca mayaṃ, bhante, sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṃ vassaṃ vasimhā, na ca piṇḍakena kilamimhā”ti. Jānantāpi tathāgatā pucchanti, jānantāpi na pucchanti. Kālaṃ viditvā pucchanti[V 0.0037], kālaṃ viditvā na pucchanti. Atthasañhitaṃ tathāgatā pucchanti, no anatthasañhitaṃ. Anatthasañhite setughāto tathāgatānaṃ. Dvīhākārehi buddhā [T 2.0211] bhagavanto bhikkhū paṭipucchanti – dhammaṃ vā desessāma, sāvakānaṃ vā sikkhāpadaṃ paññapessāmāti.

68. It is customary for monks who have completed the rains residence to visit the Blessed One. So those monks, having completed the rains residence at the end of three months, set their lodgings in order, took their bowls and robes, and set out for Vesālī. Gradually, they arrived at the Great Wood in Vesālī, the hall with the peaked roof, and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. At that time, monks who had completed the rains residence from other regions were thin, haggard, of poor complexion, had become pale and yellowish, and had veins standing out on their bodies. But the monks from the bank of the Vaggumudā were of good complexion, with plump faculties, with serene facial complexions, and with exceptionally clear skin complexions. It is customary for the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, to exchange greetings with visiting monks. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks from the bank of the Vaggumudā: 'I hope, monks, you are keeping well? I hope you are getting by? I hope you have dwelt for the rains comfortably, in unity, harmony, and without dispute, and have not been weary on account of alms-food?' 'We are keeping well, Blessed One. We are getting by, Blessed One. We have, venerable sir, dwelt for the rains comfortably, in unity, harmony, and without dispute, and we have not been weary on account of alms-food.' Knowing, Tathāgatas ask; knowing, they do not ask. Knowing the right time, they ask; knowing the right time, they do not ask. Tathāgatas ask what is connected with benefit, not what is unconnected with benefit. For Tathāgatas, there is a barrier against what is unconnected with benefit. The Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, question the monks for two reasons: either 'We will teach the Dhamma,' or 'We will lay down a training rule for the disciples.'

Atha kho bhagavā vaggumudātīriye bhikkhū etadavoca – “yathā kathaṃ pana tumhe, bhikkhave, samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṃ vassaṃ vasittha, na ca piṇḍakena kilamitthā”ti? Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Kacci pana vo, bhikkhave, bhūta”nti? “Bhūtaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, bhikkhave, udarassa kāraṇā gihīnaṃ aññamaññassa uttarimanussadhammassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsissatha! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –
