Then the Blessed One said this to the monks on the bank of the Vaggumudā River: ‐‐How is it, monks, that you spent the rains in concord, rejoicing, without disputing, in comfort, and did not suffer for lack of alms?‐‐ Then those monks informed the Blessed One of this matter. ‐‐Monks, is your statement true?‐‐ ‐‐It is true, Blessed One.‐‐ The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… ‐‐How indeed could you, monks, for the sake of your bellies, speak to householders of one another’s praise of states superior to human states? This, monks, is not for the confidence of those who are not yet confident… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule in this way:‐‐

69. “Yo pana bhikkhu anupasampannassa uttarimanussadhammaṃ āroceyya bhūtasmiṃ, pācittiya”nti.

69. “Whatever monk should inform one who is not fully ordained of a state superior to human states, when it is true, it is an offense of expiation.”

70. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

70. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatsoever kind… ‘Monk’ means: …in this sense, this is the one intended as ‘monk’.

Anupasampanno nāma bhikkhuñca bhikkhuniñca ṭhapetvā, avaseso anupasampanno nāma.

‘One who is not fully ordained’ means: setting aside a monk and a nun, the remainder is called ‘one who is not fully ordained’.

pārā. 198 Uttarimanussadhammo nāma jhānaṃ, vimokkho, samādhi, samāpatti, ñāṇadassanaṃ, maggabhāvanā, phalasacchikiriyā, kilesappahānaṃ, vinīvaraṇatā cittassa, suññāgāre abhirati.

‘A state superior to human states’ means: jhāna, liberation, concentration, attainment, knowledge and vision, development of the path, realization of the fruit, abandonment of defilements, the state of the mind being free from hindrances, and delight in a secluded place.

pārā. 199 Jhānanti [M 0.0038] paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ, dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ, tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ.

‘Jhāna’ means: the first jhāna, the second jhāna, the third jhāna, the fourth jhāna.

pārā. 199 Vimokkhoti suññato vimokkho, animitto vimokkho, appaṇihito vimokkho.

‘Liberation’ means: liberation through emptiness, signless liberation, desireless liberation.

pārā. 199 Samādhīti suññato samādhi, animitto samādhi, appaṇihito [T 2.0212] samādhi.

‘Concentration’ means: concentration on emptiness, signless concentration, desireless concentration.

pārā. 199 Samāpattīti suññatā samāpatti, animittā samāpatti, appaṇihitā samāpatti.

‘Attainment’ means: the attainment of emptiness, the signless attainment, the desireless attainment.

pārā. 199 Ñāṇadassananti [P 4.0026][V 0.0038] tisso vijjā.

‘Knowledge and vision’ means: the three kinds of knowledge.

pārā. 199 Maggabhāvanāti cattāro satipaṭṭhānā, cattāro sammappadhānā, cattāro iddhipādā, pañcindriyāni, pañca balāni, satta bojjhaṅgā, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo.

‘Development of the path’ means: the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right strivings, the four bases of spiritual power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the Noble Eightfold Path.

pārā. 199 Phalasacchikiriyāti sotāpattiphalassa sacchikiriyā, sakadāgāmiphalassa sacchikiriyā, anāgāmiphalassa sacchikiriyā, arahattassa arahattaphalassa (syā.) sacchikiriyā.

‘Realization of the fruit’ means: the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, the realization of the fruit of the once-returner, the realization of the fruit of the non-returner, and the realization of arahantship.

pārā. 199 Kilesappahānanti rāgassa pahānaṃ, dosassa pahānaṃ, mohassa pahānaṃ.

‘Abandonment of defilements’ means: the abandonment of lust, the abandonment of aversion, the abandonment of delusion.

pārā. 199 Vinīvaraṇatā cittassāti rāgā cittaṃ vinīvaraṇatā, dosā cittaṃ vinīvaraṇatā, mohā cittaṃ vinīvaraṇatā.

‘The state of the mind being free from hindrances’ means: the mind’s freedom from lust, the mind’s freedom from aversion, and the mind’s freedom from delusion.

pārā. 199 Suññāgāre abhiratīti paṭhamena jhānena suññāgāre abhirati, dutiyena jhānena suññāgāre abhirati, tatiyena jhānena suññāgāre abhirati, catutthena jhānena suññāgāre abhirati.

‘Delight in a secluded place’ means: delighting in a secluded place with the first jhāna, delighting in a secluded place with the second jhāna, delighting in a secluded place with the third jhāna, and delighting in a secluded place with the fourth jhāna.

71. Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji”nti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

71. ‘Should inform’ means: for one who says to an unordained person, ‘I have entered the first jhāna,’ there is an offense of expiation.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmī”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should inform’ means: for one who says to an unordained person, ‘I am entering the first jhāna,’ there is an offense of expiation.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpanno”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should inform’ means: for one who says to an unordained person, ‘I am one who has entered the first jhāna,’ there is an offense of expiation.

Āroceyyāti [M 0.0039] anupasampannassa – “paṭhamassa jhānassa lābhimhī”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should inform’ means: for one who says to an unordained person, ‘I am a gainer of the first jhāna,’ there is an offense of expiation.

Āroceyyāti [V 0.0039] anupasampannassa – “paṭhamassa jhānassa vasimhī”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should inform’ means: for one who says to an unordained person, ‘I have mastery of the first jhāna,’ there is an offense of expiation.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “paṭhamaṃ [T 2.0213] jhānaṃ sacchikataṃ mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should inform’ means: for one who says to an unordained person, ‘The first jhāna has been realized by me,’ there is an offense of expiation.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; catutthassa jhānassa lābhimhi, vasimhi; catutthaṃ jhānaṃ sacchikataṃ mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should inform’ means: for one who says to an unordained person, ‘I have entered the second jhāna… the third jhāna… the fourth jhāna; I am entering it; I am one who has entered it; I am a gainer of the fourth jhāna; I have mastery of it; the fourth jhāna has been realized by me,’ there is an offense of expiation.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “suññataṃ vimokkhaṃ… animittaṃ vimokkhaṃ… appaṇihitaṃ vimokkhaṃ… suññataṃ samādhiṃ… animittaṃ samādhiṃ… appaṇihitaṃ samādhiṃ samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; appaṇihitassa samādhissa lābhimhi, vasimhi; appaṇihito samādhi sacchikato mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should inform’ means: for one who says to an unordained person, ‘I have entered liberation through emptiness… signless liberation… desireless liberation… concentration on emptiness… signless concentration… desireless concentration; I am entering it; I am one who has entered it; I am a gainer of desireless concentration; I have mastery of it; desireless concentration has been realized by me,’ there is an offense of expiation.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “suññataṃ samāpattiṃ… animittaṃ samāpattiṃ… appaṇihitaṃ samāpattiṃ samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; appaṇihitāya samāpattiyā lābhimhi, vasimhi; appaṇihitā samāpatti sacchikatā mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should inform’ means: for one who says to an unordained person, ‘I have entered the attainment of emptiness… the signless attainment… the desireless attainment; I am entering it; I am one who has entered it; I am a gainer of the desireless attainment; I have mastery of it; the desireless attainment has been realized by me,’ there is an offense of expiation.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “tisso vijjā samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; tissannaṃ vijjānaṃ lābhimhi, vasimhi; tisso vijjā sacchikatā mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should inform’ means: for one who says to an unordained person, ‘I have entered the three kinds of knowledge; I am entering them; I am one who has entered them; I am a gainer of the three kinds of knowledge; I have mastery of them; the three kinds of knowledge have been realized by me,’ there is an offense of expiation.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “cattāro [P 4.0027] satipaṭṭhāne… cattāro sammappadhāne… cattāro iddhipāde samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ lābhimhi, vasimhi; cattāro iddhipādā [T 2.0214] sacchikatā mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should inform’ means: for one who says to an unordained person, ‘I have entered the four foundations of mindfulness… the four right strivings… the four bases of spiritual power; I am entering them; I am one who has entered them; I am a gainer of the four bases of spiritual power; I have mastery of them; the four bases of spiritual power have been realized by me,’ there is an offense of expiation.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “pañcindriyāni… pañca balāni samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi[V 0.0040], samāpanno; pañcannaṃ balānaṃ lābhimhi, vasimhi; pañca balāni sacchikatāni mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should inform’ means: for one who says to an unordained person, ‘I have entered the five faculties… the five powers; I am entering them; I am one who has entered them; I am a gainer of the five powers; I have mastery of them; the five powers have been realized by me,’ there is an offense of expiation.

Āroceyyāti [M 0.0040] anupasampannassa – “satta bojjhaṅge samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ lābhimhi, vasimhi; satta bojjhaṅgā sacchikatā mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

If he declares to an unordained person, 'I have attained, am attaining, or am one who has attained the seven factors of enlightenment; I am a gainer of the seven factors of enlightenment, I have mastery over them; the seven factors of enlightenment have been realized by me,' there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa lābhimhi, vasimhi; ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo sacchikato mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

If he declares to an unordained person, 'I have attained, am attaining, or am one who has attained the noble eightfold path; I am a gainer of the noble eightfold path, I have mastery over it; the noble eightfold path has been realized by me,' there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “sotāpattiphalaṃ… sakadāgāmiphalaṃ… anāgāmiphalaṃ… arahattaṃ samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; arahattassa lābhimhi, vasimhi; arahattaṃ arahattaphalaṃ (syā.) sacchikataṃ mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

If he declares to an unordained person, 'I have attained, am attaining, or am one who has attained the fruit of stream-entry... the fruit of once-returning... the fruit of non-returning... arahantship; I am a gainer of arahantship, I have mastery over it; arahantship has been realized by me,' there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “rāgo me catto… doso me catto… moho me catto, vanto, mutto, pahīno, paṭinissaṭṭho, ukkheṭito[T 2.0215], samukkheṭito”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

If he declares to an unordained person, 'Lust has been abandoned by me... hatred has been abandoned by me... delusion has been abandoned by me, vomited, released, dispelled, relinquished, uprooted, completely uprooted,' there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “rāgā me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇaṃ… dosā me citta vinīvaraṇaṃ… mohā me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇa”nti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

If he declares to an unordained person, 'My mind is without hindrance from lust... my mind is without hindrance from hatred... my mind is without hindrance from delusion,' there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “suññāgāre paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; suññāgāre catutthassa jhānassa lābhimhi, vasimhi; suññāgāre catutthaṃ jhānaṃ sacchikataṃ mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

If he declares to an unordained person, 'In a secluded dwelling, I have attained, am attaining, or am one who has attained the first jhāna... the second jhāna... the third jhāna... the fourth jhāna; in a secluded dwelling, I am a gainer of the fourth jhāna, I have mastery over it; in a secluded dwelling, the fourth jhāna has been realized by me,' there is an offense of pācittiya.

72. Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “paṭhamañca jhānaṃ dutiyañca jhānaṃ samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; paṭhamassa ca jhānassa dutiyassa ca jhānassa lābhimhi, vasimhi; paṭhamañca jhānaṃ dutiyañca jhānaṃ sacchikataṃ mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

72. If he declares to an unordained person, 'I have attained, am attaining, or am one who has attained the first jhāna and the second jhāna; I am a gainer of the first jhāna and the second jhāna, I have mastery over them; the first jhāna and the second jhāna have been realized by me,' there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti [V 0.0041] anupasampannassa – “paṭhamañca jhānaṃ tatiyañca jhānaṃ… paṭhamañca jhānaṃ catutthañca jhānaṃ samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; paṭhamassa ca jhānassa catutthassa ca jhānassa lābhimhi, vasimhi; paṭhamañca jhānaṃ catutthañca jhānaṃ sacchikataṃ mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

If he declares to an unordained person, 'I have attained, am attaining, or am one who has attained the first jhāna and the third jhāna... the first jhāna and the fourth jhāna; I am a gainer of the first jhāna and the fourth jhāna, I have mastery over them; the first jhāna and the fourth jhāna have been realized by me,' there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti [M 0.0041] anupasampannassa – “paṭhamañca jhānaṃ suññatañca vimokkhaṃ… animittañca vimokkhaṃ… appaṇihitañca vimokkhaṃ… suññatañca [T 2.0216] samādhiṃ… animittañca samādhiṃ… appaṇihitañca samādhiṃ samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; paṭhamassa ca jhānassa appaṇihitassa ca samādhissa lābhimhi, vasimhi; paṭhamañca jhānaṃ appaṇihito ca samādhi sacchikato mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

If he declares to an unordained person, 'I have attained, am attaining, or am one who has attained the first jhāna and the liberation of emptiness... the signless liberation... the desireless liberation... the concentration of emptiness... the signless concentration... the desireless concentration; I am a gainer of the first jhāna and the desireless concentration, I have mastery over them; the first jhāna and the desireless concentration have been realized by me,' there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “paṭhamañca jhānaṃ suññatañca samāpattiṃ… animittañca samāpattiṃ… appaṇihitañca samāpattiṃ samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; paṭhamassa ca jhānassa appaṇihitāya ca samāpattiyā lābhimhi, vasimhi; paṭhamañca jhānaṃ appaṇihitā ca samāpatti sacchikatā mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

If he declares to an unordained person, 'I have attained, am attaining, or am one who has attained the first jhāna and the attainment of emptiness... the signless attainment... the desireless attainment; I am a gainer of the first jhāna and the desireless attainment, I have mastery over them; the first jhāna and the desireless attainment have been realized by me,' there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “paṭhamañca jhānaṃ tisso ca vijjā samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; paṭhamassa ca jhānassa tissannañca vijjānaṃ lābhimhi, vasimhi; paṭhamañca jhānaṃ tisso ca vijjā sacchikatā mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

If he declares to an unordained person, 'I have attained, am attaining, or am one who has attained the first jhāna and the three knowledges; I am a gainer of the first jhāna and the three knowledges, I have mastery over them; the first jhāna and the three knowledges have been realized by me,' there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “paṭhamañca [P 4.0028] jhānaṃ cattāro ca satipaṭṭhāne…pe… cattāro ca sammappadhāne… cattāro ca iddhipāde samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; paṭhamassa ca jhānassa catunnañca iddhipādānaṃ lābhimhi, vasimhi; paṭhamañca jhānaṃ cattāro ca iddhipādā sacchikatā mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

If he declares to an unordained person, 'I have attained, am attaining, or am one who has attained the first jhāna and the four foundations of mindfulness... the four right exertions... the four bases of spiritual power; I am a gainer of the first jhāna and the four bases of spiritual power, I have mastery over them; the first jhāna and the four bases of spiritual power have been realized by me,' there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti [T 2.0217] anupasampannassa – “paṭhamañca jhānaṃ, pañca ca indriyāni… pañca ca balāni samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; paṭhamassa ca jhānassa pañcannañca balānaṃ lābhimhi, vasimhi; paṭhamañca jhānaṃ pañca ca balāni sacchikatāni mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

If he declares to an unordained person, 'I have attained, am attaining, or am one who has attained the first jhāna and the five faculties... the five powers; I am a gainer of the first jhāna and the five powers, I have mastery over them; the first jhāna and the five powers have been realized by me,' there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti [V 0.0042] anupasampannassa – “paṭhamañca jhānaṃ satta ca bojjhaṅge samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; paṭhamassa ca jhānassa sattannañca bojjhaṅgānaṃ lābhimhi, vasimhi; paṭhamañca jhānaṃ satta ca bojjhaṅgā sacchikatā mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

If he declares to an unordained person, 'I have attained, am attaining, or am one who has attained the first jhāna and the seven factors of enlightenment; I am a gainer of the first jhāna and the seven factors of enlightenment, I have mastery over them; the first jhāna and the seven factors of enlightenment have been realized by me,' there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “paṭhamañca jhānaṃ ariyañca aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; paṭhamassa ca jhānassa ariyassa ca aṭṭhaṅgikassa [M 0.0042] maggassa lābhimhi, vasimhi; paṭhamañca jhānaṃ ariyo ca aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo sacchikato mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

If he declares to an unordained person, 'I have attained, am attaining, or am one who has attained the first jhāna and the noble eightfold path; I am a gainer of the first jhāna and the noble eightfold path, I have mastery over them; the first jhāna and the noble eightfold path have been realized by me,' there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “paṭhamañca jhānaṃ sotāpattiphalañca… sakadāgāmiphalañca… anāgāmiphalañca… arahattañca arahattaphalañca (syā.) samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; paṭhamassa ca jhānassa arahattassa arahattaphalassa (syā.) ca lābhimhi, vasimhi; paṭhamañca jhānaṃ arahattañca sacchikataṃ mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

Should one declare to an unordained person: "I have entered, am entering, or have entered the first jhāna and the fruit of stream-entry... the fruit of once-returning... the fruit of non-returning... and arahantship; I am an obtainer and master of the first jhāna and of arahantship; the first jhāna and arahantship have been realized by me," for one who speaks thus, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti [T 2.0218] anupasampannassa – “paṭhamañca jhānaṃ samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno… rāgo ca me catto… doso ca me catto… moho ca me catto, vanto, mutto, pahīno, paṭinissaṭṭho, ukkheṭito, samukkheṭito”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

Should one declare to an unordained person: "I have entered, am entering, or have entered the first jhāna... and by me lust has been abandoned... and by me hatred has been abandoned... and by me delusion has been abandoned, disgorged, released, relinquished, given up, uprooted, completely uprooted," for one who speaks thus, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “paṭhamañca jhānaṃ samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno… rāgā ca me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇaṃ… dosā ca me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇaṃ… mohā ca me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇa”nti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

Should one declare to an unordained person: "I have entered, am entering, or have entered the first jhāna... and my mind is free from lust... and my mind is free from hatred... and my mind is free from delusion," for one who speaks thus, there is an offense of pācittiya.

73. Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “dutiyañca jhānaṃ tatiyañca jhānaṃ… dutiyañca jhānaṃ catutthañca jhānaṃ samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; dutiyassa ca jhānassa catutthassa ca jhānassa lābhimhi, vasimhi; dutiyañca jhānaṃ catutthañca jhānaṃ sacchikataṃ mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

73. Should one declare to an unordained person: "I have entered, am entering, or have entered the second jhāna and the third jhāna... the second jhāna and the fourth jhāna; I am an obtainer and master of the second jhāna and of the fourth jhāna; the second jhāna and the fourth jhāna have been realized by me," for one who speaks thus, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “dutiyañca jhānaṃ suññatañca vimokkhaṃ…pe… mohā ca me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇa”nti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

Should one declare to an unordained person: "The second jhāna and the liberation through emptiness... and my mind is free from delusion," for one who speaks thus, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti [V 0.0043] anupasampannassa – “dutiyañca jhānaṃ paṭhamañca jhānaṃ samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; dutiyassa ca jhānassa paṭhamassa ca jhānassa lābhimhi, vasimhi; dutiyañca jhānaṃ paṭhamañca jhānaṃ sacchikataṃ mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe….

Should one declare to an unordained person: "I have entered, am entering, or have entered the second jhāna and the first jhāna; I am an obtainer and master of the second jhāna and of the first jhāna; the second jhāna and the first jhāna have been realized by me," for one who speaks thus, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Mūlaṃ saṃkhittaṃ.

The root is abbreviated.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “mohā ca me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇaṃ, paṭhamañca jhānaṃ [T 2.0219] samāpajjiṃ, samāpajjāmi, samāpanno; mohā ca me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇaṃ, paṭhamassa [M 0.0043] ca jhānassa lābhimhi, vasimhi; mohā ca me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇaṃ, paṭhamañca jhānaṃ sacchikataṃ mayā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe….

Should one declare to an unordained person: "My mind is free from delusion, and I have entered, am entering, or have entered the first jhāna; my mind is free from delusion, and I am an obtainer and master of the first jhāna; my mind is free from delusion, and the first jhāna has been realized by me," for one who speaks thus, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “mohā ca me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇaṃ, dosā ca me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇa”nti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa…pe….

Should one declare to an unordained person: "My mind is free from delusion, and my mind is free from hatred," for one who speaks thus, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “paṭhamañca jhānaṃ dutiyañca jhānaṃ tatiyañca jhānaṃ catutthañca jhānaṃ suññatañca vimokkhaṃ animittañca vimokkhaṃ appaṇihitañca vimokkhaṃ suññatañca samādhiṃ animittañca samādhiṃ appaṇihitañca samādhiṃ suññatañca samāpattiṃ animittañca samāpattiṃ appaṇihitañca samāpattiṃ tisso ca vijjā cattāro ca satipaṭṭhāne cattāro ca sammappadhāne cattāro ca iddhipāde pañca ca indriyāni pañca ca balāni satta ca bojjhaṅge ariyañca aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ sotāpattiphalañca [P 4.0029] sakadāgāmiphalañca anāgāmiphalañca arahattañca arahattaphalañca (syā.) samāpajjiṃ…pe… rāgo ca me catto, doso ca me catto, moho ca me catto, vanto, mutto, pahīno, paṭinissaṭṭho, ukkheṭito samukkheṭito, rāgā ca me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇaṃ, dosā ca me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇaṃ, mohā ca me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇa”nti bhaṇantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

Should one declare to an unordained person: "I have entered, am entering, or have entered the first jhāna, the second jhāna, the third jhāna, the fourth jhāna, the liberation through emptiness, the signless liberation, the desireless liberation, the concentration of emptiness, the signless concentration, the desireless concentration, the attainment of emptiness, the signless attainment, the desireless attainment, the three knowledges, the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right exertions, the four bases of spiritual power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, the noble eightfold path, the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and arahantship; and by me lust has been abandoned, and by me hatred has been abandoned, and by me delusion has been abandoned, disgorged, released, relinquished, given up, uprooted, completely uprooted; and my mind is free from lust, and my mind is free from hatred, and my mind is free from delusion," for one who speaks thus, there is an offense of pācittiya.

74. Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji”nti [T 2.0220] vattukāmo “dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji”nti bhaṇantassa paṭivijānantassa āpatti pācittiyassa, na paṭivijānantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa.

74. Should one declare to an unordained person—intending to say, 'I entered the first jhāna,' but saying, 'I entered the second jhāna'—for one who speaks thus, if the listener understands, there is an offense of pācittiya; if the listener does not understand, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Āroceyyāti [V 0.0044] anupasampannassa – “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji”nti vattukāmo “tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ, suññataṃ vimokkhaṃ, animittaṃ vimokkhaṃ, appaṇihitaṃ vimokkhaṃ, suññataṃ samādhiṃ, animittaṃ samādhiṃ, appaṇihitaṃ samādhiṃ, suññataṃ samāpattiṃ, animittaṃ samāpattiṃ, appaṇihitaṃ samāpattiṃ, tisso vijjā, cattāro satipaṭṭhāne, cattāro sammappadhāne, cattāro iddhipāde, pañcindriyāni, pañca balāni, satta bojjhaṅge, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ, sotāpattiphalaṃ, sakadāgāmiphalaṃ, anāgāmiphalaṃ, arahattaṃ arahattaphalaṃ (syā.) samāpajjiṃ…pe… rāgo me catto, doso me catto, moho me catto, vanto, mutto, pahīno; paṭinissaṭṭho, ukkheṭito, samukkheṭito; rāgā me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇaṃ, dosā me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇaṃ, mohā me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇa”nti bhaṇantassa paṭivijānantassa āpatti pācittiyassa, na paṭivijānantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Should one declare to an unordained person—intending to say, 'I entered the first jhāna,' but saying, 'I entered the third jhāna… the fourth jhāna, the liberation through emptiness, the signless liberation, the desireless liberation, the concentration of emptiness, the signless concentration, the desireless concentration, the attainment of emptiness, the signless attainment, the desireless attainment, the three knowledges, the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right exertions, the four bases of spiritual power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, the Noble Eightfold Path, the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, arahantship… by me lust has been abandoned, by me hatred has been abandoned, by me delusion has been abandoned, disgorged, released, relinquished, given up, uprooted, completely uprooted; my mind is free from lust, my mind is free from hatred, my mind is free from delusion'—for one who speaks thus, if the listener understands, there is an offense of pācittiya; if the listener does not understand, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Āroceyyāti [M 0.0044] anupasampannassa – “dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji”nti vattukāmo…pe… “mohā me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇa”nti bhaṇantassa paṭivijānantassa āpatti pācittiyassa, na paṭivijānantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa…pe….

Should one declare to an unordained person—intending to say, 'I entered the second jhāna,'… but saying, 'my mind is free from delusion'—for one who speaks thus, if the listener understands, there is an offense of pācittiya; if the listener does not understand, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji”nti vattukāmo – “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji”nti bhaṇantassa [T 2.0221] paṭivijānantassa āpatti pācittiyassa, na paṭivijānantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa…pe….

If he should disclose to one not fully ordained—intending to say, “I attained the second jhāna,” but saying, “I attained the first jhāna”—if the listener understands, it is an offense entailing expiation; if the listener does not understand, it is an offense of wrong conduct.

Mūlaṃ saṃkhittaṃ.

The original text is abbreviated.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “mohā me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇa”nti vattukāmo – “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji”nti bhaṇantassa paṭivijānantassa āpatti pācittiyassa, na paṭivijānantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa…pe….

If he should disclose to one not fully ordained—intending to say, “My mind is unhindered by delusion,” but saying, “I attained the first jhāna”—if the listener understands, it is an offense entailing expiation; if the listener does not understand, it is an offense of wrong conduct.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “mohā me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇa”nti vattukāmo – “dosā me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇa”nti bhaṇantassa paṭivijānantassa āpatti pācittiyassa, na paṭivijānantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa…pe….

Should he disclose to one not fully ordained—intending to say, “My mind is unhindered by delusion,” but saying, “My mind is unhindered by hatred”—if the listener understands, it is an offense entailing expiation; if the listener does not understand, it is an offense of wrong conduct.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “paṭhamañca jhānaṃ dutiyañca jhānaṃ tatiyañca jhānaṃ catutthañca jhānaṃ [V 0.0045] …pe… dosā ca me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇa”nti vattukāmo – “mohā me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇa”nti bhaṇantassa paṭivijānantassa āpatti pācittiyassa, na paṭivijānantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Should he disclose to one not fully ordained—intending to say, “The first jhāna, and the second jhāna, and the third jhāna, and the fourth jhāna… and my mind is unhindered by hatred,” but saying, “My mind is unhindered by delusion”—if the listener understands, it is an offense entailing expiation; if the listener does not understand, it is an offense of wrong conduct.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “dutiyañca jhānaṃ tatiyañca jhānaṃ catutthañca jhānaṃ…pe… mohā ca me cittaṃ vinīvaraṇa”nti vattukāmo – “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji”nti bhaṇantassa paṭivijānantassa āpatti pācittiyassa, na paṭivijānantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa…pe….

Should he disclose to one not fully ordained—intending to say, “The second jhāna, and the third jhāna, and the fourth jhāna… and my mind is unhindered by delusion,” but saying, “I attained the first jhāna”—if the listener understands, it is an offense entailing expiation; if the listener does not understand, it is an offense of wrong conduct.

75. Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “yo te vihāre vasi so bhikkhu paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, samāpajjati, samāpanno; so bhikkhu [T 2.0222] paṭhamassa jhānassa lābhī, vasī; tena bhikkhunā paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ sacchikata”nti bhaṇantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa.

75. Should he disclose to one not fully ordained, saying: “The monk who stayed in your dwelling attained the first jhāna, is attaining it, has attained it; that monk is a gainer of the first jhāna, a master of it; by that monk, the first jhāna has been realized”—it is an offense of wrong conduct.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “yo te vihāre vasi so bhikkhu dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, samāpajjati, samāpanno; so bhikkhu catutthassa jhānassa lābhī, vasī; tena bhikkhunā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ sacchikata”nti bhaṇantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Should he disclose to one not fully ordained, saying: “The monk who stayed in your dwelling attained the second jhāna… the third jhāna, the fourth jhāna, is attaining it, has attained it; that monk is a gainer of the fourth jhāna, a master of it; by that monk, the fourth jhāna has been realized”—it is an offense of wrong conduct.

Āroceyyāti [M 0.0045] anupasampannassa – “yo te vihāre vasi so bhikkhu suññataṃ vimokkhaṃ…pe… animittaṃ vimokkhaṃ appaṇihitaṃ vimokkhaṃ suññataṃ samādhiṃ animittaṃ samādhiṃ appaṇihitaṃ samādhiṃ samāpajji, samāpajjati, samāpanno; so bhikkhu appaṇihitassa samādhissa lābhī, vasī; tena bhikkhunā appaṇihito samādhi sacchikato”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Should he disclose to one not fully ordained, saying: “The monk who stayed in your dwelling attained the deliverance of emptiness… the signless deliverance, the desireless deliverance, the concentration of emptiness, the signless concentration, the desireless concentration, is attaining it, has attained it; that monk is a gainer of the desireless concentration, a master of it; by that monk, the desireless concentration has been realized”—it is an offense of wrong conduct.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “yo te vihāre vasi so bhikkhu suññataṃ samāpattiṃ…pe… animittaṃ samāpattiṃ appaṇihitaṃ samāpattiṃ samāpajji, samāpajjati, samāpanno; appaṇihitāya samāpattiyā lābhī, vasī; tena bhikkhunā appaṇihitā samāpatti sacchikatā”ti bhaṇantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Should he disclose to one not fully ordained, saying: “The monk who stayed in your dwelling attained the attainment of emptiness… the signless attainment, the desireless attainment, is attaining it, has attained it; he is a gainer of the desireless attainment, a master of it; by that monk, the desireless attainment has been realized”—it is an offense of wrong conduct.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “yo te vihāre vasi so bhikkhu tisso vijjā [V 0.0046] …pe… cattāro satipaṭṭhāne, cattāro sammappadhāne, cattāro iddhipāde, pañcindriyāni, pañca balāni, satta bojhaṅge, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ, sotāpattiphalaṃ, sakadāgāmiphalaṃ, anāgāmiphalaṃ, arahattaṃ arahattaphalaṃ (syā.) samāpajji…pe… samāpajjati, samāpanno…pe… tassa bhikkhuno rāgo catto, doso catto, moho [P 4.0030] catto, vanto, mutto, pahīno, paṭinissaṭṭho, ukkheṭito, samukkheṭito; tassa bhikkhuno rāgā cittaṃ vinīvaraṇaṃ, dosā cittaṃ vinīvaraṇaṃ, mohā cittaṃ vinīvaraṇa”nti bhaṇantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Should he disclose to one not fully ordained, saying: “The monk who stayed in your dwelling attained the three knowledges… the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right exertions, the four bases of spiritual power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, the Noble Eightfold Path, the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, arahantship, is attaining it, has attained it… that monk’s lust is abandoned, hatred is abandoned, delusion is abandoned, vomited, released, given up, relinquished, eradicated, completely eradicated; that monk’s mind is unhindered by lust, his mind is unhindered by hatred, his mind is unhindered by delusion”—it is an offense of wrong conduct.

Āroceyyāti [T 2.0223] anupasampannassa – “yo te vihāre vasi so bhikkhu suññāgāre paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, samāpajjati, samāpanno; so bhikkhu suññāgāre catutthassa jhānassa lābhī, vasī; tena bhikkhunā suññāgāre catutthaṃ jhānaṃ sacchikata”nti bhaṇantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If he informs one not fully ordained, saying: “The monk who stayed in your dwelling attained the first jhāna in a secluded place… the second jhāna, the third jhāna, the fourth jhāna, is attaining it, has attained it; that monk is a gainer of the fourth jhāna in a secluded place, a master of it; by that monk, the fourth jhāna in a secluded place has been realized”—it is an offense of wrong conduct.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “yo te cīvaraṃ paribhuñji, yo te piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñji, yo te senāsanaṃ paribhuñji, yo te gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ paribhuñji so bhikkhu suññāgāre catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, samāpajjati, samāpanno; so bhikkhu suññāgāre catutthassa jhānassa lābhī, vasī; tena bhikkhunā suññāgāre catutthaṃ jhānaṃ sacchikata”nti bhaṇantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If he informs one not fully ordained, saying: “The monk who used your robe, who used your almsfood, who used your lodging, who used your medicinal requisites for the sick, attained the fourth jhāna in a secluded place, is attaining it, has attained it; that monk is a gainer of the fourth jhāna in a secluded place, a master of it; by that monk, the fourth jhāna in a secluded place has been realized”—it is an offense of wrong conduct.

76. Āroceyyāti [M 0.0046] anupasampannassa – “yena te vihāro paribhutto…pe… yena te cīvaraṃ paribhuttaṃ, yena te piṇḍapāto paribhutto, yena te senāsanaṃ paribhuttaṃ, yena te gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāro paribhutto so bhikkhu suññāgāre catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, samāpajjati, samāpanno; so bhikkhu suññāgāre catutthassa jhānassa lābhī, vasī; tena bhikkhunā suññāgāre catutthaṃ jhānaṃ sacchikata”nti bhaṇantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa.

76. If he informs one not fully ordained, saying: “The monk by whom your dwelling was used… by whom your robe was used, by whom your almsfood was used, by whom your lodging was used, by whom your medicinal requisites for the sick were used, attained the fourth jhāna in a secluded place, is attaining it, has attained it; that monk is a gainer of the fourth jhāna in a secluded place, a master of it; by that monk, the fourth jhāna in a secluded place has been realized”—it is an offense of wrong conduct.

Āroceyyāti anupasampannassa – “yaṃ tvaṃ āgamma vihāraṃ adāsi…pe… cīvaraṃ adāsi, piṇḍapātaṃ adāsi, senāsanaṃ adāsi, gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ [T 2.0224] adāsi so bhikkhu suññāgāre catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, samāpajjati, samāpanno; so bhikkhu suññāgāre catutthassa jhānassa lābhī, vasī; tena bhikkhunā suññāgāre catutthaṃ jhānaṃ sacchikata”nti bhaṇantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Should one report to an unordained person, saying: 'The bhikkhu on whose account you gave a dwelling... gave a robe, gave almsfood, gave lodging, gave requisites of medicine for the sick—that bhikkhu, in a secluded place, has entered the fourth jhāna, is entering it, or is one who has entered it; that bhikkhu, in a secluded place, is a gainer of the fourth jhāna, is a master of it; by that bhikkhu, in a secluded place, the fourth jhāna has been realized,' for one who speaks thus, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

77. Anāpatti [V 0.0047] upasampannassa, bhūtaṃ āroceti, ādikammikassāti.

77. There is no offense if one reports what is true to an ordained person, or for the first offender.

Bhūtārocanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The eighth training rule on reporting a true attainment is concluded.

9. Duṭṭhullārocanasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Training Rule on Reporting a Grave Offense

78. Tena [T 2.0225] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā upanando sakyaputto chabbaggiyehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ bhaṇḍanakato hoti. So sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā saṅghaṃ tassā āpattiyā parivāsaṃ yāci. Tassa saṅgho tassā āpattiyā parivāsaṃ adāsi. Tena kho pana samayena sāvatthiyaṃ aññatarassa pūgassa saṅghabhattaṃ hoti. So parivasanto bhattagge āsanapariyante nisīdi. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū te upāsake etadavocuṃ – “eso, āvuso, āyasmā upanando sakyaputto tumhākaṃ sambhāvito kulūpako; yeneva hatthena saddhādeyyaṃ bhuñjati teneva hatthena upakkamitvā asuciṃ mocesi. So sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ āpattiṃ [P 4.0031] āpajjitvā saṅghaṃ tassā āpattiyā parivāsaṃ yāci. Tassa saṅgho tassā āpattiyā parivāsaṃ adāsi[M 0.0047]. So parivasanto āsanapariyante nisinno”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhussa duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ anupasampannassa ārocessantī”ti…pe… “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, bhikkhussa duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ anupasampannassa ārocethā”ti? “Saccaṃ[T 2.0226], bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, bhikkhussa duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ anupasampannassa ārocessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

78. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the venerable Upananda the Sakyan had quarreled with the bhikkhus of the group of six. Having committed the offense of intentional emission of semen, he asked the Saṅgha for probation for that offense. The Saṅgha granted him probation for that offense. Now at that time, a certain association in Sāvatthī had a meal for the Saṅgha. While undergoing probation, he sat at the end of the seating area in the meal hall. The bhikkhus of the group of six said this to those lay supporters: 'Friends, this venerable Upananda the Sakyan is a respected visitor to your families. With the very hand that he eats what is given in faith, with that same hand he made an effort and released impurity. Having committed the offense of intentional emission of semen, he asked the Saṅgha for probation for that offense. The Saṅgha granted him probation for that offense. While undergoing probation, he is seated at the end of the seating area.' Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes... criticized, complained, and spread it about, saying: 'How indeed can the bhikkhus of the group of six report a bhikkhu's grave offense to an unordained person?'... 'Is it true, bhikkhus, that you reported a bhikkhu's grave offense to an unordained person?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... 'How indeed, foolish men, can you report a bhikkhu's grave offense to an unordained person? This, foolish men, is not for the confidence of the faithless... And so, bhikkhus, you should set forth this training rule in this way:

79. “Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhussa duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ anupasampannassa āroceyya, aññatra bhikkhusammutiyā bhikkhusammatiyā (syā.), pācittiya”nti.

79. Whatever bhikkhu should report a bhikkhu's grave offense to an unordained person, except with authorization from the bhikkhus, it is an offense of expiation.

80. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

80. Whatever: means, whoever, of whatever kind... Bhikkhu: means... in this sense is this person intended as 'bhikkhu'.

Bhikkhussāti aññassa bhikkhussa.

Of a bhikkhu: means of another bhikkhu.

Duṭṭhullā [V 0.0048] nāma āpatti – cattāri ca pārājikāni, terasa ca saṅghādisesā.

A grave offense means: the four Pārājikas and the thirteen Saṅghādisesas.

Anupasampanno nāma bhikkhuñca bhikkhuniñca ṭhapetvā avaseso anupasampanno nāma.

An unordained person means: setting aside a bhikkhu and a bhikkhunī, the remainder is called an unordained person.

Āroceyyāti āroceyya itthiyā vā purisassa vā gahaṭṭhassa vā pabbajitassa vā.

Should report: means one might report to a woman or a man, to a householder or to one who has gone forth.

Aññatra bhikkhusammutiyāti ṭhapetvā bhikkhusammutiṃ.

Except with authorization from the bhikkhus: means setting aside the authorization from the bhikkhus.

Atthi bhikkhusammuti āpattipariyantā, na kulapariyantā. Atthi bhikkhusammuti kulapariyantā, na āpattipariyantā, atthi bhikkhusammuti āpattipariyantā ca kulapariyantā ca, atthi bhikkhusammuti neva āpattipariyantā na kulapariyantā.

There is an authorization from the bhikkhus limited by offense, not limited by family. There is an authorization from the bhikkhus limited by family, not limited by offense. There is an authorization from the bhikkhus limited by both offense and family. There is an authorization from the bhikkhus limited by neither offense nor family.

Āpattipariyantā nāma āpattiyo pariggahitāyo honti – “ettakāhi āpattīhi ārocetabbo”ti.

Limited by offense means: offenses are specified, thus: 'It should be reported for this many offenses.'

Kulapariyantā [M 0.0048] nāma kulāni pariggahitāni honti – “ettakesu kulesu ārocetabbo”ti. Āpattipariyantā ca kulapariyantā ca nāma āpattiyo [T 2.0227] ca pariggahitāyo honti, kulāni ca pariggahitāni honti – “ettakāhi āpattīhi ettakesu kulesu ārocetabbo”ti. Neva āpattipariyantā na kulapariyantā nāma āpattiyo ca apariggahitāyo honti, kulāni ca apariggahitāni honti – “ettakāhi āpattīhi ettakesu kulesu ārocetabbo”ti.

Limited by family means: families are specified, thus: 'It should be reported in this many families.' Limited by both offense and family means: both offenses are specified and families are specified, thus: 'It should be reported for this many offenses in this many families.' Limited by neither offense nor family means: neither offenses are specified nor are families specified.

81. Āpattipariyante yā āpattiyo pariggahitāyo honti, tā āpattiyo ṭhapetvā aññāhi āpattīhi āroceti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

81. In the case of a limit by offense, if, setting aside the offenses that have been specified, one reports other offenses, there is an offense of expiation.

Kulapariyante yāni kulāni pariggahitāni honti, [P 4.0032] tāni kulāni ṭhapetvā aññesu kulesu āroceti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

In the case of a limit by family, if, setting aside the families that have been specified, one reports in other families, there is an offense of expiation.

Āpattipariyante ca kulapariyante ca yā āpattiyo pariggahitāyo honti, tā āpattiyo [V 0.0049] ṭhapetvā yāni kulāni pariggahitāni honti, tāni kulāni ṭhapetvā aññāhi āpattīhi aññesu kulesu āroceti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

In the case of a limit by both offense and family, if, setting aside the offenses that have been specified and setting aside the families that have been specified, one reports other offenses in other families, there is an offense of expiation.

Neva āpattipariyante na kulapariyante, anāpatti.

In the case of no limit by offense and no limit by family, there is no offense.

82. Duṭṭhullāya āpattiyā duṭṭhullāpattisaññī anupasampannassa āroceti, aññatra bhikkhusammutiyā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

82. Regarding a grave offense, being one who perceives it as a grave offense, if one reports it to an unordained person—except with authorization from the bhikkhus—there is an offense of expiation.

Duṭṭhullāya āpattiyā vematiko anupasampannassa āroceti, aññatra bhikkhusammutiyā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

Regarding a grave offense, being uncertain, if one reports it to an unordained person—except with authorization from the bhikkhus—there is an offense of expiation.

Duṭṭhullāya āpattiyā aduṭṭhullāpattisaññī anupasampannassa āroceti, aññatra bhikkhusammutiyā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

Regarding a grave offense, being one who perceives it as not a grave offense, if one reports it to an unordained person—except with authorization from the bhikkhus—there is an offense of expiation.

Aduṭṭhullaṃ [T 2.0228] āpattiṃ āroceti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one reports an offense that is not grave, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

Anupasampannassa duṭṭhullaṃ vā aduṭṭhullaṃ vā ajjhācāraṃ āroceti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one reports a transgression, whether grave or not grave, of an unordained person, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

Aduṭṭhullāya [M 0.0049] āpattiyā duṭṭhullāpattisaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In the case of a non-grave offense, if one, perceiving it as a grave offense, informs, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Aduṭṭhullāya āpattiyā vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In the case of a non-grave offense, if one, being doubtful, informs, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Aduṭṭhullāya āpattiyā aduṭṭhullāpattisaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In the case of a non-grave offense, if one, perceiving it as a non-grave offense, informs, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

83. Anāpatti vatthuṃ āroceti no āpattiṃ, āpattiṃ āroceti no vatthuṃ, bhikkhusammutiyā, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

83. There is no offense if one informs of the matter but not the offense; if one informs of the offense but not the matter; for one authorized by the bhikkhus; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Duṭṭhullārocanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.

The ninth training rule on informing of a grave offense is finished.

10. Pathavīkhaṇanasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Training Rule on Digging the Earth

84. Tena [T 2.0229][V 0.0050] samayena buddho bhagavā āḷaviyaṃ viharati aggāḷave cetiye. Tena kho pana samayena āḷavakā āḷavikā (syā.) bhikkhū navakammaṃ karontā pathaviṃ khaṇantipi khaṇāpentipi. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā pathaviṃ khaṇissantipi khaṇāpessantipi! Ekindriyaṃ samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jīvaṃ viheṭhentī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āḷavakā bhikkhū pathaviṃ khaṇissantipi khaṇāpessantipī”ti…pe… “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, pathaviṃ khaṇathapi khaṇāpethapī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, pathaviṃ khaṇissathapi khaṇāpessathapi! Jīvasaññino hi, moghapurisā, [P 4.0033] manussā pathaviyā. Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

84. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Āḷavī at the Aggāḷava shrine. Now at that time, the bhikkhus of Āḷavī, while doing new work, were digging the earth and having it dug. People complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How can the Sakyan ascetics dig the earth and have it dug! The Sakyan ascetics are harming life with one faculty!” The bhikkhus heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How can the bhikkhus of Āḷavī dig the earth and have it dug!”… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that you dig the earth and have it dug?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How can you, foolish men, dig the earth and have it dug! For, foolish men, people perceive the earth as having life. This, foolish men, is not for the inspiring of faith in the uninspired… And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule in this way:

85. “Yo pana bhikkhu pathaviṃ khaṇeyya vā khaṇāpeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

85. “Whatever bhikkhu should dig the earth or have it dug, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

86. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

86. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhu’ means… in this sense is a bhikkhu intended.

Pathavī nāma dve pathaviyo [T 2.0230] – jātā ca pathavī ajātā ca pathavī.

‘Earth’ means: there are two kinds of earth—‘born’ earth and ‘unborn’ earth.

Jātā [M 0.0050] nāma pathavī – suddhapaṃsu suddhamattikā appapāsāṇā appasakkharā appakaṭhalā appamarumbā appavālikā, yebhuyyenapaṃsukā, yebhuyyenamattikā. Adaḍḍhāpi vuccati jātā pathavī. Yopi paṃsupuñjo vā mattikāpuñjo vā atirekacātumāsaṃ ovaṭṭho, ayampi vuccati jātā pathavī.

‘Born earth’ is: pure dust, pure clay, with few stones, few pebbles, few potsherds, few hard gravel, little sand; mostly dust, mostly clay. Even unfired earth is called ‘born earth’. Any heap of dust or heap of clay that has been rained on for more than four months is also called ‘born earth’.

Ajātā nāma pathavī – suddhapāsāṇā suddhasakkharā suddhakaṭhalā suddhamarumbā suddhavālikā appapaṃsukā appamattikā, yebhuyyenapāsāṇā, yebhuyyenasakkharā, yebhuyyenakaṭhalā, yebhuyyenamarumbā, yebhuyyenavālikā. Daḍḍhāpi vuccati ajātā pathavī. Yopi paṃsupuñjo vā mattikāpuñjo vā omakacātumāsaṃ ovaṭṭho, ayampi vuccati ajātā pathavī.

‘Unborn earth’ is: pure rock, pure pebbles, pure potsherds, pure hard gravel, pure sand; with little dust, little clay; mostly rock, mostly pebbles, mostly potsherds, mostly hard gravel, mostly sand. Even fired earth is called ‘unborn earth’. Any heap of dust or heap of clay that has been rained on for less than four months is also called ‘unborn earth’.

Khaṇeyyāti [V 0.0051] sayaṃ khaṇati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should dig’ means: if one digs oneself, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Khaṇāpeyyāti aññaṃ āṇāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Sakiṃ āṇatto bahukampi khaṇati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should have dug’ means: if one commands another, there is an offense of pācittiya. If, having been commanded once, that person digs many times, there is an offense of pācittiya.

87. Pathaviyā pathavisaññī khaṇati vā khaṇāpeti vā, bhindati vā bhedāpeti vā, dahati vā dahāpeti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

87. In the case of earth, if one, perceiving it as earth, digs it or has it dug, breaks it or has it broken, burns it or has it burned, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Pathaviyā vematiko khaṇati vā khaṇāpeti vā, bhindati vā bhedāpeti vā, dahati vā dahāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In the case of earth, if one is doubtful, and digs it or has it dug, breaks it or has it broken, burns it or has it burned, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Pathaviyā apathavisaññī khaṇati vā khaṇāpeti vā, bhindati vā bhedāpeti vā, dahati [T 2.0231] vā dahāpeti vā, anāpatti.

In the case of earth, if one, perceiving it as non-earth, digs it or has it dug, breaks it or has it broken, burns it or has it burned, there is no offense.

Apathaviyā pathavisaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Apathaviyā vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Apathaviyā apathavisaññī, anāpatti.

In the case of non-earth, if one perceives it as earth, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. In the case of non-earth, if one is doubtful, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. In the case of non-earth, if one perceives it as non-earth, there is no offense.

88. Anāpatti – “imaṃ jāna, imaṃ dehi, imaṃ āhara, iminā attho, imaṃ kappiyaṃ karohī”ti bhaṇati, asañcicca, asatiyā, ajānantassa, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

88. There is no offense: if one says, “Know this, give this, bring this, this is needed, make this allowable”; if it is unintentional; if unmindful; for one who does not know; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Pathavīkhaṇanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

The tenth training rule, on digging the earth, is finished.

Musāvādavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter on False Speech.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for this is:

Musā [M 0.0051] omasapesuññaṃ, padaseyyāya ve duve;

Aññatra viññunā bhūtā, duṭṭhullāpatti khaṇanāti.

False speech, abusive speech, slander, word-by-word teaching, and two on sleeping together; teaching without a knowledgeable man, informing of an actual attainment, a grave offense, and digging.

2. Bhūtagāmavaggo

2. The Chapter on Plant Life.

1. Bhūtagāmasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The Training Rule on Plant Life.

89. Tena [T 2.0232][P 4.0034][V 0.0052] samayena buddho bhagavā āḷaviyaṃ viharati aggāḷave cetiye. Tena kho pana samayena āḷavakā bhikkhū navakammaṃ karontā rukkhaṃ chindantipi chedāpentipi. Aññataropi āḷavako bhikkhu rukkhaṃ chindati. Tasmiṃ rukkhe adhivatthā devatā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “mā, bhante, attano bhavanaṃ kattukāmo mayhaṃ bhavanaṃ chindī”ti. So bhikkhu anādiyanto chindi yeva, tassā ca devatāya dārakassa bāhuṃ ākoṭesi. Atha kho tassā devatāya etadahosi – “yaṃnnūnāhaṃ imaṃ bhikkhuṃ idheva jīvitā voropeyya”nti. Atha kho tassā devatāya etadahosi – “na kho metaṃ patirūpaṃ yāhaṃ imaṃ bhikkhuṃ idheva jīvitā voropeyyaṃ. Yannūnāhaṃ bhagavato etamatthaṃ āroceyya”nti. Atha kho sā devatā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. “Sādhu sādhu devate! Sādhu kho tvaṃ, devate, taṃ bhikkhuṃ jīvitā na voropesi. Sacajja tvaṃ, devate, taṃ bhikkhuṃ jīvitā voropeyyāsi, bahuñca tvaṃ, devate, apuññaṃ pasaveyyāsi. Gaccha tvaṃ, devate, amukasmiṃ okāse rukkho vivitto tasmiṃ upagacchā”ti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā rukkhaṃ chindissantipi chedāpessantipi ekindriyaṃ [T 2.0233] samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jīvaṃ viheṭhessantī”ti!

89. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling at Āḷavī in the Aggāḷava Shrine. Now at that time, the monks of Āḷavī, while engaged in new construction, were cutting down trees and having them cut down. A certain monk of Āḷavī was cutting down a tree. The goddess dwelling in that tree said to that monk: 'Venerable, wishing to make your own dwelling, do not cut down my dwelling.' That monk, not heeding, just kept cutting, and he struck the arm of the goddess's child. Then it occurred to that goddess: 'What if I were to deprive this monk of life right here?' Then it occurred to that goddess: 'It is not proper for me to deprive this monk of life right here. What if I were to inform the Blessed One of this matter?' Then that goddess approached the Blessed One; having approached, she informed the Blessed One of this matter. 'Good, good, goddess! It is good, goddess, that you did not deprive that monk of life. If today, goddess, you had deprived that monk of life, you would have produced much demerit. Go, goddess, in a certain place there is an unoccupied tree; go to that one.' People complained, criticized, and spread it about: 'How can the ascetics, the sons of the Sakyan, cut down a tree and have it cut down? The ascetics, the sons of the Sakyan, are harming a living being with one faculty!'

Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āḷavakā bhikkhū rukkhaṃ chindissantipi chedāpessantipī”ti…pe… “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, rukkhaṃ chindathāpi chedāpethāpī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, rukkhaṃ chindissathāpi, chedāpessathāpi! Jīvasaññino hi, moghapurisā, manussā rukkhasmiṃ, [M 0.0052] netaṃ moghapurisā appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those monks who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: 'How can the monks of Āḷavī cut down a tree and have it cut down?'… 'Is it true, monks, as it is said, that you cut down a tree and have it cut down?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… 'How indeed, foolish men, could you cut down a tree and have it cut down! Foolish men, people perceive that there is life in a tree. This, foolish men, is not for the faith of the faithless…' … 'And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:'

90. “Bhūtagāmapātabyatāya pācittiya”nti.

90. For the destruction of plant life, there is an offense of pācittiya.

91. Bhūtagāmo [V 0.0053] nāma pañca bījajātāni – mūlabījaṃ, khandhabījaṃ, phaḷubījaṃ, aggabījaṃ, bījabījameva bījabījañceva (itipi) pañcamaṃ.

91. 'Plant life' means five kinds of seeds: root-seed, stem-seed, joint-seed, tip-seed, and seed-seed itself as the fifth.

Mūlabījaṃ [P 4.0035] nāma – haliddi, siṅgiveraṃ, vacā, vacattaṃ, ativisā, kaṭukarohiṇī, usīraṃ, bhaddamūttakaṃ, yāni vā panaññānipi atthi mūle jāyanti, mūle sañjāyanti, etaṃ mūlabījaṃ nāma.

'Root-seed' means: turmeric, ginger, sweet flag, white sweet flag, ativisā, kaṭukarohiṇī, vetiver, bhaddamuttaka, or whatever else there is that grows from a root or originates well from a root—this is called 'root-seed'.

Khandhabījaṃ nāma – assattho, nigrodho, pilakkho, udumbaro, kacchako, kapitthano, yāni vā panaññānipi atthi khandhe jāyanti, khandhe sañjāyanti, etaṃ khandhabījaṃ nāma.

'Stem-seed' means: the assattha tree, the banyan tree, the pilakkha tree, the udumbara tree, the kacchaka tree, the kapitthana tree, or whatever else there is that grows from a stem or originates well from a stem—this is called 'stem-seed'.

Phaḷubījaṃ nāma – ucchu, veḷu, naḷo, yāni vā panaññānipi atthi pabbe jāyanti, pabbe [T 2.0234] sañjāyanti, etaṃ phaḷubījaṃ nāma.

'Joint-seed' means: sugarcane, bamboo, reeds, or whatever else there is that grows from a joint or originates well from a joint—this is called 'joint-seed'.

Aggabījaṃ nāma – ajjukaṃ, phaṇijjakaṃ, hiriveraṃ, yāni vā panaññānipi atthi agge jāyanti, agge sañjāyanti, etaṃ aggabījaṃ nāma.

'Tip-seed' means: ajjuka, phaṇijjaka, hirivera, or whatever else there is that grows from the tip or originates well from the tip—this is called 'tip-seed'.

Bījabījaṃ nāma – pubbaṇṇaṃ, aparaṇṇaṃ, yāni vā panaññānipi atthi bīje jāyanti, bīje sañjāyanti, etaṃ bījabījaṃ nāma.

'Seed-seed' means: early grain, later grain, or whatever else there is that grows from a seed or originates well from a seed—this is called 'seed-seed'.

92. Bīje bījasaññī chindati vā chedāpeti vā, bhindati vā bhedāpeti vā, pacati vā pacāpeti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Bīje vematiko chindati vā chedāpeti vā, bhindati vā bhedāpeti vā, pacati vā pacāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Bīje abījasaññī chindati vā chedāpeti vā, bhindati vā bhedāpeti vā, pacati vā pacāpeti vā, anāpatti. Abīje bījasaññī āpatti dukkaṭassa. Abīje vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Abīje abījasaññī, anāpatti.

92. If, perceiving it to be a seed, one cuts or causes it to be cut, breaks or causes it to be broken, or cooks or causes it to be cooked, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one is in doubt about it being a seed and one cuts or causes it to be cut, breaks or causes it to be broken, or cooks or causes it to be cooked, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If, perceiving it not to be a seed, one cuts or causes it to be cut, breaks or causes it to be broken, or cooks or causes it to be cooked, there is no offense. If one perceives what is not a seed to be a seed, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If one is in doubt about what is not a seed, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If one perceives what is not a seed not to be a seed, there is no offense.

93. Anāpatti – “imaṃ jāna, imaṃ dehi, imaṃ āhara, iminā attho, imaṃ kappiyaṃ karohī”ti bhaṇati, asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

93. There is no offense: if one says, “Know this, give this, bring this, this is needed, make this allowable;” if one acts unintentionally, unmindfully, or unknowingly; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Bhūtagāmasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The first training rule on plant life is concluded.

2. Aññavādakasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Training Rule on Speaking Otherwise.

94. Tena [T 2.0235][M 0.0053][V 0.0054] samayena buddho bhagavā kosambiyaṃ viharati ghositārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā channo anācāraṃ ācaritvā saṅghamajjhe āpattiyā anuyuñjīyamāno aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati – “ko āpanno, kiṃ āpanno, kismiṃ āpanno, kathaṃ āpanno, kaṃ bhaṇatha, kiṃ bhaṇathā”ti? Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā channo saṅghamajjhe āpattiyā anuyuñjīyamāno aññenaññaṃ paṭicarissati – ko āpanno, kiṃ āpanno, kismiṃ āpanno, kathaṃ āpanno, kaṃ bhaṇatha, kiṃ bhaṇathā”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, channa, saṅghamajjhe āpattiyā anuyuñjīyamāno aññenaññaṃ paṭicarasi – ko āpanno, kiṃ āpanno, kismiṃ āpanno, kathaṃ āpanno, kaṃ bhaṇatha, kiṃ bhaṇathāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, saṅghamajjhe āpattiyā anuyuñjīyamāno aññenaññaṃ paṭicarissasi – ko āpanno, kiṃ āpanno, kismiṃ āpanno, kathaṃ āpanno, kaṃ bhaṇatha, kiṃ bhaṇathāti! Netaṃ, [P 4.0036] moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno aññavādakaṃ ropetu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave[T 2.0236], ropetabbaṃ. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

94. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Kosambī at the Ghositārāma. Now at that time, the Venerable Channa, having committed improper conduct, when being questioned about an offense in the midst of the Saṅgha, concealed one matter with another, saying: “Who has committed an offense? What offense has been committed? Regarding what matter has an offense been committed? In what manner has an offense been committed? Of whom do you speak? What do you say?” Those bhikkhus who were of few desires… criticized, found fault, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the Venerable Channa, when being questioned about an offense in the midst of the Saṅgha, conceal one matter with another, saying: ‘Who has committed an offense? What offense has been committed? Regarding what matter has an offense been committed? In what manner has an offense been committed? Of whom do you speak? What do you say?’” … “Is it true, as is said, Channa, that when being questioned about an offense in the midst of the Saṅgha, you conceal one matter with another, saying: ‘Who has committed an offense? What offense has been committed? Regarding what matter has an offense been committed? In what manner has an offense been committed? Of whom do you speak? What do you say?’” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “Worthless man, how indeed can you, when being questioned about an offense in the midst of the Saṅgha, conceal one matter with another, saying: ‘Who has committed an offense? What offense has been committed? Regarding what matter has an offense been committed? In what manner has an offense been committed? Of whom do you speak? What do you say?’ This, worthless man, is not for inspiring faith in the faithless… After rebuking him… and having given a discourse on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus: “In that case, bhikkhus, let the Saṅgha impose on the bhikkhu Channa the formal act for speaking otherwise. And, bhikkhus, it should be imposed thus: The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhu:

95. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ channo bhikkhu saṅghamajjhe āpattiyā anuyuñjīyamāno aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno aññavādakaṃ ropeyya. Esā ñatti.

95. “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu Channa, when being questioned about an offense in the midst of the Saṅgha, conceals one matter with another. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should impose on the bhikkhu Channa the formal act for speaking otherwise. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ channo bhikkhu saṅghamajjhe āpattiyā anuyuñjīyamāno aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati. Saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno aññavādakaṃ ropeti. Yassāyasmato khamati channassa bhikkhuno aññavādakassa ropanā, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu Channa, when being questioned about an offense in the midst of the Saṅgha, conceals one matter with another. The Saṅgha imposes on the bhikkhu Channa the formal act for speaking otherwise. To whichever venerable the imposition of the formal act for speaking otherwise on the bhikkhu Channa is agreeable, he should be silent; to whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.”

“Ropitaṃ saṅghena channassa bhikkhuno aññavādakaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The formal act for speaking otherwise has been imposed by the Saṅgha on the bhikkhu Channa. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I take this to be.”

Atha [M 0.0054][V 0.0055] kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ channaṃ anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā dubbharatāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

Then the Blessed One, having rebuked the Venerable Channa in many ways for being difficult to support… said: “And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Aññavādake pācittiya”nti.

“In speaking otherwise, there is a pācittiya offense.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And thus this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhus.

96. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā channo saṅghamajjhe āpattiyā anuyuñjīyamāno “aññenaññaṃ paṭicaranto – “āpattiṃ āpajjissāmī”ti tuṇhībhūto saṅghaṃ viheseti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā channo saṅghamajjhe āpattiyā anuyuñjīyamāno tuṇhībhūto saṅghaṃ vihesessatī”ti…pe… [T 2.0237] saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, channa, saṅghamajjhe āpattiyā anuyuñjīyamāno tuṇhībhūto saṅghaṃ vihesesīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, saṅghamajjhe āpattiyā anuyuñjīyamāno tuṇhībhūto saṅghaṃ vihesessasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno vihesakaṃ ropetu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, ropetabbaṃ. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

96. Now at that time, the Venerable Channa, when being questioned about an offense in the midst of the Saṅgha, thinking, “If I conceal one matter with another, I will commit an offense,” remained silent and vexed the Saṅgha. Those bhikkhus who were of few desires… criticized, found fault, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the Venerable Channa, when being questioned about an offense in the midst of the Saṅgha, remain silent and vex the Saṅgha?” … “Is it true, as is said, Channa, that when being questioned about an offense in the midst of the Saṅgha, you remain silent and vex the Saṅgha?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “Worthless man, how indeed can you, when being questioned about an offense in the midst of the Saṅgha, remain silent and vex the Saṅgha? This, worthless man, is not for inspiring faith in the faithless… After rebuking him… and having given a discourse on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus: “In that case, bhikkhus, let the Saṅgha impose on the bhikkhu Channa the formal act for vexation. And, bhikkhus, it should be imposed thus: The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhu:

97. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ channo bhikkhu saṅghamajjhe āpattiyā anuyuñjīyamāno tuṇhībhūto saṅghaṃ viheseti. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno vihesakaṃ ropeyya. Esā ñatti.

97. “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu Channa, when being questioned about an offense in the midst of the Saṅgha, remains silent and vexes the Saṅgha. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should impose on the bhikkhu Channa the formal act for vexation. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ channo bhikkhu saṅghamajjhe āpattiyā anuyuñjīyamāno tuṇhībhūto saṅghaṃ viheseti. Saṅgho channassa bhikkhuno vihesakaṃ ropeti. Yassāyasmāto khamati channassa bhikkhuno vihesakassa ropanā, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu Channa, when being questioned about an offense in the midst of the Saṅgha, remains silent and vexes the Saṅgha. The Saṅgha imposes on the bhikkhu Channa the formal act for vexation. To whichever venerable the imposition of the formal act for vexation on the bhikkhu Channa is agreeable, he should be silent; to whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.”

“Ropitaṃ saṅghena channassa bhikkhuno vihesakaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The formal act for vexation has been imposed by the Saṅgha on the bhikkhu Channa. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I take this to be.”

Atha [V 0.0056] kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ channaṃ anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā dubbharatāya…pe… [T 2.0238] evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

Then the Blessed One, having rebuked the Venerable Channa in many ways for being difficult to support… said: “And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

98. “Aññavādake [M 0.0055] vihesake pācittiya”nti.

98. “In speaking otherwise and in vexation, there is a pācittiya offense.”

99. Aññavādako [P 4.0037] nāma saṅghamajjhe vatthusmiṃ vā āpattiyā vā anuyuñjīyamāno taṃ na kathetukāmo taṃ na ugghāṭetukāmo aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati – “ko āpanno, kiṃ āpanno, kismiṃ āpanno, kathaṃ āpanno, kaṃ bhaṇatha, kiṃ bhaṇathā”ti. Eso aññavādako nāma.

99. ‘Speaking otherwise’ is defined as: when being questioned in the midst of the Saṅgha about a matter or an offense, being unwilling to speak about it, being unwilling to reveal it, one conceals one matter with another, saying: “Who has committed an offense? What offense has been committed? Regarding what matter has an offense been committed? In what manner has an offense been committed? Of whom do you speak? What do you say?” This is called ‘speaking otherwise’.

Vihesako nāma saṅghamajjhe vatthusmiṃ vā āpattiyā vā anuyuñjīyamāno taṃ na kathetukāmo taṃ na ugghāṭetukāmo tuṇhībhūto saṅghaṃ viheseti. Eso vihesako nāma.

‘Vexing’ means when being questioned in the midst of the Saṅgha about a matter or an offense, being unwilling to speak about it, being unwilling to reveal it, one remains silent and vexes the Saṅgha. This is called ‘vexing’.

100. Āropite aññavādake saṅghamajjhe vatthusmiṃ vā āpattiyā vā anuyuñjīyamāno taṃ na kathetukāmo taṃ na ugghāṭetukāmo aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati – “ko āpanno, kiṃ āpanno, kismiṃ āpanno, kathaṃ āpanno, kaṃ bhaṇatha, kiṃ bhaṇathā”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Āropite vihesake saṅghamajjhe vatthusmiṃ vā āpattiyā vā anuyuñjīyamāno taṃ na kathetukāmo taṃ na ugghāṭetukāmo tuṇhībhūto saṅghaṃ viheseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ropite aññavādake saṅghamajjhe vatthusmiṃ vā āpattiyā vā anuyuñjīyamāno taṃ na kathetukāmo taṃ na ugghāṭetukāmo aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati – “ko āpanno, kiṃ āpanno, kismiṃ āpanno, kathaṃ āpanno, kaṃ bhaṇatha, kiṃ bhaṇathā”ti, āpatti pācittiyassa[T 2.0239]. Ropite vihesake saṅghamajjhe vatthusmiṃ vā āpattiyā vā anuyuñjīyamāno taṃ na kathetukāmo taṃ na ugghāṭetukāmo tuṇhībhūto saṅghaṃ viheseti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

100. When the formal act concerning evasive speech has not been imposed, if he, being questioned in the midst of the Saṅgha regarding a matter or an offense, and being unwilling to answer about it or to reveal it, conceals one matter with another, saying: 'Who has incurred an offense? What offense has been incurred? In what matter has an offense been incurred? In what manner has an offense been incurred? To whom do you speak? What do you speak?', there is an offense of wrong-doing. When the formal act concerning vexation has not been imposed, if he, being questioned in the midst of the Saṅgha regarding a matter or an offense, and being unwilling to answer about it or to reveal it, remains silent and vexes the Saṅgha, there is an offense of wrong-doing. When the formal act concerning evasive speech has been imposed, if he, being questioned in the midst of the Saṅgha regarding a matter or an offense, and being unwilling to answer about it or to reveal it, conceals one matter with another, saying: 'Who has incurred an offense? What offense has been incurred? In what matter has an offense been incurred? In what manner has an offense been incurred? To whom do you speak? What do you speak?', there is an offense entailing expiation. When the formal act concerning vexation has been imposed, if he, being questioned in the midst of the Saṅgha regarding a matter or an offense, and being unwilling to answer about it or to reveal it, remains silent and vexes the Saṅgha, there is an offense entailing expiation.

101. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññī aññavādake vihesake, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme vematiko aññavādake vihesake, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññī aññavādake vihesake, āpatti pācittiyassa. Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

101. In a lawful formal act, perceiving it as a lawful formal act, for evasive speech or vexation, there is an offense entailing expiation. In a lawful formal act, being doubtful, for evasive speech or vexation, there is an offense entailing expiation. In a lawful formal act, perceiving it as an unlawful formal act, for evasive speech or vexation, there is an offense entailing expiation. In an unlawful formal act, perceiving it as a lawful formal act, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In an unlawful formal act, being doubtful, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In an unlawful formal act, perceiving it as an unlawful formal act, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

102. Anāpatti [M 0.0056] ajānanto pucchati, gilāno vā na katheti; “saṅghassa bhaṇḍanaṃ vā [V 0.0057] kalaho vā viggaho vā vivādo vā bhavissatī”ti na katheti; “saṅghabhedo vā saṅgharāji vā bhavissatī”ti na katheti; “adhammena vā vaggena vā nakammārahassa vā kammaṃ karissatī”ti na katheti; ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

102. There is no offense if one asks out of ignorance; or if one is sick and does not speak; or if one does not speak thinking, 'There will be quarreling, strife, contention, or dispute for the Saṅgha'; or if one does not speak thinking, 'There will be a schism in the Saṅgha or a fissure in the Saṅgha'; or if one does not speak thinking, 'They will perform a formal act unlawfully, or by an incomplete group, or on one unworthy of the act'; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Aññavādakasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The second training rule on evasive speech is finished.

3. Ujjhāpanakasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Training Rule on Causing Disparagement

103. Tena [T 2.0240] samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā dabbo mallaputto saṅghassa senāsanañca paññapeti bhattāni ca uddisati. Tena kho pana samayena mettiyabhūmajakā mettiyabhūmmajakā (sī. syā.) bhikkhū navakā ceva honti appapuññā ca[P 4.0038]. Yāni saṅghassa lāmakāni senāsanāni tāni tesaṃ pāpuṇanti lāmakāni ca bhattāni. Te āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ bhikkhū ujjhāpenti – “chandāya dabbo mallaputto senāsanaṃ paññapeti, chandāya ca bhattāni uddisatī”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ bhikkhū ujjhāpessantī”ti…pe… “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ bhikkhū ujjhāpethā”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ bhikkhū ujjhāpessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

103. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Veḷuvana, the Kalandakanivāpa. Now at that time, the Venerable Dabba Mallaputta was assigning lodgings and allocating meals for the Saṅgha. Now at that time, the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus were junior and of little merit. Whatever inferior lodgings of the Saṅgha there were, those fell to them, and inferior meals. They caused the bhikkhus to know contemptuously of the Venerable Dabba Mallaputta, saying: “Dabba Mallaputta assigns lodgings out of partiality, and he allocates meals out of partiality.” Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… they criticized, denigrated, and spoke disparagingly, saying: “For what reason indeed would the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus cause the bhikkhus to know contemptuously of the Venerable Dabba Mallaputta?” … “Is it true, as is said, bhikkhus, that you cause the bhikkhus to know contemptuously of Dabba Mallaputta?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “For what reason indeed, worthless men, would you cause the bhikkhus to know contemptuously of Dabba Mallaputta! This, worthless men, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced…” “…And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus—”

“Ujjhāpanake pācittiya”nti.

“For causing disparagement, there is an offense entailing expiation.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule was laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

104. Tena [T 2.0241] kho pana samayena mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū – “bhagavatā ujjhāpanakaṃ paṭikkhitta”nti, “ettāvatā bhikkhū sossantī”ti vihesissantīti (itipi) bhikkhūnaṃ sāmantā āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ khiyyanti – “chandāya dabbo mallaputto senāsanaṃ [M 0.0057] paññapeti, chandāya ca bhattāni uddisatī”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ khiyyissantī”ti…pe… “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ khiyyathā”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi [V 0.0058] buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ khiyyissatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

104.
