Now at that time, the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus, thinking, “Causing disparagement has been prohibited by the Blessed One,” and, “By this much, the bhikkhus will be troubled,” denigrated the Venerable Dabba Mallaputta in the vicinity of the bhikkhus, saying, “Dabba Mallaputta assigns lodgings out of partiality, and he allocates meals out of partiality.” Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… they criticized, denigrated, and spoke disparagingly, saying, “For what reason indeed would the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka bhikkhus denigrate the Venerable Dabba Mallaputta?”… “Is it true, as is said, bhikkhus, that you denigrate Dabba Mallaputta?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “For what reason indeed, worthless men, would you denigrate Dabba Mallaputta! This, worthless men, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced…” “…And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus—”

105. “Ujjhāpanake khiyyanake pācittiya”nti.

105. “For causing disparagement or for denigrating, there is an offense entailing expiation.”

106. Ujjhāpanakaṃ nāma upasampannaṃ saṅghena sammataṃ senāsanapaññāpakaṃ vā bhattuddesakaṃ vā yāgubhājakaṃ vā phalabhājakaṃ vā khajjabhājakaṃ vā appamattakavissajjakaṃ vā avaṇṇaṃ kattukāmo, ayasaṃ kattukāmo, maṅkukattukāmo, upasampannaṃ ujjhāpeti vā khiyyati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññī ujjhāpanake khiyyanake āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme vematiko ujjhāpanake khiyyanake āpatti [T 2.0242] pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññī ujjhāpanake khiyyanake āpatti pācittiyassa.

106. Causing disparagement means: wishing to cause disrepute, wishing to cause ill-fame, wishing to cause embarrassment to a fully ordained one appointed by the Saṅgha as an assigner of lodgings, or a distributor of meals, or a distributor of gruel, or a distributor of fruit, or a distributor of hard food, or a dispenser of minor things, one causes that fully ordained one to be disparaged or one denigrates them; this is an offense entailing expiation. Regarding a lawful formal act, if one perceives it as a lawful formal act, for causing disparagement or for denigrating, it is an offense entailing expiation. Regarding a lawful formal act, if one is uncertain, for causing disparagement or for denigrating, it is an offense entailing expiation. Regarding a lawful formal act, if one perceives it as not a lawful formal act, for causing disparagement or for denigrating, it is an offense entailing expiation.

Anupasampannaṃ ujjhāpeti vā khiyyati vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Upasampannaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ senāsanapaññāpakaṃ vā bhattuddesakaṃ vā yāgubhājakaṃ vā phalabhājakaṃ vā khajjabhājakaṃ vā appamattakavissajjakaṃ vā avaṇṇaṃ kattukāmo, ayasaṃ kattukāmo, maṅkukattukāmo, upasampannaṃ vā anupasampannaṃ vā ujjhāpeti vā khiyyati vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannaṃ saṅghena sammataṃ vā asammataṃ vā senāsanapaññāpakaṃ vā bhattuddesakaṃ vā yāgubhājakaṃ vā phalabhājakaṃ vā khajjabhājakaṃ vā appamattakavissajjakaṃ vā avaṇṇaṃ kattukāmo, ayasaṃ kattukāmo, maṅkukattukāmo, upasampannaṃ vā anupasampannaṃ vā ujjhāpeti vā khiyyati [P 4.0039] vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññī āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one causes one who is not fully ordained to be disparaged or denigrates them, there is an offense of wrong conduct. If, wishing to cause lack of praise, wishing to cause ill-fame, wishing to make them crestfallen, to a fully ordained one not appointed by the Saṅgha as an assigner of lodgings, a distributor of meals, a distributor of gruel, a distributor of fruit, a distributor of hard food, or a dispenser of minor things, one causes a fully ordained one or one not fully ordained to be disparaged or denigrates them, there is an offense of wrong conduct. If, wishing to cause lack of praise, wishing to cause ill-fame, wishing to make them crestfallen, to one not fully ordained, whether appointed or not appointed by the Saṅgha as an assigner of lodgings, a distributor of meals, a distributor of gruel, a distributor of fruit, a distributor of hard food, or a dispenser of minor things, one causes a fully ordained one or one not fully ordained to be disparaged or denigrates them, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding an illegitimate formal act, if one perceives it as a legitimate formal act, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding an illegitimate formal act, if one is uncertain, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding an illegitimate formal act, if one perceives it as an illegitimate formal act, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

107. Anāpatti pakatiyā chandā dosā mohā bhayā karontaṃ ujjhāpeti vā khiyyati vā, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

107. There is no offense for causing one who acts by nature out of desire, aversion, delusion, or fear to be disparaged or for denigrating them; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Ujjhāpanakasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The third training rule on causing disparagement is finished.

4. Paṭhamasenāsanasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The First Training Rule on Lodgings

108. Tena [T 2.0243][M 0.0058][V 0.0059] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū hemantike kāle ajjhokāse senāsanaṃ paññapetvā kāyaṃ otāpentā kāle ārocite taṃ pakkamantā neva uddhariṃsu na uddharāpesuṃ, anāpucchā pakkamiṃsu. Senāsanaṃ ovaṭṭhaṃ hoti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathaṃ hi nāma bhikkhū ajjhokāse senāsanaṃ paññapetvā taṃ pakkamantā neva uddharissanti na uddharāpessanti, anāpucchā pakkamissanti, senāsanaṃ ovaṭṭha”nti! Atha kho te bhikkhū te anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhū ajjhokāse…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

108. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, during the winter season, monks, having prepared lodgings in the open air and warming their bodies, when the time was announced, departed without putting them away or having them put away; they departed without asking permission. The lodging was rained upon. Those monks who were of few desires… complained, grumbled, and criticized, saying: “How indeed can monks, having prepared lodgings in the open air, depart without putting them away or having them put away, and depart without asking permission, so that the lodging is rained upon?” Then those monks, having criticized them in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, monks, that monks in the open air…?” … “And thus, monks, you should set forth this training rule:

109. “Yo pana bhikkhu saṅghikaṃ mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā bhisiṃ vā kocchaṃ vā ajjhokāse [T 2.0244] santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā taṃ pakkamanto neva uddhareyya na uddharāpeyya, anāpucchaṃ vā gaccheyya, pācittiya”nti.

109. “Whatever monk, having spread out or having had spread out a bed, a stool, a mattress, or a cushion belonging to the Saṅgha in the open air, should, when departing, neither put it away nor have it put away, or should depart without asking permission, there is a pācittiya offense.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

Thus this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.

110. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ajjhokāse vasitvā kālasseva senāsanaṃ abhiharanti. Addasā kho bhagavā te bhikkhū kālasseva senāsanaṃ abhiharante. Disvāna etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭha māse avassikasaṅkete vasituṃ avassikasaṃkete (itipi) maṇḍape [P 4.0040] vā rukkhamūle vā yattha kākā vā kulalā vā na ūhadanti tattha senāsanaṃ nikkhipitu”nti.

110. Now at that time, monks, having dwelt in the open air, would bring back their lodgings very early. The Blessed One saw those monks bringing back their lodgings very early. Having seen this, on this occasion and in this connection, he gave a talk on the Dhamma and addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow you to place lodgings for eight months in a place designated as not rainy, in a pavilion or at the foot of a tree where crows or kites do not defecate.”

111. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

111. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever sort… ‘Monk’ means… in this sense, this is what is intended by ‘monk’.

Saṅghikaṃ nāma saṅghassa dinnaṃ hoti pariccattaṃ.

‘Belonging to the Saṅgha’ means what has been given to the Saṅgha, what has been relinquished.

Mañco [V 0.0060] nāma cattāro mañcā – masārako, bundikābaddho, kuḷīrapādako, āhaccapādako.

‘A bed’ means four kinds of beds: a masāraka, a bundikābaddha, a kuḷīrapādaka, and an āhaccapādaka.

Pīṭhaṃ [M 0.0059] nāma cattāri pīṭhāni – masārakaṃ, bundikābaddhaṃ, kuḷīrapādakaṃ, āhaccapādakaṃ.

‘A stool’ means four kinds of stools: a masāraka, a bundikābaddha, a kuḷīrapādaka, and an āhaccapādaka.

Bhisi nāma pañca bhisiyo – uṇṇabhisi, coḷabhiti, vākabhisi, tiṇabhisi, paṇṇabhisi.

‘A mattress’ means five kinds of mattresses: a mattress stuffed with wool, a mattress stuffed with coarse cloth, a mattress stuffed with bark-fibre, a mattress stuffed with grass, and a mattress stuffed with leaves.

Kocchaṃ nāma – vākamayaṃ vā usīramayaṃ vā muñjamayaṃ vā pabbajamayaṃ babbajamayaṃ (sī.) vā anto saṃveṭhetvā baddhaṃ hoti.

‘A cushion’ means one made of bark-fibre, or of vetiver grass, or of muñja grass, or of pabbaja grass, which is rolled up inside and bound.

Santharitvāti sayaṃ santharitvā.

‘Having spread it out’ means having spread it out oneself.

Santharāpetvāti aññaṃ santharāpetvā. Anupasampannaṃ santharāpeti, tassa [T 2.0245] palibodho. Upasampannaṃ santharāpeti, santhārakassa santhatassa (itipi) palibodho.

‘Having had it spread out’ means having had another spread it out. If one has it spread out by one who is not fully ordained, the responsibility is his. If one has it spread out by one who is fully ordained, the responsibility belongs to the one who spreads it out.

Taṃ pakkamanto neva uddhareyyāti na sayaṃ uddhareyya.

‘When departing, he should not put it away’ means he should not put it away himself.

Na uddharāpeyyāti na aññaṃ uddharāpeyya.

‘Nor should he have it put away’ means he should not have another put it away.

Anāpucchaṃ vā gaccheyyāti bhikkhuṃ vā sāmaṇeraṃ vā ārāmikaṃ vā anāpucchā majjhimassa purisassa leḍḍupātaṃ atikkamantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Or should depart without asking permission’ means: for one who departs without asking permission of a monk, a novice, or a monastery attendant, upon crossing the distance of a clod-throw by a man of average build, there is a pācittiya offense.

112. Saṅghike saṅghikasaññī ajjhokāse santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā taṃ pakkamanto neva uddhareyya na uddharāpeyya anāpucchaṃ vā gaccheyya, āpatti pācittiyassa. Saṅghike vematiko…pe… saṅghike puggalikasaññī ajjhokāse santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā taṃ pakkamanto neva uddhareyya na uddharāpeyya, anāpucchaṃ vā gaccheyya, āpatti pācittiyassa.

112. Regarding what belongs to the Saṅgha, if one perceives it as belonging to the Saṅgha, and having spread it out or having had it spread out in the open air, when departing, one neither puts it away nor has it put away, or departs without asking permission, there is a pācittiya offense. Regarding what belongs to the Saṅgha, if one is in doubt… there is a pācittiya offense. Regarding what belongs to the Saṅgha, if one perceives it as belonging to an individual, and having spread it out or having had it spread out in the open air, when departing, one neither puts it away nor has it put away, or departs without asking permission, there is a pācittiya offense.

Cimilikaṃ vā uttarattharaṇaṃ vā bhūmattharaṇaṃ vā taṭṭikaṃ vā cammakhaṇḍaṃ vā pādapuñchaniṃ vā [V 0.0061] phalakapīṭhaṃ vā ajjhokāse santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā taṃ pakkamanto neva uddhareyya na uddharāpeyya, anāpucchaṃ vā gaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Puggalike saṅghikasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Puggalike vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Puggalike puggalikasaññī aññassa puggalike, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Attano puggalike anāpatti.

If one spreads out or has spread out in the open air a coarse cloth cover, an upper cover, a ground cover, a mat, a piece of hide, a foot-wiper, or a board-stool, and when departing, one neither puts it away nor has it put away, or departs without asking permission, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding what belongs to an individual, if one perceives it as belonging to the Saṅgha, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding what belongs to an individual, if one is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding what belongs to an individual, if one perceives it as belonging to an individual, when it is the property of another individual, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding one's own property, there is no offense.

113. Anāpatti [T 2.0246][M 0.0060] uddharitvā gacchati, uddharāpetvā gacchati, āpucchaṃ gacchati, otāpento gacchati, kenaci palibuddhaṃ hoti, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

113. There is no offense if one departs having put it away; if one departs having had it put away; if one departs having asked permission; if one departs while sunning it; if one is hindered by something; in times of calamity; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Paṭhamasenāsanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.

The First Training Rule on Lodgings, the fourth, is finished.

5. Dutiyasenāsanasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Second Training Rule Concerning Lodgings

114. Tena [T 2.0247][P 4.0041] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū sahāyakā honti. Te vasantāpi ekatova vasanti, pakkamantāpi ekatova pakkamanti. Te aññatarasmiṃ saṅghike vihāre seyyaṃ santharitvā taṃ pakkamantā neva uddhariṃsu na uddharāpesuṃ, anāpucchā pakkamiṃsu. Senāsanaṃ upacikāhi khāyitaṃ hoti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū saṅghike vihāre seyyaṃ santharitvā taṃ pakkamantā neva uddharissanti na uddharāpessanti, anāpucchā pakkamissanti, senāsanaṃ upacikāhi khāyita”nti! Atha kho te bhikkhū sattarasavaggiye bhikkhū anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū saṅghike vihāre seyyaṃ santharitvā taṃ pakkamantā neva uddhariṃsu na uddharāpesuṃ, anāpucchā pakkamiṃsu, senāsanaṃ upacikāhi khāyita”nti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā saṅghike vihāre seyyaṃ santharitvā taṃ pakkamantā neva uddharissanti na uddharāpessanti, anāpucchā pakkamissanti, senāsanaṃ upacikāhi khāyitaṃ! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana[T 2.0248], bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

114. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the monks known as the group-of-seventeen were companions. When dwelling, they dwelt together; when departing, they departed together. In a certain monastery belonging to the Sangha, having spread out bedding, when departing, they neither put it away themselves nor had it put away, and they departed without asking leave. The lodging was eaten by termites. Those monks who were of few desires... they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How is it that the monks of the group-of-seventeen, having spread out bedding in a monastery belonging to the Sangha, when departing, neither put it away themselves nor had it put away, and departed without asking leave? The lodging was eaten by termites!” Then those monks, having rebuked the monks of the group-of-seventeen in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One... “Is it true, it is said, monks, that the monks of the group-of-seventeen, having spread out bedding in a monastery belonging to the Sangha, when departing, neither put it away themselves nor had it put away, and departed without asking leave, and the lodging was eaten by termites?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... “How is it, monks, that those foolish men, having spread out bedding in a monastery belonging to the Sangha, when departing, neither put it away themselves nor had it put away, and departed without asking leave? The lodging was eaten by termites! Monks, this is not for the confidence of the unconvinced... And so, monks, you should recite this training rule in this way:

115. “Yo pana bhikkhu saṅghike vihāre seyyaṃ santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā taṃ pakkamanto neva uddhareyya na uddharāpeyya, anāpucchaṃ vā gaccheyya, pācittiya”nti.

115. “Whatever monk, in a monastery belonging to the Sangha, having spread out bedding himself or having had it spread out, when departing, should neither put it away himself nor have it put away, or should go without asking leave, it is a pācittiya offense.”

116. Yo [M 0.0061][V 0.0062] panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

116. As to ‘whatever’: whoever, of whatever sort... As to ‘monk’: ... in this sense, this is what is meant by ‘monk’.

Saṅghiko nāma vihāro saṅghassa dinno hoti pariccatto.

A monastery belonging to the Sangha, so-called, is one that has been given to the Sangha, has been relinquished.

Seyyaṃ nāma bhisi, cimilikā uttarattharaṇaṃ, bhūmattharaṇaṃ, taṭṭikā, cammakhaṇḍo, nisīdanaṃ, paccattharaṇaṃ, tiṇasanthāro, paṇṇasanthāro.

Bedding, so-called, is: a mattress, a coarse cloth spread, an upper covering, a ground covering, a mat of woven strips, a piece of hide, a sitting cloth, a bedspread, a grass spread, or a leaf spread.

Santharitvāti sayaṃ santharitvā.

‘Having spread out’: having spread it out oneself.

Santharāpetvāti aññaṃ santharāpetvā.

‘Having had it spread out’: having had another spread it out.

Taṃ pakkamanto neva uddhareyyāti na sayaṃ uddhareyya.

‘When departing, should neither put it away’: should not put it away oneself.

Na uddharāpeyyāti na aññaṃ uddharāpeyya.

‘Nor have it put away’: should not have another put it away.

Anāpucchaṃ vā gaccheyyāti bhikkhuṃ vā sāmaṇeraṃ vā ārāmikaṃ [P 4.0042] vā anāpucchā parikkhittassa ārāmassa parikkhepaṃ atikkamantassa āpatti pācittiyassa. Aparikkhittassa ārāmassa upacāraṃ atikkamantassa āpatti pācittiyassa. Saṅghike saṅghikasaññī seyyaṃ santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā taṃ pakkamanto neva uddhareyya na uddharāpeyya, anāpucchaṃ vā gaccheyya, āpatti pācittiyassa. Saṅghike vematiko seyyaṃ santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā taṃ pakkamanto neva uddhareyya na uddharāpeyya, anāpucchaṃ vā gaccheyya, āpatti pācittiyassa. Saṅghike puggalikasaññī seyyaṃ santharitvā vā santharāpetvā [T 2.0249] vā taṃ pakkamanto neva uddhareyya na uddharāpeyya, anāpucchaṃ vā gaccheyya, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Or should go without asking leave’: for one who, without asking leave of a monk, a novice, or a monastery attendant, crosses the enclosure of an enclosed monastery, there is a pācittiya offense. For one who crosses the precinct of an unenclosed monastery, there is a pācittiya offense. In what belongs to the Sangha, being perceptive that it belongs to the Sangha, having spread out bedding or having had it spread out, when departing, should one neither put it away himself nor have it put away, or should one go without asking leave, there is a pācittiya offense. In what belongs to the Sangha, being doubtful, having spread out bedding or having had it spread out, when departing, should one neither put it away himself nor have it put away, or should one go without asking leave, there is a pācittiya offense. In what belongs to the Sangha, being perceptive that it is personal property, having spread out bedding or having had it spread out, when departing, should one neither put it away himself nor have it put away, or should one go without asking leave, there is a pācittiya offense.

117. Vihārassa upacāre vā upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ vā maṇḍape vā rukkhamūle vā seyyaṃ santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā taṃ pakkamanto neva uddhareyya na uddharāpeyya, anāpucchaṃ vā gaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā vihāre vā vihārassūpacāre vā upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ vā maṇḍape vā rukkhamūle vā santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā taṃ pakkamanto neva uddhareyya na uddharāpeyya, anāpucchaṃ vā gaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

117. In the precinct of a monastery, or in an attendance hall, or in a pavilion, or at the root of a tree, having spread out bedding or having had it spread out, when departing, should one neither put it away himself nor have it put away, or should one go without asking leave, there is a dukkaṭa offense. A couch or a chair, in a monastery, or in the precinct of a monastery, or in an attendance hall, or in a pavilion, or at the root of a tree, having set it up or having had it set up, when departing, should one neither put it away himself nor have it put away, or should one go without asking leave, there is a dukkaṭa offense.

Puggalike [V 0.0063] saṅghikasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Puggalike vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Puggalike puggalikasaññī aññassa puggalike āpatti dukkaṭassa. Attano puggalike anāpatti.

In what is personal property, being perceptive that it belongs to the Sangha, there is a dukkaṭa offense. In what is personal property, being doubtful, there is a dukkaṭa offense. In what is personal property, being perceptive that it is personal property, if it is the personal property of another, there is a dukkaṭa offense. In one's own personal property, there is no offense.

118. Anāpatti [M 0.0062] uddharitvā gacchati, uddharāpetvā gacchati, āpucchaṃ gacchati, kenaci palibuddhaṃ hoti, sāpekkho gantvā tattha ṭhito āpucchati, kenaci palibuddho hoti, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

118. There is no offense: if one goes having put it away; if one goes having had it put away; if one goes having asked leave; if one is obstructed by some danger; if, going with concern, one stands there and asks leave; if one is obstructed by some danger; in times of calamity; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Dutiyasenāsanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Second Training Rule Concerning Lodgings, the fifth, is finished.

6. Anupakhajjasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Training Rule on Encroaching

119. Tena [T 2.0250] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū varaseyyāyo palibundhenti, therā bhikkhū vuṭṭhāpenti ettha te iti kammapadaṃ ūnaṃ viya dissati. Atha kho chabbaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kena nu kho mayaṃ upāyena idheva vassaṃ vaseyyāmā”ti? Atha kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhū there bhikkhū anupakhajja seyyaṃ kappenti – yassa sambādho bhavissati so pakkamissatīti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū there bhikkhū anupakhajja seyyaṃ kappessantī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū chabbaggiye bhikkhū anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ [P 4.0043]…pe… “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, there bhikkhū anupakhajja seyyaṃ kappethā”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, there bhikkhū anupakhajja seyyaṃ kappessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

119. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time, the monks of the group of six were obstructing the choice sleeping places, and the senior monks made them get up. Then this thought occurred to the monks of the group of six: “By what means might we dwell for the rains-residence right here?” Then the monks of the group of six, encroaching upon the senior monks, prepared sleeping places, thinking, “Whoever finds it crowded will depart.” Those monks who were of few wishes… criticized, censured, and complained: “How indeed can the monks of the group of six, encroaching upon the senior monks, prepare sleeping places?” Then those monks, having rebuked the monks of the group of six in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, monks, that you, encroaching upon the senior monks, prepared sleeping places?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “Foolish men, how indeed can you, encroaching upon the senior monks, prepare sleeping places? This, foolish men, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

120. “Yo pana bhikkhu saṅghike vihāre jānaṃ pubbupagataṃ bhikkhuṃ anupakhajja seyyaṃ kappeyya – yassa sambādho bhavissati so pakkamissatī’ti, etadeva paccayaṃ karitvā anaññaṃ, pācittiya”nti.

120. “Whatever monk, in a monastery belonging to the Sangha, knowingly encroaches upon a monk who has previously arrived and prepares a sleeping place—thinking, ‘Whoever finds it crowded will depart,’—making just this the reason and no other, it is an offense of expiation.”

121. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ 2.0251 atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

121. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever sort… ‘Monk’ means: …in this sense, this one is intended as ‘monk’.

Saṅghiko [V 0.0064] nāma vihāro saṅghassa dinno hoti pariccatto.

A monastery called ‘belonging to the Sangha’ is one that has been given, has been relinquished to the Sangha.

Jānāti [M 0.0063] nāma vuḍḍhoti jānāti, gilānoti jānāti, saṅghena dinnoti jānāti.

‘Knows’ means: he knows, ‘He is senior;’ he knows, ‘He is sick;’ he knows, ‘It has been given by the Sangha.’

Anupakhajjāti anupavisitvā.

‘Encroaching’ means: having entered closely.

Seyyaṃ kappeyyāti mañcassa vā pīṭhassa vā pavisantassa vā nikkhamantassa vā upacāre seyyaṃ santharati vā santharāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Abhinisīdati vā abhinipajjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Prepares a sleeping place’ means: in the vicinity of a bed or a bench, or of one entering or leaving, if one spreads out a sleeping place or has it spread out, it is an offense of wrong-doing. If one sits down upon it or lies down upon it, it is an offense of expiation.

Etadeva paccayaṃ karitvā anaññanti na añño koci paccayo hoti anupakhajja seyyaṃ kappetuṃ.

‘Making just this the reason and no other’ means: there is no other reason for preparing a sleeping place by encroaching.

122. Saṅghike saṅghikasaññī anupakhajja seyyaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Saṅghike vematiko anupakhajja seyyaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Saṅghike puggalikasaññī anupakhajja seyyaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

122. In what belongs to the Sangha, being perceptive of it as belonging to the Sangha, if one encroaches and prepares a sleeping place, it is an offense of expiation. In what belongs to the Sangha, being in doubt, if one encroaches and prepares a sleeping place, it is an offense of expiation. In what belongs to the Sangha, being perceptive of it as belonging to an individual, if one encroaches and prepares a sleeping place, it is an offense of expiation.

Mañcassa vā pīṭhassa vā pavisantassa vā nikkhamantassa vā upacāraṃ ṭhapetvā seyyaṃ santharati vā santharāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Abhinisīdati vā abhinipajjati vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Vihārassa upacāre vā upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ vā maṇḍape vā rukkhamūle vā ajjhokāse vā seyyaṃ santharati vā santharāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Abhinisīdati vā abhinippajjati vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Puggalike saṅghikasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Puggalike vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Puggalike puggalikasaññī aññassa puggalike āpatti dukkaṭassa[T 2.0252]. Attano puggalike anāpatti.

Leaving aside the vicinity of a bed or a bench, or of one entering or leaving, if one spreads out a sleeping place or has it spread out, it is an offense of wrong-doing. If one sits down upon it or lies down upon it, it is an offense of wrong-doing. In the vicinity of a monastery, or in an assembly hall, or in a pavilion, or at the foot of a tree, or in the open, if one spreads out a sleeping place or has it spread out, it is an offense of wrong-doing. If one sits down upon it or lies down upon it, it is an offense of wrong-doing. In what is personal property, if one is perceptive of it as belonging to the Sangha, it is an offense of wrong-doing. In what is personal property, if one is in doubt, it is an offense of wrong-doing. In what is personal property, being perceptive of it as personal property, if it is the personal property of another, it is an offense of wrong-doing. In one's own personal property, there is no offense.

123. Anāpatti gilāno pavisati, sītena vā uṇhena vā pīḷito pavisati, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

123. There is no offense: if a sick person enters; if one oppressed by cold or heat enters; in calamities; for one who is insane; for the first-doer.

Anupakhajjasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The sixth training rule on encroaching is finished.

7. Nikkaḍḍhanasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Training Rule on Expulsion.

124. Tena [T 2.0253][P 4.0044][V 0.0065] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū aññataraṃ paccantimaṃ mahāvihāraṃ paṭisaṅkharonti – “idha mayaṃ vassaṃ vasissāmā”ti[M 0.0064]. Addasaṃsu kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sattarasavaggiye bhikkhū vihāraṃ paṭisaṅkharonte. Disvāna evamāhaṃsu – “ime, āvuso, sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū vihāraṃ paṭisaṅkharonti. Handa ne vuṭṭhāpessāmā”ti! Ekacce evamāhaṃsu – “āgamethāvuso, yāva paṭisaṅkharonti; paṭisaṅkhate vuṭṭhāpessāmā”ti.

124. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, in the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the monks from the group-of-seventeen were repairing a certain large, outlying monastery, thinking, “Here we will spend the rains-residence.” The monks from the group-of-six saw the monks from the group-of-seventeen repairing the monastery. Having seen them, they said thus: “Friends, these monks from the group-of-seventeen are repairing a monastery. Come, let us make them leave!” Some said thus: “Wait, friends, for as long as they are repairing it; when it has been repaired, we will make them leave.”

Atha kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sattarasavaggiye bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “uṭṭhethāvuso, amhākaṃ vihāro pāpuṇātī”ti. “Nanu, āvuso, paṭikacceva paṭigacceva (sī.) ācikkhitabbaṃ, mayañcaññaṃ paṭisaṅkhareyyāmā”ti. “Nanu, āvuso, saṅghiko vihāro”ti? “Āmāvuso, saṅghiko vihāro”ti. “Uṭṭhethāvuso, amhākaṃ vihāro pāpuṇātī”ti. “Mahallako, āvuso, vihāro. Tumhepi vasatha, mayampi vasissāmā”ti. “Uṭṭhethāvuso, amhākaṃ vihāro pāpuṇātī”ti kupitā anattamanā gīvāyaṃ gahetvā nikkaḍḍhanti. Te nikkaḍḍhīyamānā rodanti. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “kissa tumhe, āvuso, rodathā”ti? “Ime, āvuso, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kupitā anattamanā amhe saṅghikā vihārā nikkaḍḍhantī”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti [T 2.0254] khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kupitā anattamanā bhikkhū saṅghikā vihārā nikkaḍḍhissantī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū chabbaggiye bhikkhū anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, kupitā anattamanā bhikkhū saṅghikā vihārā nikkaḍḍhathā”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, kupitā anattamanā bhikkhū saṅghikā vihārā nikkaḍḍhissatha? Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

Then the monks from the group-of-six said this to the monks from the group-of-seventeen: “Get up, friends, the monastery falls to us.” “Friends, should you not have told us earlier, so that we could have repaired another monastery?” “Friends, is it not a monastery belonging to the Sangha?” “Yes, friends, it is a monastery belonging to the Sangha.” “Get up, friends, the monastery falls to us.” “Friends, the monastery is large. You too can stay, and we too will stay.” “Get up, friends, the monastery falls to us.” Being angry and displeased, they grabbed them by the neck and expelled them. As they were being expelled, they wept. The monks said thus: “Friends, why do you weep?” “Friends, these monks from the group-of-six, being angry and displeased, are expelling us from a monastery belonging to the Sangha.” Those monks who were of few desires… they criticized, scorned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the monks from the group-of-six, being angry and displeased, expel monks from a monastery belonging to the Sangha!” Then those monks, having rebuked the monks from the group-of-six in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Monks, is it true that you, being angry and displeased, expel monks from a monastery belonging to the Sangha?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “Foolish men, how indeed could you, being angry and displeased, expel monks from a monastery belonging to the Sangha? Foolish men, this is not for inspiring faith in the faithless… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

125. “Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ kupito anattamano saṅghikā vihārā nikkaḍḍheyya vā nikkaḍḍhāpeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

125. “Whatever monk, being angry and displeased, should expel or cause to be expelled a monk from a monastery belonging to the Sangha, it is an offense entailing confession.”

126. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

126. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘monk’ means… in this context, this is what is intended by ‘monk’.

Bhikkhunti [P 4.0045][V 0.0066] aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ.

‘A monk’ means: another monk.

Kupito [M 0.0065] anattamanoti anabhiraddho āhatacitto khilajāto.

‘Angry, displeased’ means: not delighted, with an afflicted mind, resentful.

Saṅghiko nāma vihāro saṅghassa dinno hoti pariccatto.

A monastery ‘belonging to the Sangha’ means: it has been given to the Sangha, it has been relinquished.

Nikkaḍḍheyyāti gabbhe gahetvā pamukhaṃ nikkaḍḍhati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Pamukhe gahetvā bahi nikkaḍḍhati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ekena payogena bahukepi dvāre atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should expel’ means: grabbing him in an inner chamber, he expels him to the entrance; there is an offense entailing confession. Grabbing him at the entrance, he expels him outside; there is an offense entailing confession. With a single effort, he makes him pass through many doors; there is an offense entailing confession.

Nikkaḍḍhāpeyyāti aññaṃ āṇāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa dukkaṭassa (katthaci). Sakiṃ āṇatto bahukepi dvāre atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should cause to be expelled’ means: he orders another; there is an offense entailing confession. The one who was ordered once makes him pass through many doors; there is an offense entailing confession.

127. Saṅghike [T 2.0255] saṅghikasaññī kupito anattamano nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Saṅghike vematiko kupito anattamano nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Saṅghike puggalikasaññī kupito anattamano nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

127. In what belongs to the Sangha, being percipient of it as belonging to the Sangha, being angry and displeased, he expels or causes to be expelled; there is an offense entailing confession. In what belongs to the Sangha, being doubtful, being angry and displeased, he expels or causes to be expelled; there is an offense entailing confession. In what belongs to the Sangha, being percipient of it as belonging to an individual, being angry and displeased, he expels or causes to be expelled; there is an offense entailing confession.

Tassa parikkhāraṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Vihārassa upacārā vā upaṭṭhānasālāya vā maṇḍapā vā rukkhamūlā vā ajjhokāsā vā nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Tassa parikkhāraṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannaṃ vihārā vā vihārassa upacārā vā upaṭṭhānasālāya vā maṇḍapā vā rukkhamūlā vā ajjhokāsā vā nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Tassa parikkhāraṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

He expels or causes to be expelled that monk’s requisites; there is an offense of wrong conduct. From the precincts of a monastery, or from a meeting hall, or from a pavilion, or from the root of a tree, or from an open space, he expels or causes to be expelled; there is an offense of wrong conduct. He expels or causes to be expelled that monk’s requisites; there is an offense of wrong conduct. An unordained person, from a monastery, or from the precincts of a monastery, or from a meeting hall, or from a pavilion, or from the root of a tree, or from an open space, he expels or causes to be expelled; there is an offense of wrong conduct. He expels or causes to be expelled that person’s requisites; there is an offense of wrong conduct.

Puggalike saṅghikasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Puggalike vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Puggalike puggalikasaññī aññassa puggalike āpatti dukkaṭassa. Attano puggalike anāpatti.

In what belongs to an individual, being percipient of it as belonging to the Sangha, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In what belongs to an individual, being doubtful, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In what belongs to an individual, being percipient of it as belonging to an individual, if it is the property of another individual, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In what belongs to oneself as an individual, there is no offense.

128. Anāpatti alajjiṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, tassa parikkhāraṃ nikkaḍḍhati [V 0.0067] vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, ummattakaṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, tassa parikkhāraṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā [T 2.0256] nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, bhaṇḍanakārakaṃ kalahakārakaṃ vivādakārakaṃ bhassakārakaṃ saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakaṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti [M 0.0066] vā, tassa parikkhāraṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, antevāsikaṃ vā saddhivihārikaṃ vā na sammā vattantaṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, tassa parikkhāraṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

128. There is no offense: if he expels or causes to be expelled a shameless person, or if he expels or causes to be expelled that person’s requisites; if he expels or causes to be expelled an insane person, or if he expels or causes to be expelled that person’s requisites; if he expels or causes to be expelled one who is quarrelsome, who causes strife, who causes disputes, who is argumentative, who creates legal issues in the Sangha, or if he expels or causes to be expelled that person’s requisites; if he expels or causes to be expelled a resident pupil or a co-resident who is not behaving properly, or if he expels or causes to be expelled that person’s requisites; for one who is insane, for the first offender.

Nikkaḍḍhanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.

The seventh training rule on expulsion is finished.

8. Vehāsakuṭisikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Training Rule on the Upper-Story Dwelling

129. Tena [T 2.0257] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena [P 4.0046] dve bhikkhū saṅghike vihāre uparivehāsakuṭiyā viharanti?. Eko heṭṭhā viharati viharanti, eko heṭṭhā (?), eko upari. Uparimo bhikkhu āhaccapādakaṃ mañcaṃ sahasā abhinisīdi. Mañcapādo nippatitvā patitvā (syā.) heṭṭhimassa bhikkhuno matthake avatthāsi. So bhikkhu vissaramakāsi. Bhikkhū upadhāvitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavocuṃ – “kissa tvaṃ, āvuso, vissaramakāsī”ti? Atha kho so bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhu saṅghike vihāre uparivehāsakuṭiyā āhaccapādakaṃ mañcaṃ sahasā abhinisīdissatī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū taṃ bhikkhuṃ anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, bhikkhu, saṅghike vihāre uparivehāsakuṭiyā āhaccapādakaṃ mañcaṃ sahasā abhinisīdasī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, saṅghike vihāre uparivehāsakuṭiyā āhaccapādakaṃ mañcaṃ sahasā abhinisīdissasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

129. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, two monks were dwelling in a monastery belonging to the Sangha, in an upper-story dwelling. One dwelt below, and one dwelt above. The monk above sat down abruptly on a bed with inserted legs. A leg of the bed slipped out and struck the head of the monk below. That monk cried out. Monks ran up and said to that monk, “Venerable, why did you cry out?” Then that monk told the monks of this matter. Those monks who were of few wishes… they criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying, “How indeed could a monk, in a monastery belonging to the Sangha, in an upper-story dwelling, sit down abruptly on a bed with inserted legs?” Then those monks, having rebuked that monk in many ways, told this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, it is said, monk, that in a monastery belonging to the Sangha, in an upper-story dwelling, you sat down abruptly on a bed with inserted legs?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “Worthless man, how indeed could you, in a monastery belonging to the Sangha, in an upper-story dwelling, sit down abruptly on a bed with inserted legs? This is not, worthless man, for the pleasing of those not yet pleased… And so, monks, you should set forth this training rule thus:

130. “Yo pana bhikkhu saṅghike vihāre uparivehāsakuṭiyā āhaccapādakaṃ mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ [T 2.0258] vā abhinisīdeyya vā abhinipajjeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

130. “Whatever monk, in an upper-story dwelling in a monastery belonging to the Sangha, should forcefully sit down or forcefully lie down on a bed or a bench with inserted legs, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

131. Yo [M 0.0067][V 0.0068] panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

131. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever sort… ‘Monk’ means… in this sense, this is the monk who is intended.

Saṅghiko nāma vihāro saṅghassa dinno hoti pariccatto.

What is called ‘belonging to the Sangha’ is a monastery that has been given to the Sangha, has been relinquished.

Vehāsakuṭi nāma majjhimassa purisassa asīsaghaṭṭā.

What is called a ‘high-ceilinged dwelling’ is a dwelling in which the head of a man of medium height does not touch.

Āhaccapādako nāma mañco aṅge vijjhitvā ṭhito hoti. Āhaccapādakaṃ nāma pīṭhaṃ aṅge vijjhitvā ṭhitaṃ hoti.

What is called a ‘bed with inserted legs’ is one that stands by having its legs pierced into its frame. What is called a ‘bench with inserted legs’ is one that stands by having its legs pierced into its frame.

Abhinisīdeyyāti tasmiṃ abhinisīdati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should forcefully sit down’ means: if one forcefully sits down on it, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Abhinipajjeyyāti tasmiṃ abhinipajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should forcefully lie down’ means: if one forcefully lies down on it, it is an offense of pācittiya.

132. Saṅghike saṅghikasaññī uparivehāsakuṭiyā āhaccapādakaṃ mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā abhinisīdati vā abhinipajjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Saṅghike vematiko…pe… saṅghike puggalikasaññī uparivehāsakuṭiyā āhaccapādakaṃ mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā abhinisīdati vā abhinipajjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

132. In what belongs to the Sangha, perceiving it as belonging to the Sangha, if one forcefully sits down or forcefully lies down on a bed or a bench with inserted legs in an upper-story dwelling, it is an offense of pācittiya. In what belongs to the Sangha, being uncertain… In what belongs to the Sangha, perceiving it as personal property, if one forcefully sits down or forcefully lies down on a bed or a bench with inserted legs in an upper-story dwelling, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Puggalike saṅghikasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Puggalike vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Puggalike puggalikasaññī aññassa puggalike, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Attano puggalike, anāpatti.

In what is personal property, perceiving it as belonging to the Sangha, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. In what is personal property, being uncertain, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. In what is personal property, perceiving it as personal property, if it is the personal property of another, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. In one’s own personal property, there is no offense.

133. Anāpatti – avehāsakuṭiyā sīsaghaṭṭāya heṭṭhā aparibhogaṃ [T 2.0259] hoti, padarasañcitaṃ hoti, paṭāṇi dinnā hoti, tasmiṃ ṭhito gaṇhati vā laggeti vā, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

133. There is no offense: in a dwelling that is not high-ceilinged; in one where the head touches; if the space below is not used for living; if it is laid with planks; if a peg is applied; if, standing on it, one takes or hangs something; for one who is insane; for the originator of the matter.

Vehāsakuṭisikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The eighth training rule, concerning an upper-story dwelling, is concluded.

9. Mahallakavihārasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Training Rule Concerning a Large Dwelling

134. Tena [T 2.0260][P 4.0047][V 0.0069] samayena buddho bhagavā kosambiyaṃ viharati ghositārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato channassa upaṭṭhāko mahāmatto āyasmato channassa vihāraṃ kārāpeti. Atha kho āyasmā channo katapariyositaṃ vihāraṃ punappunaṃ chādāpeti, punappunaṃ [M 0.0068] lepāpeti. Atibhārito vihāro paripati. Atha kho āyasmā channo tiṇañca kaṭṭhañca saṃkaḍḍhanto aññatarassa brāhmaṇassa yavakhettaṃ dūsesi. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma bhadantā amhākaṃ yavakhettaṃ dūsessantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tassa brāhmaṇassa ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā channo katapariyositaṃ vihāraṃ punappunaṃ chādāpessati, punappunaṃ lepāpessati, atibhārito vihāro paripatī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ channaṃ anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, channa, katapariyositaṃ vihāraṃ punappunaṃ chādāpesi, punappunaṃ lepāpesi, atibhārito vihāro paripatī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, katapariyositaṃ vihāraṃ punappunaṃ chādāpessasi, punappunaṃ lepāpessasi[T 2.0261], atibhārito vihāro paripati! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

134. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Kosambī in Ghosita’s Park. Now at that time a great minister, an attendant of the Venerable Channa, was having a dwelling built for the Venerable Channa. Then the Venerable Channa repeatedly had the completed dwelling roofed and repeatedly had it plastered. The dwelling, being overburdened, collapsed. Then the Venerable Channa, while gathering grass and wood, damaged a certain brahmin’s barley field. Then that brahmin complained, grumbled, and protested, saying, “How can these venerable ones damage our barley field?” The monks heard that brahmin complaining, grumbling, and protesting. Those monks who were of few wishes… complained, grumbled, and protested, saying, “How can the Venerable Channa repeatedly have a completed dwelling roofed and repeatedly have it plastered, so that the dwelling, being overburdened, collapses?” Then those monks, having rebuked the Venerable Channa in many ways, informed the Blessed One of this matter… “Is it true, Channa, that you repeatedly had a completed dwelling roofed and repeatedly had it plastered, so that the dwelling, being overburdened, collapses?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “Foolish man, how can you repeatedly have a completed dwelling roofed and repeatedly have it plastered, so that the dwelling, being overburdened, collapses? This, foolish man, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

135. “Mahallakaṃ pana bhikkhunā vihāraṃ kārayamānena yāvadvārakosā aggaḷaṭṭhapanāya ālokasandhiparikammāya dvatticchadanassa pariyāya appaharite ṭhitena adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ. Tato ce uttariṃ appaharitepi ṭhito adhiṭṭhaheyya pācittiya”nti.

135. “But when a monk is having a large dwelling built, while standing in a place without green crops, he may supervise up to the door-frame, for the placing of the bolt, for the finishing of the window-opening, and for two or three layers of roofing. If, beyond that, he should supervise, even while standing in a place without green crops, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

136. Mahallako nāma vihāro sassāmiko vuccati.

136. A large dwelling, it is said, is one that has a sponsor.

Vihāro nāma ullitto vā hoti avalitto vā ullittāvalitto vā.

A dwelling, it is said, is one that is plastered on the inside, or plastered on the outside, or plastered on both the inside and outside.

Kārayamānenāti karonto vā kārāpento vā.

‘Having it built’ means either building it oneself or having it built.

Yāva dvārakosāti piṭṭhasaṅghāṭassa pīṭhasaṃghāṭassa (itipi), piṭṭhisaṅghāṭassa (syā.) samantā hatthapāsā.

‘Up to the door-frame’ means up to a distance of two cubits and a span all around the door-frame.

Aggaḷaṭṭhapanāyāti [V 0.0070] dvāraṭṭhapanāya.

‘For the placing of the bolt’ means for the placing of the door-leaf.

Ālokasandhiparikammāyāti vātapānaparikammāya setavaṇṇaṃ kāḷavaṇṇaṃ gerukaparikammaṃ mālākammaṃ latākammaṃ makaradantakaṃ pañcapaṭikaṃ.

‘For the finishing of the window-opening’ means for the finishing of the window: white color, black color, finishing with red ochre, flower work, creeper work, makara-tooth work, and five-finger-mark work.

Dvatticchadanassa [P 4.0048][M 0.0069] pariyāyaṃ appaharite ṭhitena adhiṭṭhātabbanti – haritaṃ nāma pubbaṇṇaṃ aparaṇṇaṃ. Sace harite ṭhito adhiṭṭhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Maggena chādentassa dve magge adhiṭṭhahitvā tatiyaṃ maggaṃ āṇāpetvā pakkamitabbaṃ. Pariyāyena chādentassa dve pariyāye adhiṭṭhahitvā tatiyaṃ pariyāyaṃ āṇāpetvā pakkamitabbaṃ.

‘A turn for a roof of two or three layers should be supervised while standing in a place without green crops’: ‘Green’ is defined as early grain or later grain. If one supervises while standing in a green place, there is a dukkaṭa offense. For one who is roofing by rows, having supervised two rows, one should give the order for the third row and depart. For one who is roofing in layers, having supervised two layers, one should give the order for the third layer and depart.

137. Tato ce uttari appaharitepi ṭhito adhiṭṭhaheyyāti iṭṭhakāya 2.0262 chādentassa iṭṭhakiṭṭhakāya āpatti pācittiyassa. Silāya chādentassa silāya silāya āpatti pācittiyassa. Sudhāya chādentassa piṇḍe piṇḍe āpatti pācittiyassa. Tiṇena chādentassa karaḷe karaḷe āpatti pācittiyassa. Paṇṇena chādentassa paṇṇe paṇṇe āpatti pācittiyassa.

137. ‘If, beyond that, he should supervise while standing even in a place without green crops’: For one roofing with bricks, for each and every brick, there is a pācittiya offense. For one roofing with stone slabs, for each and every stone slab, there is a pācittiya offense. For one roofing with plaster, for each and every lump of plaster, there is a pācittiya offense. For one roofing with thatch, for each and every bundle of thatch, there is a pācittiya offense. For one roofing with leaves, for each and every leaf, there is a pācittiya offense.

Atirekadvattipariyāye atirekasaññī adhiṭṭhāti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Atirekadvattipariyāye vematiko adhiṭṭhāti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Atirekadvattipariyāye ūnakasaññī adhiṭṭhāti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

In a case exceeding two or three layers, if one supervises perceiving it as exceeding, there is a pācittiya offense. In a case exceeding two or three layers, if one supervises while being uncertain, there is a pācittiya offense. In a case exceeding two or three layers, if one supervises perceiving it as less, there is a pācittiya offense.

Ūnakadvattipariyāye atirekasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ūnakadvattipariyāye vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ūnakadvattipariyāye ūnakasaññī, anāpatti.

In a case of less than two or three layers, if one supervises perceiving it as exceeding, there is a dukkaṭa offense. In a case of less than two or three layers, if one supervises while being uncertain, there is a dukkaṭa offense. In a case of less than two or three layers, if one supervises perceiving it as less, there is no offense.

138. Anāpatti dvattipariyāye, ūnakadvattipariyāye, leṇe, guhāya, tiṇakuṭikāya, aññassatthāya, attano dhanena, vāsāgāraṃ ṭhapetvā sabbattha anāpatti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

138. There is no offense for two or three layers; for less than two or three layers; in a rock-shelter; in a cave; in a grass hut; for the benefit of another; with one's own wealth; excepting a dwelling place, there is no offense in all other cases; for one who is insane; and for the first offender.

Mahallakavihārasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.

The ninth training rule, concerning a large dwelling, is finished.

10. Sappāṇakasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Training Rule on Water Containing Living Beings

139. Tena [T 2.0263][V 0.0071] samayena buddho bhagavā āḷaviyaṃ viharati aggāḷave cetiye. Tena kho pana samayena āḷavakā bhikkhū navakammaṃ karontā jānaṃ sappāṇakaṃ udakaṃ tiṇampi mattikampi siñcantipi siñcāpentipi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āḷavakā [M 0.0070] bhikkhū jānaṃ sappāṇakaṃ udakaṃ tiṇampi mattikampi siñcissantipi siñcāpessantipī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū āḷavake bhikkhū anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, jānaṃ sappāṇakaṃ udakaṃ tiṇampi mattikampi siñcathapi siñcāpethapī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, jānaṃ sappāṇakaṃ udakaṃ tiṇampi mattikampi siñcissathapi siñcāpessathapi! Netaṃ, [P 4.0049] moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

139. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Āḷavī, at the Aggāḷava Shrine. Now at that time the bhikkhus of Āḷavī, while doing new construction work, knowingly poured or caused to be poured water containing living beings on grass and clay. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… criticized, condemned, and spread disparaging remarks: “How can the bhikkhus of Āḷavī knowingly pour or cause to be poured water containing living beings on grass and clay?” Then those bhikkhus, having rebuked the bhikkhus of Āḷavī in many ways, reported the matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that you knowingly pour or cause to be poured water containing living beings on grass and clay?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How can you, foolish men, knowingly pour or cause to be poured water containing living beings on grass and clay? This, foolish men, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus—”

140. “Yo pana bhikkhu jānaṃ sappāṇakaṃ udakaṃ tiṇaṃ vā mattikaṃ vā siñceyya vā siñcāpeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

140. “Whatever bhikkhu should knowingly pour water containing living beings, or cause it to be poured, on grass or clay, it is a pācittiya offense.”

141. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

141. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever kind of… ‘bhikkhu’ means: … in this sense, this is the intended bhikkhu.

Jānāti nāma jānaṃ nāma (syā.) sāmaṃ vā jānāti aññe vā tassa ārocenti.

‘Knows’ means: one knows by oneself, or others inform him.

Siñceyyāti sayaṃ siñcati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should pour’ means: one pours by oneself; it is a pācittiya offense.

Siñcāpeyyāti [T 2.0264] aññaṃ āṇāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa āpatti dukkaṭassa (katthaci). Sakiṃ āṇatto bahukampi siñcati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should cause to be poured’ means: one commands another; it is a pācittiya offense. If one who is commanded once pours many times, it is a pācittiya offense.

142. Sappāṇake sappāṇakasaññī tiṇaṃ vā mattikaṃ vā siñcati vā siñcāpeti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Sappāṇake vematiko tiṇaṃ vā mattikaṃ vā siñcati vā siñcāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sappāṇake appāṇakasaññī tiṇaṃ vā mattikaṃ vā siñcati [V 0.0072] vā siñcāpeti vā, anāpatti. Appāṇake sappāṇakasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Appāṇake vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Appāṇake appāṇakasaññī, anāpatti.

142. If, in what contains living beings, one is percipient of it as containing living beings and pours or causes it to be poured on grass or clay, it is a pācittiya offense. If, in what contains living beings, one is doubtful and pours or causes it to be poured on grass or clay, it is a dukkaṭa offense. If, in what contains living beings, one is percipient of it as not containing living beings and pours or causes it to be poured on grass or clay, there is no offense. If, in what does not contain living beings, one is percipient of it as containing living beings, it is a dukkaṭa offense. If, in what does not contain living beings, one is doubtful, it is a dukkaṭa offense. If, in what does not contain living beings, one is percipient of it as not containing living beings, there is no offense.

143. Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

143. There is no offense for one who acts unintentionally, for one who is unmindful, for one who does not know, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Sappāṇakasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

The tenth training rule on water containing living beings is finished.

Bhūtagāmavaggo dutiyo.

The Second Chapter on Plant Life is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of it:

Bhūtaṃ [M 0.0071] aññāya ujjhāyaṃ, pakkamantena te duve;

Pubbe nikkaḍḍhanāhacca, dvāraṃ sappāṇakena cāti.

Plant Life, Evasive Speech, and Disparaging; the two on Departing; Previously being there, Evicting, and Forcefully sitting; the Door, and With Living Beings.

3. Ovādavaggo

3. The Chapter on Exhortation

1. Ovādasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The Training Rule on Exhortation

144. Tena [T 2.0265] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena therā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo ovadantā lābhino honti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṃ. Atha kho chabbaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “etarahi kho, āvuso, therā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo ovadantā lābhino honti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṃ. Handāvuso, mayampi bhikkhuniyo ovadāmā”ti. Atha kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – “amhepi, [P 4.0050] bhaginiyo, upasaṅkamatha; mayampi ovadissāmā”ti.

144. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the elder monks, while exhorting the nuns, were recipients of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick. Then this thought occurred to the monks of the group of six: “Friends, at present the elder monks, while exhorting the nuns, are recipients of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick. Come, friends, let us also exhort the nuns.” Then the monks of the group of six, having approached the nuns, said this: “Sisters, approach us also; we too will exhort.”

Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo yena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā chabbaggiye bhikkhū abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Atha kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhunīnaṃ [V 0.0073] parittaññeva dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā divasaṃ tiracchānakathāya vītināmetvā uyyojesuṃ – “gacchatha, bhaginiyo”ti. Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhagavā etadavoca – “kacci, bhikkhuniyo, ovādo iddho ahosī”ti? “Kuto, bhante, ovādo iddho bhavissati! Ayyā chabbaggiyā parittaññeva dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā divasaṃ tiracchānakathāya vītināmetvā uyyojesu”nti. Atha kho bhagavā tā bhikkhuniyo dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi[T 2.0266]. Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkamiṃsu.

Then those nuns approached the place where the monks of the group of six were. Having approached, they paid homage to the monks of the group of six and sat down to one side. Then the monks of the group of six, having given the nuns only a brief Dhamma talk, spent the day in worldly talk and then dismissed them, saying, “Go, sisters.” Then those nuns approached the place where the Blessed One was. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. The Blessed One said this to those nuns standing to one side: “Nuns, was the exhortation successful?” “Venerable Sir, how could the exhortation be successful? The venerable ones of the group of six, having given only a brief Dhamma talk, spent the day in worldly talk and then dismissed us.” Then the Blessed One instructed, established, roused, and gladdened those nuns with a Dhamma talk. Then those nuns, having been instructed, established, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping him on their right, and departed.

Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā chabbaggiye bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīnaṃ [M 0.0072] parittaññeva dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā divasaṃ tiracchānakathāya vītināmetvā uyyojethā”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, bhikkhunīnaṃ parittaññeva dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā divasaṃ tiracchānakathāya vītināmetvā uyyojessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhunovādakaṃ sammannituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbo. Paṭhamaṃ bhikkhu yācitabbo. Yācitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having had the Saṅgha of monks assemble, questioned the monks of the group of six: “Is it true, it is said, monks, that having given the nuns only a brief Dhamma talk, you spent the day in worldly talk and then dismissed them?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them…: “How indeed, you foolish men, could you, having given the nuns only a brief Dhamma talk, spend the day in worldly talk and then dismiss them! This is not, foolish men, for the confidence of the unconfident…” Having rebuked them… and having given a Dhamma talk, he addressed the monks: “I allow, monks, the appointment of an exhorter of nuns. And in this way, monks, he is to be appointed. First, a monk should be requested. Having requested, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:

145. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ bhikkhunovādakaṃ sammanneyya. Esā ñatti.

145. “Venerable Sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should appoint the monk named so-and-so as an exhorter of nuns. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ bhikkhunovādakaṃ sammannati. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno bhikkhunovādakassa sammuti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable Sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. The Saṅgha appoints the monk named so-and-so as an exhorter of nuns. To whichever venerable one the appointment of the monk named so-and-so as an exhorter of nuns is agreeable, he should be silent; to whom it is not agreeable, he should speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ [T 2.0267] bhikkhunovādakaṃ sammannati. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno bhikkhunovādakassa sammuti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“For a second time I state this matter… and for a third time I state this matter: Venerable Sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. The Saṅgha appoints the monk named so-and-so as an exhorter of nuns. To whichever venerable one the appointment of the monk named so-and-so as an exhorter of nuns is agreeable, he should be silent; to whom it is not agreeable, he should speak.”

“Sammato [V 0.0074] saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu bhikkhunovādako. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The monk named so-and-so has been appointed by the Saṅgha as an exhorter of nuns. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I take it.”

Atha kho bhagavā chabbaggiye bhikkhū anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā [P 4.0051] dubbharatāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

Then the Blessed One, having rebuked the monks of the group of six in many ways for being difficult to support… and so on… And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

146. “Yo pana bhikkhu asammato bhikkhuniyo ovadeyya pācittiya”nti.

146. “Whatever monk, not having been appointed, should exhort the nuns, it is an offense requiring expiation (`pācittiya`).”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

In this way, this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.

147. Tena kho pana samayena therā bhikkhū sammatā bhikkhuniyo ovadantā tatheva lābhino honti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṃ. Atha kho chabbaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “etarahi kho, āvuso, therā bhikkhū sammatā bhikkhuniyo ovadantā tatheva [M 0.0073] lābhino honti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṃ. Handāvuso, mayampi nissīmaṃ gantvā aññamaññaṃ bhikkhunovādakaṃ sammannitvā bhikkhuniyo ovadāmā”ti. Atha kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhū nissīmaṃ gantvā aññamaññaṃ bhikkhunovādakaṃ sammannitvā bhikkhuniyo upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – “mayampi, bhaginiyo, sammatā. Amhepi upasaṅkamatha. Mayampi ovadissāmā”ti.

147. Now at that time, the elder monks who had been appointed, while exhorting the nuns, were likewise recipients of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick. Then this thought occurred to the monks of the group of six: “Friends, at present the elder monks who have been appointed, while exhorting the nuns, are likewise recipients of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick. Come, friends, let us also, having gone outside the boundary and having appointed one another as exhorters of nuns, exhort the nuns.” Then the monks of the group of six, having gone outside the boundary and having appointed one another as exhorters of nuns, approached the nuns and said this: “Sisters, we too have been appointed. Approach us also. We too will exhort.”

Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo yena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā chabbaggiye bhikkhū abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Atha kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhū [T 2.0268] bhikkhunīnaṃ parittaññeva dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā divasaṃ tiracchānakathāya vītināmetvā uyyojesuṃ – “gacchatha bhaginiyo”ti. Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhagavā etadavoca – “kacci, bhikkhuniyo, ovādo iddho ahosī”ti? “Kuto, bhante, ovādo iddho bhavissati! Ayyā chabbaggiyā parittaññeva dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā divasaṃ tiracchānakathāya vītināmetvā uyyojesu”nti.

Then those nuns approached the monks of the group of six. Having approached, they paid homage to the monks of the group of six and sat down to one side. Then the monks of the group of six, having given the nuns only a brief Dhamma talk, spent the day in worldly talk and then dismissed them, saying, “Go, sisters.” Then those nuns approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. The Blessed One said this to those nuns standing to one side: “Nuns, was the instruction successful?” “Venerable sir, how could the instruction be successful? The venerable ones of the group of six, having given only a brief Dhamma talk, spent the day in worldly talk and then dismissed us.”

Atha kho bhagavā tā bhikkhuniyo dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi…pe… atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā [V 0.0075] padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkamiṃsu. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā chabbaggiye bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīnaṃ parittaññeva dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā divasaṃ tiracchānakathāya vītināmetvā uyyojethā”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, bhikkhunīnaṃ parittaññeva dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā divasaṃ tiracchānakathāya vītināmetvā uyyojessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ bhikkhunovādakaṃ sammannituṃ. Sīlavā hoti[T 2.0269], pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu; bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā [M 0.0074] pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasā anupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā; ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso; kalyāṇavāco hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo; yebhuyyena bhikkhunīnaṃ piyo hoti manāpo; paṭibalo hoti bhikkhuniyo ovadituṃ; na kho panetaṃ pana taṃ (?) bhagavantaṃ uddissa pabbajitāya kāsāyavatthavasanāya garudhammaṃ ajjhāpannapubbo hoti; vīsativasso vā hoti atirekavīsativasso vā – anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imehi aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ bhikkhunovādakaṃ sammannitu”nti.

Then the Blessed One instructed those nuns with a talk on the Dhamma... Then those nuns, having been instructed, established, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a talk on the Dhamma, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping him to their right, and departed. Then the Blessed One, on that occasion, in connection with that matter, having convened the Sangha of monks, questioned the monks of the group of six: “Is it true, monks, that having given only a brief talk on the Dhamma to the nuns, you spent the day in worldly talk and then dismissed them?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, worthless men, could you, having given only a brief talk on the Dhamma to the nuns, spend the day in worldly talk and then dismiss them? This, worthless men, is not for the confidence of the unconfident…” Having rebuked them… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow a monk endowed with eight factors to be appointed as an instructor of nuns. He is virtuous; he dwells restrained by the Pātimokkha restraint, is endowed with right conduct and resort, and sees danger in the slightest faults; he trains by undertaking the training rules. He is learned, a bearer of what has been heard, an accumulator of what has been heard. Those teachings that are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, which proclaim the perfectly complete and pure holy life—such teachings have been much heard by him, are borne in mind, are familiarized by speech, are mentally examined, and are well penetrated by view. Both Pātimokkhas have been well transmitted to him in detail, are well analyzed, well established, and well decided upon, according to the text and according to the detailed phrasing. He has a good voice and a good delivery. He is for the most part dear and agreeable to the nuns. He is capable of instructing the nuns. He has not previously fallen into a grave offense concerning a woman wearing the ochre robe who has gone forth with the Blessed One in mind. He is of twenty years’ standing or more than twenty years’ standing. Monks, I allow a monk endowed with these eight factors to be appointed as an instructor of nuns.”

148. Yo [P 4.0052] panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

148. ‘Whatever monk’ means whoever, of whatever sort... ‘Monk’ means... in this context, this is the monk who is intended.

Asammato nāma ñatticatutthena kammena asammato.

‘Unappointed’ means one who has not been appointed by a formal act consisting of a motion and three announcements.

Bhikkhuniyo nāma ubhatosaṅghe upasampannā.

‘Nuns’ means those who have been fully ordained in both Sanghas.

Ovadeyyāti aṭṭhahi garudhammehi ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Aññena dhammena ovadati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ekatoupasampannaṃ ovadati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

‘Should instruct’ means: if he instructs with the eight grave rules, there is an offense of pācittiya. If he instructs with another teaching, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If he instructs a nun ordained on one side only, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

149. Tena [T 2.0270][V 0.0076] sammatena bhikkhunā pariveṇaṃ sammajjitvā pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā āsanaṃ paññapetvā dutiyaṃ gahetvā nisīditabbaṃ. Bhikkhunīhi tattha gantvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīditabbaṃ. Tena bhikkhunā pucchitabbā – “samaggāttha, bhaginiyo”ti? Sace “samaggāmhāyyā”ti bhaṇanti, “vattanti, bhaginiyo, aṭṭha garudhammā”ti? Sace “vattantāyyā”ti bhaṇanti, “eso, bhaginiyo, ovādo”ti niyyādetabbo niyyātetabbo (itipi). Sace “na vattantāyyā”ti bhaṇanti, osāretabbā. “Vassasatūpasampannāya bhikkhuniyā tadahupasampannassa bhikkhuno abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ kātabbaṃ; ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā mānetvā pūjetvā [M 0.0075] yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo. Na bhikkhuniyā abhikkhuke āvāse vassaṃ vasitabbaṃ; ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo. Anvaddhamāsaṃ bhikkhuniyā bhikkhusaṅghato dve dhammā paccāsīsitabbā paccāsiṃsitabbā (itipi) uposathapucchakañca ovādupasaṅkamanañca, ayampi dhammo…pe… vassaṃ vuṭṭhāya bhikkhuniyā ubhatosaṅghe tīhi ṭhānehi pavāretabbaṃ diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā; ayampi dhammo…pe… garudhammaṃ ajjhāpannāya bhikkhuniyā ubhatosaṅghe pakkhamānattaṃ caritabbaṃ; ayampi [T 2.0271] dhammo…pe… dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya sikkhamānāya ubhatosaṅghe upasampadā pariyesitabbā; ayampi dhammo…pe… na bhikkhuniyā kena ci pariyāyena bhikkhu akkositabbo paribhāsitabbo; ayampi dhammo…pe… ajjatagge ovaṭo bhikkhunīnaṃ bhikkhūsu vacanapatho, anovaṭo bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīsu vacanapatho; ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garukatvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyo”ti.

149. That appointed monk should sweep the precinct, set out drinking water and water for use, prepare a seat, take a companion, and sit down. The nuns should go there, pay respects to that monk, and sit to one side. That monk should ask them: ‘Sisters, are you in harmony?’ If they say, ‘We are in harmony, venerable sir,’ he should ask, ‘Sisters, do you know the eight grave rules by heart?’ If they say, ‘We know them by heart, venerable sir,’ he should present the exhortation: ‘Sisters, this is the exhortation.’ If they say, ‘We do not know them by heart, venerable sir,’ he should recite them. ‘A nun who has been ordained for a hundred years should pay respects, rise up, greet with joined palms, and perform the act of veneration towards a monk ordained that very day; this rule too should be honored, respected, esteemed, and revered, and not transgressed for life. A nun should not spend the rains in a residence without monks; this rule too should be honored, respected, esteemed, and revered, and not transgressed for life. Every half-month, a nun should seek two things from the community of monks: asking about the observance day and approaching for instruction; this rule too... After the rains, a nun should invite criticism from both communities regarding three matters: what was seen, heard, or suspected; this rule too... A nun who has violated a grave rule should undergo the half-month penance in both communities; this rule too... A probationer who has trained for two years in the six rules should seek full ordination from both communities; this rule too... A nun should not, in any way, revile or abuse a monk; this rule too... From this day forward, the path of speech for nuns towards monks is closed, but the path of speech for monks towards nuns is not closed; this rule too should be honored, respected, esteemed, and revered, and not transgressed for life.’”

Sace “samaggāmhāyyā”ti bhaṇantaṃ aññaṃ dhammaṃ bhaṇati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sace “vaggāmhāyyā”ti bhaṇantaṃ aṭṭha garudhamme bhaṇati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ovādaṃ aniyyādetvā aññaṃ dhammaṃ bhaṇati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If, when they say, ‘We are in harmony, venerable sir,’ he speaks of another teaching, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If, when they say, ‘We are in discord, venerable sir,’ he speaks of the eight grave rules, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If, without presenting the exhortation, he speaks of another teaching, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

150. Adhammakamme [P 4.0053] adhammakammasaññī vaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ vaggasaññī ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññī vaggaṃ bhikkhunīsaṅghaṃ vematiko ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññī vaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ samaggasaññī ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

150. In the case of an unlawful formal act, perceiving it as an unlawful formal act, if one advises a divided community of nuns, perceiving it as divided, there is an offense of expiation. In the case of an unlawful formal act, perceiving it as an unlawful formal act, if one advises a divided community of nuns, being uncertain about it, there is an offense of expiation. In the case of an unlawful formal act, perceiving it as an unlawful formal act, if one advises a divided community of nuns, perceiving it as united, there is an offense of expiation.

Adhammakamme vematiko vaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ vaggasaññī ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Adhammakamme vematiko vaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ vematiko ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa[V 0.0077]. Adhammakamme vematiko vaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ samaggasaññī ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

In the case of an unlawful formal act, being uncertain about it, if one advises a divided community of nuns, perceiving it as divided, there is an offense of expiation. In the case of an unlawful formal act, being uncertain about it, if one advises a divided community of nuns, being uncertain about it, there is an offense of expiation. In the case of an unlawful formal act, being uncertain about it, if one advises a divided community of nuns, perceiving it as united, there is an offense of expiation.

Adhammakamme [T 2.0272] dhammakammasaññī vaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ vaggasaññī ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññī vaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ vematiko ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññī vaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ samaggasaññī ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

In the case of an unlawful formal act, perceiving it as a lawful formal act, if one advises a divided community of nuns, perceiving it as divided, there is an offense of expiation. In the case of an unlawful formal act, perceiving it as a lawful formal act, if one advises a divided community of nuns, being uncertain about it, there is an offense of expiation. In the case of an unlawful formal act, perceiving it as a lawful formal act, if one advises a divided community of nuns, perceiving it as united, there is an offense of expiation.

Adhammakamme [M 0.0076] adhammakammasaññī samaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ vaggasaññī ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññī samaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ vematiko ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññī samaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ samaggasaññī ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

In the case of an unlawful formal act, perceiving it as an unlawful formal act, if one advises a united community of nuns, perceiving it as divided, there is an offense of expiation.
