In the case of an unlawful formal act, perceiving it as an unlawful formal act, if one advises a united community of nuns, being uncertain about it, there is an offense of expiation. In the case of an unlawful formal act, perceiving it as an unlawful formal act, if one advises a united community of nuns, perceiving it as united, there is an offense of expiation.

Adhammakamme vematiko samaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ vaggasaññī ovadati…pe… vematiko ovadati…pe… samaggasaññī ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

In the case of an unlawful formal act, being uncertain about it, if one advises a united community of nuns, perceiving it as divided... or being uncertain about it... or perceiving it as united, there is an offense of expiation.

Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññī samaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ vaggasaññī ovadati…pe… vematiko ovadati…pe… samaggasaññī ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

In the case of an unlawful formal act, perceiving it as a lawful formal act, if one advises a united community of nuns, perceiving it as divided... or being uncertain about it... or perceiving it as united, there is an offense of expiation.

151. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññī vaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ vaggasaññī ovadati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññī vaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ vematiko ovadati…pe… samaggasaññī ovadati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

151. In the case of a lawful formal act, perceiving it as an unlawful formal act, if one advises a divided community of nuns, perceiving it as divided, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of a lawful formal act, perceiving it as an unlawful formal act, if one advises a divided community of nuns, being uncertain about it... or perceiving it as united, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Dhammakamme vematiko vaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ vaggasaññī ovadati…pe… vematiko ovadati…pe… samaggasaññī ovadati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In the case of a lawful formal act, being uncertain about it, if one advises a divided community of nuns, perceiving it as divided... or being uncertain about it... or perceiving it as united, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Dhammakamme [T 2.0273] dhammakammasaññī vaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ vaggasaññī ovadati…pe… vematiko ovadati…pe… samaggasaññī ovadati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In the case of a lawful formal act, perceiving it as a lawful formal act, if one advises a divided community of nuns, perceiving it as divided... or being uncertain about it... or perceiving it as united, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Dhammakamme [V 0.0078] adhammakammasaññī samaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ vaggasaññī ovadati…pe… vematiko ovadati…pe… samaggasaññī ovadati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In the case of a lawful formal act, perceiving it as an unlawful formal act, if one advises a united community of nuns, perceiving it as divided... or being uncertain about it... or perceiving it as united, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Dhammakamme vematiko samaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ vaggasaññī ovadati…pe… vematiko ovadati…pe… samaggasaññī ovadati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In the case of a lawful formal act, being uncertain about it, if one advises a united community of nuns, perceiving it as divided... or being uncertain about it... or perceiving it as united, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññī samaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ vaggasaññī ovadati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññī samaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ vematiko ovadati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññī samaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ samaggasaññī ovadati, anāpatti.

In the case of a lawful formal act, perceiving it as a lawful formal act, if one advises a united community of nuns while perceiving it as divided, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of a lawful formal act, perceiving it as a lawful formal act, if one advises a united community of nuns while being uncertain, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of a lawful formal act, perceiving it as a lawful formal act, if one advises a united community of nuns while perceiving it as united, there is no offense.

152. Anāpatti uddesaṃ dento, paripucchaṃ dento, “osārehi ayyā”ti vuccamāno, osāreti, pañhaṃ pucchati, pañhaṃ puṭṭho katheti, aññassatthāya bhaṇantaṃ bhikkhuniyo suṇanti, sikkhamānāya, sāmaṇeriyā, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

152. There is no offense: when giving the Pāḷi text; when giving the commentary; when, being told, ‘Venerable one, recite,’ one recites; when one asks a question; when, having been asked a question, one answers; when bhikkhunīs listen to one teaching for the benefit of another; when advising a female probationer or a female novice; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Ovādasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The first training rule on exhortation is concluded.

2. Atthaṅgatasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Training Rule on Sunset

153. Tena [T 2.0274][P 4.0054][M 0.0077] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena therā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo ovadanti pariyāyena. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato cūḷapanthakassa pariyāyo hoti bhikkhuniyo ovadituṃ. Bhikkhuniyo evamāhaṃsu – “na dāni ajja ovādo iddho bhavissati, taññeva dāni udānaṃ ayyo cūḷapanthako punappunaṃ bhaṇissatī”ti. Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo yenāyasmā cūḷapanthako tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ cūḷapanthakaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho tā bhikkhuniyo āyasmā cūḷapanthako etadavoca – “samaggāttha, bhaginiyo”ti? “Samaggāmhāyyā”ti. “Vattanti, bhaginiyo, aṭṭha garudhammā”ti? “Vattantāyyā”ti. “Eso, bhaginiyo, ovādo”ti niyyādetvā imaṃ udānaṃ punappunaṃ abhāsi –

153. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the elder bhikkhus were exhorting the bhikkhunīs in turn. And at that time, it was the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka's turn to exhort the bhikkhunīs. The bhikkhunīs said this: 'Now, today the exhortation will not be powerful, for the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka will just repeat that same inspired utterance over and over again.' Then those bhikkhunīs approached the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka; having approached, they paid homage to the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka and sat down to one side. To those bhikkhunīs sitting to one side, the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka said this: 'Sisters, are you in concord?' 'We are in concord, venerable sir.' 'Sisters, are the eight weighty principles known to you by heart?' 'They are known, venerable sir.' 'Sisters, this is the exhortation.' Having delivered this, he repeated this inspired utterance again and again:

udā. 37 “Adhicetaso [V 0.0079] appamajjato, munino monapathesu sikkhato;

Sokā na bhavanti tādino, upasantassa sadā satīmato”ti.

“For the sage with a higher mind, who is heedful, training in the paths to sagehood; for such a one, who is tranquil and ever mindful, sorrows do not exist.”

Bhikkhuniyo evamāhaṃsu – “nanu avocumhā – na dāni ajja ovādo iddho bhavissati, taññeva dāni udānaṃ ayyo cūḷapanthako punappunaṃ [T 2.0275] bhaṇissatī”ti! Assosi kho āyasmā cūḷapanthako tāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ imaṃ kathāsallāpaṃ. Atha kho āyasmā cūḷapanthako vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā ākāse antalikkhe caṅkamatipi tiṭṭhatipi nisīdatipi seyyampi kappeti dhūmāyatipi pajjalatipi antaradhāyatipi, tañceva taññeva (itipi) udānaṃ bhaṇati aññañca bahuṃ buddhavacanaṃ. Bhikkhuniyo evamāhaṃsu – “acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho, na vata no ito pubbe ovādo evaṃ iddho bhūtapubbo yathā ayyassa cūḷapanthakassā”ti. Atha kho āyasmā cūḷapanthako tā bhikkhuniyo yāva samandhakārā ovaditvā uyyojesi – gacchatha bhaginiyoti.

The bhikkhunīs said: “Did we not say, ‘Now, today the exhortation will not be powerful, for the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka will just repeat that same inspired utterance over and over again’?” The Venerable Cūḷapanthaka heard this conversation of those bhikkhunīs. Then the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka, having risen up into the air, also walked, also stood, also sat, and also made a posture of lying down in the sky, in mid-air; he also emitted smoke, also blazed with flames, and also disappeared; and he recited that same inspired utterance and much other speech of the Buddha. The bhikkhunīs said: “Sirs, it is truly amazing! Sirs, it is truly wonderful! Never before has an exhortation been so powerful for us as that of the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka.” Then the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka, having exhorted those bhikkhunīs until it was dark, dismissed them, saying, “Go, sisters.”

Atha [M 0.0078] kho tā bhikkhuniyo nagaradvāre thakite bahinagare vasitvā kālasseva nagaraṃ pavisanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “abrahmacāriniyo imā bhikkhuniyo; ārāme bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ vasitvā idāni nagaraṃ pavisantī”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ [P 4.0055] ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā cūḷapanthako atthaṅgate sūriye bhikkhuniyo ovadissatī”ti…pe… “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, cūḷapanthaka, atthaṅgate sūriye bhikkhuniyo ovadasī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, cūḷapanthaka, atthaṅgate sūriye bhikkhuniyo ovadissasi! Netaṃ, cūḷapanthaka, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

Then those bhikkhunīs, as the city gate was closed, stayed outside the city and entered the city early in the morning. People complained, criticized, and spread disparaging words: “These bhikkhunīs are unchaste; having stayed in the monastery with the bhikkhus, they are now entering the city.” The bhikkhus heard the words of those people who were complaining, criticizing, and spreading disparaging words. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread disparaging words: “How indeed could the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka exhort the bhikkhunīs after the sun has set?”… “Is it true, Cūḷapanthaka, that you exhort the bhikkhunīs after the sun has set?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “How indeed could you, Cūḷapanthaka, exhort the bhikkhunīs after the sun has set? This, Cūḷapanthaka, is not for inspiring faith in those who are without faith… And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

154. “Sammatopi [T 2.0276] ce bhikkhu atthaṅgate sūriye bhikkhuniyo ovadeyya, pācittiya”nti.

154. “Should even an appointed bhikkhu exhort bhikkhunīs after the sun has set, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

155. Sammato nāma ñatticatutthena kammena sammato.

155. Appointed means appointed by a formal act having the motion as the fourth part.

Atthaṅgate sūriyeti oggate sūriye.

After the sun has set means when the sun has gone down.

Bhikkhunī [V 0.0080] nāma ubhatosaṅghe upasampannā.

A bhikkhunī means one who is fully ordained in both communities.

Ovadeyyāti aṭṭhahi vā garudhammehi aññena vā dhammena ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should exhort’ means: if one exhorts with the eight weighty principles or with another teaching, there is an offense of pācittiya.

156. Atthaṅgate atthaṅgatasaññī ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Atthaṅgate vematiko ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Atthaṅgate anatthaṅgatasaññī ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

156. When the sun has set, if one exhorts while perceiving it as set, there is an offense of pācittiya. When the sun has set, if one exhorts while being uncertain, there is an offense of pācittiya. When the sun has set, if one exhorts while perceiving it as not set, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Ekatoupasampannāya ovadati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anatthaṅgate atthaṅgatasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anatthaṅgate vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anatthaṅgate anatthaṅgatasaññī, anāpatti.

If one exhorts a bhikkhunī ordained by one community only, there is an offense of wrong conduct. When the sun has not set, if one perceives it as set, there is an offense of wrong conduct. When the sun has not set, if one is uncertain, there is an offense of wrong conduct. When the sun has not set, while perceiving it as not set, there is no offense.

157. Anāpatti uddesaṃ dento, paripucchaṃ dento, “osārehi ayyā”ti vuccamāno, osāreti, pañhaṃ pucchati, pañhaṃ puṭṭho katheti, aññassatthāya bhaṇantaṃ bhikkhuniyo suṇanti, sikkhamānāya sāmaṇeriyā, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

157. There is no offense when giving the Pāli text; when giving the commentary; when, being told, ‘Venerable one, recite,’ one recites; when one asks a question; when, having been asked a question, one answers; when bhikkhunīs listen to one teaching for the benefit of another; for a female probationer; for a female novice; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Atthaṅgatasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The second training rule on sunset is concluded.

3. Bhikkhunupassayasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Training Rule Concerning the Bhikkhunīs' Residence

158. Tena [T 2.0277][M 0.0079] samayena buddho bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhunupassayaṃ upasaṅkamitvā chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ovadanti. Bhikkhuniyo chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo etadavocuṃ – “ethāyye, ovādaṃ [P 4.0056] gamissāmā”ti. “Yampi yaṃ hi (ka.) mayaṃ, ayye, gaccheyyāma ovādassa kāraṇā, ayyā chabbaggiyā idheva āgantvā amhe ovadantī”ti. Bhikkhuniyo ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhunupassayaṃ upasaṅkamitvā bhikkhuniyo ovadissantī”ti chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ovādaṃ na gacchissantīti (sī.)! Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhunupassayaṃ upasaṅkamitvā bhikkhuniyo ovadissantī”ti…pe… “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave[V 0.0081], bhikkhunupassayaṃ upasaṅkamitvā bhikkhuniyo ovadathā”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, bhikkhunupassayaṃ upasaṅkamitvā bhikkhuniyo ovadissatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

158. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Nigrodhārāma. Now at that time, the bhikkhus of the group-of-six, having approached the bhikkhunīs' residence, instructed the bhikkhunīs of the group-of-six. The bhikkhunīs said this to the bhikkhunīs of the group-of-six: 'Come, venerable ladies, let us go for instruction.' 'Venerable ladies, to the very place we would go for the sake of instruction, the venerable bhikkhus of the group-of-six come right here and instruct us.' The bhikkhunīs complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: 'How indeed can the bhikkhus of the group-of-six, having approached the bhikkhunīs' residence, instruct the bhikkhunīs!' Then those bhikkhunīs informed the bhikkhus of this matter. Those bhikkhus who were of few desires… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: 'How indeed can the bhikkhus of the group-of-six, having approached the bhikkhunīs' residence, instruct the bhikkhunīs!'… 'Is it true, bhikkhus, that you, having approached the bhikkhunīs' residence, instruct the bhikkhunīs?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… 'How indeed can you, foolish men, having approached the bhikkhunīs' residence, instruct the bhikkhunīs! This, foolish men, is not for inspiring faith in those who are without faith… And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:'

“Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhunupassayaṃ upasaṅkamitvā bhikkhuniyo ovadeyya, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever bhikkhu, having approached a bhikkhunīs' residence, should instruct bhikkhunīs, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

Evañcidaṃ [T 2.0278] bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

In this way, this training rule was laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

159. Tena kho pana samayena mahāpajāpati gotamī gilānā hoti. Therā bhikkhū yena mahāpajāpati gotamī tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā mahāpajāpatiṃ gotamiṃ etadavocuṃ – “kacci te, gotami, khamanīyaṃ kacci yāpanīya”nti? “Na me, ayyā, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ”. “Iṅghayyā, dhammaṃ desethā”ti. “Na, bhagini, kappati bhikkhunupassayaṃ upasaṅkamitvā bhikkhuniyo dhammaṃ desetu”nti kukkuccāyantā na desesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena mahāpajāpati gotamī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā mahāpajāpatiṃ gotamiṃ etadavoca – “kacci te, gotami, khamanīyaṃ kacci yāpanīya”nti[M 0.0080]? “Pubbe me, bhante, therā bhikkhū āgantvā dhammaṃ desenti. Tena me phāsu hoti. Idāni pana – “bhagavatā paṭikkhitta”nti, kukkuccāyantā na desenti. Tena me na phāsu hotī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā mahāpajāpatiṃ gotamiṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhunupassayaṃ upasaṅkamitvā gilānaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ovadituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

159. Now at that time, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī was sick. The elder bhikkhus went to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī and said this: 'Gotamī, are you bearing up? Are you getting by?' 'Venerable sirs, I am not bearing up, I am not getting by. Please, venerable sirs, teach the Dhamma.' But being scrupulous, they did not teach, thinking, 'Sister, it is not allowable to approach a nuns' residence to teach the Dhamma to bhikkhunīs.' Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and went to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One said this to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī: 'Gotamī, are you bearing up? Are you getting by?' 'Venerable sir, previously the elder bhikkhus would come and teach me the Dhamma. Because of that, I was comfortable. But now, being scrupulous, thinking, "It has been prohibited by the Blessed One," they do not teach. Because of that, I am not comfortable.' Then the Blessed One instructed, established, roused, and gladdened Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī with a talk on the Dhamma. He then got up from his seat and departed. Then, on this occasion, in this connection, after delivering a talk on the Dhamma, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: 'Bhikkhus, I allow you to approach a nuns' residence to instruct a sick bhikkhunī. And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:'

160. “Yo [P 4.0057] pana bhikkhu bhikkhunupassayaṃ upasaṅkamitvā bhikkhuniyo ovadeyya, aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ[T 2.0279]. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Gilānā hoti bhikkhunī – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

160. Whatever bhikkhu, having approached a nuns' residence, should instruct bhikkhunīs, except on the proper occasion, it is an offense of expiation. Therein, this is the proper occasion: a bhikkhunī is ill—this is the proper occasion therein.

161. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

161. As for 'Whatever bhikkhu': whoever, of whatever kind… As for 'bhikkhu': … in this sense, this is the bhikkhu who is intended.

Bhikkhunupassayo [V 0.0082] nāma yattha bhikkhuniyo ekarattampi vasanti.

A nuns' residence is a place where bhikkhunīs reside even for a single night.

Upasaṅkamitvāti tattha gantvā.

Having approached: having gone there.

Bhikkhunī nāma ubhatosaṅghe upasampannā.

A bhikkhunī is one who has been fully ordained in both Saṅghas.

Ovadeyyāti aṭṭhahi garudhammehi ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

Should instruct: if he instructs with the eight weighty rules, there is an offense of expiation.

Aññatra samayāti ṭhapetvā samayaṃ.

Except on the proper occasion: setting aside the proper occasion.

Gilānā nāma bhikkhunī na sakkoti ovādāya vā saṃvāsāya vā gantuṃ.

A sick bhikkhunī is one who is unable to go for instruction or for communion.

162. Upasampannāya upasampannasaññī bhikkhunupassayaṃ upasaṅkamitvā aññatra samayā ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampannāya vematiko bhikkhunupassayaṃ upasaṅkamitvā aññatra samayā ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampannāya anupasampannasaññī bhikkhunupassayaṃ upasaṅkamitvā aññatra samayā ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

162. If, regarding a fully ordained bhikkhunī, he perceives her as fully ordained and, having approached the nuns' residence, instructs her except on the proper occasion, there is an offense of expiation. If, regarding a fully ordained bhikkhunī, he is in doubt and, having approached the nuns' residence, instructs her except on the proper occasion, there is an offense of expiation. If, regarding a fully ordained bhikkhunī, he perceives her as not fully ordained and, having approached the nuns' residence, instructs her except on the proper occasion, there is an offense of expiation.

Aññena dhammena ovadati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ekatoupasampannāya ovadati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya upasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa[M 0.0081]. Anupasampannāya vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya anupasampannasaññī, anāpatti.

If he instructs with another teaching, there is an offense of wrong doing. If he instructs one ordained by only one Saṅgha, there is an offense of wrong doing. If, regarding one not fully ordained, he perceives her as fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong doing. If, regarding one not fully ordained, he is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong doing. If, regarding one not fully ordained, he perceives her as not fully ordained, there is no offense.

163. Anāpatti samaye, uddesaṃ dento, paripucchaṃ dento, “osārehi [T 2.0280] ayyā”ti vuccamāno osāreti, pañhaṃ pucchati, pañhaṃ puṭṭho katheti, aññassatthāya bhaṇantaṃ bhikkhuniyo suṇanti, sikkhamānāya sāmaṇeriyā, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

163. There is no offense: on the proper occasion; when giving the recitation; when giving an explanation; when, being told, 'Venerable sir, recite,' he recites; when he asks a question; when, having been asked a question, he answers; when bhikkhunīs listen as he is speaking for the benefit of another; when instructing a probationer or a female novice; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Bhikkhunupassayasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The third training rule concerning the nuns' residence is concluded.

4. Āmisasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Training Rule Concerning Material Gain

164. Tena [T 2.0281] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme[V 0.0083]. Tena kho pana samayena therā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo ovadantā lābhino honti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṃ. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū evaṃ vadanti – “na bahukatā therā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo ovadituṃ; āmisahetu therā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo [P 4.0058] ovadantī”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū evaṃ vakkhanti – ‘na bahukatā therā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo ovadituṃ; āmisahetu therā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo ovadantī’”ti…pe… “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṃ vadetha – ‘na bahukatā therā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo ovadituṃ; āmisahetu therā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo ovadantī’”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, evaṃ vakkhatha – na bahukatā therā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo ovadituṃ; āmisahetu therā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo ovadantīti! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

164. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the elder bhikkhus, while instructing the bhikkhunīs, became recipients of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick. The group-of-six bhikkhus said this: 'The elder bhikkhus do not hold in high regard the instructing of the bhikkhunīs; it is for the sake of material gain that the elder bhikkhus instruct the bhikkhunīs.' Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes... criticized, found fault, and spread it about, saying: 'How indeed can the group-of-six bhikkhus say this: “The elder bhikkhus do not hold in high regard the instructing of the bhikkhunīs; it is for the sake of material gain that the elder bhikkhus instruct the bhikkhunīs”?'... 'Is it true, it is said, bhikkhus, that you say this: “The elder bhikkhus do not hold in high regard the instructing of the bhikkhunīs; it is for the sake of material gain that the elder bhikkhus instruct the bhikkhunīs”?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... 'How indeed can you, foolish men, say this: “The elder bhikkhus do not hold in high regard the instructing of the bhikkhunīs; it is for the sake of material gain that the elder bhikkhus instruct the bhikkhunīs”! This, foolish men, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced... And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule in this way:'

165. “Yo pana bhikkhu evaṃ vadeyya – ‘āmisahetu therā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo ovandatī’ti, pācittiya”nti.

165. Whatever bhikkhu should say this: 'It is for the sake of material gain that the elder bhikkhus instruct the bhikkhunīs,' it is an offense of expiation.

166. Yo [T 2.0282][M 0.0082] panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

166. As for 'Whatever bhikkhu': whoever, of whatever kind… As for 'bhikkhu': … in this sense, this is the bhikkhu who is intended.

Āmisahetūti cīvarahetu piṇḍapātahetu senāsanahetu gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu sakkārahetu garukārahetu mānanahetu vandanahetu pūjanahetu.

As for 'for the sake of material gain': for the sake of robes, for the sake of almsfood, for the sake of lodging, for the sake of medicinal requisites for the sick, for the sake of honor, for the sake of respect, for the sake of esteem, for the sake of homage, for the sake of veneration.

Evaṃ vadeyyāti upasampannaṃ saṅghena sammataṃ bhikkhunovādakaṃ avaṇṇaṃ kattukāmo ayasaṃ kattukāmo maṅkukattukāmo evaṃ vadeti – “cīvarahetu piṇḍapātahetu senāsanahetu gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu sakkārahetu garukārahetu mānanahetu vandanahetu pūjanahetu ovadatī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should say thus’ means: desiring to disparage, desiring to cause disrepute, desiring to make ashamed, one speaks thus about a fully ordained instructor of nuns who has been appointed by the Sangha: ‘He instructs for the sake of robes, for the sake of almsfood, for the sake of lodging, for the sake of medicinal requisites for the sick, for the sake of honor, for the sake of respect, for the sake of esteem, for the sake of homage, for the sake of veneration.’ If one says this, there is an offense of expiation.

167. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññī evaṃ vadeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme vematiko evaṃ vadeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññī evaṃ vadeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

167. Regarding a valid formal act, if one perceives it as a valid formal act and speaks thus, there is an offense of expiation. Regarding a valid formal act, if one is in doubt and speaks thus, there is an offense of expiation. Regarding a valid formal act, if one perceives it as an invalid formal act and speaks thus, there is an offense of expiation.

Upasampannaṃ [V 0.0084] saṅghena asammataṃ bhikkhunovādakaṃ avaṇṇaṃ kattukāmo ayasaṃ kattukāmo maṅkukattukāmo evaṃ vadeti – “cīvarahetu…pe… pūjanahetu ovadatī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannaṃ saṅghena sammataṃ vā asammataṃ vā bhikkhunovādakaṃ avaṇṇaṃ kattukāmo ayasaṃ kattukāmo maṅkukattukāmo evaṃ vadeti [T 2.0283] – “cīvarahetu piṇḍapātahetu senāsanahetu gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu sakkārahetu garukārahetu mānanahetu vandanahetu pūjanahetu ovadatī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Desiring to disparage, desiring to cause disrepute, desiring to make ashamed, one speaks thus about a fully ordained instructor of nuns who has not been appointed by the Sangha: ‘He instructs for the sake of robes… for the sake of veneration.’ If one says this, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Desiring to disparage, desiring to cause disrepute, desiring to make ashamed, one speaks thus about an instructor of nuns who is not fully ordained, whether appointed by the Sangha or not: ‘He instructs for the sake of robes, for the sake of almsfood, for the sake of lodging, for the sake of medicinal requisites for the sick, for the sake of honor, for the sake of respect, for the sake of esteem, for the sake of homage, for the sake of veneration.’ If one says this, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding an invalid formal act, if one perceives it as a valid formal act, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding an invalid formal act, if one is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding an invalid formal act, if one perceives it as an invalid formal act, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

168. Anāpatti pakatiyā cīvarahetu piṇḍapātahetu senāsanahetu gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu sakkārahetu garukārahetu mānanahetu vandanahetu pūjanahetu ovadantaṃ bhaṇati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

168. There is no offense if one speaks about someone who in fact instructs for the sake of robes, for the sake of almsfood, for the sake of lodging, for the sake of medicinal requisites for the sick, for the sake of honor, for the sake of respect, for the sake of esteem, for the sake of homage, or for the sake of veneration; there is no offense for one who is insane, nor for the first offender.

Āmisasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.

The fourth training rule concerning material gain is concluded.

5. Cīvaradānasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Training Rule on Giving a Robe

169. Tena [T 2.0284][P 4.0059][M 0.0083] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu sāvatthiyaṃ aññatarissā visikhāya piṇḍāya carati. Aññatarāpi bhikkhunī tassā visikhāya piṇḍāya carati. Atha kho so bhikkhu taṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “gaccha, bhagini, amukasmiṃ okāse bhikkhā diyyatī”ti. Sāpi kho evamāha – “gacchāyya, amukasmiṃ okāse bhikkhā diyyatī”ti. Te abhiṇhadassanena sandiṭṭhā ahesuṃ. Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa cīvaraṃ bhājīyati. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī ovādaṃ gantvā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ kho taṃ bhikkhuniṃ so bhikkhu etadavoca – “ayaṃ me, bhagini, cīvarapaṭivīso paṭiviṃso (sī.), paṭiviso (itipi); sādiyissasī”ti? “Āmāyya, dubbalacīvarāmhī”ti.

169. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu was walking for alms in a certain street in Sāvatthī. A certain bhikkhunī was also walking for alms in that street. Then that bhikkhu said this to that bhikkhunī: “Go, sister, alms are being given in such-and-such a place.” She also said this: “Go, venerable sir, alms are being given in such-and-such a place.” Through frequent seeing, they became acquainted. Now at that time, robes were being distributed to the Sangha. Then that bhikkhunī, having gone for the exhortation, approached that bhikkhu; having approached, she paid homage to him and stood to one side. To that bhikkhunī standing to one side, that bhikkhu said this: “Sister, this is my share of robes; will you accept it?” “Yes, venerable sir, I have a poor robe.”

Atha kho so bhikkhu tassā bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ adāsi. Sopi kho bhikkhu dubbalacīvaro hoti. Bhikkhū taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavocuṃ – “karohi dāni te, āvuso, cīvara”nti[V 0.0085]. Atha kho so bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhu bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ dassatī”ti…pe… “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ adāsī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. “Ñātikā te[T 2.0285], bhikkhu, aññātikā”ti? “Aññātikā, bhagavā”ti. “Aññātako, moghapurisa, aññātikāya na jānāti patirūpaṃ vā appatirūpaṃ vā santaṃ vā asantaṃ vā. Kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ dassasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

Then that bhikkhu gave the robe to that bhikkhunī. That bhikkhu also had a poor robe. The bhikkhus said this to that bhikkhu: “Friend, now make your robe.” Then that bhikkhu informed the bhikkhus of this matter. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… they grumbled, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed could a bhikkhu give a robe to a bhikkhunī?” … “Is it true, bhikkhu, as is said, that you gave a robe to a bhikkhunī?” “It is true, Blessed One.” “Is she a relative of yours, bhikkhu, or not a relative?” “Not a relative, Blessed One.” “Worthless man, a non-relative does not know what is suitable or unsuitable for another non-relative, nor whether they are in need or not. How indeed could you, worthless man, give a robe to a bhikkhunī who is not a relative! This, worthless man, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… and so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Yo pana bhikkhu aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ dadeyya, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever bhikkhu should give a robe to a bhikkhunī who is not a relative, it is an offense of expiation.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhus.

170. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā bhikkhunīnaṃ pārivattakaṃ pārivaṭṭakaṃ (itipi) cīvaraṃ na denti. Bhikkhuniyo ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā amhākaṃ pārivattakaṃ cīvaraṃ [P 4.0060] na dassantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū [M 0.0084] tāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ ujjhāyantīnaṃ khiyyantīnaṃ vipācentīnaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ pārivattakaṃ dātuṃ. Bhikkhussa, bhikkhuniyā, sikkhamānāya, sāmaṇerassa, sāmaṇeriyā – anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imesaṃ pañcannaṃ pārivattakaṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

170. Now at that time, bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not give exchange robes to the bhikkhunīs. The bhikkhunīs grumbled, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed could the venerable sirs not give us exchange robes!” The bhikkhus heard those bhikkhunīs grumbling, criticizing, and speaking disparagingly. Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow the giving of an exchange to five: to a bhikkhu, to a bhikkhunī, to a female probationer, to a male novice, and to a female novice. Bhikkhus, I allow the giving of an exchange to these five. And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

171. “Yo pana bhikkhu aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ dadeyya, aññatra pārivattakā, pācittiya”nti.

171. “Whatever bhikkhu should give a robe to a bhikkhunī who is not a relative, except in exchange, it is an offense of expiation.”

172. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

172. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhu’ means: …in this context, this is the bhikkhu who is intended.

Aññātikā nāma mātito vā [T 2.0286] pitito vā yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā asambaddhā.

‘Not a relative’ means: one not related on the mother’s side or on the father’s side up to the seventh ancestral generation.

Bhikkhunī [V 0.0086] nāma ubhatosaṅghe upasampannā.

‘Bhikkhunī’ means: one who has been fully ordained in both Sanghas.

Cīvaraṃ nāma channaṃ cīvarānaṃ aññataraṃ cīvaraṃ vikappanupagaṃ pacchimaṃ vikappanupagapacchimaṃ (sī.).

A 'robe' means any one of the six kinds of robes, the minimum of which is suitable for formal determination (vikappana).

Aññatra pārivattakāti ṭhapetvā pārivattakaṃ deti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

'Except for an exchange' means: setting aside an exchange, if one gives, there is an offense of pācittiya.

173. Aññātikāya aññātikasaññī cīvaraṃ deti, aññatra pārivattakā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Aññātikāya vematiko cīvaraṃ deti, aññatra pārivattakā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Aññātikāya ñātikasaññī cīvaraṃ deti, aññatra pārivattakā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

173. If he gives a robe to one who is not a relative, perceiving her as not a relative, other than by way of exchange, there is an offense of pācittiya. If he gives a robe to one who is not a relative, being in doubt, other than by way of exchange, there is an offense of pācittiya. If he gives a robe to one who is not a relative, perceiving her as a relative, other than by way of exchange, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Ekato upasampannāya cīvaraṃ deti, aññatra pārivattakā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñātikāya aññātikasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñātikāya vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñātikāya ñātikasaññī, anāpatti.

If he gives a robe to one ordained in one Saṅgha only, other than by way of exchange, there is an offense of wrong-doing. To a relative, perceiving her as not a relative, there is an offense of wrong-doing. To a relative, being in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing. To a relative, perceiving her as a relative, there is no offense.

174. Anāpatti ñātikāya, pārivattakaṃ parittena vā vipulaṃ, vipulena vā parittaṃ, bhikkhunī vissāsaṃ gaṇhāti, tāvakālikaṃ gaṇhāti, cīvaraṃ ṭhapetvā aññaṃ parikkhāraṃ deti, sikkhamānāya, sāmaṇeriyā, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

174. There is no offense: if it is to a relative; if it is an exchange, a small one for a large one, or a large one for a small one; if a bhikkhunī takes it based on trust; if she takes it temporarily; if, setting aside a robe, he gives another requisite; if it is to a female probationer or to a female novice; if the giver is insane; if he is the first offender.

Cīvaradānasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The fifth training rule on giving a robe is concluded.

6. Cīvarasibbanasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Training Rule on Sewing a Robe

175. Tena [T 2.0287][M 0.0085] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā udāyī paṭṭo paṭṭho (sī. syā.) hoti cīvarakammaṃ kātuṃ. Aññatarā [P 4.0061] bhikkhunī yenāyasmā udāyī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, ayyo cīvaraṃ sibbatū”ti. Atha kho āyasmā udāyī tassā bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ sibbitvā surattaṃ suparikammakataṃ katvā majjhe paṭibhānacittaṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā saṃharitvā nikkhipi. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī yenāyasmā udāyī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ etadavoca – “kahaṃ taṃ, bhante, cīvara”nti? “Handa, bhagini[V 0.0087], imaṃ cīvaraṃ yathāsaṃhaṭaṃ haritvā nikkhipitvā yadā bhikkhunisaṅgho ovādaṃ āgacchati tadā imaṃ cīvaraṃ pārupitvā bhikkhunisaṅghassa piṭṭhito piṭṭhito āgacchā”ti. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī taṃ cīvaraṃ yathāsaṃhaṭaṃ haritvā nikkhipitvā yadā bhikkhunisaṅgho ovādaṃ āgacchati tadā taṃ cīvaraṃ pārupitvā bhikkhunisaṅghassa piṭṭhito piṭṭhito āgacchati. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “yāva chinnikā imā bhikkhuniyo dhuttikā ahirikāyo, yatra hi nāma cīvare paṭibhānacittaṃ vuṭṭhāpessantī”ti!

175. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the Venerable Udāyī was skilled in doing robe-work. A certain bhikkhunī approached where the Venerable Udāyī was; having approached, she said this to the Venerable Udāyī: “Venerable sir, please, may the noble one sew my robe.” Then the Venerable Udāyī, having sewn the robe for that bhikkhunī, having made it well-dyed and well-finished, and having caused an inventive design depicting sexual intercourse to appear in the middle, folded it and put it aside. Then that bhikkhunī approached where the Venerable Udāyī was; having approached, she said this to the Venerable Udāyī: “Venerable sir, where is that robe?” “Here, sister, take this robe as it is folded, put it away, and when the community of bhikkhunīs comes for the exhortation, then, having put on this robe, come behind, behind the community of bhikkhunīs.” Then that bhikkhunī, having taken that robe as it is folded and put it away, when the community of bhikkhunīs came for the exhortation, then, having put on that robe, came behind, behind the community of bhikkhunīs. People complained, scorned, and spread it about: “How very shameless, dissolute, and without conscience are these bhikkhunīs, that they would cause an inventive design depicting sexual intercourse to appear on a robe!”

Bhikkhuniyo evamāhaṃsu – “kassidaṃ kamma”nti? “Ayyassa udāyissā”ti. “Yepi te chinnakā dhuttakā ahirikā tesampi evarūpaṃ [T 2.0288] na sobheyya, kiṃ pana ayyassa udāyissā”ti! Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā udāyī bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ sibbissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, udāyi, bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ sibbasī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. “Ñātikā te, udāyi, aññātikā”ti? “Aññātikā, bhagavā”ti. “Aññātako, moghapurisa, aññātikāya na jānāti patirūpaṃ vā appatirūpaṃ vā pāsādikaṃ vā apāsādikaṃ vā. Kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ sibbissasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

The bhikkhunīs said thus: “Whose work is this?” “It is the work of the noble Udāyī.” “Even for those who are shameless, dissolute, and without conscience, such a deed would not be fitting. How then could it be fitting for the noble Udāyī!” Then those bhikkhunīs reported this matter to the bhikkhus. Those bhikkhus who were of few desires… complained, scorned, and spread it about: “How indeed could the Venerable Udāyī sew a robe for a bhikkhunī?”… “Is it true, Udāyī, that you sew a robe for a bhikkhunī?” “It is true, Blessed One.” “Is she your relative, Udāyī, or not a relative?” “Not a relative, Blessed One.” “Foolish man, one who is not a relative does not know for one who is not a relative what is suitable or unsuitable, or what is inspiring or not inspiring. How indeed could you, foolish man, sew a robe for a bhikkhunī who is not a relative! This, foolish man, is not for the inspiration of the uninspired… And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

176. “Yo [M 0.0086] pana bhikkhu aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ sibbeyya vā sibbāpeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

176. “Whatever bhikkhu should sew a robe for a bhikkhunī who is not a relative, or should cause one to be sewn, it is a pācittiya.”

177. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

177. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhu’ means… in this context, this is the bhikkhu who is intended.

Aññātikā nāma mātito vā pitito vā yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā asambaddhā.

‘Not a relative’ means: one who is not connected on the mother’s side or on the father’s side up to the seventh generation of ancestors.

Bhikkhunī nāma ubhatosaṅghe upasampannā.

‘Bhikkhunī’ means: one who has been fully ordained in both Saṅghas.

Cīvaraṃ nāma channaṃ cīvarānaṃ aññataraṃ cīvaraṃ.

‘Robe’ means: any one of the six kinds of robes.

Sibbeyyāti [P 4.0062][V 0.0088] sayaṃ sibbati ārāpathe ārāpathe āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should sew’ means: he sews it himself. For every single stitch, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Sibbāpeyyāti aññaṃ āṇāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Sakiṃ āṇatto bahukampi sibbati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should cause to be sewn’ means: he commands another; there is an offense of pācittiya. If, having been commanded once, that person sews a great deal, there is an offense of pācittiya.

178. Aññātikāya [T 2.0289] aññātikasaññī cīvaraṃ sibbati vā sibbāpeti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Aññātikāya vematiko cīvaraṃ sibbati vā sibbāpeti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Aññātikāya ñātikasaññī cīvaraṃ sibbati vā sibbāpeti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

178. To a non-relative, perceiving her as a non-relative, if he sews or causes a robe to be sewn, there is an offense of pācittiya. To a non-relative, while being in doubt, if he sews or causes a robe to be sewn, there is an offense of pācittiya. To a non-relative, perceiving her as a relative, if he sews or causes a robe to be sewn, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Ekatoupasampannāya cīvaraṃ sibbati vā sibbāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñātikāya aññātikasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñātikāya vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñātikāya ñātikasaññī, anāpatti.

If he sews or causes a robe to be sewn for one who has been ordained by one Saṅgha, there is an offense of wrong-doing. To a relative, perceiving her as a non-relative, there is an offense of wrong-doing. To a relative, while being in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing. To a relative, perceiving her as a relative, there is no offense.

179. Anāpatti ñātikāya, cīvaraṃ ṭhapetvā aññaṃ parikkhāraṃ sibbati vā sibbāpeti vā, sikkhamānāya, sāmaṇeriyā, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

179. There is no offense: for a relative; if, setting aside a robe, he sews or causes another requisite to be sewn; for a probationer; for a female novice; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Cīvarasibbanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The sixth training rule on sewing a robe is finished.

7. Saṃvidhānasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Training Rule on Making an Arrangement

180. Tena [T 2.0290] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhunīhi [M 0.0087] saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “yatheva mayaṃ sapajāpatikā āhiṇḍāma, evamevime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya āhiṇḍantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjissantī”ti…pe… “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjathā”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi [V 0.0089] nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjissatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha.

180. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the monks of the group-of-six, having made an arrangement with nuns, were undertaking a single long journey. People complained, criticized, and disparaged, saying: ‘Just as we wander about with our wives, in the very same way these ascetics, the sons of the Sakyan, having made an arrangement, wander about together with nuns!’ The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and disparaging. Those monks who were of few desires… they complained, criticized, and disparaged, saying: ‘How indeed could the monks of the group-of-six, having made an arrangement with nuns, undertake a single long journey?’ … ‘Is it true, monks, as is said, that you, having made an arrangement with nuns, are undertaking a single long journey?’ ‘It is true, Blessed One.’ The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… ‘How indeed, you worthless men, could you, having made an arrangement with nuns, undertake a single long journey? This, worthless men, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule in this way:

“Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjeyya, antamaso gāmantarampi, pācittiya”nti.

‘Whatever monk, having made an arrangement with a nun, should undertake a single long journey, even so much as to another village, it is a Pācittiya offense.’

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

Thus this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.

181. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo [P 4.0063] ca sāketā [T 2.0291] sāvatthiṃ addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti. Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo te bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “mayampi ayyehi saddhiṃ gamissāmā”ti. “Na, bhaginī, kappati bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjituṃ. Tumhe vā paṭhamaṃ gacchatha mayaṃ vā gamissāmā”ti. “Ayyā, bhante, aggapurisā. Ayyāva paṭhamaṃ gacchantū”ti. Atha kho tāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ pacchā gacchantīnaṃ antarāmagge corā acchindiṃsu ca dūsesuñca. Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo sāvatthiṃ gantvā bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, satthagamanīye magge sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

181. Now at that time, many monks and nuns were undertaking a long journey from Sāketa to Sāvatthī. Then those nuns said to those monks, ‘Venerable sirs, we too will go together with you.’ ‘Sisters, it is not allowable, having made an arrangement with a nun, to undertake a single long journey. Either you go first, or we will go.’ ‘Venerable sirs, the venerable ones are foremost men. Let the venerable ones go first.’ Then, as those nuns were traveling behind, thieves on the road both robbed and violated them. Then those nuns, having gone to Sāvatthī, reported this matter to the nuns. The nuns reported this matter to the monks. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: ‘Monks, I allow one to undertake a single long journey with a nun, having made an arrangement, on a road that requires a caravan, that is acknowledged as being risky, and is fraught with danger. And so, monks, you should recite this training rule in this way:

182. “Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjeyya, antamaso gāmantarampi, aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ samayo [M 0.0088]. Satthagamanīyo hoti maggo sāsaṅkasammato sappaṭibhayo – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

182. ‘Whatever monk, having made an arrangement with a nun, should undertake a single long journey, even so much as to another village, except for the proper occasion, it is a Pācittiya offense. Therein, this is the proper occasion: the road requires a caravan, is acknowledged as being risky, and is fraught with danger—this is the proper occasion therein.’

183. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

183. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever kind… and so on… ‘Monk’ means… and so on… in this sense, this is the monk who is intended.

Bhikkhunī nāma ubhatosaṅghe upasampannā.

A bhikkhunī is one who has been fully ordained in both Saṅghas.

Saddhinti [V 0.0090] ekato.

‘Together with’ means: as one.

Saṃvidhāyāti – “gacchāma, bhagini, gacchāmāyya; gacchāmāyya, gacchāma, bhagini; ajja vā hiyyo [T 2.0292] vā pare vā gacchāmā”ti saṃvidahati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

‘Having made an arrangement’ means: if one makes an arrangement, saying, ‘Let us go, sister; let us go, venerable sir,’ or ‘Let us go, venerable sir; let us go, sister,’ or ‘Let us go today, or tomorrow, or the day after,’ there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Antamaso gāmantarampīti kukkuṭasampāte gāme, gāmantare gāmantare āpatti pācittiyassa. Agāmake araññe, addhayojane addhayojane āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Even so much as to another village’ means: in an inhabited area, there is a Pācittiya offense for each village boundary one crosses. In a villageless wilderness, for every half-yojana, there is a Pācittiya offense.

Aññatra samayāti ṭhapetvā samayaṃ.

‘Except for the proper occasion’ means: setting aside the proper occasion.

Satthagamanīyo nāma maggo na sakkā hoti vinā satthena gantuṃ.

A road that requires a caravan is a road that is not possible to travel without a caravan.

Sāsaṅkaṃ nāma tasmiṃ magge yasmiṃ magge (?) corānaṃ niviṭṭhokāso dissati, bhuttokāso dissati, ṭhitokāso dissati, nisinnokāso dissati, nipannokāso dissati.

‘Risky’ means: on that road, a place where thieves have entered is seen, a place where they have eaten is seen, a place where they have stood is seen, a place where they have sat is seen, a place where they have lain down is seen.

Sappaṭibhayaṃ nāma tasmiṃ magge corehi manussā hatā dissanti, viluttā dissanti, ākoṭitā dissanti, sappaṭibhayaṃ [P 4.0064] gantvā appaṭibhayaṃ dassetvā uyyojetabbā – “gacchatha bhaginiyo”ti.

‘Fraught with danger’ means: on that road, people killed by thieves are seen, people robbed are seen, people beaten are seen. Having traveled through the dangerous part and shown the safe part, they should be sent on their way, saying, ‘Go, sisters.’

184. Saṃvidahite saṃvidahitasaññī ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjati, antamaso gāmantarampi, aññatra samayā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Saṃvidahite vematiko ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjati, antamaso gāmantarampi, aññatra samayā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Saṃvidahite, asaṃvidahitasaññī ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjati, antamaso gāmantarampi, aññatra samayā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

184. When an arrangement has been made, if one perceives it as arranged and undertakes a single long journey, even so much as to another village, except for the proper occasion, there is a Pācittiya offense. When an arrangement has been made, if one is in doubt and undertakes a single long journey, even so much as to another village, except for the proper occasion, there is a Pācittiya offense. When an arrangement has been made, if one perceives it as not arranged and undertakes a single long journey, even so much as to another village, except for the proper occasion, there is a Pācittiya offense.

Bhikkhu saṃvidahati bhikkhunī na saṃvidahati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Asaṃvidahite saṃvidahitasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Asaṃvidahite vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Asaṃvidahite asaṃvidahitasaññī, anāpatti.

A monk makes an arrangement, but the nun does not: there is an offense of wrong-doing. When no arrangement has been made, if one perceives it as arranged and undertakes the journey, there is an offense of wrong-doing. When no arrangement has been made, if one is in doubt and undertakes the journey, there is an offense of wrong-doing. When no arrangement has been made, if one perceives it as not arranged and undertakes the journey, there is no offense.

185. Anāpatti [M 0.0089][V 0.0091] samaye, asaṃvidahitvā gacchati, bhikkhunī saṃvidahati[T 2.0293], bhikkhu na saṃvidahati, visaṅketena gacchanti, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

185. There is no offense: on the proper occasion; if one goes without having made an arrangement; if the nun makes an arrangement but the monk does not; if they go at a different time from the one arranged; in times of calamity; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Saṃvidhānasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.

The seventh training rule, on making an arrangement, is concluded.

8. Nāvābhiruhanasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Training Rule on Embarking on a Boat

186. Tena [T 2.0294] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaṃ nāvaṃ ekanāvaṃ (syā.) abhiruhanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “yatheva mayaṃ sapajāpatikā nāvāya ekanāvāya (syā.) kīḷāma, evamevime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya nāvāya kīḷantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaṃ nāvaṃ abhiruhissantī”ti…pe… “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaṃ nāvaṃ abhiruhathā”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaṃ nāvaṃ abhiruhissatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

186. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhus of the group of six, having made an arrangement with bhikkhunīs, embarked on a single boat. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “Just as we play on a boat together with our wives, in the same way these ascetics, sons of the Sakyan, having made an arrangement with bhikkhunīs, play on a boat!” The bhikkhus heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhus who were of few desires… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the bhikkhus of the group of six, having made an arrangement with bhikkhunīs, embark on a single boat?” … “Is it true, bhikkhus, as is said, that you, having made an arrangement with bhikkhunīs, embark on a single boat?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “Worthless men, how indeed could you, having made an arrangement with bhikkhunīs, embark on a single boat? This, worthless men, does not lead to the faith of the faithless… And so, bhikkhus, you should set forth this training rule in this way:

“Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaṃ nāvaṃ ekanāvaṃ (syā.) abhiruheyya, uddhaṃgāminiṃ vā adhogāminiṃ [T 2.0295] vā, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever bhikkhu, having made an arrangement with a bhikkhunī, should embark on a single boat, whether going upstream or downstream, it is an offense of expiation.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

In this way, this training rule was laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

187. Tena [P 4.0065] kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca sāketā sāvatthiṃ addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti. Antarāmagge nadī taritabbā uttaritabbā (syā.) hoti. Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo te bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “mayampi ayyehi saddhiṃ uttarissāmā”ti. “Na, bhaginī, kappati bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaṃ nāvaṃ abhiruhituṃ; tumhe vā paṭhamaṃ uttaratha mayaṃ vā uttarissāmā”ti[M 0.0090]. “Ayyā, bhante, aggapurisā. Ayyāva paṭhamaṃ uttarantū”ti. Atha kho tāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ pacchā uttarantīnaṃ corā acchindiṃsu ca dūsesuñca[V 0.0092]. Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo sāvatthiṃ gantvā bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tiriyaṃ taraṇāya bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaṃ nāvaṃ abhiruhituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

187. Now at that time, many bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs were traveling on the long road from Sāketa to Sāvatthī. On the way, a river had to be crossed. Then those bhikkhunīs said to those bhikkhus: “We too will cross together with the venerable sirs.” “Sisters, it is not allowable to embark on a single boat having made an arrangement with a bhikkhunī. Either you cross first, or we will cross.” “Venerable sirs, you are excellent men. Let the venerable sirs cross first.” Then, as those bhikkhunīs were crossing afterwards, robbers robbed and violated them. Then those bhikkhunīs, having gone to Sāvatthī, reported this matter to the bhikkhunīs. The bhikkhunīs reported this matter to the bhikkhus. The bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then, on this occasion, in this matter, the Blessed One, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow you to embark on a single boat with a bhikkhunī after making an arrangement for the purpose of crossing over. And so, bhikkhus, you should set forth this training rule in this way:

188. “Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaṃ nāvaṃ abhiruheyya uddhaṃgāminiṃ vā adhogāminiṃ vā, aññatra tiriyaṃ taraṇāya, pācittiya”nti.

188. “Whatever bhikkhu, having made an arrangement with a bhikkhunī, should embark on a single boat, whether going upstream or downstream, except for crossing over, it is an offense of expiation.”

189. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

189. Whatever: whichever… A bhikkhu: …in this matter, this is the bhikkhu who is meant.

Bhikkhunī nāma ubhatosaṅghe upasampannā[T 2.0296].

A bhikkhunī is one who has received the higher ordination in both Saṅghas.

Saddhinti ekato.

Together with: as one.

Saṃvidhāyāti “abhiruhāma, bhagini, abhiruhāmāyya; abhiruhāmāyya, abhiruhāma, bhagini; ajja vā hiyyo vā pare vā abhiruhāmā”ti saṃvidahati āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Having made an arrangement: If one makes an arrangement, saying: “Let us embark, sister; let us embark, venerable sir. Let us embark, venerable sir; let us embark, sister. Let us embark today, or tomorrow, or the day after tomorrow,” it is an offense of wrong conduct.

Bhikkhuniyā abhiruḷhe bhikkhu abhiruhati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Bhikkhumhi abhiruḷhe bhikkhunī abhiruhati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ubho vā abhiruhanti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

When a bhikkhunī has embarked, a bhikkhu embarks; it is an offense of expiation. When a bhikkhu has embarked, a bhikkhunī embarks; it is an offense of expiation. Or if both embark, it is an offense of expiation.

Uddhaṃgāmininti ujjavanikāya.

Going upstream: by a boat going upstream.

Adhogāmininti ojavanikāya.

Going downstream: by a boat going downstream.

Aññatra tiriyaṃ taraṇāyāti ṭhapetvā tiriyaṃ taraṇaṃ.

Except for crossing over: setting aside crossing over.

Kukkuṭasampāte gāme, gāmantare gāmantare āpatti pācittiyassa. Agāmake araññe, aḍḍhayojane aḍḍhayojane āpatti pācittiyassa.

In a village within a chicken's flight, for every village interval, it is an offense of expiation. In a forest without villages, for every half-yojana, it is an offense of expiation.

190. Saṃvidahite [V 0.0093] saṃvidahitasaññī ekaṃ nāvaṃ abhiruhati uddhaṃgāminiṃ vā adhogāminiṃ vā, aññatra tiriyaṃ taraṇāya[P 4.0066], āpatti pācittiyassa. Saṃvidahite [M 0.0091] vematiko ekaṃ nāvaṃ abhiruhati uddhaṃgāminiṃ vā adhogāminiṃ vā, aññatra tiriyaṃ taraṇāya, āpatti pācittiyassa. Saṃvidahite asaṃvidahitasaññī ekaṃ nāvaṃ abhiruhati uddhaṃgāminiṃ vā adhogāminiṃ vā, aññatra tiriyaṃ taraṇāya, āpatti pācittiyassa.

190. When an arrangement has been made, if one is perceptive that an arrangement has been made and embarks on a single boat going upstream or downstream, except for crossing over, it is an offense of expiation. When an arrangement has been made, if one is doubtful and embarks on a single boat going upstream or downstream, except for crossing over, it is an offense of expiation. When an arrangement has been made, if one is perceptive that no arrangement has been made and embarks on a single boat going upstream or downstream, except for crossing over, it is an offense of expiation.

Bhikkhu saṃvidahati, bhikkhunī na saṃvidahati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Asaṃvidahite saṃvidahitasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Asaṃvidahite vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Asaṃvidahite, asaṃvidahitasaññī, anāpatti.

A bhikkhu makes an arrangement, but the bhikkhunī does not; it is an offense of wrong conduct. When no arrangement has been made, if one is perceptive that an arrangement has been made, it is an offense of wrong conduct. When no arrangement has been made, if one is doubtful, it is an offense of wrong conduct. When no arrangement has been made, if one is perceptive that no arrangement has been made, there is no offense.

191. Anāpatti tiriyaṃ taraṇāya, asaṃvidahitvā abhiruhanti, bhikkhunī [T 2.0297] saṃvidahati, bhikkhu na saṃvidahati, visaṅketena abhiruhanti, āpadāsu ummattakassa, ādikammissāti.

191. There is no offense: for crossing over; if they embark without having made an arrangement; if a bhikkhunī makes an arrangement but the bhikkhu does not; if they embark by a missed appointment; in times of danger; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Nāvābhiruhanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The eighth training rule, on embarking on a boat, is finished.

9. Paripācitasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Training Rule on Specially Prepared Food

192. Tena [T 2.0298] samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī aññatarassa kulassa kulūpikā hoti niccabhattikā. Tena ca gahapatinā therā bhikkhū nimantitā honti. Atha kho thullanandā bhikkhunī pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena taṃ kulaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “kimidaṃ, gahapati, pahūtaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyatta”nti? “Therā mayā, ayye, nimantitā”ti. “Ke pana te, gahapati, therā”ti? “Ayyo sāriputto ayyo mahāmoggallāno ayyo mahākaccāno ayyo mahākoṭṭhiko ayyo mahākappino ayyo mahācundo ayyo anuruddho ayyo revato ayyo upāli ayyo ānando ayyo rāhulo”ti. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, gahapati, mahānāge tiṭṭhamāne ceṭake nimantesī”ti?

192. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Ground. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā was one who frequented a certain family and had a regular meal there. And by that householder, the elder bhikkhus had been invited. Then the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having dressed in the morning and taken her bowl and robe, approached that household. Having approached, she said this to that householder: “Why, householder, is this abundant hard and soft food prepared?” “The elders, venerable lady, have been invited by me.” “But who, householder, are those elders of yours?” “The Venerable Sāriputta, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, the Venerable Mahākaccāna, the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita, the Venerable Mahākappina, the Venerable Mahācunda, the Venerable Anuruddha, the Venerable Revata, the Venerable Upāli, the Venerable Ānanda, and the Venerable Rāhula.” “But why, householder, while the great Arahants are present, do you invite junior monks?”

“Ke pana te, ayye, mahānāgā”ti? “Ayyo devadatto ayyo kokāliko ayyo kaṭamodakatissako kaṭamorakatissako (sī.) katamorakatissako (syā.) ayyo khaṇḍadeviyā putto [M 0.0092] ayyo samuddadatto”ti. Ayaṃ carahi thullanandāya [V 0.0094] bhikkhuniyā antarā kathā vippakatā, atha te therā bhikkhū pavisiṃsu. “Saccaṃ mahānāgā kho tayā, gahapati, nimantitā”ti. “Idāneva kho tvaṃ, ayye, ceṭake akāsi; idāni [T 2.0299] mahānāge”ti. Gharato ca nikkaḍḍhi, niccabhattañca pacchindi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma devadatto jānaṃ bhikkhuniparipācitaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjissatī”ti…pe… “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, devadatta, jānaṃ bhikkhuniparipācitaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjasī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, jānaṃ bhikkhuniparipācitaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjissasi. Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

“But who, venerable lady, are those great Arahants of yours?” “The Venerable Devadatta, the Venerable Kokālika, the Venerable Kaṭamodakatissaka, the Venerable son of Khaṇḍadevī, and the Venerable Samuddadatta.” While this conversation of the bhikkhunī Thullanandā was still unfinished, those elder bhikkhus entered. She said, “Householder, it is true that great Arahants have been invited by you.” He replied, “Just now, venerable lady, you made them into junior monks; now you make them into great Arahants.” And he drove her out of the house and cut off her regular meal. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could Devadatta knowingly eat almsfood arranged by a bhikkhunī?”… “Is it true, Devadatta, that you knowingly ate almsfood arranged by a bhikkhunī?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “How indeed, worthless man, could you knowingly eat almsfood arranged by a bhikkhunī? This, worthless man, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule in this way:

“Yo [P 4.0067] pana bhikkhu jānaṃ bhikkhuniparipācitaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjeyya, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever bhikkhu should knowingly eat almsfood arranged by a bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

Thus this training rule was laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

193. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu rājagahā pabbajito ñātikulaṃ agamāsi. Manussā – “cirassampi bhadanto āgato”ti sakkaccaṃ bhattaṃ akaṃsu. Tassa kulassa kulūpikā bhikkhunī te manusse etadavoca – “dethayyassa, āvuso, bhatta”nti. Atha kho so bhikkhu – “bhagavatā paṭikkhittaṃ jānaṃ bhikkhuniparipācitaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjitu”nti kukkuccāyanto na paṭiggahesi. Nāsakkhi piṇḍāya carituṃ, chinnabhatto ahosi. Atha kho so bhikkhu ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ [T 2.0300] kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pubbe gihisamārambhe jānaṃ bhikkhuniparipācitaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

193. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu who had gone forth from Rājagaha went to his relatives' family. The people, thinking, “The good master has come after a long time,” respectfully prepared a meal. A bhikkhunī who frequented that family said to those people, “Friends, give the meal to the venerable one.” Then that bhikkhu, being scrupulous and thinking, “It has been forbidden by the Blessed One to knowingly eat almsfood arranged by a bhikkhunī,” did not accept it. He was unable to go for alms; he was without a meal. Then that bhikkhu, having gone to the monastery, reported this matter to the bhikkhus. The bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this context, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus: “I allow, bhikkhus, to eat almsfood arranged by a bhikkhunī, knowing it to be so, when it was previously arranged by laypeople. And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule in this way:

194. “Yo pana bhikkhu jānaṃ bhikkhuniparipācitaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjeyya, aññatra pubbe gihisamārambhā, pācittiya”nti.

194. “Whatever bhikkhu should knowingly eat almsfood arranged by a bhikkhunī, except when previously arranged by laypeople, it is an offense of expiation.”

195. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

195. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever sort… ‘Bhikkhu’ means: …in this sense, this is the bhikkhu who is meant.

Jānāti [M 0.0093][V 0.0095] nāma sāmaṃ vā jānāti aññe vā tassa ārocenti sā vā āroceti.

‘Knows’ means: either he knows by himself, or others inform him, or she informs him.

Bhikkhunī nāma ubhatosaṅghe upasampannā.

‘Bhikkhunī’ means: one who is ordained in both Saṅghas.

Paripāceti nāma pubbe adātukāmānaṃ akattukāmānaṃ – “ayyo bhāṇako, ayyo bahussuto, ayyo suttantiko, ayyo vinayadharo, ayyo dhammakathiko, detha ayyassa, karotha ayyassā”ti esā paripāceti nāma.

‘Arranges’ means: regarding those previously unwilling to give or to act, she persuades them by saying, “The venerable one is a reciter, the venerable one is very learned, the venerable one is an expert on the Suttas, the venerable one is a master of the Vinaya, the venerable one is a Dhamma-preacher. Give to the venerable one! Act for the venerable one!” This is what ‘arranges’ means.

Piṇḍapāto nāma pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ aññataraṃ bhojanaṃ.

‘Almsfood’ means: any one of the five kinds of staple food.

Aññatra pubbe gihisamārambhāti ṭhapetvā gihisamārambhaṃ.

‘Except when previously arranged by laypeople’ means: setting aside that which is arranged by laypeople.

Gihisamārambho nāma ñātakā vā honti pavāritā vā pakatipaṭiyattaṃ vā.

‘Arrangement by laypeople’ means: it is by relatives, or by those who have invited him, or it is prepared as a regular practice.

Aññatra pubbe gihisamārambhā bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre, āpatti pācittiyassa.

If, except in a case previously arranged by laypeople, he accepts it thinking, ‘I will eat,’ he commits an offense of wrong conduct. For every mouthful, he commits an offense of expiation.

196. Paripācite [P 4.0068] paripācitasaññī bhuñjati, aññatra pubbe gihisamārambhā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Paripācite vematiko bhuñjati, aññatra pubbe gihisamārambhā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Paripācite [T 2.0301] aparipācitasaññī bhuñjati, aññatra pubbe gihisamārambhā, anāpatti. Ekatoupasampannāya paripācitaṃ bhuñjati, aññatra pubbe gihisamārambhā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Aparipācite paripācitasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Aparipācitte vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Aparipācite aparipācitasaññī, anāpatti.

196. If it was arranged, and he perceives it as arranged, he commits an offense of expiation if he eats it, unless it was previously arranged by laypeople. If it was arranged, but he is uncertain, he commits an offense of wrong conduct if he eats it, unless it was previously arranged by laypeople. If it was arranged, but he perceives it as not arranged, there is no offense if he eats it. If he eats food arranged by a bhikkhunī ordained in only one Saṅgha, he commits an offense of wrong conduct, unless it was previously arranged by laypeople. If it was not arranged, but he perceives it as arranged, he commits an offense of wrong conduct. If it was not arranged, but he is uncertain, he commits an offense of wrong conduct. If it was not arranged, and he perceives it as not arranged, there is no offense.

197. Anāpatti pubbe gihisamārambhe, sikkhamānā paripāceti, sāmaṇerī paripāceti, pañca bhojanāni ṭhapetvā sabbattha anāpatti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

197. There is no offense: if it was previously arranged by laypeople; if a probationer arranges it; if a female novice arranges it; for any edible apart from the five kinds of staple food; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Paripācitasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.

The ninth training rule, on arranged food, is finished.

10. Rahonisajjasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Training Rule on Sitting in Seclusion

198. Tena [T 2.0302][V 0.0096] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato udāyissa [M 0.0094] purāṇadutiyikā bhikkhunīsu pabbajitā hoti. Sā āyasmato udāyissa santike abhikkhaṇaṃ āgacchati, āyasmāpi udāyī tassā bhikkhuniyā santike abhikkhaṇaṃ gacchati. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā udāyī tassā bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappesi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā udāyī bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, udāyi, bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappesīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappessasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

198. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the former wife of the Venerable Udāyī had gone forth among the bhikkhunīs. She frequently came to the Venerable Udāyī, and the Venerable Udāyī also frequently went to that bhikkhunī. On that occasion, the Venerable Udāyī sat with that bhikkhunī, one-on-one in a secluded place. Those bhikkhus who were of few desires… they complained, became indignant, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the Venerable Udāyī sit with a bhikkhunī, one-on-one in a secluded place?”… “Is it true, as is said, Udāyī, that you sat with a bhikkhunī, one-on-one in a secluded place?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “Worthless man, how indeed could you sit with a bhikkhunī, one-on-one in a secluded place? Worthless man, this is not for inspiring confidence in the uninspired… And so, bhikkhus, you should set forth this training rule in this way:

199. “Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappeyya, pācittiya”nti.

199. “Whatever bhikkhu should sit with a bhikkhunī, one-on-one in a secluded place, it is an offense of expiation.”

200. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

200. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhu’ means… in this sense, this one is intended as ‘bhikkhu’.

Bhikkhunī nāma ubhatosaṅghe upasampannā[T 2.0303].

A ‘bhikkhunī’ is one who is ordained in both Saṅghas.

Saddhinti ekato.

‘With’ means together.

Eko ekāyāti bhikkhu ceva hoti bhikkhunī ca.

‘One with one’ means there is a bhikkhu and a bhikkhunī.

pāci. 286, 291; pārā. 445,454 Raho [P 4.0069] nāma cakkhussa raho sotassa raho. Cakkhussa raho nāma na sakkā hoti akkhiṃ vā nikhaṇīyamāne bhamukaṃ vā ukkhipīyamāne sīsaṃ vā ukkhipīyamāne passituṃ. Sotassa raho nāma na sakkā hoti pakatikathā sotuṃ.

‘Secluded’ means out of sight and out of hearing. ‘Out of sight’ means it is not possible to see by winking the eye, or by raising the eyebrow, or by raising the head. ‘Out of hearing’ means it is not possible to hear ordinary speech.

Nisajjaṃ [V 0.0097] kappeyyāti bhikkhuniyā nisinnāya bhikkhu upanisinno vā hoti upanipanno vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should sit’ means: if a bhikkhu sits near or lies down near a bhikkhunī who is sitting, he incurs an offense of expiation.

Bhikkhu nisinne bhikkhunī upanisinnā vā hoti upanipannā vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ubho vā nisinnā honti ubho vā nipannā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

If a bhikkhunī sits near or lies down near a bhikkhu who is sitting, he incurs an offense of expiation. If both are sitting or if both are lying down, he incurs an offense of expiation.

201. Raho [M 0.0095] rahosaññī eko ekāya nisajjaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Raho vematiko eko ekāya nisajjaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Raho arahosaññī eko ekāya nisajjaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

201. If he sits one-on-one in a secluded place, perceiving it as secluded, he incurs an offense of expiation. If he sits one-on-one in a secluded place while being uncertain, he incurs an offense of expiation. If he sits one-on-one in a secluded place, perceiving it as not secluded, he incurs an offense of expiation.

Araho rahosaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Araho vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Araho arahosaññī, anāpatti.

In a place that is not secluded, if he perceives it as secluded, he incurs an offense of wrong conduct. In a place that is not secluded, if he is uncertain, he incurs an offense of wrong conduct. In a place that is not secluded, if he perceives it as not secluded, there is no offense.

202. Anāpatti yo koci viññū dutiyo hoti, tiṭṭhati na nisīdati, arahopekkho, aññavihito nisīdati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

202. There is no offense if there is any discerning person as a companion, if one stands and does not sit, if one is not seeking seclusion, if one sits with one's mind on something else, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Rahonisajjasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

The tenth training rule, on sitting in a secluded place, is finished.

Ovādavaggo tatiyo.

The third chapter, the Chapter on Admonition, is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary is as follows:

Asammataatthaṅgatū[T 2.0304], passayāmisadānena;

Sibbati addhānaṃ nāvaṃ bhuñjeyya, eko ekāya te dasāti.

Unauthorized, sunset, dwelling, material gain, giving, sewing, a journey, a boat, eating, one with one—these are the ten.

4. Bhojanavaggo

4. The Chapter on Food

1. Āvasathapiṇḍasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The Training Rule on Almsfood from a Public Rest House

203. Tena [T 2.0305][V 0.0098] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sāvatthiyā avidūre aññatarassa pūgassa āvasathapiṇḍo paññatto hoti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pavisitvā piṇḍaṃ alabhamānā āvasathaṃ agamaṃsu. Manussā – “cirassampi bhadantā āgatā”ti te sakkaccaṃ parivisiṃsu. Atha kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhū dutiyampi divasaṃ…pe… tatiyampi divasaṃ pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pavisitvā piṇḍaṃ alabhamānā āvasathaṃ gantvā bhuñjiṃsu. Atha kho chabbaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kiṃ mayaṃ karissāma ārāmaṃ gantvā! Hiyyopi idheva āgantabbaṃ bhavissatī”ti, tattheva anuvasitvā anuvasitvā [P 4.0070] āvasathapiṇḍaṃ bhuñjanti.
