Titthiyā apasakkanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma [M 0.0096] samaṇā sakyaputtiyā anuvasitvā anuvasitvā āvasathapiṇḍaṃ bhuñjissanti! Nayimesaññeva āvasathapiṇḍo paññatto; sabbesaññeva āvasathapiṇḍo paññatto”ti.

203. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, not far from Sāvatthī, almsfood at a public rest house had been provided by a certain association. The group-of-six bhikkhus, having dressed in the morning, taking their bowls and robes, entered Sāvatthī for alms. Not receiving alms, they went to the public rest house. The people said, “The venerable ones have come after a long time,” and served them respectfully. Then, on the second day… and on the third day, the group-of-six bhikkhus, having dressed in the morning, taking their bowls and robes, entered Sāvatthī for alms. Not receiving alms, they went to the public rest house and ate. Then this thought occurred to the group-of-six bhikkhus: “What shall we do by going to the monastery? Tomorrow, too, we will have to come right here.” Staying there day after day, they ate the almsfood from the public rest house. The sectarians went away. The people complained, became indignant, and spread it about, saying: “How can the Sakyan ascetics stay day after day and eat the almsfood from the public rest house? This almsfood at the public rest house was not provided for them alone; it was provided for everyone.”

Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū anuvasitvā anuvasitvā āvasathapiṇḍaṃ bhuñjissantīti…pe… [T 2.0306] saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, anuvasitvā anuvasitvā āvasathapiṇḍaṃ bhuñjathāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, anuvasitvā anuvasitvā āvasathapiṇḍaṃ bhuñjissatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

The bhikkhus heard those people complaining, becoming indignant, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhus who were of few desires… complained, became indignant, and spread it about, saying: “How can the group-of-six bhikkhus stay day after day and eat the almsfood from the public rest house?”… “Is it true, bhikkhus, as is said, that you stay day after day and eat the almsfood from the public rest house?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “Worthless men, how can you stay day after day and eat the almsfood from the public rest house? This, worthless men, is not for inspiring confidence in the uninspired… And so, bhikkhus, you should set forth this training rule in this way:

“Eko āvasathapiṇḍo bhuñjitabbo. Tato ce uttariṃ bhuñjeyya, pācittiya”nti.

“Almsfood from a public rest house may be eaten once. If one should eat more than that, it is an offense of expiation.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And in this way, this training rule was laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

204. Tena [V 0.0099] kho pana samayena āyasmā sāriputto kosalesu janapade sāvatthiṃ gacchanto yena aññataro āvasatho tenupasaṅkami. Manussā – “cirassampi thero āgato”ti sakkaccaṃ parivisiṃsu. Atha kho āyasmato sāriputtassa bhuttāvissa kharo ābādho uppajji, nāsakkhi tamhā āvasathā pakkamituṃ. Atha kho te manussā dutiyampi divasaṃ āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – “bhuñjatha, bhante”ti. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto – “bhagavatā paṭikkhittaṃ anuvasitvā anuvasitvā āvasathapiṇḍaṃ bhuñjitu”nti kukkuccāyanto na paṭiggahesi; chinnabhatto ahosi. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto sāvatthiṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi [T 2.0307] – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānena bhikkhunā anuvasitvā anuvasitvā āvasathapiṇḍaṃ bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

204. Now at that time, the Venerable Sāriputta, while traveling through the Kosalan country on his way to Sāvatthī, approached a certain public rest house. The people said, “The elder has come after a long time,” and served him respectfully. Then, after the Venerable Sāriputta had eaten, a severe illness arose, and he was unable to depart from that public rest house. On the second day, those people said this to the Venerable Sāriputta: “Please eat, venerable sir.” But the Venerable Sāriputta, feeling scrupulous and thinking, “The Blessed One has forbidden eating the almsfood from a public rest house day after day,” did not accept. He was without food. Then the Venerable Sāriputta went to Sāvatthī and informed the monks of this matter. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow a sick monk to eat the almsfood from a public rest house day after day. And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

205. “Agilānena bhikkhunā eko āvasathapiṇḍo bhuñjitabbo. Tato ce uttari bhuñjeyya, pācittiya”nti.

205. “A monk who is not sick may eat one meal of almsfood from a public rest house. If he should eat more than that, it is an offense of expiation.”

206. Agilāno [M 0.0097] nāma sakkoti tamhā āvasathā pakkamituṃ.

206. Not sick means one is able to depart from that public rest house.

Gilāno nāma na sakkoti tamhā āvasathā pakkamituṃ.

Sick means one is not able to depart from that public rest house.

Āvasathapiṇḍo [P 4.0071] nāma pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ aññataraṃ bhojanaṃ – sālāya vā maṇḍape vā rukkhamūle vā ajjhokāse vā anodissa yāvadattho paññatto hoti. Agilānena bhikkhunā sakiṃ bhuñjitabbo. Tato ce uttari ‘bhuñjissāmī’ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

Almsfood from a public rest house means any one of the five staple foods, provided in a hall, a pavilion, at the foot of a tree, or in an open space, without specific dedication, as much as is wanted. A monk who is not sick may eat it once. If he accepts more than that with the thought, “I will eat,” it is an offense of wrong-doing. For every mouthful eaten, it is an offense of expiation.

207. Agilāno agilānasaññī tatuttari āvasathapiṇḍaṃ bhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Agilāno vematiko tatuttari āvasathapiṇḍaṃ bhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Agilāno gilānasaññī tatuttariṃ āvasathapiṇḍaṃ bhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

207. If a monk who is not sick, perceiving himself as not sick, eats more than that of the almsfood from the public rest house, it is an offense of expiation. If a monk who is not sick, being doubtful, eats more than that of the almsfood from the public rest house, it is an offense of expiation. If a monk who is not sick, perceiving himself as sick, eats more than that of the almsfood from the public rest house, it is an offense of expiation.

Gilāno [V 0.0100] agilānasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Gilāno vematiko āpatti dukkaṭassa. Gilāno gilānasaññī, anāpatti.

If a monk who is sick, perceiving himself as not sick, eats, it is an offense of wrong-doing. If a monk who is sick, being doubtful, eats, it is an offense of wrong-doing. If a monk who is sick, perceiving himself as sick, eats, there is no offense.

208. Anāpatti gilānassa, agilāno sakiṃ bhuñjati, gacchanto, vā āgacchanto vā bhuñjati, sāmikā nimantetvā bhojenti, odissa [T 2.0308] paññatto hoti, na yāvadattho paññatto hoti, pañca bhojanāni ṭhapetvā sabbattha anāpatti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

208. There is no offense: for one who is sick; if one who is not sick eats once; if one eats while going or coming; if the owners invite and serve the food; if it is provided with specific dedication; if it is not provided as 'as much as is wanted'; in all cases of edibles, excepting the five staple foods; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Āvasathapiṇḍasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The first training rule, concerning almsfood from a public rest house, is finished.

2. Gaṇabhojanasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Training Rule Concerning Group Meals

209. Tena [T 2.0309] samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena devadatto parihīnalābhasakkāro sapariso kulesu viññāpetvā viññāpetvā bhuñjati. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā kulesu viññāpetvā viññāpetvā bhuñjissanti! Kassa sampannaṃ na manāpaṃ, kassa sāduṃ na ruccatī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti [M 0.0098] khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma devadatto sapariso kulesu viññāpetvā viññāpetvā bhuñjissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, devadatta, sapariso kulesu viññāpetvā viññāpetvā bhuñjasīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, sapariso kulesu viññāpetvā viññāpetvā bhuñjissasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

209. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Ground. Now at that time, Devadatta, whose gains and honor had declined, was going from family to family with his retinue, repeatedly requesting and eating. People complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How can these Sakyan ascetics go from family to family, repeatedly requesting and eating? Who does not find a delicious meal agreeable? Who does not enjoy what is tasty?” The monks heard these people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those monks who were of few desires… they complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How can Devadatta with his retinue go from family to family, repeatedly requesting and eating?” … “Is it true, Devadatta, that you with your retinue go from family to family, repeatedly requesting and eating?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him: “… Worthless man, how can you with your retinue go from family to family, repeatedly requesting and eating? This, worthless man, will not lead to confidence in the unconvinced… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Gaṇabhojane pācittiya”nti.

“In the case of a group meal, it is an offense of expiation.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

In this way, this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.

210. Tena [T 2.0310][P 4.0072] kho pana samayena manussā gilāne bhikkhū bhattena nimantenti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nādhivāsenti – “paṭikkhittaṃ bhagavatā gaṇabhojana”nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi [V 0.0101] – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānena bhikkhunā gaṇabhojanaṃ bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

210. Now at that time, people invited sick monks for a meal. The monks, being scrupulous, did not consent, thinking, “The group meal has been prohibited by the Blessed One.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow a sick monk to eat a group meal. And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Gaṇabhojane, aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Gilānasamayo – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

“In the case of a group meal, except for an occasion, it is an offense of expiation. Therein, this is the occasion: the time of sickness—this is the occasion therein.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

In this way, this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.

211. Tena kho pana samayena manussā cīvaradānasamaye sacīvarabhattaṃ paṭiyādetvā bhikkhū nimantenti – “bhojetvā cīvarena acchādessāmā”ti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nādhivāsenti – “paṭikkhittaṃ bhagavatā gaṇabhojana”nti. Cīvaraṃ parittaṃ uppajjati. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cīvaradānasamaye gaṇabhojanaṃ bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

211. Now at that time, at the time of giving robes, people prepared a meal together with robes and invited the monks, thinking, “Having fed them, we will clothe them with robes.” The monks, being scrupulous, did not consent, thinking, “The group meal has been prohibited by the Blessed One.” Few robes arose. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Monks, I allow a group meal to be eaten at the time of giving robes. And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Gaṇabhojane, aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Gilānasamayo, cīvaradānasamayo – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

“There is an offence of expiation for eating a group meal, except on an occasion. In this connection, this is the occasion: a time of illness, a time of giving robes—this is the occasion in this connection.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

In this way, this training rule was laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

212. Tena kho pana samayena manussā cīvarakārake bhikkhū bhattena nimantenti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nādhivāsenti – “paṭikkhittaṃ bhagavatā [T 2.0311] gaṇabhojana”nti[M 0.0099]. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cīvarakārasamaye gaṇabhojanaṃ bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

212. Now at that time, people invited bhikkhus who were making robes for a meal. The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not consent, thinking, “A group meal has been prohibited by the Blessed One.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Bhikkhus, I allow a group meal to be eaten at the time of robe-making. And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Gaṇabhojane, aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Gilānasamayo, cīvaradānasamayo, cīvarakārasamayo – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

“There is an offence of expiation for eating a group meal, except on an occasion. In this connection, this is the occasion: a time of illness, a time of giving robes, a time of making robes—this is the occasion in this connection.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

In this way, this training rule was laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

213. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū manussehi saddhiṃ addhānaṃ [P 4.0073] gacchanti. Atha kho [V 0.0102] te bhikkhū te manusse etadavocuṃ – “muhuttaṃ, āvuso, āgametha; piṇḍāya carissāmā”ti. Te evamāhaṃsu – “idheva, bhante, bhuñjathā”ti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā na paṭiggaṇhanti – “paṭikkhittaṃ bhagavatā gaṇabhojana”nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, addhānagamanasamaye gaṇabhojanaṃ bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

213. Now at that time, bhikkhus were going on a long journey together with some people. Then those bhikkhus said to those people: “Friends, please wait a moment; we will go for alms-food.” They replied: “Venerable sirs, please eat right here.” The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not accept, thinking: “A group meal has been prohibited by the Blessed One.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Bhikkhus, I allow a group meal to be eaten at the time of going on a journey. And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Gaṇabhojane, aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Gilānasamayo, cīvaradānasamayo, cīvarakārasamayo, addhānagamanasamayo – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

“There is an offence of expiation for eating a group meal, except on an occasion. In this connection, this is the occasion: a time of illness, a time of giving robes, a time of making robes, a time of going on a journey—this is the occasion in this connection.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

In this way, this training rule was laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

214. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū manussehi saddhiṃ nāvāya gacchanti. Atha kho te bhikkhū te manusse etadavocuṃ – “muhuttaṃ, āvuso, tīraṃ upanetha; piṇḍāya carissāmā”ti. Te evamāhaṃsu [T 2.0312] – “idheva, bhante, bhuñjathā”ti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā na paṭiggaṇhanti – “paṭikkhittaṃ bhagavatā gaṇabhojana”nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, nāvābhiruhanasamaye gaṇabhojanaṃ bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

214. Now at that time, bhikkhus were traveling by boat together with some people. Then those bhikkhus said to those people: “Friends, please bring the boat to shore for a moment; we will go for alms-food.” They replied: “Venerable sirs, please eat right here.” The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not accept, thinking: “A group meal has been prohibited by the Blessed One.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Bhikkhus, I allow a group meal to be eaten at the time of embarking on a boat. And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Gaṇabhojane, aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Gilānasamayo, cīvaradānasamayo, cīvarakārasamayo, addhānagamanasamayo, nāvābhiruhanasamayo – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

“There is an offence of expiation for eating a group meal, except on an occasion. In this connection, this is the occasion: a time of illness, a time of giving robes, a time of making robes, a time of going on a journey, a time of embarking on a boat—this is the occasion in this connection.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

In this way, this training rule was laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

215. Tena [M 0.0100]0 kho pana samayena disāsu vassaṃvuṭṭhā bhikkhū rājagahaṃ āgacchanti bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Manussā nānāverajjake bhikkhū passitvā bhattena nimantenti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nādhivāsenti – “paṭikkhittaṃ bhagavatā gaṇabhojana”nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mahāsamaye gaṇabhojanaṃ bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

215. Now at that time, bhikkhus who had spent the rains in various regions came to Rājagaha to see the Blessed One. People, seeing bhikkhus from various districts, invited them for a meal. The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not consent, thinking, “A group meal has been prohibited by the Blessed One.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Bhikkhus, I allow a group meal to be eaten on a great occasion. And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Gaṇabhojane[V 0.0103], aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Gilānasamayo, cīvaradānasamayo, cīvarakārasamayo, addhānagamanasamayo, nāvābhiruhanasamayo, mahāsamayo – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

“There is an offence of expiation for eating a group meal, except on an occasion. In this connection, this is the occasion: a time of illness, a time of giving robes, a time of making robes, a time of going on a journey, a time of embarking on a boat, a great occasion—this is the occasion in this connection.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

In this way, this training rule was laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

216. Tena [P 4.0074] kho pana samayena rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa ñātisālohito ājīvakesu pabbajito hoti. Atha kho so [T 2.0313] ājīvako yena rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ seniyaṃ bimbisāraṃ etadavoca – “icchāmahaṃ, mahārāja, sabbapāsaṇḍikabhattaṃ kātu”nti. “Sace tvaṃ, bhante, buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṭhamaṃ bhojeyyāsi”. “Evaṃ kareyyāmī”ti. Atha kho so ājīvako bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – “adhivāsentu me bhikkhū svātanāya bhatta”nti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nādhivāsenti – “paṭikkhittaṃ bhagavatā gaṇabhojana”nti. Atha kho so ājīvako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho so ājīvako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “bhavampi gotamo pabbajito, ahampi pabbajito; arahati pabbajito pabbajitassa piṇḍaṃ paṭiggahetuṃ. Adhivāsetu me bhavaṃ gotamo svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho so ājīvako bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, samaṇabhattasamaye gaṇabhojanaṃ bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

216. Now at that time, a blood relative of King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha had gone forth among the Ājīvakas. Then that Ājīvaka approached King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha and said to him: “Great king, I wish to prepare a meal for all ascetic groups.” The king replied: “Venerable sir, if you would first feed the community of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha, I will do so.” Then that Ājīvaka sent a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying: “May the bhikkhus accept my meal for tomorrow.” The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not consent, thinking: “A group meal has been prohibited by the Blessed One.” Then that Ājīvaka approached the Blessed One, exchanged greetings, and after an exchange of friendly and courteous conversation, stood to one side. Standing there, he said to the Blessed One: “The venerable Gotama is a renunciant, and I am a renunciant. It is fitting for a renunciant to accept alms from a renunciant. May the venerable Gotama accept tomorrow's meal together with the community of bhikkhus.” The Blessed One consented by remaining silent. Understanding the Blessed One's consent, the Ājīvaka departed. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow a group meal to be eaten at the time of a meal given by an ascetic. And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

217. Gaṇabhojane [M 0.0101], aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Gilānasamayo, cīvaradānasamayo, cīvarakārasamayo, addhānagamanasamayo, nāvābhiruhanasamayo, mahāsamayo, samaṇabhattasamayo – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

217. “In the case of a group meal, except at the proper time, there is an offense of pācittiya. Herein, this is the proper time: the time of sickness, the time of robe-giving, the time of robe-making, the time of going on a journey, the time of embarking on a boat, a great occasion, the time of a meal for ascetics—this is the proper time herein.”

218. Gaṇabhojanaṃ [T 2.0314] nāma yattha cattāro bhikkhū pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ aññatarena bhojanena nimantitā bhuñjanti. Etaṃ gaṇabhojanaṃ nāma.

218. What is called a group meal? It is where four monks, having been invited with any one of the five staple foods, eat. This is called a group meal.

Aññatra samayāti ṭhapetvā samayaṃ.

“Except at the proper time” means excluding the proper time.

Gilānasamayo [V 0.0104] nāma antamaso pādāpi phalitā phālitā (syā. ka.) honti. “Gilānasamayo”ti bhuñjitabbaṃ.

The time of sickness is when, at the very least, even one's feet are cracked. One may eat, considering it 'the time of sickness'.

Cīvaradānasamayo nāma anatthate kathine vassānassa pacchimo māso, atthate kathine pañcamāsā. “Cīvaradānasamayo”ti bhuñjitabbaṃ.

The time of robe-giving is, when the Kathina has not been spread, the last month of the rains retreat; when the Kathina has been spread, it is five months. One may eat, considering it 'the time of robe-giving'.

Cīvarakārasamayo nāma cīvare kayiramāne. “Cīvarakārasamayo”ti bhuñjitabbaṃ.

The time of robe-making is when a robe is being made. One may eat, considering it 'the time of robe-making'.

Addhānagamanasamayo [P 4.0075] nāma “addhayojanaṃ gacchissāmī”ti bhuñjitabbaṃ, gacchantena bhuñjitabbaṃ, gatena bhuñjitabbaṃ.

The time of going on a journey is when one may eat thinking, “I will go half a yojana.” One who is going may eat; one who has gone may eat.

Nāvābhiruhanasamayo nāma “nāvaṃ abhiruhissāmī”ti bhuñjitabbaṃ, āruḷhena bhuñjitabbaṃ, oruḷhena bhuñjitabbaṃ.

The time of embarking on a boat is when one may eat thinking, “I will embark on a boat.” One who has embarked may eat; one who has disembarked may eat.

Mahāsamayo nāma yattha dve tayo bhikkhū piṇḍāya caritvā yāpenti, catutthe āgate na yāpenti. “Mahāsamayo”ti bhuñjitabbaṃ.

A great occasion is where two or three monks can sustain themselves by going for alms, but when a fourth arrives, they cannot. One may eat, considering it 'a great occasion'.

Samaṇabhattasamayo nāma yo koci paribbājakasamāpanno bhattaṃ karoti. “Samaṇabhattasamayo”ti bhuñjitabbaṃ.

The time of a meal for ascetics is when any person included among the wanderers prepares a meal. One may eat, considering it 'the time of a meal for ascetics'.

“Aññatra samayā bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

If one accepts, thinking, “I will eat apart from the proper time,” there is an offense of wrong-doing. For each mouthful, there is an offense of pācittiya.

219. Gaṇabhojane gaṇabhojanasaññī, aññatra samayā, bhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Gaṇabhojane vematiko, aññatra samayā, bhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Gaṇabhojane nagaṇabhojanasaññī, aññatra samayā, bhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

219. In the case of a group meal, if one, perceiving it as a group meal, eats apart from the proper time, there is an offense of pācittiya. In the case of a group meal, if one, being uncertain, eats apart from the proper time, there is an offense of pācittiya. In the case of a group meal, if one, perceiving it as not a group meal, eats apart from the proper time, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Nagaṇabhojane [M 0.0102] gaṇabhojanasaññī[T 2.0315], āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nagaṇabhojane vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nagaṇabhojane nagaṇabhojanasaññī, anāpatti.

When it is not a group meal, if one perceives it as a group meal, there is an offense of wrong-doing. When it is not a group meal, if one is uncertain, there is an offense of wrong-doing. When it is not a group meal, if one perceives it as not a group meal, there is no offense.

220. Anāpatti [V 0.0105] samaye, dve tayo ekato bhuñjanti, piṇḍāya caritvā ekato sannipatitvā bhuñjanti, niccabhattaṃ, salākabhattaṃ, pakkhikaṃ, uposathikaṃ, pāṭipadikaṃ, pañca bhojanāni ṭhapetvā sabbattha anāpatti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

220. There is no offense: at the proper time; if two or three eat together; if, having gone for alms, they gather together and eat; in the case of a regular meal, a ticket meal, a fortnightly meal, an Uposatha-day meal, or a first-day-of-the-fortnight meal. Except for the five staple foods, there is no offense in any other case. There is no offense for one who is insane or for the first offender.

Gaṇabhojanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The second training rule on group meals is finished.

3. Paramparabhojanasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Training Rule on Eating in Succession

221. Tena [T 2.0316] samayena buddho bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena vesāliyaṃ paṇītānaṃ bhattānaṃ bhattapaṭipāṭi adhiṭṭhitā hoti. Atha kho aññatarassa daliddassa kammakārassa kammakarassa (sī.) etadahosi – “na kho idaṃ orakaṃ bhavissati yathayime manussā sakkaccaṃ bhattaṃ karonti; yaṃnūnāhampi bhattaṃ kareyya”nti. Atha kho so daliddo kammakāro yena kirapatiko tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ kirapatikaṃ etadavoca – “icchāmahaṃ, ayyaputta, buddhappamukhassa [P 4.0076] bhikkhusaṅghassa bhattaṃ kātuṃ. Dehi me vetana”nti. Sopi kho kirapatiko saddho hoti pasanno. Atha kho so kirapatiko tassa daliddassa kammakārassa abbhātirekaṃ atirekaṃ (syā.) vetanaṃ adāsi. Atha kho so daliddo kammakāro yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so daliddo kammakāro bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. “Mahā kho, āvuso, bhikkhusaṅgho. Jānāhī”ti. “Hotu hotu me (ka.) bhante, mahā bhikkhusaṅgho. Bahū me badarā paṭiyattā badaramissena peyyā paripūrissantī”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena.

221. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Vesālī, in the Great Wood, at the Peaked Roof Hall. Now at that time in Vesālī, a sequence of excellent meals had been established. Then this thought occurred to a certain poor laborer: 'The way these people are carefully preparing meals, this will not be an inferior matter. What if I too were to prepare a meal?' Then that poor laborer approached a person named Kirapatika. Having approached, he said this to that Kirapatika: 'Sir, I wish to prepare a meal for the community of monks with the Buddha at its head. Give me my wages.' That Kirapatika was faithful and devoted. Then that Kirapatika gave that poor laborer extra wages. Then that poor laborer approached the Blessed One. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, that poor laborer said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, may the Blessed One consent to a meal from me tomorrow, together with the community of monks.' 'Friend, the community of monks is large. You should know this.' 'Venerable sir, let the community of monks be large. Many jujubes have been prepared by me; the gruel mixed with jujubes will be sufficient.' The Blessed One consented by remaining silent.

Atha [M 0.0103] kho so daliddo kammakāro bhagavato [T 2.0317] adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū – “daliddena kira kammakārena svātanāya buddhappamukho bhikkhusaṅgho nimantito, badaramissena peyyā paripūrissantī”ti. Te kālasseva piṇḍāya caritvā bhuñjiṃsu. Assosuṃ kho manussā – “daliddena kira kammakārena buddhappamukho bhikkhusaṅgho nimantito”ti. Te daliddassa kammakārassa pahūtaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ abhihariṃsu. Atha kho so daliddo kammakāro tassā rattiyā accayena paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – “kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti.

Then that poor laborer, knowing the Blessed One's consent, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him respectfully, and departed. The monks heard: 'It is said that a poor laborer has invited the community of monks with the Buddha at its head for tomorrow, and the gruel mixed with jujubes will be sufficient.' They, having gone for alms early, ate. The people heard: 'It is said that a poor laborer has invited the community of monks with the Buddha at its head.' They brought abundant solid food and soft food for the poor laborer. Then that poor laborer, after the passing of that night, having had excellent solid food and soft food prepared, had the time announced to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, it is time; the meal is ready.'

Atha [V 0.0106] kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena tassa daliddassa kammakārassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho so daliddo kammakāro bhattagge bhikkhū parivisati. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “thokaṃ, āvuso, dehi. Thokaṃ, āvuso, dehī”ti. “Mā kho tumhe, bhante, ‘ayaṃ daliddo kammakāro’ti thokaṃ thokaṃ paṭiggaṇhittha. Pahūtaṃ me khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyattaṃ.

Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and approached the dwelling of that poor laborer. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the community of bhikkhus. Then that poor laborer served the bhikkhus in the dining hall. The bhikkhus said thus: 'Friend, give a little. Friend, give a little.' 'Venerable sirs, please do not accept just a little, thinking, "This is a poor laborer." Abundant solid and soft food has been prepared by me.

Paṭiggaṇhatha, bhante, yāvadattha”nti. “Na kho mayaṃ, āvuso, etaṃkāraṇā thokaṃ thokaṃ paṭiggaṇhāma. Apica, mayaṃ kālasseva piṇḍāya caritvā bhuñjimhā; tena mayaṃ thokaṃ thokaṃ paṭiggaṇhāmā”ti.

Venerable sirs, please accept as much as you need.' 'Friend, it is not for that reason that we accept just a little. But rather, we, having gone for alms early, have eaten; for that reason, we accept just a little.'

Atha kho so daliddo kammakāro ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma [T 2.0318] bhadantā mayā nimantitā aññatra bhuñjissanti! Na cāhaṃ paṭibalo yāvadatthaṃ dātu”nti? Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tassa daliddassa kammakārassa [P 4.0077] ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhū aññatra nimantitā aññatra bhuñjissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhū aññatra nimantitā aññatra bhuñjantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā aññatra nimantitā aññatra bhuñjissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

Then that poor laborer complained, grumbled, and criticized: 'How indeed could the venerable sirs, having been invited by me, eat elsewhere? Am I not able to give as much as is needed?' The bhikkhus heard that poor laborer complaining, grumbling, and criticizing. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes... they complained, grumbled, and criticized: 'How indeed could bhikkhus, having been invited to one place, eat elsewhere?' ... 'Bhikkhus, is it true, it is said, that bhikkhus, having been invited to one place, eat elsewhere?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... 'How indeed, bhikkhus, could those foolish men, having been invited to one place, eat elsewhere? Bhikkhus, this is not for the confidence of the unconfident... And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Paramparabhojane [M 0.0104] pācittiya”nti.

'For eating a succession-meal, there is an offense of expiation.'

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhus.

222. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu gilāno hoti. Aññataro bhikkhu piṇḍapātaṃ ādāya yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “bhuñjāhi, āvuso”ti. “Alaṃ, āvuso, atthi me bhattapaccāsā”ti. Tassa bhikkhuno piṇḍapāto ussūre ussūrena (ka.) āharīyittha. So bhikkhu na cittarūpaṃ bhuñji. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānena bhikkhunā paramparabhojanaṃ bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana[T 2.0319], bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

222. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu was sick. Another bhikkhu, taking almsfood, approached that bhikkhu. Having approached, he said this to that bhikkhu: 'Friend, eat.' 'Enough, friend, I have an expectation of a meal.' That bhikkhu's almsfood was brought late. That bhikkhu did not eat to his satisfaction. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this context, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus: 'Bhikkhus, I allow a sick bhikkhu to eat a succession-meal. And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Paramparabhojane, [V 0.0107] aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Gilānasamayo – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

'For eating a succession-meal, except on an occasion, there is an offense of expiation. Therein, this is the occasion: the occasion of sickness. This is the occasion therein.'

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhus.

223. Tena kho pana samayena manussā cīvaradānasamaye sacīvarabhattaṃ paṭiyādetvā paṭiyādāpetvā (itipi) bhikkhū nimantenti – “bhojetvā cīvarena acchādessāmā”ti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nādhivāsenti – “paṭikkhittaṃ bhagavatā paramparabhojana”nti. Cīvaraṃ parittaṃ uppajjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cīvaradānasamaye paramparabhojanaṃ bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

223. At that time, people, during the robe-offering occasion, having prepared food together with robes, invited the bhikkhus, saying, “Having fed you, we will clothe you with robes.” The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not accept, thinking, “The Blessed One has prohibited succession-meals.” Few robes were offered. They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “I allow, bhikkhus, to eat a succession-meal on a robe-offering occasion.” And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:

“Paramparabhojane, aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Gilānasamayo, cīvaradānasamayo – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

'For eating a succession-meal, except on an occasion, there is an offense of expiation. Therein, this is the occasion: the occasion of sickness, the occasion of robe-offering. This is the occasion therein.'

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhus.

224. Tena kho pana samayena manussā cīvarakārake bhikkhū bhattena nimantenti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nādhivāsenti – “paṭikkhittaṃ bhagavatā paramparabhojana”nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cīvarakārasamaye paramparabhojanaṃ bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

224. Now at that time, people invited bhikkhus who were making robes to a meal. The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not accept, thinking, “The Blessed One has forbidden succession-meals.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “I allow, bhikkhus, to eat a succession-meal on a robe-making occasion.” And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:

225. “Paramparabhojane, [M 0.0105] aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Gilānasamayo, cīvaradānasamayo, cīvarakārasamayo – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

225. 'For eating a succession-meal, except on an occasion, there is an offense of expiation. Therein, this is the occasion: the occasion of sickness, the occasion of robe-offering, the occasion of robe-making. This is the occasion therein.'

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhus.

226. Atha [T 2.0320] kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya [P 4.0078] āyasmatā ānandena pacchāsamaṇena yena aññataraṃ kulaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho te manussā bhagavato ca āyasmato ca ānandassa bhojanaṃ adaṃsu. Āyasmā ānando kukkuccāyanto na paṭiggaṇhāti. “Gaṇhāhi patigaṇhāhi (sī.), ānandā”ti. “Alaṃ, bhagavā[V 0.0108], atthi me bhattapaccāsā”ti. “Tenahānanda, vikappetvā gaṇhāhī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vikappetvā bhattapaccāsaṃ vikappetvā (syā.) paramparabhojanaṃ bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, vikappetabbaṃ – ‘mayhaṃ bhattapaccāsaṃ itthannāmassa dammī’”ti.

226. Then, in the morning, the Blessed One, having dressed, took his bowl and robe, and with the Venerable Ānanda as his attendant bhikkhu, went to a certain family. Having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat. Then those people offered food to the Blessed One and the Venerable Ānanda. The Venerable Ānanda, being scrupulous, did not accept it. “Accept it, Ānanda.” “Enough, Blessed One, I have an expectation of a meal.” “Well then, Ānanda, accept it after making a formal transfer.” Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in connection with this matter, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the bhikkhus: “I allow, bhikkhus, to eat a succession-meal after making a formal transfer. And thus, bhikkhus, the formal transfer should be made thus: ‘I give my expectation of a meal to the one named so-and-so.’”

227. Paramparabhojanaṃ nāma pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ aññatarena bhojanena nimantito, taṃ ṭhapetvā aññaṃ pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ aññataraṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjati, etaṃ paramparabhojanaṃ nāma.

227. What is called 'eating in succession' is this: being invited with one of the five kinds of food, one sets that aside and eats another of the five kinds of food. This is called 'eating in succession'.

Aññatra samayāti ṭhapetvā samayaṃ.

‘Except for the occasion’ means setting aside the occasion.

Gilānasamayo nāma na sakkoti ekāsane nisinno yāvadatthaṃ bhuñjituṃ. “Gilānasamayo”ti bhuñjitabbaṃ.

What is called 'the occasion of sickness' is when one is unable to eat one’s fill while sitting in one seat. One may eat, thinking, ‘It is the occasion of sickness.’

Cīvaradānasamayo nāma anatthate kathine vassānassa pacchimo māso, atthate kathine pañca māsā. “Cīvaradānasamayo”ti bhuñjitabbaṃ.

What is called 'the occasion of robe-offering' is the last month of the rains when the kathina has not been spread, or five months when the kathina has been spread. One may eat, thinking, ‘It is the occasion of robe-offering.’

Cīvarakārasamayo nāma cīvare kayiramāne. “Cīvarakārasamayo”ti bhuñjitabbaṃ.

What is called 'the occasion of robe-making' is when a robe is being made. One may eat, thinking, ‘It is the occasion of robe-making.’

“Aññatra samayā bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre [T 2.0321] ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

If one accepts food thinking, ‘I will eat outside the occasion,’ there is an offense of wrongful conduct. For each mouthful, there is an offense of expiation.

228. Paramparabhojane [M 0.0106] paramparabhojanasaññī, aññatra samayā, bhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Paramparabhojane vematiko, aññatra samayā, bhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Paramparabhojane naparamparabhojanasaññī, aññatra samayā, bhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

228. Regarding eating in succession, if one perceives it as eating in succession and eats outside the occasion, there is an offense of expiation. Regarding eating in succession, if one is doubtful and eats outside the occasion, there is an offense of expiation. Regarding eating in succession, if one perceives it as not eating in succession and eats outside the occasion, there is an offense of expiation.

Naparamparabhojane paramparabhojanasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Naparamparabhojane vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Naparamparabhojane naparamparabhojanasaññī, anāpatti.

Regarding what is not eating in succession, if one perceives it as eating in succession, there is an offense of wrongful conduct. Regarding what is not eating in succession, if one is doubtful, there is an offense of wrongful conduct. Regarding what is not eating in succession, if one perceives it as not eating in succession, there is no offense.

229. Anāpatti samaye, vikappetvā bhuñjati, dve tayo nimantane ekato bhuñjati, nimantanapaṭipāṭiyā bhuñjati, sakalena gāmena nimantito tasmiṃ gāme yattha katthaci bhuñjati[V 0.0109], sakalena pūgena nimantito tasmiṃ pūge yattha katthaci bhuñjati, nimantiyamāno bhikkhaṃ gahessāmīti bhaṇati, niccabhatte, salākabhatte, pakkhike, uposathike, pāṭipadike, pañca bhojanāni ṭhapetvā sabbattha anāpatti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

229. There is no offense: on the occasion; if one eats after making a formal transfer; if one eats from two or three invitations together; if one eats in the sequence of the invitations; if, having been invited by an entire village, one eats anywhere in that village; if, having been invited by an entire group, one eats anywhere in that group; if, while being invited, one says, ‘I will take alms-food’; at a regular meal, a ticket-meal, a fortnightly meal, an uposatha-day meal, or a first-day-of-the-fortnight meal; for anything apart from the five kinds of food; for one who is insane, and for the first offender.

Paramparabhojanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The third training rule on eating in succession is finished.

4. Kāṇamātusikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Training Rule concerning Kāṇā’s Mother

230. Tena [T 2.0322] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena [P 4.0079] kāṇamātā upāsikā saddhā hoti pasannā. Kāṇā gāmake aññatarassa purisassa dinnā hoti. Atha kho kāṇā mātugharaṃ agamāsi kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho kāṇāya sāmiko kāṇāya santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – “āgacchatu kāṇā, icchāmi kāṇāya āgata”nti. Atha kho kāṇamātā upāsikā “kismiṃ viya rittahatthaṃ gantu”nti pūvaṃ pūpaṃ (ṇvādi) paci. Pakke pūve aññataro piṇḍacāriko bhikkhu kāṇamātāya upāsikāya nivesanaṃ pāvisi. Atha kho kāṇamātā upāsikā tassa bhikkhuno pūvaṃ dāpesi. So nikkhamitvā aññassa ācikkhi. Tassapi pūvaṃ dāpesi. Sopi nikkhamitvā aññassa ācikkhi. Tassapi pūvaṃ [M 0.0107] dāpesi. Yathāpaṭiyattaṃ pūvaṃ parikkhayaṃ agamāsi. Dutiyampi kho kāṇāya sāmiko kāṇāya santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – “āgacchatu kāṇā, icchāmi kāṇāya āgata”nti. Dutiyampi kho kāṇamātā upāsikā “kismiṃ viya rittahattaṃ gantu”nti pūvaṃ paci. Pakke pūve aññataro piṇḍacāriko bhikkhu kāṇamātāya upāsikāya nivesanaṃ pāvisi. Atha kho kāṇamātā upāsikā tassa bhikkhuno pūvaṃ dāpesi. So nikkhamitvā aññassa ācikkhi. Tassapi pūvaṃ [T 2.0323] dāpesi. Sopi nikkhamitvā aññassa ācikkhi. Tassapi pūvaṃ dāpesi. Yathāpaṭiyattaṃ pūvaṃ parikkhayaṃ agamāsi. Tatiyampi kho kāṇāya sāmiko kāṇāya santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – “āgacchatu kāṇā, icchāmi kāṇāya āgataṃ. Sace kāṇā nāgacchissati, ahaṃ aññaṃ pajāpatiṃ ānessāmī”ti. Tatiyampi kho kāṇamātā upāsikā kismiṃ viya rittahatthaṃ gantunti pūvaṃ paci. Pakke pūve aññataro piṇḍacāriko bhikkhu kāṇamātāya upāsikāya nivesanaṃ pāvisi. Atha kho kāṇamātā upāsikā tassa bhikkhuno pūvaṃ dāpesi. So nikkhamitvā aññassa ācikkhi. Tassapi pūvaṃ dāpesi. Sopi nikkhamitvā aññassa ācikkhi. Tassapi [V 0.0110] pūvaṃ dāpesi. Yathāpaṭiyattaṃ pūvaṃ parikkhayaṃ agamāsi. Atha kho kāṇāya sāmiko aññaṃ pajāpatiṃ ānesi.

230. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the laywoman Kāṇamātā was faithful and devoted. Kāṇā had been given to a certain man in a small village. Then Kāṇā went to her mother’s house for some business. Then Kāṇā’s husband sent a messenger to Kāṇā, saying: ‘Let Kāṇā come; I desire Kāṇā’s coming.’ Then the laywoman Kāṇamātā, thinking, ‘It is somewhat shameful to go empty-handed,’ fried a cake. When the cake was cooked, a certain alms-gathering monk entered the dwelling of the laywoman Kāṇamātā. Then the laywoman Kāṇamātā had a cake given to that monk. Having gone out, he told another monk. She had a cake given to that monk also. He too, having gone out, told another monk. She had a cake given to him also. The cake that had been prepared was exhausted. For a second time, Kāṇā’s husband sent a messenger to Kāṇā, saying: ‘Let Kāṇā come; I desire Kāṇā’s coming.’ For a second time, the laywoman Kāṇamātā, thinking, ‘It is somewhat shameful to go empty-handed,’ fried a cake. When the cake was cooked, a certain alms-gathering monk entered the dwelling of the laywoman Kāṇamātā. Then the laywoman Kāṇamātā had a cake given to that monk. Having gone out, he told another monk. She had a cake given to that monk also. He too, having gone out, told another monk. She had a cake given to him also. The cake that had been prepared was exhausted. For a third time, Kāṇā’s husband sent a messenger to Kāṇā, saying: ‘Let Kāṇā come; I desire Kāṇā’s coming. If Kāṇā does not come, I will bring another wife.’ For a third time, the laywoman Kāṇamātā, thinking, ‘It is somewhat shameful to go empty-handed,’ fried a cake. When the cake was cooked, a certain alms-gathering monk entered the dwelling of the laywoman Kāṇamātā. Then the laywoman Kāṇamātā had a cake given to that monk. Having gone out, he told another monk. She had a cake given to that monk also. He too, having gone out, told another monk. She had a cake given to him also. The cake that had been prepared was exhausted. Then Kāṇā’s husband brought another wife.

Assosi kho kāṇā – “tena kira purisena aññā pajāpati ānītā”ti. Sā rodantī aṭṭhāsi. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena kāṇamātāya upāsikāya nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho kāṇamātā upāsikā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho kāṇamātaraṃ upāsikaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “kissāyaṃ kāṇā rodatī”ti? Atha kho kāṇamātā upāsikā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Atha kho bhagavā kāṇamātaraṃ upāsikaṃ dhammiyā kathāya [T 2.0324] sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

Kāṇā heard: ‘It is said that another wife has been brought by that man.’ She stood weeping. Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning time, taking his bowl and robe, approached the dwelling of the laywoman Kāṇamātā. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Then the laywoman Kāṇamātā approached the Blessed One. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, she sat down at a suitable place. The Blessed One spoke this word to the laywoman Kāṇamātā who was sitting at a suitable place: ‘Why is this Kāṇā weeping?’ Then the laywoman Kāṇamātā informed the Blessed One of this matter. Then the Blessed One, having shown, caused to undertake, caused to exert, and caused to rejoice the laywoman Kāṇamātā with a talk on the Dhamma, rose from his seat and departed.

231. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro sattho rājagahā paṭiyālokaṃ gantukāmo hoti. Aññataro piṇḍacāriko bhikkhu taṃ satthaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Aññataro upāsako tassa bhikkhuno sattuṃ [M 0.0108] dāpesi. So nikkhamitvā aññassa ācikkhi. Tassapi sattuṃ dāpesi. So nikkhamitvā aññassa ācikkhi. Tassapi sattuṃ dāpesi. Yathāpaṭiyattaṃ pātheyyaṃ parikkhayaṃ agamāsi[P 4.0080]. Atha kho so upāsako te manusse etadavoca – “ajjaṇho, ayyā, āgametha, yathāpaṭiyattaṃ pātheyyaṃ ayyānaṃ dinnaṃ. Pātheyyaṃ paṭiyādessāmī”ti. “Nāyyo nāyya (syā.) sakkā āgametuṃ, payāto sattho”ti agamaṃsu. Atha kho tassa upāsakassa pātheyyaṃ paṭiyādetvā pacchā gacchantassa corā acchindiṃsu. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā na mattaṃ jānitvā paṭiggahessanti! Ayaṃ imesaṃ datvā pacchā gacchanto corehi acchinno”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññapessāmi [T 2.0325] dasa atthavase paṭicca – saṅghasuṭṭhutāya, saṅghaphāsutāya…pe… vinayānuggahāya. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

231. At that time, a certain caravan was desirous of going from Rājagaha to the western region. A certain alms-gathering monk entered that caravan for alms. A certain lay follower had balls of meal given to that monk. Having gone out, he told another. He had balls of meal given to him also. Having gone out, he told another. He had balls of meal given to him also. The prepared provisions for the journey were exhausted. Then that lay follower said to those people, ‘Sirs, please wait today. The provisions that were prepared have been given to the venerable sirs. I will prepare provisions.’ ‘Sir, it is not possible to wait; the caravan has departed,’ they said, and departed. Then, as that lay follower was going behind after preparing the provisions, robbers plundered him. People complained, criticized, and grumbled, ‘How indeed could the ascetics, the sons of the Sakyan, accept without knowing the measure? This man, having given to them and going behind, was plundered by robbers.’ The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and grumbling. Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this context, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: ‘In that case, monks, I will lay down a training rule for the monks, based on ten reasons: for the excellence of the Sangha, for the comfort of the Sangha… for the support of the discipline. And so, monks, you should recite this training rule in this way:

232. “Bhikkhuṃ paneva kulaṃ upagataṃ pūvehi vā manthehi vā abhihaṭṭhuṃ pavāreyya, ākaṅkhamānena bhikkhunā dvattipattapūrā paṭiggahetabbā tato ce uttari paṭiggaṇheyya pācittiyaṃ. Dvattipattapūre [V 0.0111] paṭiggahetvā tato nīharitvā bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ saṃvibhajitabbaṃ. Ayaṃ tattha sāmīcī”ti.

232. ‘Should a monk who has approached a family be invited with an offering of cakes or twisted sweetmeats, two or three bowlfuls are to be accepted by a monk who so desires. If he should accept more than that, it is a pācittiya offense. Having accepted two or three bowlfuls, having brought them from there, they are to be shared with the monks. This is the proper conduct in that case.’

233. Bhikkhuṃ paneva kulaṃ upagatanti kulaṃ nāma cattāri kulāni – khattiyakulaṃ, brāhmaṇakulaṃ, vessakulaṃ, suddakulaṃ.

233. A monk who has approached a family: ‘family’ means four families—the noble family, the brahmin family, the merchant family, and the commoner family.

Upagatanti tattha gataṃ.

Having approached: means having gone there.

Pūvaṃ nāma yaṃkiñci paheṇakatthāya paṭiyattaṃ.

‘Cakes’ means whatever is prepared as a gift.

Manthaṃ nāma yaṃkiñci pātheyyatthāya paṭiyattaṃ.

‘Twisted sweetmeats’ means whatever is prepared as provisions for a journey.

Abhihaṭṭhuṃ pavāreyyāti yāvatakaṃ icchasi tāvatakaṃ gaṇhāhīti.

‘To invite with an offering’ means to invite saying, ‘Take as much as you wish.’

Ākaṅkhamānenāti icchamānena.

‘By one who so desires’ means by one who wishes.

Dvattipattapūrā paṭiggahetabbāti dvetayo pattapūrā paṭiggahetabbā.

‘Two or three bowlfuls are to be accepted’ means two or three bowlfuls are to be accepted.

Tato [M 0.0109] ce uttari paṭigaṇheyyāti tatuttari paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘If he should accept more than that’ means if he accepts more than that, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Dvattipattapūre paṭiggahetvā tato nikkhamantena bhikkhuṃ passitvā ācikkhitabbaṃ – “amutra mayā dvattipattapūrā paṭiggahitā, mā kho tattha paṭiggaṇhī”ti. Sace passitvā na ācikkhati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sace ācikkhite paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Having accepted two or three bowlfuls, a monk who is leaving from there, upon seeing another monk, should inform him, saying, ‘In that house, I have accepted two or three bowlfuls; do not accept any there.’ If, having seen him, he does not inform him, there is an offense of wrong conduct. If, having been informed, he accepts, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

Tato [T 2.0326][P 4.0081] nīharitvā bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ saṃvibhajitabbanti paṭikkamanaṃ nīharitvā saṃvibhajitabbaṃ.

‘Having taken them from there and shared them with the monks’ means having taken them to the dining hall, they should be shared.

Ayaṃ tattha sāmīcīti ayaṃ tattha anudhammatā.

‘This is the proper conduct in that case’ means this is the conduct conforming to the Dhamma in that case.

234. Atirekadvattipattapūre atirekasaññī paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Atirekadvattipattapūre [V 0.0112] vematiko paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Atirekadvattipattapūre ūnakasaññī paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

234. If he accepts more than two or three bowlfuls, perceiving it as more, there is an offense of pācittiya. If he accepts more than two or three bowlfuls, being uncertain, there is an offense of pācittiya. If he accepts more than two or three bowlfuls, perceiving it as less, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Ūnakadvattipattapūre atirekasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ūnakadvattipattapūre vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ūnakadvattipattapūre ūnakasaññī, anāpatti.

If he accepts less than two or three bowlfuls, perceiving it as more, there is an offense of wrong conduct. If he accepts less than two or three bowlfuls, being uncertain, there is an offense of wrong conduct. If he accepts less than two or three bowlfuls, perceiving it as less, there is no offense.

235. Anāpatti dvattipattapūre paṭiggaṇhāti, ūnakadvattipattapūre paṭiggaṇhāti, na paheṇakatthāya na pātheyyatthāya paṭiyattaṃ denti, paheṇakatthāya vā pātheyyatthāya vā paṭiyattasesakaṃ denti, gamane paṭippassaddhe denti, ñātakānaṃ pavāritānaṃ, aññassatthāya, attano dhanena, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

235. There is no offense if he accepts two or three bowlfuls; if he accepts less than two or three bowlfuls; if they give what was not prepared as a gift or as provisions for a journey; if they give what remains of what was prepared as a gift or as provisions for a journey; if they give when the journey has been canceled; if he accepts what is prepared for relatives or for those who have invited him; if he accepts for the sake of another; if he accepts with his own wealth; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Kāṇamātusikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.

The fourth training rule, concerning Kāṇamātā, is concluded.

5. Paṭhamapavāraṇāsikkhāpadaṃ

5. The First Training Rule on Declining Further Food

236. Tena [T 2.0327] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro brāhmaṇo bhikkhū nimantetvā bhojesi. Bhikkhū bhuttāvī pavāritā ñātikulāni [M 0.0110] gantvā ekacce bhuñjiṃsu ekacce piṇḍapātaṃ ādāya agamaṃsu. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo paṭivissake paṭivisake (yojanā) etadavoca – “bhikkhū mayā ayyā santappitā. Etha, tumhepi santappessāmī”ti. Te evamāhaṃsu – “kiṃ tvaṃ, ayyo ayya (syā.), amhe santappessasi? Yepi tayā nimantitā tepi amhākaṃ gharāni āgantvā ekacce bhuñjiṃsu ekacce piṇḍapātaṃ ādāya agamaṃsū”ti!

236. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. At that time, a certain brahmin invited monks and served them a meal. The monks, having eaten and declined further offerings, went to their relatives’ families; some ate, and some took almsfood and departed. Then that brahmin said to his neighbors, “Sirs, I have satisfied the monks. Come, I will satisfy you too.” They replied, “How will you satisfy us, sir? Even the monks you invited came to our homes; some ate, and some took almsfood and departed!”

Atha kho so brāhmaṇo ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma bhadantā amhākaṃ ghare bhuñjitvā aññatra bhuñjissanti! Na cāhaṃ paṭibalo yāvadatthaṃ dātu”nti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tassa brāhmaṇassa ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhū bhuttāvī pavāritā aññatra bhuñjissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhuttāvī pavāritā aññatra bhuñjantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā bhuttāvī [P 4.0082] pavāritā aññatra bhuñjissanti[V 0.0113]! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ [T 2.0328] vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

Then that brahmin complained, grumbled, and spread the word disparagingly, “How can the venerables eat in our home and then eat elsewhere! Am I not able to give as much as is needed?” The monks heard that brahmin complaining, grumbling, and spreading the word disparagingly. Those monks who were of few wishes… they complained, grumbled, and spread the word disparagingly, “How can monks, having eaten and declined further offerings, eat elsewhere?”… “Is it true, monks, that monks, having eaten and declined further offerings, eat elsewhere?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How can those foolish men, having eaten and declined further offerings, eat elsewhere! This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Yo pana bhikkhu bhuttāvī pavārito khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever monk, having eaten and declined further offerings, should chew or eat edible food or staple food, it is an offense of expiation.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

Thus this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.

237. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū gilānānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ paṇīte piṇḍapāte nīharanti. Gilānā na cittarūpaṃ bhuñjanti. Tāni bhikkhū chaṭṭenti. Assosi kho bhagavā uccāsaddaṃ mahāsaddaṃ kākoravasaddaṃ. Sutvāna āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “kiṃ nu kho so, ānanda, uccāsaddo mahāsaddo kākoravasaddo”ti? Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. “Bhuñjeyyuṃ panānanda, bhikkhū gilānātiritta”nti. “Na bhuñjeyyuṃ, bhagavā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi bhikkhave, gilānassa ca agilānassa ca atirittaṃ bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, atirittaṃ kātabbaṃ – “alametaṃ sabba”nti. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

237. At that time, monks would bring choice almsfood for sick monks. The sick monks did not eat as much as they wished. The other monks would discard that food. The Blessed One heard a loud noise, a great noise, the sound of crows gathering. Having heard, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Ānanda, what is that loud noise, that great noise, that sound of crows gathering?” Then the Venerable Ānanda informed the Blessed One of this matter. “But Ānanda, may monks eat the leftovers of the sick?” “They may not, Blessed One.” Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this context, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: “I allow, monks, the eating of leftovers from both the sick and the not-sick. And so, monks, the leftovers should be made thus: ‘This is all sufficient.’ And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

238. “Yo [M 0.0111] pana bhikkhu bhuttāvī pavārito anatirittaṃ khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

238. “Whatever monk, having eaten and declined further offerings, should chew or eat edible food or staple food that has not been made leftover, it is an offense of expiation.”

239. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

239. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘Monk’ means… in this context, this is the monk who is intended.

Bhuttāvī nāma pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ [T 2.0329] aññataraṃ bhojanaṃ antamaso kusaggenapi bhuttaṃ hoti.

‘Having eaten’ means having eaten any one of the five kinds of staple food, even as little as with the tip of a kusa-grass blade.

Pavārito nāma asanaṃ paññāyati, bhojanaṃ paññāyati, hatthapāse ṭhito abhiharati, paṭikkhepo paññāyati.

‘Having declined’ means: the act of eating is apparent, food is apparent, one standing within arm’s reach offers it, and the refusal is apparent.

Anatirittaṃ nāma akappiyakataṃ hoti, appaṭiggahitakataṃ hoti, anuccāritakataṃ hoti[V 0.0114], ahatthapāse kataṃ hoti, abhuttāvinā kataṃ hoti, bhuttāvinā pavāritena āsanā vuṭṭhitena kataṃ hoti, “alametaṃ sabbanti avuttaṃ hoti, na gilānātirittaṃ hoti” – etaṃ anatirittaṃ nāma.

‘Not made leftover’ means: it is made unallowable; it is not formally received; it is not lifted up; it is done outside of arm’s reach; it is done by one who has not eaten; it is done by one who, having eaten and declined further offerings, has risen from their seat; “This is all sufficient” is not said; it is not the leftover of a sick person—this is called ‘not made leftover’.

Atirittaṃ nāma kappiyakataṃ hoti, paṭiggahitakataṃ hoti, uccāritakataṃ hoti, hatthapāse kataṃ hoti, bhuttāvinā kataṃ hoti, bhuttāvinā pavāritena āsanā avuṭṭhitena kataṃ hoti, “alametaṃ sabba”nti vuttaṃ hoti, gilānātirittaṃ hoti – etaṃ atirittaṃ nāma.

‘Made leftover’ means: it is made allowable; it is formally received; it is lifted up; it is done within arm’s reach; it is done by one who is eating; it is done by one who, having eaten and declined further offerings, has not risen from their seat; “This is all sufficient” is said; it is the leftover of a sick person—this is called ‘made leftover’.

Khādanīyaṃ [P 4.0083] nāma pañca bhojanāni – yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ khādanīyaṃ nāma.

‘Edible food’ means: setting aside the five staple foods, items allowable for a watch of the night, items allowable for seven days, and items allowable for life, the remainder is called ‘edible food’.

Bhojanīyaṃ nāma pañca bhojanāni – odano, kummāso, sattu, maccho, maṃsaṃ.

‘Staple food’ means the five staple foods: cooked rice, barley meal, roasted grain flour, fish, and meat.

“Khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

If one accepts it thinking, “I will chew this, I will eat this,” there is an offense of wrong conduct. For every mouthful swallowed, there is an offense of expiation.

240. Anatiritte anatirittasaññī khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anatiritte vematiko khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anatiritte atirittasaññī khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

240. In the case of what has not been made leftover, if one, perceiving it as not made leftover, chews or eats edible food or staple food, there is an offense of expiation. In the case of what has not been made leftover, if one, being doubtful, chews or eats edible food or staple food, there is an offense of expiation. In the case of what has not been made leftover, if one, perceiving it as made leftover, chews or eats edible food or staple food, there is an offense of expiation.

Yāmakālikaṃ [T 2.0330][M 0.0112] sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ āhāratthāya paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti dukkaṭassa. Atiritte anatirittasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Atiritte vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Atiritte atirittasaññī, anāpatti.

If one accepts an item allowable for a watch of the night, an item allowable for seven days, or an item allowable for life for the purpose of a meal, there is an offense of wrong conduct. For every mouthful swallowed, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of what has been made leftover, if one perceives it as not made leftover, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of what has been made leftover, if one is doubtful, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of what has been made leftover, if one perceives it as made leftover, there is no offense.

241. Anāpatti atirittaṃ kārāpetvā bhuñjati, “atirittaṃ kārāpetvā bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, aññassatthāya haranto gacchati, gilānassa sesakaṃ bhuñjati, yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ sati paccaye paribhuñjati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

241. There is no offense: if one eats after having had it made leftover; if one accepts it thinking, “I will eat after having had it made leftover”; if one goes while carrying it for the sake of another; if one eats the remainder from a sick person; if, there being a reason, one partakes of an item allowable for a watch of the night, an item allowable for seven days, or an item allowable for life; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Paṭhamapavāraṇāsikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The fifth, the First Training Rule on Declining, is concluded.

6. Dutiyapavāraṇāsikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Second Training Rule on Declining

242. Tena [T 2.0331][V 0.0115] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena dve bhikkhū kosalesu janapade sāvatthiṃ addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti. Eko bhikkhu anācāraṃ ācarati. Dutiyo bhikkhu taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “māvuso, evarūpamakāsi, netaṃ kappatī”ti. So tasmiṃ upanandhi. Atha kho te bhikkhū sāvatthiṃ agamaṃsu. Tena kho pana samayena sāvatthiyaṃ aññatarassa pūgassa saṅghabhattaṃ hoti. Dutiyo bhikkhu bhuttāvī pavārito hoti. Upanaddho upanandho (ka.) bhikkhu ñātikulaṃ gantvā piṇḍapātaṃ ādāya yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “bhuñjāhi, āvuso”ti. “Alaṃ, āvuso, paripuṇṇomhī”ti. “Sundaro, āvuso, piṇḍapāto, bhuñjāhī”ti. Atha kho so bhikkhu tena bhikkhunā nippīḷiyamāno taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñji. Upanaddho bhikkhu [P 4.0084] taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “tvampi tvaṃ hi (syā.) nāma, āvuso, maṃ vattabbaṃ maññasi yaṃ tvaṃ bhuttāvī pavārito anatirittaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjasī”ti. “Nanu, āvuso, ācikkhitabba”nti. “Nanu, āvuso, pucchitabba”nti.

242. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, two monks were traveling on the long road through the Kosalan country to Sāvatthī. One monk was behaving improperly. The second monk said to that monk, “Friend, do not do such a thing; this is not allowable.” That monk bore a grudge against him. Then those monks arrived in Sāvatthī. Now at that time, a certain group in Sāvatthī was offering a meal to the Saṅgha. The second monk had eaten and had declined further food. The grudge-bearing monk, having gone to a relative's home and taken almsfood, approached that monk. Having approached, he said to that monk, “Eat, friend.” “Enough, friend, I am full.” “The almsfood is excellent, friend, eat.” Then, being pressed by that monk, he ate that almsfood. The grudge-bearing monk said to that monk, “Friend, do you really think you should admonish me, when you, having eaten and declined, eat food that was not a leftover?” “Friend, should it not have been told?” “Friend, should it not have been asked?”

Atha kho so bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhu [M 0.0113] bhikkhuṃ bhuttāviṃ pavāritaṃ anatirittena bhojanena abhihaṭṭhuṃ [T 2.0332] pavāressatī” ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhikkhuṃ bhuttāviṃ pavāritaṃ anatirittena bhojanena abhihaṭṭhuṃ pavāresīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, bhikkhuṃ bhuttāviṃ pavāritaṃ anatirittena bhojanena abhihaṭṭhuṃ pavāressasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana bhikkhave imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

Then that monk told this matter to the monks. Those monks who were of few wishes… they criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could a monk invite another monk who has eaten and declined, by bringing food that was not a leftover?” … “Is it true, it is said, monk, that you invited a monk who has eaten and declined, by bringing food that was not a leftover?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “How indeed could you, foolish man, invite a monk who has eaten and declined, by bringing food that was not a leftover! This, foolish man, is not for the pleasing of the unpleased… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule in this way:

243. “Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ bhuttāviṃ pavāritaṃ anatirittena khādanīyena vā bhojanīyena vā abhihaṭṭhuṃ pavāreyya – ‘handa, bhikkhu, khāda vā bhuñja vā’ti, jānaṃ āsādanāpekkho, bhuttasmiṃ, pācittiya”nti.

243. “Whatever monk, with the aim of vexing, should knowingly bring forward and invite a monk who has eaten and declined, with hard food or soft food that was not a leftover, saying, ‘Come now, monk, chew or eat,’ when it has been eaten, it is an offense of expiation.”

244. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

244. ‘Whatever monk’ means: whatever kind… and so on… ‘Monk’ means… and so on… in this sense, this is the monk who is intended.

Bhikkhunti [V 0.0116] aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ.

‘A monk’ means another monk.

Bhuttāvī nāma pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ aññataraṃ bhojanaṃ, antamaso kusaggenapi bhuttaṃ hoti.

‘One who has eaten’ means one who has eaten any one of the five kinds of staple food, even if only with the tip of a blade of kusa grass.

Pavārito nāma asanaṃ paññāyati, bhojanaṃ paññāyati, hatthapāse ṭhito abhiharati, paṭikkhepo paññāyati.

‘One who has declined’ means: the act of eating is apparent, the food is apparent, one standing within hand's reach brings it forward, and the refusal is apparent.

Anatirittaṃ nāma akappiyakataṃ hoti, appaṭiggahitakataṃ hoti, anuccāritakataṃ hoti, ahatthapāse kataṃ hoti, abhuttāvinā kataṃ hoti, bhuttāvinā pavāritena āsanā vuṭṭhitena kataṃ hoti, “alametaṃ sabba”nti avuttaṃ hoti, na gilānātirittaṃ hoti – etaṃ anatirittaṃ nāma.

‘Not a leftover’ means: it has been made unallowable; it has been made from what was not received; it has been made without being lifted up; it has been made when not within hand's reach; it has been made by one who has not eaten; it has been made by one who has eaten, declined, and has risen from his seat; “enough of all this” has not been said; it is not the leftover of a sick person. This is what is called ‘not a leftover’.

Khādanīyaṃ nāma pañca bhojanāni – yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ khādanīyaṃ nāma.

‘Hard food’ means: setting aside the five staple foods, tonics for a limited period, medicines for seven days, and medicines for a lifetime, the remainder is called ‘hard food’.

Bhojanīyaṃ nāma [T 2.0333] pañca bhojanāni – odano, kummāso, sattu, maccho, maṃsaṃ.

‘Soft food’ means the five staple foods: cooked rice, barley-meal, parched grain flour, fish, and meat.

Abhihaṭṭhuṃ pavāreyyāti yāvatakaṃ icchasi tāvatakaṃ gaṇhāhīti.

‘To bring forward and invite’ means to invite saying, ‘Take as much as you wish.’

Jānāti [M 0.0114] nāma sāmaṃ vā jānāti, aññe vā tassa ārocenti, so vā āroceti.

‘Knows’ means: one knows by oneself, or others inform him, or he himself states it.

Āsādanāpekkhoti “iminā imaṃ codessāmi sāressāmi paṭicodessāmi paṭisāressāmi maṅku karissāmī”ti abhiharati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Tassa vacanena “khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti dukkaṭassa. Bhojanapariyosāne āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘With the aim of vexing’ means: one brings it forward thinking, ‘With this I will accuse him, make him remember, counter-accuse him, make him remember again, I will cause him to be humiliated’—there is an offense of wrong conduct. At his word, if one accepts it thinking, ‘I will chew, I will eat’—there is an offense of wrong conduct. For every mouthful, there is an offense of wrong conduct. At the end of the meal, there is an offense of expiation.

245. Pavārite pavāritasaññī anatirittena khādanīyena vā bhojanīyena vā abhihaṭṭhuṃ pavāreti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Pavārite vematiko anatirittena khādanīyena vā bhojanīyena vā abhihaṭṭhuṃ pavāreti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Pavārite appavāritasaññī anatirittena [V 0.0117] khādanīyena vā bhojanīyena vā abhihaṭṭhuṃ pavāreti, anāpatti. Yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ āhāratthāya abhiharati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Tassa vacanena “khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti dukkaṭassa. Appavārite pavāritasaññī[P 4.0085], āpatti dukkaṭassa. Appavārite vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Appavārite appavāritasaññī, anāpatti.

245. Perceiving that one has declined when one has declined, one brings forward and invites with hard food or soft food that was not a leftover: there is an offense of expiation. Being doubtful when one has declined, one brings forward and invites with hard food or soft food that was not a leftover: there is an offense of wrong conduct. Perceiving that one has not declined when one has declined, one brings forward and invites with hard food or soft food that was not a leftover: there is no offense. If one brings forward tonics for a limited period, medicines for seven days, or medicines for a lifetime for the purpose of a meal: there is an offense of wrong conduct. At his word, if one accepts it thinking, ‘I will chew, I will eat,’ there is an offense of wrong conduct. For every mouthful, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Perceiving that one has declined when one has not declined: there is an offense of wrong conduct. Being doubtful when one has not declined: there is an offense of wrong conduct. Perceiving that one has not declined when one has not declined: there is no offense.

246. Anāpatti atirittaṃ kārāpetvā deti, “atirittaṃ kārāpetvā [T 2.0334] bhuñjāhī”ti deti, aññassatthāya haranto gacchāhīti deti, gilānassa sesakaṃ deti, “yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ sati paccaye paribhuñjā”ti deti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

246. There is no offense: if one gives it after having had it made a leftover; if one gives it saying, “Having had it made a leftover, eat”; if one gives it saying, “Go, carrying this for the sake of another”; if one gives the remainder from a sick person; if one gives it saying, “Consume this tonic for a limited period, medicine for seven days, or medicine for a lifetime when there is a reason”; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Dutiyapavāraṇāsikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Second Training Rule Concerning Invitation, the sixth, is finished.

7. Vikālabhojanasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Training Rule on Eating at the Wrong Time

247. Tena [T 2.0335] samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena rājagahe giraggasamajjo hoti. Sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū giraggasamajjaṃ dassanāya agamaṃsu. Manussā sattarasavaggiye bhikkhū passitvā nahāpetvā vilimpetvā bhojetvā khādanīyaṃ [M 0.0115] adaṃsu. Sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū khādanīyaṃ ādāya ārāmaṃ gantvā chabbaggiye bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “gaṇhāthāvuso, khādanīyaṃ khādathā”ti. “Kuto tumhehi, āvuso, khādanīyaṃ laddha”nti? Sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū chabbaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Kiṃ pana tumhe, āvuso, vikāle bhojanaṃ bhuñjathā”ti? “Evamāvuso”ti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū vikāle bhojanaṃ bhuñjissantī”ti! Atha kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū vikāle bhojanaṃ bhuñjissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, vikāle bhojanaṃ bhuñjathāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, vikāle bhojanaṃ bhuñjissatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

247. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Place. Now at that time, a mountain-top festival was held in Rājagaha. The monks of the group of seventeen went to see the mountain-top festival. People, having seen the monks of the group of seventeen, bathed them, anointed them, fed them, and gave them hard food. The monks of the group of seventeen, taking the hard food, went to the monastery and said this to the monks of the group of six: “Venerable sirs, take and eat the hard food.” “Venerable sirs, from where did you get this hard food?” The monks of the group of seventeen reported this matter to the monks of the group of six. “But venerable sirs, do you eat food in the wrong-time?” “Yes, venerable sirs.” The monks of the group of six complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed could the monks of the group of seventeen eat food in the wrong-time!” Then the monks of the group of six reported this matter to the monks. Those monks who were of few wishes... they complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed could the monks of the group of seventeen eat food in the wrong-time!”... “Is it true, it is said, monks, that you eat food in the wrong-time?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... “How indeed, foolish men, could you eat food in the wrong-time! This, foolish men, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced... And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

248. Yo [V 0.0118] pana bhikkhu vikāle khādanīyaṃ [T 2.0336] vā bhojanīyaṃ vā khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

248. “Whatever monk, in the wrong-time, should chew hard food or eat soft food, it is an offense entailing expiation.”

249. Yo [P 4.0086] panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

249. As for ‘whatever’: whoever, of whatever kind... As for ‘monk’: ...in this sense, this monk is intended.

Vikālo nāma majjhanhike vītivatte yāva aruṇuggamanā.

‘Wrong-time’ means from when midday has passed until the arising of dawn.

Khādanīyaṃ nāma pañca bhojanāni – yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ khādanīyaṃ nāma.

‘Hard food’ means: having set aside the five staple foods, what is allowable for a watch, what is allowable for seven days, and what is allowable for life, the remainder is called ‘hard food’.

Bhojanīyaṃ nāma pañca bhojanāni – odano, kummāso, sattu, maccho, maṃsaṃ.

‘Soft food’ means the five staple foods: cooked rice, barley-meal, parched grain flour, fish, and meat.
