“Khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

If one accepts it with the thought, ‘I will chew, I will eat,’ there is an offense of wrong-doing. For every swallow, there is an offense entailing expiation.

250. Vikāle vikālasaññī khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Vikāle vematiko khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Vikāle [M 0.0116] kālasaññī khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

250. In the wrong-time, perceiving it as the wrong-time, if one chews hard food or eats soft food, there is an offense entailing expiation. In the wrong-time, being doubtful, if one chews hard food or eats soft food, there is an offense entailing expiation. In the wrong-time, perceiving it as the right time, if one chews hard food or eats soft food, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ āhāratthāya paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāle vikālasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāle vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāle kālasaññī, anāpatti.

If one accepts what is allowable for a watch, for seven days, or for life for the purpose of food, there is an offense of wrong-doing. For every swallow, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the right time, perceiving it as the wrong-time, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the right time, being doubtful, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the right time, perceiving it as the right time, there is no offense.

251. Anāpatti yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ sati paccaye paribhuñjati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

251. There is no offense: if one consumes what is allowable for a watch, for seven days, or for life when there is a reason; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Vikālabhojanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.

The seventh training rule on eating in the wrong-time is finished.

8. Sannidhikārakasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Training Rule on Storing Food

252. Tena [T 2.0337][V 0.0119] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato ānandassa upajjhāyo āyasmā belaṭṭhasīso belaṭṭhisīso (sī.) veḷaṭṭhasīso (syā.) araññe viharati. So piṇḍāya caritvā sukkhakuraṃ ārāmaṃ haritvā sukkhāpetvā nikkhipati. Yadā āhārena attho hoti, tadā udakena temetvā temetvā bhuñjati, cirena gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisati. Bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ belaṭṭhasīsaṃ etadavocuṃ – “kissa tvaṃ, āvuso, cirena gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisasī”ti? Atha kho āyasmā belaṭṭhasīso bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, āvuso, sannidhikārakaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjasī”ti? “Evamāvuso”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā belaṭṭhasīso sannidhikārakaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, belaṭṭhasīsa, sannidhikārakaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjasīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, belaṭṭhasīsa, sannidhikārakaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjissasi! Netaṃ, belaṭṭhasīsa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

252. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the Venerable Belaṭṭhasīsa, the preceptor of the Venerable Ānanda, was dwelling in the forest. Having gone for alms, he would bring dried rice to the monastery, dry it, and put it aside. When there was a need for food, he would eat it, having moistened it again and again with water, and he would enter the village for alms only after a long time. The monks said to the Venerable Belaṭṭhasīsa, “Venerable sir, why do you enter the village for alms only after a long time?” Then the Venerable Belaṭṭhasīsa told this matter to the monks. “But venerable sir, do you eat food that has been stored?” “Yes, venerable sirs.” Those monks who were of few wishes… criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying, “How indeed can the Venerable Belaṭṭhasīsa eat food that has been stored?”… “Belaṭṭhasīsa, is it true, as is said, that you eat food that has been stored?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “How indeed can you, Belaṭṭhasīsa, eat food that has been stored! Belaṭṭhasīsa, this is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule in this way:

253. “Yo [P 4.0087] pana bhikkhu sannidhikārakaṃ khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā [T 2.0338] khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

253. “Whatever monk should chew or eat hard food or soft food that has been stored, it is an offense entailing expiation.”

254. Yo [M 0.0117] panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

254. As for ‘whatever’: whoever, of whatever kind... As for ‘monk’: ...in this sense, this is the monk who is intended.

Sannidhikārakaṃ nāma ajja paṭiggahitaṃ aparajju khāditaṃ hoti.

‘Stored’ means: having been received today, it is eaten on another day.

Khādanīyaṃ nāma pañca bhojanāni – yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ khādanīyaṃ nāma.

‘Hard food’ means: excluding the five staple foods, items allowable for a watch, items allowable for seven days, and items allowable for a lifetime, the remainder is called ‘hard food’.

Bhojanīyaṃ nāma pañca bhojanāni – odano, kummāso, sattu, maccho, maṃsaṃ.

‘Soft food’ means the five staple foods: cooked rice, barley-meal, roasted grain flour, fish, and meat.

“Khādissāmi [V 0.0120] bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

If one accepts it with the thought, “I will chew, I will eat,” there is an offense of wrong-doing. For every swallow, there is an offense entailing expiation.

255. Sannidhikārake sannidhikārakasaññī khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Sannidhikārake vematiko khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Sannidhikārake asannidhikārakasaññī khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

255. Regarding stored food, if one, perceiving it to be stored, chews or eats either hard food or soft food, there is an offense of pācittiya. Regarding stored food, if one is in doubt and chews or eats either hard food or soft food, there is an offense of pācittiya. Regarding stored food, if one, perceiving it not to be stored, chews or eats either hard food or soft food, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ āhāratthāya paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti dukkaṭassa. Asannidhikārake sannidhikārakasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Asannidhikārake vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Asannidhikārake asannidhikārakasaññī, anāpatti.

If one accepts an item allowable for a watch, for seven days, or for a lifetime for the purpose of food, there is an offense of wrong-doing. For every swallow, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Regarding that which is not stored, if one perceives it as stored, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Regarding that which is not stored, if one is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Regarding that which is not stored, if one perceives it as not stored, there is no offense.

256. Anāpatti yāvakālikaṃ yāvakāle nidahitvā bhuñjati, yāmakālikaṃ yāme nidahitvā bhuñjati, sattāhakālikaṃ sattāhaṃ nidahitvā [T 2.0339] bhuñjati, yāvajīvikaṃ sati paccaye paribhuñjati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

256. There is no offense: if one eats an item allowable for the proper time, having stored it within that proper time; if one eats an item allowable for a watch, having stored it within that watch; if one eats an item allowable for seven days, having stored it for seven days; if one uses an item allowable for a lifetime when there is a reason; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Sannidhikārakasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The eighth training rule on storing food is finished.

9. Paṇītabhojanasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Training Rule on Choice Foods

257. Tena [T 2.0340][M 0.0118] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū paṇītabhojanāni attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā paṇītabhojanāni attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjissanti! Kassa sampannaṃ na manāpaṃ, kassa sāduṃ na ruccatī”ti!! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū paṇītabhojanāni attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjissantī”ti [P 4.0088]…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, paṇītabhojanāni attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjathāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā [V 0.0121] …pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, paṇītabhojanāni attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjissatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

257. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the monks of the group of six, having requested choice foods for their own sake, ate them. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, “How indeed can the ascetics, the sons of the Sakyan, request choice foods for their own sake and eat them! To whom is what is well-prepared not pleasing? To whom is what is tasty not agreeable?” The monks heard these people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those monks who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, “How indeed can the monks of the group of six request choice foods for their own sake and eat them?” … “Is it true, monks, that you request choice foods for your own sake and eat them?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed can you, worthless men, request choice foods for your own sake and eat them? This, worthless men, is not for the confidence of those who are not yet confident… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Yāni kho pana tāni paṇītabhojanāni, seyyathidaṃ – sappi navanītaṃ telaṃ madhu phāṇitaṃ maccho maṃsaṃ khīraṃ dadhi. Yo pana bhikkhu evarūpāni paṇītabhojanāni attano atthāya viññāpetvā [T 2.0341] bhuñjeyya, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever choice foods there are, namely: ghee, fresh butter, oil, honey, molasses, fish, meat, milk, and curd. Whatever monk, having requested such choice foods for his own sake, should eat them, it is a pācittiya offense.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the monks.

258. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū gilānā honti. Gilānapucchakā bhikkhū gilāne bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “kaccāvuso khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīya”nti? “Pubbe mayaṃ, āvuso, paṇītabhojanāni attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjāma, tena no phāsu hoti; idāni pana “bhagavatā paṭikkhitta”nti kukkuccāyantā na viññāpema, tena no na phāsu hotī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānena bhikkhunā paṇītabhojanāni attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

258. Now at that time, some monks were ill. Monks inquiring after the ill said this to the ill monks: “Venerable sirs, are you enduring? Are you getting by?” “Formerly, venerable sirs, we would request choice foods for our own sake and eat them, and because of that, we were comfortable. But now, being scrupulous and thinking, ‘It has been forbidden by the Blessed One,’ we do not request them, and because of that, we are not comfortable.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a discourse on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: “I allow, monks, a sick monk to request choice foods for his own sake and to eat them. And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

259. “Yāni [M 0.0119] kho pana tāni paṇītabhojanāni, seyyathidaṃ – sappi navanītaṃ telaṃ madhu phāṇitaṃ maccho maṃsaṃ khīraṃ dadhi. Yo pana bhikkhu evarūpāni paṇītabhojanāni agilāno attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjeyya, pācittiya”nti.

259. “Whatever choice foods there are, namely: ghee, fresh butter, oil, honey, molasses, fish, meat, milk, and curd. Whatever monk who is not ill, having requested such choice foods for his own sake, should eat them, it is a pācittiya offense.”

260. Yāni kho pana tāni paṇītabhojanānīti sappi nāma gosappi vā ajikāsappi vā mahiṃsasappi vā, yesaṃ maṃsaṃ kappati tesaṃ sappi.

260. ‘Whatever choice foods there are’: ‘Ghee’ means cow ghee, goat ghee, or buffalo ghee, or the ghee of those animals whose meat is permissible.

Navanītaṃ nāma tesaññeva navanītaṃ.

‘Fresh butter’ means the fresh butter of those same animals.

Telaṃ nāma tilatelaṃ sāsapatelaṃ madhukatelaṃ eraṇḍatelaṃ vasātelaṃ.

‘Oil’ means sesame oil, mustard oil, mahua oil, castor oil, or animal fat oil.

Madhu [V 0.0122] nāma makkhikāmadhu[T 2.0342].

‘Honey’ means bee honey.

Phāṇitaṃ nāma ucchumhā nibbattaṃ.

‘Molasses’ means that which is produced from sugarcane.

Maccho nāma udako udakacaro (syā. ka.) vuccati.

‘Fish’ refers to an aquatic animal.

Maṃsaṃ nāma yesaṃ maṃsaṃ kappati, tesaṃ maṃsaṃ.

‘Meat’ means the meat of those animals whose meat is permissible.

Khīraṃ nāma gokhīraṃ vā ajikākhīraṃ vā mahiṃsakhīraṃ vā, yesaṃ maṃsaṃ kappati, tesaṃ khīraṃ.

‘Milk’ means cow milk, goat milk, or buffalo milk, or the milk of those animals whose meat is permissible.

Dadhi nāma tesaññeva dadhi.

‘Curd’ means the curd of those same animals.

Yo [P 4.0089] panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

‘Whatever’: means whoever, of whatever sort… ‘Monk’ means… in this sense, this is the monk who is intended.

Evarūpāni paṇītabhojanānīti tathārūpāni paṇītabhojanāni.

‘Such choice foods’ means choice foods of that nature.

Agilāno nāma yassa vinā paṇītabhojanāni phāsu hoti.

‘Not ill’ means one for whom there is comfort without choice foods.

Gilāno nāma yassa vinā paṇītabhojanāni na phāsu hoti.

‘Ill’ means one for whom there is no comfort without choice foods.

Agilāno attano atthāya viññāpeti, payoge payoge payoge (ka.) dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena “bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

One who is not ill requests for his own sake; for each attempt, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Upon receiving it, if he accepts it thinking, “I will eat,” there is an offense of wrong-doing. For every swallow, there is an offense of pācittiya.

261. Agilāno agilānasaññī paṇītabhojanāni attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Agilāno vematiko [M 0.0120] paṇītabhojanāni attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Agilāno gilānasaññī paṇītabhojanāni attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

261. If a bhikkhu who is not ill, perceiving himself as not ill, having requested choice foods for his own sake, eats them, it is an offense of expiation. If a bhikkhu who is not ill, being in doubt, having requested choice foods for his own sake, eats them, it is an offense of expiation. If a bhikkhu who is not ill, perceiving himself as ill, having requested choice foods for his own sake, eats them, it is an offense of expiation.

Gilāno [V 0.0123] agilānasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Gilāno vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Gilāno gilānasaññī anāpatti.

A bhikkhu who is ill, perceiving himself as not ill: it is an offense of wrong-doing. A bhikkhu who is ill, being in doubt: it is an offense of wrong-doing. A bhikkhu who is ill, perceiving himself as ill: there is no offense.

262. Anāpatti [T 2.0343] gilānassa, gilāno hutvā viññāpetvā agilāno bhuñjati, gilānassa sesakaṃ bhuñjati, ñātakānaṃ pavāritānaṃ aññassatthāya attano dhanena, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

262. There is no offense for a bhikkhu who is ill; if, having requested while ill, he eats when no longer ill; if he eats the leftovers of an ill bhikkhu; if he requests from relatives or from those who have given an invitation; if he requests for the sake of another; if he requests with his own wealth; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Paṇītabhojanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.

The Ninth Training Rule on Choice Foods is concluded.

10. Dantaponasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Training Rule on Tooth-Cleaners

263. Tena [T 2.0344] samayena buddho bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu sabbapaṃsukūliko susāne viharati. So manussehi diyyamānaṃ na icchati paṭiggahetuṃ, susānepi rukkhamūlepi ummārepi ayyavosāṭitakāni sāmaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjati bhuñjati (syā.). Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayaṃ bhikkhu amhākaṃ ayyavosāṭitakāni sāmaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjissati! Theroyaṃ bhikkhu vaṭharo manussamaṃsaṃ maññe khādatī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhu adinnaṃ mukhadvāraṃ āhāraṃ āharissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, bhikkhu, adinnaṃ mukhadvāraṃ āhāraṃ āharasīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, adinnaṃ mukhadvāraṃ āhāraṃ āharissasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

263. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Vesālī, in the Great Wood, in the hall with a gabled roof. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu who wore only robes made from discarded rags was dwelling in a charnel ground. He did not wish to accept what was given by people. In the charnel ground, at the foot of a tree, or on a threshold, he himself took and consumed the food that had been placed for the benefit of deceased ancestors. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed can this bhikkhu himself take and consume the food placed for the benefit of our deceased ancestors! This bhikkhu is stout, he is plump; I think he eats human flesh!” The bhikkhus heard these people complaining, criticizing, and speaking disparagingly. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed can a bhikkhu convey food that has not been formally offered to the mouth-door?”… “Is it true, bhikkhu, as has been heard, that you convey food that has not been formally offered to the mouth-door?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “Foolish man, how indeed can you convey food that has not been formally offered to the mouth-door? This does not lead, foolish man, to the confidence of the unconfident… And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:

“Yo [P 4.0090] pana bhikkhu adinnaṃ mukhadvāraṃ āhāraṃ āhareyya, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever bhikkhu should convey food that has not been formally offered to the mouth-door, it is an offense of expiation.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

Thus this training rule was laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

264. Tena [M 0.0121] kho pana samayena bhikkhū udakadantapone udakadantapoṇe (syā. ka.) kukkuccāyanti[T 2.0345]. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ [V 0.0124] ārocesuṃ…pe… “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udakadantaponaṃ sāmaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

264. Now at that time, the bhikkhus were scrupulous about water and tooth-cleaners. They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Bhikkhus, I allow you to take and use water and tooth-cleaners yourselves. And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:

265. “Yo pana bhikkhu adinnaṃ mukhadvāraṃ āhāraṃ āhareyya, aññatra udakadantaponā, pācittiya”nti.

265. “Whatever bhikkhu, except for water and tooth-cleaners, should convey food that has not been formally offered to the mouth-door, it is an offense of expiation.”

266. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

266. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever sort… ‘Bhikkhu’ means: … in this context, this is the bhikkhu who is intended.

Adinnaṃ nāma appaṭiggahitakaṃ vuccati.

‘Not formally offered’ means that which has not been formally received.

Dinnaṃ nāma kāyena vā kāyapaṭibaddhena vā nissaggiyena vā dente hatthapāse ṭhito kāyena vā kāyapaṭibaddhena vā paṭiggaṇhāti, etaṃ dinnaṃ nāma.

‘Formally offered’ means: when a person gives with the body, with something connected to the body, or by casting it, and one who is standing within arm’s reach receives it with the body or with something connected to the body. This is called ‘formally offered’.

Āhāro nāma udakadantaponaṃ ṭhapetvā yaṃkiñci ajjhoharaṇīyaṃ, eso āhāro nāma.

‘Food’ means, setting aside water and tooth-cleaners, any swallowable item whatsoever. This is called ‘food’.

Aññatra udakadantaponāti ṭhapetvā udakadantaponaṃ.

‘Except for water and tooth-cleaners’ means setting aside water and tooth-cleaners.

“Khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti gaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

If one takes it with the thought, ‘I will chew, I will eat,’ it is an offense of wrong-doing. For every swallow, it is an offense of expiation.

267. Appaṭiggahitake appaṭiggahitakasaññī adinnaṃ mukhadvāraṃ āhāraṃ āhāreti, aññatra udakadantaponā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Appaṭiggahitake vematiko adinnaṃ mukhadvāraṃ āhāraṃ āhāreti, aññatra udakadantaponā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Appaṭiggahitake paṭiggahitakasaññī adinnaṃ mukhadvāraṃ āhāraṃ āhāreti, aññatra udakadantaponā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

267. Regarding what has not been formally received, if one perceives it as not formally received and conveys food that has not been formally offered to the mouth-door—except for water and tooth-cleaners—it is an offense of expiation. Regarding what has not been formally received, if one is doubtful and conveys food that has not been formally offered to the mouth-door—except for water and tooth-cleaners—it is an offense of expiation. Regarding what has not been formally received, if one perceives it as formally received and conveys food that has not been formally offered to the mouth-door—except for water and tooth-cleaners—it is an offense of expiation.

Paṭiggahitake appaṭiggahitakasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Paṭiggahitake vematiko, āpatti [T 2.0346] dukkaṭassa. Paṭiggahitake paṭiggahitakasaññī, anāpatti.

Regarding what has been formally received, if one perceives it as not formally received, it is an offense of wrong-doing. Regarding what has been formally received, if one is doubtful, it is an offense of wrong-doing. Regarding what has been formally received, if one perceives it as formally received, there is no offense.

268. Anāpatti [M 0.0122][V 0.0125] udakadantapone, cattāri mahāvikatāni sati paccaye asati kappiyakārake sāmaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

268. There is no offense: for water and tooth-cleaners; if, regarding the four great potent medicines, there is a reason and no one to make them allowable, one takes and consumes them oneself; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Dantaponasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Tenth Training Rule on Tooth-Cleaners is concluded.

Bhojanavaggo catuttho.

The Fourth Chapter, on Food, is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Piṇḍo gaṇaṃ paraṃ pūvaṃ, dve ca vuttā pavāraṇā;

Vikāle sannidhī khīraṃ, dantaponena te dasāti.

Almsfood in a rest house, a group meal, consecutive meals, cakes, and the two declared invitations; eating at the wrong time, storing food, choice foods, and with tooth-cleaners—these are the ten.

5. Acelakavaggo

5. The Chapter on Naked Ascetics

1. Acelakasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The Training Rule on Naked Ascetics

269. Tena [T 2.0347][P 4.0091] samayena buddho bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa khādanīyaṃ ussannaṃ hoti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. “Tenahānanda, vighāsādānaṃ pūvaṃ dehī”ti. “Evaṃ bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissuṇitvā vighāsāde paṭipāṭiyā nisīdāpetvā ekekaṃ pūvaṃ dento aññatarissā paribbājikāya ekaṃ maññamāno dve pūve adāsi. Sāmantā paribbājikāyo taṃ paribbājikaṃ etadavocuṃ – “jāro te eso samaṇo”ti. “Na me so samaṇo jāro, ekaṃ maññamāno dve pūve adāsī”ti. Dutiyampi kho…pe… tatiyampi kho āyasmā ānando ekekaṃ pūvaṃ dento tassāyeva paribbājikāya ekaṃ maññamāno dve pūve adāsi. Sāmantā paribbājikāyo taṃ paribbājikaṃ etadavocuṃ – “jāro te eso samaṇo”ti. “Na me so samaṇo jāro, ekaṃ maññamāno dve pūve adāsī”ti. “Jāro na jāro”ti bhaṇḍiṃsu. Aññataropi ājīvako parivesanaṃ agamāsi. Aññataro bhikkhu pahūtena sappinā odanaṃ madditvā tassa ājīvakassa [T 2.0348] mahantaṃ piṇḍaṃ adāsi. Atha kho so ājīvako taṃ piṇḍaṃ ādāya agamāsi. Aññataro ājīvako taṃ ājīvakaṃ etadavoca – “kuto [V 0.0126] tayā, āvuso, piṇḍo laddho”ti? “Tassāvuso, [M 0.0123] samaṇassa gotamassa muṇḍagahapatikassa parivesanāya laddho”ti.

269. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling at Vesālī in the Great Wood, in the Hall with the Peaked Roof. Now at that time the Saṅgha had an abundance of food. Then the Venerable Ānanda informed the Blessed One of this matter. The Buddha said: “Well then, Ānanda, give cakes to those who eat scraps.” “Yes, Venerable Sir,” replied the Venerable Ānanda to the Blessed One. Having assented, he seated those who eat scraps in a row and, while giving one cake to each, thinking it was one, gave two cakes to a certain female wanderer. The neighboring female wanderers said to that female wanderer, “This monk is your lover.” “This monk is not my lover; thinking it was one, he gave two cakes,” she replied. A second time… a third time the Venerable Ānanda, while giving one cake to each, thinking it was one, gave two cakes to that same female wanderer. The neighboring female wanderers said to that female wanderer, “This monk is your lover.” “This monk is not my lover; thinking it was one, he gave two cakes,” she replied. They quarreled, saying, “Lover or not lover.” Meanwhile, a certain Ājīvaka went to the distribution. A certain monk, having mixed rice with abundant ghee, gave a large lump of almsfood to that Ājīvaka. Then that Ājīvaka took the lump of almsfood and departed. Another Ājīvaka asked him, “Friend, where did you get this lump of almsfood?” “Friend, I got it at the distribution of that shaven householder, the ascetic Gotama,” he replied.

Assosuṃ kho upāsakā tesaṃ ājīvakānaṃ imaṃ kathāsallāpaṃ. Atha kho te upāsakā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te upāsakā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “ime, bhante, titthiyā avaṇṇakāmā buddhassa avaṇṇakāmā dhammassa avaṇṇakāmā saṅghassa. Sādhu, bhante, ayyā titthiyānaṃ sahatthā na dadeyyu”nti. Atha kho bhagavā te upāsake dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho te upāsakā bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkamiṃsu. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññapessāmi dasa atthavase paṭicca – saṅghasuṭṭhutāya, saṅghaphāsutāya [P 4.0092]…pe… saddhammaṭṭhitiyā, vinayānuggahāya. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

The lay followers heard this conversation among those Ājīvakas. Then those lay followers approached the Blessed One; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, those lay followers said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, these sectarians are desirous of the Buddha's discredit, desirous of the Dhamma's discredit, desirous of the Saṅgha's discredit. It would be good, venerable sir, if the venerables would not give to the sectarians with their own hands.” Then the Blessed One instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened those lay followers with a Dhamma talk. Having been instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, those lay followers rose from their seats, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping him to their right, and departed. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: “Well then, monks, I will lay down a training rule for the monks on account of ten benefits: for the excellence of the Saṅgha, for the comfort of the Saṅgha … for the endurance of the true Dhamma, for supporting the discipline. And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

270. “Yo pana bhikkhu acelakassa vā paribbājakassa vā paribbājikāya vā [T 2.0349] sahatthā khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā dadeyya, pācittiya”nti.

270. “Whatever monk should give, with his own hand, hard food or soft food to a naked ascetic, a male wanderer, or a female wanderer, it is an offense of expiation.”

271. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

271. Whatever means: whoever, of whatever kind… A monk means: … in this context, this is what is intended by 'monk'.

Acelako nāma yo koci paribbājakasamāpanno naggo.

A naked ascetic means: any naked person who has become a wanderer.

Paribbājako nāma bhikkhuñca sāmaṇerañca ṭhapetvā yo koci paribbājakasamāpanno.

A male wanderer means: excluding a monk and a novice, any person who has become a wanderer.

Paribbājikā nāma bhikkhuniñca sikkhamānañca sāmaṇeriñca ṭhapetvā yā kāci paribbājikasamāpannā.

A female wanderer means: excluding a nun, a probationary nun, and a female novice, any woman who has become a female wanderer.

Khādanīyaṃ nāma pañca bhojanāni – udakadantaponaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ khādanīyaṃ nāma.

Hard food means: excluding the five staple foods and water and tooth-cleaners, the remainder is called hard food.

Bhojanīyaṃ [M 0.0124][V 0.0127] nāma pañca bhojanāni – odano, kummāso, sattu, maccho, maṃsaṃ.

Soft food means: the five staple foods—cooked rice, barley-meal, parched-grain flour, fish, and meat.

Dadeyyāti kāyena vā kāyapaṭibaddhena vā nissaggiyena vā deti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

Should give means: if one gives with the body, with something connected to the body, or by throwing, one commits an offense of expiation.

272. Titthiye titthiyasaññī sahatthā khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā deti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Titthiye vematiko sahatthā khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā deti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Titthiye atitthiyasaññī sahatthā khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā deti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

272. Regarding a sectarian, if one is perceptive that they are a sectarian and gives hard food or soft food with one's own hand, one commits an offense of expiation. Regarding a sectarian, if one is in doubt and gives hard food or soft food with one's own hand, one commits an offense of expiation. Regarding a sectarian, if one is perceptive that they are not a sectarian and gives hard food or soft food with one's own hand, one commits an offense of expiation.

Udakadantaponaṃ deti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Atitthiye titthiyasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Atitthiye vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Atitthiye atitthiyasaññī, anāpatti.

If one gives water and tooth-cleaners, one commits an offense of wrong-doing. Regarding a non-sectarian, if one is perceptive that they are a sectarian, one commits an offense of wrong-doing. Regarding a non-sectarian, if one is in doubt, one commits an offense of wrong-doing. Regarding a non-sectarian, if one is perceptive that they are not a sectarian, there is no offense.

273. Anāpatti dāpeti na deti, upanikkhipitvā deti, bāhirālepaṃ deti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

273. There is no offense if one has another give but does not give oneself; if one gives by placing it nearby; if one gives an external ointment; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Acelakasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The first training rule, concerning the naked ascetic, is concluded.

2. Uyyojanasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Training Rule on Dismissing

274. Tena [T 2.0350] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā upanando sakyaputto bhātuno saddhivihārikaṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “ehāvuso, gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisissāmā”ti. Tassa adāpetvā uyyojesi – “gacchāvuso, na me tayā saddhiṃ kathā vā nisajjā vā phāsu hoti, ekakassa me kathā [P 4.0093] vā nisajjā vā phāsu hotī”ti. Atha kho so bhikkhu upakaṭṭhe kāle nāsakkhi piṇḍāya carituṃ, paṭikkamanepi bhattavissaggaṃ na sambhāvesi, chinnabhatto ahosi. Atha kho so bhikkhu ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā upanando sakyaputto bhikkhuṃ – ‘ehāvuso, gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisissāmā’ti tassa adāpetvā [M 0.0125] uyyojessatī”ti [V 0.0128] …pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, upananda, bhikkhuṃ – “ehāvuso, gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisissāmā”ti tassa adāpetvā uyyojesīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, bhikkhuṃ – “ehāvuso, gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisissāmā”ti tassa adāpetvā uyyojessasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave[T 2.0351], imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

274. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan said this to a monk who was the co-resident of his brother: “Come, friend, let us enter the village for alms.” Without causing him to be given anything, he dismissed him, saying: “Go, friend, for me, speaking or sitting with you is not comfortable; for me, speaking or sitting alone is comfortable.” Then that monk, as the time was near noon, was unable to wander for alms, and in the dining hall, he did not get to the meal distribution; he was one with a missed meal. Then that monk, having gone to the monastery, informed the monks about this matter. Those monks who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan, having said to a monk, ‘Come, friend, let us enter the village for alms,’ dismiss him without causing him to be given anything?” … “Is it true, it is heard, Upananda, that you, having said to a monk, ‘Come, friend, let us enter the village for alms,’ dismissed him without causing him to be given anything?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “How indeed could you, foolish man, having said to a monk, ‘Come, friend, let us enter the village for alms,’ dismiss him without causing him to be given anything? This, foolish man, is not for inspiring confidence in the uninspired… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

275. “Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ – “ehāvuso, gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā piṇḍāya pavisissāmā’ti tassa dāpetvā vā adāpetvā vā uyyojeyya – ‘gacchāvuso, na me tayā saddhiṃ kathā vā nisajjā vā phāsu hoti, ekakassa me kathā vā nisajjā vā phāsu hotī’ti, etadeva paccayaṃ karitvā anaññaṃ, pācittiya”nti.

275. “Whatever monk, having said to a monk, ‘Come, friend, let us enter a village or a market town for alms,’ whether having caused him to be given something or not, should dismiss him, having made this very reason the cause and no other: ‘Go, friend, for me, speaking or sitting with you is not comfortable; for me, speaking or sitting alone is comfortable,’ it is an offense of expiation.”

276. Yo panāti yo, yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

276. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever sort… ‘Monk’ means… in this sense, this is the monk who is intended.

Bhikkhunti aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ.

‘A monk’ means: another monk.

Ehāvuso, gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vāti gāmopi nigamopi nagarampi, gāmo ceva nigamo ca.

‘Come, friend, a village or a market town’ means: a village, a market town, or a city; it is both a village and a market town.

Tassa dāpetvāti yāguṃ vā bhattaṃ vā khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā dāpetvā.

‘Having caused him to be given’ means: having caused gruel, or cooked rice, or hard food, or soft food to be given.

Adāpetvāti na kiñci dāpetvā.

‘Not having caused to be given’ means: not having caused anything to be given.

Uyyojeyyāti mātugāmena saddhiṃ hasitukāmo kīḷitukāmo raho nisīditukāmo anācāraṃ ācaritukāmo evaṃ vadeti – “gacchāvuso, na me tayā saddhiṃ kathā vā nisajjā vā phāsu hoti, ekakassa me kathā vā nisajjā vā phāsu hotī”ti uyyojeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Dassanūpacāraṃ vā savanūpacāraṃ vā vijahantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa. Vijahite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should dismiss’ means: desiring to laugh with a woman, desiring to play, desiring to sit in a secluded place, desiring to practice improper conduct, if he speaks thus: ‘Go, friend, for me, speaking or sitting with you is not comfortable; for me, speaking or sitting alone is comfortable,’ and dismisses him, there is an offense for wrongdoing. While he is leaving the range of sight or the range of hearing, there is an offense for wrongdoing. When he has left, there is an offense of expiation.

Etadeva paccayaṃ karitvā anaññanti na añño koci paccayo hoti uyyojetuṃ.

‘Having made this very reason the cause and no other’ means: there is no other reason whatsoever to dismiss him.

277. Upasampanne [M 0.0126][V 0.0129] upasampannasaññī uyyojeti, āpatti pācittiyassa[T 2.0352]. Upasampanne vematiko uyyojeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne anupasampannasaññī uyyojeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

277. Regarding an ordained person, perceiving him as ordained, if he dismisses him, there is an offense of expiation. Regarding an ordained person, being in doubt, if he dismisses him, there is an offense of expiation. Regarding an ordained person, perceiving him as not ordained, if he dismisses him, there is an offense of expiation.

Kalisāsanaṃ āropeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannaṃ uyyojeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kalisāsanaṃ āropeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne [P 4.0094] upasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne anupasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If he admonishes him out of anger, there is an offense for wrongdoing. If he dismisses a non-ordained person, there is an offense for wrongdoing. If he admonishes him out of anger, there is an offense for wrongdoing. Regarding a non-ordained person, perceiving him as ordained, if he dismisses him, there is an offense for wrongdoing. Regarding a non-ordained person, being in doubt, if he dismisses him, there is an offense for wrongdoing. Regarding a non-ordained person, perceiving him as not ordained, if he dismisses him, there is an offense for wrongdoing.

278. Anāpatti “ubho ekato na yāpessāmā”ti uyyojeti, “mahagghaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ passitvā lobhadhammaṃ uppādessatī”ti uyyojeti, “mātugāmaṃ passitvā anabhiratiṃ uppādessatī”ti uyyojeti, “gilānassa vā ohiyyakassa vā vihārapālassa vā yāguṃ vā bhattaṃ vā khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā nīharā”ti uyyojeti, na anācāraṃ ācaritukāmo, sati karaṇīye uyyojeti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

278. There is no offense if he dismisses him thinking, ‘We two cannot get along together;’ or if he dismisses him thinking, ‘Seeing valuable goods, he will give rise to greed;’ or if he dismisses him thinking, ‘Seeing a woman, he will give rise to discontent;’ or if he dismisses him saying, ‘Bring gruel, cooked rice, hard food, or soft food for a sick person, or for one left behind, or for the monastery keeper;’ if he does not desire to practice improper conduct; if he dismisses him when there is a duty to be done; for an insane person; or for the first offender.

Uyyojanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The second training rule on dismissing is finished.

3. Sabhojanasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Training Rule on a Household Meal

279. Tena [T 2.0353] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā upanando sakyaputto sahāyakassa gharaṃ gantvā tassa pajāpatiyā saddhiṃ sayanighare sayanīghare (syā.) nisajjaṃ kappesi. Atha kho so puriso yenāyasmā upanando sakyaputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so puriso pajāpatiṃ etadavoca – “dadehāyyassa bhikkha”nti. Atha kho sā itthī āyasmato upanandassa sakyaputtassa bhikkhaṃ adāsi. Atha kho so puriso āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ etadavoca – “gacchatha, bhante, yato ayyassa bhikkhā dinnā”ti. Atha kho sā itthī sallakkhetvā – “pariyuṭṭhito ayaṃ puriso”ti, āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ etadavoca [M 0.0127] – “nisīdatha, bhante, mā agamitthā”ti. Dutiyampi kho so puriso…pe… tatiyampi kho so puriso āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ etadavoca [V 0.0130] – “gacchatha, bhante, yato ayyassa bhikkhā dinnā”ti. Tatiyampi kho sā itthī āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ etadavoca – “nisīdatha, bhante, mā agamitthā”ti.

279. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the venerable Upananda the Sakyan went to the house of a friend and arranged to sit in the sleeping chamber with his wife. Then that man approached the venerable Upananda the Sakyan; having approached, he paid homage to the venerable Upananda the Sakyan and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, that man said this to his wife: “Give almsfood to the venerable.” Then that woman gave almsfood to the venerable Upananda the Sakyan. Then that man said this to the venerable Upananda the Sakyan: “Go, venerable sir, since almsfood has been given to the venerable.” Then that woman, having noted, “This man is overcome by lust,” said this to the venerable Upananda the Sakyan: “Please stay seated, venerable sir, do not go.” For a second time, that man… For a third time, that man said this to the venerable Upananda the Sakyan: “Go, venerable sir, since almsfood has been given to the venerable.” For a third time, that woman said this to the venerable Upananda the Sakyan: “Please stay seated, venerable sir, do not go.”

Atha kho so puriso nikkhamitvā bhikkhū ujjhāpesi – “ayaṃ, bhante, ayyo upanando mayhaṃ pajāpatiyā saddhiṃ sayanighare nisinno. So mayā [T 2.0354] uyyojīyamāno na icchati gantuṃ. Bahukiccā mayaṃ bahukaraṇīyā”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā upanando sakyaputto sabhojane kule anupakhajja [P 4.0095] nisajjaṃ kappessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, upananda, sabhojane kule anupakhajja nisajjaṃ kappesīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, sabhojane kule anupakhajja nisajjaṃ kappessasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

Then that man, having left, complained to the monks: “Venerable sirs, this venerable Upananda is sitting in the sleeping chamber with my wife. When sent away by me, he does not wish to go. We have much to do, much to attend to.” Those monks who were of few desires… complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed could the venerable Upananda the Sakyan enter and sit down in a household with a couple?” … “Is it true, Upananda, that you entered and sat down in a household with a couple?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “Foolish man, how indeed could you enter and sit down in a household with a couple? This, foolish man, is not for the confidence of the unconverted… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

280. “Yo pana bhikkhu sabhojane kule anupakhajja nisajjaṃ kappeyya, pācittiya”nti.

280. “Whatever monk should enter and sit down in a household with a couple, it is an offense of expiation.”

281. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

281. ‘Whatever’: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘Monk’: …in this context, this is the monk who is intended.

Sabhojanaṃ nāma kulaṃ itthī ceva hoti puriso ca, itthī ca puriso ca ubho anikkhantā honti, ubho avītarāgā.

A household with a couple means one where there is both a woman and a man; both the woman and the man have not gone out, and both are not free from passion.

Anupakhajjāti anupavisitvā.

‘Entering’: means having entered into their presence.

Nisajjaṃ kappeyyāti mahallake ghare piṭṭhasaṅghāṭassa piṭṭhisaṅghāṭassa (syā.) hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā nisīdati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Khuddake ghare piṭṭhivaṃsaṃ atikkamitvā nisīdati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should arrange a sitting’: if, in a large house, he sits down having left the door-post beyond arm’s reach, he incurs an offense of expiation. If, in a small house, he sits down having gone beyond the ridge-pole, he incurs an offense of expiation.

282. Sayanighare sayanigharasaññī sabhojane kule anupakhajja nisajjaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Sayanighare vematiko sabhojane kule [M 0.0128] anupakhajja nisajjaṃ kappeti, āpatti [V 0.0131] pācittiyassa. Sayanighare nasayanigharasaññī [T 2.0355] sabhojane kule anupakhajja nisajjaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

282. In a sleeping chamber, perceiving it as a sleeping chamber, he enters and sits down in a household with a couple: he incurs an offense of expiation. In a sleeping chamber, being uncertain, he enters and sits down in a household with a couple: he incurs an offense of expiation. In a sleeping chamber, perceiving it as not a sleeping chamber, he enters and sits down in a household with a couple: he incurs an offense of expiation.

Nasayanighare sayanigharasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nasayanighare vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nasayanighare nasayanigharasaññī, anāpatti.

Not in a sleeping chamber, but perceiving it as a sleeping chamber: there is an offense of wrong conduct. Not in a sleeping chamber, but being uncertain: there is an offense of wrong conduct. Not in a sleeping chamber, and perceiving it as not a sleeping chamber: there is no offense.

283. Anāpatti mahallake ghare piṭṭhasaṅghāṭassa hatthapāsaṃ avijahitvā nisīdati, khuddake ghare piṭṭhivaṃsaṃ anatikkamitvā nisīdati, bhikkhu dutiyo hoti, ubho nikkhantā honti, ubho vītarāgā, nasayanighare, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

283. There is no offense: if, in a large house, one sits without leaving the door-post beyond arm’s reach; if, in a small house, one sits without having gone beyond the ridge-pole; if a second monk is present; if both have gone out; if both are free from passion; if it is not in a sleeping chamber; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Sabhojanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The third training rule, concerning a household with a couple, is concluded.

4. Rahopaṭicchannasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Training Rule concerning a Secluded and Concealed Seat

284. Tena [T 2.0356] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā upanando sakyaputto sahāyakassa gharaṃ gantvā tassa pajāpatiyā saddhiṃ raho paṭicchanne āsane [P 4.0096] nisajjaṃ kappesi. Atha kho so puriso ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma ayyo upanando mayhaṃ pajāpatiyā saddhiṃ raho paṭicchanne āsane nisajjaṃ kappessatī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tassa purisassa ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – kathañhi nāma āyasmā upanando sakyaputto mātugāmena saddhiṃ raho paṭicchanne āsane nisajjaṃ kappessatīti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, upananda, mātugāmena saddhiṃ raho paṭicchanne āsane nisajjaṃ kappesīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, mātugāmena saddhiṃ raho paṭicchanne āsane nisajjaṃ kappessasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

284. At one time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. At that time, the venerable Upananda the Sakyan went to the house of a friend and sat down on a secluded and concealed seat with that man's wife. Then that man complained, grumbled, and denounced, saying, “How could the noble Upananda sit on a secluded and concealed seat with my wife?” The monks heard that man complaining, grumbling, and denouncing. Those monks who were of few desires… they complained, grumbled, and denounced, saying, “How could the venerable Upananda the Sakyan sit on a secluded and concealed seat with a woman?” … “Is it true, Upananda, that you sat on a secluded and concealed seat with a woman?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “Foolish man, how could you sit on a secluded and concealed seat with a woman! This, foolish man, is not for the confidence of the faithless… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule in this way:

285. “Yo [M 0.0129] pana bhikkhu mātugāmena saddhiṃ raho paṭicchanne āsane nisajjaṃ kappeyya, pācittiya”nti.

285. “Whatever monk should sit down on a secluded, concealed seat together with a woman, it is an offense of expiation.”

286. Yo [T 2.0357][V 0.0132] panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

286. ‘Whatever’: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘Monk’: …in this context, this is the monk who is intended.

Mātugāmo nāma manussitthī, na yakkhī na petī na tiracchānagatā, antamaso tadahujātāpi dārikā, pageva mahattarī.

A woman means a human female, not a female yakkha, not a female peta, not a female animal; at the very least, even a baby girl born on that day is called a woman, to say nothing of an older woman.

Saddhinti ekato.

‘Together with’ means together.

pāci. 200,291; pārā. 445,454 Raho nāma cakkhussa raho sotassa raho. Cakkhussa raho nāma na sakkā hoti akkhiṃ vā nikhaṇīyamāne bhamukaṃ vā ukkhipīyamāne sīsaṃ vā ukkhipīyamāne passituṃ. Sotassa raho nāma na sakkā hoti pakatikathā sotuṃ.

Secluded means secluded from the eye and secluded from the ear. Secluded from the eye means it is not possible to see by blinking the eye, or by raising the eyebrow, or by lifting the head. Secluded from the ear means it is not possible to hear ordinary conversation.

pārā. 445 Paṭicchannaṃ nāma āsanaṃ kuṭṭena kuḍḍena (sī. syā.) vā kavāṭena vā kilañjena vā sāṇipākārena vā rukkhena vā thambhena vā kotthaḷiyā koṭṭhaḷiyā (sī. syā.) kotthaḷikāya (ka.) vā, yena kenaci paṭicchannaṃ hoti.

A concealed seat means it is concealed by a wall, or by a door-leaf, or by a screen, or by a curtain, or by a tree, or by a pillar, or by a gateway, or by anything whatsoever.

Nisajjaṃ kappeyyāti mātugāme nisinne bhikkhu upanisinno vā hoti upanipanno vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Bhikkhu nisinne mātugāmo upanisinno vā hoti upanipanno vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ubho vā nisinnā honti ubho vā nipannā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

Should sit down means: when a woman is seated, should a monk be seated near or be lying down near, it is an offense of expiation. When a monk is seated, should a woman be seated near or be lying down near, it is an offense of expiation. Should both be seated or should both be lying down, it is an offense of expiation.

287. Mātugāme mātugāmasaññī raho paṭicchanne āsane nisajjaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Mātugāme vematiko raho paṭicchanne āsane nisajjaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Mātugāme amātugāmasaññī raho paṭicchanne āsane nisajjaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

287. Regarding a woman, perceiving her as a woman, one sits on a secluded, concealed seat; it is an offense of expiation. Regarding a woman, being uncertain, one sits on a secluded, concealed seat; it is an offense of expiation. Regarding a woman, perceiving her as not a woman, one sits on a secluded, concealed seat; it is an offense of expiation.

Yakkhiyā vā petiyā vā paṇḍakena vā [T 2.0358] tiracchānagatāya vā manussaviggahitthiyā vā saddhiṃ raho paṭicchanne āsane nisajjaṃ kappeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Amātugāme mātugāmasaññī, āpatti [P 4.0097] dukkaṭassa. Amātugāme vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Amātugāme amātugāmasaññī, anāpatti.

If one arranges to sit on a secluded, concealed seat with a female yakkha, or a female peta, or a paṇḍaka, or a female animal, or a female with a human appearance, it is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of one who is not a woman, if one perceives her as a woman, it is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of one who is not a woman, if one is uncertain, it is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of one who is not a woman, if one perceives her as not a woman, there is no offense.

288. Anāpatti [M 0.0130][V 0.0133] yo koci viññū puriso dutiyo hoti, tiṭṭhati na nisīdati, arahopekkho, aññavihito nisīdati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

288. There is no offense if any discerning man is present as a second person; if one stands and does not sit; if one sits without regard for seclusion, with one's mind directed elsewhere; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Rahopaṭicchannasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.

The fourth training rule, concerning a secluded and concealed place, is concluded.

5. Rahonisajjasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Training Rule on Sitting in Private

289. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā upanando sakyaputto sahāyakassa gharaṃ gantvā tassa pajāpatiyā saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappesi. Atha kho so puriso ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma ayyo upanando mayhaṃ pajāpatiyā saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappessatī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tassa purisassa ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā upanando sakyaputto mātugāmena saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, upananda, mātugāmena saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappesīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, mātugāmena saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappessasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pāsādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

289. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the venerable Upananda the Sakyan, having gone to the house of a friend, arranged to sit alone in private with that friend’s wife. Then that man criticized, condemned, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed could the noble Upananda arrange to sit alone in private with my wife?” The bhikkhus heard that man criticizing, condemning, and speaking disparagingly. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… they criticized, condemned, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed could the venerable Upananda the Sakyan arrange to sit alone in private with a woman?” … “Is it true, Upananda, that you arranged to sit alone in private with a woman?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “How indeed, foolish man, could you arrange to sit alone in private with a woman? This, foolish man, is not for the confidence of the faithless… And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

290. “Yo pana bhikkhu mātugāmena saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappeyya, pācittiya”nti.

290. “Whatever bhikkhu should arrange to sit alone in private with a woman, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

291. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ [T 2.0360] imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

291. Whatever: whichever kind… Bhikkhu: …in this sense, this is the bhikkhu who is meant.

Mātugāmo nāma manussitthī, na yakkhī na petī na tiracchānagatā, viññū paṭibalā subhāsitadubbhāsitaṃ duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ ājānituṃ.

A woman means a human female, not a female yakkha, not a female peta, not a female animal; one who is discerning and capable of understanding what is well-spoken and ill-spoken, what is coarse and not coarse.

Saddhinti ekato.

With means together.

Eko [V 0.0134] ekāyāti bhikkhu ceva hoti mātugāmo ca.

One with one means there is a bhikkhu and a woman.

pāci. 200,286; pārā. 445,454 Raho [M 0.0131] nāma cakkhussa raho, sotassa raho. Cakkhussa raho nāma na sakkā hoti akkhiṃ vā nikhaṇīyamāne bhamukaṃ vā ukkhipīyamāne sīsaṃ vā ukkhipīyamāne passituṃ. Sotassa raho nāma na sakkā hoti pakatikathā sotuṃ.

In private means private to the eye and private to the ear. Private to the eye means it is not possible to see if an eye is being winked, or an eyebrow is being raised, or the head is being raised. Private to the ear means it is not possible to hear ordinary conversation.

Nisajjaṃ kappeyyāti mātugāme nisinne bhikkhu upanisinno vā hoti upanipanno vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Bhikkhu nisinne mātugāmo upanisinno vā hoti upanipanno vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ubho vā nisinnā honti ubho vā nipannā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

Should arrange to sit means: if, while a woman is sitting, a bhikkhu is sitting or lying down nearby, it is an offense of pācittiya. If, while a bhikkhu is sitting, a woman is sitting or lying down nearby, it is an offense of pācittiya. Or if both are sitting or both are lying down, it is an offense of pācittiya.

292. Mātugāme mātugāmasaññī eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Mātugāme vematiko eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Mātugāme amātugāmasaññī eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

292. Regarding a woman, if, perceiving her as a woman, one arranges to sit alone in private, it is an offense of pācittiya. Regarding a woman, if one is uncertain and arranges to sit alone in private, it is an offense of pācittiya. Regarding a woman, if, perceiving her as not a woman, one arranges to sit alone in private, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Yakkhiyā vā petiyā vā paṇḍakena vā tiracchānagatamanussaviggahitthiyā vā tiracchānagatāya vā manussaviggahitthiyā vā (ka.) saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Amātugāme mātugāmasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Amātugāme vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Amātugāme [T 2.0361] amātugāmasaññī, anāpatti.

If one arranges to sit alone in private with a female yakkha, or a female peta, or a paṇḍaka, or a female animal with a human appearance, it is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of one who is not a woman, if one perceives her as a woman, it is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of one who is not a woman, if one is uncertain, it is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of one who is not a woman, if one perceives her as not a woman, there is no offense.

293. Anāpatti yo koci viññū puriso dutiyo hoti, tiṭṭhati na nisīdati, arahopekkho aññavihito nisīdati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

293. There is no offense if any discerning man is a companion; if one stands and does not sit; if, not aiming for privacy, one sits with the mind directed elsewhere; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Rahonisajjasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The fifth training rule on sitting in private is concluded.

6. Cārittasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Training Rule on Conduct

294. Tena [T 2.0362][P 4.0098] samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato upanandassa sakyaputtassa [M 0.0132] upaṭṭhākakulaṃ āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ bhattena nimantesi. Aññepi bhikkhū bhattena nimantesi. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā upanando [V 0.0135] sakyaputto purebhattaṃ, kulāni payirupāsati. Atha kho te bhikkhū te manusse etadavocuṃ – “dethāvuso bhatta”nti. “Āgametha, bhante, yāvāyyo upanando āgacchatī”ti. Dutiyampi kho te bhikkhū…pe… tatiyampi kho te bhikkhū te manusse etadavocuṃ – “dethāvuso, bhattaṃ; pure kālo atikkamatī”ti. “Yampi mayaṃ, bhante, bhattaṃ karimhā ayyassa upanandassa kāraṇā. Āgametha, bhante, yāvāyyo upanando āgacchatī”ti.

294. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Veḷuvana, the Kalandakanivāpa. Now at that time, the attendant family of the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan invited the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan for a meal; they also invited other bhikkhus for a meal. Now at that time, the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan was attending upon families before the meal. Then those bhikkhus said to those people, “Friends, give the meal.” “Venerable sirs, please wait until the noble Upananda arrives.” For a second time... For a third time those bhikkhus said to those people, “Friends, give the meal; the time before noon is passing.” “Venerable sirs, it is on account of the noble Upananda that we have prepared this meal. Venerable sirs, please wait until the noble Upananda arrives.”

Atha kho āyasmā upanando sakyaputto purebhattaṃ kulāni payirupāsitvā divā āgacchati. Bhikkhū na cittarūpaṃ bhuñjiṃsu. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā upanando sakyaputto nimantito sabhatto samāno purebhattaṃ kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, upananda, nimantito sabhatto samāno purebhattaṃ kulesu cārittaṃ [T 2.0363] āpajjasīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, nimantito sabhatto samāno purebhattaṃ kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjissasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

Then the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan, having attended upon families before the meal, arrived late in the day. The bhikkhus did not eat to their satisfaction. Those bhikkhus who were of few desires… complained, criticized, and spoke dispraisingly, saying: “How indeed could the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan, having been invited and provided with a meal, engage in wandering among families before the meal?”… “Is it true, Upananda, that you, having been invited and provided with a meal, engage in wandering among families before the meal?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “How indeed, worthless man, could you, having been invited and provided with a meal, engage in wandering among families before the meal! This, worthless man, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced…” … “And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:

“Yo pana bhikkhu nimantito sabhatto samāno purebhattaṃ kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjeyya, pācittiya”nti.

‘Whatever bhikkhu, having been invited and provided with a meal, should engage in wandering among families before the meal, it is an offense of Pācittiya.’

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule was laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

295. mahāva. 277 Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato upanandassa sakyaputtassa upaṭṭhākakulaṃ saṅghassatthāya khādanīyaṃ pāhesi – “ayyassa upanandassa dassetvā saṅghassa dātabba”nti. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā upanando sakyaputto gāmaṃ piṇḍāya paviṭṭho hoti. Atha kho te manussā ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhū pucchiṃsu – “kahaṃ, bhante, ayyo upanando”ti[P 4.0099]? “Esāvuso, āyasmā upanando sakyaputto gāmaṃ piṇḍāya paviṭṭho”ti. “Idaṃ, bhante, khādanīyaṃ ayyassa upanandassa dassetvā saṅghassa dātabba”nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ [M 0.0133] pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, paṭiggahetvā nikkhipatha yāva upanando āgacchatī”ti.

295. Now at that time, the attendant family of the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan sent solid food for the benefit of the Saṅgha, with the instruction: “It is to be given to the Saṅgha after showing it to the noble Upananda.” Now at that time, the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan had entered the village for alms-food. Then those people, having gone to the monastery, asked the bhikkhus, “Venerable sirs, where is the noble Upananda?” “Friends, this Venerable Upananda the Sakyan has entered the village for alms-food.” “Venerable sirs, this solid food is to be given to the Saṅgha after showing it to the noble Upananda.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus: “In that case, bhikkhus, having accepted it, set it aside until Upananda arrives.”

Atha kho āyasmā upanando sakyaputto – “bhagavatā paṭikkhittaṃ purebhattaṃ kulesu cārittaṃ [V 0.0136] āpajjitu”nti pacchābhattaṃ kulāni [T 2.0364] payirupāsitvā divā paṭikkami, khādanīyaṃ ussāriyittha. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā upanando sakyaputto pacchābhattaṃ kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, upananda, pacchābhattaṃ kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjasīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, pacchābhattaṃ kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjissasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana bhikkhave imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

Then the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan, thinking, “Engaging in wandering among families before the meal has been prohibited by the Blessed One,” attended upon families after the meal and departed late in the day. The solid food was taken back. Those bhikkhus who were of few desires… complained, criticized, and spoke dispraisingly, saying: “How indeed could the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan engage in wandering among families after the meal?”… “Is it true, Upananda, that you engage in wandering among families after the meal?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “How indeed, worthless man, could you engage in wandering among families after the meal! This, worthless man, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced…” … “And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:

“Yo pana bhikkhu nimantito sabhatto samāno purebhattaṃ vā pacchābhattaṃ vā kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjeyya, pācittiya”nti.

‘Whatever bhikkhu, having been invited and provided with a meal, should engage in wandering among families either before the meal or after the meal, it is an offense of Pācittiya.’

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule was laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

296. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū cīvaradānasamaye kukkuccāyantā kulāni na payirupāsanti. Cīvaraṃ parittaṃ uppajjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cīvaradānasamaye kulāni payirupāsituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

296. Now at that time, during the robe-offering season, the bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not attend upon families. Few robes arose. They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “I allow, bhikkhus, attending upon families during the robe-offering season. And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:

“Yo pana bhikkhu nimantito sabhatto samāno purebhattaṃ vā pacchābhattaṃ vā kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjeyya, aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Cīvaradānasamayo – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

‘Whatever bhikkhu, having been invited and provided with a meal, should engage in wandering among families either before the meal or after the meal, except at the proper time, it is an offense of Pācittiya. Therein, this is the proper time: the robe-offering season—this is the proper time therein.’

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule was laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

297. Tena [T 2.0365] kho pana samayena bhikkhū cīvarakammaṃ karonti, attho ca hoti sūciyāpi suttenapi satthakenapi. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā kulāni na payirupāsanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cīvarakārasamaye kulāni payirupāsituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

297. Now at that time, the bhikkhus were doing robe-making work, and there was a need for a needle, thread, and a knife. The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not attend upon families. They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “I allow, bhikkhus, attending upon families during the robe-making season. And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:

“Yo [P 4.0100] pana bhikkhu nimantito sabhatto samāno purebhattaṃ vā pacchābhattaṃ vā kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjeyya[V 0.0137], aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ[M 0.0134]. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Cīvaradānasamayo, cīvarakārasamayo – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

‘Whatever bhikkhu, having been invited and provided with a meal, should engage in wandering among families either before the meal or after the meal, except at the proper time, it is an offense of Pācittiya. Therein, this is the proper time: the robe-offering season, the robe-making season—this is the proper time therein.’

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule was laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

298. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū gilānā honti, attho ca hoti bhesajjehi. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā kulāni na payirupāsanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, santaṃ bhikkhuṃ āpucchā kulāni payirupāsituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

298. Now at that time, bhikkhus were ill, and there was a need for medicines. The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not attend upon families. They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “I allow, bhikkhus, after asking a bhikkhu who is present, to attend upon families. And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:

299. “Yo pana bhikkhu nimantito sabhatto samāno santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā purebhattaṃ vā pacchābhattaṃ vā kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjeyya, aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Cīvaradānasamayo, cīvarakārasamayo – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

299. ‘Whatever bhikkhu, having been invited and provided with a meal, without asking a bhikkhu who is present, should engage in wandering among families either before the meal or after the meal, except at the proper time, it is an offense of Pācittiya. Therein, this is the proper time: the robe-offering season, the robe-making season—this is the proper time therein.’

300. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

300. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhu’ means… in this sense, this is the bhikkhu who is meant.

Nimantito nāma pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ aññatarena bhojanena nimantito.

‘Invited’ means: invited with one or another of the five kinds of food.

Sabhatto nāma yena nimantito [T 2.0366] tena sabhatto.

‘Having a meal’ means: having the meal for which one was invited.

Santaṃ nāma bhikkhuṃ sakkā hoti āpucchā pavisituṃ.

‘A bhikkhu who is present’ means: a bhikkhu whom it is possible to ask before entering.

Asantaṃ nāma bhikkhuṃ na sakkā hoti āpucchā pavisituṃ.

‘A bhikkhu who is not present’ means: a bhikkhu whom it is not possible to ask before entering.

Purebhattaṃ nāma yena nimantito taṃ abhuttāvī.

‘Before the meal’ means: not yet having eaten that meal for which one was invited.

Pacchābhattaṃ nāma yena nimantito taṃ antamaso kusaggenapi aruṇuggamanepi (sī.) bhuttaṃ hoti.

‘After the meal’ means: when that meal for which one was invited has been eaten, even if only as much as a tip of kusa grass.

Kulaṃ nāma cattāri kulāni – khattiyakulaṃ, brāhmaṇakulaṃ, vessakulaṃ, suddakulaṃ.

‘Family’ means: there are four families—the warrior family, the brahmin family, the merchant family, and the servant family.

Kulesu [V 0.0138] cārittaṃ āpajjeyyāti aññassa gharūpacāraṃ okkamantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa. Paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ ummāraṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Dutiyaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should visit families’ means: for one who enters the vicinity of another’s house, there is an offense of wrong-doing. When he makes the first foot cross the threshold, there is an offense of wrong-doing. When he makes the second foot cross, there is an offense of expiation.

Aññatra [M 0.0135] samayāti ṭhapetvā samayaṃ.

‘Except on a suitable occasion’ means: setting aside the occasion.

Cīvaradānasamayo nāma anatthate kathine vassānassa pacchimo māso, atthate kathine pañca māsā.

‘The robe-offering season’ means: when the kathina is not spread, it is the last month of the rains; when the kathina is spread, it is five months.

Cīvarakārasamayo nāma cīvare kayiramāne.

‘The robe-making season’ means: when a robe is being made.

301. Nimantite nimantitasaññī santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā purebhattaṃ vā pacchābhattaṃ vā kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjati, aññatra samayā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Nimantite vematiko santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā purebhattaṃ vā pacchābhattaṃ vā kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjati, aññatra samayā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Nimantite animantitasaññī santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā purebhattaṃ vā pacchābhattaṃ vā kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjati, aññatra samayā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

301. When invited, if he perceives it as an invitation and visits families without asking a bhikkhu who is present, whether before or after the meal, except on a suitable occasion, there is an offense of expiation. When invited, if he is doubtful and visits families without asking a bhikkhu who is present, whether before or after the meal, except on a suitable occasion, there is an offense of expiation. When invited, if he perceives it as not an invitation and visits families without asking a bhikkhu who is present, whether before or after the meal, except on a suitable occasion, there is an offense of expiation.

Animantite nimantitasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Animantite vematiko[P 4.0101], āpatti dukkaṭassa. Animantite animantitasaññī, anāpatti.

When not invited, if he perceives it as an invitation, there is an offense of wrong-doing. When not invited, if he is doubtful, there is an offense of wrong-doing. When not invited, if he perceives it as not an invitation, there is no offense.

302. Anāpatti [T 2.0367] samaye, santaṃ bhikkhuṃ āpucchā pavisati, asantaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā pavisati, aññassa gharena maggo hoti, gharūpacārena maggo hoti, antarārāmaṃ gacchati, bhikkhunupassayaṃ gacchati, titthiyaseyyaṃ gacchati, paṭikkamanaṃ gacchati, bhattiyagharaṃ gacchati, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

302. There is no offense: on the proper occasion; if one enters after asking a bhikkhu who is present; if one enters without asking a bhikkhu who is not present; if the path is through another's house; if the path is through the vicinity of a house; if one goes into a monastery; if one goes to a nunnery; if one goes to a lodging of sectarians; if one goes to a dining hall; if one goes to a kitchen; in times of danger; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Cārittasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The sixth training rule concerning conduct is concluded.

7. Mahānāmasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Training Rule concerning Mahānāma

303. Tena [T 2.0368][V 0.0139] samayena buddho bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Tena kho pana samayena mahānāmassa sakkassa bhesajjaṃ ussannaṃ hoti. Atha kho mahānāmo sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho mahānāmo sakko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “icchāmahaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ catumāsaṃ catummāsaṃ (sī.) cātumāsaṃ (syā.) bhesajjena pavāretu”nti. “Sādhu sādhu[M 0.0136], mahānāma! Tena hi tvaṃ, mahānāma, saṅghaṃ catumāsaṃ bhesajjena pavārehī”ti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nādhivāsenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, catumāsaṃ bhesajjappaccayapavāraṇaṃ sāditunti.

303. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling among the Sakyans in Kapilavatthu, in the Banyan Park. Now at that time, Mahānāma the Sakyan had an abundance of medicine. Then Mahānāma the Sakyan approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Mahānāma the Sakyan said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, I wish to invite the Sangha with medicine for four months.” “Good, good, Mahānāma! In that case, Mahānāma, you should invite the Sangha with medicine for four months.” The monks, being scrupulous, did not consent. They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Monks, I allow the acceptance of an invitation for the requisite of medicine for four months.”

304. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū mahānāmaṃ sakkaṃ parittaṃ bhesajjaṃ viññāpenti. Tatheva mahānāmassa sakkassa bhesajjaṃ ussannaṃ hoti. Dutiyampi kho mahānāmo sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho mahānāmo sakko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “icchāmahaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ aparampi catumāsaṃ bhesajjena pavāretu”nti. “Sādhu sādhu, mahānāma! Tena hi tvaṃ, mahānāma, saṅghaṃ aparampi catumāsaṃ bhesajjena pavārehī”ti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nādhivāsenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, puna pavāraṇampi sāditunti.

304. Now at that time, the monks requested a small amount of medicine from Mahānāma the Sakyan. Even so, Mahānāma the Sakyan had an abundance of medicine. For a second time, Mahānāma the Sakyan approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Mahānāma the Sakyan said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, I wish to invite the Sangha with medicine for another four months.” “Good, good, Mahānāma! In that case, you should invite the Sangha with medicine for another four months.” The monks, being scrupulous, did not consent. They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Monks, I allow the acceptance of a renewed invitation.”

305. Tena [T 2.0369] kho pana samayena bhikkhū mahānāmaṃ sakkaṃ parittaṃyeva bhesajjaṃ viññāpenti. Tatheva mahānāmassa sakkassa bhesajjaṃ ussannaṃ hoti. Tatiyampi kho mahānāmo [P 4.0102] sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho mahānāmo sakko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “icchāmahaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ yāvajīvaṃ bhesajjena pavāretu”nti. “Sādhu sādhu, mahānāma! Tena hi tvaṃ, mahānāma, saṅghaṃ yāvajīvaṃ bhesajjena pavārehī”ti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nādhivāsenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, niccapavāraṇampi sāditunti.

305. Now at that time, the monks requested only a small amount of medicine from Mahānāma the Sakyan. Even so, Mahānāma the Sakyan had an abundance of medicine. For a third time, Mahānāma the Sakyan approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Mahānāma the Sakyan said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, I wish to invite the Sangha with medicine for a lifetime.” “Good, good, Mahānāma! In that case, you should invite the Sangha with medicine for a lifetime.” The monks, being scrupulous, did not consent. They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Monks, I allow the acceptance of a permanent invitation.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū dunnivatthā honti duppārutā anākappasampannā. Mahānāmo sakko vattā hoti – “kissa tumhe, bhante, dunnivatthā duppārutā anākappasampannā? Nanu nāma pabbajitena sunivatthena bhavitabbaṃ supārutena ākappasampannenā”ti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū mahānāme sakke upanandhiṃsu. Atha kho chabbaggiyānaṃ [V 0.0140] bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kena nu kho mayaṃ upāyena mahānāmaṃ sakkaṃ maṅku kareyyāmā”ti? Atha kho chabbaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “mahānāmena kho, āvuso, sakkena saṅgho bhesajjena pavārito. Handa mayaṃ, āvuso, mahānāmaṃ sakkaṃ [M 0.0137] sappiṃ [T 2.0370] viññāpemā”ti. Atha kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhū yena mahānāmo sakko tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā mahānāmaṃ sakkaṃ etadavocuṃ – “doṇena, āvuso, sappinā attho”ti. “Ajjaṇho, bhante, āgametha. Manussā vajaṃ gatā sappiṃ āharituṃ. Kālaṃ āharissathā”ti kāle harissathāti (syā.).

Now at that time, the monks of the group-of-six were badly dressed, badly robed, and not endowed with proper deportment. Mahānāma the Sakyan was one who would say: “Venerable sirs, why are you badly dressed, badly robed, and not endowed with proper deportment? Should not one who has gone forth be well-dressed, well-robed, and endowed with proper deportment?” The monks of the group-of-six bore a grudge against Mahānāma the Sakyan. Then this thought occurred to the monks of the group-of-six: “By what means could we humiliate Mahānāma the Sakyan?” Then this thought occurred to the monks of the group-of-six: “Friends, Mahānāma the Sakyan has invited the Saṅgha with medicine.
