Come, friends, let us request ghee from Mahānāma the Sakyan.” Then the monks of the group-of-six approached Mahānāma the Sakyan; having approached, they said this to Mahānāma the Sakyan: “Friend, there is a need for a doṇa of ghee.” “Venerable sirs,” he replied, “please wait for today. The men have gone to the cattle-pen to fetch ghee. You may fetch it at the proper time.”

Dutiyampi kho…pe… tatiyampi kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhū mahānāmaṃ sakkaṃ etadavocuṃ – “doṇena, āvuso, sappinā attho”ti. “Ajjaṇho, bhante, āgametha. Manussā vajaṃ gatā sappiṃ āharituṃ. Kālaṃ āharissathā”ti. “Kiṃ pana tayā, āvuso, adātukāmena pavāritena, yaṃ tvaṃ pavāretvā na desī”ti! Atha kho mahānāmo sakko ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma bhadantā – ‘ajjaṇho, bhante, āgamethā’ti vuccamānā nāgamessantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū mahānāmassa sakkassa ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū mahānāmena sakkena – ‘ajjaṇho, bhante, āgamethā’ti vuccamānā nāgamessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, mahānāmena sakkena – “ajjaṇho, bhante, āgamethā”ti vuccamānā nāgamethāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, mahānāmena sakkena – “ajjaṇho, bhante āgamethā”ti vuccamānā nāgamessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ [T 2.0371] uddiseyyātha –

For a second time… and for a third time, the monks of the group-of-six said this to Mahānāma the Sakyan: “Friend, there is a need for a doṇa of ghee.” “Venerable sirs,” he replied, “please wait for today. The men have gone to the cattle-pen to fetch ghee. You may fetch it at the proper time.” “Friend, what is the use of your having invited us, if you are unwilling to give? That you, having invited us, do not give?” Then Mahānāma the Sakyan criticized, condemned, and disparaged them, saying: “How is it that the venerable sirs, when told, ‘Venerable sirs, please wait for today,’ will not wait?” The monks heard Mahānāma the Sakyan criticizing, condemning, and disparaging. Those monks who were of few wishes… criticized, condemned, and disparaged them, saying: “How is it that the monks of the group-of-six, when told by Mahānāma the Sakyan, ‘Venerable sirs, please wait for today,’ will not wait?”… “Is it true, monks, that when told by Mahānāma the Sakyan, ‘Venerable sirs, please wait for today,’ you did not wait?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “Worthless men, how is it that you, when told by Mahānāma the Sakyan, ‘Venerable sirs, please wait for today,’ would not wait? This, worthless men, is not for the inspiration of the uninspired… And so, monks, you should set forth this training rule in this way:”

306. “Agilānena bhikkhunā catumāsappaccayapavāraṇā sāditabbā[P 4.0103], aññatra punapavāraṇāya, aññatra niccapavāraṇāya; tato ce uttari sādiyeyya, pācittiya”nti.

306. “An invitation for the requisite of medicine for four months is to be accepted by a monk who is not sick, except for a renewed invitation, and except for a permanent invitation. If he should accept beyond that, it is an offense of expiation.”

307. Agilānena bhikkhunā catumāsappaccayapavāraṇā sāditabbāti gilānappaccayapavāraṇā sāditabbā.

307. ‘An invitation for the requisite of medicine for four months is to be accepted by a monk who is not sick’ means: an invitation of requisites for the sick is to be accepted.

Punapavāraṇāpi sāditabbāti yadā gilāno bhavissāmi tadā viññāpessāmīti.

‘A renewed invitation should also be accepted’ means: it should be accepted thus, “When I am sick, then I will request.”

Niccapavāraṇāpi sāditabbāti yadā gilāno bhavissāmi tadā viññāpessāmīti.

‘A permanent invitation should also be accepted’ means: it should be accepted thus, “When I am sick, then I will request.”

Tato [M 0.0138][V 0.0141] ce uttari sādiyeyyāti atthi pavāraṇā bhesajjapariyantā na rattipariyantā, atthi pavāraṇā rattipariyantā na bhesajjapariyantā, atthi pavāraṇā bhesajjapariyantā ca rattipariyantā ca, atthi pavāraṇā neva bhesajjapariyantā na rattipariyantā.

‘If one should accept beyond that’ means: there is an invitation limited by medicine, not by nights; there is an invitation limited by nights, not by medicine; there is an invitation limited by both medicine and by nights; there is an invitation limited by neither medicine nor by nights.

Bhesajjapariyantā nāma bhesajjāni pariggahitāni honti – “ettakehi bhesajjehi pavāremī”ti. Rattipariyantā nāma rattiyo pariggahitāyo honti – “ettakāsu rattīsu pavāremī”ti. Bhesajjapariyantā ca rattipariyantā ca nāma bhesajjāni ca pariggahitāni honti rattiyo ca pariggahitāyo honti – “ettakehi bhesajjehi ettakāsu rattīsu pavāremī”ti. Neva bhesajjapariyantā na rattipariyantā nāma bhesajjāni ca apariggahitāni honti rattiyo ca apariggahitāyo honti.

‘Limited by medicine’ means that medicines are specified: “I invite with this much medicine.” ‘Limited by nights’ means that nights are specified: “I invite for this many nights.” ‘Limited by both medicine and nights’ means that both medicines and nights are specified: “I invite with this much medicine for this many nights.” ‘Limited by neither medicine nor nights’ means that neither medicines nor nights are specified.

308. Bhesajjapariyante [T 2.0372] – yehi bhesajjehi pavārito hoti tāni bhesajjāni ṭhapetvā aññāni bhesajjāni viññāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Rattipariyante – yāsu rattīsu pavārito hoti, tā rattiyo ṭhapetvā aññāsu rattīsu viññāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Bhesajjapariyante ca rattipariyante ca – yehi bhesajjehi pavārito hoti, tāni bhesajjāni ṭhapetvā yāsu rattīsu pavārito hoti, tā rattiyo ṭhapetvā aññāni bhesajjāni aññāsu rattīsu viññāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Neva bhesajjapariyante na rattipariyante, anāpatti.

308. In the case of an invitation limited by medicine: if, having set aside those medicines with which one has been invited, one requests other medicines, there is an offense of expiation. In the case of an invitation limited by nights: if, having set aside those nights for which one has been invited, one requests on other nights, there is an offense of expiation. In the case of an invitation limited by both medicine and nights: if, having set aside those medicines with which one has been invited, and having set aside those nights for which one has been invited, one requests other medicines on other nights, there is an offense of expiation. In the case of an invitation limited by neither medicine nor nights, there is no offense.

309. Na bhesajjena karaṇīyena karaṇīye (sī. syā.) bhesajjaṃ viññāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Aññena bhesajjena karaṇīyena aññaṃ bhesajjaṃ viññāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Tatuttari tatuttarisaññī bhesajjaṃ viññāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Tatuttari vematiko bhesajjaṃ viññāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Tatuttari natatuttarisaññī bhesajjaṃ viññāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

309. If one requests medicine when there is no need for medicine, there is an offense of expiation. If one requests one medicine when there is need for another medicine, there is an offense of expiation. If it is beyond the limit and one perceives it as beyond the limit when requesting medicine, there is an offense of expiation. If it is beyond the limit and one is doubtful when requesting medicine, there is an offense of expiation. If it is beyond the limit but one perceives it as not beyond the limit when requesting medicine, there is an offense of expiation.

Natatuttari tatuttarisaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Natatuttari vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Natatuttari natatuttarisaññī, anāpatti.

If it is not beyond the limit but one perceives it as beyond the limit, there is an offense of wrongdoing. If it is not beyond the limit but one is doubtful, there is an offense of wrongdoing. If it is not beyond the limit and one perceives it as not beyond the limit, there is no offense.

310. Anāpatti [M 0.0139] yehi bhesajjehi pavārito hoti tāni bhesajjāni viññāpeti, yāsu rattīsu pavārito hoti tāsu rattīsu viññāpeti[T 2.0373], “imehi tayā [P 4.0104] bhesajjehi pavāritāmha[V 0.0142], amhākañca iminā ca iminā ca bhesajjena attho”ti ācikkhitvā viññāpeti, “yāsu tayā rattīsu pavāritāmha tāyo ca rattiyo vītivattā amhākañca bhesajjena attho”ti ācikkhitvā viññāpeti, ñātakānaṃ pavāritānaṃ, aññassatthāya, attano dhanena, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

310. There is no offense if one requests those medicines with which one was invited; if one requests on those nights for which one was invited; if, having stated, “We were invited by you with these medicines, and we have need of this and that medicine,” one requests; if, having stated, “Those nights for which you invited us have passed, and we have need of medicine,” one requests; if one requests from relatives or from those who have invited; for the sake of another; with one’s own property; for one who is insane; for the originator of the matter.

Mahānāmasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.

The seventh training rule concerning Mahānāma is concluded.

8. Uyyuttasenāsikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Training Rule Concerning a Deployed Army

311. Tena [T 2.0374] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena rājā pasenadi kosalo senāya abbhuyyāto hoti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uyyuttaṃ senaṃ dassanāya agamaṃsu. Addasā kho rājā pasenadi kosalo chabbaggiye bhikkhū dūratova āgacchante. Disvāna pakkosāpetvā etadavoca – “kissa tumhe, bhante, āgatatthā”ti? “Mahārājānaṃ mayaṃ daṭṭhukāmā” mahārāja mahārājānaṃ mayaṃ daṭṭhukāmā (ka.) ti. “Kiṃ, bhante, maṃ diṭṭhena yuddhābhinandinaṃ yuddhābhinandinā (ka.); nanu bhagavā passitabbo”ti? Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā uyyuttaṃ senaṃ dassanāya āgacchissanti! Amhākampi alābhā, amhākampi dulladdhaṃ, ye mayaṃ ājīvassa hetu puttadārassa kāraṇā senāya āgacchāmā”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uyyuttaṃ senaṃ dassanāya gacchissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, uyyuttaṃ senaṃ dassanāya gacchathāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, uyyuttaṃ senaṃ dassanāya gacchissatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… [T 2.0375] evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

311. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, King Pasenadi of Kosala had gone forth with his army. The group-of-six bhikkhus went to see the deployed army. King Pasenadi of Kosala saw the group-of-six bhikkhus coming from afar. Having seen them, he had them summoned and said this: “For what reason, venerable sirs, have you come?” “We desire to see the great king.” “Venerable sirs, what is there in seeing me, who delights in warfare? Should not the Blessed One be seen?” The people censured, condemned, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed can the Sakyan recluses come to see a deployed army? It is no gain for us, it is ill-gotten for us, that we come with the army for the sake of our livelihood and for the sake of our wives and children!” The bhikkhus heard those people censuring, condemning, and speaking disparagingly. Those bhikkhus who were of few wants... censured, condemned, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed can the group-of-six bhikkhus go to see a deployed army?”... “Bhikkhus, is it true that you go to see a deployed army?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... “How indeed, foolish men, can you go to see a deployed army? This, foolish men, is not for the faith of the faithless... And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Yo [M 0.0140] pana bhikkhu uyyuttaṃ senaṃ dassanāya gaccheyya, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever bhikkhu should go to see a deployed army, it is a pācittiya offense.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

In this way, this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhus.

312. Tena [P 4.0105] kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno mātulo senāya gilāno hoti[V 0.0143]. So tassa bhikkhuno santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – “ahañhi senāya gilāno. Āgacchatu bhadanto. Icchāmi bhadantassa āgata”nti. Atha kho tassa bhikkhuno etadahosi – “bhagavatā sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ – ‘na uyyuttaṃ senaṃ dassanāya gantabba’nti. Ayañca me mātulo senāya gilāno. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tathārūpappaccayā senāya gantuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

312. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu’s maternal uncle was sick in the army. He sent a messenger to that bhikkhu, saying: “I am sick in the army. Let the good master come. I desire the good master’s arrival.” Then it occurred to that bhikkhu: “The Blessed One has laid down the training rule: ‘One should not go to see a deployed army.’ And this maternal uncle of mine is sick in the army. How now should I act?” He reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a discourse on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus: “I allow, bhikkhus, going to the army for a reason of such a nature. And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

313. “Yo pana bhikkhu uyyuttaṃ senaṃ dassanāya gaccheyya, aññatra tathārūpappaccayā, pācittiya”nti.

313. “Whatever bhikkhu should go to see a deployed army, except for a reason of such a nature, it is a pācittiya offense.”

314. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

314. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever sort... ‘Bhikkhu’ means... the bhikkhu who is intended in this context is ‘bhikkhu’.

Uyyuttā nāma senā gāmato nikkhamitvā niviṭṭhā vā hoti payātā vā.

A ‘deployed army’ is one that, having marched out from a village, is either encamped or has marched on.

Senā nāma hatthī assā rathā pattī. Dvādasapuriso hatthī, tipuriso asso, catupuriso ratho, cattāro purisā sarahatthā patti. Dassanāya gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yattha ṭhito passati, āpatti [T 2.0376] pācittiyassa. Dassanūpacāraṃ vijahitvā punappunaṃ passati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

An army means: elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry. An elephant unit has twelve men; a horse unit has three men; a chariot unit has four men; infantry are four men with arrows in hand. If one goes to see it, there is an offense of wrong-doing. At the place where one stands and sees it, there is an offense of pācittiya. If, having left the range of sight, one sees it again and again, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Aññatra tathārūpappaccayāti ṭhapetvā tathārūpappaccayaṃ.

‘Except for a reason of such a nature’ means: setting aside a reason of such a nature.

315. Uyyutte uyyuttasaññī dassanāya gacchati, aññatra tathārūpappaccayā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Uyyutte vematiko dassanāya gacchati, aññatra tathārūpappaccayā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Uyyutte anuyyuttasaññī dassanāya gacchati, aññatra tathārūpappaccayā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

315. When it is deployed, if one perceives it as deployed and goes to see it—except for a reason of such a nature—there is an offense of pācittiya. When it is deployed, if one is in doubt and goes to see it—except for a reason of such a nature—there is an offense of pācittiya. When it is deployed, if one perceives it as not deployed and goes to see it—except for a reason of such a nature—there is an offense of pācittiya.

Ekamekaṃ [M 0.0141] dassanāya gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yattha ṭhito passati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Dassanūpacāraṃ vijahitvā punappunaṃ passati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anuyyutte uyyuttasaññī[V 0.0144], āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anuyyutte vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anuyyutte anuyyuttasaññī, anāpatti.

If one goes to see each single component, there is an offense of wrong-doing. At the place where one stands and sees it, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If, having left the range of sight, one sees it again and again, there is an offense of wrong-doing. When it is not deployed, if one perceives it as deployed, there is an offense of wrong-doing. When it is not deployed, if one is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing. When it is not deployed, if one perceives it as not deployed, there is no offense.

316. Anāpatti ārāme ṭhito passati, bhikkhussa ṭhitokāsaṃ vā nisinnokāsaṃ vā nipannokāsaṃ vā āgacchati, paṭipathaṃ gacchanto passati, tathārūpappaccayā, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

316. There is no offense: if one sees it while standing in a monastery; if it comes to the bhikkhu’s standing place, sitting place, or lying place; if one sees it while meeting it on the path; for a reason of such a nature; in times of danger; for one who is insane; for the originator of the matter.

Uyyuttasenāsikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The eighth training rule, concerning a deployed army, is concluded.

9. Senāvāsasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Training Rule Concerning Lodging with an Army

317. Tena [T 2.0377][P 4.0106] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sati karaṇīye senaṃ gantvā atirekatirattaṃ senāya vasanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā senāya vasissanti! Amhākampi alābhā, amhākampi dulladdhaṃ, ye mayaṃ ājīvassa hetu puttadārassa kāraṇā senāya paṭivasāmā”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū atirekatirattaṃ senāya vasissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, atirekatirattaṃ senāya vasathāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, atirekatirattaṃ senāya vasissatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

317. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, when there was some business to be done, the bhikkhus of the group-of-six went to an army and stayed with the army for more than three nights. People complained, grumbled, and criticized, “How can these Sakyan recluses stay with an army! It is our loss, it is our misfortune, that we have to stay in an army for the sake of our livelihood and for the sake of our wives and children.” The bhikkhus heard those people complaining, grumbling, and criticizing. Those bhikkhus who were of few desires… complained, grumbled, and criticized, “How can the bhikkhus of the group-of-six stay with an army for more than three nights?”… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that you stayed with the army for more than three nights?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How can you, foolish men, stay with the army for more than three nights? This, foolish men, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And thus, bhikkhus, this training rule should be recited:

318. “Siyā ca tassa bhikkhuno kocideva paccayo senaṃ gamanāya, dirattatirattaṃ tena bhikkhunā senāya vasitabbaṃ. Tato ce uttariṃ vaseyya, pācittiya”nti.

318. “Should there be for that bhikkhu some reason for going to an army, that bhikkhu may stay with the army for two or three nights. Should he stay longer than that, it is an offense of expiation.”

319. Siyā ca tassa bhikkhuno kocideva paccayo senaṃ gamanāyāti [T 2.0378] siyā paccayo siyā karaṇīyaṃ.

319. ‘Should there be for that bhikkhu some reason for going to an army’ means: there may be a reason, there may be some business to be done.

Dirattatirattaṃ [M 0.0142][V 0.0145] tena bhikkhunā senāya vasitabbanti dvetisso rattiyo vasitabbaṃ.

‘That bhikkhu may stay with the army for two or three nights’ means: he may stay for two or three nights.

Tato ce uttari vaseyyāti catutthe divase atthaṅgate sūriye senāya vasati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should he stay longer than that’ means: if on the fourth day, after the sun has set, he stays with the army, he incurs an offense of expiation.

320. Atirekatiratte atirekasaññī senāya vasati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Atirekatiratte vematiko senāya vasati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Atirekatiratte ūnakasaññī senāya vasati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

320. When it is more than three nights, if he perceives it as more and stays with the army, he incurs an offense of expiation. When it is more than three nights, if he is uncertain and stays with the army, he incurs an offense of expiation. When it is more than three nights, if he perceives it as less and stays with the army, he incurs an offense of expiation.

Ūnakatiratte atirekasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ūnakatiratte vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ūnakatiratte ūnakasaññī, anāpatti.

When it is less than three nights, if he perceives it as more, he incurs an offense of wrong-doing. When it is less than three nights, if he is uncertain, he incurs an offense of wrong-doing. When it is less than three nights, if he perceives it as less, there is no offense.

321. Anāpatti dvetisso rattiyo vasati, ūnakadvetisso rattiyo vasati, dve rattiyo vasitvā tatiyāya rattiyā purāruṇā nikkhamitvā puna vasati, gilāno vasati, gilānassa karaṇīyena vasati, senā [P 4.0107] vā paṭisenāya ruddhā hoti, kenaci palibuddho hoti, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

321. There is no offense: if one stays for two or three nights; if one stays for less than two or three nights; if, having stayed for two nights, one leaves before dawn on the third night and then stays again; if one stays while sick; if one stays on account of business for a sick person; if the army is besieged by another army; if one is hindered by some danger; in times of calamity; for one who is insane; and for the first offender.

Senāvāsasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.

The Ninth Training Rule Concerning Lodging with an Army is concluded.

10. Uyyodhikasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Training Rule on a Military Engagement

322. Tena [T 2.0379] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū dirattatirattaṃ senāya vasamānā uyyodhikampi balaggampi senābyūhampi anīkadassanampi gacchanti. Aññataropi chabbaggiyo bhikkhu uyyodhikaṃ gantvā kaṇḍena paṭividdho hoti. Manussā taṃ bhikkhuṃ uppaṇḍesuṃ – “kacci, bhante, suyuddhaṃ ahosi, kati te lakkhāni laddhānī”ti? So bhikkhu tehi manussehi uppaṇḍīyamāno maṅku ahosi. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā uyyodhikaṃ dassanāya āgacchissanti! Amhākampi alābhā, amhākampi dulladdhaṃ, ye mayaṃ ājīvassa hetu [M 0.0143] puttadārassa kāraṇā uyyodhikaṃ āgacchāmā”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ[V 0.0146]. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uyyodhikaṃ dassanāya gacchissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, uyyodhikaṃ dassanāya gacchathāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, uyyodhikaṃ dassanāya gacchissatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave[T 2.0380], imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

322. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. At that time the group-of-six bhikkhus, while staying with an army for two or three nights, went to see a military engagement, a troop muster, an army formation, or a troop review. A certain bhikkhu of the group-of-six went to a military engagement and was pierced by an arrow. People mocked him, saying, “Venerable, was it a good battle? How many rewards did you get?” That bhikkhu, being mocked by those people, was ashamed. The people complained, grumbled, and spread it about: “How can these recluses, sons of the Sakyan, come to see a military engagement! It is no gain for us, it is ill-gotten for us, that we come to a military engagement for the sake of our livelihood and for the sake of our wives and children.” The bhikkhus heard those people complaining, grumbling, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhus who were of few desires… they complained, grumbled, and spread it about: “How can the group-of-six bhikkhus go to see a military engagement?”… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that you go to see a military engagement?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, foolish men, can you go to see a military engagement! This, foolish men, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And so, bhikkhus, this training rule should be recited:

323. “Dirattatirattaṃ ce bhikkhu senāya vasamāno uyyodhikaṃ vā balaggaṃ vā senābyūhaṃ vā anīkadassanaṃ vā gaccheyya, pācittiya”nti.

323. “If a bhikkhu, staying with an army for two or three nights, should go to a military engagement, or a troop muster, or an army formation, or a troop review, it is an offense of expiation.”

324. Dirattatirattaṃ ce bhikkhu senāya vasamānoti dvetisso rattiyo vasamāno.

324. ‘A bhikkhu staying with an army for two or three nights’ means a bhikkhu staying for two or three nights.

Uyyodhikaṃ nāma yattha sampahāro dissati.

A military engagement means where combat is seen.

Balaggaṃ nāma ettakā hatthī, ettakā assā, ettakā rathā, ettakā pattī.

A troop muster means: so many elephants, so many horses, so many chariots, so many foot-soldiers.

Senābyūhaṃ nāma ito hatthī hontu, ito assā hontu, ito rathā hontu, ito pattikā hontu.

An army formation means: “Let there be elephants here, let there be horses here, let there be chariots here, let there be foot-soldiers here.”

Anīkaṃ nāma hatthānīkaṃ, assānīkaṃ[P 4.0108], rathānīkaṃ, pattānīkaṃ. Tayo hatthī pacchimaṃ hatthānīkaṃ, tayo assā pacchimaṃ assānīkaṃ, tayo rathā pacchimaṃ rathānīkaṃ, cattāro purisā sarahatthā pattī pacchimaṃ pattānīkaṃ. Dassanāya gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yattha ṭhito passati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dassanūpacāraṃ vijahitvā punappunaṃ passati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A military troop means: an elephant troop, a horse troop, a chariot troop, or a foot-soldier troop. Three elephants are the minimum for an elephant troop; three horses are the minimum for a horse troop; three chariots are the minimum for a chariot troop; four men on foot with arrows in hand are the minimum for a foot-soldier troop. If one goes for the purpose of seeing, there is an offense of wrong-doing. From the place where one stands and sees, there is an offense of expiation. Having left the range of sight, if one sees again and again, there is an offense of expiation.

Ekamekaṃ dassanāya gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yattha ṭhito passati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Dassanūpacāraṃ vijahitvā punappunaṃ passati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one goes to see each one, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one stands in a place and sees, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Having left the range of sight, if one sees again and again, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

325. Anāpatti [M 0.0144] ārāme ṭhito passati, bhikkhussa ṭhitokāsaṃ vā nisinnokāsaṃ vā [V 0.0147] nipannokāsaṃ vā āgantvā sampahāro dissati, paṭipathaṃ gacchanto passati, sati karaṇīye gantvā passati[T 2.0381], āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

325. There is no offense if one sees while standing in the monastery; if combat comes into view at the bhikkhu’s standing place, sitting place, or lying place; if one sees while proceeding along the path; if one goes and sees when there is a duty to be performed; in times of misfortune; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Uyyodhikasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

The tenth training rule, on military engagements, is concluded.

Acelakavaggo pañcamo.

The fifth, the Acelaka Chapter, is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Pūvaṃ kathopanandassa, tayaṃpaṭṭhākameva ca;

Mahānāmo pasenadi, senāviddho ime dasāti acelakaṃ uyyojañca, sabhojanaṃ duve raho; sabhattakañca bhesajjaṃ, uyyuttaṃ senuyyodhikaṃ.

Cakes, Upananda's speech, the three, and the attendant; Mahānāma, Pasenadi, the army, the pierced—these are the ten.

6. Surāpānavaggo

6. The Chapter on Drinking Liquor

1. Surāpānasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The Training Rule on Drinking Liquor

326. Tena [T 2.0382][V 0.0148] samayena buddho bhagavā cetiyesu cārikaṃ caramāno yena bhaddavatikā tena pāyāsi. Addasaṃsu kho gopālakā pasupālakā kassakā pathāvino bhagavantaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “mā kho, bhante, bhagavā ambatitthaṃ agamāsi. Ambatitthe, bhante, jaṭilassa assame nāgo paṭivasati iddhimā āsiviso āsīviso (sī. syā.) ghoraviso. So bhagavantaṃ mā viheṭhesī”ti. Evaṃ vutte bhagavā tuṇhī ahosi. Dutiyampi kho…pe… tatiyampi kho gopālakā pasupālakā kassakā pathāvino bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “mā kho, bhante, bhagavā ambatitthaṃ agamāsi. Ambatitthe, bhante, jaṭilassa assame nāgo paṭivasati iddhimā āsiviso ghoraviso. So bhagavantaṃ mā viheṭhesī”ti. Tatiyampi kho bhagavā tuṇhī ahosi.

326. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was wandering on tour in the Ceti country and arrived at Bhaddavatika. Cowherds, shepherds, farmers, and travelers saw the Blessed One coming from afar. Having seen him, they said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One not go to Ambatittha. At Ambatittha, Venerable Sir, in the hermitage of the matted-hair ascetic, there lives a nāga that is powerful, of swift venom, and of terrible venom. May he not harm the Blessed One.” When this was said, the Blessed One remained silent. For a second time… For a third time, the cowherds, shepherds, farmers, and travelers said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One not go to Ambatittha. At Ambatittha, Venerable Sir, in the hermitage of the matted-hair ascetic, there lives a nāga that is powerful, of swift venom, and of terrible venom. May he not harm the Blessed One.” For a third time, the Blessed One remained silent.

Atha kho bhagavā anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena bhaddavatikā tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā bhaddavatikāyaṃ viharati[P 4.0109]. Atha kho āyasmā sāgato yena ambatitthassa ambatitthakassa (sī.), ambatitthaṃ (syā.) jaṭilassa assamo tenupasaṅkami[M 0.0145]; upasaṅkamitvā agyāgāraṃ pavisitvā tiṇasanthārakaṃ paññapetvā nisīdi pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. Addasā kho so nāgo āyasmantaṃ sāgataṃ paviṭṭhaṃ[T 2.0383]. Disvāna dummano dukkhī dummano (sī. syā.) padhūpāyi padhūpāsi (syā. ka.). Āyasmāpi sāgato padhūpāyi padhūpāsi (syā. ka.). Atha kho so nāgo makkhaṃ asahamāno pajjali. Āyasmāpi sāgato tejodhātuṃ samāpajjitvā pajjali. Atha kho āyasmā sāgato tassa nāgassa tejasā tejaṃ pariyādiyitvā yena bhaddavatikā tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho bhagavā bhaddavatikāyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena kosambī tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Assosuṃ kho kosambikā upāsakā – “ayyo kira sāgato ambatitthikena nāgena saddhiṃ saṅgāmesī”ti.

Then the Blessed One, wandering on tour by stages, arrived at Bhaddavatika. The Blessed One dwelt there in Bhaddavatika. Then the Venerable Sāgata approached the hermitage of the matted-hair ascetic of Ambatittha. Having approached, he entered the fire-hut, spread out a grass mat, and sat down, folding his legs crosswise, setting his body erect, and establishing mindfulness before him. That nāga saw the Venerable Sāgata entering. Having seen him, it was displeased and emitted smoke. The Venerable Sāgata also emitted smoke. Then that nāga, unable to endure its anger, burst into flames. The Venerable Sāgata also, having attained the absorption on the fire element, burst into flames. Then the Venerable Sāgata, having overcome the nāga’s power with his own power, approached Bhaddavatika. Then the Blessed One, having dwelt at Bhaddavatika for as long as he wished, set out on tour toward Kosambī. The lay followers of Kosambī heard: “It is said that the venerable Sāgata did battle with the nāga of Ambatittha.”

Atha kho bhagavā anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena kosambī tadavasari. Atha kho kosambikā upāsakā bhagavato paccuggamanaṃ karitvā yenāyasmā sāgato tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ sāgataṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho kosambikā [V 0.0149] upāsakā āyasmantaṃ sāgataṃ etadavocuṃ – “kiṃ, bhante, ayyānaṃ dullabhañca manāpañca, kiṃ paṭiyādemā”ti? Evaṃ vutte chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kosambike upāsake etadavocuṃ – “atthāvuso, kāpotikā nāma pasannā bhikkhūnaṃ dullabhā ca manāpā ca, taṃ paṭiyādethā”ti. Atha kho kosambikā upāsakā ghare ghare kāpotikaṃ pasannaṃ paṭiyādetvā āyasmantaṃ sāgataṃ piṇḍāya paviṭṭhaṃ disvāna āyasmantaṃ sāgataṃ etadavocuṃ – “pivatu, bhante, ayyo sāgato kāpotikaṃ pasannaṃ, pivatu[T 2.0384], bhante, ayyo sāgato kāpotikaṃ pasanna”nti. Atha kho āyasmā sāgato ghare ghare kāpotikaṃ pasannaṃ pivitvā nagaramhā nikkhamanto nagaradvāre paripati.

Then the Blessed One, wandering on tour by stages, arrived at Kosambī. Then the lay followers of Kosambī, having gone out to meet the Blessed One, approached the Venerable Sāgata. Having approached and paid homage to the Venerable Sāgata, they stood to one side. Standing to one side, the lay followers of Kosambī said this to the Venerable Sāgata: “Venerable Sir, what is both rare and pleasing for the venerables? What should we prepare?” When this was said, the group-of-six bhikkhus said this to the lay followers of Kosambī: “Friends, there is a clear liquor called ‘pigeon-foot colored’ that is rare and pleasing for the bhikkhus. Prepare that.” Then the lay followers of Kosambī, having prepared the clear, pigeon-foot colored liquor in every house, and seeing the Venerable Sāgata entering for alms, said this to the Venerable Sāgata: “Venerable Sir, may the venerable Sāgata drink the clear, pigeon-foot colored liquor. Venerable Sir, may the venerable Sāgata drink the clear, pigeon-foot colored liquor.” Then the Venerable Sāgata, having drunk the clear, pigeon-foot colored liquor in every house, fell down at the city gate as he was leaving the city.

Atha kho bhagavā sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ nagaramhā nikkhamanto addasa āyasmantaṃ sāgataṃ nagaradvāre paripatantaṃ. Disvāna bhikkhū āmantesi – “gaṇhatha, bhikkhave, sāgata”nti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paṭissuṇitvā āyasmantaṃ sāgataṃ ārāmaṃ netvā yena bhagavā tena sīsaṃ katvā nipātesuṃ. Atha kho āyasmā sāgato parivattitvā yena bhagavā tena pāde karitvā seyyaṃ kappesi[M 0.0146]. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “nanu, bhikkhave, pubbe sāgato tathāgate sagāravo ahosi sappatisso”ti[P 4.0110]? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Api nu kho, bhikkhave, sāgato etarahi tathāgate sagāravo sappatisso”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Nanu, bhikkhave, sāgato ambatitthikena nāgena ḍeḍḍubhenāpi (sī. syā.) saddhiṃ saṅgāmesī”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Api nu kho, bhikkhave, sāgato etarahi pahoti nāgena saddhiṃ saṅgāmetu”nti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Api nu kho, bhikkhave, taṃ pātabbaṃ yaṃ pivitvā visaññī assā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Ananucchavikaṃ, bhikkhave, sāgatassa ananulomikaṃ appatirūpaṃ assāmaṇakaṃ akappiyaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, sāgato majjaṃ pivissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca [T 2.0385] pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

Then the Blessed One, leaving the city with many monks, saw the Venerable Sāgata collapsing at the city gate. Seeing him, he addressed the monks: “Monks, take Sāgata.” “Yes, Venerable Sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One. They took the Venerable Sāgata to the monastery and laid him down with his head toward the Blessed One. Then the Venerable Sāgata turned over and lay down with his feet toward the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks, was not Sāgata formerly respectful and deferential toward the Tathāgata?” “Yes, Venerable Sir.” “But now, monks, is Sāgata respectful and deferential toward the Tathāgata?” “No, indeed, Venerable Sir.” “Monks, did not Sāgata engage in battle with the nāga of Ambatittha?” “Yes, Venerable Sir.” “But now, monks, is Sāgata able to engage in battle with a nāga?” “No, indeed, Venerable Sir.” “Monks, should that be drunk which, having been drunk, one would become senseless?” “No, indeed, Venerable Sir.” “Monks, this is unbecoming for Sāgata, unsuitable, improper, not the conduct of a recluse, unallowable, not to be done. How indeed could Sāgata drink an intoxicant! This, monks, is not for inspiring faith in the unfaithful… and so, monks, you should recite this training rule in this way:

327. “Surāmerayapāne pācittiya”nti.

327. “In the drinking of fermented liquor and distilled spirits, there is an offense requiring expiation.”

328. Surā nāma piṭṭhasurā pūvasurā odanasurā kiṇṇapakkhittā sambhārasaṃyuttā.

328. Fermented liquor means: liquor made from flour, liquor made from cakes, liquor made from rice, that to which yeast has been added, and that which is combined with various ingredients.

Merayo nāma pupphāsavo phalāsavo madhvāsavo guḷāsavo sambhārasaṃyutto.

Distilled spirits means: a liquor made from flowers, a liquor made from fruits, a liquor made from honey, a liquor made from molasses, and that which is combined with various ingredients.

Piveyyāti [V 0.0150] antamaso kusaggenapi pivati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should one drink’: if one drinks even with the tip of a blade of kusa grass, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Majje majjasaññī pivati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Majje vematiko pivati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Majje amajjasaññī pivati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

Regarding an intoxicant, if one perceives it as an intoxicant and drinks it, there is an offense requiring expiation. Regarding an intoxicant, if one is doubtful and drinks it, there is an offense requiring expiation. Regarding an intoxicant, if one perceives it as not an intoxicant and drinks it, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Amajje majjasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Amajje vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Amajje amajjasaññī, anāpatti.

Regarding a non-intoxicant, if one perceives it as an intoxicant, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Regarding a non-intoxicant, if one is doubtful, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Regarding a non-intoxicant, if one perceives it as a non-intoxicant, there is no offense.

329. Anāpatti amajjañca hoti majjavaṇṇaṃ majjagandhaṃ majjarasaṃ taṃ pivati, sūpasampāke, maṃsasampāke, telasampāke, āmalakaphāṇite, amajjaṃ ariṭṭhaṃ pivati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

329. There is no offense if it is a non-intoxicant that has the color, smell, or taste of an intoxicant and one drinks it; in the case of intoxicants added to soup preparations, meat preparations, oil preparations, or myrobalan molasses; if one drinks a non-intoxicant medicinal tincture; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Surāpānasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The first training rule on drinking intoxicants is concluded.

2. Aṅgulipatodakasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Training Rule on Poking with a Finger

330. Tena [T 2.0386][M 0.0147] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sattarasavaggiyaṃ bhikkhuṃ aṅgulipatodakena hāsesuṃ. So bhikkhu uttanto anassāsako kālamakāsi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ aṅgulipatodakena [P 4.0111] hāsessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ aṅgulipatodakena hāsethāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, bhikkhuṃ aṅgulipatodakena hāsessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

330. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus made a bhikkhu of the group-of-seventeen laugh by poking him with a finger. That bhikkhu, having gone into convulsions and being unable to breathe, passed away. Those bhikkhus who were of few desires… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the group-of-six bhikkhus make a bhikkhu laugh by poking him with a finger?”… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that you made a bhikkhu laugh by poking him with a finger?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, foolish men, could you make a bhikkhu laugh by poking him with a finger! This, foolish men, is not for inspiring faith in the unfaithful… And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule in this way:

331. “Aṅgulipatodake pācittiya”nti.

331. “In poking with a finger, there is an offense requiring expiation.”

332. Aṅgulipatodako nāma aṅgulipatodako nāma aṅguliyāpi tudanti (syā.) upasampanno upasampannaṃ hasādhippāyo hassādhippāyo (sī. syā.) kāyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne upasampannasaññī aṅgulipatodakena hāseti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne vematiko aṅgulipatodakena hāseti, āpatti pācittiyassa[V 0.0151]. Upasampanne anupasampannasaññī aṅgulipatodakena [T 2.0387] hāseti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

332. ‘Poking with a finger’ means: should a fully ordained person, with the intention of making another fully ordained person laugh, touch body with body, there is an offense requiring expiation. Regarding a fully ordained person, if, perceiving him as fully ordained, one makes him laugh by poking with a finger, there is an offense requiring expiation. Regarding a fully ordained person, if, being doubtful, one makes him laugh by poking with a finger, there is an offense requiring expiation. Regarding a fully ordained person, if, perceiving him as not fully ordained, one makes him laugh by poking with a finger, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Kāyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissaggiyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissaggiyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissaggiyena nissaggiyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one touches something connected to the body with one's body, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one touches the body with something connected to the body, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one touches something connected to the body with something connected to the body, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one touches the body with something to be relinquished, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one touches something connected to the body with something to be relinquished, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one touches something to be relinquished with something to be relinquished, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

333. Anupasampannaṃ kāyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissaggiyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa[M 0.0148]. Nissaggiyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissaggiyena nissaggiyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne upasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne anupasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

333. If one touches a person not fully ordained, body to body, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one touches something connected to the body with one's body, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one touches the body with something connected to the body, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one touches something connected to the body with something connected to the body, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one touches the body with something to be relinquished, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one touches something connected to the body with something to be relinquished, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one touches something to be relinquished with something to be relinquished, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Regarding a person not fully ordained, if, perceiving him as fully ordained, one makes him laugh, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Regarding a person not fully ordained, if, being doubtful, one makes him laugh, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Regarding a person not fully ordained, if, perceiving him as not fully ordained, one makes him laugh, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

334. Anāpatti na hasādhippāyo, sati karaṇīye āmasati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

334. There is no offense if one does not have the intention to make another laugh; if one touches when there is a task to be done; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Aṅgulipatodakasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The second training rule on poking with a finger is concluded.

3. Hasadhammasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Training Rule on Playful Conduct

335. Tena [T 2.0388] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū aciravatiyā nadiyā [P 4.0112] udake kīḷanti. Tena kho pana samayena rājā pasenadi kosalo mallikāya deviyā saddhiṃ uparipāsādavaragato hoti. Addasā kho rājā pasenadi kosalo sattarasavaggiye bhikkhū aciravatiyā nadiyā udake kīḷante. Disvāna mallikaṃ deviṃ etadavoca – “ete te, mallike, arahanto udake kīḷantī”ti. “Nissaṃsayaṃ kho, mahārāja, bhagavatā sikkhāpadaṃ apaññattaṃ. Te vā bhikkhū appakataññuno”ti. Atha kho rañño pasenadissa kosalassa etadahosi – “kena nu kho ahaṃ upāyena bhagavato ca na āroceyyaṃ, bhagavā ca jāneyya ime [V 0.0152] bhikkhū udake kīḷitā”ti? Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo sattarasavaggiye bhikkhū pakkosāpetvā mahantaṃ guḷapiṇḍaṃ adāsi – “imaṃ, bhante, guḷapiṇḍaṃ bhagavato dethā”ti. Sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū taṃ guḷapiṇḍaṃ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “imaṃ, bhante, guḷapiṇḍaṃ rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavato detī”ti. “Kahaṃ pana tumhe, bhikkhave, rājā addasā”ti. “Aciravatiyā nadiyā, bhagavā, udake kīḷante”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, udake kīḷissatha! Netaṃ[T 2.0389], moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

335. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. Now at that time, the monks from the group of seventeen were playing in the water of the river Aciravatī. At that time, King Pasenadi of Kosala was on the excellent upper story of his palace with Queen Mallikā. King Pasenadi of Kosala saw the monks from the group of seventeen playing in the water of the river Aciravatī. Having seen them, he said this to Queen Mallikā: “Mallikā, these arahants of yours are playing in the water.” “Surely, great king, a training rule has not been laid down by the Blessed One, or those monks are uninstructed.” Then this thought occurred to King Pasenadi of Kosala: “By what means might I not inform the Blessed One, and yet the Blessed One might come to know that these monks played in the water?” Then King Pasenadi of Kosala had the monks from the group of seventeen summoned and gave them a large lump of jaggery, saying: “Venerables, give this lump of jaggery to the Blessed One.” The monks from the group of seventeen took that lump of jaggery and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, King Pasenadi of Kosala gives this lump of jaggery to the Blessed One.” “But where, monks, did the king see you?” “In the water of the river Aciravatī, Blessed One, while we were playing.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, foolish men, can you play in the water? This, foolish men, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:—

336. “Udake [M 0.0149] hasadhamme hassadhamme (sī. syā.) pācittiya”nti.

336. ‐‐For playful sport in water, there is an offense of pācittiya.‐‐

337. Udake hasadhammo nāma uparigopphake udake hasādhippāyo nimujjati vā ummujjati vā palavati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

337. Playful sport in water means: when, in water deeper than the ankles, with the intention of playing, one dives, emerges, or swims, there is an offense of pācittiya.

338. Udake hasadhamme hasadhammasaññī, āpatti pācittiyassa. Udake hasadhamme vematiko, āpatti pācittiyassa. Udake hasadhamme ahasadhammasaññī, āpatti pācittiyassa.

338. In the case of playful sport in water, if one perceives it as playful sport, there is an offense of pācittiya. In the case of playful sport in water, if one is doubtful, there is an offense of pācittiya. In the case of playful sport in water, if one perceives it as not playful sport, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Heṭṭhāgopphake udake kīḷati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Udake nāvāya kīḷati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Hatthena vā pādena vā kaṭṭhena vā kaṭhalāya vā udakaṃ paharati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Bhājanagataṃ udakaṃ vā kañjikaṃ vā khīraṃ vā takkaṃ vā rajanaṃ vā passāvaṃ vā cikkhallaṃ vā kīḷati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one plays in water shallower than the ankles, there is an offense of wrong conduct. If one plays with a boat in water, there is an offense of wrong conduct. If one strikes the water with one's hand, or with a foot, or with a piece of wood, or with a potsherd, there is an offense of wrong conduct. If one plays with water, sour gruel, milk, buttermilk, dye, urine, or mud that is in a vessel, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

Udake ahasadhamme hasadhammasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Udake ahasadhamme vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Udake ahasadhamme ahasadhammasaññī, anāpatti.

In what is not playful sport in water, if one perceives it as playful sport, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In what is not playful sport in water, if one is doubtful, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In what is not playful sport in water, if one perceives it as not playful sport, there is no offense.

339. Anāpatti na hasādhippāyo, sati karaṇīye udakaṃ otaritvā nimujjati [P 4.0113] vā ummujjati vā palavati vā, pāraṃ gacchanto nimujjati [T 2.0390] vā ummujjati vā palavati vā, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

339. There is no offense if there is no intention to play; if, there being a task to be done, one enters the water and dives, emerges, or swims; if, while going to the other shore, one dives, emerges, or swims; in times of calamity; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Hasadhammasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The training rule on playful sport, the third, is finished.

4. Anādariyasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The training rule on disrespect.

340. Tena [T 2.0391][V 0.0153] samayena buddho bhagavā kosambiyaṃ viharati ghositārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā channo anācāraṃ ācarati. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “māvuso channa, evarūpaṃ akāsi. Netaṃ kappatī”ti. So anādariyaṃ paṭicca karotiyeva. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā channo anādariyaṃ karissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, channa, anādariyaṃ karosīti[M 0.0150]? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, anādariyaṃ karissasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

340. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Kosambī in the Ghositārāma. Now at that time, the Venerable Channa was practicing improper conduct. The monks said to him, ‐‐Venerable Channa, do not do such a thing. This is not allowable.‐‐ But he, out of disrespect, continued to do so. Those monks who were of few wishes… they complained, disparaged, and spread it about, saying, ‐‐How indeed could the Venerable Channa show disrespect?‐‐… ‐‐Is it true, Channa, as is said, that you show disrespect?‐‐ ‐‐It is true, Blessed One.‐‐ The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… ‐‐Worthless man, how indeed could you show disrespect? Worthless man, this is not for the confidence of those who are not yet confident… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:‐‐

341. “Anādariye pācittiya”nti.

341. ‐‐In the case of disrespect, there is an offense of pācittiya.‐‐

342. Anādariyaṃ nāma dve anādariyāni – puggalānādariyañca dhammānādariyañca.

342. Disrespect is of two kinds: disrespect for persons and disrespect for the Dhamma.

Puggalānādariyaṃ nāma upasampannena paññattena vuccamāno – “ayaṃ ukkhittako vā vambhito vā garahito vā, imassa vacanaṃ akataṃ bhavissatī”ti anādariyaṃ karoti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

Disrespect for a person means when, being spoken to by a fully ordained monk regarding a training rule that has been laid down, one shows disrespect, thinking, ‐‐This monk is one who has been suspended, or scorned, or censured. The word of this monk will not be followed.‐‐ He incurs an offense of pācittiya.

Dhammānādariyaṃ nāma upasampannena paññattena vuccamāno “kathāyaṃ nasseyya vā vinasseyya vā antaradhāyeyya vā”, taṃ vā na sikkhitukāmo anādariyaṃ karoti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

Disrespect for the Dhamma means when, being spoken to by a fully ordained monk regarding a training rule that has been laid down, one shows disrespect, thinking, ‐‐How might this Dhamma be lost, or perish, or disappear?‐‐ or not wishing to train in that training rule. He incurs an offense of pācittiya.

343. Upasampanne [T 2.0392] upasampannasaññī anādariyaṃ karoti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne vematiko anādariyaṃ karoti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne anupasampannasaññī anādariyaṃ karoti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

343. If one shows disrespect towards a fully ordained monk while perceiving him as fully ordained, one incurs an offense of pācittiya. If one shows disrespect towards a fully ordained monk while being in doubt, one incurs an offense of pācittiya. If one shows disrespect towards a fully ordained monk while perceiving him as not fully ordained, one incurs an offense of pācittiya.

Apaññattena vuccamāno – “idaṃ na sallekhāya na dhutatthāya na pāsādikatāya na apacayāya na vīriyārambhāya saṃvattatī”ti anādariyaṃ karoti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannena paññattena vā apaññattena vā vuccamāno – “idaṃ na sallekhāya na dhutatthāya na [V 0.0154] pāsādikatāya na apacayāya na vīriyārambhāya saṃvattatī”ti anādariyaṃ karoti, āpatti [P 4.0114] dukkaṭassa.

When being admonished regarding what has not been laid down, if one shows disrespect, thinking, “This does not conduce to effacement, to shaking off defilements, to inspiring confidence, to diminishing defilements, or to the arousal of energy,” one incurs an offense of wrong conduct. When being admonished by one not fully ordained regarding what has been laid down or what has not been laid down, if one shows disrespect, thinking, “This does not conduce to effacement, to shaking off defilements, to inspiring confidence, to diminishing defilements, or to the arousal of energy,” one incurs an offense of wrong conduct.

Anupasampanne upasampannasaññī āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne anupasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one shows disrespect towards one not fully ordained while perceiving him as fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong conduct. If one shows disrespect towards one not fully ordained while being in doubt, there is an offense of wrong conduct. If one shows disrespect towards one not fully ordained while perceiving him as not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

344. Anāpatti – “evaṃ amhākaṃ ācariyānaṃ uggaho paripucchā”ti bhaṇati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

344. There is no offense for one who says, “Thus is the learning and inquiry of our teachers”; for one who is insane; and for the first offender.

Anādariyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.

The fourth training rule on disrespect is finished.

5. Bhiṃsāpanasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Training Rule on Frightening

345. Tena [T 2.0393][M 0.0151] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sattarasavaggiye bhikkhū bhiṃsāpenti. Te bhiṃsāpīyamānā rodanti. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “kissa tumhe, āvuso, rodathā”ti? “Ime, āvuso, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū amhe bhiṃsāpentī”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ bhiṃsāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ bhiṃsāpethāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, bhikkhuṃ bhiṃsāpessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

345. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. At that time, the monks of the group-of-six were frightening the monks of the group-of-seventeen. Being frightened, they wept. The monks said to them: “Why, friends, do you weep?” “Friends, these monks of the group-of-six are frightening us.” Those monks who were of few wishes…pe… they complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed could the monks of the group-of-six frighten a monk?”…pe… “Is it true, as has been heard, monks, that you frighten a monk?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them…pe… “How indeed could you, foolish men, frighten a monk! This, foolish men, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced…pe… And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

346. “Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ bhiṃsāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

346. “Whatever monk should frighten a monk, it is a pācittiya offense.”

347. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

347. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind…pe… ‘Monk’ means…pe… in this context, this is the monk who is intended.

Bhikkhunti aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ.

‘A monk’ means another monk.

Bhiṃsāpeyyāti [V 0.0155] upasampanno upasampannaṃ bhiṃsāpetukāmo rūpaṃ vā saddaṃ vā gandhaṃ vā rasaṃ vā phoṭṭhabbaṃ vā upasaṃharati. Bhāyeyya vā so na vā bhāyeyya, āpatti pācittiyassa. Corakantāraṃ vā vāḷakantāraṃ vā pisācakantāraṃ vā ācikkhati. Bhāyeyya vā so [T 2.0394] na vā bhāyeyya, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should frighten’ means: a fully ordained person, wishing to frighten a fully ordained person, brings near a form, a sound, a smell, a taste, or a tangible object. Whether that monk is frightened or not, there is a pācittiya offense. Or he tells of a wilderness with thieves, a wilderness with wild beasts, or a wilderness with ghosts. Whether that monk is frightened or not, there is a pācittiya offense.

348. Upasampanne upasampannasaññī bhiṃsāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne vematiko bhiṃsāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. ‘Upasampanne anupasampannasaññī bhiṃsāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

348. Regarding one who is fully ordained, if one perceives him as fully ordained and frightens him, there is a pācittiya offense. Regarding one who is fully ordained, if one is doubtful and frightens him, there is a pācittiya offense. Regarding one who is fully ordained, if one perceives him as not fully ordained and frightens him, there is a pācittiya offense.

Anupasampannaṃ bhiṃsāpetukāmo rūpaṃ vā saddaṃ vā gandhaṃ vā rasaṃ vā phoṭṭhabbaṃ vā upasaṃharati. Bhāyeyya vā so na vā bhāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Corakantāraṃ vā vāḷakantāraṃ vā pisācakantāraṃ vā ācikkhati. Bhāyeyya vā so na vā bhāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa[M 0.0152]. Anupasampanne upasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne [P 4.0115] vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne anupasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Wishing to frighten one who is not fully ordained, one brings near a form, a sound, a smell, a taste, or a tangible object. Whether that person is frightened or not, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Or one tells of a wilderness with thieves, a wilderness with wild beasts, or a wilderness with ghosts. Whether that person is frightened or not, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding one who is not fully ordained, if one perceives him as fully ordained and frightens him, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding one who is not fully ordained, if one is doubtful and frightens him, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding one who is not fully ordained, if one perceives him as not fully ordained and frightens him, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

349. Anāpatti na bhiṃsāpetukāmo rūpaṃ vā saddaṃ vā gandhaṃ vā rasaṃ vā phoṭṭhabbaṃ vā upasaṃharati, corakantāraṃ vā vāḷakantāraṃ vā pisācakantāraṃ vā ācikkhati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

349. There is no offense for one who, not wishing to frighten, brings near a form, a sound, a smell, a taste, or a tangible object, or tells of a wilderness with thieves, a wilderness with wild beasts, or a wilderness with ghosts; nor for one who is insane, nor for the first offender.

Bhiṃsāpanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Training Rule on Frightening, the fifth, is concluded.

6. Jotikasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Training Rule on Fire

350. Tena [T 2.0395] samayena buddho bhagavā bhaggesu viharati suṃsumāragire suṃsumāragire (sī. syā.) saṃsumāragire (ka.) bhesakaḷāvane migadāye. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū hemantike kāle aññataraṃ mahantaṃ susirakaṭṭhaṃ jotiṃ samādahitvā visibbesuṃ. Tasmiñca susire kaṇhasappo agginā santatto nikkhamitvā bhikkhū paripātesi. Bhikkhū tahaṃ tahaṃ upadhāviṃsu. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhū jotiṃ samādahitvā visibbessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhū jotiṃ samādahitvā visibbentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave[V 0.0156], moghapurisā jotiṃ samādahitvā visibbessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

350. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling among the Bhaggas at Suṃsumāragira, in the Bhesakaḷā Forest, a sanctuary for deer. Now at that time, during the winter season, the monks kindled a fire in a large hollow log and were warming themselves. In that hollow log, a black snake, being heated by the fire, came out and chased the monks. The monks ran here and there. Those monks who were of few wants…pe… they criticized, scorned, and spoke disparagingly, saying: “How indeed can monks kindle a fire and warm themselves?” …pe… “Is it true, monks, that monks kindle a fire and warm themselves?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them…pe… “How indeed, monks, can those worthless men kindle a fire and warm themselves! This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced…pe… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Yo pana bhikkhu visibbanāpekkho jotiṃ samādaheyya vā samādahāpeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever monk, desiring to warm himself, should kindle a fire or cause one to be kindled, it is a pācittiya offense.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

In this way, this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the monks.

351. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū gilānā honti. Gilānapucchakā bhikkhū gilāne bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “kaccāvuso, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīya”nti? “Pubbe mayaṃ, āvuso, jotiṃ samādahitvā visibbema; tena [T 2.0396] no phāsu hoti. Idāni pana “bhagavatā paṭikkhitta”nti kukkuccāyantā [M 0.0153] na visibbema, tena no na phāsu hotī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānena bhikkhunā jotiṃ samādahitvā vā samādahāpetvā vā visibbetuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

351. Now at that time, some monks were sick. Monks inquiring after the sick approached the sick monks and said this: “Venerable sirs, are you enduring? Are you managing?” “Formerly, venerable sirs, we would kindle a fire and warm ourselves; by that, we were comfortable. But now, being hesitant that ‘it has been forbidden by the Blessed One,’ we do not warm ourselves; because of that, we are not comfortable.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One…pe… “I allow, monks, a sick monk to kindle a fire or cause one to be kindled to warm himself. And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Yo pana bhikkhu agilāno visibbanāpekkho jotiṃ samādaheyya [P 4.0116] vā samādahāpeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever monk, not being ill, desiring to warm himself, should kindle a fire or cause one to be kindled, it is a pācittiya offense.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

In this way, this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the monks.

352. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū padīpepi jotikepi jantāgharepi kukkuccāyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tathārūpappaccayā jotiṃ samādahituṃ samādahāpetuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

352. Now at that time, the bhikkhus were scrupulous about lighting a lamp, about making a fire for a purpose such as baking a bowl, and about a steam-bath house. They reported this matter to the Blessed One... “I allow, bhikkhus, to kindle a fire or cause one to be kindled for a suitable reason. And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

353. “Yo pana bhikkhu agilāno visibbanāpekkho jotiṃ samādaheyya vā samādahāpeyya vā, aññatra tathārūpappaccayā, pācittiya”nti.

353. “Whatever bhikkhu, not being ill, desiring to warm himself, should kindle a fire or cause one to be kindled, except for a suitable reason, it is an offense entailing expiation.”

354. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

354. ‘Whatever’: means of whatever sort... ‘Bhikkhu’: ...in this context, this is the bhikkhu who is intended.

Agilāno [V 0.0157] nāma yassa vinā agginā phāsu hoti.

‘Not ill’ means one who is comfortable without fire.

Gilāno nāma yassa vinā agginā na phāsu hoti.

‘Ill’ means one who is not comfortable without fire.

Visibbanāpekkhoti tappitukāmo.

‘Desiring to warm himself’ means wishing to warm oneself.

Joti nāma aggi vuccati.

‘Joti’ means what is called fire.

Samādaheyyāti sayaṃ samādahati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should kindle’: if he kindles it himself, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Samādahāpeyyāti [T 2.0397] aññaṃ āṇāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Sakiṃ āṇatto bahukampi samādahati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should cause one to be kindled’: if he orders another, there is an offense entailing expiation. If, having been ordered once, that person kindles many times, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Aññatra tathā rūpappaccayāti ṭhapetvā tathārūpappaccayaṃ.

‘Except for a suitable reason’ means setting aside a suitable reason.

355. Agilāno agilānasaññī visibbanāpekkho jotiṃ samādahati vā samādahāpeti vā, aññatra tathārūpappaccayā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Agilāno vematiko visibbanāpekkho jotiṃ samādahati [M 0.0154] vā samādahāpeti vā, aññatra tathārūpappaccayā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Agilāno gilānasaññī visibbanāpekkho jotiṃ samādahati vā samādahāpeti vā, aññatra tathārūpappaccayā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

355. If one who is not ill, perceiving himself as not ill, desiring to warm himself, kindles a fire or causes one to be kindled—except for a suitable reason—there is an offense entailing expiation. If one who is not ill, being doubtful, desiring to warm himself, kindles a fire or causes one to be kindled—except for a suitable reason—there is an offense entailing expiation. If one who is not ill, perceiving himself as ill, desiring to warm himself, kindles a fire or causes one to be kindled—except for a suitable reason—there is an offense entailing expiation.

Paṭilātaṃ ukkhipati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Gilāno agilānasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Gilāno vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Gilāno gilānasaññī, anāpatti.

If he lifts up a firebrand, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one who is ill, perceiving himself as not ill, kindles a fire or causes one to be kindled, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one who is ill is doubtful and kindles a fire or causes one to be kindled, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one who is ill, perceiving himself as ill, kindles a fire or causes one to be kindled, there is no offense.

356. Anāpatti gilānassa, aññena kataṃ visibbeti, vītaccitaṅgāraṃ visibbeti, padīpe jotike jantāghare tathārūpappaccayā, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

356. There is no offense: for one who is ill; if one warms himself with a fire made by another; if one warms himself with a flameless ember; in the case of a lamp; in the case of making a fire for a purpose; in a steam-bath house; for a suitable reason; in times of calamity; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Jotikasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The sixth training rule, on fire, is concluded.

7. Nahānasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Training Rule on Bathing

357. Tena [T 2.0398][V 0.0158] samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū tapode nahāyanti. Tena kho pana samayena atha kho (sī. syā.) rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro “sīsaṃ nahāyissāmī”ti tapodaṃ [P 4.0117] gantvā – “yāvāyyā nahāyantī”ti ekamantaṃ paṭimānesi. Bhikkhū yāva samandhakārā nahāyiṃsu. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro vikāle sīsaṃ nahāyitvā, nagaradvāre thakite bahinagare vasitvā, kālasseva asambhinnena vilepanena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ seniyaṃ bimbisāraṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “kissa tvaṃ, mahārāja, kālasseva āgato asambhinnena vilepanenā”ti? Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Atha kho bhagavā rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ seniyaṃ bimbisāraṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito uṭṭhāyāsanā [M 0.0155] bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhū rājānampi passitvā na mattaṃ [T 2.0399] jānitvā nahāyantī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā rājānampi passitvā na mattaṃ jānitvā nahāyissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

357. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Ground. Now at that time, monks were bathing in the Tapodā river. And at that time, King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, thinking, “I will bathe my head,” went to the Tapodā river and waited in a suitable place, thinking, “I will wait as long as the venerables are bathing.” The monks bathed until it was dark. Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, having bathed his head at the wrong time, and with the city gate closed, stayed outside the city. In the early morning, with his fragrant paste undiminished, he approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down in a suitable place. The Blessed One said to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha as he was sitting in a suitable place, “Why, great king, have you come so early in the morning with your fragrant paste undiminished?” Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha informed the Blessed One of this matter. Then the Blessed One instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha with a Dhamma talk. Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, having been instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him to the right, and departed. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having had the Sangha of monks assembled, questioned the monks, “Is it true, monks, that monks, even when seeing the king, do not know the proper measure and continue to bathe?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How, monks, can these foolish men, even when seeing the king, not know the proper measure and continue to bathe? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Yo pana bhikkhu orenaddhamāsaṃ nahāyeyya, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever bhikkhu should bathe within a half-month, it is an offense entailing expiation.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.

358. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū uṇhasamaye pariḷāhasamaye kukkuccāyantā na nahāyanti, sedagatena gattena sayanti. Cīvarampi senāsanampi dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uṇhasamaye pariḷāhasamaye orenaddhamāsaṃ nahāyituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

358. Now at that time, during the hot season, a time of oppressive heat, monks were scrupulous and did not bathe. They slept with sweat-covered bodies. Their robes and lodgings became soiled. They informed the Blessed One of this matter… “I allow, monks, to bathe within a half-month during the hot season, a time of oppressive heat. And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Yo [V 0.0159] pana bhikkhu orenaddhamāsaṃ nahāyeyya, aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Diyaḍḍho māso seso gimhānanti gimhānaṃ (itipi) vassānassa paṭhamo māso iccete aḍḍhateyyamāsā uṇhasamayo pariḷāhasamayo – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

“Whatever bhikkhu should bathe within a half-month, except at the proper time, it is an offense entailing expiation. Therein, this is the time: when a month and a half of the hot months remain and the first month of the rainy season—these two and a half months are the hot season, the time of oppressive heat. This is the proper time therein.”

Evañcidaṃ [P 4.0118] bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.

359. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū gilānā honti. Gilānapucchakā bhikkhū gilāne bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “kaccāvuso, khamanīyaṃ, kacci [T 2.0400] yāpanīya”nti? “Pubbe mayaṃ, āvuso, orenaddhamāsaṃ nahāyāma, tena no phāsu hoti; idāni pana “bhagavatā paṭikkhitta”nti kukkuccāyantā na nahāyāma, tena no na phāsu hotī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānena bhikkhunā orenaddhamāsaṃ nahāyituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

359. Now at that time, some monks were sick. Monks who inquired after the sick said to the sick monks: “Friends, are you enduring, are you getting by?” “Previously, friends, we would bathe within a half-month, and because of that, we were comfortable. But now, being scrupulous, thinking, ‘It has been forbidden by the Blessed One,’ we do not bathe, and because of that, we are not comfortable.” They informed the Blessed One of this matter… “I allow, monks, a sick monk to bathe within a half-month. And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Yo pana bhikkhu orenaddhamāsaṃ nahāyeyya, aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Diyaḍḍho māso seso gimhānanti gimhānaṃ (itipi) vassānassa [M 0.0156] paṭhamo māso iccete aḍḍhateyyamāsā uṇhasamayo, pariḷāhasamayo, gilānasamayo – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

“Whatever monk should bathe within a half-month, except at the proper time, it is a pācittiya offense. Therein, this is the proper time: the last month and a half of the hot season and the first month of the rainy season—these two and a half months are the time of heat and the time of oppressive heat—and the time of sickness. This is the proper time therein.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.

360. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū navakammaṃ katvā kukkuccāyantā na nahāyanti. Te sedagatena gattena sayanti. Cīvarampi senāsanampi dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kammasamaye orenaddhamāsaṃ nahāyituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

360. Now at that time, monks, having done new work, were scrupulous and did not bathe. They slept with sweat-covered bodies. Their robes and lodgings became soiled. They informed the Blessed One of this matter… “I allow, monks, to bathe within a half-month at a time of work. And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Yo pana bhikkhu orenaddhamāsaṃ nahāyeyya, aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Diyaḍḍho māso seso gimhānanti vassānassa paṭhamo māso iccete aḍḍhateyyamāsā uṇhasamayo, pariḷāhasamayo, gilānasamayo, kammasamayo – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

“Whatever monk should bathe within a half-month, except at the proper time, it is a pācittiya offense. Therein, this is the proper time: the last month and a half of the hot season and the first month of the rainy season—these two and a half months are the time of heat and the time of oppressive heat—and the time of sickness, and the time of work. This is the proper time therein.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.

361. Tena [T 2.0401][V 0.0160] kho pana samayena bhikkhū addhānaṃ gantvā kukkuccāyantā na nahāyanti. Te sedagatena gattena sayanti. Cīvarampi senāsanampi dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, addhānagamanasamaye orenaddhamāsaṃ nahāyituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

361. Now at that time, monks, having gone on a long journey, were scrupulous and did not bathe. They slept with sweat-covered bodies. Their robes and lodgings became soiled. They informed the Blessed One of this matter… “I allow, monks, to bathe within a half-month at a time of travelling on a long journey. And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Yo pana bhikkhu orenaddhamāsaṃ nahāyeyya, aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Diyaḍḍho māso seso gimhānanti vassānassa paṭhamo māso iccete aḍḍhateyyamāsā uṇhasamayo, pariḷāhasamayo, gilānasamayo, kammasamayo, addhānagamanasamayo – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

“Whatever monk should bathe within a half-month, except at the proper time, it is a pācittiya offense. Therein, this is the proper time: the last month and a half of the hot season and the first month of the rainy season—these two and a half months are the time of heat and the time of oppressive heat—and the time of sickness, the time of work, and the time of travelling on a long journey. This is the proper time therein.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.

362. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū ajjhokāse cīvarakammaṃ karontā sarajena vātena okiṇṇā honti. Devo ca thokaṃ thokaṃ phusāyati. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā na nahāyanti, kilinnena [M 0.0157] gattena sayanti. Cīvarampi senāsanampi [P 4.0119] dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vātavuṭṭhisamaye orenaddhamāsaṃ nahāyituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

362. Now at that time, many monks were doing robe-work in the open air and were covered with dust by a dusty wind. And it was drizzling a little. The monks, being scrupulous, did not bathe and slept with their bodies soiled. Their robes and lodgings also became soiled. They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “I allow, monks, at a time of wind and rain, to bathe within a half-month. And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

363. “Yo pana bhikkhu orenaddhamāsaṃ nahāyeyya, aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ samayo. Diyaḍḍho māso seso gimhānanti vassānassa paṭhamo māso iccete aḍḍhateyyamāsā uṇhasamayo, pariḷāhasamayo, gilānasamayo, kammasamayo, addhānagamanasamayo, vātavuṭṭhisamayo [T 2.0402] – ayaṃ tattha samayo”ti.

363. “Whatever monk should bathe within a half-month, except at the proper time, it is a pācittiya offense. Therein, this is the proper time: the last month and a half of the hot season and the first month of the rainy season—these two and a half months are the time of heat and the time of oppressive heat—and the time of sickness, the time of work, the time of travelling on a long journey, and the time of wind and rain. This is the proper time therein.”

364. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.
