364. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever is of whatever kind… ‘Monk’ means… the monk who is intended in this context.

Orenaddhamāsanti ūnakaddhamāsaṃ.

‘Within a half-month’ means less than a half-month.

Nahāyeyyāti cuṇṇena vā mattikāya vā nahāyati, payoge payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Nahānapariyosāne, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should bathe’ means: if one bathes with bath powder or with clay, for every effort, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred. At the conclusion of the bathing, a pācittiya offense is incurred.

Aññatra [V 0.0161] samayāti ṭhapetvā samayaṃ.

‘Except at the proper time’ means setting aside the proper time.

Uṇhasamayo nāma diyaḍḍho māso seso gimhānaṃ. Pariḷāhasamayo nāma vassānassa paṭhamo māso “iccete aḍḍhateyyamāsā uṇhasamayo pariḷāhasamayo”ti nahāyitabbaṃ.

‘The time of heat’ means the last month and a half of the hot season. ‘The time of oppressive heat’ means the first month of the rainy season. Thinking, “These two and a half months are the time of heat and the time of oppressive heat,” one should bathe.

Gilānasamayo nāma yassa vinā nahānena na phāsu hoti. Gilānasamayoti nahāyitabbaṃ.

‘The time of sickness’ means when one is not comfortable without bathing. Thinking, ‘It is the time of sickness,’ one should bathe.

Kammasamayo nāma antamaso pariveṇampi sammaṭṭhaṃ hoti. “Kammasamayo”ti nahāyitabbaṃ.

‘The time of work’ means when at least the monastery grounds have been swept. Thinking, ‘It is the time of work,’ one should bathe.

Addhānagamanasamayo nāma “addhayojanaṃ gacchissāmī”ti nahāyitabbaṃ, gacchantena nahāyitabbaṃ, gatena nahāyitabbaṃ.

‘The time of travelling on a long journey’ means: thinking, “I will go half a yojana,” one should bathe. One who is travelling should bathe; one who has travelled should bathe.

Vātavuṭṭhisamayo nāma bhikkhū sarajena vātena okiṇṇā honti, dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni kāye patitāni honti. “Vātavuṭṭhisamayo”ti nahāyitabbaṃ.

‘The time of wind and rain’ means when monks are covered with dust by a dusty wind, or when two or three drops of water have fallen on their bodies. Thinking, ‘It is the time of wind and rain,’ one should bathe.

365. Ūnakaddhamāse ūnakasaññī, aññatra samayā, nahāyati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ūnakaddhamāse vematiko, aññatra samayā, nahāyati, āpatti [M 0.0158] pācittiyassa. Ūnakaddhamāse atirekasaññī, aññatra samayā, nahāyati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

365. If he bathes when it is less than a half-month, except at the proper time, perceiving it as less, a pācittiya offense is incurred. If he bathes when it is less than a half-month, except at the proper time, being in doubt, a pācittiya offense is incurred. If he bathes when it is less than a half-month, except at the proper time, perceiving it as more, a pācittiya offense is incurred.

Atirekaddhamāse ūnakasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Atirekaddhamāse vematiko[T 2.0403], āpatti dukkaṭassa. Atirekaddhamāse atirekasaññī, anāpatti.

If he bathes when it is more than a half-month, perceiving it as less, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred. If he bathes when it is more than a half-month, being in doubt, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred. If he bathes when it is more than a half-month, perceiving it as more, there is no offense.

366. Anāpatti samaye, addhamāsaṃ nahāyati, atirekaddhamāsaṃ nahāyati, pāraṃ gacchanto nahāyati, sabbapaccantimesu janapadesu, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

366. There is no offense: at the proper time; if one bathes every half-month; if one bathes when it is more than a half-month; if one bathes while crossing to the other shore; in all border regions; in times of danger; for one who is insane; for the originator of the rule.

Nahānasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.

The seventh training rule on bathing is finished.

8. Dubbaṇṇakaraṇasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Training Rule on Making a Discolouring Mark

367. Tena [T 2.0404][P 4.0120][V 0.0162] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū ca paribbājakā ca sāketā sāvatthiṃ addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti. Antarāmagge corā nikkhamitvā te acchindiṃsu. Sāvatthiyā rājabhaṭā nikkhamitvā te core sabhaṇḍe gahetvā bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pāhesuṃ – “āgacchantu, bhadantā, sakaṃ sakaṃ cīvaraṃ sañjānitvā gaṇhantū”ti. Bhikkhū na sañjānanti. Te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhadantā attano attano cīvaraṃ na sañjānissantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhūnaṃ tadanucchavikaṃ tadanulomikaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññapessāmi dasa atthavase paṭicca – saṅghasuṭṭhutāya, saṅghaphāsutāya…pe… saddhammaṭṭhitiyā, vinayānuggahāya. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

367. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, many monks and wanderers were traveling the long road from Sāketa to Sāvatthī. On the way, thieves came out and robbed them. The king's men from Sāvatthī went out, captured those thieves together with the goods, and sent a messenger to the monks, saying: 'Venerable sirs, let them come, and having recognized their own robes, let them take them.' The monks did not recognize them. Those people complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: 'How is it that the venerable sirs will not recognize their own robes?' The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on account of this cause, in this instance, had the Sangha of monks assembled, and having given a Dhamma talk suitable and appropriate to the occasion, addressed the monks: 'In that case, monks, I will lay down a training rule for the monks, based on ten reasons: for the excellence of the Sangha, for the comfort of the Sangha... for the stability of the true Dhamma, and for the support of the discipline. And so, monks, you should recite this training rule in this way:

368. “Navaṃ pana bhikkhunā cīvaralābhena tiṇṇaṃ dubbaṇṇakaraṇānaṃ aññataraṃ dubbaṇṇakaraṇaṃ ādātabbaṃ – nīlaṃ vā kaddamaṃ vā kāḷasāmaṃ vā. Anādā [M 0.0159] ce bhikkhu tiṇṇaṃ dubbaṇṇakaraṇānaṃ aññataraṃ dubbaṇṇakaraṇaṃ [T 2.0405] navaṃ cīvaraṃ paribhuñjeyya, pācittiya”nti.

368. “When a monk has obtained a new robe, one of the three means of making a discolouring mark should be applied: blue, mud, or dark brown. If a monk should use a new robe without applying one of the three means of making a discolouring mark, it is an offense of expiation.”

369. Navaṃ nāma akatakappaṃ vuccati.

369. ‘New’ refers to that which has not had the ‘kappa’ mark applied.

Cīvaraṃ nāma channaṃ cīvarānaṃ aññataraṃ cīvaraṃ.

‘Robe’ means any one of the six kinds of robes.

Tiṇṇaṃ dubbaṇṇakaraṇānaṃ aññataraṃ dubbaṇṇakaraṇaṃ ādātabbanti antamaso kusaggenapi ādātabbaṃ.

‘One of the three means of making a discolouring mark should be applied’ means it should be applied at least with the tip of a blade of kusa grass.

Nīlaṃ nāma dve nīlāni – kaṃsanīlaṃ, palāsanīlaṃ.

‘Blue’ means two kinds of blue: bronze-blue and leaf-blue.

Kaddamo nāma odako vuccati.

‘Mud’ refers to watery mud.

Kāḷasāmaṃ [V 0.0163] nāma yaṃkiñci kāḷasāmakaṃ kāḷakaṃ (sī. syā.).

‘Dark brown’ means any kind of dark brown color.

Anādā ce bhikkhu tiṇṇaṃ dubbaṇṇakaraṇānaṃ aññataraṃ dubbaṇṇakaraṇanti antamaso kusaggenapi anādiyitvā tiṇṇaṃ [P 4.0121] dubbaṇṇakaraṇānaṃ aññataraṃ dubbaṇṇakaraṇaṃ navaṃ cīvaraṃ paribhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘If a monk, without applying one of the three means of making a discolouring mark...’ means: if, without having applied one of the three means of making a discolouring mark—not even at least with the tip of a blade of kusa grass—he uses a new robe, it is an offense of expiation.

370. Anādinne anādinnasaññī paribhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anādinne vematiko paribhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anādinne ādinnasaññī paribhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

370. In the case of an unmarked robe, if he uses it perceiving it as unmarked, it is an offense of expiation. In the case of an unmarked robe, if he uses it while in doubt, it is an offense of expiation. In the case of an unmarked robe, if he uses it perceiving it as marked, it is an offense of expiation.

Ādinne anādinnasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ādinne vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ādinne ādinnasaññī, anāpatti.

In the case of a marked robe, if he perceives it as unmarked, it is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of a marked robe, if he is in doubt, it is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of a marked robe, if he perceives it as marked, there is no offense.

371. Anāpattiādiyitvā paribhuñjati, kappo naṭṭho hoti, kappakatokāso jiṇṇo hoti, kappakatena akappakataṃ saṃsibbitaṃ hoti, aggaḷe anuvāte paribhaṇḍe, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

371. There is no offense: if he uses it after applying the mark; if the mark is lost; if the place where the mark was made is worn out; if a marked robe is sewn together with an unmarked one; if the mark is on an upper layer, a lengthwise border, or a widthwise border; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Dubbaṇṇakaraṇasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The eighth training rule on making a discolouring mark is finished.

9. Vikappanasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Training Rule on Assignment

372. Tena [T 2.0406] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā upanando [M 0.0160] sakyaputto bhātuno saddhivihārikassa bhikkhuno sāmaṃ cīvaraṃ vikappetvā appaccuddhāraṇaṃ apaccuddhārakaṃ (sī. syā.) paribhuñjati. Atha kho so bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi – “ayaṃ, āvuso, āyasmā upanando sakyaputto mayhaṃ cīvaraṃ sāmaṃ vikappetvā appaccuddhāraṇaṃ paribhuñjatī”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā upanando sakyaputto bhikkhussa sāmaṃ cīvaraṃ vikappetvā appaccuddhāraṇaṃ paribhuñjissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, upananda, bhikkhussa sāmaṃ cīvaraṃ vikappetvā appaccuddhāraṇaṃ paribhuñjasīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, bhikkhussa sāmaṃ cīvaraṃ [V 0.0164] vikappetvā appaccuddhāraṇaṃ paribhuñjissasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

372. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time the venerable Upananda the Sakyan, having himself assigned a robe to a monk who was his brother’s co-resident, used it without it having been restored. Then that monk informed the other monks of this matter: “Friends, this venerable Upananda the Sakyan, having himself assigned my robe, uses it without it having been restored.” Those monks who were of few wishes… they criticized, censured, and spread it about: “How indeed could the venerable Upananda the Sakyan, having himself assigned a monk's robe, use it without it having been restored?” … “Is it true, Upananda, as is said, that you, having yourself assigned a monk's robe, use it without it having been restored?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “Worthless man, how indeed could you, having yourself assigned a monk's robe, use it without it having been restored? This, worthless man, does not lead to the faith of the faithless… And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

373. “Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā sikkhamānāya vā sāmaṇerassa vā sāmaṇeriyā vā sāmaṃ cīvaraṃ vikappetvā appaccuddhāraṇaṃ apaccuddhārakaṃ (sī. syā.) paribhuñjeyya, pācittiya”nti.

373. “Whatever monk, having himself assigned a robe to a monk, a nun, a probationary nun, a male novice, or a female novice, should use it without it having been restored, it is an offense of expiation.”

374. Yo panāti [T 2.0407] yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

374. Whatever means: whoever, of whatever kind... A monk means: ... In this context, this is the monk who is intended.

Bhikkhussāti [P 4.0122] aññassa bhikkhussa.

To a monk means: to another monk.

Bhikkhunī nāma ubhatosaṅghe upasampannā.

A nun is one who has been fully ordained in both Sanghas.

Sikkhamānā nāma dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā.

A probationary nun is one who has trained for two years in the six rules.

Sāmaṇero nāma dasasikkhāpadiko.

A male novice is one who holds the ten training rules.

Sāmaṇerī nāma dasasikkhāpadikā.

A female novice is one who holds the ten training rules.

Sāmanti sayaṃ vikappetvā.

Himself means: having oneself assigned.

Cīvaraṃ nāma channaṃ cīvarānaṃ aññataraṃ cīvaraṃ vikappanupagaṃ pacchimaṃ.

A robe means: any one of the six kinds of robes, at minimum, suitable for assignment.

Vikappanā nāma dve vikappanā – sammukhāvikappanā ca parammukhāvikappanā ca.

Assignment means two kinds of assignment: assignment in one’s presence and assignment in one’s absence.

Sammukhāvikappanā nāma “imaṃ cīvaraṃ tuyhaṃ vikappemi itthannāmassa vā”ti.

Assignment in one’s presence means: “I assign this robe to you, or to so-and-so.”

Parammukhāvikappanā [M 0.0161] nāma “imaṃ cīvaraṃ vikappanatthāya tuyhaṃ dammī”ti. Tena vattabbo – “ko te mitto vā sandiṭṭho vā”ti? “Itthannāmo ca itthannāmo cā”ti. Tena vattabbo – “ahaṃ tesaṃ dammi, tesaṃ santakaṃ paribhuñja vā vissajjehi vā yathāpaccayaṃ vā karohī”ti.

Assignment in one’s absence means: “I give you this robe for the purpose of assignment.” He should then be asked: “Who is your friend or acquaintance?” “So-and-so and so-and-so.” He should then be told: “I give it to them; use what belongs to them, or give it away, or do with it as is suitable.”

Appaccuddhāraṇaṃ [V 0.0165] nāma tassa vā adinnaṃ, tassa vā avissasanto paribhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Without it having been restored’ means: it has not been given by that person, or one uses it without being on trusting terms with him; there is an offense of expiation.

375. Appaccuddhāraṇe appaccuddhāraṇasaññī paribhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Appaccuddhāraṇe vematiko paribhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Appaccuddhāraṇe appaccuddhāraṇasaññī paribhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

375. When it has not been restored, if he uses it perceiving it as not restored, there is an offense of expiation. When it has not been restored, if he is in doubt and uses it, there is an offense of expiation. When it has not been restored, if he uses it perceiving it as having been restored, there is an offense of expiation.

Adhiṭṭheti vā vissajjeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Paccuddhāraṇe appaccuddhāraṇasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa[T 2.0408]. Paccuddhāraṇe vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Paccuddhāraṇe paccuddhāraṇasaññī, anāpatti.

If he determines it or relinquishes it, there is an offense of wrong-doing. When it has been restored, if he perceives it as not restored, there is an offense of wrong-doing. When it has been restored, if he is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing. When it has been restored, if he perceives it as restored, there is no offense.

376. Anāpatti so vā deti, tassa vā vissasanto paribhuñjati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

376. There is no offense if that person gives it, or if one uses it while on trusting terms with him; for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Vikappanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.

The ninth training rule on Assignment is finished.

10. Cīvaraapanidhānasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Training Rule on Hiding a Robe

377. Tena [T 2.0409] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū asannihitaparikkhārā honti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sattarasavaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pattampi cīvarampi apanidhenti. Sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū chabbaggiye bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “dethāvuso, amhākaṃ [P 4.0123] pattampi cīvarampī”ti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū hasanti, te rodanti. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “kissa tumhe, āvuso, rodathā”ti? “Ime, āvuso, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū amhākaṃ pattampi cīvarampi apanidhentī”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhūnaṃ pattampi [M 0.0162] cīvarampi apanidhessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pattampi cīvarampi apanidhethāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, bhikkhūnaṃ pattampi cīvarampi apanidhessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

377. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time the monks of the group of seventeen had their requisites not put away. The monks of the group of six hid the bowls and robes of the monks of the group of seventeen. The monks of the group of seventeen said this to the monks of the group of six: “Friends, give us our bowls and robes.” The monks of the group of six laughed, and they cried. The monks asked them, “Friends, why do you cry?” “Friends, these monks of the group of six are hiding our bowls and robes.” Those monks who were of few desires … complained, criticized, and spread it about, “How indeed could the monks of the group of six hide the bowls and robes of monks?” … “Is it true, as has been heard, monks, that you hide the bowls and robes of monks?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … “How indeed could you, foolish men, hide the bowls and robes of monks? This does not, foolish men, lead to inspiring confidence in the uninspired … And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

378. “Yo [V 0.0166] pana bhikkhu bhikkhussa pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā nisīdanaṃ vā sūcigharaṃ vā kāyabandhanaṃ vā apanidheyya vā apanidhāpeyya vā, antamaso hasāpekkhopi, pācittiya”nti.

378. “Whatever monk should hide or cause to be hidden a monk’s bowl, or robe, or sitting-cloth, or needle-case, or belt, even if only for the sake of a joke, it is an offense of expiation.”

379. Yo [T 2.0410] panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

379. ‘Whatever monk’ means: whoever, of whatever kind... ‘Monk’ means: ... in this sense, this is the monk who is intended.

Bhikkhussāti aññassa bhikkhussa.

‘Of a monk’ means: of another monk.

Patto nāma dve pattā – ayopatto, mattikāpatto.

A bowl, by name: there are two kinds of bowls—an iron bowl and a clay bowl.

Cīvaraṃ nāma channaṃ cīvarānaṃ aññataraṃ cīvaraṃ, vikappanupagaṃ pacchimaṃ.

A robe, by name, is any one of the six robes, at minimum large enough to be subject to assignment.

Nisīdanaṃ nāma sadasaṃ vuccati.

A sitting-cloth, by name, is said to be one with a border.

Sūcigharaṃ nāma sasūcikaṃ vā asūcikaṃ vā.

A needle-case, by name, is one with a needle or without a needle.

Kāyabandhanaṃ nāma dve kāyabandhanāni – paṭṭikā, sūkarantakaṃ.

A belt, by name: there are two kinds of belts—a cloth band and a plaited belt.

Apanidheyya vāti sayaṃ apanidheti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should hide’ means: if he himself hides it, there is an offense of expiation.

Apanidhāpeyya vāti aññaṃ āṇāpesi, āpatti pācittiyassa. Apanidhāpeyya vā ti ayyaṃ āṇāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Sakiṃ āṇatto bahukampi apanidheti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should cause to be hidden’ means: if he orders another, there is an offense of expiation. If, having been ordered once, that person hides it many times, there is an offense of expiation.

Antamaso hasāpekkhopīti kīḷādhippāyo.

‘Even if only for the sake of a joke’ means: having the intention to play.

380. Upasampanne upasampannasaññī pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā nisīdanaṃ vā sūcigharaṃ vā kāyabandhanaṃ vā apanidheti vā apanidhāpeti vā, antamaso hasāpekkhopi, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne vematiko…pe… upasampanne anupasampannasaññī pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā nisīdanaṃ vā sūcigharaṃ vā kāyabandhanaṃ vā apanidheti vā apanidhāpeti vā, antamaso hasāpekkhopi, āpatti pācittiyassa.

380. In the case of a fully ordained monk, if one perceives him as fully ordained and hides or causes to be hidden his bowl, or robe, or sitting-cloth, or needle-case, or belt, even if only for the sake of a joke, there is an offense of expiation. In the case of a fully ordained monk, if one is uncertain... In the case of a fully ordained monk, if one perceives him as not fully ordained and hides or causes to be hidden his bowl, or robe, or sitting-cloth, or needle-case, or belt, even if only for the sake of a joke, there is an offense of expiation.

Aññaṃ [M 0.0163][V 0.0167] parikkhāraṃ apanidheti vā apanidhāpeti vā, antamaso hasāpekkhopi, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannassa pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ [T 2.0411] vā aññaṃ vā parikkhāraṃ apanidheti vā apanidhāpeti vā, antamaso hasāpekkhopi, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne upasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa[P 4.0124]. Anupasampanne vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne anupasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one hides or causes to be hidden another requisite, even if only for the sake of a joke, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one hides or causes to be hidden the bowl, or robe, or other requisite of one who is not fully ordained, even if only for the sake of a joke, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of one who is not fully ordained, if one perceives him as fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of one who is not fully ordained, if one is uncertain, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of one who is not fully ordained, if one perceives him as not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

381. Anāpatti nahasādhippāyo, dunnikkhittaṃ paṭisāmeti, “dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā dassāmī”ti paṭisāmeti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

381. There is no offense: if there is no intention to joke; if one puts away what was badly placed; if one puts it away thinking, “Having given a Dhamma talk, I will give it back;” for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Cīvaraapanidhānasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

The tenth training rule, on hiding a robe, is finished.

Surāpānavaggo chaṭṭho.

The Sixth Chapter, on Drinking Liquor, is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of it:

Surā aṅguli hāso ca toyañca (itipi), anādariyañca bhiṃsanaṃ;

Jotinahānadubbaṇṇaṃ, sāmaṃ apanidhena cāti.

Liquor, tickling, playing in jest, disrespect, frightening, kindling a fire, bathing, discoloring, assigning, and hiding.

7. Sappāṇakavaggo

7. The Chapter on Living Beings

1. Sañciccasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The Training Rule on Intention

382. Tena [T 2.0412] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā udāyī issāso hoti, kākā cassa amanāpā honti. So kāke vijjhitvā vijjhitvā sīsaṃ chinditvā sūle paṭipāṭiyā ṭhapesi. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “kenime, āvuso, kākā jīvitā voropitā”ti? “Mayā, āvuso. Amanāpā me kākā”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā udāyī sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, udāyi, sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropesīti? “Saccaṃ[V 0.0168], bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropessasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

382. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the Venerable Udāyī was an archer, and crows were disagreeable to him. Having shot the crows again and again, and having cut off their heads, he placed them in a row on stakes. The monks said thus: “Friends, by whom were these crows deprived of life?” “By me, friends. Crows are disagreeable to me.” Those monks who were of few desires… criticized, scorned, and spread the word, saying: “How indeed could the Venerable Udāyī intentionally deprive a living being of life?” … “Is it true, they say, Udāyī, that you intentionally deprived a living being of life?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “Worthless man, how indeed could you intentionally deprive a living being of life! This, worthless man, does not lead to the confidence of the unconfident… And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:”

383. “Yo [M 0.0164] pana bhikkhu sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropeyya, pācittiya”nti.

383. “Whatever monk should intentionally deprive a living being of life, it is a pācittiya offense.”

384. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

384. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘Monk’ means… in this sense, this is the monk who is intended.

Sañciccāti jānanto sañjānanto cecca abhivitaritvā vītikkamo.

‘Intentionally’ means a transgression committed while knowing, clearly knowing, having decided, and having deliberated.

Pāṇo nāma tiracchānagatapāṇo vuccati.

‘Living being’ refers to an animal.

Jīvitā voropeyyāti jīvitindriyaṃ upacchindati uparodheti [T 2.0413] santatiṃ vikopeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should deprive of life’ means: he cuts off the life faculty, he causes it to cease, he destroys the continuity; it is the incurring of a pācittiya offense.

385. Pāṇe [P 4.0125] pāṇasaññī jīvitā voropeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Pāṇe vematiko jīvitā voropeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Pāṇe appāṇasaññī jīvitā voropeti, anāpatti. Appāṇe pāṇasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Appāṇe vemitako, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Appāṇe appāṇasaññī, anāpatti.

385. Regarding a living being, if one perceives it as a living being and deprives it of life, it is the incurring of a pācittiya offense. Regarding a living being, if one is in doubt and deprives it of life, it is the incurring of a dukkaṭa offense. Regarding a living being, if one perceives it as not a living being and deprives it of life, there is no offense. Regarding a non-living being, if one perceives it as a living being, it is the incurring of a dukkaṭa offense. Regarding a non-living being, if one is in doubt, it is the incurring of a dukkaṭa offense. Regarding a non-living being, if one perceives it as not a living being, there is no offense.

386. Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, namaraṇādhippāyassa, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

386. There is no offense: if it is unintentional; through inattention; for one who does not know; for one with no intention to cause death; for one who is insane; and for the first offender.

Sañciccasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The first training rule on intention is finished.

2. Sappāṇakasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Training Rule on Water with Living Beings

387. Tena [T 2.0414] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū jānaṃ sappāṇakaṃ udakaṃ paribhuñjanti. Ye [V 0.0169] te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū jānaṃ sappāṇakaṃ udakaṃ paribhuñjissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, jānaṃ sappāṇakaṃ udakaṃ paribhuñjathāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, jānaṃ sappāṇakaṃ udakaṃ paribhuñjissatha! Netaṃ[M 0.0165], moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

387. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the monks of the group-of-six knowingly consumed water containing living beings. Those monks who were of few desires… complained, murmured, and criticized them: “How indeed could the monks of the group-of-six knowingly consume water containing living beings?” … “Is it true, as is heard, monks, that you knowingly consume water containing living beings?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed could you, worthless men, knowingly consume water containing living beings! This, worthless men, does not lead to the faith of the unfaithful… And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

388. “Yo pana bhikkhu jānaṃ sappāṇakaṃ udakaṃ paribhuñjeyya, pācittiya”nti.

388. “Whatever monk should knowingly consume water containing living beings, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

389. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

389. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘Monk’ means… in this context, this is the monk who is intended.

Jānāti nāma sāmaṃ vā jānāti, aññe vā tassa ārocenti. “Sappāṇaka”nti jānanto, “paribhogena marissantī”ti jānanto paribhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Knows’ means: he knows by himself, or others inform him. Knowing it ‘contains living beings,’ and knowing, ‘they will die by being consumed,’ if he consumes it, it is an offense of pācittiya.

390. Sappāṇake sappāṇakasaññī paribhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Sappāṇake vematiko paribhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa[T 2.0415]. Sappāṇake appāṇakasaññī paribhuñjati, anāpatti. Appāṇake sappāṇakasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Appāṇake vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Appāṇake appāṇakasaññī, anāpatti.

390. Regarding that which contains living beings, if he is percipient that it contains living beings and consumes it, it is an offense of pācittiya. Regarding that which contains living beings, if he is doubtful and consumes it, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. Regarding that which contains living beings, if he is percipient that it does not contain living beings and consumes it, there is no offense. Regarding that which does not contain living beings, if he is percipient that it contains living beings, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. Regarding that which does not contain living beings, if he is doubtful, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. Regarding that which does not contain living beings, if he is percipient that it does not contain living beings, there is no offense.

391. Anāpatti “sappāṇaka”nti ajānanto, “appāṇaka”nti jānanto, “paribhogena na marissantī”ti jānanto paribhuñjati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

391. There is no offense for one who does not know it ‘contains living beings;’ for one who knows it ‘does not contain living beings;’ for one who, knowing ‘they will not die from the consumption,’ consumes it; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Sappāṇakasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The second training rule, on water with living beings, is finished.

3. Ukkoṭanasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Training Rule on Re-agitation

392. Tena [T 2.0416][P 4.0126] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū jānaṃ yathādhammaṃ nihatādhikaraṇaṃ punakammāya ukkoṭenti – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kammaṃ anihataṃ dunnihataṃ [V 0.0170] puna nihanitabba”nti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū jānaṃ yathādhammaṃ nihatādhikaraṇaṃ punakammāya ukkoṭessantī”ti [M 0.0166] …pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, jānaṃ yathādhammaṃ nihatādhikaraṇaṃ punakammāya ukkoṭethā”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, jānaṃ yathādhammaṃ nihatādhikaraṇaṃ punakammāya ukkoṭessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

392. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the monks of the group-of-six, knowingly, re-agitated for a new formal act a legal issue that had been settled in accordance with the Dhamma, saying, “The formal act was not done, the formal act was badly done, the formal act must be done again; it was not settled, it was badly settled, it must be settled again.” Those monks who were of few desires… complained, murmured, and criticized: “How indeed could the monks of the group-of-six, knowingly, re-agitate for a new formal act a legal issue that had been settled in accordance with the Dhamma?”… “Is it true, as is heard, monks, that you, knowingly, re-agitate for a new formal act a legal issue that had been settled in accordance with the Dhamma?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed could you, worthless men, knowingly, re-agitate for a new formal act a legal issue that had been settled in accordance with the Dhamma! This, worthless men, does not lead to the faith of the unfaithful… And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

393. “Yo pana bhikkhu jānaṃ yathādhammaṃ nihatādhikaraṇaṃ punakammāya ukkoṭeyya, pācittiya”nti.

393. “Whatever monk, knowingly, should re-agitate for a new formal act a legal issue that has been settled in accordance with the Dhamma, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

394. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

394. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘Monk’ means… in this context, this is the monk who is intended.

Jānāti nāma sāmaṃ vā jānāti, aññe vā tassa ārocenti, so vā āroceti.

‘Knows’ means: he knows by himself, or others inform him, or he informs.

Yathādhammaṃ nāma dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena kataṃ, etaṃ yathādhammaṃ nāma.

‘In accordance with the Dhamma’ means: a formal act done by the Dhamma, by the Vinaya, and by the Teacher’s instruction. This formal act is called ‘in accordance with the Dhamma.’”

Adhikaraṇaṃ [T 2.0417] nāma cattāri adhikaraṇāni – vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, kiccādhikaraṇaṃ.

An issue, so-called, is fourfold: an issue of dispute, an issue of accusation, an issue of offense, and an issue of procedure.

Punakammāya ukkoṭeyyāti “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ punakātabbaṃ kammaṃ anihataṃ dunnihataṃ puna nihanitabbaṃ”ti ukkoṭeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should one agitate for a new formal act’ means: if one agitates, saying, ‘The formal act was not done, the formal act was badly done, the formal act must be done again; it was not settled, it was badly settled, it must be settled again,’ it is an offense of pācittiya.

395. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññī ukkoṭeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme vematiko ukkoṭeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññī ukkoṭeti, anāpatti. Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññī, anāpatti.

395. Regarding a lawful formal act, if one is percipient that it is a lawful formal act and agitates, it is an offense of pācittiya. Regarding a lawful formal act, if one is doubtful and agitates, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. Regarding a lawful formal act, if one is percipient that it is an unlawful formal act and agitates, there is no offense. Regarding an unlawful formal act, if one is percipient that it is a lawful formal act, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. Regarding an unlawful formal act, if one is doubtful, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. Regarding an unlawful formal act, if one is percipient that it is an unlawful formal act, there is no offense.

396. Anāpatti [V 0.0171] “adhammena vā vaggena vā na kammārahassa vā kammaṃ kata”nti jānanto ukkoṭeti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

396. There is no offense if one agitates, knowing, ‘The formal act was done unlawfully, or by a faction, or for one not worthy of the formal act;’ for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Ukkoṭanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The third training rule, on agitation, is finished.

4. Duṭṭhullasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Training Rule on a Grave Offense

397. Tena [T 2.0418][M 0.0167][P 4.0127] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā upanando sakyaputto sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā bhātuno saddhivihārikassa bhikkhuno ārocesi – “ahaṃ, āvuso, sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ āpattiṃ āpanno. Mā kassaci ārocehī”ti. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā saṅghaṃ tassā āpattiyā parivāsaṃ yāci. Tassa saṅgho tassā āpattiyā parivāsaṃ adāsi. So parivasanto taṃ bhikkhuṃ passitvā etadavoca – “ahaṃ, āvuso, sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā saṅghaṃ tassā āpattiyā parivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho tassā āpattiyā parivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivasāmi, vediyāmahaṃ vedayāmahaṃ (syā.), āvuso, vediyatī”ti maṃ āyasmā dhāretū”ti.

397. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the venerable Upananda the Sakyan, having committed an offense of intentional emission of semen, informed a bhikkhu who was his brother's co-resident: 'Friend, I have committed an offense of intentional emission of semen. Do not tell anyone.' Now at that time, another bhikkhu, having committed an offense of intentional emission of semen, requested the Saṅgha for probation for that offense. The Saṅgha granted him probation for that offense. While undergoing probation, he saw that bhikkhu and said this: 'Friend, having committed an offense of intentional emission of semen, I requested the Saṅgha for probation for that offense. The Saṅgha granted me probation for that offense, and so I am undergoing probation. I am making it known, friend. May the venerable one remember me as "one who is making it known".'

“Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, yo aññopi imaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati sopi evaṃ karotī”ti? “Evamāvuso”ti. “Ayaṃ, āvuso, āyasmā upanando sakyaputto sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā āpajji (?) so me āroceti mā kassaci ārocehī”ti. “Kiṃ pana [T 2.0419] tvaṃ, āvuso, paṭicchādesī”ti? “Evamāvuso”ti. Atha kho so bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhu bhikkhussa jānaṃ duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ paṭicchādessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhikkhussa jānaṃ duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ paṭicchādesīti. “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, bhikkhussa jānaṃ duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ paṭicchādessasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

‘Friend, does any other who commits this offense also do so?’ ‘Yes, friend.’ ‘Friend, this venerable Upananda the Sakyan, having committed an offense of intentional emission of semen, told me, “Do not tell anyone.”’ ‘But friend, did you conceal it?’ ‘Yes, friend.’ Then that bhikkhu told the bhikkhus about this matter. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… criticized, scorned, and disparaged, saying, ‘How indeed could a bhikkhu, knowing, conceal a grave offense of a bhikkhu?’ … ‘Is it true, it is said, that you, bhikkhu, knowing, concealed a grave offense of a bhikkhu?’ ‘It is true, Blessed One.’ The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… ‘How indeed could you, worthless man, knowing, conceal a grave offense of a bhikkhu! This, worthless man, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:’

398. “Yo [V 0.0172] pana bhikkhu bhikkhussa jānaṃ duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ paṭicchādeyya, pācittiya”nti.

398. ‘Whatever bhikkhu should knowingly conceal a grave offense of a bhikkhu, it is an offense of pācittiya.’

399. Yo [M 0.0168] panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

399. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhu’ means… this is the bhikkhu who is meant in this context.

Bhikkhussāti aññassa bhikkhussa.

‘Of a bhikkhu’ means: of another bhikkhu.

Jānāti nāma sāmaṃ vā jānāti aññe vā tassa ārocenti, so vā āroceti.

‘Knowing’ means: one knows by oneself, or others inform one, or the offender himself informs one.

Duṭṭhullā [P 4.0128] nāma āpatti cattāri ca pārājikāni terasa ca saṅghādisesā.

‘A grave offense’ means: the four pārājika offenses and the thirteen saṅghādisesa offenses.

Paṭicchādeyyāti “imaṃ jānitvā codessanti, sāressanti khuṃsessanti, vambhessanti, maṅkuṃ karissanti nārocessāmī”ti dhuraṃ nikkhittamatte, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should conceal’ means: upon thinking, ‘Knowing about this one, they will charge him, remind him, reprove him, disparage him, and make him ashamed—I will not tell,’ just on setting aside the responsibility, it is an offense of pācittiya.

400. Duṭṭhullāya āpattiyā duṭṭhullāpattisaññī paṭicchādeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Duṭṭhullāya āpattiyā vematiko paṭicchādeti[T 2.0420], āpatti dukkaṭassa. Duṭṭhullāya āpattiyā aduṭṭhullāpattisaññī paṭicchādeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ paṭicchādeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannassa duṭṭhullaṃ vā aduṭṭhullaṃ vā ajjhācāraṃ paṭicchādeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Aduṭṭhullāya āpattiyā duṭṭhullāpattisaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Aduṭṭhullāya āpattiyā vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Aduṭṭhullāya āpattiyā aduṭṭhullāpattisaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

400. If one conceals a grave offense, perceiving it as a grave offense, it is an offense of pācittiya. If one conceals a grave offense while being doubtful, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. If one conceals a grave offense, perceiving it as a non-grave offense, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. If one conceals a non-grave offense, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. If one conceals a grave or non-grave transgression of an unordained person, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. If one conceals a non-grave offense, perceiving it as a grave offense, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. If one conceals a non-grave offense while being doubtful, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. If one conceals a non-grave offense, perceiving it as a non-grave offense, it is an offense of dukkaṭa.

401. Anāpatti – “saṅghassa bhaṇḍanaṃ vā kalaho vā viggaho vā vivādo vā bhavissatī”ti nāroceti, “saṅghabhedo vā saṅgharāji vā bhavissatī”ti nāroceti, “ayaṃ kakkhaḷo pharuso jīvitantarāyaṃ vā brahmacariyantarāyaṃ vā karissatī”ti nāroceti, aññe patirūpe bhikkhū apassanto nāroceti, nachādetukāmo nāroceti, “paññāyissati sakena kammenā”ti nāroceti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

401. There is no offense: if one does not report it thinking, ‘There will be a quarrel, dispute, conflict, or contention in the Saṅgha’; if one does not report it thinking, ‘There will be a schism in the Saṅgha or a fissure in the Saṅgha’; if one does not report it thinking, ‘This one is harsh and rough; he will create a danger to life or a danger to the holy life’; if one does not report it because one does not see other suitable bhikkhus; if one does not report it without the desire to conceal; if one does not report it thinking, ‘He will become known by his own action’; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Duṭṭhullasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.

The fourth training rule on a grave offense is finished.

5. Ūnavīsativassasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Training Rule Concerning One Under Twenty Years of Age

402. Tena [T 2.0421][M 0.0169][V 0.0173] samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. idaṃ vatthu mahāva. 99 Tena kho pana samayena rājagahe sattarasavaggiyā dārakā sahāyakā honti. Upālidārako tesaṃ pāmokkho hoti. Atha kho upālissa mātāpitūnaṃ etadahosi – “kena nu kho upāyena upāli amhākaṃ accayena sukhañca jīveyya na ca kilameyyā”ti? Atha kho upālissa mātāpitūnaṃ etadahosi – “sace kho upāli lekhaṃ sikkheyya, evaṃ kho upāli amhākaṃ accayena sukhañca jīveyya, na ca kilameyyā”ti. Atha kho upālissa mātāpitūnaṃ etadahosi – “sace kho upāli lekhaṃ sikkhissati, aṅguliyo [P 4.0129] dukkhā bhavissanti. Sace kho upāli gaṇanaṃ sikkheyya, evaṃ kho upāli amhākaṃ accayena sukhañca jīveyya na ca kilameyyā”ti. Atha kho upālissa mātāpitūnaṃ etadahosi – “sace kho upāli gaṇanaṃ sikkhissati, urassa dukkho bhavissati. Sace kho upāli rūpaṃ sikkheyya, evaṃ kho upāli amhākaṃ accayena sukhañca jīveyya na ca kilameyyā”ti. Atha kho upālissa mātāpitūnaṃ etadahosi – “sace kho upāli rūpaṃ sikkhissati, akkhīni dukkhā bhavissanti. Ime kho samaṇā sakyaputtiyā sukhasīlā sukhasamācārā subhojanāni bhuñjitvā nivātesu sayanesu [T 2.0422] sayanti. Sace kho upāli samaṇesu sakyaputtiyesu pabbajeyya, evaṃ kho upāli amhākaṃ accayena sukhañca jīveyya, na ca kilameyyā”ti.

402. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Rājagaha at the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Ground. Now at that time in Rājagaha, there were boys of the group of seventeen who were friends. The boy Upāli was their leader. Then this thought occurred to Upāli’s parents: 'By what means could Upāli, after our passing, live in comfort and not be weary?' Then this thought occurred to Upāli’s parents: 'If Upāli were to learn the art of writing, in this way, after our passing, Upāli could live in comfort and not be weary.' Then this thought occurred to Upāli’s parents: 'If Upāli learns the art of writing, his fingers will become painful. If Upāli were to learn the art of calculation, in this way, after our passing, Upāli could live in comfort and not be weary.' Then this thought occurred to Upāli’s parents: 'If Upāli learns the art of calculation, his chest will become painful. If Upāli were to learn the art of money-changing, in this way, after our passing, Upāli could live in comfort and not be weary.' Then this thought occurred to Upāli’s parents: 'If Upāli learns the art of money-changing, his eyes will become painful. These recluses, sons of the Sakyan, are of comfortable habits and comfortable conduct; having eaten good food, they sleep in sheltered beds. If Upāli were to go forth among the recluses, the sons of the Sakyan, in this way, after our passing, Upāli could live in comfort and not be weary.'

Assosi kho upālidārako mātāpitūnaṃ imaṃ kathāsallāpaṃ. Atha kho upālidārako yena te dārakā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te dārake etadavoca – “etha mayaṃ, ayyā, samaṇesu sakyaputtiyesu pabbajissāmā”ti. “Sace kho tvaṃ, ayya, pabbajissasi, evaṃ mayampi pabbajissāmā”ti. Atha kho te dārakā ekamekassa mātāpitaro upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – “anujānātha maṃ agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā”ti. Atha kho tesaṃ dārakānaṃ mātāpitaro – “sabbepime dārakā samānacchandā kalyāṇādhippāyā”ti anujāniṃsu. Te bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā pabbajjaṃ yāciṃsu. Te bhikkhū pabbājesuṃ upasampādesuṃ. Te rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya rodanti – “yāguṃ detha[M 0.0170], bhattaṃ detha, khādanīyaṃ dethā”ti. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “āgametha, āvuso, yāva ratti vibhāyati. Sace yāgu bhavissati, pivissatha. Sace bhattaṃ bhavissati, bhuñjissatha. Sace khādanīyaṃ bhavissati, khādissatha. No ce bhavissati yāgu vā bhattaṃ vā khādanīyaṃ vā, piṇḍāya caritvā bhuñjissathā”ti. Evampi kho [V 0.0174] te bhikkhū bhikkhūhi vuccamānā rodantiyeva – “yāguṃ detha, bhattaṃ detha, khādanīyaṃ dethā”ti. Senāsanaṃ ūhadantipi ummihantipi.

The boy Upāli heard this conversation of his parents. Then the boy Upāli went to where those boys were; having gone, he said this to those boys: 'Come, sirs, let us go forth among the recluses, the sons of the Sakyan.' 'If you, sir, will go forth, then we too will go forth.' Then those boys, having approached their own parents, said this: 'Permit me to go forth from the household life into homelessness.' Then the parents of those boys, thinking, 'All these boys have the same wish and a good intention,' gave their permission. They approached the bhikkhus and asked for the going forth. The bhikkhus gave them the going forth and the higher ordination. Having risen early at dawn, they would cry, 'Give us gruel! Give us rice! Give us hard food!' The bhikkhus said this: 'Wait, friends, until the night brightens. If there is gruel, you will drink. If there is rice, you will eat. If there is hard food, you will eat. If there is no gruel or rice or hard food, you will eat after going for alms.' Even when spoken to thus by the bhikkhus, they just cried, 'Give us gruel! Give us rice! Give us hard food!' They also defecated and urinated in the lodging.

Assosi [T 2.0423] kho bhagavā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya dārakasaddaṃ. Sutvāna āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “kiṃ nu kho so, ānanda, dārakasaddo”ti? Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ [P 4.0130] kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhū jānaṃ ūnavīsativassaṃ puggalaṃ upasampādentī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā jānaṃ ūnavīsativassaṃ puggalaṃ upasampādessanti! Ūnakavīsativasso, bhikkhave, puggalo akkhamo hoti sītassa uṇhassa jighacchāya pipāsāya ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṃ duruttānaṃ durāgatānaṃ vacanapathānaṃ uppannānaṃ sārīrikānaṃ vedanānaṃ dukkhānaṃ tibbānaṃ kharānaṃ kaṭukānaṃ asātānaṃ amanāpānaṃ pāṇaharānaṃ anadhivāsakajātiko hoti. Vīsativassova kho, bhikkhave, puggalo khamo hoti sītassa uṇhassa…pe… pāṇaharānaṃ adhivāsakajātiko hoti. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

The Blessed One, having risen early at dawn, heard the sound of boys crying. Having heard it, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda: 'Ānanda, what is that sound of boys crying?' Then the Venerable Ānanda informed the Blessed One of this matter. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, for this reason, had the Saṅgha of bhikkhus assembled and questioned the bhikkhus: 'Is it true, bhikkhus, that bhikkhus knowingly give the higher ordination to a person under twenty years of age?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… How indeed, bhikkhus, can those worthless men knowingly give the higher ordination to a person under twenty years of age? A person under twenty years, bhikkhus, is unable to endure cold, heat, hunger, thirst, the touch of gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping things, and badly spoken, badly delivered ways of speech; he is of a nature unable to endure the arisen bodily feelings that are painful, sharp, harsh, bitter, disagreeable, unpleasant, and life-taking. A person of twenty years, bhikkhus, is able to endure cold, heat… he is of a nature able to endure life-taking feelings. This, bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

403. “Yo pana bhikkhu jānaṃ ūnavīsativassaṃ puggalaṃ upasampādeyya, so ca puggalo anupasampanno[T 2.0424], te ca bhikkhū gārayhā, idaṃ tasmiṃ pācittiya”nti.

403. “Whatever bhikkhu should knowingly give the higher ordination to a person under twenty years of age, that person is not ordained, and those bhikkhus are to be censured. This, for him, is a pācittiya offense.”

404. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

404. 'Whatever' means: whoever is of such a kind… and so on… 'Bhikkhu' means… and so on… in this context, this is the bhikkhu who is intended.

Jānāti nāma sāmaṃ vā jānāti, aññe vā tassa ārocenti, so vā āroceti.

'Knowing' means: either he knows by himself, or others inform him, or the person himself informs him.

Ūnavīsativasso [M 0.0171] nāma appattavīsativasso.

'Under twenty years of age' means one who has not reached twenty years of age.

“Upasampādessāmī”ti gaṇaṃ vā ācariyaṃ vā pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati sammanati (ka.), āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne upajjhāyassa āpatti pācittiyassa. Gaṇassa ca ācariyassa ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Thinking, 'I will give the higher ordination,' if he seeks a chapter, a teacher, a bowl, or robes, or if he designates a boundary, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. For the motion, there is a dukkaṭa. For the two proclamations, there are dukkaṭas. At the conclusion of the proclamations, for the preceptor, there is an offense of pācittiya. For the chapter and for the teacher, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

405. Ūnavīsativasse [V 0.0175] ūnavīsativassasaññī upasampādeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ūnavīsativasse vematiko upasampādeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ūnavīsativasse paripuṇṇavīsativassasaññī upasampādeti, anāpatti. Paripuṇṇavīsativasse ūnavīsativassasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Paripuṇṇavīsativasse vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Paripuṇṇavīsativasse paripuṇṇavīsativassasaññī, anāpatti.

405. If one gives the higher ordination to a person under twenty years of age, perceiving him as under twenty years of age, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one gives the higher ordination to a person under twenty years of age, being in doubt, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If one gives the higher ordination to a person under twenty years of age, perceiving him as fully twenty years of age, there is no offense. In the case of a person who is fully twenty years of age, perceiving him as under twenty years of age, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. In the case of a person who is fully twenty years of age, being in doubt, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. In the case of a person who is fully twenty years of age, perceiving him as fully twenty years of age, there is no offense.

406. Anāpatti ūnavīsativassaṃ paripuṇṇavīsativassasaññī upasampādeti, paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ paripuṇṇavīsativassasaññī upasampādeti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

406. There is no offense if one gives the higher ordination to a person under twenty years of age perceiving him as fully twenty years of age; if one gives the higher ordination to a person fully twenty years of age perceiving him as fully twenty years of age; for an insane monk; for the first offender.

Ūnavīsativassasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The fifth training rule, concerning one under twenty years of age, is finished.

6. Theyyasatthasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Training Rule on a Thieving Caravan

407. Tena [T 2.0425][P 4.0131] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro sattho rājagahā paṭiyālokaṃ gantukāmo hoti. Aññataro bhikkhu te manusse etadavoca – “ahampāyasmantehi saddhiṃ gamissāmī”ti. “Mayaṃ kho, bhante, suṅkaṃ pariharissāmā”ti. “Pajānāthāvuso”ti. Assosuṃ kho kammiyā kammikā (sī. syā.) – “sattho kira suṅkaṃ pariharissatī”ti. Te magge pariyuṭṭhiṃsu. Atha kho te kammikā taṃ satthaṃ gahetvā acchinditvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavocuṃ – “kissa tvaṃ, bhante, jānaṃ theyyasatthena saddhiṃ gacchasī”ti? Palibundhetvā muñciṃsu. Atha kho so bhikkhu sāvatthiṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ [M 0.0172] ārocesi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhu jānaṃ theyyasatthena saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, bhikkhu, jānaṃ theyyasatthena saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjasīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, jānaṃ theyyasatthena saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjissasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

407. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, a certain caravan was desirous of going from Rājagaha to the western region. A certain monk said this to those people: “I too will go with you, venerable sirs.” “Venerable sir, we will be evading the toll.” “Friends, you should know.” The king's officials heard: “A caravan, it seems, will be evading the toll.” They lay in wait on the road. Then those officials, having seized and plundered that caravan, said this to that monk: “Venerable sir, why do you, knowing, travel with a thieving caravan?” Having detained him, they released him. Then that monk, having gone to Sāvatthī, related this matter to the monks. Those monks who were of few wishes… they criticized, complained, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could a monk, knowing, having made an arrangement, travel on a long, single journey with a thieving caravan?”… “Is it true, monk, that you, knowing, having made an arrangement, travel on a long, single journey with a thieving caravan?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “Foolish man, how indeed could you, knowing, having made an arrangement, travel on a long, single journey with a thieving caravan? This, foolish man, is not for the confidence of the faithless… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

408. “Yo [V 0.0176] pana bhikkhu jānaṃ theyyasatthena [T 2.0426] saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjeyya, antamaso gāmantarampi, pācittiya”nti.

408. “Whatever monk, knowing, having made an arrangement with a thieving caravan, should travel on a long, single journey, even just to another village, it is a pācittiya.”

409. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

409. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘Monk’ means: … in this context, this is what is meant by ‘monk’.

Jānāti nāma sāmaṃ vā jānāti, aññe vā tassa ārocenti, so vā āroceti.

‘Knows’ means: either one knows by oneself, or others inform one, or a member of the caravan informs one.

Theyyasattho nāma corā katakammā vā honti akatakammā vā, rājānaṃ vā theyyaṃ gacchanti suṅkaṃ vā pariharanti.

‘Thieving caravan’ means: they are thieves, whether they have committed a crime or not, or they go stealing from the king, or they evade the toll.

Saddhinti ekato.

‘With’ means: together.

Saṃvidhāyāti – “gacchāmāvuso, gacchāma bhante; gacchāma bhante, gacchāmāvuso, ajja vā hiyyo vā pare vā gacchāmā”ti saṃvidahati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

‘Having made an arrangement’ means: if one makes an arrangement, saying, “Friends, we will go,” “Venerable sir, we will go,” “Venerable sir, we will go,” “Friends, we will go,” or “Let us go today, or tomorrow, or the day after,” there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Antamaso gāmantarampīti kukkuṭasampāte gāme gāmantare gāmantare āpatti pācittiyassa. Agāmake araññe addhayojane addhayojane āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Even just to another village’ means: in a village within a cock's flight, for every interval between villages, there is an offense of pācittiya. In a forest without villages, for every half-yojana, there is an offense of pācittiya.

410. Theyyasatthe [P 4.0132] theyyasatthasaññī saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjati, antamaso gāmantarampi, āpatti pācittiyassa. Theyyasatthe vematiko saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjati, antamaso gāmantarampi, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Theyyasatthe atheyyasatthasaññī saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjati, antamaso gāmantarampi, anāpatti. Bhikkhu saṃvidahati, manussā na saṃvidahanti, āpatti [M 0.0173] dukkaṭassa. Atheyyasatthe theyyasatthasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Atheyyasatthe vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Atheyyasatthe atheyyasatthasaññī [T 2.0427] anāpatti.

410. In the case of a thieving caravan, if one perceives it as a thieving caravan and, having made an arrangement, travels on a long, single journey, even just to another village, there is an offense of pācittiya. In the case of a thieving caravan, if one is in doubt and, having made an arrangement, travels on a long, single journey, even just to another village, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. In the case of a thieving caravan, if one perceives it as not a thieving caravan and, having made an arrangement, travels on a long, single journey, even just to another village, there is no offense. If the monk makes an arrangement, but the people do not, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. In the case of a non-thieving caravan, if one perceives it as a thieving caravan, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. In the case of a non-thieving caravan, if one is in doubt, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. In the case of a non-thieving caravan, if one perceives it as not a thieving caravan, there is no offense.

411. Anāpatti asaṃvidahitvā gacchati, manussā saṃvidahanti bhikkhu na saṃvidahati, visaṅketena gacchati, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

411. There is no offense if one goes without having made an arrangement; if the people make an arrangement but the monk does not; if one goes having missed the appointed time or place; in times of danger; for an insane monk; for the first offender.

Theyyasatthasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The sixth training rule, on the thieving caravan, is finished.

7. Saṃvidhānasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Training Rule on Making an Arrangement

412. Tena [T 2.0428][V 0.0177] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu kosalesu janapade sāvatthiṃ gacchanto aññatarena gāmadvārena atikkamati. Aññatarā itthī sāmikena saha bhaṇḍitvā gāmato nikkhamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ passitvā etadavoca – “kahaṃ, bhante, ayyo gamissatī”ti? “Sāvatthiṃ kho ahaṃ, bhagini, gamissāmī”ti. “Ahaṃ ayyena saddhiṃ gamissāmī”ti. “Eyyāsi, bhaginī”ti. Atha kho tassā itthiyā sāmiko gāmato nikkhamitvā manusse pucchi – “apāyyo apayyā (sī. syā.) evarūpiṃ itthiṃ passeyyāthā”ti? “Esāyyo, pabbajitena saha gacchatī”ti. Atha kho so puriso anubandhitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ gahetvā ākoṭetvā muñci. Atha kho so bhikkhu aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle padhūpento nisīdi. Atha kho sā itthī taṃ purisaṃ etadavoca – “nāyyo so bhikkhu maṃ nippātesi; apica, ahameva tena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ gacchāmi; akārako so bhikkhu; gaccha, naṃ khamāpehī”ti. Atha kho so puriso taṃ bhikkhuṃ khamāpesi. Atha kho so bhikkhu sāvatthiṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhu mātugāmena saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mātugāmena [T 2.0429] saddhiṃ [P 4.0133] saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjasīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, mātugāmena [M 0.0174] saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjissasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ, uddiseyyātha –

412. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. On that occasion, a certain monk was traveling through the Kosala country on his way to Sāvatthī when he passed through a certain village gate. A certain woman, having quarreled with her husband, left the village and, seeing that monk, said to him: “Venerable sir, where are you going?” “I am going to Sāvatthī, sister.” “I will go with you, venerable sir.” “Come along, sister.” Then that woman’s husband, having left the village, asked some people: “Sirs, have you perhaps seen such a woman?” “Sir, she is going with a renunciant.” That man followed them, seized the monk, beat him, and then released him. The monk then sat down at the foot of a tree, brooding. The woman said to the man: “That monk did not lead me away. Rather, I myself went with that monk. That monk is not the doer. Go and ask for his forgiveness.” The man then asked for the monk's forgiveness. The monk went to Sāvatthī and informed the monks about the matter. Those monks who were of few wishes … criticized, censured, and spread it about: “How could a monk make an arrangement to travel together with a woman on the same long road?” … “Is it true, monk, that you made an arrangement to travel together with a woman on the same long road?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him: “… Foolish man, how could you make an arrangement to travel together with a woman on the same long road! This will not inspire confidence in those without it … And so, monks, you should recite this training rule:

413. “Yo pana bhikkhu mātugāmena saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjeyya, antamaso gāmantarampi, pācittiya”nti.

413. “Whatever monk, having made an arrangement, should travel on the same long road together with a woman, even as far as to another village, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

414. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

414. ‘Whatever’: whoever of whatever sort … ‘monk’: … in this context, this is the monk who is meant.

Mātugāmo nāma manussitthī, na yakkhī na petī na tiracchānagatā viññū paṭibalā subhāsitadubbhāsitaṃ duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ ājānituṃ.

A ‘woman’ means a human female, not a female yakkha, not a female peta, not a female animal; one who is intelligent and capable of knowing what is well-spoken and ill-spoken, what is coarse and not coarse.

Saddhinti [V 0.0178] ekato.

‘Together’ means in one company.

Saṃvidhāyāti – “gacchāma bhagini, gacchāmāyya, gacchāmāyya, gacchāma bhagini, ajja vā hiyyo vā pare vā gacchāmā”ti saṃvidahati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

‘Having made an arrangement’: If one makes an arrangement, saying, “Let’s go, sister; let’s go, venerable sir; let’s go, venerable sir; let’s go, sister; let’s go today or tomorrow or the day after,” there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Antamaso gāmantarampīti kukkuṭasampāte gāme gāmantare gāmantare āpatti pācittiyassa. Agāmake araññe addhayojane addhayojane āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Even as far as to another village’: Where villages are within a cock's flight of each other, there is an offense of pācittiya for each interval between villages. In a wilderness without villages, there is an offense of pācittiya for every half-yojana.

415. Mātugāme mātugāmasaññī saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjati, antamaso gāmantarampi, āpatti pācittiyassa. Mātugāme vematiko saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjati, antamaso gāmantarampi, āpatti pācittiyassa. Mātugāme amātugāmasaññī saṃvidhāya [T 2.0430] ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjati, antamaso gāmantarampi, āpatti pācittiyassa.

415. In the case of a woman, if he perceives her as a woman and, having made an arrangement, travels on the same long road, even as far as another village, there is an offense of pācittiya. In the case of a woman, if he is doubtful and, having made an arrangement, travels on the same long road, even as far as another village, there is an offense of pācittiya. In the case of a woman, if he perceives her as not a woman and, having made an arrangement, travels on the same long road, even as far as another village, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Bhikkhu saṃvidahati mātugāmo na saṃvidahati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yakkhiyā vā petiyā paṇḍakena vā tiracchānagatamanussaviggahitthiyā vā saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjati, antamaso gāmantarampi, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Amātugāme mātugāmasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Amātugāme vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Amātugāme amātugāmasaññī, anāpatti.

If the monk makes an arrangement but the woman does not, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If, having made an arrangement with a female yakkha, or a female peta, or a paṇḍaka, or a female animal in human form, one travels on the same long road, even as far as another village, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of what is not a woman, if one perceives it as a woman, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of what is not a woman, if one is doubtful, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of what is not a woman, if one perceives it as not a woman, there is no offense.

416. Anāpatti [M 0.0175] asaṃvidahitvā gacchati, mātugāmo saṃvidahati bhikkhu na saṃvidahati, visaṅketena gacchati, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

416. There is no offense: if one goes without having made an arrangement; if the woman makes an arrangement but the monk does not; if one goes because the appointment was missed; in times of danger; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Saṃvidhānasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.

The seventh training rule on making an arrangement is finished.

8. Ariṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Training Rule concerning Ariṭṭha

417. idaṃ vatthu cūḷava. 65; ma. ni. 1.234 Tena [T 2.0431] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena ariṭṭhassa nāma bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa [P 4.0134] gandhabādhipubbassa (syā. ka.) evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti – “tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā”ti. Assosuṃ kho sambahulā bhikkhū [V 0.0179] – “ariṭṭhassa kira nāma bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā, te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū yena ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ etadavocuṃ – “saccaṃ kira te, āvuso ariṭṭha, evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā, te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā”ti? “Evaṃbyākho ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi – ‘yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’”ti.

417. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. At that time, a bhikkhu named Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture-killer, had this evil wrong view arise in him: “As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructions are not able to cause an obstruction for one who partakes of them.” A number of bhikkhus heard: “It seems that the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture-killer, has had this evil wrong view arise in him: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructions are not able to cause an obstruction for one who partakes of them.’” Then those bhikkhus approached the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture-killer, and having approached, they said to the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture-killer: “Is it true, friend Ariṭṭha, that this evil wrong view has arisen in you: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructions are not able to cause an obstruction for one who partakes of them’?” “Exactly so, friends, as I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructions are not able to cause an obstruction for one who partakes of them.”

“Mā, āvuso ariṭṭha, evaṃ avaca. Mā bhagavantaṃ abbhācikkhi. Na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṃ abbhācikkhanaṃ (itipi). Na hi bhagavā evaṃ vadeyya[T 2.0432]. Anekapariyāyenāvuso ariṭṭha, antarāyikā dhammā antarāyikā vuttā bhagavatā. Alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāya. Appassādā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo [M 0.0176] ettha bhiyyo. Maṃsapesūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā…pe… tiṇukkūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… aṅgārakāsūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… supinakūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… yācitakūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… rukkhaphalūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… asisūnūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… sattisūlūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… sappasirūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo”ti.

“Do not speak thus, friend Ariṭṭha. Do not misrepresent the Blessed One. For it is not good to misrepresent the Blessed One. The Blessed One would not speak thus. In many ways, friend Ariṭṭha, obstructive things have been declared by the Blessed One to be obstructive. And indeed, for one who partakes of them, they are able to cause an obstruction. Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One as having little satisfaction, much suffering, and much distress; the danger in them is greater. Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One as like a skeleton—much suffering, much distress; the danger in them is greater. Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One as like a piece of flesh… like a grass torch… like a pit of glowing coals… like a dream… like borrowed goods… like fruit on a tree… like a chopping block… like a spear and stake… like a snake’s head—much suffering, much distress; the danger in them is greater.”

Evampi kho ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo tehi bhikkhūhi vuccamāno tatheva taṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ thāmasā parāmāsā abhinivissa voharati – “evaṃbyākho ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, – ‘yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā, te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’”ti. Yato ca kho te bhikkhū nāsakkhiṃsu ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetuṃ, atha kho te bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha [T 2.0433] kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne [P 4.0135] etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira te, ariṭṭha, evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’”ti[V 0.0180]? “Evaṃbyākho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi – ‘yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’”ti.

Even when the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture-killer, was spoken to thus by those bhikkhus, he still obstinately clung to that evil wrong view, holding on to it and insisting: “Exactly so, friends, as I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructions are not able to cause an obstruction for one who partakes of them.” When those bhikkhus were unable to dissuade the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture-killer, from that evil wrong view, then those bhikkhus approached the Blessed One; and having approached, they reported the matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and for this reason, having assembled the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, questioned the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture-killer: “Is it true, Ariṭṭha, that this evil wrong view has arisen in you: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructions are not able to cause an obstruction for one who partakes of them’?” “Indeed so, venerable sir, as I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructions are not able to cause an obstruction for one who partakes of them.”

Kassa nu kho nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, mayā evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāsi? Nanu mayā, moghapurisa, anekapariyāyena antarāyikā dhammā antarāyikā vuttā. Alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāya. Appassādā kāmā vuttā mayā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā…pe… maṃsapesūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… tiṇukkūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… aṅgārakāsūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… supinakūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… yācitakūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… rukkhaphalūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… asisūnūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… sattisūlūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… sappasirūpamā kāmā [M 0.0177] vuttā mayā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Atha ca pana tvaṃ, moghapurisa, attanā duggahitena amhe [T 2.0434] ceva abbhācikkhasi, attānañca khaṇasi, bahuñca apuññaṃ pasavasi. Tañhi te, moghapurisa, bhavissati dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya. Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe…. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

“For whose sake, foolish man, do you understand the Dhamma taught by me in this way? Have I not, foolish man, in many ways declared obstructive things to be obstructive? And for one who partakes of them, they are able to cause an obstruction. I have declared sensual pleasures as having little satisfaction, much suffering, and much distress; the danger in them is greater. I have declared sensual pleasures as like a skeleton… like a piece of flesh… like a grass torch… like a pit of glowing coals… like a dream… like borrowed goods… like fruit on a tree… like a chopping block… like a spear and stake… like a snake’s head—much suffering, much distress; the danger in them is greater. And yet you, foolish man, through your own wrong grasp, both misrepresent us and uproot yourself, and you generate much demerit. That, foolish man, will be for your long-term harm and suffering. This, foolish man, is not for the conviction of the unconvinced… And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:”

418. “Yo pana bhikkhu evaṃ vadeyya – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā, te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’ti so bhikkhu bhikkhūhi evamassa vacanīyo – ‘māyasmā evaṃ avaca, mā bhagavantaṃ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṃ, na hi bhagavā evaṃ vadeyya, anekapariyāyenāvuso, antarāyikā dhammā antarāyikā vuttā bhagavatā, alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāyā’ti. Evañca evañca pana (ka.) so bhikkhu bhikkhūhi vuccamāno tatheva paggaṇheyya, so bhikkhu bhikkhūhi yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsitabbo tassa paṭinissaggāya. Yāvatatiyañce samanubhāsiyamāno taṃ paṭinissajjeyya, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ, no ce paṭinissajjeyya, pācittiya”nti.

418. “Whatever bhikkhu should speak thus: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things which have been declared by the Blessed One to be obstructive are not able to cause obstruction for one who indulges in them,’ that bhikkhu should be told by the bhikkhus thus: ‘Venerable one, do not speak thus. Do not misrepresent the Blessed One, for it is not good to misrepresent the Blessed One. The Blessed One would not speak thus. In many ways, friend, obstructive things have been declared to be obstructive by the Blessed One, and they are indeed able to cause obstruction for one who indulges in them.’ And if that bhikkhu, being admonished thus by the bhikkhus, should persist in that very way, that bhikkhu should be formally admonished by the bhikkhus up to the third time for the relinquishment of that view. If, being formally admonished up to the third time, he should relinquish it, that is good. If he should not relinquish it, it is an offense of Pācittiya.”

419. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

419. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘bhikkhu’… this is the bhikkhu who is intended in this context.

Evaṃ vadeyyāti – “tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā”ti.

‘Should speak thus’ means: “As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things which have been declared by the Blessed One to be obstructive are not able to cause obstruction for one who indulges in them.”

So [V 0.0181] bhikkhūti yo so evaṃvādī bhikkhu.

‘That bhikkhu’ means: that bhikkhu who speaks thus.

Bhikkhūhīti aññehi [T 2.0435] bhikkhūhi. Ye passanti ye suṇanti tehi vattabbo – “māyasmā evaṃ avaca, mā bhagavantaṃ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṃ, na hi bhagavā evaṃ vadeyya, anekapariyāyenāvuso antarāyikā dhammā antarāyikā vuttā bhagavatā. Alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāyā”ti. Dutiyampi vattabbo. Tatiyampi vattabbo. Sace paṭinissajjati[P 4.0136], iccetaṃ kusalaṃ; no ce paṭinissajjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sutvā na vadanti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. So bhikkhu saṅghamajjhampi [M 0.0178] ākaḍḍhitvā vattabbo – “māyasmā evaṃ avaca, mā bhagavantaṃ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṃ, na hi bhagavā evaṃ vadeyya, anekapariyāyenāvuso antarāyikā dhammā antarāyikā vuttā bhagavatā. Alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāyā”ti. Dutiyampi vattabbo. Tatiyampi vattabbo. Sace paṭinissajjati, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce paṭinissajjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. So bhikkhu samanubhāsitabbo. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, samanubhāsitabbo. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

‘By the bhikkhus’ means: by other bhikkhus. By those who see, by those who hear, he should be told: “Venerable one, do not speak thus. Do not misrepresent the Blessed One, for it is not good to misrepresent the Blessed One. The Blessed One would not speak thus. In many ways, friend, obstructive things have been declared to be obstructive by the Blessed One. And they are indeed able to cause obstruction for one who indulges in them.” He should be told a second time. He should be told a third time. If he relinquishes, that is good; if he does not relinquish, it is an offense of wrong-doing. If they, having heard, do not speak, it is an offense of wrong-doing. That bhikkhu should be brought into the midst of the Sangha and told: “Venerable one, do not speak thus. Do not misrepresent the Blessed One, for it is not good to misrepresent the Blessed One. The Blessed One would not speak thus. In many ways, friend, obstructive things have been declared to be obstructive by the Blessed One. And they are indeed able to cause obstruction for one who indulges in them.” He should be told a second time. He should be told a third time. If he relinquishes, that is good.
