If he does not relinquish, it is an offense of wrong-doing. That bhikkhu should be formally admonished. And thus, bhikkhus, should he be formally admonished. The Sangha should be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhu:

420. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmassa bhikkhuno evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā, te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’ti. So taṃ diṭṭhiṃ na paṭinissajjati. Yadi [T 2.0436] saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ samanubhāseyya – tassā diṭṭhiyā paṭinissaggāya. Esā ñatti.

420. “Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. A bhikkhu named so-and-so has had such a wicked wrong view arise: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructive are not able to cause obstruction for one who indulges in them.’ He does not relinquish that view. If it is now the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should formally admonish the bhikkhu named so-and-so for the relinquishment of that view. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmassa bhikkhuno evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā, te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’ti. So taṃ diṭṭhiṃ na paṭinissajjati. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ samanubhāsati tassā diṭṭhiyā paṭinissaggāya. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno samanubhāsanā, tassā diṭṭhiyā paṭinissaggāya, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. A bhikkhu named so-and-so has had such a wicked wrong view arise: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructive are not able to cause obstruction for one who indulges in them.’ He does not relinquish that view. The Sangha formally admonishes the bhikkhu named so-and-so for the relinquishment of that view. Whichever venerable one approves of the formal admonishment of the bhikkhu named so-and-so for the relinquishment of that view, he should remain silent; whomever does not approve, he should speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmassa bhikkhuno evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’ti[V 0.0182]. So taṃ diṭṭhiṃ na paṭinissajjati. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ samanubhāsati tassā diṭṭhiyā paṭinissaggāya. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno samanubhāsanā, tassā diṭṭhiyā paṭinissaggāya, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“A second time I speak on this matter… A third time I speak on this matter: ‘Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. A bhikkhu named so-and-so has had such a wicked wrong view arise: “As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructive are not able to cause obstruction for one who indulges in them.” He does not relinquish that view. The Sangha formally admonishes the bhikkhu named so-and-so for the relinquishment of that view. Whichever venerable one approves of the formal admonishment of the bhikkhu named so-and-so for the relinquishment of that view, he should remain silent; whomever does not approve, he should speak.’”

“Samanubhaṭṭho [M 0.0179] saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu, tassā diṭṭhiyā paṭinissaggāya. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The bhikkhu named so-and-so has been formally admonished by the Sangha for the relinquishment of that view. The Sangha approves; therefore, it is silent. Thus do I hold it.”

Ñattiyā [T 2.0437] dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti pācittiyassa.

An offense of wrong-doing is incurred for the motion. For the two formal announcements, offenses of wrong-doing are incurred. At the conclusion of the formal announcements, an offense of Pācittiya is incurred.

421. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññī na paṭinissajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme vematiko na paṭinissajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa dhammakamme adhammakammasaññī na paṭinissajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

421. In a lawful act, perceiving it as a lawful act, if he does not relinquish, an offense of Pācittiya is incurred. In a lawful act, being doubtful, if he does not relinquish, an offense of Pācittiya is incurred. In a lawful act, perceiving it as an unlawful act, if he does not relinquish, an offense of Pācittiya is incurred.

Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In an unlawful act, perceiving it as a lawful act, an offense of wrong-doing is incurred. In an unlawful act, being doubtful, an offense of wrong-doing is incurred. In an unlawful act, perceiving it as an unlawful act, an offense of wrong-doing is incurred.

422. Anāpatti asamanubhāsantassa, paṭinissajjantassa, ummattakassāti.

422. There is no offense for one who is not formally admonished, for one who relinquishes, or for one who is insane.

Ariṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The eighth training rule, concerning Ariṭṭha, is finished.

9. Ukkhittasambhogasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Training Rule on Associating with One Who Has Been Suspended

423. Tena [T 2.0438][P 4.0137] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū jānaṃ tathāvādinā ariṭṭhena bhikkhunā bhikkhunā gaddhabādhipubbena (?) akaṭānudhammena taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissaṭṭhena saddhiṃ sambhuñjantipi saṃvasantipi sahāpi seyyaṃ kappenti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū jānaṃ tathāvādinā ariṭṭhena bhikkhunā bhikkhunā gaddhabādhipubbena (?) akaṭānudhammena taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissaṭṭhena saddhiṃ sambhuñjissantipi saṃvasissantipi sahāpi seyyaṃ kappessantīti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, jānaṃ tathāvādinā ariṭṭhena bhikkhunā bhikkhunā gaddhabādhipubbena (?) akaṭānudhammena [V 0.0183] taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissaṭṭhena saddhiṃ sambhuñjathāpi saṃvasathāpi sahāpi seyyaṃ kappethāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, jānaṃ tathāvādinā ariṭṭhena bhikkhunā bhikkhunā gaddhabādhipubbane (?) akaṭānudhammena taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissaṭṭhena saddhiṃ sambhuñjissathāpi saṃvasissathāpi sahāpi seyyaṃ kappessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

423. At one time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were communing with, living together with, and sleeping together with the monk Ariṭṭha, knowing that he spoke thus, that the formal act had not been carried out for him, and that he had not relinquished that view. Those monks who were of few desires… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: ‘How indeed can the group-of-six monks, knowing that the monk Ariṭṭha speaks thus, that the formal act has not been carried out for him, and that he has not relinquished that view, commune with, live together with, and sleep together with him?’… ‘Is it true, it is said, monks, that you, knowing that the monk Ariṭṭha speaks thus, that the formal act has not been carried out for him, and that he has not relinquished that view, commune with, live together with, and sleep together with him?’ ‘It is true, Blessed One.’ The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… ‘How indeed can you, foolish men, knowing that the monk Ariṭṭha speaks thus, that the formal act has not been carried out for him, and that he has not relinquished that view, commune with, live together with, and sleep together with him! This, foolish men, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule in this way:

424. “Yo [M 0.0180] pana bhikkhu jānaṃ tathāvādinā bhikkhunā akaṭānudhammena taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissaṭṭhena saddhiṃ sambhuñjeyya vā saṃvaseyya vā saha vā seyyaṃ [T 2.0439] kappeyya, pācittiya”nti.

424. “Whatever monk, knowing, should commune with, live together with, or sleep together with a monk who speaks thus, for whom the formal act has not been carried out, and who has not relinquished that view, it is an offense of expiation.”

425. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

425. Whatever: whoever, of whatever sort… monk:… this is the monk who is meant in this context.

Jānāti nāma sāmaṃ vā jānāti, aññe vā tassa ārocenti, so vā āroceti.

‘Knowing’ means: he knows by himself, or others inform him, or that monk himself informs.

Tathāvādināti – “tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā, te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā”ti evaṃ vādinā.

‘Who speaks thus’ means: with one who speaks in this way, ‘I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One in such a way that those things called obstructive by the Blessed One are not able to be an obstruction for one who engages in them.’

Akaṭānudhammo nāma ukkhitto anosārito.

‘For whom the formal act has not been carried out’ means he has been suspended and not reinstated.

Taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissaṭṭhena saddhinti etaṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissaṭṭhena saddhiṃ.

‘With one who has not relinquished that view’ means with a monk who has not relinquished that view.

Sambhuñjeyya vāti sambhogo nāma dve sambhogā – āmisasambhogo ca dhammasambhogo ca. Āmisasambhogo nāma āmisaṃ deti vā paṭiggaṇhāti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammasambhogo nāma uddisati vā uddisāpeti vā, padena uddisati vā uddisāpeti vā, pade pade āpatti pācittiyassa. Akkharāya uddisati vā uddisāpeti vā, akkharakkharāya āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Or should commune with’: ‘communion’ means there are two kinds of communion: material communion and Dhamma communion. ‘Material communion’ means one gives or receives material things; it is an offense of expiation. ‘Dhamma communion’ means one teaches or has someone teach; if one teaches or has someone teach by the phrase, for every phrase it is an offense of expiation. If one teaches or has someone teach by the syllable, for every syllable it is an offense of expiation.

Saṃvaseyya [P 4.0138] vāti ukkhittakena saddhiṃ uposathaṃ vā pavāraṇaṃ vā saṅghakammaṃ vā karoti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Or should live together’ means one performs the Uposatha, or the Pavāraṇā, or a Sangha act with a suspended monk; it is an offense of expiation.

Saha [V 0.0184] vā seyyaṃ kappeyyāti ekacchanne ukkhittake nipanne bhikkhu nipajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Bhikkhu nipanne ukkhittako nipajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ubho vā nipajjanti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Uṭṭhahitvā punappunaṃ nipajjanti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Or should sleep together’ means: under one roof, when a suspended monk is lying down, a monk lies down; it is an offense of expiation. When a monk is lying down, a suspended monk lies down; it is an offense of expiation. Or if both lie down, it is an offense of expiation. Getting up, they lie down again and again; it is an offense of expiation.

426. Ukkhittake [T 2.0440] ukkhittakasaññī sambhuñjati vā saṃvasati vā saha vā seyyaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ukkhittake vematiko sambhuñjati vā saṃvasati vā saha vā seyyaṃ kappeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ukkhittake anukkhittakasaññī sambhuñjati vā saṃvasati vā saha vā seyyaṃ kappeti, anāpatti[M 0.0181]. Anukkhittake ukkhittakasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anukkhittake vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anukkhittake anukkhittakasaññī, anāpatti.

426. Regarding a suspended monk, if one perceives him as suspended and communes, lives together, or sleeps together with him, it is an offense of expiation. Regarding a suspended monk, if one is doubtful and communes, lives together, or sleeps together with him, it is an offense of wrong-doing. Regarding a suspended monk, if one perceives him as not suspended and communes, lives together, or sleeps together with him, there is no offense. Regarding a non-suspended monk, if one perceives him as suspended, it is an offense of wrong-doing. Regarding a non-suspended monk, if one is doubtful, it is an offense of wrong-doing. Regarding a non-suspended monk, if one perceives him as not suspended, there is no offense.

427. Anāpatti anukkhittoti jānāti, ukkhitto osāritoti jānāti, ukkhitto taṃ diṭṭhiṃ paṭinissaṭṭhoti jānāti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

427. There is no offense if one knows he is not suspended; if one knows a suspended monk has been reinstated; if one knows he has relinquished that view; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Ukkhittasambhogasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.

The ninth training rule on communing with a suspended monk is finished.

10. Kaṇṭakasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Training Rule Concerning Kaṇṭaka

428. Tena [T 2.0441] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena kaṇṭakassa kaṇḍakassa (syā. ka.) nāma samaṇuddesassa evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti – “tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā”ti. Assosuṃ kho sambahulā bhikkhū kaṇṭakassa nāma kira samaṇuddesassa evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – “tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā, te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū yena kaṇṭako samaṇuddeso tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā kaṇṭakaṃ samaṇuddesaṃ etadavocuṃ – “saccaṃ kira te, āvuso kaṇṭaka, evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, yathā ye’me antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’”ti? “Evaṃbyākho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi – ‘yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’”ti.

428. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, an evil wrong view of this sort had arisen in a novice named Kaṇṭaka: “I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One in such a way that those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructions are not able to be an obstruction for one who partakes of them.” Many monks heard: “It is said that an evil wrong view of this sort has arisen in a novice named Kaṇṭaka: ‘I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One in such a way that those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructions are not able to be an obstruction for one who partakes of them.’” Then those monks approached the novice Kaṇṭaka. Having approached him, they said this to the novice Kaṇṭaka: “Friend Kaṇṭaka, is it true, as is said, that an evil wrong view of this sort has arisen in you: ‘I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One in such a way that those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructions are not able to be an obstruction for one who partakes of them’?” “It is just so, venerable sirs. I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One in such a way that those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructions are not able to be an obstruction for one who partakes of them.”

Mā[V 0.0185], āvuso kaṇṭaka, evaṃ avaca. Mā bhagavantaṃ abbhācikkhi. Na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṃ. Na hi bhagavā evaṃ vadeyya. Anekapariyāyena, āvuso kaṇṭaka, antarāyikā [T 2.0442] dhammā antarāyikā vuttā bhagavatā. Alañca [M 0.0182] pana te paṭisevato antarāyāya. Appassādā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo…pe… evampi kho kaṇṭako samaṇuddeso tehi bhikkhūhi vuccamāno tatheva taṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ thāmasā parāmāsā abhinivissa voharati – “evaṃbyākho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi – ‘yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’”ti.

“Friend Kaṇṭaka, do not speak thus. Do not misrepresent the Blessed One. For it is not good to misrepresent the Blessed One. The Blessed One would not speak in such a way. In many ways, friend Kaṇṭaka, obstructive things have been declared by the Blessed One to be obstructive, and they are indeed able to be an obstruction for one who partakes of them. Sensual pleasures have been declared by the Blessed One to be of little gratification, of much suffering, of much tribulation, and the danger in them is greater… Even when spoken to in this way by those bhikkhus, the novice Kaṇṭaka still adhered to that same evil wrong view, holding to it tenaciously and grasping it wrongly, insisting: ‘It is just so, venerable sirs, I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One in such a way that those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructive are not able to be an obstruction for one who partakes of them.’”

Yato ca kho te bhikkhū nāsakkhiṃsu kaṇṭakaṃ samaṇuddesaṃ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetuṃ, atha kho te bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā kaṇṭakaṃ samaṇuddesaṃ paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira te, kaṇṭaka, evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā [T 2.0443] dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’”ti? “Evaṃbyākho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi – ‘yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’”ti.

And when those bhikkhus were unable to dissuade the novice Kaṇṭaka from that evil wrong view, they approached the Blessed One. Having approached him, they reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, had the Saṅgha of bhikkhus assembled and questioned the novice Kaṇṭaka: “Kaṇṭaka, is it true, as is said, that an evil wrong view of this sort has arisen in you: ‘I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One in such a way that those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructive are not able to be an obstruction for one who partakes of them’?” “It is just so, venerable sir. I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One in such a way that those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructive are not able to be an obstruction for one who partakes of them.”

“Kassa nu kho nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, mayā evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāsi? Nanu mayā, moghapurisa, anekapariyāyena antarāyikā dhammā antarāyikā vuttā, alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāya? Appassādā kāmā vuttā mayā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā…pe… sappasirūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Atha ca pana tvaṃ, moghapurisa, attanā duggahitena amhe ceva abbhācikkhasi attānañca khaṇasi bahuñca apuññaṃ pasavasi. Tañhi te, moghapurisa, bhavissati dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya. Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… [T 2.0444] pasannānañca ekaccānaṃ aññathattāyā”ti. Vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho kaṇṭakaṃ samaṇuddesaṃ nāsetu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, nāsetabbo – ajjatagge te, āvuso kaṇṭaka, na [P 4.0139] ceva so bhagavā satthā apadisitabbo. Yampi caññe samaṇuddesā labhanti bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ dirattatirattaṃ sahaseyyaṃ sāpi [M 0.0183] te natthi. Cara pire vinassā”ti. Atha kho saṅgho kaṇṭakaṃ samaṇuddesaṃ nāsesi.

“Worthless man, how is it that you understand the Dhamma to have been taught by me in this way? Have I not, worthless man, in many ways declared obstructive things to be obstructive, and that they are indeed able to be an obstruction for one who partakes of them? Sensual pleasures have been declared by me to be of little gratification, of much suffering, of much tribulation, and the danger in them is greater. Sensual pleasures have been declared by me to be like a chain of bones… like a snake’s head, of much suffering, of much tribulation, and the danger in them is greater. And yet you, worthless man, by your own wrong grasp, both misrepresent us and undermine yourself, and you generate much demerit. That, worthless man, will be for your harm and suffering for a long time. This, worthless man, is not for inspiring confidence in the unconfident... nor for the wavering of some who are confident.” Having rebuked him… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus: “In that case, bhikkhus, let the Saṅgha banish the novice Kaṇṭaka. And he is to be banished in this way: ‘From this day forth, friend Kaṇṭaka, you are not to refer to that Blessed One as your Teacher. And that lodging together with the bhikkhus for two or three nights, which other novices receive, that is not for you. Go, you wretched one! Be gone!’” Then the Saṅgha banished the novice Kaṇṭaka.

Tena [V 0.0186] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū jānaṃ tathānāsitaṃ kaṇṭakaṃ samaṇuddesaṃ upalāpentipi upaṭṭhāpentipi sambhuñjantipi sahāpi seyyaṃ kappenti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū jānaṃ tathānāsitaṃ kaṇṭakaṃ samaṇuddesaṃ upalāpessantipi upaṭṭhāpessantipi sambhuñjissantipi sahāpi seyyaṃ kappessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, jānaṃ tathānāsitaṃ kaṇṭakaṃ samaṇuddesaṃ upalāpethāpi upaṭṭhāpethāpi sambhuñjathāpi sahāpi seyyaṃ kappethāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, jānaṃ tathānāsitaṃ kaṇṭakaṃ samaṇuddesaṃ upalāpessathāpi upaṭṭhāpessathāpi sambhuñjissathāpi sahāpi seyyaṃ kappessatha[T 2.0445]! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

At that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus knowingly enticed, attended upon, shared meals with, and shared a sleeping place with the novice Kaṇṭaka who had been banished in that manner. Those bhikkhus who were of few wants… criticized, complained, and spread it about: “How can the group-of-six bhikkhus knowingly entice, attend upon, share meals with, and share a sleeping place with the novice Kaṇṭaka who has been banished in that manner?”… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that you knowingly entice, attend upon, share meals with, and share a sleeping place with the novice Kaṇṭaka who has been banished in that manner?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Blessed One, the Buddha, rebuked them… “Worthless men, how can you knowingly entice, attend upon, share meals with, and share a sleeping place with the novice Kaṇṭaka who has been banished in that manner? This, worthless men, is not for inspiring confidence in the unconfident…” … “And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule in this way:

429. “Samaṇuddesopi ce evaṃ vadeyya – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’ti, so samaṇuddeso bhikkhūhi evamassa vacanīyo – ‘māvuso samaṇuddesa, evaṃ avaca, mā bhagavantaṃ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṃ, na hi bhagavā evaṃ vadeyya. Anekapariyāyenāvuso samaṇuddesa, antarāyikā dhammā antarāyikā vuttā bhagavatā. Alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāyā’ti. Evañca evañca pana (ka.) so samaṇuddeso bhikkhūhi vuccamāno tatheva paggaṇheyya, so samaṇuddeso bhikkhūhi evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ajjatagge te, āvuso samaṇuddesa, na ceva so bhagavā satthā apadisitabbo. Yampi caññe samaṇuddesā labhanti bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ dirattatirattaṃ sahaseyyaṃ sāpi te natthi. Cara pire vinassā’ti. Yo pana bhikkhu jānaṃ tathānāsitaṃ samaṇuddesaṃ upalāpeyya vā upaṭṭhāpeyya vā sambhuñjeyya vā saha vā seyyaṃ kappeyya, pācittiya”nti.

429. “If a novice should speak thus: ‘I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One in such a way that those things declared by the Blessed One to be obstructive are not able to be an obstruction for one who partakes of them,’ that novice should be addressed by the bhikkhus in this way: ‘Do not speak thus, friend novice. Do not misrepresent the Blessed One, for it is not good to misrepresent the Blessed One. The Blessed One would not speak in such a way. In many ways, friend novice, obstructive things have been declared by the Blessed One to be obstructive, and they are indeed able to be an obstruction for one who partakes of them.’ And if that novice, being addressed by the bhikkhus in this way, should hold to it just as before, that novice should be addressed by the bhikkhus in this way: ‘From this day forth, friend novice, you are not to refer to that Blessed One as the Teacher. And that which other novices receive—sharing a sleeping place with the bhikkhus for two or three nights—that is not for you. Go, wretch! Be gone!’ Should any bhikkhu, knowing a novice has been banished in that manner, entice him, or attend upon him, or eat together with him, or share a sleeping place with him, it is an offense of expiation.”

430. Samaṇuddeso nāma sāmaṇero vuccati.

430. By 'samaṇuddesa' is meant a novice (sāmaṇera).

Evaṃ [M 0.0184] vadeyyāti – “tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā, te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā”ti.

‘Should speak thus’ means: ‘I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One in such a way that those things called obstructive by the Blessed One are not able to be an obstruction for one who partakes of them.’

So [P 4.0140] samaṇuddesoti [T 2.0446] yo so evaṃvādī samaṇuddeso.

‘That novice’ means: that novice who speaks in that way.

Bhikkhūhīti [V 0.0187] aññehi bhikkhūhi, ye passanti ye suṇanti tehi vattabbo – “mā, āvuso samaṇuddesa, evaṃ avaca. Mā bhagavantaṃ abbhācikkhi. Na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṃ. Na hi bhagavā evaṃ vadeyya. Anekapariyāyenāvuso samaṇuddesa, antarāyikā dhammā antarāyikā vuttā bhagavatā. Alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāyā”ti. Dutiyampi vattabbo… tatiyampi vattabbo…pe… sace paṭinissajjati iccetaṃ kusalaṃ, no ce paṭinissajjati so samaṇuddeso bhikkhūhi evamassa vacanīyo – “ajjatagge te, āvuso samaṇuddesa, na ceva so bhagavā satthā apadisitabbo. Yampi caññe samaṇuddesā labhanti bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ dirattatirattaṃ sahaseyyaṃ sāpi te natthi. Cara pire vinassā”ti.

‘By the bhikkhus’ means by other bhikkhus; those who see or those who hear, by them he should be addressed: ‘Do not speak thus, friend novice. Do not misrepresent the Blessed One. It is not good to misrepresent the Blessed One. The Blessed One would not speak in such a way. In many ways, friend novice, obstructive things have been called obstructive by the Blessed One, and they are indeed able to be an obstruction for one who partakes of them.’ He should be addressed a second time… a third time he should be addressed… If he relinquishes it, that is good. If he does not relinquish it, that novice should be addressed by the bhikkhus in this way: ‘From this day forth, friend novice, you are not to refer to that Blessed One as the Teacher. And that which other novices receive—sharing a sleeping place with the bhikkhus for two or three nights—that is not for you. Go, wretch! Perish!’

Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

‘Whoever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘a bhikkhu’… in this context, this is the bhikkhu who is meant.

Jānāti nāma sāmaṃ vā jānāti, aññe vā tassa ārocenti, so vā āroceti.

‘Knowing’ means: he knows by himself, or others inform him, or he (the novice) himself informs him.

Tathānāsitanti evaṃ nāsitaṃ.

‘Banished in that manner’ means banished in this way.

Samaṇuddeso nāma sāmaṇero vuccati.

By 'samaṇuddesa' is meant a novice (sāmaṇera).

Upalāpeyya vāti tassa pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā uddesaṃ vā paripucchaṃ vā dassāmīti upalāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Or should entice’ means: if one entices him by saying, ‘I will give you a bowl, or a robe, or a text for recitation, or an explanation of the meaning,’ he incurs an offense of expiation.

Upaṭṭhāpeyya vāti tassa cuṇṇaṃ vā mattikaṃ vā dantakaṭṭhaṃ vā mukhodakaṃ vā sādiyati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Or should have him attend upon one’ means: if one accepts from him bath powder, or clay, or a tooth-stick, or water for washing the face, he incurs an offense of expiation.

Sambhuñjeyya vāti [T 2.0447] sambhogo nāma dve sambhogā – āmisasambhogo ca dhammasambhogo ca. Āmisasambhogo nāma āmisaṃ deti vā paṭiggaṇhāti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammasambhogo nāma uddisati vā uddisāpeti vā, padena uddisati vā uddisāpeti vā, pade pade āpatti [M 0.0185] pācittiyassa. Akkharāya uddisati vā uddisāpeti vā, akkharakkharāya āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Or should eat together with’ means: Communion is of two kinds: communion in material things and communion in the Dhamma. Communion in material things means one gives or receives material things; he incurs an offense of expiation. Communion in the Dhamma means one teaches or has someone teach; if one teaches or has someone teach by the phrase, for every phrase he incurs an offense of expiation. If one teaches or has someone teach by the syllable, for every syllable he incurs an offense of expiation.

Saha [V 0.0188] vā seyyaṃ kappeyyāti ekacchanne nāsitake samaṇuddese nipanne bhikkhu nipajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Bhikkhu nipanne nāsitako samaṇuddeso nipajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ubho vā nipajjanti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Uṭṭhahitvā punappunaṃ nipajjanti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Or should share a sleeping place’ means: under one roof, when a banished novice is lying down, a bhikkhu lies down, he incurs an offense of expiation. When a bhikkhu is lying down, a banished novice lies down, he incurs an offense of expiation. Or if both lie down together, he incurs an offense of expiation. Having gotten up, if they lie down again and again, he incurs an offense of expiation for each instance.

431. Nāsitake nāsitakasaññī upalāpeti vā upaṭṭhāpeti vā sambhuñjati vā saha vā seyyaṃ kappeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Nāsitake vematiko upalāpeti vā upaṭṭhāpeti vā sambhuñjati vā saha vā seyyaṃ kappeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nāsitake anāsitakasaññī upalāpeti vā upaṭṭhāpeti vā sambhuñjati vā saha vā seyyaṃ kappeti, anāpatti. Anāsitake nāsitakasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anāsitake vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anāsitake anāsitakasaññī, anāpatti.

431. In the case of one who has been banished, if, perceiving him as banished, one entices him, or has him attend upon one, or eats together with him, or lies down together with him, there is an offense of pācittiya. In the case of one who has been banished, if, being in doubt, one entices him, or has him attend upon one, or eats together with him, or lies down together with him, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. In the case of one who has been banished, if, perceiving him as not banished, one entices him, or has him attend upon one, or eats together with him, or lies down together with him, there is no offense. In the case of one who has not been banished, if one perceives him as banished, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. In the case of one who has not been banished, if one is in doubt, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. In the case of one who has not been banished, if one perceives him as not banished, there is no offense.

432. Anāpatti [T 2.0448] anāsitakoti jānāti, taṃ diṭṭhiṃ paṭinissaṭṭhoti jānāti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

432. There is no offense if one knows he is not banished, if one knows he has abandoned that view, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Kaṇṭakasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

The tenth training rule, the Kaṇṭaka, is concluded.

Sappāṇakavaggo sattamo.

The Sappāṇaka Chapter, the Seventh.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Sañciccavadhasappāṇaṃ, ukkoṭaṃ duṭṭhullachādanaṃ;

Ūnavīsati satthañca, saṃvidhānaṃ ariṭṭhakaṃ;

Ukkhittaṃ kaṇṭakañceva, dasa sikkhāpadā imeti.

Intentional killing, living beings, raking up, concealing a grave offense; under twenty years, travelling with thieves, making an arrangement, Ariṭṭhaka; associating with a suspended bhikkhu, and Kaṇṭaka—these are the ten training rules.

8. Sahadhammikavaggo

8. The Sahadhammika Chapter

1. Sahadhammikasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The Sahadhammika Training Rule

433. Tena [T 2.0449][P 4.0141][V 0.0189] samayena buddho bhagavā kosambiyaṃ viharati ghositārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā channo anācāraṃ [M 0.0186] ācarati. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “māvuso channa, evarūpaṃ akāsi. Netaṃ kappatī”ti. So evaṃ vadeti – “na tāvāhaṃ, āvuso, etasmiṃ sikkhāpade sikkhissāmi yāva na aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ byattaṃ vinayadharaṃ paripucchāmī”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā channo bhikkhūhi sahadhammikaṃ vuccamāno evaṃ vakkhati – na tāvāhaṃ, āvuso, etasmiṃ sikkhāpade sikkhissāmi yāva na aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ byattaṃ vinayadharaṃ paripucchāmī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, channa, bhikkhūhi sahadhammikaṃ vuccamāno evaṃ vadesi – “na tāvāhaṃ, āvuso, etasmiṃ sikkhāpade sikkhissāmi yāva na aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ byattaṃ vinayadharaṃ paripucchāmī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, bhikkhūhi sahadhammikaṃ vuccamāno evaṃ vakkhasi – “na tāvāhaṃ, āvuso, etasmiṃ sikkhāpade sikkhissāmi yāva na aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ byattaṃ vinayadharaṃ paripucchāmī”ti. Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

433. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Kosambī in Ghosita’s Park. Now at that time, the Venerable Channa was conducting himself improperly. The bhikkhus said this: “Venerable Channa, do not do such a thing. This is not allowable.” He said this: “Venerables, I will not train in this training rule until I have questioned another bhikkhu who is competent and an expert in the Vinaya.” Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can the Venerable Channa, when being justly admonished by the bhikkhus, say: ‘Venerables, I will not train in this training rule until I have questioned another bhikkhu who is competent and an expert in the Vinaya’?” … “Is it true, Channa, that when being justly admonished by the bhikkhus, you said this: ‘Venerables, I will not train in this training rule until I have questioned another bhikkhu who is competent and an expert in the Vinaya’?” “It is true, Blessed One,” he said. The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “Foolish man, how can you, when being justly admonished by the bhikkhus, say this: ‘Venerables, I will not train in this training rule until I have questioned another bhikkhu who is competent and an expert in the Vinaya’? This, foolish man, is not for the confidence of the faithless… And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule in this way:

434. “Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhūhi sahadhammikaṃ vuccamāno evaṃ vadeyya [T 2.0450] – ‘na tāvāhaṃ, āvuso, etasmiṃ sikkhāpade sikkhissāmi yāva na aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ byattaṃ vinayadharaṃ paripucchāmī’ti, pācittiyaṃ. Sikkhamānena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā aññātabbaṃ paripucchitabbaṃ paripañhitabbaṃ. Ayaṃ tattha sāmīcī”ti.

434. “Whatever bhikkhu, when being admonished by bhikkhus in accordance with the Dhamma, should say: ‘Venerables, I will not train in this training rule until I have questioned another bhikkhu who is competent and an expert in the Vinaya,’ it is an offense of pācittiya. Bhikkhus, by a bhikkhu who wishes to train, it should be known, it should be questioned, it should be investigated. This is the proper practice in that case.”

435. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

435. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever sort… ‘Bhikkhu’ means: … in this context, this is the bhikkhu who is intended.

Bhikkhūhīti aññehi bhikkhūhi.

‘By bhikkhus’ means: by other bhikkhus.

Sahadhammikaṃ [V 0.0190] nāma yaṃ bhagavatā paññattaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ etaṃ sahadhammikaṃ nāma. Tena vuccamāno evaṃ vadeti vadeyya (ka.) – “na tāvāhaṃ, āvuso, etasmiṃ sikkhāpade sikkhissāmi yāva na aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ byattaṃ vinayadharaṃ paripucchāmī”ti imāni padāni syā. potthake na dissanti. Paṇḍitaṃ byattaṃ imāni padāni syā. potthake na dissanti medhāviṃ bahussutaṃ dhammakathikaṃ paripucchāmīti bhaṇati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

What is called ‘in accordance with the Dhamma’? It is the training rule laid down by the Blessed One; this is what is called ‘in accordance with the Dhamma’. When being admonished by means of it, if one says: ‘Venerables, I will not train in this training rule until I have questioned another bhikkhu who is competent and an expert in the Vinaya,’ or if one says that one will question a bhikkhu who is wise, competent, intelligent, learned, and a Dhamma-teacher, there is an offense of pācittiya.

436. Upasampanne [M 0.0187] upasampannasaññī evaṃ vadeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne vematiko evaṃ vadeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne anupasampannasaññī [P 4.0142] evaṃ vadeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

436. In the case of an ordained person, if, perceiving him as ordained, one speaks thus, there is an offense of pācittiya. In the case of an ordained person, if, being in doubt, one speaks thus, there is an offense of pācittiya. In the case of an ordained person, if, perceiving him as not ordained, one speaks thus, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Apaññattena vuccamāno – “idaṃ na sallekhāya na dhutatthāya na pāsādikatāya na apacayāya na vīriyārambhāya saṃvattatī”ti evaṃ vadeti, “na tāvāhaṃ, āvuso, etasmiṃ sikkhāpade sikkhissāmi yāva na aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ byattaṃ vinayadharaṃ paṇḍitaṃ medhāviṃ bahussutaṃ dhammakathikaṃ paripucchāmī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

When being admonished with something not laid down as a rule, if one says: ‘This does not lead to effacement, to shaking off defilements, to inspiring confidence, to diminution, or to the arousing of energy,’ and then says: ‘Venerables, I will not train in this training rule until I have questioned another bhikkhu who is competent, an expert in the Vinaya, wise, intelligent, learned, and a Dhamma-teacher,’ there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Anupasampannena paññattena vā apaññattena vā vuccamāno [T 2.0451] – “idaṃ na sallekhāya na dhutatthāya na pāsādikatāya na apacayāya na vīriyārambhāya saṃvattatī”ti evaṃ vadeti, “na tāvāhaṃ, āvuso, etasmiṃ sikkhāpade sikkhissāmi yāva na aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ byattaṃ vinayadharaṃ paṇḍitaṃ medhāviṃ bahussutaṃ dhammakathikaṃ paripucchāmī”ti bhaṇati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne upasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne anupasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

When being admonished by one who is not ordained, whether with what is laid down as a rule or what is not, if one says: ‘This does not lead to effacement, to shaking off defilements, to inspiring confidence, to diminution, or to the arousing of energy,’ and then says: ‘Venerables, I will not train in this training rule until I have questioned another bhikkhu who is competent, an expert in the Vinaya, wise, intelligent, learned, and a Dhamma-teacher,’ there is an offense of dukkaṭa. In the case of one who is not ordained, if one perceives him as ordained, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. In the case of one who is not ordained, if one is in doubt, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. In the case of one who is not ordained, if one perceives him as not ordained, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Sikkhamānenāti sikkhitukāmena.

‘By one who wishes to train’ means: by one who desires to train.

Aññātabbanti jānitabbaṃ.

‘It should be known’ means: it should be known.

Paripucchitabbanti “idaṃ, bhante, kathaṃ; imassa vā kvattho”ti?

‘It should be questioned’ means: ‘Venerable sir, how is this? Or what is its meaning?’

Paripañhitabbanti cintetabbaṃ tulayitabbaṃ.

‘It should be investigated’ means: it should be reflected upon and weighed.

Ayaṃ tattha sāmīcīti ayaṃ tattha anudhammatā.

‘This is the proper practice in that case’ means: this is the conduct that is in accordance with the Dhamma in that case.

437. Anāpatti [V 0.0191] “jānissāmi sikkhissāmī”ti bhaṇati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

437. There is no offense if one says, ‘I will come to know; I will train’; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Sahadhammikasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The first Sahadhammika Training Rule is concluded.

2. Vilekhanasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Training Rule on Disparagement

438. Tena [T 2.0452] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. idaṃ vatthu cūḷava. 320 Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā bhikkhūnaṃ anekapariyāyena vinayakathaṃ katheti, vinayassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, vinayapariyattiyā [M 0.0188] vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, ādissa ādissa āyasmato upālissa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi bhikkhū bhagavā (syā. ka.) – “bhagavā kho anekapariyāyena vinayakathaṃ katheti, vinayassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, vinayapariyattiyā vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, ādissa ādissa āyasmato upālissa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Handa mayaṃ, āvuso, āyasmato upālissa santike vinayaṃ pariyāpuṇāmā”ti, te ca bahū bhikkhū therā ca navā ca majjhimā ca āyasmato upālissa santike vinayaṃ pariyāpuṇanti.

438. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the Blessed One was, in many ways, giving a talk on the Discipline to the bhikkhus, speaking in praise of the Discipline, speaking in praise of learning the Discipline, and, referring to him again and again, speaking in praise of the Venerable Upāli. This thought occurred to the bhikkhus: “The Blessed One is, in many ways, giving a talk on the Discipline, speaking in praise of the Discipline, speaking in praise of learning the Discipline, and, referring to him again and again, speaking in praise of the Venerable Upāli. Come now, friends, let us learn the Discipline in the presence of the Venerable Upāli.” And many bhikkhus—elders, newly ordained, and those of middle standing—learned the Discipline in the presence of the Venerable Upāli.

Atha kho chabbaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi [P 4.0143] – “etarahi kho, āvuso, bahū bhikkhū therā ca navā ca majjhimā ca āyasmato upālissa santike vinayaṃ pariyāpuṇanti. Sace ime vinaye pakataññuno bhavissanti amhe yenicchakaṃ yadicchakaṃ yāvadicchakaṃ ākaḍḍhissanti parikaḍḍhissanti. Handa mayaṃ, āvuso, vinayaṃ vivaṇṇemā”ti. Atha kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadanti – “kiṃ panimehi khuddānukhuddakehi sikkhāpadehi uddiṭṭhehi, yāvadeva kukkuccāya vihesāya vilekhāya saṃvattantī”ti! Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – kathañhi [T 2.0453] nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū vinayaṃ vivaṇṇessantīti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, vinayaṃ vivaṇṇethāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, vinayaṃ vivaṇṇessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

Then this thought occurred to the bhikkhus of the group of six: “Friends, at present many bhikkhus—elders, newly ordained, and those of middle standing—are learning the Discipline in the presence of the Venerable Upāli. If they become skilled in the Discipline, they will drag us and pull us about however, whatever, and as much as they wish. Come now, friends, let us disparage the Discipline.” Then the bhikkhus of the group of six approached the bhikkhus and said this: “What is the use of these minor and insignificant training rules being recited? They only lead to scrupulousness, vexation, and mental distress!” Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, “How can the bhikkhus of the group of six disparage the Discipline?”… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that you disparage the Discipline?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Blessed One, the Buddha, rebuked them… “How, foolish men, can you disparage the Discipline? This is not, foolish men, for the confidence of the faithless…” … “And so, bhikkhus, this training rule should be recited thus:

439. “Yo pana bhikkhu pātimokkhe uddissamāne evaṃ vadeyya – ‘kiṃ panimehi khuddānukhuddakehi [V 0.0192] sikkhāpadehi uddiṭṭhehi, yāvadeva kukkuccāya vihesāya vilekhāya saṃvattantī’ti, sikkhāpadavivaṇṇake pācittiya”nti.

439. “Whatever bhikkhu, while the Pātimokkha is being recited, should say thus: ‘What is the use of these minor and insignificant training rules being recited? They only lead to scrupulousness, vexation, and mental distress,’ for disparaging the training rules, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

440. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

440. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever sort… ‘Bhikkhu’ means: … in this context, this is the bhikkhu who is intended.

Pātimokkhe uddissamāneti uddisante vā uddisāpente vā sajjhāyaṃ vā karonte.

‘While the Pātimokkha is being recited’ means: while reciting it, or causing it to be recited, or making a recitation.

Evaṃ [M 0.0189] vadeyyāti – “kiṃ panimehi khuddānukhuddakehi sikkhāpadehi uddiṭṭhehi, yāvadeva kukkuccāya vihesāya vilekhāya saṃvattantīti. “Ye imaṃ pariyāpuṇanti tesaṃ kukkuccaṃ hoti, vihesā hoti, vilekhā hoti, ye imaṃ na pariyāpuṇanti tesaṃ kukkuccaṃ na hoti vihesā na hoti vilekhā na hoti. Anuddiṭṭhaṃ idaṃ varaṃ, anuggahitaṃ idaṃ varaṃ, apariyāpuṭaṃ idaṃ varaṃ, adhāritaṃ idaṃ varaṃ, vinayo vā antaradhāyatu, ime vā bhikkhū apakataññuno hontū”ti upasampannassa vinayaṃ vivaṇṇeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

Should say thus: “What is the use of these minor and very minor training rules being recited? They only lead to scrupulousness, vexation, and mental distress. For those who learn this, there is scrupulousness, there is vexation, there is mental distress; for those who do not learn this, there is no scrupulousness, no vexation, no mental distress. It would be better if this were not recited, better if it were not taken up, better if it were not learned, better if it were not retained. Let the Vinaya disappear, or let these bhikkhus become unskilled!” If one disparages the Vinaya to a fully ordained person, it is an offense of pācittiya.

441. Upasampanne upasampannasaññī vinayaṃ vivaṇṇeti, āpatti pācittiyassa[T 2.0454]. Upasampanne vematiko vinayaṃ vivaṇṇeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne anupasampannasaññī vinayaṃ vivaṇṇeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

441. Regarding a fully ordained person, if one perceives them as fully ordained and disparages the Vinaya, it is an offense of pācittiya. Regarding a fully ordained person, if one is uncertain and disparages the Vinaya, it is an offense of pācittiya. Regarding a fully ordained person, if one perceives them as not fully ordained and disparages the Vinaya, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Aññaṃ dhammaṃ vivaṇṇeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannassa vinayaṃ vā aññaṃ vā dhammaṃ vivaṇṇeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne upasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne [P 4.0144] vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne anupasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one disparages another teaching, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. If one disparages the Vinaya or another teaching to a person who is not fully ordained, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. Regarding a person who is not fully ordained: if one perceives them as fully ordained, it is an offense of dukkaṭa; if one is uncertain, it is an offense of dukkaṭa; if one perceives them as not fully ordained, it is an offense of dukkaṭa.

442. Anāpatti na vivaṇṇetukāmo, “iṅgha tvaṃ suttante vā gāthāyo vā abhidhammaṃ vā pariyāpuṇassu, pacchā vinayaṃ pariyāpuṇissasī”ti bhaṇati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

442. There is no offense if one has no wish to disparage and says, “Come, you should first learn the Suttantas, or the Gāthās, or the Abhidhamma; afterwards you will learn the Vinaya”; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Vilekhanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The second training rule, on causing mental distress, is finished.

3. Mohanasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Training Rule on Feigning Ignorance

443. Tena [T 2.0455][V 0.0193] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū anācāraṃ ācaritvā “aññāṇakena āpannāti jānantū”ti pātimokkhe uddissamāne evaṃ vadanti – “idāneva kho mayaṃ jānāma, ayampi kira dhammo suttāgato suttapariyāpanno anvaddhamāsaṃ uddesaṃ āgacchatī”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū pātimokkhe uddissamāne evaṃ vakkhanti – idāneva kho mayaṃ jānāma[M 0.0190], ayampi kira dhammo suttāgato suttapariyāpanno anvaddhamāsaṃ uddesaṃ āgacchatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, pātimokkhe uddissamāne evaṃ vadetha – “idāneva kho mayaṃ jānāma, ayampi kira dhammo suttāgato suttapariyāpanno anvaddhamāsaṃ uddesaṃ āgacchatī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, pātimokkhe uddissamāne evaṃ vakkhatha – “idāneva kho mayaṃ jānāma, ayampi kira dhammo suttāgato suttapariyāpanno anvaddhamāsaṃ uddesaṃ āgacchatī”ti! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

443. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus, having committed an improper act, would say this when the Pātimokkha was being recited, so that others would think, “They have committed an offense through ignorance”: “Only now do we know that this rule, it seems, has come down in the code, is included in the code, and comes up for recitation every half-month.” Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… they criticized, scorned, and spread it about, saying: “How can the group-of-six bhikkhus say this when the Pātimokkha is being recited: ‘Only now do we know that this rule, it seems, has come down in the code, is included in the code, and comes up for recitation every half-month’?”… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that when the Pātimokkha is being recited, you say this: ‘Only now do we know that this rule, it seems, has come down in the code, is included in the code, and comes up for recitation every half-month’?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How, foolish men, can you say this when the Pātimokkha is being recited: ‘Only now do we know that this rule, it seems, has come down in the code, is included in the code, and comes up for recitation every half-month’? This, foolish men, is not for the faith of the faithless… And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

444. “Yo pana bhikkhu anvaddhamāsaṃ [T 2.0456] pātimokkhe uddissamāne evaṃ vadeyya – ‘idāneva kho ahaṃ jānāmi, ayampi kira dhammo suttāgato suttapariyāpanno anvaddhamāsaṃ uddesaṃ āgacchatī’ti. Tañce bhikkhuṃ aññe bhikkhū jāneyyuṃ nisinnapubbaṃ iminā bhikkhunā dvattikkhattuṃ pātimokkhe uddissamāne, ko pana vādo bhiyyo bhiyyoti (syā.), na ca tassa bhikkhuno aññāṇakena mutti atthi, yañca tattha āpattiṃ āpanno tañca yathādhammo kāretabbo, uttari cassa moho āropetabbo – ‘tassa te, āvuso, alābhā, tassa te dulladdhaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ pātimokkhe uddissamāne na sādhukaṃ aṭṭhiṃ katvā aṭṭhikatvā (syā. ka.) manasi karosī’ti. Idaṃ tasmiṃ mohanake pācittiya”nti.

444. “Whatever bhikkhu, when the Pātimokkha is being recited every half-month, should speak thus: ‘Only now do I know that this rule, it seems, has come down in the code, is included in the code, and comes up for recitation every half-month.’ If other bhikkhus should know of that bhikkhu that he has previously sat through the recitation of the Pātimokkha two or three times—what is there to say of more?—there is no release for that bhikkhu through feigning ignorance. And whatever offense he has committed there, he is to be dealt with according to the rule, and furthermore, a charge of feigning ignorance is to be brought against him: ‘It is no gain for you, friend, it is ill-gotten by you, that when the Pātimokkha is being recited, you do not pay proper, careful attention and take it to heart.’ This is a pācittiya offense in the case of feigning ignorance.”

445. Yo [P 4.0145] panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

445. Whatever: whoever, of whatever kind… and so on. Bhikkhu: …and so on. In this context, this is the bhikkhu who is meant.

Anvaddhamāsanti anuposathikaṃ.

Every half-month means: on every Uposatha day.

Pātimokkhe uddissamāneti uddisante.

When the Pātimokkha is being recited means: while it is being recited.

Evaṃ [V 0.0194] vadeyyāti anācāraṃ ācaritvā – “aññāṇakena āpannoti jānantū”ti pātimokkhe uddissamāne evaṃ vadeti – “idāneva kho ahaṃ jānāmi, ayampi kira dhammo suttāgato suttapariyāpanno anvaddhamāsaṃ uddesaṃ āgacchatī”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Should speak thus means: having committed an improper act, so that others would think, “He has committed an offense through ignorance,” when the Pātimokkha is being recited, he says: ‘Only now do I know that this rule, it seems, has come down in the code, is included in the code, and comes up for recitation every half-month.’ It is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Tañce [M 0.0191] mohetukāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ aññe bhikkhū jāneyyuṃ nisinnapubbaṃ iminā bhikkhunā dvattikkhattuṃ pātimokkhe uddissamāne, ko [T 2.0457] pana vādo bhiyyo, na ca tassa bhikkhuno aññāṇakena mutti atthi, yañca tattha āpattiṃ āpanno, tañca yathādhammo kāretabbo, uttari cassa moho āropetabbo. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, āropetabbo. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

If other bhikkhus should know of that bhikkhu who desires to feign ignorance that he has previously sat through the recitation of the Pātimokkha two or three times—what is there to say of more?—there is no release for that bhikkhu through feigning ignorance. And whatever offense he has committed there, he is to be dealt with according to the rule, and furthermore, a charge of feigning ignorance is to be brought against him. And so, bhikkhus, it should be brought. A competent and capable bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:

446. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu pātimokkhe uddissamāne na sādhukaṃ aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasi karoti. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno mohaṃ āropeyya. Esā ñatti.

446. “Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu, so-and-so by name, when the Pātimokkha is being recited, does not pay proper, careful attention and take it to heart. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should bring a charge of feigning ignorance against the bhikkhu so-and-so. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu pātimokkhe uddissamāne na sādhukaṃ aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasi karoti. Saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno mohaṃ āropeti. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno mohassa āropanā, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhu, so-and-so by name, when the Pātimokkha is being recited, does not pay proper, careful attention and take it to heart. The Saṅgha brings a charge of feigning ignorance against the bhikkhu so-and-so. He for whom the bringing of a charge of feigning ignorance against the bhikkhu so-and-so is agreeable, let him be silent. He for whom it is not agreeable, let him speak.”

“Āropito saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno moho. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The charge of feigning ignorance has been brought by the Saṅgha against the bhikkhu so-and-so. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I record it.”

Anāropite mohe moheti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Āropite mohe moheti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

If he feigns ignorance when a charge of feigning ignorance has not been brought, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If he feigns ignorance when a charge of feigning ignorance has been brought, there is a pācittiya offense.

447. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññī, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme vematiko, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññī moheti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

447. If he feigns ignorance during a valid formal act, perceiving it as a valid formal act, there is a pācittiya offense. If he feigns ignorance during a valid formal act, being doubtful about it, there is a pācittiya offense. If he feigns ignorance during a valid formal act, perceiving it as an invalid formal act, there is a pācittiya offense.

Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematiko[T 2.0458], āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If he feigns ignorance during an invalid formal act, perceiving it as a valid formal act, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If he feigns ignorance during an invalid formal act, being doubtful about it, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If he feigns ignorance during an invalid formal act, perceiving it as an invalid formal act, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

448. Anāpatti [V 0.0195] na vitthārena sutaṃ hoti, ūnakadvattikkhattuṃ vitthārena sutaṃ hoti, na mohetukāmassa, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

448. There is no offense if one has not heard it in detail; if one has heard it in detail fewer than two or three times; for one who does not intend to feign ignorance; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Mohanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Training Rule on Feigning Ignorance, the third, is finished.

4. Pahārasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Training Rule on Striking

449. Tena [T 2.0459][M 0.0192] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena [P 4.0146] chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kupitā anattamanā sattarasavaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pahāraṃ denti. Te rodanti. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “kissa tumhe, āvuso, rodathā”ti? “Ime, āvuso, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kupitā anattamanā amhākaṃ pahāraṃ dentī”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kupitā anattamanā bhikkhūnaṃ pahāraṃ dassantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, kupitā anattamanā bhikkhūnaṃ pahāraṃ dethāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, kupitā anattamanā bhikkhūnaṃ pahāraṃ dassatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

449. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks, being angry and displeased, gave a strike to the group-of-seventeen monks. They wept. The monks said to them, “Venerable sirs, why do you weep?” “Venerable sirs, these group-of-six monks, being angry and displeased, gave us a strike.” Those monks who were of few desires… complained, criticized, and spread it about, “How indeed could the group-of-six monks, being angry and displeased, give a strike to monks?”… “Is it true, it is said, monks, that you, being angry and displeased, gave a strike to monks?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed could you, foolish men, being angry and displeased, give a strike to monks? This, foolish men, is not for the confidence of those not yet confident… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

450. “Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhussa kupito anattamano pahāraṃ dadeyya, pācittiya”nti.

450. “Whatever monk, being angry and displeased, should give a strike to a monk, it is a pācittiya offense.”

451. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

451. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever sort… ‘A monk’ means… in this context, this is the monk who is intended.

Bhikkhussāti aññassa bhikkhussa.

‘To a monk’ means: to another monk.

Kupito anattamanoti anabhiraddho āhatacitto khilajāto.

‘Angry and displeased’ means: not delighted, with a mind that is struck, having become resentful.

Pahāraṃ dadeyyāti kāyena vā kāyapaṭibaddhena vā nissaggiyena vā antamaso uppalapattenapi [T 2.0460] pahāraṃ deti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should give a strike’ means: if one gives a strike with the body, or with something connected to the body, or with something thrown, even so much as with a lotus petal, there is a pācittiya offense.

452. Upasampanne [V 0.0196] upasampannasaññī kupito anattamano pahāraṃ deti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne vematiko kupito anattamano pahāraṃ deti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne anupasampannasaññī kupito anattamano pahāraṃ deti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

452. In the case of a fully ordained person: if one, being angry and displeased, gives a strike while perceiving him as fully ordained, there is a pācittiya offense. If one, being angry and displeased, gives a strike while in doubt, there is a pācittiya offense. If one, being angry and displeased, gives a strike while perceiving him as not fully ordained, there is a pācittiya offense.

Anupasampannassa kupito anattamano pahāraṃ deti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne upasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne vematiko[M 0.0193], āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne anupasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one, being angry and displeased, gives a strike to a person who is not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of a person not fully ordained, if one gives a strike while perceiving him as fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of a person not fully ordained, if one gives a strike while in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of a person not fully ordained, if one gives a strike while perceiving him as not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

453. Anāpatti kenaci viheṭhīyamāno mokkhādhippāyo pahāraṃ deti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

453. There is no offense if, being harassed by someone, one gives a strike with the intention of escaping; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Pahārasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Training Rule on Striking, the fourth, is finished.

5. Talasattikasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Training Rule on Raising the Flat of the Hand

454. Tena [T 2.0461] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kupitā anattamanā sattarasavaggiyānaṃ [P 4.0147] bhikkhūnaṃ talasattikaṃ uggiranti. Te pahārasamuccitā rodanti. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “kissa tumhe, āvuso, rodathā”ti? “Ime, āvuso, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kupitā anattamanā amhākaṃ talasattikaṃ uggirantī”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kupitā anattamanā sattarasavaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ talasattikaṃ uggirissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, kupitā anattamanā sattarasavaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ talasattikaṃ uggirathāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, kupitā anattamanā sattarasavaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ talasattikaṃ uggirissatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

454. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks, being angry and displeased, raised the flat of their hands toward the group-of-seventeen monks. Fearing a blow, they wept. The monks said this: “Venerable sirs, why do you weep?” “Venerable sirs, these group-of-six monks, being angry and displeased, are raising the flat of their hands toward us.” Those monks who were of few desires… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the group-of-six monks, being angry and displeased, raise the flat of their hands toward the group-of-seventeen monks?”… “Is it true, it is said, monks, that you, being angry and displeased, are raising the flat of your hands toward the group-of-seventeen monks?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed can you, foolish men, being angry and displeased, raise the flat of your hands toward the group-of-seventeen monks? This, foolish men, is not for the confidence of those not yet confident… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule in this way:

455. “Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhussa kupito anattamano talasattikaṃ uggireyya, pācittiya”nti.

455. “Whatever monk, being angry and displeased, should raise the flat of his hand toward another monk, there is a pācittiya offense.”

456. Yo [V 0.0197] panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

456. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever, of whatever sort… ‘Monk’ means… in this sense, this is the monk who is intended.

Bhikkhussāti aññassa bhikkhussa.

‘To a monk’ means: to another monk.

Kupito anattamanoti anabhiraddho āhatacitto khilajāto.

‘Angry and displeased’ means: not delighted, with an affected mind, having become like a stump.

Talasattikaṃ [M 0.0194] uggireyyāti [T 2.0462] kāyaṃ vā kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ vā antamaso uppalapattampi uccāreti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should raise the flat of the hand’ means: if one raises the body, or what is connected to the body, or even so much as a lotus leaf, there is a pācittiya offense.

457. Upasampanne upasampannasaññī kupito anattamano talasattikaṃ uggirati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne vematiko kupito anattamano talasattikaṃ uggirati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne anupasampannasaññī kupito anattamano talasattikaṃ uggirati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

457. Toward one who is fully ordained, if, perceiving him as fully ordained, being angry and displeased, one raises the flat of the hand, there is an offense of expiation. Toward one who is fully ordained, if, being in doubt, being angry and displeased, one raises the flat of the hand, there is an offense of expiation. Toward one who is fully ordained, if, perceiving him as not fully ordained, being angry and displeased, one raises the flat of the hand, there is an offense of expiation.

Anupasampannassa kupito anattamano talasattikaṃ uggirati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne upasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne anupasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Toward one who is not fully ordained, if, being angry and displeased, one raises the flat of the hand, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Toward one who is not fully ordained, if one perceives him as fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Toward one who is not fully ordained, if one is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Toward one who is not fully ordained, if one perceives him as not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

458. Anāpatti kenaci viheṭhīyamāno mokkhādhippāyo talasattikaṃ uggirati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

458. There is no offense if, being harassed by someone, one raises the flat of the hand with the intention of escaping; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Talasattikasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Talasattika Training Rule, the fifth, is concluded.

6. Amūlakasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Training Rule on a Groundless Accusation

459. Tena [T 2.0463] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ amūlakena saṅghādisesena anuddhaṃsenti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ amūlakena saṅghādisesena anuddhaṃsessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ amūlakena saṅghādisesena anuddhaṃsethāti[V 0.0198]? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi [P 4.0148] buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, bhikkhuṃ amūlakena saṅghādisesena anuddhaṃsessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

459. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks groundlessly accused a monk of a Saṅghādisesa offense. Those monks who were of few wishes... grumbled, criticized, and complained, “How indeed could the group-of-six monks groundlessly accuse a monk of a Saṅghādisesa offense?”... “Is it true, monks, as is said, that you groundlessly accused a monk of a Saṅghādisesa offense?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... “How indeed could you, worthless men, groundlessly accuse a monk of a Saṅghādisesa offense? This, worthless men, does not lead to the confidence of the unconvinced...”... “And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

460. “Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ amūlakena saṅghādisesena anuddhaṃseyya, pācittiya”nti.

460. “Whatever monk should groundlessly accuse a monk of a Saṅghādisesa offense, it is an offense of expiation.”

461. Yo [M 0.0195] panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

461. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever, of whatever sort... ‘Monk’ means... the monk who is intended in this context.

Bhikkhunti aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ.

‘A monk’ means: another monk.

Amūlakaṃ nāma adiṭṭhaṃ assutaṃ aparisaṅkitaṃ.

‘Groundless’ means: not seen, not heard, not suspected.

Saṅghādisesenāti terasannaṃ aññatarena.

‘By a Saṅghādisesa offense’ means: by any one of the thirteen.

Anuddhaṃseyyāti codeti vā codāpeti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should accuse’ means: if one accuses or causes another to accuse, there is an offense of expiation.

462. Upasampanne upasampannasaññī amūlakena saṅghādisesena anuddhaṃseti[T 2.0464], āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne vematiko amūlakena saṅghādisesena anuddhaṃseti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne anupasampannasaññī amūlakena saṅghādisesena anuddhaṃseti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

462. Toward one who is fully ordained, if, perceiving him as fully ordained, one groundlessly accuses him of a Saṅghādisesa offense, there is an offense of expiation. Toward one who is fully ordained, if, being in doubt, one groundlessly accuses him of a Saṅghādisesa offense, there is an offense of expiation. Toward one who is fully ordained, if, perceiving him as not fully ordained, one groundlessly accuses him of a Saṅghādisesa offense, there is an offense of expiation.

Ācāravipattiyā vā diṭṭhivipattiyā vā anuddhaṃseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannaṃ anuddhaṃseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne upasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne anupasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one accuses another of a corruption of conduct or a corruption of view, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one accuses one who is not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Toward one who is not fully ordained, if, perceiving him as fully ordained, one accuses him, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Toward one who is not fully ordained, if, being in doubt, one accuses him, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Toward one who is not fully ordained, if, perceiving him as not fully ordained, one accuses him, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

463. Anāpatti tathāsaññī codeti, vā codāpeti vā, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

463. There is no offense for one who, perceiving the accusation to be true, accuses or causes another to accuse; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Amūlakasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Amūlaka Training Rule, the sixth, is concluded.

7. Sañciccasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Training Rule on Deliberately Causing Remorse

464. Tena [T 2.0465][V 0.0199] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sattarasavaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ sañcicca kukkuccaṃ upadahanti – “bhagavatā, āvuso, sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ – ‘na ūnavīsativasso puggalo upasampādetabbo’ti. Tumhe ca ūnavīsativassā upasampannā. Kacci no tumhe anupasampannā”ti? Te rodanti. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “kissa tumhe, āvuso, rodathā”ti? “Ime[M 0.0196], āvuso, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū amhākaṃ sañcicca kukkuccaṃ upadahantī”ti[P 4.0149]. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhūnaṃ sañcicca kukkuccaṃ upadahissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ sañcicca kukkuccaṃ upadahathāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, bhikkhūnaṃ sañcicca kukkuccaṃ upadahissatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

464. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the monks of the group-of-six deliberately caused remorse to the monks of the group-of-seventeen, saying: “Friends, the Blessed One has laid down a training rule: ‘A person who is less than twenty years of age should not be ordained.’ And you were ordained while being less than twenty years of age. Could it be that you are unordained?” They wept. The monks said: “Friends, why do you weep?” “Friends, these monks of the group-of-six are deliberately causing us remorse.” Those monks who were of few desires… criticized, censured, and spread it about: “How indeed could the monks of the group-of-six deliberately cause remorse to monks?”… “Is it true, it is said, monks, that you deliberately cause remorse to monks?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “Worthless men, how indeed could you deliberately cause remorse to monks! This, worthless men, does not lead to the confidence of the unconvinced… And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

465. “Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhussa sañcicca kukkuccaṃ upadaheyya uppādeyya (itipi) – ‘itissa muhuttampi aphāsu bhavissatī’ti etadeva paccayaṃ karitvā anaññaṃ, pācittiya”nti.

465. “Whatever monk should deliberately cause remorse to another monk, making this the only reason and no other, thinking, ‘Thus he will be uncomfortable even for a moment,’ it is an offense of expiation.”

466. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ [T 2.0466] atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

466. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever, of whatever sort... ‘Monk’ means... the monk who is intended in this context.

Bhikkhussāti aññassa bhikkhussa.

‘To a monk’ means: to another monk.

Sañciccāti jānanto sañjānanto cecca abhivitaritvā vītikkamo.

‘Deliberately’ means: knowing, clearly knowing, having instigated, having overcome, it is a transgression.

Kukkuccaṃ upadaheyyāti “ūnavīsativasso maññe tvaṃ upasampanno, vikāle maññe tayā bhuttaṃ, majjaṃ maññe tayā pītaṃ, mātugāmena saddhiṃ raho maññe tayā nisinna”nti kukkuccaṃ upadahati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should cause remorse’ means: if one causes remorse by saying, “I suppose you were ordained when less than twenty years of age; I suppose you ate at the wrong time; I suppose you drank liquor; I suppose you sat together with a woman in a secluded place,” there is an offense of expiation.

Etadeva [V 0.0200] paccayaṃ karitvā, anaññanti na añño koci paccayo hoti kukkuccaṃ upadahituṃ.

‘Making this the only reason and no other’ means: there is no other reason for causing remorse.

467. Upasampanne upasampannasaññī sañcicca kukkuccaṃ upadahati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne vematiko sañcicca kukkuccaṃ upadahati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne anupasampannasaññī sañcicca kukkuccaṃ upadahati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

467. Regarding a fully ordained person, if one, perceiving him as fully ordained, deliberately causes him remorse, it is an offense entailing expiation. Regarding a fully ordained person, if one, being in doubt, deliberately causes him remorse, it is an offense entailing expiation. Regarding a fully ordained person, if one, perceiving him as not fully ordained, deliberately causes him remorse, it is an offense entailing expiation.

Anupasampannassa sañcicca kukkuccaṃ upadahati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne upasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne anupasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one deliberately causes remorse to a person who is not fully ordained, it is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding a person who is not fully ordained, if one perceives him as fully ordained, it is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding a person who is not fully ordained, if one is in doubt, it is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding a person who is not fully ordained, if one perceives him as not fully ordained, it is an offense of wrong conduct.

468. Anāpatti [M 0.0197] na kukkuccaṃ upadahitukāmo “ūnavīsativasso maññe tvaṃ upasampanno, vikāle maññe tayā bhuttaṃ, majjaṃ maññe tayā pītaṃ, mātugāmena saddhiṃ raho maññe tayā nisinnaṃ, iṅgha jānāhi, mā te pacchā kukkuccaṃ ahosī”ti bhaṇati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

468. There is no offense for one who, not wishing to cause remorse, says, “I suppose you were ordained when less than twenty years of age; I suppose you ate at the wrong time; I suppose you drank liquor; I suppose you sat together with a woman in a secluded place. Come now, find out, lest you have remorse later”; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Sañciccasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.

The seventh training rule, on acting deliberately, is concluded.

8. Upassutisikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Training Rule on Eavesdropping

469. Tena [T 2.0467][P 4.0150] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū pesalehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ bhaṇḍanti. Pesalā bhikkhū evaṃ vadanti – “alajjino ime, āvuso, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū. Na sakkā imehi saha bhaṇḍitu”nti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū evaṃ vadanti – “kissa tumhe, āvuso, amhe alajjivādena pāpethā”ti? “Kahaṃ pana tumhe, āvuso, assutthā”ti? “Mayaṃ āyasmantānaṃ upassutiṃ upassuti (?) tiṭṭhamhā”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhūnaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ upassutiṃ upassuti (?) tiṭṭhissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ upassutiṃ upassuti (?) tiṭṭhathāti? “Sacca, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, bhikkhūnaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ [V 0.0201] kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ upassutiṃ upassuti (?) tiṭṭhissatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

469. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus were quarreling with the virtuous bhikkhus. The virtuous bhikkhus said, “Friends, these group-of-six bhikkhus are shameless. It is not possible to quarrel with them.” The group-of-six bhikkhus said, “Friends, why do you accuse us of being shameless?” “But where, friends, did you hear this?” “We were standing within earshot of the venerables.” Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… censured, condemned, and spread it about, saying, “How indeed can the group-of-six bhikkhus stand within earshot of bhikkhus who have become quarrelsome, become contentious, and have entered into disputes?”… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that you stand within earshot of bhikkhus who have become quarrelsome, become contentious, and have entered into disputes?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Blessed One, the Buddha, rebuked them… “Foolish men, how indeed can you stand within earshot of bhikkhus who have become quarrelsome, become contentious, and have entered into disputes? This, foolish men, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

470. “Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ upassutiṃ tiṭṭheyya – ‘yaṃ ime bhaṇissanti taṃ sossāmī’ti etadeva paccayaṃ karitvā anaññaṃ, pācittiya”nti.

470. “Whatever bhikkhu should stand within earshot of bhikkhus who have become quarrelsome, become contentious, and have entered into disputes, thinking, ‘Whatever they will say, that I shall hear,’ making this the sole reason and no other, it is an offense entailing expiation.”

471. Yo [T 2.0468] panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

471. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhu’ means: …in this sense, this is the bhikkhu who is intended.

Bhikkhūnanti [M 0.0198] aññesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ.

‘Of bhikkhus’ means: of other bhikkhus.

Bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānanti adhikaraṇajātānaṃ.

‘Who have become quarrelsome, become contentious, and have entered into disputes’ means: of those for whom a legal issue has arisen.

Upassutiṃ tiṭṭheyyāti “imesaṃ sutvā codessāmi sāressāmi paṭicodessāmi paṭisāressāmi maṅkū karissāmī”ti gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yattha ṭhito suṇāti, āpatti pācittiyassa.
