Pacchato gacchanto turito gacchati sossāmīti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yattha ṭhito suṇāti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Purato gacchanto ohiyyati sossāmīti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yattha ṭhito suṇāti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Bhikkhussa ṭhitokāsaṃ vā nisinnokāsaṃ vā nipannokāsaṃ vā āgantvā mantentaṃ ukkāsitabbaṃ[P 4.0151], vijānāpetabbaṃ, no ce ukkāseyya vā vijānāpeyya vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should stand within earshot’ means: if one goes with the thought, “Having heard them, I will accuse them, I will remind them, I will counter-accuse them, I will counter-remind them, I will cause them embarrassment,” it is an offense of wrong conduct. At the place where, having stood, one listens, it is an offense entailing expiation. If, while going behind, one hurries with the thought, “I will listen,” it is an offense of wrong conduct. At the place where, having stood, one listens, it is an offense entailing expiation. If, while going in front, one lags behind with the thought, “I will listen,” it is an offense of wrong conduct. At the place where, having stood, one listens, it is an offense entailing expiation. Having approached a bhikkhu’s place of standing, sitting, or lying down while he is conferring, one should clear one's throat or make oneself known. If one does not clear one's throat or make oneself known, it is an offense entailing expiation.

Etadeva paccayaṃ karitvā anaññanti na añño koci paccayo hoti upassutiṃ tiṭṭhituṃ.

‘Making this the sole reason and no other’ means: there is no other reason whatsoever for standing within earshot.

472. Upasampanne upasampannasaññī upassutiṃ tiṭṭhati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne vematiko upassutiṃ tiṭṭhati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne anupasampannasaññī upassutiṃ tiṭṭhati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

472. Regarding a fully ordained person, if one, perceiving him as fully ordained, stands within earshot, it is an offense entailing expiation. Regarding a fully ordained person, if one, being in doubt, stands within earshot, it is an offense entailing expiation. Regarding a fully ordained person, if one, perceiving him as not fully ordained, stands within earshot, it is an offense entailing expiation.

Anupasampannassa upassutiṃ tiṭṭhati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne upasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne vematiko, āpatti [V 0.0202] dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne [T 2.0469] anupasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one stands within earshot of one who is not fully ordained, it is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding one who is not fully ordained, if one perceives him as fully ordained, it is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding one who is not fully ordained, if one is in doubt, it is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding one who is not fully ordained, if one perceives him as not fully ordained, it is an offense of wrong conduct.

473. Anāpatti – “imesaṃ sutvā oramissāmi viramissāmi vūpasamissāmi vūpasamessāmi (sī.) attānaṃ parimocessāmī”ti gacchati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

473. There is no offense: if one goes with the thought, “Having heard them, I will desist, I will especially desist, I will become pacified, I will free myself”; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Upassutisikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The eighth training rule, on eavesdropping, is concluded.

9. Kammapaṭibāhanasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Training Rule on Obstructing a Formal Act

474. Tena [T 2.0470][M 0.0199] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū anācāraṃ ācaritvā ekamekassa kamme kayiramāne paṭikkosanti. Tena kho pana samayena saṅgho sannipatito hoti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū cīvarakammaṃ karontā ekassa chandaṃ adaṃsu. Atha kho saṅgho – “ayaṃ, āvuso, chabbaggiyo bhikkhu ekako āgato, handassa mayaṃ kammaṃ karomā”ti tassa kammaṃ akāsi. Atha kho so bhikkhu yena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavocuṃ – “kiṃ, āvuso, saṅgho akāsī”ti? “Saṅgho me, āvuso, kammaṃ akāsī”ti. “Na mayaṃ, āvuso, etadatthāya chandaṃ adamhā – “tuyhaṃ kammaṃ karissatī”ti. Sace ca mayaṃ jāneyyāma “tuyhaṃ kammaṃ karissatī”ti, na mayaṃ chandaṃ dadeyyāmā”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū dhammikānaṃ kammānaṃ chandaṃ datvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ khiyyadhammaṃ (itipi) āpajjissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, dhammikānaṃ kammānaṃ [P 4.0152] chandaṃ datvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ khiyyadhammaṃ (itipi) āpajjathāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, dhammikānaṃ kammānaṃ chandaṃ datvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ [T 2.0471] khiyyadhammaṃ (itipi) āpajjissatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

474. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. At that time, the bhikkhus of the group of six, having engaged in misconduct, were protesting against the formal acts being performed for each one. At that time, the Saṅgha had assembled for some business. The bhikkhus of the group of six, while doing robe-work, gave their consent through one of them. Then the Saṅgha thought, “Friends, this bhikkhu from the group of six has come alone. Come, let us perform a formal act against him.” So they performed the formal act against him. Then that bhikkhu approached the bhikkhus of the group of six. The bhikkhus of the group of six said to that bhikkhu, “Friend, what did the Saṅgha do?” “Friends, the Saṅgha performed a formal act against me.” “Friend, we did not give our consent for this purpose, thinking, ‘They will perform a formal act against you.’ If we had known, ‘They will perform a formal act against you,’ we would not have given our consent.” Those bhikkhus who were of few desires… complained, grumbled, and criticized: “How indeed could the bhikkhus of the group of six, after giving their consent for lawful formal acts, later fall into a state of criticism?”… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that you gave your consent for lawful formal acts and later fell into a state of criticism?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “Worthless men, how indeed could you give your consent for lawful formal acts and later fall into a state of criticism? This, worthless men, is not for inspiring confidence in the unconfident… And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

475. “Yo pana bhikkhu dhammikānaṃ kammānaṃ chandaṃ datvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ āpajjeyya, pācittiya”nti.

475. “Whatever bhikkhu, having given consent for lawful formal acts, should afterwards fall into a state of criticism, it is a pācittiya offense.”

476. Yo [V 0.0203] panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

476. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever sort… ‘bhikkhu’ means… in this sense, this is the bhikkhu who is intended.

Dhammikaṃ nāma kammaṃ apalokanakammaṃ ñattikammaṃ ñattidutiyakammaṃ ñatticatutthakammaṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena kataṃ, etaṃ dhammikaṃ nāma kammaṃ. Chandaṃ datvā khiyyati āpatti pācittiyassa.

A lawful formal act means an act of information, an act by motion, an act by motion and a second announcement, or an act by motion and a fourth announcement, performed in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher's instruction. This is called a lawful formal act. Having given consent, if one criticizes it, there is a pācittiya offense.

477. Dhammakamme [M 0.0200] dhammakammasaññī chandaṃ datvā khiyyati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme vematiko chandaṃ datvā khiyyati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññī chandaṃ datvā khiyyati, anāpatti. Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññī, anāpatti.

477. In a lawful formal act, if one, perceiving it as a lawful formal act, gives consent and then criticizes it, there is a pācittiya offense. In a lawful formal act, if one, being uncertain, gives consent and then criticizes it, there is a dukkaṭa offense. In a lawful formal act, if one, perceiving it as an unlawful formal act, gives consent and then criticizes it, there is no offense. In an unlawful formal act, if one, perceiving it as a lawful formal act, gives consent and then criticizes it, there is a dukkaṭa offense. In an unlawful formal act, if one, being uncertain, gives consent and then criticizes it, there is a dukkaṭa offense. In an unlawful formal act, if one, perceiving it as an unlawful formal act, gives consent and then criticizes it, there is no offense.

478. Anāpatti – “adhammena vā vaggena vā na kammārahassa vā kammaṃ kata”nti jānanto khiyyati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

478. There is no offense: if one criticizes, knowing, “The formal act was performed unlawfully, or by an incomplete quorum, or for one not deserving of the act”; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Kammapaṭibāhanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.

The ninth training rule, on rejecting a formal act, is finished.

10. Chandaṃadatvāgamanasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Training Rule on Going Without Giving Consent

479. Tena [T 2.0472] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena saṅgho sannipatito hoti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū cīvarakammaṃ karontā ekassa chandaṃ adaṃsu. Atha kho saṅgho “yassatthāya sannipatito taṃ kammaṃ karissāmī”ti ñattiṃ ṭhapesi. Atha kho so bhikkhu – “evamevime ekamekassa kammaṃ karonti, kassa tumhe kammaṃ karissathā”ti chandaṃ adatvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhu saṅghe vinicchayakathāya vattamānāya [P 4.0153] chandaṃ adatvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, bhikkhu, saṅghe vinicchayakathāya vattamānāya chandaṃ adatvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamasīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, saṅghe vinicchayakathāya vattamānāya chandaṃ adatvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamissasi[V 0.0204]! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

479. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the Saṅgha had assembled for some business. The bhikkhus of the group of six, while doing robe-work, gave their consent through one of them. Then the Saṅgha established a motion, thinking, 'We will perform that act for the purpose of which we have assembled.' Then that bhikkhu—thinking, 'Thus these bhikkhus perform an act against each and every one; against whom will you perform the act?'—without giving his consent, rose from his seat and departed. Those bhikkhus who were of few desires… complained, grumbled, and criticized: 'How could a bhikkhu, while a discussion for a decision was being conducted in the Saṅgha, rise from his seat and depart without giving his consent?'… 'Is it true, bhikkhu, that you rose from your seat and departed without giving your consent while a discussion for a decision was being conducted in the Saṅgha?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him: '…Worthless man, how could you rise from your seat and depart without giving your consent while a discussion for a decision is being conducted in the Saṅgha? This, worthless man, is not for inspiring confidence in the unconfident… And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

480. “Yo pana bhikkhu saṅghe vinicchayakathāya vattamānāya chandaṃ adatvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkameyya, pācittiya”nti.

480. “Whatever bhikkhu, while a discussion for a decision is proceeding in the Saṅgha, should rise from his seat and depart without giving consent, it is a pācittiya offense.”

481. Yo [T 2.0473][M 0.0201] panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

481. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever sort… ‘Bhikkhu’ means… in this sense, this is the bhikkhu who is intended.

Saṅghe vinicchayakathā nāma vatthu vā ārocitaṃ hoti avinicchitaṃ, ñatti vā ṭhapitā hoti, kammavācā vā vippakatā hoti.

A discussion for a decision means: a matter has been announced but is undecided, or a motion has been placed, or the formal wording of the act is unfinished.

Chandaṃ adatvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkameyyāti – “kathaṃ idaṃ kammaṃ kuppaṃ assa vaggaṃ assa na kareyyā”ti gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Parisāya hatthapāsaṃ vijahantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa. Vijahite āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should rise from his seat and depart without giving consent’: if he goes thinking, 'How might this act be invalidated, become a factional act, or not be done?' there is a dukkaṭa offense. For one abandoning the hand-reach of the assembly, there is a dukkaṭa offense. When it has been abandoned, there is a pācittiya offense.

482. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññī chandaṃ adatvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme vematiko chandaṃ adatvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññī chandaṃ adatvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamati, anāpatti. Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññī, anāpatti.

482. If it is a lawful act and he perceives it as a lawful act, and he rises from his seat and departs without giving consent, there is an offense of expiation. If it is a lawful act and he is doubtful, and he rises from his seat and departs without giving consent, there is an offense of wrongdoing. If it is a lawful act and he perceives it as an unlawful act, and he rises from his seat and departs without giving consent, there is no offense. If it is an unlawful act and he perceives it as a lawful act, there is an offense of wrongdoing. If it is an unlawful act and he is doubtful, there is an offense of wrongdoing. If it is an unlawful act and he perceives it as an unlawful act, there is no offense.

483. Anāpatti – “saṅghassa bhaṇḍanaṃ vā kalaho vā viggaho vā vivādo vā bhavissatī”ti gacchati, “saṅghabhedo vā saṅgharāji vā bhavissatī”ti gacchati, “adhammena vā vaggena vā na kammārahassa vā kammaṃ karissatī”ti gacchati, gilāno gacchati, gilānassa karaṇīyena gacchati, uccārena vā passāvena vā pīḷito gacchati, “na kammaṃ [T 2.0474] kopetukāmo puna paccāgamissāmī”ti gacchati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

483. There is no offense: if one departs thinking, 'Contention, or a quarrel, or a dispute, or an argument will arise in the Saṅgha'; if one departs thinking, 'A schism in the Saṅgha or a fissure in the Saṅgha will arise'; if one departs thinking, 'They will perform the act unlawfully, or factionally, or for one not deserving of the act'; if a sick person departs; if one departs on an errand for a sick person; if one departs being pressed by feces or urine; if one departs thinking, 'Not wishing to invalidate the act, I will return'; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Chandaṃ adatvā gamanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

The tenth training rule on departing without giving consent is concluded.

11. Dubbalasikkhāpadaṃ

11. The Training Rule on the Worn-out Robe

484. Tena [T 2.0475][P 4.0154][V 0.0205] samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā dabbo mallaputto saṅghassa senāsanañca paññapeti bhattāni ca uddisati. So cāyasmā dubbalacīvaro hoti. Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa ekaṃ cīvaraṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Atha kho saṅgho taṃ cīvaraṃ āyasmato dabbassa mallaputtassa adāsi[M 0.0202]. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “yathāsanthutaṃ bhikkhū saṅghikaṃ lābhaṃ pariṇāmentī”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū samaggena saṅghena cīvaraṃ datvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ āpajjissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, samaggena saṅghena cīvaraṃ datvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ āpajjathāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, samaggena saṅghena cīvaraṃ datvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ āpajjissatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ, vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

484. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Veḷuvana, the squirrel sanctuary. Now at that time, the venerable Dabba the Mallian was preparing the lodgings and designating the almsfood for the Saṅgha. And that venerable one had a worn-out robe. Now at that time, a single robe had arisen for the Saṅgha. Then the Saṅgha gave that robe to the venerable Dabba the Mallian. The monks of the group of six criticized, disparaged, and found fault, saying: “The monks divert the Saṅgha’s gain according to their intimacy!” Those monks who were of few wishes… they criticized, disparaged, and found fault, saying: “How indeed could the monks of the group of six, after having given a robe together with the united Saṅgha, later fall into a state of disparagement?”… “Is it true, as is said, monks, that after having given a robe together with the united Saṅgha, you later fell into a state of disparagement?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed could you, foolish men, after having given a robe together with the united Saṅgha, later fall into a state of disparagement! This will not, foolish men, lead to the confidence of the faithless or to the increase of the faithful… And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

485. “Yo pana bhikkhu samaggena saṅghena cīvaraṃ datvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ āpajjeyya ‘yathāsanthutaṃ bhikkhū saṅghikaṃ lābhaṃ pariṇāmentī’ti, pācittiya”nti.

485. “Whatever monk, having given a robe together with the united Saṅgha, should afterwards fall into a state of disparagement, saying, ‘The monks divert the Saṅgha’s gain according to their intimacy,’ it is an offense of expiation.”

486. Yo [T 2.0476] panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

486. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘Monk’ means… in this sense, this is the monk who is intended.

Samaggo nāma saṅgho samānasaṃvāsako samānasīmāyaṃ ṭhito.

A united Saṅgha is one having the same communion, established within the same boundary.

Cīvaraṃ nāma channaṃ cīvarānaṃ aññataraṃ cīvaraṃ vikappanupagaṃ pacchimaṃ.

A robe means any one of the six kinds of robes, at the very least one that is suitable for shared use.

Datvāti sayaṃ datvā.

‘Having given’ means having given oneself.

Yathāsanthutaṃ nāma yathāmittatā yathāsandiṭṭhatā yathāsambhattatā yathāsamānupajjhāyakatā yathāsamānācariyakatā.

‘According to intimacy’ means: according to friendship, according to being an acquaintance, according to close association, according to having the same preceptor, according to having the same teacher.

Saṅghikaṃ [V 0.0206] nāma saṅghassa dinnaṃ hoti pariccattaṃ.

‘Belonging to the Saṅgha’ means it has been given to the Saṅgha, relinquished.

Lābho nāma cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā, antamaso cuṇṇapiṇḍopi, dantakaṭṭhampi, dasikasuttampi.

‘Gain’ means robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick; even down to a lump of powdered soap, a tooth-stick, or a piece of thread.

Pacchā [P 4.0155] khīyanadhammaṃ āpajjeyyāti upasampannassa saṅghena sammatassa senāsanapaññāpakassa vā bhattuddesakassa vā yāgubhājakassa vā phalabhājakassa vā khajjabhājakassa vā appamattakavissajjakassa vā cīvaraṃ dinne khiyyati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should afterwards fall into a state of disparagement’ means: if one disparages after a robe has been given to a fully ordained monk who has been appointed by the Saṅgha as an arranger of lodgings, or a designator of meals, or a distributor of gruel, or a distributor of fruit, or a distributor of hard food, or a dispenser of small items, there is an offense of expiation.

487. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññī cīvaraṃ dinne khiyyati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme vematiko cīvaraṃ dinne khiyyati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññī cīvaraṃ dinne khiyyati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

487. Regarding a lawful act, if one perceives it as a lawful act and disparages after a robe has been given, there is an offense of expiation. Regarding a lawful act, if one is doubtful and disparages after a robe has been given, there is an offense of expiation. Regarding a lawful act, if one perceives it as an unlawful act and disparages after a robe has been given, there is an offense of expiation.

Aññaṃ [M 0.0203] parikkhāraṃ dinne khiyyati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Upasampannassa saṅghena asammatassa senāsanapaññāpakassa vā bhattuddesakassa vā yāgubhājakassa vā phalabhājakassa vā khajjabhājakassa vā appamattakavissajjakassa vā cīvaraṃ vā aññaṃ vā parikkhāraṃ dinne khiyyati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannassa saṅghena [T 2.0477] sammatassa vā asammatassa vā senāsanapaññāpakassa vā bhattuddesakassa vā yāgubhājakassa vā phalabhājakassa vā khajjabhājakassa vā appamattakavissajjakassa vā cīvaraṃ vā aññaṃ vā parikkhāraṃ dinne khiyyati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññī, anāpatti.

If one disparages after another requisite has been given, there is an offense of wrongdoing. If one disparages after a robe or another requisite has been given to a fully ordained monk who has not been appointed by the Saṅgha as an arranger of lodgings, a designator of meals, a distributor of gruel, a distributor of fruit, a distributor of hard food, or a dispenser of small items, there is an offense of wrongdoing. If one disparages after a robe or another requisite has been given to one who is not fully ordained, whether appointed by the Saṅgha or not, as an arranger of lodgings, a designator of meals, a distributor of gruel, a distributor of fruit, a distributor of hard food, or a dispenser of small items, there is an offense of wrongdoing. Regarding an unlawful act, if one perceives it as a lawful act, there is an offense of wrongdoing. Regarding an unlawful act, if one is doubtful, there is an offense of wrongdoing. Regarding an unlawful act, if one perceives it as an unlawful act, there is no offense.

488. Anāpatti – pakatiyā chandā dosā mohā bhayā karontaṃ “kvattho tassa dinnena laddhāpi vinipātessati na sammā upanessatī”ti khiyyati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

488. There is no offense: if one disparages the act being done out of natural inclination, desire, aversion, delusion, or fear; if one disparages, thinking, “What is the use of giving to him? Even having received it, he will destroy it and not use it properly”; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Dubbalasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ ekādasamaṃ.

The eleventh training rule, on the worn-out robe, is concluded.

12. Pariṇāmanasikkhāpadaṃ

12. The Training Rule on Diversion

489. idaṃ vatthu pārā. 657 Tena [T 2.0478][V 0.0207] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sāvatthiyaṃ aññatarassa pūgassa saṅghassa sacīvarabhattaṃ paṭiyattaṃ hoti – “bhojetvā cīvarena acchādessāmā”ti. Atha kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhū yena so pūgo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ pūgaṃ etadavocuṃ – “dethāvuso, imāni cīvarāni imesaṃ bhikkhūna”nti. “Na mayaṃ, bhante, dassāma. Amhākaṃ saṅghassa anuvassaṃ sacīvarabhikkhā paññattā”ti. “Bahū, āvuso, saṅghassa dāyakā, bahū saṅghassa bhattā bhaddā (ka.). Ime tumhe nissāya tumhe sampassantā idha viharanti. Tumhe ce imesaṃ na dassatha, atha ko [P 4.0156] carahi imesaṃ dassati? Dethāvuso, imāni cīvarāni imesaṃ bhikkhūna”nti. Atha kho so pūgo chabbaggiyehi bhikkhūhi nippīḷiyamāno yathāpaṭiyattaṃ cīvaraṃ chabbaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ datvā saṅghaṃ bhattena parivisi. Ye te bhikkhū jānanti [M 0.0204] saṅghassa sacīvarabhattaṃ paṭiyattaṃ “na ca jānanti chabbaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dinna”nti te evamāhaṃsu – “oṇojethāvuso, saṅghassa cīvara”nti. “Natthi, bhante. Yathāpaṭiyattaṃ cīvaraṃ ayyā chabbaggiyā ayyānaṃ chabbaggiyānaṃ pariṇāmesu”nti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū jānaṃ saṅghikaṃ lābhaṃ pariṇataṃ puggalassa pariṇāmessantī”ti…pe… [T 2.0479] saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, jānaṃ saṅghikaṃ lābhaṃ pariṇataṃ puggalassa pariṇāmethāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, jānaṃ saṅghikaṃ lābhaṃ pariṇataṃ puggalassa pariṇāmessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

489. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time in Sāvatthī, a certain association had prepared a meal together with robes for the Saṅgha, thinking, “Having fed them, we will clothe them with robes.” Then the group-of-six monks approached that association. Having approached, they said this to that association: “Friends, give these robes to these monks.” “Venerable sirs, we will not give them. For us, a meal with robes is established annually for the Saṅgha.” “Friends, there are many donors for the Saṅgha, there are many meals for the Saṅgha. These monks dwell here depending on you, looking up to you. If you do not give to them, then who indeed will give to them? Friends, give these robes to these monks.” Then that association, being pressured by the group-of-six monks, gave the robes as prepared to the group-of-six monks and served the Saṅgha with the meal. Those monks who knew that a meal with robes had been prepared for the Saṅgha, but did not know that it had been given to the group-of-six monks, said this: “Friends, present the robes to the Saṅgha.” “There are none, venerable sirs. The venerable group-of-six diverted the robes as prepared to the venerable group-of-six.” Those monks who were of few wishes… they criticized, complained, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the group-of-six monks, knowing, divert to an individual a gain belonging to and dedicated to the Saṅgha?” … “Is it true, as is said, monks, that you, knowing, diverted to an individual a gain belonging to and dedicated to the Saṅgha?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “Worthless men, how indeed could you, knowing, divert to an individual a gain belonging to and dedicated to the Saṅgha? Worthless men, this is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:”

490. “Yo pana bhikkhu jānaṃ saṅghikaṃ lābhaṃ pariṇataṃ puggalassa pariṇāmeyya, pācittiya”nti.

490. “Whatever monk, knowing, should divert to an individual a gain belonging to and dedicated to the Saṅgha, it is an offense of expiation.”

491. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

491. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever kind… ‘Monk’ means: …in this context, this is the monk who is intended.

Jānāti nāma sāmaṃ vā jānāti, aññe vā tassa ārocenti, so vā āroceti.

‘Knows’ means: he knows by himself, or others tell him, or the donor tells him.

Saṅghikaṃ [V 0.0208] nāma saṅghassa dinnaṃ hoti pariccattaṃ.

‘Belonging to the Saṅgha’ means: it has been given to the Saṅgha, it has been relinquished.

Lābho nāma cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā, antamaso cuṇṇapiṇḍopi, dantakaṭṭhampi, dasikasuttampi.

‘Gain’ means: robes, almsfood, lodging, requisites for the sick, and medicines; at the very least, even a lump of cosmetic powder, a tooth-stick, or a bit of thread.

Pariṇataṃ nāma “dassāma karissāmā”ti vācā bhinnā hoti, taṃ puggalassa pariṇāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Dedicated’ means the words, “We will give,” or “We will do,” have been uttered. If one diverts that gain to an individual, one commits an offense of expiation.

492. Pariṇate pariṇatasaññī puggalassa pariṇāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Pariṇate vematiko puggalassa pariṇāmeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Pariṇate apariṇatasaññī puggalassa pariṇāmeti, anāpatti. Saṅghassa pariṇataṃ aññasaṅghassa vā cetiyassa vā pariṇāmeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Cetiyassa pariṇataṃ aññacetiyassa [T 2.0480] vā saṅghassa vā puggalassa vā pariṇāmeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Puggalassa pariṇataṃ aññapuggalassa vā saṅghassa vā cetiyassa vā pariṇāmeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa[M 0.0205]. Apariṇate pariṇatasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Apariṇate vematiko[P 4.0157], āpatti dukkaṭassa. Apariṇate apariṇatasaññī, anāpatti.

492. When it is dedicated, perceiving that it is dedicated, if he diverts it to an individual, it is an offense of expiation. When it is dedicated, being doubtful, if he diverts it to an individual, it is an offense of wrong conduct. When it is dedicated, perceiving that it is not dedicated, if he diverts it to an individual, there is no offense. If he diverts a gain dedicated to the Saṅgha to another Saṅgha or to a cetiya, it is an offense of wrong conduct. If he diverts a gain dedicated to a cetiya to another cetiya, or to the Saṅgha, or to an individual, it is an offense of wrong conduct. If he diverts a gain dedicated to an individual to another individual, or to the Saṅgha, or to a cetiya, it is an offense of wrong conduct. When it is not dedicated, if he perceives it as dedicated, it is an offense of wrong conduct. When it is not dedicated, if he is doubtful, it is an offense of wrong conduct. When it is not dedicated, if he perceives it as not dedicated, there is no offense.

493. Anāpatti – “kattha demā”ti pucchīyamāno – “yattha tumhākaṃ deyyadhammo paribhogaṃ vā labheyya paṭisaṅkhāraṃ vā labheyya ciraṭṭhitiko vā assa yattha vā pana tumhākaṃ cittaṃ pasīdati tattha dethā”ti bhaṇati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

493. There is no offense: when asked, “To whom should we give?” if he says, “Give where your gift might be used, or might be repaired, or might be long-lasting, or else where your mind has confidence”; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Pariṇāmanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dvādasamaṃ.

The twelfth training rule on diversion is finished.

Sahadhammikavaggo aṭṭhamo.

The eighth chapter, the Sahadhammika Vagga, is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of it:

Sahadhamma-vivaṇṇañca, mohāpanaṃ pahārakaṃ;

Talasatti amūlañca, sañcicca ca upassuti;

Paṭibāhanachandañca, dabbañca pariṇāmananti.

With the Dhamma, disparagement, causing bewilderment, and striking; Raising the hand, groundless, intentional, and eavesdropping; Obstruction, consent, Dabba, and diversion.

9. Ratanavaggo

9. The Chapter on Jewels

1. Antepurasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The Training Rule Concerning the Inner Apartments

494. Tena [T 2.0481][V 0.0209] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena rājā pasenadi kosalo uyyānapālaṃ āṇāpesi – “gaccha, bhaṇe, uyyānaṃ sodhehi. Uyyānaṃ gamissāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho so uyyānapālo rañño pasenadissa kosalassa paṭissutvā uyyānaṃ sodhento addasa bhagavantaṃ aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisinnaṃ. Disvāna yena rājā pasenadi kosalo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ etadavoca – “suddhaṃ, deva, uyyānaṃ. Apica, bhagavā tattha nisinno”ti. “Hotu, bhaṇe! Mayaṃ bhagavantaṃ payirupāsissāmā”ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo uyyānaṃ gantvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro upāsako bhagavantaṃ payirupāsanto nisinno hoti. Addasā kho rājā pasenadi kosalo taṃ upāsakaṃ bhagavantaṃ payirupāsantaṃ nisinnaṃ. Disvāna bhīto aṭṭhāsi. Atha kho rañño pasenadissa kosalassa etadahosi – “nārahatāyaṃ puriso pāpo hotuṃ[M 0.0206], yathā bhagavantaṃ payirupāsatī”ti. Yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Atha kho so upāsako bhagavato gāravena rājānaṃ [P 4.0158] pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ neva abhivādesi na paccuṭṭhāsi. Atha kho rājā pasenadi [T 2.0482] kosalo anattamano ahosi – “kathañhi nāmāyaṃ puriso mayi āgate neva abhivādessati na paccuṭṭhessatī”ti! Atha kho bhagavā rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ anattamanaṃ viditvā rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ etadavoca – “eso kho, mahārāja, upāsako bahussuto āgatāgamo kāmesu vītarāgo”ti. Atha kho rañño pasenadissa kosalassa etadahosi – “nārahatāyaṃ upāsako orako hotuṃ, bhagavāpi imassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsatī”ti. Taṃ upāsakaṃ etadavoca – “vadeyyāsi, upāsaka, yena attho”ti. “Suṭṭhu, devā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

494. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, King Pasenadi of Kosala ordered his park-keeper: “Go, good fellow, clean the park. We will visit the park.” “Yes, Your Majesty,” replied the park-keeper to King Pasenadi of Kosala. While cleaning the park, he saw the Blessed One seated at the foot of a certain tree. Having seen him, he approached King Pasenadi of Kosala and said: “The park is clean, Your Majesty. Moreover, the Blessed One is seated there.” “Very well, good fellow! We shall attend upon the Blessed One.” Then King Pasenadi of Kosala went to the park and approached the Blessed One. Now at that time, a certain lay follower was seated, attending upon the Blessed One. King Pasenadi of Kosala saw that lay follower seated, attending upon the Blessed One. Upon seeing him, he was afraid and stood there. Then it occurred to King Pasenadi of Kosala: “This man cannot be wicked, in the way that he attends upon the Blessed One.” He approached the Blessed One, paid homage to the Blessed One, and sat down to one side. Then that lay follower, out of reverence for the Blessed One, neither paid homage to King Pasenadi of Kosala nor rose to greet him. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala became displeased: “How is it that this man, when I have arrived, neither pays homage nor rises to greet me?” Then the Blessed One, knowing that King Pasenadi of Kosala was displeased, said to him: “This lay follower, great king, is very learned, versed in tradition, and free from lust for sensual pleasures.” Then it occurred to King Pasenadi of Kosala: “This lay follower cannot be insignificant, since even the Blessed One speaks his praise.” He said to that lay follower: “Speak, lay follower, of what you need.” “Very well, Your Majesty.” Then the Blessed One instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened King Pasenadi of Kosala with a Dhamma talk. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala, having been instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him respectfully, and departed.

495. Tena [V 0.0210] kho pana samayena rājā pasenadi kosalo uparipāsādavaragato hoti. Addasā kho rājā pasenadi kosalo taṃ upāsakaṃ rathikāya rathiyāya (itipi) chattapāṇiṃ gacchantaṃ. Disvāna pakkosāpetvā etadavoca – “tvaṃ kira, upāsaka, bahussuto āgatāgamo. Sādhu, upāsaka, amhākaṃ itthāgāraṃ dhammaṃ vācehī”ti. “Yamahaṃ yampāhaṃ (sī.), deva, jānāmi ayyānaṃ vāhasā, ayyāva devassa itthāgāraṃ dhammaṃ vācessantī”ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo – “saccaṃ kho upāsako āhā”ti yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā [T 2.0483] ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu, bhante, bhagavā ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ āṇāpetu yo amhākaṃ itthāgāraṃ dhammaṃ vācessatī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi…pe… padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “tenahānanda, rañño itthāgāraṃ dhammaṃ vācehī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato [M 0.0207] paṭissutvā kālena kālaṃ pavisitvā rañño itthāgāraṃ dhammaṃ vāceti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena rañño pasenadissa kosalassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami.

495. At that time, King Pasenadi of Kosala was on the excellent upper palace. He saw that lay follower walking along the street with a parasol in hand. Having seen him, the king summoned him and said, “It is said, lay follower, that you are learned and versed in tradition. Good, lay follower, please teach the Dhamma to our women’s quarters.” “Your Majesty, what Dhamma I know, I know on account of the noble ones. The noble ones themselves should teach the Dhamma to Your Majesty's women's quarters.” Then King Pasenadi of Kosala, thinking, “The lay follower speaks the truth,” approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Blessed One, “Good, venerable sir, may the Blessed One appoint a monk who will teach the Dhamma to our women’s quarters.” Then the Blessed One instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened King Pasenadi of Kosala with a Dhamma talk… Having circumambulated him respectfully, he departed. Then the Blessed One addressed Venerable Ānanda: “Well then, Ānanda, teach the Dhamma to the king’s women’s quarters.” “Yes, venerable sir,” Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. Entering from time to time, he taught the Dhamma to the king’s women’s quarters. Then Venerable Ānanda, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, went to the residence of King Pasenadi of Kosala.

496. Tena kho pana samayena rājā pasenadi kosalo mallikāya deviyā saddhiṃ sayanagato hoti. Addasā kho mallikā devī āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna sahasā vuṭṭhāsi; pītakamaṭṭhaṃ [P 4.0159] dussaṃ pabhassittha. Atha kho āyasmā ānando tatova paṭinivattitvā ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā ānando pubbe appaṭisaṃvidito rañño antepuraṃ pavisissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ [T 2.0484] kira tvaṃ, ānanda, pubbe appaṭisaṃvidito rañño antepuraṃ pavisasīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, ānanda, pubbe appaṭisaṃvidito rañño antepuraṃ pavisissasi! Netaṃ, ānanda, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

496. At that time, King Pasenadi of Kosala was in the bedchamber with Queen Mallikā. Queen Mallikā saw Venerable Ānanda coming from afar. Having seen him, she quickly got up, and her smooth yellow cloth slipped off. Then Venerable Ānanda turned back from that very spot, went to the monastery, and informed the monks about this matter. Those monks who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and disparaged him: “How could Venerable Ānanda enter the king’s inner palace without prior notice?”… “Is it true, Ānanda, that you entered the king’s inner palace without prior notice?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “How could you, Ānanda, enter the king’s inner palace without prior notice! This, Ānanda, is not for inspiring faith in the uninspired…” Having rebuked him… he gave a Dhamma talk and addressed the monks:

497. a. ni. 10.45 “Dasayime, bhikkhave, ādīnavā rājantepurappavesane. Katame dasa? Idha, bhikkhave, rājā mahesiyā saddhiṃ nisinno hoti, tattha bhikkhu pavisati. Mahesī vā bhikkhuṃ disvā sitaṃ pātukaroti. Bhikkhu vā mahesiṃ disvā sitaṃ pātukaroti. Tattha rañño evaṃ hoti – “addhā imesaṃ kataṃ vā karissanti vā”ti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane.

497. “Monks, there are these ten drawbacks in entering the royal inner palace. What ten? Here, monks, a king is sitting with his chief queen, and a monk enters. The chief queen, seeing the monk, might smile. Or the monk, seeing the chief queen, might smile. Then it occurs to the king: ‘Surely, these two have committed a wrongful act, or will do so.’ This, monks, is the first drawback in entering the royal inner palace.

“Puna [V 0.0211] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, rājā bahukicco bahukaraṇīyo. Aññataraṃ itthiṃ gantvā nassarati. Sā tena gabbhaṃ gaṇhi. Tattha rañño evaṃ hoti – “na kho idha añño koci pavisati aññatra pabbajitena. Siyā nu kho pabbajitassa kamma”nti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, dutiyo ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane.

“Furthermore, monks, a king is very busy and has much to do. He goes to a certain woman and then forgets about her. She conceives by him. Then it occurs to the king: ‘No one else enters here except a renunciate. Could this be the renunciate’s doing?’ This, monks, is the second drawback in entering the royal inner palace.”

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, rañño antepure aññataraṃ ratanaṃ nassati. Tattha rañño evaṃ hoti – “na kho idha añño koci pavisati aññatra pabbajitena. Siyā nu kho pabbajitassa kamma”nti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, tatiyo ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane.

“Furthermore, monks, in the king's inner palace, a certain treasure is lost. Then it occurs to the king: ‘No one else enters here except a renunciate. Could this be the renunciate’s doing?’ This, monks, is the third drawback in entering the royal inner palace.”

“Puna [T 2.0485][M 0.0208] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, rañño antepure abbhantarā guyhamantā bahiddhā sambhedaṃ gacchanti. Tattha rañño evaṃ hoti – “na kho idha añño koci pavisati aññatra pabbajitena. Siyā nu kho pabbajitassa kamma”nti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, catuttho ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane.

“Furthermore, monks, in the king's inner palace, secret counsels from within are divulged outside. Then it occurs to the king: ‘No one else enters here except a renunciate. Could this be the renunciate’s doing?’ This, monks, is the fourth drawback in entering the royal inner palace.”

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, rañño antepure putto vā pitaraṃ pattheti pitā vā puttaṃ pattheti. Tesaṃ evaṃ hoti – “na kho idha añño koci pavisati aññatra pabbajitena. Siyā nu kho pabbajitassa kamma”nti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, pañcamo ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane.

“Furthermore, monks, in the king's inner palace, a son desires to kill his father, or a father desires to kill his son. It occurs to them: ‘No one else enters here except a renunciate. Could this be the renunciate’s doing?’ This, monks, is the fifth drawback in entering the royal inner palace.”

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, rājā nīcaṭṭhāniyaṃ ucce ṭhāne ṭhapeti. Yesaṃ taṃ amanāpaṃ tesaṃ evaṃ hoti – “rājā kho pabbajitena saṃsaṭṭho. Siyā nu kho pabbajitassa kamma”nti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, chaṭṭho ādīnavo, rājantepurappavesane.

“Furthermore, monks, a king may appoint a person of low station to a high position. To those for whom this is displeasing, it occurs: ‘The king associates with a renunciate. Could this be the renunciate’s doing?’ This, monks, is the sixth drawback in entering the royal inner palace.”

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, rājā uccaṭṭhāniyaṃ nīce ṭhāne ṭhapeti. Yesaṃ taṃ amanāpaṃ tesaṃ evaṃ hoti – “rājā kho pabbajitena saṃsaṭṭho. Siyā nu kho pabbajitassa kamma”nti. Ayaṃ[P 4.0160], bhikkhave, sattamo ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane.

“Furthermore, monks, a king may place a person of high station in a low position. To those for whom this is displeasing, it occurs: ‘The king associates with a renunciate. Could this be the renunciate’s doing?’ This, monks, is the seventh drawback in entering the royal inner palace.”

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, rājā akāle senaṃ uyyojeti. Yesaṃ taṃ amanāpaṃ tesaṃ evaṃ hoti – “rājā kho pabbajitena saṃsaṭṭho. Siyā nu kho pabbajitassa kamma”nti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, aṭṭhamo ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane.

“Furthermore, monks, a king sends out the army at an untimely moment. To those for whom this is displeasing, it occurs: ‘The king associates with a renunciate. Could this be the renunciate’s doing?’ This, monks, is the eighth drawback in entering the royal inner palace.”

“Puna [T 2.0486][V 0.0212] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, rājā kāle senaṃ uyyojetvā antarāmaggato nivattāpeti. Yesaṃ taṃ amanāpaṃ tesaṃ evaṃ hoti – “‘rājā kho pabbajitena saṃsaṭṭho. Siyā nu kho pabbajitassa kamma”nti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, navamo ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane.

“Furthermore, monks, a king, having sent out an army at the right time, orders it to turn back from midway. To those for whom this is displeasing, it occurs: ‘The king associates with a renunciate. Could this be the renunciate’s doing?’ This, monks, is the ninth drawback in entering the royal inner palace.”

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, rañño rājantepuraṃ hatthisammaddaṃ assasammaddaṃ rathasammaddaṃ rajjanīyāni rajjanīyāni (ka.) rūpasaddagandharasaphoṭṭhabbāni, yāni na pabbajitassa sāruppāni. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, dasamo ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane. Ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa ādīnavā rājantepurappavesane”ti. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ [M 0.0209] anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā dubbharatāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

“Furthermore, monks, the king’s inner palace is crowded with elephants, crowded with horses, and crowded with chariots; there are passion-inciting sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangible objects, which are not suitable for a renunciate. This, monks, is the tenth drawback in entering the king’s inner palace. These, monks, are the ten drawbacks in entering the king’s inner palace.” Then the Blessed One, having rebuked the Venerable Ānanda in many ways for being difficult to support… and so on… “And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

498. “Yo pana bhikkhu rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa muddhābhisittassa (syā.) anikkhantarājake aniggataratanake pubbe appaṭisaṃvidito indakhīlaṃ atikkāmeyya, pācittiya”nti.

498. “Whatever monk, in the case of a consecrated Khattiya king, when the king has not departed and the jewel has not departed, should cross the threshold without having been announced beforehand, it is an offense entailing expiation.”

499. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

499. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever sort… and so on… ‘Monk’ means: …and so on… in this sense, this is the monk who is intended.

Khattiyo nāma ubhato sujāto hoti, mātito ca pitito ca saṃsuddhagahaṇiko, yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakuṭṭho jātivādena.

A Khattiya is one who is well-born on both sides, from his mother and from his father, of pure conception, not rejected and not reproached with regard to birth up to the seventh generation of paternal ancestors.

Muddhāvasitto nāma [T 2.0487] khattiyābhisekena abhisitto hoti.

‘Head-anointed’ means one who has been anointed with the Khattiya consecration.

Anikkhantarājaketi rājā sayanigharā anikkhanto hoti.

‘When the king has not departed’ means the king has not departed from the sleeping chamber.

Aniggataratanaketi mahesī sayanigharā anikkhantā hoti, ubho vā anikkhantā honti.

‘When the jewel has not departed’ means the chief queen has not departed from the sleeping chamber, or both have not departed.

Pubbe appaṭisaṃviditoti pubbe anāmantetvā.

‘Without having been announced beforehand’ means without having informed beforehand.

Indakhīlo nāma sayanigharassa ummāro vuccati.

‘Indra-post’ is said to be the threshold of the sleeping chamber.

Sayanigharaṃ [V 0.0213] nāma yattha katthaci rañño sayanaṃ paññattaṃ hoti, antamaso sāṇipākāraparikkhittampi.

‘Sleeping chamber’ means any place where a bed is prepared for the king, even if it is enclosed only by a hemp-cloth wall.

Indakhīlaṃ atikkāmeyyāti paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ ummāraṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Dutiyaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should cross the threshold’ means: when one causes the first foot to cross the threshold, there is an offense of wrong-doing. When one causes the second foot to cross, there is an offense entailing expiation.

500. Appaṭisaṃvidite appaṭisaṃviditasaññī indakhīlaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Appaṭisaṃvidite vematiko indakhīlaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Appaṭisaṃvidite paṭisaṃviditasaññī indakhīlaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

500. When it has not been announced, if one, perceiving it as not announced, crosses the threshold, there is an offense entailing expiation. When it has not been announced, if one, being uncertain, crosses the threshold, there is an offense entailing expiation. When it has not been announced, if one, perceiving it as announced, crosses the threshold, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Paṭisaṃvidite appaṭisaṃviditasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Paṭisaṃvidite vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Paṭisaṃvidite paṭisaṃviditasaññī, anāpatti.

When it has been announced, if one perceives it as not announced, there is an offense of wrong-doing. When it has been announced, if one is uncertain, there is an offense of wrong-doing. When it has been announced, if one perceives it as announced, there is no offense.

501. Anāpatti [P 4.0161][M 0.0210] paṭisaṃvidite, na khattiyo hoti, na khattiyābhisekena abhisitto hoti, rājā sayanigharā nikkhanto hoti, mahesī sayanigharā nikkhantā hoti, ubho vā nikkhantā honti, na sayanighare, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

501. There is no offense: if it has been made known; if he is not a khattiya; if he has not been consecrated with the royal consecration; if the king has departed from the sleeping chamber; if the chief queen has departed from the sleeping chamber; or if both have departed; if it is not in the sleeping chamber; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Antepurasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The first training rule concerning the inner palace is concluded.

2. Ratanasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Training Rule Concerning Valuables

502. Tena [T 2.0488] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu aciravatiyā nadiyā nahāyati. Aññataropi brāhmaṇo pañcasatānaṃ thavikaṃ thale nikkhipitvā aciravatiyā nadiyā nahāyanto vissaritvā agamāsi. Atha kho so bhikkhu – “tassāyaṃ brāhmaṇassa thavikā, mā idha nassī”ti aggahesi. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo saritvā turito ādhāvitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “api me, bho, thavikaṃ passeyyāsī”ti? “Handa, brāhmaṇā”ti adāsi. Atha kho tassa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – “kena nu kho ahaṃ upāyena imassa bhikkhuno puṇṇapattaṃ na dadeyya”nti! “Na me, bho, pañcasatāni, sahassaṃ me”ti palibundhetvā muñci. Atha kho so bhikkhu ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te [V 0.0214] ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhu ratanaṃ uggahessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, bhikkhu, ratanaṃ uggahesīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, ratanaṃ uggahessasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ [T 2.0489] sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

502. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu was bathing in the Aciravatī River. A certain brahmin also, having placed a bag of five hundred on the bank, forgot it while bathing in the Aciravatī River and went away. Then that bhikkhu took it, thinking, “This is that brahmin’s bag; let it not be lost here.” Then that brahmin, remembering, ran back quickly and said to that bhikkhu, “Sir, did you see my bag?” “Here, brahmin,” he said, and gave it to him. Then this thought occurred to that brahmin: “By what means, I wonder, might I not give this bhikkhu a reward?” He made a false claim, saying, “Sir, mine was not five hundred, mine was a thousand,” and let him go. Then that bhikkhu, having gone to the monastery, related this matter to the bhikkhus. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could a bhikkhu pick up a valuable?”… “Is it true, bhikkhu, that you picked up a valuable?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “How indeed, foolish man, could you pick up a valuable? This, foolish man, is not for inspiring confidence in the uninspired…” And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Yo pana bhikkhu ratanaṃ vā ratanasammataṃ vā uggaṇheyya vā uggaṇhāpeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever bhikkhu should pick up a valuable or what is considered a valuable, or should cause one to be picked up, it is an offense of expiation.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

Thus was this training rule laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

503. Tena kho pana samayena sāvatthiyā ussavo hoti. Manussā alaṅkatappaṭiyattā uyyānaṃ gacchanti. Visākhāpi migāramātā alaṅkatappaṭiyattā [M 0.0211] “uyyānaṃ gamissāmī”ti gāmato [P 4.0162] nikkhamitvā – “kyāhaṃ karissāmi uyyānaṃ gantvā, yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhagavantaṃ payirupāseyya”nti ābharaṇaṃ omuñcitvā uttarāsaṅgena bhaṇḍikaṃ bandhitvā dāsiyā adāsi – “handa, je, imaṃ bhaṇḍikaṃ gaṇhāhī”ti. Atha kho visākhā migāramātā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho visākhaṃ migāramātaraṃ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho visākhā migāramātā bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho sā dāsī taṃ bhaṇḍikaṃ vissaritvā agamāsi. Bhikkhū passitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, uggahetvā nikkhipathā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ratanaṃ vā ratanasammataṃ vā ajjhārāme uggahetvā vā uggahāpetvā vā nikkhipituṃ – “yassa bhavissati [T 2.0490] so harissatī”ti. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

503. Now at that time there was a festival in Sāvatthī. People, adorned and prepared, were going to the park. Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, also adorned and prepared, thought, “I will go to the park.” But after leaving the village, she reconsidered, “What will I do by going to the park? It would be better if I were to attend upon the Blessed One.” So she took off her ornaments, tied them in a bundle with her upper robe, and gave it to her female servant, saying, “Here, girl, take this bundle.” Then Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. The Blessed One instructed, roused, urged, and gladdened Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, who was sitting to one side, with a talk on the Dhamma. Then Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, having been instructed, roused, urged, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a talk on the Dhamma, rose from her seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him respectfully, and departed. Then that female servant forgot the bundle and went away. The bhikkhus saw it and reported the matter to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said, “In that case, bhikkhus, pick it up and set it aside.” Then, on this occasion, in this context, the Blessed One gave a talk on the Dhamma and addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow you to pick up a valuable or what is considered a valuable, or have it picked up, within the monastery and set it aside, thinking, ‘Whoever it belongs to will take it.’ And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:”

“Yo pana bhikkhu ratanaṃ vā ratanasammataṃ vā, aññatra ajjhārāmā, uggaṇheyya vā uggaṇhāpeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever bhikkhu should pick up a valuable or what is considered a valuable, or should cause one to be picked up, outside of a monastery, it is an offense of expiation.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

Thus was this training rule laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

504. Tena [V 0.0215] kho pana samayena kāsīsu janapade anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa kammantagāmo hoti. Tena ca gahapatinā antevāsī āṇatto hoti – “sace bhadantā āgacchanti bhattaṃ kareyyāsī”ti. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū kāsīsu janapade cārikaṃ caramānā yena anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa kammantagāmo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Addasā kho so puriso te bhikkhū dūratova āgacchante. Disvāna yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū abhivādetvā etadavoca – “adhivāsentu, bhante, ayyā svātanāya gahapatino bhatta”nti. Adhivāsesuṃ kho te bhikkhū tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho so puriso tassā rattiyā accayena paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā kālaṃ ārocāpetvā aṅgulimuddikaṃ omuñcitvā te bhikkhū bhattena parivisitvā – “ayyā bhuñjitvā gacchantu, ahampi kammantaṃ gamissāmī”ti aṅgulimuddikaṃ [M 0.0212] vissaritvā agamāsi. Bhikkhū passitvā [P 4.0163] – “sace mayaṃ gamissāma nassissatāyaṃ aṅgulimuddikā”ti tattheva acchiṃsu. Atha kho so puriso kammantā āgacchanto te bhikkhū passitvā etadavoca – “kissa, bhante, ayyā idheva [T 2.0491] acchantī”ti? Atha kho te bhikkhū tassa purisassa etamatthaṃ ārocetvā sāvatthiṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ratanaṃ vā ratanasammataṃ vā ajjhārāme vā ajjhāvasathe vā uggahetvā vā uggahāpetvā vā nikkhipituṃ – yassa bhavissati so harissatī”ti. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

504. Now at that time, in the country of Kāsi, there was a work village belonging to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika. That householder had instructed his attendant: “If the venerable ones come, you should prepare a meal.” Now at that time, many bhikkhus, while wandering on tour in the country of Kāsi, approached the work village of the householder Anāthapiṇḍika. That man saw those bhikkhus coming from a distance. Having seen them, he approached those bhikkhus; having approached, he paid homage to those bhikkhus and said this: “Venerable sirs, may the masters accept the householder’s meal for tomorrow.” Those bhikkhus consented through silence. Then that man, after that night had passed, had fine food, both hard and soft, prepared, had the time announced, took off his signet ring, served those bhikkhus with the meal, and saying, “May the masters eat and then go; I too will go to my work,” he forgot his signet ring and left. The bhikkhus, seeing it, thought: “If we go, this signet ring will be lost,” and they remained right there. Then that man, returning from his work, saw those bhikkhus and said this: “Why, venerable sirs, are the masters still here?” Then those bhikkhus, having explained this matter to that man, went to Sāvatthī and reported this matter to the bhikkhus. The bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow you to pick up a jewel or what is considered a jewel, or have it picked up, within a monastery or within a dwelling, and to put it aside, thinking: ‘Whoever it belongs to will take it.’ And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

505. “Yo pana bhikkhu ratanaṃ vā ratanasammataṃ vā, aññatra ajjhārāmā vā ajjhāvasathā vā, uggaṇheyya vā uggaṇhāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṃ. Ratanaṃ vā pana bhikkhunā ratanasammataṃ vā ajjhārāme vā ajjhāvasathe vā uggahetvā vā uggahāpetvā vā nikkhipitabbaṃ – ‘yassa bhavissati so harissatī’ti. Ayaṃ tattha sāmīcī”ti.

505. “Whatever bhikkhu should pick up or cause to be picked up a jewel or what is considered a jewel, elsewhere than within a monastery or within a dwelling, it is an offense of expiation. Furthermore, a jewel or what is considered a jewel, having been picked up or caused to be picked up by a bhikkhu within a monastery or within a dwelling, should be put aside with the thought: ‘Whoever it belongs to will take it.’ This is the proper conduct in that case.”

506. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

506. ‘Whatever’: whoever, of whatever kind... and so on. ‘Bhikkhu’: ...and so on... in this sense, the bhikkhu who is intended is...

Ratanaṃ nāma muttā maṇi veḷuriyo saṅkho silā pavālaṃ rajataṃ jātarūpaṃ lohitaṅko lohitako (?) masāragallaṃ.

A jewel means: a pearl, a gem, beryl, a conch, crystal, coral, silver, gold, a ruby, a variegated gem.

Ratanasammataṃ [V 0.0216] nāma yaṃ manussānaṃ upabhogaparibhogaṃ, etaṃ ratanasammataṃ nāma.

What is considered a jewel means: whatever is for human use and enjoyment, this is called what is considered a jewel.

Aññatra ajjhārāmā vā ajjhāvasathā vāti ṭhapetvā ajjhārāmaṃ ajjhāvasathaṃ.

‘Elsewhere than within a monastery or within a dwelling’ means setting aside the inside of a monastery and the inside of a dwelling.

Ajjhārāmo nāma parikkhittassa ārāmassa anto ārāmo, aparikkhittassa upacāro.

Within a monastery means: for an enclosed monastery, it is the interior; for an unenclosed one, it is the vicinity.

Ajjhāvasatho nāma parikkhittassa āvasathassa anto [T 2.0492] āvasatho, aparikkhittassa upacāro.

Within a dwelling means: for an enclosed dwelling, it is the interior; for an unenclosed one, it is the vicinity.

Uggaṇheyyāti [M 0.0213] sayaṃ gaṇhāti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should pick up’ means: if he picks it up himself, it is an offense of expiation.

Uggaṇhāpeyyāti aññaṃ gāhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should cause to be picked up’ means: if he causes another to pick it up, it is an offense of expiation.

Ratanaṃ vā pana bhikkhunā ratanasammataṃ vā ajjhārāme vā ajjhāvasathe vā uggahetvā vā uggahāpetvā vā nikkhipitabbanti rūpena vā nimittena vā saññāṇaṃ katvā nikkhipitvā ācikkhitabbaṃ – “yassa bhaṇḍaṃ naṭṭhaṃ so āgacchatū”ti. Sace tattha āgacchati so vattabbo – “āvuso, kīdisaṃ te bhaṇḍa”nti? Sace rūpena vā nimittena vā sampādeti dātabbaṃ, no ce sampādeti “vicināhi āvuso”ti vattabbo. Tamhā āvāsā pakkamantena ye tattha honti bhikkhū patirūpā, tesaṃ hatthe nikkhipitvā [P 4.0164] pakkamitabbaṃ. No ce honti bhikkhū patirūpā, ye tattha honti gahapatikā patirūpā, tesaṃ hatthe nikkhipitvā pakkamitabbaṃ.

‘A jewel or what is considered a jewel, having been picked up or caused to be picked up by a bhikkhu within a monastery or within a dwelling, should be put aside’ means: having made a mark by its form or by a sign, and having put it aside, it should be announced: “Let him whose property is lost come.” If he comes there, he should be asked: “Friend, what is your property like?” If he identifies it by its form or by a sign, it should be given. If he does not identify it, he should be told: “Friend, please search.” A bhikkhu departing from that residence should, having placed it in the hands of whatever suitable bhikkhus are there, depart. If there are no suitable bhikkhus, he should, having placed it in the hands of whatever suitable householders are there, depart.

Ayaṃ tattha sāmīcīti ayaṃ tattha anudhammatā.

‘This is the proper conduct in that case’ means: this is the conduct in accordance with the Dhamma in that case.

507. Anāpatti ratanaṃ vā ratanasammataṃ vā ajjhārāme vā ajjhāvasathe vā uggahetvā vā uggahāpetvā vā nikkhipati – “yassa bhavissati so harissatī”ti, ratanasammataṃ vissāsaṃ gaṇhāti, tāvakālikaṃ gaṇhāti, paṃsukūlasaññissa, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

507. There is no offense if one picks up or causes to be picked up a jewel or what is considered a jewel within a monastery or within a dwelling and puts it aside, thinking, ‘Whoever it belongs to will take it.’ There is no offense if one takes what is considered a jewel trustingly, if one takes it temporarily, for one who perceives it as a refuse-rag, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Ratanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The second training rule concerning jewels is concluded.

3. Vikālagāmappavisanasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Training Rule on Entering a Village at an Improper Time

508. Tena [T 2.0493][V 0.0217] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū vikāle gāmaṃ pavisitvā sabhāyaṃ nisīditvā anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ kathenti, seyyathidaṃ – imā tiracchānakathāyo dī. 1.17; ma. ni. 2.223; saṃ. ni.[T 5.1080]; a. ni. 10.69 rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ mahāmattakathaṃ senākathaṃ bhayakathaṃ yuddhakathaṃ annakathaṃ pānakathaṃ vatthakathaṃ sayanakathaṃ mālākathaṃ gandhakathaṃ ñātikathaṃ yānakathaṃ gāmakathaṃ nigamakathaṃ nagarakathaṃ janapadakathaṃ itthikathaṃ itthikathaṃ purisakathaṃ (ka.) majjhimapaṇṇāsaṭṭhakathā 156 piṭṭhe oloketabbā sūrakathaṃ visikhākathaṃ kumbhaṭṭhānakathaṃ pubbapetakathaṃ nānattakathaṃ [M 0.0214] lokakkhāyikaṃ samuddakkhāyikaṃ itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā vikāle gāmaṃ pavisitvā sabhāyaṃ nisīditvā anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ kathessanti, seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ…pe… itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā, seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti!

508. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the monks of the group of six, having entered a village at an unseasonable time and sat down in an assembly hall, engaged in various kinds of worldly talk, that is to say: talk about kings, talk about thieves, talk about great ministers, talk about armies, talk about fears, talk about battles, talk about food, talk about drink, talk about clothing, talk about bedding, talk about garlands, talk about scents, talk about relatives, talk about vehicles, talk about villages, talk about market towns, talk about cities, talk about countries, talk about women, talk about heroes, talk about crossroads, talk about watering places, talk about those long dead, various kinds of talk, speculation about the world, speculation about the ocean, and talk of 'thus it prospers, thus it declines.' People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can these ascetics, the sons of the Sakyan, having entered a village at an unseasonable time and sat down in an assembly hall, engage in various kinds of worldly talk—that is to say: talk about kings, talk about thieves… and talk of 'thus it prospers, thus it declines'—just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures?”

Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū vikāle [T 2.0494] gāmaṃ pavisitvā sabhāyaṃ nisīditvā anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ kathessanti, seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ…pe… itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, vikāle gāmaṃ pavisitvā sabhāyaṃ nisīditvā anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ kathetha, seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ…pe… itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, vikāle gāmaṃ pavisitvā sabhāyaṃ nisīditvā anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ kathessatha, seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ…pe… itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those monks who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the monks of the group of six, having entered a village at an unseasonable time and sat down in an assembly hall, engage in various kinds of worldly talk, that is to say: talk about kings, talk about thieves… and talk of 'thus it prospers, thus it declines'?”… “Is it true, monks, it is said, that having entered a village at an unseasonable time and sat down in an assembly hall, you engage in various kinds of worldly talk, that is to say: talk about kings, talk about thieves… and talk of 'thus it prospers, thus it declines'?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed can you, foolish men, having entered a village at an unseasonable time and sat down in an assembly hall, engage in various kinds of worldly talk, that is to say: talk about kings, talk about thieves… and talk of 'thus it prospers, thus it declines'! This, foolish men, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

“Yo [P 4.0165] pana bhikkhu vikāle gāmaṃ paviseyya, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever bhikkhu should enter a village at an unseasonable time, it is a pācittiya.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

Thus this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.

509. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū kosalesu janapade sāvatthiṃ gacchantā sāyaṃ aññataraṃ gāmaṃ upagacchiṃsu. Manussā te bhikkhū passitvā etadavocuṃ – “pavisatha, bhante”ti[V 0.0218]. Atha kho te bhikkhū – “bhagavatā paṭikkhittaṃ vikāle gāmaṃ pavisitu”nti kukkuccāyantā na pavisiṃsu. Corā te bhikkhū acchindiṃsu. Atha kho te bhikkhū sāvatthiṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āpucchā [T 2.0495] vikāle gāmaṃ pavisituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

509. Now at that time, many monks traveling through the Kosalan country towards Sāvatthī approached a certain village in the evening. Seeing the monks, the people said this, “Enter, venerable sirs.” But those monks, being scrupulous and thinking, “Entering a village at an unseasonable time has been forbidden by the Blessed One,” did not enter. Thieves robbed those monks. Then those monks, having gone to Sāvatthī, informed the monks of this matter. The monks informed the Blessed One of this matter. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a discourse on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: “I allow, monks, to enter a village at an unseasonable time after having asked permission. And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

“Yo [M 0.0215] pana bhikkhu anāpucchā vikāle gāmaṃ paviseyya, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever bhikkhu should enter a village at an unseasonable time without having asked permission, it is a pācittiya.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

Thus this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.

510. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu kosalesu janapade sāvatthiṃ gacchanto sāyaṃ aññataraṃ gāmaṃ upagacchi. Manussā taṃ bhikkhuṃ passitvā etadavocuṃ – “pavisatha, bhante”ti. Atha kho so bhikkhu – “bhagavatā paṭikkhittaṃ anāpucchā vikāle gāmaṃ pavisitu”nti kukkuccāyanto na pāvisi. Corā taṃ bhikkhuṃ acchindiṃsu. Atha kho so bhikkhu sāvatthiṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, santaṃ bhikkhuṃ āpucchā vikāle gāmaṃ pavisituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

510. Now at that time, a certain monk, while traveling through the Kosalan country towards Sāvatthī, approached a certain village in the evening. The people, seeing that monk, said this, “Enter, venerable sir.” Then that monk, being scrupulous and thinking, “The Blessed One has forbidden entering a village at an unseasonable time without having asked permission,” did not enter. Thieves robbed that monk. Then that monk, having gone to Sāvatthī, informed the monks of this matter. The monks informed the Blessed One of this matter. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a discourse on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: “I allow, monks, to enter a village at an unseasonable time after having asked permission of a monk who is present. And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

“Yo pana bhikkhu santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā vikāle gāmaṃ paviseyya, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever bhikkhu should enter a village at an unseasonable time without having asked permission of a monk who is present, it is a pācittiya.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

Thus this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.

511. Tena [P 4.0166] kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu ahinā daṭṭho hoti. Aññataro bhikkhu “aggiṃ āharissāmī”ti gāmaṃ gacchati. Atha kho so bhikkhu – “bhagavatā paṭikkhittaṃ santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā vikāle gāmaṃ pavisitu”nti kukkuccāyanto na pāvisi…pe… bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[T 2.0496]. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tathārūpe accāyike [V 0.0219] karaṇīye santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā vikāle gāmaṃ pavisituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

511. At that time, a certain monk had been bitten by a snake. Another monk went to the village, thinking, “I will bring fire.” Then that monk, being scrupulous and thinking, “The Blessed One has forbidden entering a village at an unseasonable time without having asked permission of a monk who is present,” did not enter… They reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a discourse on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: “I allow, monks, when there is such an urgent matter to be done, to enter a village at an unseasonable time without having asked permission of a monk who is present. And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

512. “Yo pana bhikkhu santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā vikāle gāmaṃ paviseyya, aññatra tathārūpā accāyikā karaṇīyā, pācittiya”nti.

512. “Whatever bhikkhu, without asking permission of an available monk, should enter a village at an unseasonable time, unless there is such an urgent matter to be done, it is a pācittiya.”

513. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

513. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever sort... ‘Monk’ means: ...in this sense, this is the monk who is intended.

Santo [M 0.0216] nāma bhikkhu sakkā hoti āpucchā pavisituṃ.

‘Available’ means: a monk whom it is possible to inform before entering.

Asanto nāma bhikkhu na sakkā hoti āpucchā pavisituṃ.

‘Unavailable’ means: a monk whom it is not possible to inform before entering.

Vikālo nāma majjhanhike vītivatte yāva aruṇuggamanā.

‘Unseasonable time’ means: from when midday has passed until the rising of the dawn.

Gāmaṃ paviseyyāti parikkhittassa gāmassa parikkhepaṃ atikkamantassa āpatti pācittiyassa. Aparikkhittassa gāmassa upacāraṃ okkamantassa āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should enter a village’ means: for one who crosses the enclosure of an enclosed village, there is an offense of expiation. For one who steps into the precincts of an unenclosed village, there is an offense of expiation.

Aññatra tathārūpā accāyikā karaṇīyāti ṭhapetvā tathārūpaṃ accāyikaṃ karaṇīyaṃ.

‘Unless there is such an urgent matter to be done’ means: setting aside such an urgent matter to be done.

514. Vikāle vikālasaññī santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā gāmaṃ pavisati, aññatra tathārūpā accāyikā karaṇīyā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Vikāle vematiko santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā gāmaṃ pavisati, aññatra tathārūpā accāyikā karaṇīyā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Vikāle kālasaññī santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā gāmaṃ pavisati, aññatra tathārūpā accāyikā karaṇīyā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

514. If, at an unseasonable time, perceiving it as an unseasonable time, he enters a village without informing an available monk, unless there is such an urgent matter to be done, there is an offense of expiation. If, at an unseasonable time, being uncertain, he enters a village without informing an available monk, unless there is such an urgent matter to be done, there is an offense of expiation. If, at an unseasonable time, perceiving it as the seasonable time, he enters a village without informing an available monk, unless there is such an urgent matter to be done, there is an offense of expiation.

Kāle vikālasaññī[T 2.0497], āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāle vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāle kālasaññī, anāpatti.

If at the seasonable time, he perceives it as an unseasonable time, there is an offense of wrong conduct. If at the seasonable time, he is uncertain, there is an offense of wrong conduct. If at the seasonable time, he perceives it as the seasonable time, there is no offense.

515. Anāpatti tathārūpe accāyike karaṇīye, santaṃ bhikkhuṃ āpucchā pavisati, asantaṃ [V 0.0220] bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā pavisati, antarārāmaṃ gacchati, bhikkhunupassayaṃ gacchati, titthiyaseyyaṃ gacchati, paṭikkamanaṃ gacchati, gāmena maggo hoti, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

515. There is no offense: if there is such an urgent matter to be done; if he enters after informing an available monk; if he enters without informing an unavailable monk; if he goes between monasteries; if he goes to a bhikkhunī's residence; if he goes to a sectarian's lodging; if he goes to a rest house; if the path goes through the village; in times of danger; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Vikālagāmappavisanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The third training rule, on entering a village at an unseasonable time, is concluded.

4. Sūcigharasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Training Rule on the Needle-Case

516. Tena [T 2.0498][P 4.0167] samayena buddho bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarena dantakārena bhikkhū pavāritā honti – “yesaṃ ayyānaṃ sūcigharena attho [M 0.0217] ahaṃ sūcigharenā”ti. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū bahū sūcighare viññāpenti. Yesaṃ khuddakā sūcigharā te mahante sūcighare viññāpenti. Yesaṃ mahantā sūcigharā te khuddake sūcighare viññāpenti. Atha kho so dantakāro bhikkhūnaṃ bahū sūcighare karonto na sakkoti aññaṃ vikkāyikaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ kātuṃ, attanāpi na yāpeti, puttadāropissa kilamati. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā na mattaṃ jānitvā bahū sūcighare viññāpessanti! Ayaṃ imesaṃ bahū sūcighare karonto na sakkoti aññaṃ vikkāyikaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ kātuṃ, attanāpi na yāpeti, puttadāropissa kilamatī”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhū na mattaṃ jānitvā bahū sūcighare viññāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na mattaṃ jānitvā bahū sūcighare viññāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā na mattaṃ [T 2.0499] jānitvā bahū sūcighare viññāpessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

516. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery. Now at that time, a certain ivory-worker had invited the monks, saying, “Whatever venerable ones have need of a needle-case, I invite them with a needle-case.” Then at that time, the monks requested many needle-cases. Those who had small needle-cases requested large ones. Those who had large needle-cases requested small ones. Then that ivory-worker, while making many needle-cases for the monks, was not able to make other saleable goods. He could not support himself, and his wife and children were also weary. People complained, criticized, and spread ill-repute, saying, “How can these Sakyan recluses, not knowing moderation, request so many needle-cases? While this man is making many needle-cases for them, he is not able to make other saleable goods. He cannot support himself, and his wife and children are also weary.” The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading ill-repute. Those monks who were of few wishes... complained, criticized, and spread ill-repute, saying, “How can the monks, not knowing moderation, request so many needle-cases?” ... “Is it true, monks, that monks, not knowing moderation, request many needle-cases?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... “How can those foolish men, not knowing moderation, request so many needle-cases? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced...” “And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

517. “Yo pana bhikkhu aṭṭhimayaṃ vā dantamayaṃ vā visāṇamayaṃ vā sūcigharaṃ kārāpeyya bhedanakaṃ, pācittiya”nti.

517. “Whatever monk should have a needle-case made of bone, or of ivory, or of horn, it is an offense of expiation requiring it to be broken.”

518. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

518. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever sort... ‘Monk’ means: ...in this sense, this is the monk who is intended.

Aṭṭhi [V 0.0221] nāma yaṃ kiñci aṭṭhi.

‘Bone’ means: any bone whatsoever.

Danto nāma hatthidanto vuccati.

‘Ivory’ means elephant tusk.

Visāṇaṃ nāma yaṃ kiñci visāṇaṃ.

‘Horn’ means: any horn whatsoever.

Kārāpeyyāti karoti vā kārāpeti vā, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena bhinditvā pācittiyaṃ desetabbaṃ.
