‘Should have made’ means: he makes it or has it made. In the effort, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Upon receiving it, it should be broken and the offense of expiation should be confessed.

519. Attanā vippakataṃ attanā pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Attanā vippakataṃ parehi pariyosāpeti pariyosāvāpeti (ka.), āpatti pācittiyassa[M 0.0218]. Parehi vippakataṃ attanā pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Parehi [P 4.0168] vippakataṃ parehi pariyosāpeti pariyosāvāpeti (ka.), āpatti pācittiyassa.

519. If he himself finishes what was started by himself, there is an offense of expiation. If he has others finish what was started by himself, there is an offense of expiation. If he himself finishes what was started by others, there is an offense of expiation. If he has others finish what was started by others, there is an offense of expiation.

Aññassatthāya karoti vā kārāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Aññena kataṃ paṭilabhitvā paribhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If he makes it or has it made for the sake of another, there is an offense of wrong conduct. If, having received what was made by another, he uses it, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

520. Anāpatti gaṇṭhikāya gaṇḍikāya (syā.), araṇike, vidhe vīṭhe (sī.), vīthe (syā.), añjaniyā, añjanisalākāya, vāsijaṭe, udakapuñchaniyā, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

520. There is no offense: regarding a toggle, a fire-drill, a belt-buckle, a collyrium container, a collyrium stick, an adze handle, or a water-wiper; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Sūcigharasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.

The fourth training rule, on the needle-case, is concluded.

5. Mañcapīṭhasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Training Rule on Beds and Chairs

521. Tena [T 2.0500] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā upanando sakyaputto ucce mañce sayati. Atha kho bhagavā sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ senāsanacārikaṃ āhiṇḍanto yenāyasmato upanandassa sakyaputtassa vihāro tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho āyasmā upanando sakyaputto bhagavantaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “āgacchatu me, bhante, bhagavā sayanaṃ passatū”ti. Atha kho bhagavā tatova paṭinivattitvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “āsayato, bhikkhave, moghapuriso [V 0.0222] veditabbo”ti. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā dubbharatāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

521. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. At that time, the venerable Upananda the Sakyan was lying on a high bed. Then the Blessed One, while wandering on a tour of the lodgings together with many bhikkhus, approached the dwelling of the venerable Upananda the Sakyan. The venerable Upananda the Sakyan saw the Blessed One coming from afar. Having seen him, he said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One come. May he see my bed.” Then the Blessed One, having turned back from there, addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, a foolish man is to be known by his disposition.” Then the Blessed One, having rebuked the venerable Upananda the Sakyan in many ways for being difficult to support… and so on… “And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:”

522. “Navaṃ pana bhikkhunā mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā kārayamānena aṭṭhaṅgulapādakaṃ kāretabbaṃ sugataṅgulena, aññatra heṭṭhimāya aṭaniyā; taṃ atikkāmayato chedanakaṃ pācittiya”nti.

522. “When a bhikkhu is having a new bed or chair made, it should be made with legs of eight finger-breadths, by the Sugata’s finger-breadth, excluding the lower crosspiece. For one who exceeds that, there is a pācittiya offense entailing cutting.”

523. Navaṃ nāma karaṇaṃ upādāya vuccati.

523. ‘New’ is so called in dependence on its making.

Mañco [M 0.0219] nāma cattāro mañcā – masārako, bundikābaddho, kuḷīrapādako, āhaccapādako.

‘A bed’ means four kinds of beds: one with fixed legs, one bound with plaited straps, one with curved legs, and one with detachable legs.

Pīṭhaṃ nāma cattāri pīṭhāni – masārakaṃ, bundikābaddhaṃ, kuḷīrapādakaṃ, āhaccapādakaṃ.

‘A chair’ means four kinds of chairs: one with fixed legs, one bound with plaited straps, one with curved legs, and one with detachable legs.

Kārayamānenāti karonto vā kārāpento vā.

‘Having it made’ means making it oneself or having another make it.

Aṭṭhaṅgulapādakaṃ [T 2.0501] kāretabbaṃ sugataṅgulena, aññatra heṭṭhimāya [P 4.0169] aṭaniyāti ṭhapetvā heṭṭhimaṃ aṭaniṃ; taṃ atikkāmetvā karoti vā kārāpeti vā, payoge dukkaṭaṃ, paṭilābhena chinditvā pācittiyaṃ desetabbaṃ.

‘It should be made with legs of eight finger-breadths, by the Sugata’s finger-breadth, excluding the lower crosspiece’: this means excluding the lower crosspiece. If one makes it or has it made exceeding that, there is a dukkaṭa offense for the effort. Upon receiving it, having cut it, the pācittiya offense should be confessed.

524. Attanā vippakataṃ attanā pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Attanā vippakataṃ parehi pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Parehi vippakataṃ attanā pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Parehi vippakataṃ parehi pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

524. If one finishes by oneself what was left unfinished by oneself, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one has others finish what was left unfinished by oneself, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one finishes by oneself what was left unfinished by others, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one has others finish what was left unfinished by others, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Aññassatthāya karoti vā kārāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Aññena kataṃ paṭilabhitvā paribhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one makes it or has it made for the sake of another, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If, having received what was made by another, one uses it, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

525. Anāpatti pamāṇikaṃ karoti, ūnakaṃ karoti, aññena kataṃ pamāṇātikkantaṃ paṭilabhitvā chinditvā paribhuñjati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

525. There is no offense: if one makes it to the correct measure, if one makes it smaller; if, having received what was made by another exceeding the measure, one uses it after cutting it; for one who is insane, for the first offender.

Mañcapīṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Fifth Training Rule on Beds and Chairs is finished.

6. Tūlonaddhasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Training Rule on Cotton-Stuffed Articles

526. Tena [T 2.0502][V 0.0223] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū mañcampi pīṭhampi tūlonaddhaṃ kārāpenti. Manussā vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā mañcampi pīṭhampi tūlonaddhaṃ kārāpessanti, seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti[M 0.0220]! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū mañcampi pīṭhampi tūlonaddhaṃ kārāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, mañcampi pīṭhampi tūlonaddhaṃ kārāpethāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, mañcampi pīṭhampi tūlonaddhaṃ kārāpessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

526. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. At that time the group-of-six bhikkhus were having beds and chairs stuffed with cotton made. People wandering on a tour of the monastery saw this and complained, criticized, and grumbled: “How can these Sakyan ascetics have beds and chairs stuffed with cotton made, just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures?” The bhikkhus heard these people complaining, criticizing, and grumbling. Those bhikkhus who were modest… and so on… they complained, criticized, and grumbled: “How can the group-of-six bhikkhus have beds and chairs stuffed with cotton made?”… and so on… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that you are having beds and chairs stuffed with cotton made?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… and so on… “How can you, foolish men, have beds and chairs stuffed with cotton made? This is not, foolish men, for inspiring confidence in the unfaithful… and so on… And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:”

527. “Yo pana bhikkhu mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā tūlonaddhaṃ kārāpeyya, uddālanakaṃ pācittiya”nti.

527. “Should any bhikkhu have a bed or chair stuffed with cotton made, it is a pācittiya offense requiring the removal of the stuffing.”

528. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

528. ‘Any’ means whoever… and so on… ‘bhikkhu’ means… and so on… this refers to the bhikkhu who is intended in this context.

Mañco nāma cattāro mañcā – masārako, bundikābaddho, kuḷīrapādako, āhaccapādako.

‘A bed’ means four kinds of beds: one with fixed legs, one bound with plaited straps, one with curved legs, and one with detachable legs.

Pīṭhaṃ [T 2.0503] nāma cattāri pīṭhāni – masārakaṃ, bundikābaddhaṃ, kuḷīrapādakaṃ, āhaccapādakaṃ.

‘A chair’ means four kinds of chairs: one with fixed legs, one bound with plaited straps, one with curved legs, and one with detachable legs.

Tūlaṃ [P 4.0170] nāma tīṇi tūlāni – rukkhatūlaṃ, latātūlaṃ, poṭakitūlaṃ.

‘Cotton’ means three kinds of cotton: tree cotton, vine cotton, and grass cotton.

Kārāpeyyāti karoti vā kārāpeti vā, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena uddāletvā pācittiyaṃ desetabbaṃ.

‘Should have made’ means one makes it or has it made; there is an offense of wrong-doing for the effort. Upon acquisition, the stuffing must be removed and the pācittiya offense confessed.

529. Attanā [V 0.0224] vippakataṃ attanā pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Attanā vippakataṃ parehi pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Parehi vippakataṃ attanā pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Parehi vippakataṃ parehi pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

529. If one completes by oneself what one has begun oneself, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one has others complete what one has begun oneself, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one completes by oneself what others have begun, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one has others complete what others have begun, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Aññassatthāya karoti vā kārāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Aññena kataṃ paṭilabhitvā paribhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one makes it or has it made for the sake of another, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If, having received one made by another, one uses it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

530. Anāpatti āyoge, kāyabandhane, aṃsabaddhake, pattathavikāya, parissāvane, bibbohanaṃ karoti, aññena kataṃ paṭilabhitvā uddāletvā paribhuñjati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

530. There is no offense: for a meditation strap, a waistband, a shoulder-strap, a bowl-bag, or a water-strainer; if one makes a pillow; if, having received one made by another, one uses it after removing the stuffing; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Tūlonaddhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Sixth Training Rule on Stuffed Articles is finished.

7. Nisīdanasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Training Rule on the Sitting-Cloth

531. Tena [T 2.0504][M 0.0221] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ nisīdanaṃ anuññātaṃ hoti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū – “bhagavatā nisīdanaṃ anuññāta”nti appamāṇikāni nisīdanāni dhārenti. Mañcassapi pīṭhassapi puratopi pacchatopi olambenti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū appamāṇikāni nisīdanāni dhāressantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, appamāṇikāni nisīdanāni dhārethāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, appamāṇikāni nisīdanāni dhāressatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

531. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, a sitting-cloth had been allowed to the monks by the Blessed One. The monks of the group-of-six, thinking, “A sitting-cloth has been allowed by the Blessed One,” used sitting-cloths of limitless size. They let them hang down in front of and behind beds and benches. Those monks who were of few wishes... criticized, found fault, and spread it about, saying, “How indeed can the monks of the group-of-six use sitting-cloths of limitless size?” ... “Is it true, it is said, monks, that you use sitting-cloths of limitless size?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... “Worthless men, how indeed can you use sitting-cloths of limitless size? This, worthless men, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced... And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:”

“Nisīdanaṃ pana bhikkhunā kārayamānena pamāṇikaṃ kāretabbaṃ. Tatridaṃ pamāṇaṃ – dīghaso dve vidatthiyo, sugatavidatthiyā; tiriyaṃ diyaḍḍhaṃ. Taṃ atikkāmayato chedanakaṃ pācittiya”nti.

“A sitting-cloth, when being made by a monk, is to be made to the proper measure. This is the measure for it: in length, two spans by the Sugata-span; in width, one and a half. For one who exceeds this, it is a pācittiya offense that requires cutting.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.

532. Tena [P 4.0171][V 0.0225] kho pana samayena āyasmā udāyī mahākāyo hoti. So bhagavato purato nisīdanaṃ paññapetvā samantato samañchamāno nisīdati. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ etadavoca – “kissa [T 2.0505] tvaṃ, udāyi, nisīdanaṃ samantato samañchasi; seyyathāpi purāṇāsikoṭṭho”ti? “Tathā hi pana, bhante, bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ atikhuddakaṃ nisīdanaṃ anuññāta”nti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, nisīdanassa dasaṃ vidatthiṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

532. Now at that time, the venerable Udāyī was of large body. Having spread a sitting-cloth in front of the Blessed One, he sat down, pulling it in from all around. Then the Blessed One said this to the venerable Udāyī: “Udāyī, why do you pull in the sitting-cloth from all around, just like an old leather-worker?” “It is because, venerable sir, the sitting-cloth allowed to the monks by the Blessed One is too small.” Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow a border of a span for the sitting-cloth. And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:”

533. “Nisīdanaṃ pana bhikkhunā kārayamānena pamāṇikaṃ kāretabbaṃ. Tatridaṃ pamāṇaṃ – dīghaso dve vidatthiyo, sugatavidatthiyā; tiriyaṃ diyaḍḍhaṃ. Dasā vidatthi. Taṃ atikkāmayato chedanakaṃ pācittiya”nti.

533. “A sitting-cloth, when being made by a monk, is to be made to the proper measure. This is the measure for it: in length, two spans by the Sugata-span; in width, one and a half. The border is one span. For one who exceeds this, it is a pācittiya offense that requires cutting.”

534. Nisīdanaṃ nāma sadasaṃ vuccati.

534. A sitting-cloth is defined as that which has a border.

Kārayamānenāti [M 0.0222] karonto vā kārāpento vā pamāṇikaṃ kāretabbaṃ. Tatridaṃ pamāṇaṃ – dīghaso dve vidatthiyo, sugatavidatthiyā; tiriyaṃ diyaḍḍhaṃ. Dasā vidatthi. Taṃ atikkāmetvā karoti vā kārāpeti vā, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena chinditvā pācittiyaṃ desetabbaṃ.

‘Having it made’ means: whether making it oneself or causing another to make it, it is to be made to the proper measure. This is the measure for it: in length, two spans by the Sugata-span; in width, one and a half. The border is one span. Having exceeded that, if one makes it or causes it to be made, there is a dukkaṭa offense in the effort. Upon receiving it, having cut it, the pācittiya offense should be confessed.

535. Attanā vippakataṃ attanā pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Attanā vippakataṃ parehi pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Parehi vippakataṃ attanā pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Parehi vippakataṃ parehi pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

535. If one finishes by oneself what was left unfinished by oneself, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one has others finish what was left unfinished by oneself, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one finishes by oneself what was left unfinished by others, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one has others finish what was left unfinished by others, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Aññassatthāya karoti vā kārāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Aññena kataṃ paṭilabhitvā paribhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one makes it or causes it to be made for the sake of another, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If, having received one made by another, one uses it, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

536. Anāpatti [T 2.0506] pamāṇikaṃ karoti, ūnakaṃ karoti, aññena kataṃ pamāṇātikkantaṃ paṭilabhitvā chinditvā paribhuñjati, vitānaṃ vā bhūmattharaṇaṃ vā sāṇipākāraṃ vā bhisiṃ vā bibbohanaṃ vā karoti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

536. There is no offense if one makes it to the proper measure; if one makes it smaller; if, having received one made by another that exceeds the measure, one cuts it and then uses it; if one makes a canopy, or a floor-covering, or a curtain-wall, or a mattress, or a pillow. There is no offense for one who is insane or for the first offender.

Nisīdanasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.

The seventh training rule on the sitting-cloth is finished.

8. Kaṇḍuppaṭicchādisikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Training Rule on the Sore-Covering Cloth

537. Tena [T 2.0507][V 0.0226] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ kaṇḍuppaṭicchādi anuññātā hoti[P 4.0172]. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū – “bhagavatā kaṇḍuppaṭicchādi anuññātā”ti appamāṇikāyo kaṇḍuppaṭicchādiyo dhārenti; puratopi pacchatopi ākaḍḍhantā āhiṇḍanti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū appamāṇikāyo kaṇḍuppaṭicchādiyo dhāressantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, appamāṇikāyo kaṇḍuppaṭicchādiyo dhārethāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, appamāṇikāyo kaṇḍuppaṭicchādiyo dhāressatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ [M 0.0223] vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

537. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, a sore-covering cloth had been allowed to the monks by the Blessed One. The group-of-six monks, thinking, 'A sore-covering cloth has been allowed by the Blessed One,' wore sore-covering cloths of limitless size; they wandered about, dragging them in front and behind. Those monks who were of few desires… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: 'How can the group-of-six monks wear sore-covering cloths of limitless size?'… 'Is it true, it is said, monks, that you wear sore-covering cloths of limitless size?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… 'How can you, worthless men, wear sore-covering cloths of limitless size? This, worthless men, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

538. “Kaṇḍuppaṭicchādiṃ pana bhikkhunā kārayamānena pamāṇikā kāretabbā. Tatridaṃ pamāṇaṃ – dīghaso catasso vidatthiyo, sugatavidatthiyā; tiriyaṃ dve vidatthiyo. Taṃ atikkāmayato chedanakaṃ pācittiya”nti.

538. “But when a monk is having a sore-covering cloth made, it should be made to measure. Herein, this is the measure: in length, four spans by the Sugata-span; in width, two spans. For one who exceeds that, it is a pācittiya offense entailing cutting.”

539. Kaṇḍuppaṭicchādi nāma yassa adhonābhi ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ kaṇḍu vā pīḷakā vā assāvo vā thullakacchu vā ābādho, tassa paṭicchādanatthāya.

539. A sore-covering cloth, by name, is for the purpose of covering an itch, a boil, a discharge, or a severe scab-disease for one who has such an ailment below the navel and above the knee-circle.

Kārayamānenāti karonto vā kārāpento vā[T 2.0508]. Pamāṇikā kāretabbā. Tatridaṃ pamāṇaṃ – dīghaso catasso vidatthiyo, sugatavidatthiyā; tiriyaṃ dve vidatthiyo. Taṃ atikkāmetvā karoti vā kārāpeti vā, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena chinditvā pācittiyaṃ desetabbaṃ.

‘Having it made’ means making it oneself or having another make it. It should be made to measure. Herein, this is the measure: in length, four spans by the Sugata-span; in width, two spans. If one makes it or has it made exceeding that, there is a dukkaṭa offense in the effort. Upon obtaining it, having cut it, the pācittiya offense should be confessed.

540. Attanā vippakataṃ attanā pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Attanā vippakataṃ parehi pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Parehi vippakataṃ attanā pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Parehi vippakataṃ parehi pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

540. If one completes by oneself what was left unfinished by oneself, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one has others complete what was left unfinished by oneself, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one completes by oneself what was left unfinished by others, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one has others complete what was left unfinished by others, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Aññassatthāya [V 0.0227] karoti vā kārāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Aññena kataṃ paṭilabhitvā paribhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one makes it or has it made for the sake of another, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If, having obtained one made by another, one uses it, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

541. Anāpatti pamāṇikaṃ karoti, ūnakaṃ karoti, aññena kataṃ pamāṇātikkantaṃ paṭilabhitvā chinditvā paribhuñjati, vitānaṃ vā bhūmattharaṇaṃ vā sāṇipākāraṃ vā bhisiṃ vā bibbohanaṃ vā karoti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

541. There is no offense if one makes it to measure; if one makes it smaller; if, having obtained one made by another that exceeds the measure, one cuts it and uses it; if one makes a canopy, or a floor-covering, or a cloth-enclosure, or a mattress, or a pillow; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Kaṇḍuppaṭicchādisikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The eighth training rule on the sore-covering cloth is concluded.

9. Vassikasāṭikāsikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Training Rule on the Rains-Bathing Cloth

542. Tena [T 2.0509][M 0.0224] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ vassikasāṭikā anuññātā hoti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū – “bhagavatā vassikasāṭikā anuññātā”ti appamāṇikāyo vassikasāṭikāyo dhārenti. Puratopi pacchatopi ākaḍḍhantā āhiṇḍanti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū appamāṇikāyo vassikasāṭikāyo dhāressantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, appamāṇikāyo vassikasāṭikāyo dhārethāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, appamāṇikāyo vassikasāṭikāyo dhāressatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

542. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, a rains-bathing cloth had been permitted for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One. The group-of-six bhikkhus, thinking, “A rains-bathing cloth has been permitted by the Blessed One,” wore rains-bathing cloths of unlimited size. They wandered about, dragging them in front and behind. Those bhikkhus who were of few desires… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can the group-of-six bhikkhus wear rains-bathing cloths of unlimited size?”… “Is it true, bhikkhus, as is said, that you wear rains-bathing cloths of unlimited size?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How can you, foolish men, wear rains-bathing cloths of unlimited size? This, foolish men, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:

543. “Vassikasāṭikaṃ pana bhikkhunā kārayamānena pamāṇikā kāretabbā. Tatridaṃ pamāṇaṃ – dīghaso cha vidatthiyo, sugatavidatthiyā; tiriyaṃ aḍḍhateyyā. Taṃ atikkāmayato chedanakaṃ pācittiya”nti.

543. “When a bhikkhu is having a rains-bathing cloth made, it should be made to the proper measure. Herein, this is the measure: in length, six spans by the Sugata-span; in width, two and a half spans. For one who exceeds that, it is a pācittiya offense that involves cutting.”

544. Vassikasāṭikā [P 4.0173] nāma vassānassa catumāsatthāya.

544. A rains-bathing cloth, so-called, is for the purpose of the four months of the rainy season.

Kārayamānenāti karonto vā kārāpento vā. Pamāṇikā kāretabbā[T 2.0510]. Tatridaṃ pamāṇaṃ – dīghaso [V 0.0228] cha vidatthiyo, sugatavidatthiyā; tiriyaṃ aḍḍhateyyā. Taṃ atikkāmetvā karoti vā kārāpeti vā, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena chinditvā pācittiyaṃ desetabbaṃ.

‘Is having made’ means making it oneself or having others make it. It should be made to the proper measure. Herein, this is the measure: in length, six spans by the Sugata-span; in width, two and a half spans. Having exceeded that, if one makes it or has it made, there is a dukkaṭa offense in the effort. Upon obtaining it, having cut it, the pācittiya offense should be confessed.

545. Attanā vippakataṃ attanā pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Attanā vippakataṃ parehi pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Parehi vippakataṃ attanā pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Parehi vippakataṃ parehi pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

545. If one completes by oneself what was left unfinished by oneself, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one has others complete what was left unfinished by oneself, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one completes by oneself what was left unfinished by others, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one has others complete what was left unfinished by others, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Aññassatthāya karoti vā kārāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Aññena kataṃ paṭilabhitvā paribhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one makes it or has it made for the sake of another, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If, having obtained one made by another, one uses it, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

546. Anāpatti [M 0.0225] pamāṇikaṃ karoti, ūnakaṃ karoti, aññena kataṃ pamāṇātikkantaṃ paṭilabhitvā chinditvā paribhuñjati, vitānaṃ vā bhūmattharaṇaṃ vā sāṇipākāraṃ vā bhisiṃ vā bibbohanaṃ vā karoti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

546. There is no offense if one makes it to the proper measure; if one makes it smaller; if, having obtained one made by another that exceeds the measure, one cuts it and uses it; if one makes a canopy, a floor-covering, a curtain-wall, a mattress, or a pillow; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Vassikasāṭikāsikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.

The ninth training rule on the rains-bathing cloth is concluded.

10. Nandasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Training Rule Concerning Nanda

547. Tena [T 2.0511] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā nando bhagavato mātucchāputto abhirūpo hoti dassanīyo pāsādiko caturaṅgulomako bhagavatā bhagavato (ka.). So sugatacīvarappamāṇaṃ cīvaraṃ dhāreti. Addasaṃsu kho therā bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ nandaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna – “bhagavā āgacchatī”ti āsanā vuṭṭhahanti. Te upagate jānitvā upagataṃ sañjānitvā (syā.), upagate sañjānitvā (sī.) ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā nando sugatacīvarappamāṇaṃ cīvaraṃ dhāressatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, nanda, sugatacīvarappamāṇaṃ cīvaraṃ dhāresīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, nanda, sugatacīvarappamāṇaṃ cīvaraṃ dhāressasi! Netaṃ, nanda, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

547. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the Venerable Nanda, the Blessed One's maternal aunt's son, was very handsome, good-looking, and inspired confidence; he was four finger-breadths shorter than the Blessed One. He wore a robe of the same measure as the Sugata's robe. The elder monks saw the Venerable Nanda coming from afar. Having seen him, they rose from their seats, thinking, 'The Blessed One is coming.' When he drew near, they, having realized who it was, complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: 'How indeed can the Venerable Nanda wear a robe of the same measure as the Sugata's robe?' … 'Is it true, Nanda, that you wear a robe of the same measure as the Sugata's robe?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… 'How indeed can you, Nanda, wear a robe of the same measure as the Sugata's robe? This, Nanda, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

548. “Yo pana bhikkhu sugatacīvarappamāṇaṃ cīvaraṃ kārāpeyya atirekaṃ vā, chedanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ[V 0.0229]. Tatridaṃ sugatassa sugatacīvarappamāṇaṃ – dīghaso nava vidatthiyo, sugatavidatthiyā; tiriyaṃ cha vidatthiyo. Idaṃ sugatassa sugatacīvarappamāṇa”nti.

548. “Whatever monk should have a robe made to the Sugata's measure, or exceeding it, it is an offense of pācittiya requiring cutting. In this regard, this is the Sugata's robe-measure: in length, nine spans by the Sugata's span; in width, six spans. This is the Sugata's robe-measure.”

549. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

549. As for 'whatever': whatever, of whatever kind... As for 'monk': ...in this context, this is the monk who is intended.

Sugatacīvarappamāṇaṃ [M 0.0226] sugatacīvaraṃ (ka.) nāma dīghaso nava vidatthiyo, sugatavidatthiyā; tiriyaṃ cha vidatthiyo.

What is called 'the Sugata's robe-measure' is: in length, nine spans by the Sugata's span; in width, six spans.

Kārāpeyyāti karoti [T 2.0512] vā kārāpeti vā, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena chinditvā pācittiyaṃ desetabbaṃ.

As for 'should have made': one makes it oneself or has another make it. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. Upon receiving it, having cut it, the pācittiya offense should be confessed.

550. Attanā vippakataṃ attanā pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Attanā vippakataṃ parehi pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Parehi vippakataṃ attanā pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Parehi vippakataṃ parehi pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

550. If one finishes by oneself what was left unfinished by oneself, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one has others finish what was left unfinished by oneself, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one finishes by oneself what was left unfinished by others, there is an offense of pācittiya. If one has others finish what was left unfinished by others, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Aññassatthāya karoti vā kārāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Aññena kataṃ paṭilabhitvā paribhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one makes it or has it made for the sake of another, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If, having received a robe made by another, one uses it, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

551. Anāpatti ūnakaṃ karoti, aññena kataṃ paṭilabhitvā chinditvā [P 4.0174] paribhuñjati, vitānaṃ vā bhūmattharaṇaṃ vā sāṇipākāraṃ vā bhisiṃ vā bibbohanaṃ vā karoti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

551. There is no offense: if one makes it smaller; if, having received what was made by another, one cuts it and then uses it; if one makes a canopy, a floor-covering, a cloth screen, a mattress, or a pillow; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Nandasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

The tenth training rule concerning Nanda is concluded.

Ratanavaggo rājavaggo (sī.) navamo.

The Jewel Chapter, the ninth, is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of this is:

Rañño ca ratanaṃ santaṃ, sūci mañcañca tūlikaṃ;

Nisīdanañca kaṇḍuñca, vassikā sugatena cāti.

The king, a jewel, a monk who is present, a needle, a bed, and cotton stuffing; a sitting-cloth, a covering for an itch, the rain-bathing cloth, and with the Sugata's measure.

Uddiṭṭhā [T 2.0513][V 0.0230] kho, āyasmanto, dvenavuti pācittiyā dhammā. Tatthāyasmante pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Dutiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Tatiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Parisuddhetthāyasmanto, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti.

Venerable sirs, the ninety-two pācittiya rules have been recited. In this matter, I ask the venerable sirs: 'Are you pure?' A second time I ask: 'Are you pure?' A third time I ask: 'Are you pure?' The venerable sirs are pure in this matter; therefore, they are silent. Thus I take it.

Khuddakaṃ samattaṃ.

The Minor Section is concluded.

Pācittiyakaṇḍaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Pācittiya Section is finished.

6. Pāṭidesanīyakaṇḍaṃ

6. The Pāṭidesanīya Section

1. Paṭhamapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The First Pāṭidesanīya Training Rule

Ime [T 2.0514][P 4.0175][M 0.0227] kho panāyasmanto cattāro pāṭidesanīyā

Venerable sirs, these four Pāṭidesanīya offenses

Dhammā uddesaṃ āgacchanti.

come up for recitation.

552. Tena [V 0.0231] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā paṭikkamanakāle aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ passitvā etadavoca – “handāyya, bhikkhaṃ paṭiggaṇhā”ti. “Suṭṭhu, bhaginī”ti sabbeva aggahesi. Sā upakaṭṭhe kāle nāsakkhi piṇḍāya carituṃ, chinnabhattā ahosi. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī dutiyampi divasaṃ…pe… tatiyampi divasaṃ sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā paṭikkamanakāle taṃ bhikkhuṃ passitvā etadavoca – “handāyya, bhikkhaṃ paṭiggaṇhā”ti. “Suṭṭhu, bhaginī”ti sabbeva aggahesi. Sā upakaṭṭhe kāle nāsakkhi piṇḍāya carituṃ, chinnabhattā ahosi. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī catutthe divase rathikāya pavedhentī gacchati. Seṭṭhi gahapati rathena paṭipathaṃ āgacchanto taṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “apehāyye”ti. Sā vokkamantī tattheva paripati. Seṭṭhi gahapati taṃ bhikkhuniṃ khamāpesi – “khamāhāyye, mayāsi pātitā”ti. “Nāhaṃ, gahapati, tayā pātitā. Apica, ahameva dubbalā”ti. “Kissa pana tvaṃ, ayye, dubbalā”ti? Atha kho sā [T 2.0515] bhikkhunī seṭṭhissa gahapatissa etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Seṭṭhi gahapati taṃ bhikkhuniṃ gharaṃ netvā bhojetvā ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma bhadantā bhikkhuniyā hatthato āmisaṃ paṭiggahessanti! Kicchalābho mātugāmo”ti!

552. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī, having walked for alms in Sāvatthī, saw a certain bhikkhu on her way back and said this: “Venerable sir, please accept this almsfood.” “Very well, sister,” he said, and accepted all of it. As the time was late, she was unable to walk for alms and missed her meal. Then that bhikkhunī on the second day… and on the third day, having walked for alms in Sāvatthī, saw that bhikkhu on her way back and said this: “Venerable sir, please accept this almsfood.” “Very well, sister,” he said, and accepted all of it. As the time was late, she was unable to walk for alms and missed her meal. Then on the fourth day, that bhikkhunī was walking along the street, staggering. A wealthy householder, coming along the road in his carriage, said this to that bhikkhunī: “Step aside, venerable lady.” As she was moving aside, she fell right there. The wealthy householder apologized to that bhikkhunī: “Forgive me, venerable lady, I caused you to fall.” “It was not you, householder, who caused me to fall. Rather, I myself am weak.” “But why, venerable lady, are you weak?” Then that bhikkhunī told the matter to the wealthy householder. The wealthy householder, having led that bhikkhunī to his house and fed her, complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed can the good sirs accept material requisites from the hand of a bhikkhunī! A woman’s gains are gotten with difficulty!”

Assosuṃ [V 0.0232] kho bhikkhū tassa seṭṭhissa gahapatissa ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhu bhikkhuniyā hatthato āmisaṃ paṭiggahessatī”ti [M 0.0228] …pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhikkhuniyā hatthato āmisaṃ paṭiggahesīti[P 4.0176]? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. “Ñātikā te, bhikkhu, aññātikā”ti? “Aññātikā, bhagavā”ti. “Aññātako, moghapurisa, aññātikāya na jānāti patirūpaṃ vā appatirūpaṃ vā santaṃ vā asantaṃ vā. Kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā hatthato āmisaṃ paṭiggahessasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

The bhikkhus heard that wealthy householder complaining, criticizing, and speaking disparagingly. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed can a bhikkhu accept material requisites from the hand of a bhikkhunī?” … “Is it true, bhikkhu, as is said, that you accepted material requisites from the hand of a bhikkhunī?” “It is true, Blessed One.” “Is she your relative, bhikkhu, or a non-relative?” “A non-relative, Blessed One.” “Foolish man, one who is not a relative does not know concerning a non-relative what is suitable or unsuitable, available or unavailable. How indeed could you, foolish man, accept material requisites from the hand of a bhikkhunī who is not a relative! This, foolish man, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule in this way:

553. “Yo pana bhikkhu aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā antaragharaṃ paviṭṭhāya hatthato khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā, paṭidesetabbaṃ tena bhikkhunā – ‘gārayhaṃ, āvuso, dhammaṃ āpajjiṃ asappāyaṃ pāṭidesanīyaṃ, taṃ paṭidesemī’”ti.

553. “Whatever bhikkhu, having accepted with his own hand edible food or staple food from the hand of a bhikkhunī who is not a relative and who has entered an inhabited area, should eat or consume it, it is to be confessed by that bhikkhu thus: ‘Venerable sirs, I have committed a blameworthy, unsuitable offense requiring confession; I confess it.’”

554. Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

554. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhu’ means… the bhikkhu who is meant in this context.

Aññātikā nāma mātito vā[T 2.0516]. Pitito vā yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā asambaddhā.

‘Not a relative’ means: a woman not related on the mother’s side or the father’s side up to the seventh generation of ancestors.

Bhikkhunī nāma ubhatosaṅghe upasampannā.

‘Bhikkhunī’ means: a woman who has been fully ordained in both Saṅghas.

Antaragharaṃ nāma rathikā byūhaṃ siṅghāṭakaṃ gharaṃ.

‘Within an inhabited area’ means: a street, a thoroughfare, a crossroads, or a house.

Khādanīyaṃ nāma pañca bhojanāni – yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ khādanīyaṃ nāma.

‘Edible food’ means: setting aside the five staple foods, tonics allowable for a watch, tonics allowable for seven days, and tonics allowable for a lifetime, the remainder is called ‘edible food’.

Bhojanīyaṃ nāma pañca bhojanāni – odano, kummāso, sattu, maccho, maṃsaṃ. “Khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

‘Staple food’ means the five staple foods: cooked rice, barley-meal, parched grain, fish, and meat. If one accepts it thinking, “I will eat, I will consume,” there is an offense of wrong doing. For every mouthful swallowed, there is a Pāṭidesanīya offense.

555. Aññātikāya aññātikasaññī antaragharaṃ paviṭṭhāya hatthato khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ [V 0.0233] vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa. Aññātikāya vematiko antaragharaṃ paviṭṭhāya hatthato khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa. Aññātikāya [M 0.0229] ñātikasaññī antaragharaṃ paviṭṭhāya hatthato khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

555. If, in the case of a non-relative, perceiving her as a non-relative, one accepts with one's own hand edible food or staple food from her hand after she has entered an inhabited area, and eats or consumes it, there is an offense to be confessed. If, in the case of a non-relative, being doubtful, one accepts with one's own hand edible food or staple food from her hand after she has entered an inhabited area, and eats or consumes it, there is an offense to be confessed. If, in the case of a non-relative, perceiving her as a relative, one accepts with one's own hand edible food or staple food from her hand after she has entered an inhabited area, and eats or consumes it, there is an offense to be confessed.

Yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ āhāratthāya paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ekatoupasampannāya hatthato khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā – “khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñātikāya aññātikasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñātikāya vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñātikāya [T 2.0517] ñātikasaññī, anāpatti.

If one accepts tonics allowable for a watch, tonics allowable for seven days, or tonics allowable for a lifetime for the purpose of nourishment, there is an offense of wrong-doing. For every mouthful swallowed, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one accepts edible food or staple food from the hand of a bhikkhunī ordained in only one Saṅgha, thinking, “I will eat, I will consume,” there is an offense of wrong-doing. For every mouthful swallowed, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of a relative, if one perceives her as a non-relative, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of a relative, if one is doubtful, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of a relative, if one perceives her as a relative, there is no offense.

556. Anāpatti ñātikāya, dāpeti na deti, upanikkhipitvā deti antarārāme, bhikkhunupassaye, titthiyaseyyāya, paṭikkamane[P 4.0177], gāmato nīharitvā deti, yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ “sati paccaye paribhuñjā”ti deti, sikkhamānāya, sāmaṇeriyā, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

556. There is no offense: if she is a relative; if she has it given but does not give it herself; if she gives it after placing it nearby; if it is given within the monastery, in the bhikkhunīs' quarters, in a non-Buddhist dwelling, or in a rest house for meals; if she gives it after bringing it out of the village; if she gives tonics allowable for a watch, for seven days, or for a lifetime, saying, “Use it if there is a need”; if the food is from a probationer or a female novice; for a bhikkhu who is insane; for the first offender.

Paṭhamapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The First Pāṭidesanīya Training Rule is concluded.

2. Dutiyapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Second Pāṭidesanīya Training Rule

557. Tena [T 2.0518] samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū kulesu nimantitā bhuñjanti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo chabbaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vosāsantiyo ṭhitā honti – “idha sūpaṃ detha, idha odanaṃ dethā”ti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū yāvadatthaṃ bhuñjanti. Aññe bhikkhū na cittarūpaṃ bhuñjanti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo vosāsantiyo na nivāressantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo vosāsantiyo na nivārethāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā …pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, bhikkhuniyo vosāsantiyo na nivāressatha[V 0.0234]! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

557. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Sanctuary. Now at that time, bhikkhus, having been invited, were eating in family homes. The bhikkhunīs of the group of six, standing by, were directing the bhikkhus of the group of six, saying, 'Give soup here, give rice here.' The bhikkhus of the group of six ate as much as they wished, while the other bhikkhus did not eat to their satisfaction. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: 'How is it that the bhikkhus of the group of six do not prevent the bhikkhunīs who are directing?'... 'Is it true, bhikkhus, that you do not prevent the bhikkhunīs who are directing?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... 'How is it, foolish men, that you do not prevent the bhikkhunīs who are directing? This, foolish men, is not for the confidence of the unconverted...' ... 'And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:'

558. “Bhikkhū [M 0.0230] paneva kulesu nimantitā bhuñjanti, tatra ce sā tatra ce (syā.) bhikkhunī vosāsamānarūpā ṭhitā hoti – ‘idha sūpaṃ detha, idha odanaṃ dethā’ti, tehi bhikkhūhi sā bhikkhunī apasādetabbā – ‘apasakka tāva, bhagini, yāva bhikkhū bhuñjantī’ti. Ekassa cepi ekassapi ce (sī. syā.) bhikkhuno na paṭibhāseyya taṃ bhikkhuniṃ apasādetuṃ – ‘apasakka tāva, bhagini, yāva bhikkhū bhuñjantī’ti paṭidesetabbaṃ [T 2.0519] tehi bhikkhūhi – ‘gārayhaṃ, āvuso, dhammaṃ āpajjimhā asappāyaṃ pāṭidesanīyaṃ, taṃ paṭidesemā’”ti.

558. “Bhikkhus, having been invited, are eating in family homes. If, on that occasion, a certain bhikkhunī stands there directing, saying, ‘Give soup here, give rice here,’ that bhikkhunī is to be dismissed by those bhikkhus, saying, ‘Step aside for a while, sister, while the bhikkhus are eating.’ And if it does not occur to even one bhikkhu to dismiss that bhikkhunī, saying, ‘Step aside for a while, sister, while the bhikkhus are eating,’ it is to be confessed by those bhikkhus: ‘Friends, we have committed a blameworthy, unsuitable offense to be confessed. We confess it.’”

559. Bhikkhū paneva kulesu nimantitā bhuñjantīti kulaṃ nāma cattāri kulāni – khattiyakulaṃ, brāhmaṇakulaṃ, vessakulaṃ, suddakulaṃ.

559. Regarding 'Bhikkhus, having been invited, are eating in family homes': 'family' means the four families: the Khattiya family, the Brāhmaṇa family, the Vessa family, and the Sudda family.

Nimantitā bhuñjantīti pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ aññatarena bhojanena nimantitā bhuñjanti.

'Invited, they eat' means that having been invited with one or another of the five kinds of staple foods, they eat.

Bhikkhunī nāma ubhatosaṅghe upasampannā.

A 'bhikkhunī' is one who has been fully ordained in both Saṅghas.

Vosāsantī [P 4.0178] nāma yathāmittatā yathāsandiṭṭhatā yathāsambhattatā yathāsamānupajjhāyakatā yathāsamānācariyakatā – “idha sūpaṃ detha, idha odanaṃ dethā”ti. Esā vosāsantī nāma.

'Directing' means, on the basis of friendship, acquaintance, shared association, having the same preceptor, or having the same teacher, saying, 'Give soup here, give rice here.' This is what is called 'directing.'

Tehi bhikkhūhīti bhuñjamānehi bhikkhūhi.

'By those bhikkhus' means by the bhikkhus who are eating.

Sā bhikkhunīti yā sā vosāsantī bhikkhunī.

'That bhikkhunī' means whichever bhikkhunī is directing.

Tehi bhikkhūhi sā bhikkhunī apasādetabbā – “apasakka tāva, bhagini, yāva bhikkhū bhuñjantī”ti. Ekassa cepi ekassapi ce (sī. syā.) bhikkhuno anapasādito anapasādite (sī. syā.) – “khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

That bhikkhunī is to be dismissed by those bhikkhus, saying, 'Step aside for a while, sister, while the bhikkhus are eating.' If, she not having been dismissed, even one bhikkhu accepts food, thinking, 'I will eat, I will consume,' there is an offense of wrong-doing. For every mouthful, there is an offense to be confessed.

560. Upasampannāya upasampannasaññī vosāsantiyā na nivāreti, āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa[V 0.0235]. Upasampannāya vematiko vosāsantiyā na nivāreti, āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa. Upasampannāya anupasampannasaññī vosāsantiyā na nivāreti, āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

560. In the case of a fully ordained bhikkhunī, if, perceiving her as fully ordained, he does not prevent her from directing, there is an offense to be confessed. In the case of a fully ordained bhikkhunī, if he is in doubt, and does not prevent her from directing, there is an offense to be confessed. In the case of a fully ordained bhikkhunī, if, perceiving her as not fully ordained, he does not prevent her from directing, there is an offense to be confessed.

Ekatoupasampannāya [M 0.0231] vosāsantiyā na nivāreti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya upasampannasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya [T 2.0520] vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya anupasampannasaññī, anāpatti.

If he does not prevent a bhikkhunī ordained in one Saṅgha from directing, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of an unordained woman: if he perceives her as ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing; if he is in doubt about her, there is an offense of wrong-doing; if he perceives her as unordained, there is no offense.

561. Anāpatti attano bhattaṃ dāpeti na deti, aññesaṃ bhattaṃ deti na dāpeti, yaṃ na dinnaṃ taṃ dāpeti, yattha na dinnaṃ tattha dāpeti, sabbesaṃ samakaṃ dāpeti, sikkhamānā vosāsati, sāmaṇerī vosāsati, pañca bhojanāni ṭhapetvā sabbattha, anāpatti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

561. There is no offense if she has her own food given but does not give it herself; if she gives others' food but does not have it given; if she has something given that was not yet given; if she has it given where it was not yet given; if she has it given equally to all; if a probationer directs; if a female novice directs; if she directs regarding anything apart from the five kinds of staple foods. There is no offense for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Dutiyapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Second Pāṭidesanīya Training Rule is concluded.

3. Tatiyapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Third Pāṭidesanīya Training Rule

562. Tena [T 2.0521] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sāvatthiyaṃ aññataraṃ kulaṃ ubhatopasannaṃ hoti. Saddhāya vaḍḍhati, bhogena hāyati, yaṃ tasmiṃ kule uppajjati purebhattaṃ khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā taṃ sabbaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vissajjetvā appekadā anasitā acchanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā na mattaṃ jānitvā paṭiggahessanti! Ime imesaṃ datvā appekadā anasitā acchantī”ti!! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne [P 4.0179] etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yaṃ kulaṃ saddhāya vaḍḍhati, bhogena hāyati evarūpassa kulassa ñattidutiyena kammena sekkhasammutiṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbā. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

562. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, in the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, in Sāvatthī, a certain family was devoted, both husband and wife. It grew in faith but declined in wealth. Whatever chewable food or edible food arose in that family before noon, having given it all to the bhikkhus, they sometimes remained without having eaten. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed can the ascetics, sons of the Sakyan, accept without knowing the measure! These people, having given to them, sometimes remain without having eaten!” The bhikkhus heard those people complaining, criticizing, and speaking disparagingly. Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, concerning this matter, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow that for a family that grows in faith and declines in wealth, for such a family, the designation of ‘in training’ be given by means of an act with a motion as the second part. And, bhikkhus, it should be given in this way. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent, capable bhikkhu:

563. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmaṃ kulaṃ saddhāya vaḍḍhati, bhogena hāyati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa kulassa sekkhasammutiṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

563. “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The family of so-and-so grows in faith but declines in wealth. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should give the designation of ‘in training’ to the family of so-and-so. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu [M 0.0232][V 0.0236] me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmaṃ kulaṃ saddhāya vaḍḍhati, bhogena [T 2.0522] hāyati. Saṅgho itthannāmassa kulassa sekkhasammutiṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa kulassa sekkhasammutiyā dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The family of so-and-so grows in faith but declines in wealth. The Saṅgha gives the designation of ‘in training’ to the family of so-and-so. To whichever venerable one the giving of the designation of ‘in training’ to the family of so-and-so is agreeable, he should be silent; to whom it is not agreeable, he should speak.

“Dinnā saṅghena itthannāmassa kulassa sekkhasammuti. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The designation of ‘in training’ has been given by the Saṅgha to the family of so-and-so. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I understand this.”

Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

And in this way, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:

“Yāni kho pana tāni sekkhasammatāni kulāni, yo pana bhikkhu tathārūpesu sekkhasammatesu kulesu khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā, paṭidesetabbaṃ tena bhikkhunā – ‘gārayhaṃ, āvuso, dhammaṃ āpajjiṃ asappāyaṃ pāṭidesanīyaṃ taṃ paṭidesemī’”ti.

“Whatever families there are that are designated as ‘in training,’ whatever bhikkhu, in such families designated as ‘in training,’ having accepted with his own hand chewable food or edible food, should chew or should eat it, it should be confessed by that bhikkhu thus: ‘Friends, I have committed a blameworthy, unsuitable offense requiring confession; I confess it.’”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

Thus this training rule was laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

564. Tena kho pana samayena sāvatthiyaṃ ussavo hoti. Manussā bhikkhū nimantetvā bhojenti. Tampi kho kulaṃ bhikkhū nimantesi. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nādhivāsenti – “paṭikkhittaṃ bhagavatā sekkhasammatesu kulesu khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādituṃ bhuñjitu”nti. Te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kiṃ nu kho nāma amhākaṃ jīvitena yaṃ ayyā amhākaṃ na paṭiggaṇhantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, nimantitena sekkhasammatesu kulesu khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ [T 2.0523] vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādituṃ bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

564. Now at that time, there was a festival in Sāvatthī. People invited bhikkhus and fed them. That family also invited the bhikkhus. The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not consent, thinking: “It has been prohibited by the Blessed One to accept with one’s own hand chewable food or edible food in families designated as ‘in training’ and to chew or eat it.” Those people complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “What use is our life, since the venerables do not accept our offerings?” The bhikkhus heard those people complaining, criticizing, and speaking disparagingly. Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, concerning this matter, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow for one who has been invited to accept with his own hand chewable food or edible food in families designated as ‘in training’ and to chew or eat it. And in this way, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:

“Yāni kho pana tāni sekkhasammatāni kulāni, yo pana bhikkhu tathārūpesu sekkhasammatesu kulesu pubbe animantito [P 4.0180] khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādeyya [V 0.0237] vā bhuñjeyya vā[M 0.0233], paṭidesetabbaṃ tena bhikkhunā – ‘gārayhaṃ, āvuso, dhammaṃ āpajjiṃ asappāyaṃ pāṭidesanīyaṃ, taṃ paṭidesemī’”ti.

“Whatever families there are that are designated as ‘in training,’ whatever bhikkhu, in such families designated as ‘in training,’ not having been invited beforehand, having accepted with his own hand chewable food or edible food, should chew or should eat it, it should be confessed by that bhikkhu thus: ‘Friends, I have committed a blameworthy, unsuitable offense requiring confession; I confess it.’”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

Thus this training rule was laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One.

565. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu tassa kulassa kulūpako hoti. Atha kho so bhikkhu pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena taṃ kulaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Tena kho pana samayena so bhikkhu gilāno hoti. Atha kho te manussā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavocuṃ – “bhuñjatha, bhante”ti. Atha kho so bhikkhu – “bhagavatā paṭikkhittaṃ animantitena sekkhasammatesu kulesu khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādituṃ bhuñjitu”nti kukkuccāyanto na paṭiggahesi; nāsakkhi piṇḍāya carituṃ; chinnabhatto ahosi. Atha kho so bhikkhu ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānena bhikkhunā sekkhasammatesu kulesu khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādituṃ [T 2.0524] bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

565. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu was a frequenter of that family’s house. Then that bhikkhu, in the morning, having dressed in his lower robe and taking his bowl and outer robe, approached where that family was; having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Now at that time, that bhikkhu was sick. Then those people said this to that bhikkhu: “Venerable sir, please eat.” Then that bhikkhu, being scrupulous, did not accept, thinking: “It has been prohibited by the Blessed One for one who has not been invited to accept with his own hand chewable food or edible food in families designated as ‘in training’ and to chew or eat it.” He was not able to go for alms; he was without a meal. Then that bhikkhu, having gone to the monastery, told this matter to the bhikkhus. The bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, concerning this matter, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow for a sick bhikkhu to accept with his own hand chewable food or edible food in families designated as ‘in training’ and to chew or eat it. And in this way, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:

566. “Yāni kho pana tāni sekkhasammatāni kulāni, yo pana bhikkhu tathārūpesu sekkhasammatesu kulesu pubbe animantito agilāno khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā, paṭidesetabbaṃ tena bhikkhunā – ‘gārayhaṃ, āvuso, dhammaṃ āpajjiṃ asappāyaṃ pāṭidesanīyaṃ, taṃ paṭidesemī”ti.

566. “Whatever families are designated as 'learners', should any bhikkhu, being not ill and not previously invited, receive with his own hand either hard food or soft food in such families designated as 'learners' and then eat or consume it, it is to be confessed by that bhikkhu thus: 'Venerable sirs, I have committed a blameworthy, unsuitable act requiring confession. I confess it.'”

567. Yāni kho pana tāni sekkhasammatāni kulānīti sekkhasammataṃ nāma kulaṃ yaṃ kulaṃ saddhāya vaḍḍhati, bhogena hāyati. Evarūpassa kulassa ñattidutiyena kammena sekkhasammuti dinnā hoti.

567. As to 'those families designated as learners': a family designated as a 'learner' is a family that grows in faith but declines in wealth. To such a family, the designation as 'learner' is given by a formal act consisting of a motion and one announcement.

Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

‘Whoever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind… (and so on)… ‘Bhikkhu’ means… (and so on)… in this context, this is the bhikkhu who is intended.

Tathārūpesu sekkhasammatesu kulesūti evarūpesu sekkhasammatesu kulesu.

‘In such families designated as learners’ means: in families of such a kind designated as 'learners'.

Animantito [M 0.0234][V 0.0238] nāma ajjatanāya vā svātanāya vā animantito, gharūpacāraṃ okkamante nimanteti, eso animantito nāma.

‘Uninvited’ means: not invited for today or for tomorrow. If one is invited while entering the precincts of a house, this is called ‘uninvited’.

Nimantito [P 4.0181] nāma ajjatanāya vā svātanāya vā nimantito, gharūpacāraṃ anokkamante nimanteti, eso nimantito nāma.

‘Invited’ means: invited for today or for tomorrow. If one is invited without entering the precincts of a house, this is called ‘invited’.

Agilāno nāma sakkoti piṇḍāya carituṃ.

‘Not ill’ means: one is able to go for alms-food.

Gilāno nāma na sakkoti piṇḍāya carituṃ.

‘Ill’ means: one is not able to go for alms-food.

Khādanīyaṃ nāma pañca bhojanāni – yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ khādanīyaṃ nāma.

‘Hard food’ means: setting aside the five staple foods, time-limited items allowable for a watch of the night (yāmakālika), time-limited items allowable for seven days (sattāhakālika), and items allowable for a lifetime (yāvajīvika), the remainder is called ‘hard food’.

Bhojanīyaṃ nāma pañca bhojanāni – odano, kummāso, sattu, maccho, maṃsaṃ.

‘Soft food’ means the five staple foods: cooked rice, barley-meal, roasted grain flour, fish, and meat.

Animantito agilāno “khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa[T 2.0525]. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

Being uninvited and not ill, if one receives food thinking, ‘I will eat, I will consume,’ there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa). With every swallow, there is an offense requiring confession (pāṭidesanīya).

568. Sekkhasammate sekkhasammatasaññī animantito agilāno khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃva sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa. Sekkhasammate vematiko…pe… sekkhasammate asekkhasammatasaññī animantito agilāno khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

568. In a family designated as a 'learner', if one perceives it as designated as a 'learner', and being uninvited and not ill, receives with one's own hand either hard food or soft food and eats or consumes it, there is an offense requiring confession (pāṭidesanīya). In a family designated as a 'learner', if one is in doubt… (and so on)… In a family designated as a 'learner', if one perceives it as not designated as a 'learner', and being uninvited and not ill, receives with one's own hand either hard food or soft food and eats or consumes it, there is an offense requiring confession (pāṭidesanīya).

Yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ āhāratthāya paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti dukkaṭassa. Asekkhasammate sekkhasammatasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Asekkhasammate vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Asekkhasammate asekkhasammatasaññī, anāpatti.

If one receives a time-limited item allowable for a watch of the night (yāmakālika), a time-limited item allowable for seven days (sattāhakālika), or an item allowable for a lifetime (yāvajīvika) for the purpose of food, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa). With every swallow, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa). In a family not designated as a 'learner', if one perceives it as designated as a 'learner', there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa). In a family not designated as a 'learner', if one is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa). In a family not designated as a 'learner', if one perceives it as not designated as a 'learner', there is no offense.

569. Anāpatti nimantitassa, gilānassa, nimantitassa vā gilānassa vā sesakaṃ bhuñjati[V 0.0239], aññesaṃ bhikkhā tattha paññattā hoti, gharato nīharitvā denti, niccabhatte, salākabhatte, pakkhike, uposathike, pāṭipadike, yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ – “sati paccaye paribhuñjā”ti deti, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

569. There is no offense: for one who is invited; for one who is ill; if one eats the leftovers of one who was invited or is ill; if alms belonging to others are prepared there; if they bring it out from the house to give it; in the case of a constant meal, a ticket-meal, a fortnightly meal, an Uposatha-day meal, or a first-day-of-the-fortnight meal; if one gives a time-limited item allowable for a watch of the night, a time-limited item allowable for seven days, or an item allowable for a lifetime, saying, ‘Use this if there is a reason’; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Tatiyapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Third Training Rule Requiring Confession is concluded.

4. Catutthapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Fourth Training Rule Requiring Confession

570. Tena [T 2.0526][M 0.0235] samayena buddho bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sākiyadāsakā avaruddhā honti. Sākiyāniyo icchanti āraññakesu senāsanesu bhattaṃ kātuṃ. Assosuṃ kho sākiyadāsakā – “sākiyāniyo kira āraññakesu senāsanesu bhattaṃ kattukāmā”ti. Te magge pariyuṭṭhiṃsu. Sākiyāniyo [P 4.0182] paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ ādāya āraññakaṃ senāsanaṃ agamaṃsu. Sākiyadāsakā nikkhamitvā sākiyāniyo acchindiṃsu ca dūsesuñca. Sākiyā nikkhamitvā te core sabhaṇḍe saha bhaṇḍena (ka.) gahetvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhadantā ārāme core paṭivasante nārocessantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū sākiyānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññapessāmi dasa atthavase paṭicca – saṅghasuṭṭhutāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

570. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu, in the Banyan Tree Park. Now at that time, the Sakyan servants were blockading the roads. The Sakyan women wanted to prepare meals in forest dwellings. The Sakyan servants heard, “It seems the Sakyan women want to prepare meals in forest dwellings.” They lay in wait on the road. The Sakyan women, taking choice hard and soft food, went to the forest dwelling. The Sakyan servants came out, and they robbed and violated the Sakyan women. The Sakyans came out, seized those thieves along with the stolen goods, and complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How is it that the venerable sirs do not inform us when thieves are dwelling in the monastery!” The bhikkhus heard the Sakyans complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus: “In that case, bhikkhus, I will lay down a training rule for the bhikkhus for ten reasons: for the well-being of the Sangha… and so on… And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Yāni kho pana tāni āraññakāni senāsanāni sāsaṅkasammatāni sappaṭibhayāni, yo pana bhikkhu tathārūpesu senāsanesu senāsanesu viharanto (sī. syā.) pubbe appaṭisaṃviditaṃ khādanīyaṃ [T 2.0527] vā bhojanīyaṃ vā ajjhārāme sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā, paṭidesetabbaṃ tena bhikkhunā – ‘gārayhaṃ, āvuso, dhammaṃ āpajjiṃ asappāyaṃ pāṭidesanīyaṃ taṃ paṭidesemī’”ti.

“Whatever forest dwellings are considered to be perilous and are dangerous, should any bhikkhu, in such dwellings, receive with his own hand hard food or soft food inside the monastery that was not made known beforehand, and then eat or consume it, it is to be confessed by that bhikkhu thus: 'Venerable sirs, I have committed a blameworthy, unsuitable act requiring confession. I confess it.'”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

Thus this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhus.

571. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu āraññakesu senāsanesu gilāno hoti[V 0.0240]. Manussā khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā ādāya āraññakaṃ senāsanaṃ agamaṃsu. Atha kho te manussā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavocuṃ – “bhuñjatha, bhante”ti. Atha kho so bhikkhu – “bhagavatā paṭikkhittaṃ āraññakesu senāsanesu khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā [M 0.0236] paṭiggahetvā khādituṃ bhuñjitu”nti kukkuccāyanto na paṭiggahesi, nāsakkhi piṇḍāya carituṃ pavisituṃ (ka.), chinnabhatto ahosi. Atha kho so bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānena bhikkhunā āraññakesu senāsanesu pubbe appaṭisaṃviditaṃ khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādituṃ bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

571. Now at that time, a certain monk was ill in a forest dwelling. People, taking edible food or staple food, went to the forest dwelling. Then those people said to that monk: “Venerable sir, please eat.” Then that monk, feeling scrupulous that, “It has been forbidden by the Blessed One to receive with one’s own hand edible food or staple food in forest dwellings and to eat or consume it,” did not accept it. He was unable to go for alms-food and went without a meal. Then that monk told this matter to the monks. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: “I allow, monks, a sick monk in forest dwellings to receive with his own hand edible food or staple food that was not made known beforehand and to eat or consume it. And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

572. “Yāni kho pana tāni āraññakāni senāsanāni sāsaṅkasammatāni sappaṭibhayāni, yo pana bhikkhu tathārūpesu senāsanesu [P 4.0183] pubbe appaṭisaṃviditaṃ khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā ajjhārāme sahatthā paṭiggahetvā agilāno khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā, paṭidesetabbaṃ tena bhikkhunā – ‘gārayhaṃ, āvuso, dhammaṃ [T 2.0528] āpajjiṃ asappāyaṃ pāṭidesanīyaṃ, taṃ paṭidesemī’”ti.

572. “Whatever forest dwellings are considered to be perilous and are dangerous, should any monk who is not ill, in such dwellings, having received with his own hand edible food or staple food inside the monastery that was not made known beforehand, eat or consume it, it is to be acknowledged by that monk, saying: ‘Friends, I have committed a blameworthy, unsuitable act that is a matter to be acknowledged. I acknowledge it.’”

573. Yāni kho pana tāni āraññakāni senāsanānīti āraññakaṃ nāma senāsanaṃ pañcadhanusatikaṃ pacchimaṃ.

573. Regarding ‘those forest dwellings’: a forest dwelling is, at a minimum, five hundred bow-lengths away.

Sāsaṅkaṃ nāma ārāme ārāmūpacāre corānaṃ niviṭṭhokāso dissati, bhuttokāso dissati, ṭhitokāso dissati, nisinnokāso dissati, nipannokāso dissati.

‘Perilous’ means: in the monastery or in the vicinity of the monastery, a place where thieves have entered is seen, a place where they have eaten is seen, a place where they have stood is seen, a place where they have sat is seen, or a place where they have lain down is seen.

Sappaṭibhayaṃ nāma ārāme ārāmūpacāre corehi manussā hatā dissanti, viluttā dissanti, ākoṭitā dissanti.

‘Dangerous’ means: in the monastery or in the vicinity of the monastery, people killed by thieves are seen, people plundered are seen, or people beaten are seen.

Yo panāti yo yādiso…pe… bhikkhūti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.

‘Whoever’: means whoever, of whatever kind... and so on. ‘Monk’: ...and so on... in this sense, this is the monk who is intended.

Tathārūpesu senāsanesūti evarūpesu senāsanesu.

‘In such dwellings’ means: in dwellings of this kind.

Appaṭisaṃviditaṃ [V 0.0241] nāma pañcannaṃ paṭisaṃviditaṃ, etaṃ appaṭisaṃviditaṃ nāma. Ārāmaṃ ārāmūpacāraṃ ṭhapetvā paṭisaṃviditaṃ, etaṃ etampi (sī.) appaṭisaṃviditaṃ nāma.

‘Not made known beforehand’ means: though it has been made known to five fellow residents, this is called ‘not made known beforehand’. Though it has been made known leaving aside the monastery and its vicinity, this is called ‘not made known beforehand’.

Paṭisaṃviditaṃ [M 0.0237] nāma yo koci itthī vā puriso vā ārāmaṃ ārāmūpacāraṃ āgantvā āroceti – “itthannāmassa, bhante, khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā āharissantī”ti. Sace sāsaṅkaṃ hoti, sāsaṅkanti ācikkhitabbaṃ; sace sappaṭibhayaṃ hoti, sappaṭibhayanti ācikkhitabbaṃ; sace – “hotu, bhante, āhariyissatī”ti bhaṇati, corā vattabbā – “manussā idhūpacaranti apasakkathā”ti. Yāguyā paṭisaṃvidite tassā parivāro āhariyyati, etaṃ paṭisaṃviditaṃ nāma. Bhattena paṭisaṃvidite tassa parivāro āhariyyati, etaṃ paṭisaṃviditaṃ nāma[T 2.0529]. Khādanīyena paṭisaṃvidite tassa parivāro āhariyyati, etaṃ paṭisaṃviditaṃ nāma. Kulena paṭisaṃvidite yo tasmiṃ kule manusso khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā āharati, etaṃ paṭisaṃviditaṃ nāma. Gāmena paṭisaṃvidite yo tasmiṃ gāme manusso khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā āharati, etaṃ paṭisaṃviditaṃ nāma. Pūgena paṭisaṃvidite yo tasmiṃ pūge manusso khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā āharati, etaṃ paṭisaṃviditaṃ nāma.

‘Made known’ means: it is when any woman or man, having come to the monastery or the monastery's vicinity, announces: 'Venerable Sirs, they will bring edible food or staple food for the monk of such-and-such a name.' If it is perilous, it should be stated as 'perilous'; if it is dangerous, it should be stated as 'dangerous'. If one says, 'Let it be, Venerable Sir, it will be brought,' thieves should be told: 'People frequent this place, go away.' When it is made known by means of rice-gruel, its accompaniment is brought; this is called 'made known'. When it is made known by means of a meal, its accompaniment is brought; this is called 'made known'. When it is made known by means of edible food, its accompaniment is brought; this is called 'made known'. When it is made known by means of a family, whatever person in that family brings edible food or staple food, this is called 'made known'. When it is made known by means of a village, whatever person in that village brings edible food or staple food, this is called 'made known'. When it is made known by means of an association, whatever person in that association brings edible food or staple food, this is called 'made known'.

Khādanīyaṃ nāma pañca bhojanāni – yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ khādanīyaṃ nāma.

‘Edible food’ means: having set aside the five staple foods, what is allowable for a watch-period, what is allowable for seven days, and what is allowable for a lifetime, the remainder is called 'edible food'.

Bhojanīyaṃ nāma pañca bhojanāni – odano, kummāso, sattu, maccho, maṃsaṃ.

‘Staple food’ means: the five staple foods are cooked rice, barley-meal, parched grain flour, fish, and meat.

Ajjhārāmo nāma parikkhittassa ārāmassa antoārāmo. Aparikkhittassa upacāro.

‘Inside the monastery’ means: for an enclosed monastery, it is the inside of the monastery. For an unenclosed one, it is the vicinity.

Agilāno nāma sakkoti piṇḍāya carituṃ gantuṃ (ka.).

‘One who is not ill’ means: one is able to go for alms.

Gilāno nāma na sakkoti piṇḍāya carituṃ gantuṃ (ka.).

‘One who is ill’ means: one is unable to go for alms.

Appaṭisaṃviditaṃ [P 4.0184] agilāno “khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

If one who is not ill receives what has not been made known, thinking, ‘I will eat, I will consume,’ there is an offense of wrong-doing. For each mouthful, there is an offense requiring acknowledgement.

574. Appaṭisaṃvidite appaṭisaṃviditasaññī khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā ajjhārāme sahatthā [V 0.0242] paṭiggahetvā agilāno khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa. Appaṭisaṃvidite vematiko khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ [M 0.0238] vā ajjhārāme sahatthā paṭiggahetvā agilāno [T 2.0530] khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa. Appaṭisaṃvidite paṭisaṃviditasaññī khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā ajjhārāme sahatthā paṭiggahetvā agilāno khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

574. In the case of what has not been made known, if one perceives it as not made known, and, not being ill, having received with one's own hand edible food or staple food inside the monastery, eats or consumes it, there is an offense requiring acknowledgement. In the case of what has not been made known, if one is in doubt, and, not being ill, having received with one's own hand edible food or staple food inside the monastery, eats or consumes it, there is an offense requiring acknowledgement. In the case of what has not been made known, if one perceives it as made known, and, not being ill, having received with one's own hand edible food or staple food inside the monastery, eats or consumes it, there is an offense requiring acknowledgement.

Yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ āhāratthāya paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti dukkaṭassa. Paṭisaṃvidite appaṭisaṃviditasaññī, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Paṭisaṃvidite vematiko, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Paṭisaṃvidite paṭisaṃviditasaññī, anāpatti.

If one receives what is allowable for a watch-period, for seven days, or for a lifetime for the purpose of food, there is an offense of wrong-doing. For each mouthful, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of what has been made known, if one perceives it as not made known, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of what has been made known, if one is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of what has been made known, if one perceives it as made known, there is no offense.

575. Anāpatti paṭisaṃvidite, gilānassa, paṭisaṃvidite vā gilānassa vā sesakaṃ bhuñjati, bahārāme paṭiggahetvā antoārāme bhuñjati, tattha jātakaṃ mūlaṃ vā tacaṃ vā pattaṃ vā pupphaṃ vā phalaṃ vā bhuñjati, yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ sati paccaye paribhuñjati, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

575. There is no offense for one who has been informed, for one who is ill; if one eats the leftovers of one who has been informed or of one who is ill; if, having received it outside the monastery, one consumes it inside the monastery; if one consumes a root, bark, leaf, flower, or fruit that has grown there; if, when there is a reason, one consumes what is allowable for a watch-period, for seven days, or for a lifetime; for one who is insane, and for the first offender.

Catutthapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fourth training rule requiring confession is finished.

Uddiṭṭhā kho, āyasmanto, cattāro pāṭidesanīyā dhammā. Tatthāyasmante pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Dutiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Tatiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Parisuddhetthāyasmanto, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti.

Venerable Sirs, the four rules requiring confession have indeed been recited. Regarding these, I ask the Venerable Sirs: 'Are you pure in this matter?' A second time I ask: 'Are you pure in this matter?' A third time I ask: 'Are you pure in this matter?' The Venerable Sirs are pure in this matter; therefore, they are silent. Thus I hold it.

Pāṭidesanīyakaṇḍaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section on rules requiring confession is finished.

7. Sekhiyakaṇḍaṃ

7. The Section on Training

1. Parimaṇḍalavaggo

1. The Chapter on Wearing Robes Evenly

Ime kho panāyasmanto sekhiyā

Venerable sirs, these rules for training

Dhammā uddesaṃ āgacchanti.
