now come up for recitation.

576. Tena [T 2.0531][P 4.0185][M 0.0239][V 0.0243] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū puratopi pacchatopi olambentā nivāsenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā puratopi pacchatopi olambentā nivāsessanti, seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū puratopi pacchatopi olambentā nivāsessantī”ti! Atha kho te bhikkhū chabbaggiye bhikkhū anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā chabbaggiye bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, puratopi pacchatopi olambentā nivāsethā”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, puratopi pacchatopi olambentā nivāsessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… [T 2.0532] evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

576. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta’s Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus wore their lower robes hanging down in front and behind. People criticized, scorned, and disparaged them, saying: “How can these ascetics, sons of the Sakyan, wear their lower robes hanging down in front and behind, just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures?” The bhikkhus heard those people criticizing, scorning, and disparaging them. Those bhikkhus who were of few wants... they criticized, scorned, and disparaged them, saying: “How can the group-of-six bhikkhus wear their lower robes hanging down in front and behind?” Then those bhikkhus, having rebuked the group-of-six bhikkhus in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on account of this cause, on account of this matter, had the Saṅgha of bhikkhus assemble and questioned the group-of-six bhikkhus: “Is it true, bhikkhus, as is said, that you wear your lower robes hanging down in front and behind?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... “Worthless men, how can you wear your lower robes hanging down in front and behind? This, worthless men, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced... And so, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will wear the lower robe evenly all around,’ this training should be undertaken.

Parimaṇḍalaṃ [V 0.0244] nivāsetabbaṃ nābhimaṇḍalaṃ jāṇumaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādentena. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca purato vā pacchato vā olambento nivāseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The lower robe is to be worn evenly all around, covering the circle of the navel and the circle of the knees. Whichever bhikkhu, on account of disrespect, wears it hanging down in front or behind, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, āpadāsu, ummattakassa,

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who does not know, for one who is sick, in times of calamity, for one who is insane,

Ādikammikassāti.

and for the first offender.

Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The first training rule is finished.

577. Tena [M 0.0240] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū puratopi pacchatopi olambentā pārupanti…pe….

577. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta’s Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus wore their upper robes hanging down in front and behind...

“Parimaṇḍalaṃ pārupissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will wear the upper robe evenly all around,’ this training should be undertaken.

Parimaṇḍalaṃ pārupitabbaṃ ubho kaṇṇe samaṃ katvā. Yo [P 4.0186] anādariyaṃ paṭicca purato vā pacchato vā olambento pārupati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The upper robe is to be worn evenly all around, making both ends equal. Whichever bhikkhu, on account of disrespect, wears it hanging down in front or behind, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, āpadāsu, ummattakassa,

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who does not know, for one who is sick, in times of calamity, for one who is insane,

Ādikammikassāti.

and for the first offender.

Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The second training rule is finished.

578. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kāyaṃ vivaritvā antaraghare gacchanti…pe….

578. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta’s Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus went among houses with their bodies uncovered...

“Suppaṭicchanno antaraghare [T 2.0533] gamissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will go among houses well-covered,’ this training should be undertaken.

Suppaṭicchannena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca kāyaṃ vivaritvā antaraghare gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One is to go among houses well-covered. Whichever bhikkhu, on account of disrespect, goes among houses with his body uncovered, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti [V 0.0245] asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, āpadāsu, ummattakassa,

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who does not know, for one who is sick, in times of calamity, for one who is insane,

Ādikammikassāti.

and for the first offender.

Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The third training rule is finished.

579. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kāyaṃ vivaritvā antaraghare nisīdanti…pe….

579. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta’s Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus sat down among houses with their bodies uncovered...

“Suppaṭicchanno antaraghare nisīdissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will sit down among houses well-covered,’ this training should be undertaken.

Suppaṭicchannena antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca kāyaṃ vivaritvā antaraghare nisīdati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One is to sit down among houses well-covered. Whichever bhikkhu, on account of disrespect, sits down among houses with his body uncovered, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, vāsūpagatassa, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who does not know, for one who is sick, for one who has entered a residence, in times of calamity, for one who is insane, and for the first offender.

Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fourth training rule is finished.

580. Tena [M 0.0241] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū hatthampi pādampi kīḷāpentā antaraghare gacchanti…pe….

580. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta’s Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus went among houses swinging their hands and feet...

“Susaṃvuto antaraghare gamissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will go among houses well-restrained,’ this training should be undertaken.

Susaṃvutena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca hatthaṃ vā pādaṃ vā kīḷāpento antaraghare gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One is to go among houses well-restrained. Whichever bhikkhu, on account of disrespect, goes among houses swinging his hands or feet, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who does not know, for one who is sick, for one who is insane, and for the first offender.

Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fifth training rule is concluded.

581. Tena [V 0.0246] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū [T 2.0534] hatthampi pādampi kīḷāpentā antaraghare nisīdanti…pe….

581. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus were sitting in an inhabited area, playing with their hands and feet...

“Susaṃvuto antaraghare nisīdissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will sit in an inhabited area well-restrained,’ this is a training to be observed.

Susaṃvutena antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca hatthaṃ vā pādaṃ vā kīḷāpento antaraghare nisīdati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should sit in an inhabited area well-restrained. Whichever bhikkhu, on account of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area playing with his hands or feet, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense: if it is unintentional; if one is unmindful; for one who does not know; for one who is sick; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The sixth training rule is concluded.

582. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū tahaṃ tahaṃ olokentā antaraghare gacchanti…pe….

582. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus were going into an inhabited area looking here and there...

“Okkhittacakkhu antaraghare gamissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will go into an inhabited area with eyes downcast,’ this is a training to be observed.

Okkhittacakkhunā antaraghare gantabbaṃ yugamattaṃ pekkhantena. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca tahaṃ tahaṃ olokento antaraghare gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should go into an inhabited area with eyes downcast, looking a yoke’s length. Whichever bhikkhu, on account of disrespect, goes into an inhabited area looking here and there, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, āpadāsu, ummattakassa,

There is no offense: if it is unintentional; if one is unmindful; for one who does not know; for one who is sick; in times of danger; for one who is insane;

Ādikammikassāti.

or for the first offender.

Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The seventh training rule is concluded.

583. Tena [M 0.0242] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū tahaṃ tahaṃ olokentā antaraghare nisīdanti…pe….

583. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus were sitting in an inhabited area looking here and there...

“Okkhittacakkhu [V 0.0247] antaraghare nisīdissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will sit in an inhabited area with eyes downcast,’ this is a training to be observed.

Okkhittacakkhunā antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ yugamattaṃ pekkhantena. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca tahaṃ tahaṃ olokento antaraghare nisīdati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should sit in an inhabited area with eyes downcast, looking a yoke’s length. Whichever bhikkhu, on account of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area looking here and there, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti [T 2.0535] asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, āpadāsu, ummattakassa,

There is no offense: if it is unintentional; if one is unmindful; for one who does not know; for one who is sick; in times of danger; for one who is insane;

Ādikammikassāti.

or for the first offender.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The eighth training rule is concluded.

584. Tena [P 4.0187] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ukkhittakāya antaraghare gacchanti…pe….

584. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus were going into an inhabited area with robes hitched up...

“Na ukkhittakāya antaraghare gamissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not go into an inhabited area with my robe hitched up,’ this is a training to be observed.

Na ukkhittakāya antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca ekato vā ubhato vā ukkhipitvā antaraghare gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not go into an inhabited area with robe hitched up. Whichever bhikkhu, on account of disrespect, goes into an inhabited area with his robe hitched up on one or both sides, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, āpadāsu, ummattakassa,

There is no offense: if it is unintentional; if one is unmindful; for one who does not know; for one who is sick; in times of danger; for one who is insane;

Ādikammikassāti.

or for the first offender.

Navamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The ninth training rule is concluded.

585. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ukkhittakāya antaraghare nisīdanti…pe….

585. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus were sitting in an inhabited area with robes hitched up...

“Na ukkhittakāya antaraghare nisīdissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not sit in an inhabited area with my robe hitched up,’ this is a training to be observed.

Na ukkhittakāya antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca ekato vā ubhato vā ukkhipitvā antaraghare nisīdati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not sit in an inhabited area with robe hitched up. Whichever bhikkhu, on account of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area with his robe hitched up on one or both sides, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti [M 0.0243][V 0.0248] asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, vāsūpagatassa, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense: if it is unintentional; if one is unmindful; for one who does not know; for one who is sick; for one who has taken up residence; in times of danger; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The tenth training rule is concluded.

Parimaṇḍalavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Parimaṇḍala Chapter.

2. Ujjagghikavaggo

2. The Chapter on Loud Laughter.

586. Tena [T 2.0536] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū mahāhasitaṃ hasantā antaraghare gacchanti…pe….

586. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus were going into an inhabited area laughing loudly...

“Na ujjagghikāya antaraghare gamissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not go into an inhabited area with loud laughter,’ this is a training to be observed.

Na ujjagghikāya antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca mahāhasitaṃ hasanto antaraghare gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not go into an inhabited area with loud laughter. Whichever bhikkhu, on account of disrespect, goes into an inhabited area laughing loudly, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, hasanīyasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ mihitamattaṃ karoti, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense: if it is unintentional; if one is unmindful; for one who does not know; for one who is sick; if, when there is a reason for laughter, one merely smiles; in times of danger; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The first training rule is concluded.

587. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū mahāhasitaṃ hasantā antaraghare nisīdanti…pe….

587. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus were sitting in an inhabited area laughing loudly...

“Na ujjagghikāya antaraghare nisīdissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not sit in an inhabited area with loud laughter,’ this is a training to be observed.

Na [V 0.0249] ujjagghikāya antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca mahāhasitaṃ hasanto antaraghare nisīdati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not sit in an inhabited area with loud laughter. Whichever bhikkhu, on account of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area laughing loudly, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, hasanīyasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ mihitamattaṃ karoti, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense: if it is unintentional; if one is unmindful; for one who does not know; for one who is sick; if, when there is a reason for laughter, one merely smiles; in times of danger; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The second training rule is concluded.

588. Tena [T 2.0537][M 0.0244] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāsaddaṃ mahāsaddaṃ karontā antaraghare gacchanti…pe….

588. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were going into inhabited areas making high and loud noises... and so on.

“Appasaddo antaraghare gamissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“‘I will go into an inhabited area with little sound,’ this is a training to be observed.”

Appasaddena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca uccāsaddaṃ mahāsaddaṃ karonto antaraghare gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should go into an inhabited area with little sound. Whichever monk, out of disrespect, goes into an inhabited area making high and loud noises, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who does not know, for one who is sick, in times of calamity, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The third training rule is concluded.

589. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāsaddaṃ mahāsaddaṃ karontā antaraghare nisīdanti…pe….

589. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were sitting in inhabited areas making high and loud noises... and so on.

“Appasaddo antaraghare nisīdissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“‘I will sit in an inhabited area with little sound,’ this is a training to be observed.”

Appasaddena antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca uccāsaddaṃ mahāsaddaṃ karonto antaraghare nisīdati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should sit in an inhabited area with little sound. Whichever monk, out of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area making high and loud noises, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti [V 0.0250] asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional... and so on... or for the first offender.

Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fourth training rule is concluded.

590. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho [P 4.0188] pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kāyappacālakaṃ antaraghare gacchanti kāyaṃ olambentā…pe….

590. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were going into inhabited areas swaying the body and letting the body droop... and so on.

“Na kāyappacālakaṃ antaraghare gamissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“‘I will not go into an inhabited area swaying the body,’ this is a training to be observed.”

Na kāyappacālakaṃ antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Kāyaṃ paggahetvā gantabbaṃ[T 2.0538]. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca kāyappacālakaṃ antaraghare gacchati kāyaṃ olambento, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not go into an inhabited area swaying the body. One should go with the body held up. Whichever monk, out of disrespect, goes into an inhabited area swaying the body and letting the body droop, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional... and so on... or for the first offender.

Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fifth training rule is concluded.

591. Tena [M 0.0245] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kāyappacālakaṃ antaraghare nisīdanti, kāyaṃ olambentā…pe….

591. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were sitting in inhabited areas swaying the body and letting the body droop... and so on.

“Na kāyappacālakaṃ antaraghare nisīdissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“‘I will not sit in an inhabited area swaying the body,’ this is a training to be observed.”

Na kāyappacālakaṃ antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Kāyaṃ paggahetvā nisīditabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca kāyappacālakaṃ antaraghare nisīdati kāyaṃ olambento, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not sit in an inhabited area swaying the body. One should sit with the body held up. Whichever monk, out of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area swaying the body and letting the body droop, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, vāsūpagatassa, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who does not know, for one who is sick, for one who has taken up residence, in times of calamity, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The sixth training rule is concluded.

592. Tena [V 0.0251] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bāhuppacālakaṃ antaraghare gacchanti bāhuṃ olambentā…pe….

592. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. At that time, the group-of-six monks went into inhabited areas swaying their arms, letting their arms droop... and so on.

“Na bāhuppacālakaṃ antaraghare gamissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“‘I will not go into an inhabited area swaying my arms,’ this is a training to be observed.”

Na bāhuppacālakaṃ antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Bāhuṃ paggahetvā gantabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca bāhuppacālakaṃ antaraghare gacchati bāhuṃ olambento, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not go into an inhabited area swaying the arms. One should go with arms held up. Any monk who, out of disrespect, goes into an inhabited area swaying his arms, letting them droop, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional... and so on... or for the first offender.

Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The seventh training rule is concluded.

593. Tena [T 2.0539] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bāhuppacālakaṃ antaraghare nisīdanti bāhuṃ olambentā…pe….

593. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. At that time, the group-of-six monks sat in inhabited areas swaying their arms, letting their arms droop... and so on.

“Na bāhuppacālakaṃ antaraghare nisīdissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“‘I will not sit in an inhabited area swaying my arms,’ this is a training to be observed.”

Na bāhuppacālakaṃ antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Bāhuṃ paggahetvā nisīditabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca bāhuppacālakaṃ antaraghare nisīdati bāhuṃ olambento, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not sit in an inhabited area swaying the arms. One should sit with arms held up. Any monk who, out of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area swaying his arms, letting them droop, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti [M 0.0246] asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, vāsūpagatassa, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who does not know, for one who is sick, for one who has taken up residence, in times of calamity, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The eighth training rule is concluded.

594. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍakassa ārāme[V 0.0252]. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sīsappacālakaṃ antaraghare gacchanti sīsaṃ olambentā…pe….

594. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. At that time, the group-of-six monks went into inhabited areas swaying their heads and letting their heads droop... and so on.

“Na sīsappacālakaṃ antaraghare gamissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“‘I will not go into an inhabited area swaying my head,’ this is a training to be observed.”

Na sīsappacālakaṃ antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Sīsaṃ paggahetvā gantabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca sīsappacālakaṃ antaraghare gacchati sīsaṃ olambento, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not go into an inhabited area swaying the head. One should go with the head held up. Any monk who, out of disrespect, goes into an inhabited area swaying his head, letting it droop, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional... and so on... or for the first offender.

Navamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The ninth training rule is concluded.

595. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sīsappacālakaṃ antaraghare nisīdanti sīsaṃ olambentā…pe….

595. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. At that time, the group-of-six monks sat in inhabited areas swaying their heads, letting their heads droop... and so on.

“Na sīsappacālakaṃ antaraghare nisīdissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“‘I will not sit in an inhabited area swaying my head,’ this is a training to be observed.”

Na sīsappacālakaṃ antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Sīsaṃ paggahetvā nisīditabbaṃ[T 2.0540]. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca sīsappacālakaṃ antaraghare nisīdati sīsaṃ olambento, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not sit in an inhabited area swaying the head. One should sit with the head held up. Any monk who, out of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area swaying his head, letting it droop, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, vāsūpagatassa, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who is unknowing, for one who is sick, for one who has taken up residence, in times of danger, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The tenth training rule is concluded.

Ujjagghikavaggo dutiyo.

The Second Chapter on Laughing Loudly is concluded.

3. Khambhakatavaggo

3. The Chapter on Arms Akimbo

596. Tena [M 0.0247][V 0.0253] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū khambhakatā antaraghare gacchanti…pe….

596. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were going into an inhabited area with their arms akimbo...and so on.

“Na khambhakato antaraghare gamissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not go into an inhabited area with arms akimbo,’ this is a training to be observed.

Na [P 4.0189] khambhakatena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca ekato vā ubhato vā khambhaṃ katvā antaraghare gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not go into an inhabited area with arms akimbo. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, goes into an inhabited area with one arm akimbo or both arms akimbo, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional...and so on...or for the first offender.

Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The first training rule is concluded.

597. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū khambhakatā antaraghare nisīdanti…pe….

597. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were sitting in an inhabited area with their arms akimbo...and so on.

“Na khambhakato antaraghare nisīdissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not sit in an inhabited area with arms akimbo,’ this is a training to be observed.

Na khambhakatena antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca ekato vā ubhato vā khambhaṃ katvā antaraghare nisīdati, āpatti [T 2.0541] dukkaṭassa.

One should not sit in an inhabited area with arms akimbo. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area with one arm akimbo or both arms akimbo, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, vāsūpagatassa, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who is unknowing, for one who is sick, for one who has taken up residence, in times of danger, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The second training rule is concluded.

598. Tena [V 0.0254] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sasīsaṃ pārupitvā antaraghare gacchanti…pe….

598. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were going into an inhabited area having covered themselves including their heads...and so on.

“Na oguṇṭhito antaraghare gamissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not go into an inhabited area with my head covered,’ this is a training to be observed.

Na oguṇṭhitena antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca sasīsaṃ pārupitvā antaraghare gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not go into an inhabited area with the head covered. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, goes into an inhabited area having covered himself including his head, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional...and so on...or for the first offender.

Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The third training rule is concluded.

599. Tena [M 0.0248] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sasīsaṃ pārupitvā antaraghare nisīdanti…pe….

599. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were sitting in an inhabited area having covered themselves including their heads...and so on.

“Na oguṇṭhito antaraghare nisīdissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not sit in an inhabited area with my head covered,’ this is a training to be observed.

Na oguṇṭhitena antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca sasīsaṃ pārupitvā antaraghare nisīdati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not sit in an inhabited area with the head covered. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area having covered himself including his head, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, vāsūpagatassa, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who is unknowing, for one who is sick, for one who has taken up residence, in times of danger, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fourth training rule is concluded.

600. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ukkuṭikāya antaraghare gacchanti…pe….

600. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were going into an inhabited area on tiptoe...and so on.

“Na [V 0.0255] ukkuṭikāya antaraghare gamissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not go into an inhabited area on tiptoe,’ this is a training to be observed.

Na [T 2.0542] ukkuṭikāya antaraghare gantabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca ukkuṭikāya antaraghare gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not go into an inhabited area on tiptoe. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, goes into an inhabited area on tiptoe, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional...and so on...or for the first offender.

Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fifth training rule is concluded.

601. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū pallatthikāya pallattikāya (ka.) antaraghare nisīdanti…pe….

601. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were sitting in an inhabited area with a supporting-strap posture...and so on.

“Na pallatthikāya antaraghare nisīdissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not sit in an inhabited area with a supporting-strap posture,’ this is a training to be observed.

Na pallatthikāya antaraghare nisīditabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca hatthapallatthikāya vā dussapallatthikāya vā antaraghare nisīdati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not sit in an inhabited area with a supporting-strap posture. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area using a hand-strap or a cloth-strap, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, vāsūpagatassa, āpadāsu,

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who is unknowing, for one who is sick, for one who has taken up residence, or in times of danger.

Ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The sixth training rule is concluded.

602. Tena [M 0.0249] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho [P 4.0190] pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū asakkaccaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paṭiggaṇhanti chaḍḍetukāmā viya…pe….

602. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks received almsfood disrespectfully, as if wishing to discard it...and so on.

“Sakkaccaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paṭiggahessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will receive almsfood respectfully,’ this is a training to be observed.

Sakkaccaṃ piṇḍapāto paṭiggahetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca asakkaccaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paṭiggaṇhāti chaḍḍetukāmo viya, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Almsfood is to be received respectfully. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, receives almsfood disrespectfully, as if wishing to discard it, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti [T 2.0543][V 0.0256] asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional...and so on...or for the first offender.

Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The seventh training rule is concluded.

603. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū tahaṃ tahaṃ olokentā piṇḍapātaṃ paṭiggaṇhanti, ākirantepi atikkantepi atikkamantepi (sī.) na jānanti…pe….

603. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. At that time, the group-of-six monks, looking here and there, received almsfood; they did not know when it was being poured in or when it had passed by... and so on.

“Pattasaññī piṇḍapātaṃ paṭiggahessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“I will receive almsfood with my perception on the bowl”; this is a training to be done.

Pattasaññinā piṇḍapāto paṭiggahetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca tahaṃ tahaṃ olokento piṇḍapātaṃ paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Almsfood is to be received with perception on the bowl. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, receives almsfood while looking here and there, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional... and so on... or for the first offender.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The eighth training rule is concluded.

604. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū piṇḍapātaṃ paṭiggaṇhantā sūpaññeva bahuṃ paṭiggaṇhanti…pe….

604. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks, while receiving almsfood, received a large amount of only curry... and so on.

“Samasūpakaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paṭiggahessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“I will receive almsfood balanced with curry”; this is a training to be done.

Sūpo nāma dve sūpā – muggasūpo, māsasūpo. Hatthahāriyo samasūpako piṇḍapāto paṭiggahetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca sūpaññeva bahuṃ paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

What is called curry is of two kinds: green gram curry and black gram curry. Almsfood balanced with curry that can be taken by hand is to be received. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, receives a large amount of only curry, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, rasarase, ñātakānaṃ pavāritānaṃ, aññassatthāya, attano dhanena, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who does not know, for one who is sick, in the case of various savory liquids, for relatives and for those who have invited one, for the sake of another, with one's own funds, in times of adversity, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Navamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The ninth training rule is concluded.

605. Tena [T 2.0544][M 0.0250][V 0.0257] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū thūpīkataṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paṭiggaṇhanti…pe….

605. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. At that time, the group-of-six monks received almsfood piled up high... and so on.

“Samatittikaṃ samatitthikaṃ (ka.) piṇḍapātaṃ paṭiggahessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“I will receive almsfood level with the brim”; this is a training to be done.

Samatittiko [P 4.0191] samatitthikaṃ (ka.) piṇḍapāto paṭiggahetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca thūpīkataṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Almsfood is to be received level with the brim. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, receives almsfood piled up high, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who does not know, in times of adversity, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The tenth training rule is concluded.

Khambhakatavaggo tatiyo.

The Third Chapter on Arms Akimbo.

4. Sakkaccavaggo

4. The Chapter on Respectfulness

606. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū asakkaccaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjanti abhuñjitukāmā viya…pe….

606. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks ate almsfood disrespectfully, as if not wanting to eat…

“Sakkaccaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will eat almsfood respectfully’—this is the training to be observed.

Sakkaccaṃ piṇḍapāto bhuñjitabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca asakkaccaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Almsfood should be eaten respectfully. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, eats almsfood disrespectfully, commits an offense of wrongdoing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, āpadāsu, ummattakassa,

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who does not know, for one who is sick, in times of danger, for one who is insane,

Ādikammikassāti.

or for the first offender.

Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The first training rule is concluded.

607. Tena [V 0.0258] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū tahaṃ tahaṃ olokentā piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjanti, ākirantepi atikkantepi na jānanti…pe…[T 2.0545].

607. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were eating almsfood while looking here and there; they were not aware of those serving or those who had passed by…

“Pattasaññī [M 0.0251] piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will eat almsfood with my perception on the bowl’—this is the training to be observed.

Pattasaññinā piṇḍapāto bhuñjitabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca tahaṃ tahaṃ olokento piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Almsfood should be eaten with one's perception on the bowl. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, eats almsfood while looking here and there, commits an offense of wrongdoing.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional… and so on... or for the first offender.

Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The second training rule is concluded.

608. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū tahaṃ tahaṃ omasitvā omadditvā (ka.) piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjanti…pe….

608. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were eating almsfood, scooping from here and there…

“Sapadānaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will eat almsfood in sequence’—this is the training to be observed.

Sapadānaṃ piṇḍapāto bhuñjitabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca tahaṃ tahaṃ omasitvā omadditvā (ka.) piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Almsfood should be eaten in sequence. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, eats almsfood by scooping from here and there, commits an offense of wrongdoing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, aññesaṃ dento omasati, aññassa bhājane ākiranto omasati, uttaribhaṅge, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who does not know, for one who is sick; if one scoops from various places while giving to others; if one scoops from various places while putting food into another's bowl; in the case of side dishes; in times of danger; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The third training rule is concluded.

609. Tena [P 4.0192] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme[V 0.0259]. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjantā sūpaññeva bahuṃ bhuñjanti…pe….

609. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks, while eating almsfood, ate a large amount of only curry…

“Samasūpakaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will eat almsfood with a proportionate amount of curry’—this is the training to be observed.

Sūpo nāma dve sūpā – muggasūpo, māsasūpo hatthahāriyo. Samasūpako piṇḍapāto bhuñjitabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca sūpaññeva bahuṃ bhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

What is called curry is of two kinds that can be taken by hand: green gram curry and black gram curry. Almsfood should be eaten with a proportionate amount of curry. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, eats a large amount of only curry, commits an offense of wrongdoing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, rasarase[T 2.0546], ñātakānaṃ pavāritānaṃ, attano dhanena, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who does not know, for one who is sick; in the case of various sauces or broths; when eating the food of relatives or of those who have invited one; when eating with one’s own wealth; in times of danger; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fourth training rule is concluded.

610. Tena [M 0.0252] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū thūpakato omadditvā piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjanti…pe….

610. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were eating almsfood by pressing down from the top of the mound of food…

“Na thūpakato omadditvā piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not eat almsfood by pressing down from the top of the mound of food’—this is the training to be observed.

Na thūpakato omadditvā piṇḍapāto bhuñjitabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca thūpakato omadditvā piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjati āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Almsfood should not be eaten by pressing down from the top of the mound of food. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, eats almsfood by pressing down from the top of the mound of food, commits an offense of wrongdoing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, parittake sese ekato saṃkaḍḍhitvā omadditvā bhuñjati, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who does not know, for one who is sick; if, when only a small amount remains, one gathers it together, presses it down, and eats; in times of danger; for one who is insane; and for the first offender.

Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fifth training rule is concluded.

611. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sūpampi byañjanampi odanena paṭicchādenti bhiyyokamyataṃ upādāya…pe….

611. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks would conceal both bean curry and other curries with rice on account of a desire for more…

“Na [V 0.0260] sūpaṃ vā byañjanaṃ vā odanena paṭicchādessāmi bhiyyokamyataṃ upādāyāti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not conceal bean curry or other curries with rice on account of a desire for more’—this is the training to be observed.

Na sūpaṃ vā byañjanaṃ vā odanena paṭicchādetabbaṃ bhiyyokamyataṃ upādāya. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca sūpaṃ vā byañjanaṃ vā odanena paṭicchādeti bhiyyokamyataṃ upādāya, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Bean curry or other curries should not be concealed with rice on account of a desire for more. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, conceals bean curry or other curries with rice on account of a desire for more, commits an offense of wrongdoing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, sāmikā paṭicchādetvā denti, na bhiyyokamyataṃ upādāya, āpadāsu, ummattakassa[T 2.0547], ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional; if one is unmindful; for one who does not know; if the owners give it having concealed it; if it is not on account of a desire for more; in times of danger; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The sixth training rule is concluded.

612. Tena [P 4.0193] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sūpampi odanampi attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā sūpampi odanampi attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjissanti! Kassa sampannaṃ na manāpaṃ[M 0.0253]! Kassa sāduṃ na ruccatī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sūpampi odanampi attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, sūpampi odanampi attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjathāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, sūpampi odanampi attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjissatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

612. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time the group-of-six monks were eating soup or rice after requesting it for their own sake. People complained, grumbled, and spread it about: ‘How can these Sakyan recluses eat soup or rice after requesting it for their own sake! Who does not like what is well-provided? Who does not enjoy what is delicious?’ The monks heard these people complaining, grumbling, and spreading it about. Those monks who were of few wishes… complained, grumbled, and spread it about: ‘How can the group-of-six monks eat soup or rice after requesting it for their own sake!’… ‘Is it true, monks, that you eat soup or rice after requesting it for your own sake?’ ‘It is true, Blessed One.’ The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… ‘How can you, foolish men, eat soup or rice after requesting it for your own sake! This is not, foolish men, for inspiring confidence in the unconfident…’ And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

“Na sūpaṃ vā odanaṃ vā attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not eat soup or rice, having requested it for my own sake’—this is the training to be done.

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And thus this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the monks.

613. Tena [V 0.0261] kho pana samayena bhikkhū gilānā honti. Gilānapucchakā bhikkhū gilāne bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “kaccāvuso, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīya”nti? “Pubbe mayaṃ, āvuso, sūpampi odanampi attano atthāya [T 2.0548] viññāpetvā bhuñjāma, tena no phāsu hoti. Idāni pana – “bhagavatā paṭikkhitta”nti kukkuccāyantā na viññāpema, tena no na phāsu hotī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānena bhikkhunā sūpampi odanampi attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

613. Now at that time, some monks were sick. Monks visiting the sick said to the sick monks: ‘Are you enduring, friends? Are you getting by?’ ‘Formerly, friends, we would request soup or rice for our own sake and eat it, and that was comfortable for us. But now, being scrupulous that “It has been forbidden by the Blessed One,” we do not request it, and so it is not comfortable for us.’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One… ‘I allow, monks, a sick monk to eat soup or rice, having requested it for his own sake. And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

“Na sūpaṃ vā odanaṃ vā agilāno attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘When not sick, I will not eat soup or rice, having requested it for my own sake’—this is the training to be done.

Na sūpaṃ vā odanaṃ vā agilānena attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca sūpaṃ vā odanaṃ vā agilāno attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Soup or rice is not to be eaten by one who is not sick, having requested it for one's own sake. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, being not sick, eats soup or rice, having requested it for their own sake, commits an offense of wrongdoing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, ñātakānaṃ pavāritānaṃ, aññassatthāya, attano dhanena, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional; if one is unmindful; for one who does not know; for one who is sick; for those invited by relatives; for the sake of another; with one’s own wealth; in times of danger; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The seventh training rule is concluded.

614. Tena [P 4.0194][M 0.0254] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ujjhānasaññī paresaṃ pattaṃ olokenti…pe….

614. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. At that time the group-of-six monks, with the intention of finding fault, were looking at others’ bowls…

“Na ujjhānasaññī paresaṃ pattaṃ olokessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not look at another’s bowl with the intention of finding fault’—this is the training to be done.

Na ujjhānasaññinā paresaṃ patto oloketabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca ujjhānasaññī paresaṃ pattaṃ oloketi, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Another’s bowl is not to be looked at with the intention of finding fault. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, looks at another’s bowl with the intention of finding fault, commits an offense of wrongdoing.

Anāpatti [V 0.0262] asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, “dassāmī”ti vā [T 2.0549] “dāpessāmī”ti vā oloketi, na ujjhānasaññissa, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional; if one is unmindful; for one who does not know; if one looks with the thought, ‘I will give,’ or, ‘I will have it given’; if one does not have the intention of finding fault; in times of danger; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The eighth training rule is concluded.

615. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū mahantaṃ kabaḷaṃ karonti…pe….

615. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time the group-of-six monks were making large mouthfuls…

“Nātimahantaṃ kabaḷaṃ karissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not make an excessively large mouthful’—this is the training to be done.

Nātimahanto kabaḷo kātabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca mahantaṃ kabaḷaṃ karoti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

An excessively large mouthful is not to be made. Whichever monk, on account of disrespect, makes a large mouthful, commits an offense of wrongdoing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, khajjake, phalāphale, uttaribhaṅge, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional; if one is unmindful; for one who does not know; for one who is sick; in the case of hard foods; in the case of fruits; in the case of side dishes; in times of danger; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Navamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The ninth training rule is concluded.

616. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū dīghaṃ ālopaṃ karonti…pe….

616. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time the group-of-six bhikkhus were making long morsels…

“Parimaṇḍalaṃ ālopaṃ karissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will make a rounded morsel’—this training is to be done.

Parimaṇḍalo ālopo kātabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca dīghaṃ ālopaṃ karoti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

A rounded morsel is to be made. Whoever, on account of disrespect, makes a long morsel, commits an offense of wrongdoing.

Anāpatti [M 0.0255] asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, khajjake, phalāphale, uttaribhaṅge, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional; if one is unmindful; if one is unknowing; for one who is sick; in the case of hard foods; in the case of fruits; in the case of side dishes; in times of danger; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The tenth training rule is finished.

Sakkaccavaggo catuttho.

The Fourth Chapter: On Respectful Conduct.

5. Kabaḷavaggo

5. The Chapter on Morsels

617. Tena [T 2.0550][V 0.0263] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū anāhaṭe kabaḷe mukhadvāraṃ vivaranti…pe….

617. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus would open their mouths before a morsel was brought to it…

“Na [P 4.0195] anāhaṭe kabaḷe mukhadvāraṃ vivarissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not open my mouth before the morsel has been brought’—this training is to be done.

Na anāhaṭe kabaḷe mukhadvāraṃ vivaritabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca anāhaṭe kabaḷe mukhadvāraṃ vivarati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The mouth should not be opened before the morsel has been brought. Whatever bhikkhu, on account of disrespect, opens his mouth before the morsel has been brought, commits an offense of wrongdoing.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional… for the first offender.

Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The first training rule is finished.

618. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhuñjamānā sabbaṃ hatthaṃ mukhe pakkhipanti…pe….

618. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus, while eating, would put their entire hand into their mouths…

“Na bhuñjamāno sabbaṃ hatthaṃ mukhe pakkhipissāmīti sikkhākaraṇīyā”ti.

‘While eating, I will not put my entire hand into my mouth’—this training is to be done.

Na bhuñjamānena sabbo hattho mukhe pakkhipitabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca bhuñjamāno sabbaṃ hatthaṃ mukhe pakkhipati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

While eating, the entire hand should not be put into the mouth. Whatever bhikkhu, on account of disrespect, while eating, puts his entire hand into his mouth, commits an offense of wrongdoing.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional… for the first offender.

Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The second training rule is finished.

619. Tena [V 0.0264] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sakabaḷena mukhena byāharanti…pe….

619. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus would speak with a morsel in the mouth…

“Na [M 0.0256] sakabaḷena mukhena byāharissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not speak with a morsel in my mouth’—this training is to be done.

Na sakabaḷena mukhena byāharitabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca sakabaḷena [T 2.0551] mukhena byāharati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not speak with a morsel in the mouth. Whatever bhikkhu, on account of disrespect, speaks with a morsel in his mouth, commits an offense of wrongdoing.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional… for the first offender.

Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The third training rule is finished.

620. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū piṇḍukkhepakaṃ bhuñjanti…pe….

620. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus would eat by tossing up morsels…

“Na piṇḍukkhepakaṃ bhuñjissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not eat by tossing up morsels’—this training is to be done.

Na piṇḍukkhepakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca piṇḍukkhepakaṃ bhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not eat by tossing up morsels. Whatever bhikkhu, on account of disrespect, eats by tossing up morsels, commits an offense of wrongdoing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, khajjake, phalāphale, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who is unknowing, for one who is sick, in the case of hard food, in the case of fruits, in times of danger, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fourth training rule is finished.

621. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kabaḷāvacchedakaṃ bhuñjanti…pe….

621. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus would eat by cutting off from the morsel…

“Na [P 4.0196] kabaḷāvacchedakaṃ bhuñjissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not eat by cutting off from the morsel’—this training is to be done.

Na [V 0.0265] kabaḷāvacchedakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca kabaḷāvacchedakaṃ bhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not eat by cutting off from the morsel. Whatever bhikkhu, on account of disrespect, eats by cutting off from the morsel, commits an offense of wrongdoing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, khajjake phalāphale, uttaribhaṅge, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who is unknowing, for one who is sick, in the case of hard food, in the case of fruits, in the case of side dishes, in times of danger, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fifth training rule is finished.

622. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū avagaṇḍakārakaṃ bhuñjanti…pe….

622. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus would eat making a bulge in the cheek…

“Na [M 0.0257] avagaṇḍakārakaṃ bhuñjissāmīti sikkhā [T 2.0552] karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not eat making a bulge in the cheek’—this training is to be done.

Na avagaṇḍakārakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca ekato vā ubhato vā gaṇḍaṃ katvā bhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not eat making a bulge in the cheek. Whatever bhikkhu, on account of disrespect, eats having made a bulge in the cheek on one side or on both sides, commits an offense of wrongdoing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, phalāphale, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who is unknowing, for one who is sick, in the case of fruits, in times of danger, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The sixth training rule is finished.

623. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū hatthaniddhunakaṃ bhuñjanti…pe….

623. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus were eating while shaking their hands…

“Na hatthaniddhunakaṃ bhuñjissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not eat while shaking my hand’—this training is to be done.

Na hatthaniddhunakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca hatthaniddhunakaṃ bhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not eat while shaking the hand. Whoever, on account of disrespect, eats while shaking the hand, commits an offense of wrongdoing.

Anāpatti [V 0.0266] asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, kacavaraṃ chaḍḍento hatthaṃ niddhunāti, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense: if it is unintentional, if it is due to unmindfulness, for one who is unknowing, for one who is sick, if one shakes the hand while discarding refuse, in times of calamity, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The seventh training rule is concluded.

624. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sitthāvakārakaṃ bhuñjanti…pe….

624. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. At that time, the group-of-six monks were eating while scattering grains of rice... and so on...

“Na sitthāvakārakaṃ bhuñjissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“I will not eat while scattering grains of rice”—this is the training to be observed.

Na sitthāvakārakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca sitthāvakārakaṃ bhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not eat while scattering grains of rice. Whoever, due to disrespect, eats while scattering grains of rice, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, kacavaraṃ [P 4.0197] chaḍḍento sitthaṃ chaḍḍayati, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti[T 2.0553].

There is no offense: if it is unintentional, if it is due to unmindfulness, for one who is unknowing, for one who is sick, if one discards grains of rice while discarding refuse, in times of calamity, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The eighth training rule is concluded.

625. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū jivhānicchārakaṃ bhuñjanti…pe….

625. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. At that time, the group-of-six monks were eating while sticking out their tongues... and so on...

“Na [M 0.0258] jivhānicchārakaṃ bhuñjissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“I will not eat while sticking out my tongue”—this is the training to be observed.

Na jivhānicchārakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca jivhānicchārakaṃ bhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not eat while sticking out the tongue. Whoever, due to disrespect, eats while sticking out the tongue, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if unintentional... and so on... for the first offender.

Navamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The ninth training rule is concluded.

626. Tena [V 0.0267] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū capucapukārakaṃ bhuñjanti…pe….

626. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. At that time, the group-of-six monks were eating while making 'capu capu' sounds... and so on...

“Na capucapukārakaṃ bhuñjissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“I will not eat while making 'capu capu' sounds”—this is the training to be observed.

Na capucapukārakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca capucapukārakaṃ bhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not eat while making 'capu capu' sounds. Whoever, due to disrespect, eats while making 'capu capu' sounds, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if unintentional... and so on... for the first offender.

Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The tenth training rule is concluded.

Kabaḷavaggo pañcamo.

The Chapter on Morsels is the fifth.

6. Surusuruvaggo

6. The Chapter on Slurping

627. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā kosambiyaṃ viharati ghositārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarena brāhmaṇena saṅghassa payopānaṃ [T 2.0554] paṭiyattaṃ hoti. Bhikkhū surusurukārakaṃ khīraṃ pivanti. Aññataro naṭapubbako bhikkhu evamāha – “sabboyaṃ maññe saṅgho sītīkato”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhu saṅghaṃ ārabbha davaṃ karissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, bhikkhu, saṅghaṃ ārabbha davaṃ akāsīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, saṅghaṃ ārabbha davaṃ karissasi! Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, buddhaṃ vā dhammaṃ vā [M 0.0259] saṅghaṃ vā ārabbha davo kātabbo. Yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā taṃ bhikkhuṃ anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā dubbharatāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

627. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Kosambī in Ghosita’s Monastery. Now at that time, a certain brahmin had prepared a milk-drink for the Saṅgha. The monks were drinking the milk making a slurping sound. A certain monk who had formerly been an actor said this: “It seems this entire Saṅgha has been made cool.” Those monks who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can a monk jest concerning the Saṅgha?”… He asked: “Is it true, as is said, that you, monk, jested concerning the Saṅgha?” He said: “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “Foolish man, how indeed can you jest concerning the Saṅgha! Foolish man, this is not for the confidence of the faithless…” Having rebuked him… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks, saying: “Monks, one should not jest concerning the Buddha, the Dhamma, or the Saṅgha. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong conduct.” Then the Blessed One, having rebuked that monk in many ways for being difficult to support… said: “And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Na [V 0.0268] surusurukārakaṃ bhuñjissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“I will not eat making a slurping sound”—this training is to be undertaken.

Na surusurukārakaṃ [P 4.0198] bhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca surusurukārakaṃ bhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not eat making a slurping sound. Whoever, due to disrespect, eats making a slurping sound, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional… for the first offender.

Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The first training rule is finished.

628. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū hatthanillehakaṃ bhuñjanti…pe….

628. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were eating while licking their hands…

“Na hatthanillehakaṃ bhuñjissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“I will not eat while licking the hand”—this training is to be undertaken.

Na [T 2.0555] hatthanillehakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca hatthanillehakaṃ bhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not eat while licking the hand. Whoever, due to disrespect, eats while licking the hand, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional… for the first offender.

Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The second training rule is finished.

629. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū pattanillehakaṃ bhuñjanti…pe….

629. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were eating while licking their bowls…

“Na pattanillehakaṃ bhuñjissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“I will not eat while licking the bowl”—this training is to be undertaken.

Na pattanillehakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca pattanillehakaṃ bhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not eat while licking the bowl. Whoever, due to disrespect, eats while licking the bowl, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti [V 0.0269] asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, parittake sese ekato saṅkaḍḍhitvā nillehitvā bhuñjati, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who does not know, for one who is ill, if, when the remainder is small, one gathers it together, licks it, and eats, in times of danger, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The third training rule is finished.

630. Tena [M 0.0260] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū oṭṭhanillehakaṃ bhuñjanti…pe….

630. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were eating while licking their lips…

“Na oṭṭhanillehakaṃ bhuñjissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“I will not eat while licking the lips”—this training is to be undertaken.

Na oṭṭhanillehakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca oṭṭhanillehakaṃ bhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not eat while licking the lips. Whoever, due to disrespect, eats while licking the lips, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional… for the first offender.

Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fourth training rule is finished.

631. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā bhaggesu viharati susumāragire suṃsumāragire (sī. syā.), saṃsumāragire (ka.) bhesakaḷāvane [T 2.0556] migadāye. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū kokanade kokanude (ka.) pāsāde sāmisena hatthena pānīyathālakaṃ paṭiggaṇhanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā sāmisena hatthena pānīyathālakaṃ paṭiggahessanti, seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhū sāmisena hatthena pānīyathālakaṃ paṭiggahessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhū sāmisena hatthena pānīyathālakaṃ paṭiggaṇhantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā sāmisena hatthena pānīyathālakaṃ paṭiggahessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

631. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling among the Bhaggas at Susumāragiri, in the Bhesakaḷā forest, a sanctuary for beasts. Now at that time, at the Kokanada palace, monks were taking a water vessel with a hand soiled with food. The people complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the Sakyan ascetics take a water vessel with a hand soiled with food, just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those monks who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the monks take a water vessel with a hand soiled with food?”… “Is it true, as is said, monks, that monks take a water vessel with a hand soiled with food?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Blessed One, the Buddha, rebuked them… “Monks, how indeed can those foolish men take a water vessel with a hand soiled with food! Monks, this is not for inspiring faith in the uninspired… And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Na sāmisena hatthena pānīyathālakaṃ paṭiggahessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not take a water vessel with a hand soiled with food’; this training is to be undertaken.

Na [P 4.0199][V 0.0270] sāmisena hatthena pānīyathālako paṭiggahetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca sāmisena hatthena pānīyathālakaṃ paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

A water vessel is not to be taken with a hand soiled with food. Whichever monk, out of disrespect, takes a water vessel with a hand soiled with food, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti [M 0.0261] asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, “dhovissāmī”ti vā “dhovāpessāmī”ti vā paṭiggaṇhāti, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who does not know, for one who is ill, if one takes it thinking, ‘I will wash it’ or ‘I will have it washed,’ in times of danger, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fifth training rule is concluded.

632. Tena [T 2.0557] samayena buddho bhagavā bhaggesu viharati susumāragire bhesakaḷāvane migadāye. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū kokanade pāsāde sasitthakaṃ pattadhovanaṃ antaraghare chaḍḍenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā sasitthakaṃ pattadhovanaṃ antaraghare chaḍḍessanti, seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhū sasitthakaṃ pattadhovanaṃ antaraghare chaḍḍessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhū sasitthakaṃ pattadhovanaṃ antaraghare chaḍḍentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā sasitthakaṃ pattadhovanaṃ antaraghare chaḍḍessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

632. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling among the Bhaggas at Susumāragiri, in the Bhesakaḷā forest, a sanctuary for beasts. Now at that time, at the Kokanada palace, monks were discarding bowl-washing water containing rice grains within an inhabited area. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can the Sakyan ascetics discard bowl-washing water containing rice grains within an inhabited area, just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures?” The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those monks who were of few wishes... complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can monks discard bowl-washing water containing rice grains within an inhabited area?”... “Is it true, monks, that monks discard bowl-washing water containing rice grains within an inhabited area?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Blessed One, the Buddha, rebuked them... “How can those foolish men discard bowl-washing water containing rice grains within an inhabited area! Monks, this is not for inspiring faith in the uninspired... And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Na sasitthakaṃ pattadhovanaṃ antaraghare chaḍḍessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not discard bowl-washing water containing rice grains within an inhabited area’; this training is to be undertaken.

Na sasitthakaṃ pattadhovanaṃ antaraghare chaḍḍetabbaṃ. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca sasitthakaṃ pattadhovanaṃ antaraghare chaḍḍeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Bowl-washing water containing rice grains is not to be discarded within an inhabited area. Whichever monk, out of disrespect, discards bowl-washing water containing rice grains within an inhabited area, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, uddharitvā vā bhinditvā vā paṭiggahe vā nīharitvā vā chaḍḍeti, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.
