There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who does not know, for one who is ill, if one discards it after taking out the rice grains, or after breaking them up, or into a receptacle, or after taking it outside, in times of danger, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The sixth training rule is concluded.

633. Tena [T 2.0558][V 0.0271] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū chattapāṇissa dhammaṃ desenti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū chattapāṇissa [M 0.0262] dhammaṃ desessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, chattapāṇissa dhammaṃ desethāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, chattapāṇissa dhammaṃ desessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

633. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were teaching the Dhamma to a person holding an umbrella. Those monks who were of few wishes... complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can the group-of-six monks teach the Dhamma to a person holding an umbrella?”... “Is it true, monks, that you teach the Dhamma to a person holding an umbrella?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Blessed One, the Buddha, rebuked them... “How can you, foolish men, teach the Dhamma to a person holding an umbrella! Foolish men, this is not for inspiring faith in the uninspired... And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Na chattapāṇissa dhammaṃ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not teach the Dhamma to a person holding an umbrella’; this training is to be undertaken.

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

In this way, this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.

634. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū chattapāṇissa gilānassa dhammaṃ [P 4.0200] desetuṃ kukkuccāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā chattapāṇissa gilānassa dhammaṃ na desessantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, chattapāṇissa gilānassa dhammaṃ desetuṃ. Evañca pana[T 2.0559], bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

634. Now at that time, monks were hesitant to teach the Dhamma to a sick person holding an umbrella. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can the Sakyan ascetics not teach the Dhamma to a sick person holding an umbrella?” The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks, saying: “Monks, I allow the teaching of the Dhamma to a sick person holding an umbrella. And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

“Na chattapāṇissa agilānassa dhammaṃ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not teach the Dhamma to a person who is not ill and is holding an umbrella’; this training is to be undertaken.

Chattaṃ nāma tīṇi chattāni – setacchattaṃ, kilañjacchattaṃ, paṇṇacchattaṃ maṇḍalabaddhaṃ salākabaddhaṃ.

An umbrella means three kinds of umbrellas: a white cloth umbrella, a rush umbrella, and a leaf umbrella, constructed with a circular frame and bound with ribs.

Dhammo nāma buddhabhāsito sāvakabhāsito isibhāsito devatābhāsito atthūpasañhito dhammūpasañhito.

Dhamma means that which is spoken by the Buddha, spoken by a disciple, spoken by a sage, or spoken by a deity, and is connected with the meaning and connected with the text.

Deseyyāti padena deseti, pade pade āpatti dukkaṭassa. Akkharāya deseti, akkharakkharāya [V 0.0272] āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na chattapāṇissa agilānassa dhammo desetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca chattapāṇissa agilānassa dhammaṃ deseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one teaches by the word, for every word there is an offense of wrong conduct. If one teaches by the syllable, for every syllable there is an offense of wrong conduct. The Dhamma should not be taught to a person who is not ill and is holding an umbrella. Whichever monk, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma to a person who is not ill and is holding an umbrella, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional... for the first offender.

Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The seventh training rule is concluded.

635. Tena [M 0.0263] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū daṇḍapāṇissa dhammaṃ desenti…pe….

635. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were teaching the Dhamma to a person holding a staff...

“Na daṇḍapāṇissa agilānassa dhammaṃ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not teach the Dhamma to a person who is not ill and is holding a staff’; this training should be observed.

Daṇḍo nāma majjhimassa purisassa catuhattho daṇḍo. Tato ukkaṭṭho adaṇḍo, omako adaṇḍo.

A staff means a staff of four cubits for a man of medium build. One longer than that is not a staff; one shorter is not a staff.

Na daṇḍapāṇissa agilānassa dhammo desetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca daṇḍapāṇissa agilānassa dhammaṃ deseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The Dhamma should not be taught to a person who is not ill and is holding a staff. Whichever monk, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma to a person who is not ill and is holding a staff, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti [T 2.0560] asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional... for the first offender.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The eighth training rule is concluded.

636. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū satthapāṇissa dhammaṃ desenti…pe….

636. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were teaching the Dhamma to a person holding a sword...

“Na satthapāṇissa agilānassa dhammaṃ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not teach the Dhamma to a person who is not ill and is holding a sword’; this training should be observed.

Satthaṃ [P 4.0201] nāma ekatodhāraṃ ubhatodhāraṃ paharaṇaṃ.

A sword means a striking instrument that is single-edged or double-edged.

Na [V 0.0273] satthapāṇissa agilānassa dhammo desetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca satthapāṇissa agilānassa dhammaṃ deseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The Dhamma should not be taught to a person who is not ill and is holding a sword. Whichever monk, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma to a person who is not ill and is holding a sword, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional... for the first offender.

Navamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The ninth training rule is concluded.

637. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū āvudhapāṇissa dhammaṃ desenti…pe….

637. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were teaching the Dhamma to a person holding a weapon...

“Na āvudhapāṇissa agilānassa dhammaṃ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not teach the Dhamma to a person who is not ill and is holding a weapon’; this training should be observed.

Āvudhaṃ nāma cāpo kodaṇḍo.

A weapon means a bow or a crossbow.

Na [M 0.0264] āvudhapāṇissa agilānassa dhammo desetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca āvudhapāṇissa agilānassa dhammaṃ deseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The Dhamma should not be taught to a person who is not ill and is holding a weapon. Whichever monk, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma to a person who is not ill and is holding a weapon, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional... for the first offender.

Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The tenth training rule is concluded.

Surusuruvaggo chaṭṭho.

The sixth chapter, the Surusuruvagga, is concluded.

7. Pādukavaggo

7. The Chapter on Sandals

638. Tena [T 2.0561] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū pādukāruḷhassa dhammaṃ desenti…pe….

638. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were teaching the Dhamma to a person wearing sandals...

“Na [V 0.0274] pādukāruḷhassa agilānassa dhammaṃ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not teach the Dhamma to a person who is not ill and is wearing sandals’; this training should be observed.

Na pādukāruḷhassa agilānassa dhammo desetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca akkantassa vā paṭimukkassa vā omukkassa vā agilānassa dhammaṃ deseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The Dhamma should not be taught to a person who is not ill and is wearing sandals. Whichever monk, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma to a person who is not ill and is stepping on, has put on, or is taking off sandals, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional... for the first offender.

Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The first training rule is concluded.

639. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū upāhanāruḷhassa dhammaṃ desenti…pe….

639. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were teaching the Dhamma to a person wearing shoes...

“Na upāhanāruḷhassa agilānassa dhammaṃ desessāmīti sikkhākaraṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not teach the Dhamma to a person who is not ill and is wearing shoes’; this training should be observed.

Na upāhanāruḷhassa agilānassa dhammo desetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca akkantassa vā paṭimukkassa vā omukkassa vā agilānassa dhammaṃ deseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The Dhamma should not be taught to a person who is not ill and is wearing shoes. Whichever monk, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma to a person who is not ill and is stepping on, has put on, or is taking off shoes, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional... for the first offender.

Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The second training rule is concluded.

640. Tena [M 0.0265] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū yānagatassa dhammaṃ desenti…pe….

640. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were teaching the Dhamma to a person in a vehicle...

“Na yānagatassa agilānassa dhammaṃ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not teach the Dhamma to a person who is not ill and is in a vehicle’; this training should be observed.

Yānaṃ [T 2.0562] nāma vayhaṃ ratho sakaṭaṃ sandamānikā sivikā pāṭaṅkī.

A vehicle means a conveyance, a chariot, a cart, a sedan chair, a litter, or a palanquin.

Na yānagatassa agilānassa dhammo desetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca yānagatassa agilānassa dhammaṃ deseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The Dhamma should not be taught to a person who is not ill and is in a vehicle. Whichever monk, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma to a person who is not ill and is in a vehicle, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti [V 0.0275] asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional... for the first offender.

Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The third training rule is concluded.

641. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho [P 4.0202] pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sayanagatassa dhammaṃ desenti…pe….

641. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Monastery. Now at that time the group-of-six monks were teaching the Dhamma to one lying down...

“Na sayanagatassa agilānassa dhammaṃ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not teach the Dhamma to one who is not ill and is lying down’—this is a training to be observed.

Na sayanagatassa agilānassa dhammo desetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca antamaso chamāyampi nipannassa sayanagatassa agilānassa dhammaṃ deseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The Dhamma should not be taught to one who is not ill and is lying down. Whoever, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma to one who is not ill and is lying down—even on the ground—commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense for one who is unintentional... for the first offender.

Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fourth training rule is concluded.

642. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū pallatthikāya nisinnassa dhammaṃ desenti…pe….

642. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks taught the Dhamma to one sitting with knees bound...

“Na pallatthikāya nisinnassa agilānassa dhammaṃ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not teach the Dhamma to one who is not ill and is sitting with knees bound’—this is a training to be observed.

Na [M 0.0266] pallatthikāya nisinnassa agilānassa dhammo desetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca hatthapallatthikāya vā dussapallatthikāya vā nisinnassa agilānassa dhammaṃ deseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The Dhamma should not be taught to one who is not ill and is sitting with knees bound. Whoever, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma to one who is not ill and is sitting with knees bound by the hands or by a cloth, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti [T 2.0563] asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense for one who is unintentional... for the first offender.

Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fifth training rule is concluded.

643. Tena [V 0.0276] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū veṭhitasīsassa dhammaṃ desenti…pe….

643. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks taught the Dhamma to one with a wrapped head...

“Na veṭhitasīsassa agilānassa dhammaṃ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not teach the Dhamma to one who is not ill and has a wrapped head’—this is a training to be observed.

Veṭhitasīso nāma kesantaṃ na dassāpetvā veṭhito hoti.

A ‘wrapped head’ means one who is wrapped so that the ends of the hair are not shown.

Na veṭhitasīsassa agilānassa dhammo desetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca veṭhitasīsassa agilānassa dhammaṃ deseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The Dhamma should not be taught to one who is not ill and has a wrapped head. Whoever, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma to one who is not ill and has a wrapped head commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, kesantaṃ vivarāpetvā deseti, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense for one who is unintentional, unmindful, not knowing, or ill; if one teaches after having the ends of the hair uncovered; in emergencies; for one who is mad; or for the first offender.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The sixth training rule is concluded.

644. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū oguṇṭhitasīsassa dhammaṃ desenti…pe….

644. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks taught the Dhamma to one with a covered head...

“Na oguṇṭhitasīsassa agilānassa dhammaṃ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not teach the Dhamma to one who is not ill and has a covered head’—this is a training to be observed.

Oguṇṭhitasīso [P 4.0203] nāma sasīsaṃ pāruto vuccati.

A ‘covered head’ is said to be one who is covered including the head.

Na oguṇṭhitasīsassa agilānassa dhammo desetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca oguṇṭhitasīsassa agilānassa dhammaṃ deseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The Dhamma should not be taught to one who is not ill and has a covered head. Whoever, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma to one who is not ill and has a covered head commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, sīsaṃ vivarāpetvā deseti, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense for one who is unintentional, unmindful, not knowing, or ill; if one teaches after having the head uncovered; in emergencies; for one who is mad; or for the first offender.

Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The seventh training rule is concluded.

645. Tena [M 0.0267][V 0.0277] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū [T 2.0564] chamāya nisīditvā āsane nisinnassa dhammaṃ desenti…pe….

645. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks, sitting on the ground, taught the Dhamma to one seated on a seat...

“Na chamāyaṃ nisīditvā āsane nisinnassa agilānassa dhammaṃ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not, while sitting on the ground, teach the Dhamma to one who is not ill and is seated on a seat’—this is a training to be observed.

Na chamāyaṃ nisīditvā nisinnena (aṭṭhakathā) āsane nisinnassa agilānassa dhammo desetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca chamāyaṃ nisīditvā āsane nisinnassa agilānassa dhammaṃ deseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The Dhamma should not be taught by one sitting on the ground to one who is not ill and is seated on a seat. Whoever, out of disrespect, sits on the ground and teaches the Dhamma to one who is not ill and is seated on a seat commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense for one who is unintentional... for the first offender.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The eighth training rule is concluded.

646. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū nīce āsane nisīditvā ucce āsane nisinnassa dhammaṃ desenti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū nīce āsane nisīditvā ucce āsane nisinnassa dhammaṃ desessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, nīce āsane nisīditvā ucce āsane nisinnassa dhammaṃ desethāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, nīce āsane nisīditvā ucce āsane nisinnassa dhammaṃ desessatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

646. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks, sitting on a low seat, taught the Dhamma to one seated on a high seat. Those monks who were of few wishes... they criticized, scorned, and spread it about, saying: ‘How indeed can the group-of-six monks, sitting on a low seat, teach the Dhamma to one seated on a high seat?’... ‘Is it true, monks, that you, sitting on a low seat, teach the Dhamma to one seated on a high seat?’ ‘It is true, Blessed One.’ The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... ‘How indeed, worthless men, can you, sitting on a low seat, teach the Dhamma to one seated on a high seat! This, worthless men, is not for inspiring faith in the faithless...’ Having rebuked them... and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks:

647. “Bhūtapubbaṃ[T 2.0565], bhikkhave, bārāṇasiyaṃ aññatarassa chapakassa chavakassa (syā.) pajāpati gabbhinī ahosi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sā chapakī taṃ chapakaṃ etadavoca – ‘gabbhinīmhi, ayyaputta! Icchāmi ambaṃ khāditu’nti. ‘Natthi ambaṃ ambo (syā.), akālo ambassā’ti. ‘Sace na labhissāmi marissāmī’ti. Tena kho pana samayena, rañño ambo dhuvaphalo hoti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, so chapako yena so ambo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ ambaṃ abhiruhitvā nilīno acchi[V 0.0278]. Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā purohitena brāhmaṇena saddhiṃ yena so ambo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ucce āsane nisīditvā mantaṃ pariyāpuṇāti[P 4.0204]. Atha kho, bhikkhave[M 0.0268], tassa chapakassa etadahosi – ‘yāva adhammiko ayaṃ rājā, yatra hi nāma ucce āsane nisīditvā mantaṃ pariyāpuṇissati. Ayañca brāhmaṇo adhammiko, yatra hi nāma nīce āsane nisīditvā ucce āsane nisinnassa mantaṃ vācessati. Ahañcamhi adhammiko, yohaṃ itthiyā kāraṇā rañño ambaṃ avaharāmi. Sabbamidaṃ carimaṃ kata’nti tattheva paripati.

647. ‘Once upon a time, monks, in Bārāṇasī, the wife of a certain outcaste was pregnant. Then, monks, that female outcaste said to the outcaste, ‘Noble sir, I am pregnant! I wish to eat a mango.’ ‘There are no mangoes; it is not the season for mangoes.’ ‘If I do not get one, I will die.’ Now at that time, the king had a mango tree that bore fruit continuously. Then, monks, that outcaste went to where that mango tree was; having gone, he climbed that mango tree and hid. Then, monks, the king, together with his brahmin chaplain, went to where that mango tree was; having gone, he sat on a high seat and learned a mantra. Then, monks, it occurred to that outcaste: ‘How unrighteous is this king, who indeed, sitting on a high seat, learns a mantra! And this brahmin is unrighteous, who indeed, sitting on a low seat, teaches a mantra to one seated on a high seat! And I am unrighteous, who, for the sake of a woman, steals the king’s mango. All this is a base act.’ And right there he fell down from the tree.

imā gāthāyo jā. 1.4.33-35 jātake aññathā dissanti “Ubho atthaṃ na jānanti, ubho dhammaṃ na passare;

Yo cāyaṃ mantaṃ vāceti, yo cādhammenadhīyati.

‘Both know not the meaning, both see not the principle—he who teaches the mantra, and he who learns it unrighteously.’

“Sālīnaṃ odano bhutto, sucimaṃsūpasecano;

Tasmā dhamme na vattāmi, dhammo ariyebhi vaṇṇito.

‘I have eaten the rice of Sāli grain, served with pure meat curry; therefore, I do not practice in the Dhamma which is praised by the noble ones.’

“Dhiratthu [T 2.0566] taṃ dhanalābhaṃ, yasalābhañca brāhmaṇa;

Yā vutti vinipātena, adhammacaraṇena vā.

‘Shame on that gain of wealth and fame, O brahmin, a livelihood obtained through downfall or unrighteous conduct.’

“Paribbaja mahābrahme, pacantaññepi pāṇino;

Mā tvaṃ adhammo ācarito, asmā kumbhamivābhidā”ti.

‘Depart, great brahmin! Other beings also cook. May the unrighteousness you have practiced not break you, just as a stone breaks a pot.’

“Tadāpi me, bhikkhave, amanāpā nīce āsane nisīditvā ucce āsane nisinnassa mantaṃ vācetuṃ, kimaṅga pana etarahi na amanāpā bhavissati nīce āsane nisīditvā ucce āsane nisinnassa dhammaṃ desetuṃ. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

‘Even then, monks, it was displeasing to me to sit on a low seat and teach a mantra to one sitting on a high seat. How much more so would it now be displeasing to sit on a low seat and teach the Dhamma to one sitting on a high seat? This, monks, is not for inspiring confidence in the uninspired… And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

“Na nīce āsane nisīditvā ucce āsane nisinnassa agilānassa dhammaṃ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not, while sitting on a low seat, teach the Dhamma to a person who is not ill sitting on a high seat’; this is the training to be observed.’

Na nīce āsane nisīditvā ucce āsane nisinnassa agilānassa dhammo desetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca nīce āsane nisīditvā ucce āsane nisinnassa agilānassa dhammaṃ deseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The Dhamma should not be taught by one sitting on a low seat to a person who is not ill sitting on a high seat. Whoever, out of disrespect, while sitting on a low seat, teaches the Dhamma to a person who is not ill sitting on a high seat, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti [V 0.0279] asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional… for the first offender.

Navamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The ninth training rule is concluded.

648. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ṭhitā nisinnassa dhammaṃ desenti…pe….

648. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time the group-of-six monks, while standing, were teaching the Dhamma to one who was seated…

“Na [M 0.0269] ṭhito nisinnassa agilānassa dhammaṃ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not, while standing, teach the Dhamma to a person who is not ill and is seated’; this is the training to be observed.’

Na [T 2.0567] ṭhitena nisinnassa agilānassa dhammo desetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca ṭhito nisinnassa agilānassa dhammaṃ deseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The Dhamma should not be taught by one who is standing to a person who is not ill and is seated. Whoever, out of disrespect, while standing, teaches the Dhamma to a person who is not ill and is seated, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional… for the first offender.

Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The tenth training rule is concluded.

649. Tena [P 4.0205] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū pacchato gacchantā purato gacchantassa dhammaṃ desenti…pe….

649. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time the group-of-six monks, while going behind, were teaching the Dhamma to one going in front…

“Na pacchato gacchanto purato gacchantassa agilānassa dhammaṃ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not, while going behind, teach the Dhamma to a person who is not ill going in front’; this is the training to be observed.’

Na pacchato gacchantena purato gacchantassa agilānassa dhammo desetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca pacchato gacchanto purato gacchantassa agilānassa dhammaṃ deseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The Dhamma should not be taught by one going behind to a person who is not ill going in front. Whoever, out of disrespect, while going behind, teaches the Dhamma to a person who is not ill going in front, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional… for the first offender.

Ekādasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The eleventh training rule is concluded.

650. Tena [V 0.0280] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uppathena gacchantā pathena gacchantassa dhammaṃ desenti…pe….

650. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time the group-of-six monks, while going off the path, were teaching the Dhamma to one going on the path…

“Na uppathena gacchanto pathena gacchantassa agilānassa dhammaṃ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘I will not, while going off the path, teach the Dhamma to a person who is not ill going on the path’; this is the training to be observed.’

Na uppathena gacchantena pathena gacchantassa agilānassa dhammo desetabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca uppathena gacchanto pathena gacchantassa [T 2.0568] agilānassa dhammaṃ deseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The Dhamma should not be taught by one going off the path to a person who is not ill going on the path. Whoever, out of disrespect, while going off the path, teaches the Dhamma to a person who is not ill going on the path, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional… for the first offender.

Dvādasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The twelfth training rule is concluded.

651. Tena [M 0.0270] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ṭhitā uccārampi passāvampi karonti…pe….

651. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time the group-of-six monks were defecating and urinating while standing…

“Na ṭhito agilāno uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā karissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

‘Being not ill, I will not defecate or urinate while standing’; this is the training to be observed.’

Na ṭhitena agilānena uccāro vā passāvo vā kātabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca ṭhito agilāno uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā karoti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One who is not ill should not defecate or urinate while standing. Whoever, out of disrespect, being not ill, defecates or urinates while standing, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti asañcicca…pe… ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional… for the first offender.

Terasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The thirteenth training rule is concluded.

652. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū harite uccārampi passāvampi kheḷampi karonti…pe….

652. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time the group-of-six monks were defecating, urinating, and spitting on green vegetation… and so on.

“Na [V 0.0281] harite agilāno uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“‘Being not ill, I will not defecate, urinate, or spit on green vegetation’; this is the training to be observed.”

Na harite agilānena uccāro vā passāvo vā kheḷo vā kātabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca harite agilāno uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karoti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One who is not ill should not defecate, urinate, or spit on green vegetation. Whatever monk, on account of disrespect, while not ill, defecates, urinates, or spits on green vegetation, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti [T 2.0569] asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, appaharite kato haritaṃ ottharati, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who is unknowing, for one who is ill, if what is passed in a place with little green vegetation spreads to a green place, in times of calamity, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Cuddasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fourteenth training rule is concluded.

653. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū udake uccārampi passāvampi kheḷampi karonti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti [P 4.0206] – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā udake uccārampi passāvampi kheḷampi karissanti, seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti! Assosuṃ [M 0.0271] kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū udake uccārampi passāvampi kheḷampi karissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, udake uccārampi passāvampi kheḷampi karothāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, udake uccārampi passāvampi kheḷampi karissatha! Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

653. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time the group-of-six monks were defecating, urinating, and spitting in water. People complained, criticized, and grumbled: “How can these Sakyan ascetics defecate, urinate, and spit in water, just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures?” The monks heard these people complaining, criticizing, and grumbling. Those monks who were of few wants… and so on… they too complained, criticized, and grumbled: “How can the group-of-six monks defecate, urinate, and spit in water?”… and so on… “Is it true, monks, that you defecate, urinate, and spit in water?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… and so on… “Foolish men, how can you defecate, urinate, and spit in water! This will not lead to confidence in those without it… and so on… And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

“Na udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“‘I will not defecate, urinate, or spit in water’; this is the training to be observed.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the monks.

654. Tena kho pana samayena gilānā bhikkhū udake uccārampi passāvampi [T 2.0570] kheḷampi kātuṃ kukkuccāyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānena bhikkhunā [V 0.0282] udake uccārampi passāvampi kheḷampi kātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyātha –

654. Now at that time, monks who were ill were hesitant to defecate, urinate, or spit in water. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in connection with this matter, gave a Dhamma talk and addressed the monks: “I allow, monks, a monk who is ill to defecate, urinate, or spit in water. And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

“Na udake agilāno uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“‘Not being ill, I will not defecate, urinate, or spit in water’; this is the training to be observed.”

Na udake agilānena uccāro vā passāvo vā kheḷo vā kātabbo. Yo anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake agilāno uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karoti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Excrement, urine, or spittle should not be passed in water by one who is not ill. Whatever monk, on account of disrespect, while not being ill, passes excrement, urine, or spittle in water, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantassa, gilānassa, thale kato udakaṃ ottharati, āpadāsu, ummattakassa, khittacittassa, vedanāṭṭassa, ādikammikassāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, for one who is unknowing, for one who is ill, if what is passed on dry land flows into the water, in times of calamity, for one who is insane, for one whose mind is deranged, for one who is afflicted by pain, or for the first offender.

Pannarasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fifteenth training rule is concluded.

Pādukavaggo sattamo.

The seventh, the Chapter on Footwear.

Uddiṭṭhā [M 0.0272] kho, āyasmanto, sekhiyā dhammā. Tatthāyasmante pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Dutiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Tatiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Parisuddhetthāyasmanto, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti.

Venerable sirs, the training rules have indeed been recited. In that regard, I ask the venerable sirs: “Are you pure in this?” A second time I ask: “Are you pure in this?” A third time I ask: “Are you pure in this?” The venerable sirs are pure in this, therefore they are silent. Thus do I take this.

Sekhiyā niṭṭhitā.

The training rules are concluded.

Sekhiyakaṇḍaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section on the Training Rules is finished.

8. Adhikaraṇasamathā

8. The Settlement of Legal Questions

Ime kho panāyasmanto satta adhikaraṇasamathā

These, venerable sirs, are the seven principles for the settlement of legal questions.

Dhammā uddesaṃ āgacchanti.

These principles come up for recitation.

655. Uppannuppannānaṃ [T 2.0571][P 4.0207][V 0.0283] adhikaraṇānaṃ samathāya vūpasamāya sammukhāvinayo dātabbo, sativinayo dātabbo, amūḷhavinayo dātabbo, paṭiññāya kāretabbaṃ, yebhuyyasikā, tassapāpiyasikā, tiṇavatthārakoti.

655. For the settling and pacifying of legal questions as they arise, the procedure in the presence should be applied, the procedure of mindfulness should be applied, the procedure for one who is no longer confused should be applied, it should be carried out by acknowledgment, the decision by majority should be carried out, the procedure for one's further depravity should be carried out, and the covering over as with grass should be carried out.

Uddiṭṭhā kho, āyasmanto, satta adhikaraṇasamathā dhammā. Tatthāyasmante pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Dutiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Tatiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Parisuddhetthāyasmanto, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti.

Venerable sirs, the seven principles for the settlement of legal questions have been recited. In this matter I ask the venerable sirs: “Are you pure in this?” A second time I ask: “Are you pure in this?” A third time I ask: “Are you pure in this?” The venerable sirs are pure in this, therefore they are silent. Thus I hold it.

Adhikaraṇasamathā niṭṭhitā.

The Settlement of Legal Questions is concluded.

Uddiṭṭhaṃ kho, āyasmanto, nidānaṃ; uddiṭṭhā cattāro pārājikā dhammā; uddiṭṭhā terasa saṅghādisesā dhammā; uddiṭṭhā dve aniyatā dhammā; uddiṭṭhā tiṃsa nissaggiyā pācittiyā dhammā; uddiṭṭhā dvenavuti pācittiyā dhammā; uddiṭṭhā cattāro pāṭidesanīyā dhammā; uddiṭṭhā sekhiyā dhammā; uddiṭṭhā satta adhikaraṇasamathā dhammā. Ettakaṃ tassa bhagavato suttāgataṃ suttapariyāpannaṃ anvaddhamāsaṃ uddesaṃ āgacchati. Tattha sabbeheva samaggehi sammodamānehi avivadamānehi sikkhitabbanti.

Venerable sirs, the introduction has been recited; the four rules entailing defeat have been recited; the thirteen rules entailing a formal meeting of the Saṅgha have been recited; the two indefinite rules have been recited; the thirty rules entailing expiation with forfeiture have been recited; the ninety-two rules entailing expiation have been recited; the four rules to be acknowledged have been recited; the training rules have been recited; the seven principles for the settlement of legal questions have been recited. This much of the Blessed One’s teaching that has come down in the Pātimokkha, that is included in the Pātimokkha, comes up for recitation every half-month. Therein, all should train in concord, with mutual appreciation, without disputing.

Mahāvibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Great Analysis is concluded.

Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Bhikkhunīvibhaṅgo

The Bhikkhunī Analysis

1. Pārājikakaṇḍaṃ (bhikkhunīvibhaṅgo)

1. The Section on Defeat

1. Paṭhamapārājikaṃ

1. The First Rule of Defeat

656. Tena [T 0.0001][P 4.0211][M 0.0273][V 0.0284] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sāḷho migāranattā bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihāraṃ kattukāmo hoti. Atha kho sāḷho migāranattā bhikkhuniyo upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – “icchāmahaṃ, ayye, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihāraṃ kātuṃ. Detha me navakammikaṃ bhikkhuni”nti. Tena kho pana samayena catasso bhaginiyo bhikkhunīsu pabbajitā honti – nandā, nandavatī, sundarīnandā, thullanandāti. Tāsu sundarīnandā bhikkhunī taruṇapabbajitā abhirūpā hoti dassanīyā pāsādikā paṇḍitā byattā medhāvinī dakkhā analasā, tatrupāyāya vīmaṃsāya samannāgatā, alaṃ kātuṃ alaṃ saṃvidhātuṃ. Atha kho bhikkhunisaṅgho sundarīnandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ sammannitvā sāḷhassa migāranattuno navakammikaṃ adāsi. Tena kho pana samayena sundarīnandā bhikkhunī sāḷhassa [V 0.0285] migāranattuno nivesanaṃ abhikkhaṇaṃ gacchati – “vāsiṃ detha, parasuṃ pharasuṃ (syā. ka.) detha, kuṭhāriṃ kudhāriṃ (ka.) detha, kuddālaṃ detha, nikhādanaṃ dethā”ti. Sāḷhopi migāranattā bhikkhunupassayaṃ abhikkhaṇaṃ [T 0.0002] gacchati katākataṃ jānituṃ. Te abhiṇhadassanena paṭibaddhacittā ahesuṃ.

656. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s park. Now at that time, Sāḷha, Migāra's grandson, wished to have a dwelling built for the community of bhikkhunīs. Then Sāḷha, Migāra's grandson, approached the bhikkhunīs and said: “Venerable ladies, I wish to have a dwelling built for the community of bhikkhunīs. Give me a bhikkhunī who can manage the new work.” Now at that time, there were four sisters who had gone forth among the bhikkhunīs—Nandā, Nandavatī, Sundarīnandā, and Thullanandā. Among them, the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, having been ordained when young, was beautiful, lovely, inspiring, wise, accomplished, intelligent, skillful, not lazy, and endowed with the investigation suitable for the task; she was capable of doing, capable of managing. Then the community of bhikkhunīs, having appointed the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, gave her to Sāḷha, Migāra's grandson, to manage the new work. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā frequently went to the residence of Sāḷha, Migāra's grandson, saying: “Give me an adze, give me an axe, give me a hatchet, give me a hoe, give me a chisel.” Sāḷha, Migāra's grandson, also frequently went to the bhikkhunīs’ dwelling to know what had been done and what had not been done. Through frequent seeing, their minds became attached.

Atha kho sāḷho migāranattā sundarīnandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ dūsetuṃ okāsaṃ alabhamāno etadevatthāya bhikkhunisaṅghassa bhattaṃ akāsi. Atha kho sāḷho migāranattā bhattagge āsanaṃ paññapento – “ettakā bhikkhuniyo ayyāya sundarīnandāya vuḍḍhatarā”ti ekamantaṃ āsanaṃ paññapesi “ettakā navakatarā”ti – ekamantaṃ āsanaṃ paññapesi. Paṭicchanne okāse [M 0.0274] nikūṭe sundarīnandāya bhikkhuniyā [P 4.0212] āsanaṃ paññapesi, yathā therā bhikkhuniyo jāneyyuṃ – “navakānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ santike nisinnā”ti; navakāpi bhikkhuniyo jāneyyuṃ – “therānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ santike nisinnā”ti. Atha kho sāḷho migāranattā bhikkhunisaṅghassa kālaṃ ārocāpesi – “kālo, ayye, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Sundarīnandā bhikkhunī sallakkhetvā – “na bahukato sāḷho migāranattā bhikkhunisaṅghassa bhattaṃ akāsi; maṃ so dūsetukāmo. Sacāhaṃ gamissāmi vissaro me bhavissatī”ti, antevāsiniṃ bhikkhuniṃ āṇāpesi – “gaccha me piṇḍapātaṃ nīhara. Yo ce maṃ pucchati, ‘gilānā’ti paṭivedehī”ti. “Evaṃ, ayye”ti kho sā bhikkhunī sundarīnandāya bhikkhuniyā paccassosi.

Then Sāḷha, Migāra's grandson, not getting an opportunity to corrupt the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, prepared a meal for the community of bhikkhunīs for this very purpose. Then Sāḷha, Migāra's grandson, while arranging seats in the dining hall, arranged seats in one suitable place, thinking, “This many bhikkhunīs are senior to the venerable Sundarīnandā,” and arranged seats in another suitable place, thinking, “This many are junior.” In a concealed, corner-like place, he arranged a seat for the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, in such a way that the senior bhikkhunīs would know, “She is sitting near the junior bhikkhunīs,” and the junior bhikkhunīs would also know, “She is sitting near the senior bhikkhunīs.” Then Sāḷha, Migāra's grandson, had the time announced to the community of bhikkhunīs: “It is time, venerable ladies, the meal is ready.” The bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, considering, “Sāḷha, Migāra's grandson, did not prepare this meal for the community of bhikkhunīs out of a great desire for merit; he wants to corrupt me. If I go, there will be a scandal for me,” instructed her resident pupil bhikkhunī: “Go, bring my alms-food. If anyone asks about me, inform them that I am ill.” “Very well, venerable lady,” that bhikkhunī replied to the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā.

Tena kho pana samayena sāḷho migāranattā bahidvārakoṭṭhake ṭhito hoti sundarīnandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ paṭipucchanto – “kahaṃ, ayye, ayyā sundarīnandā? Kahaṃ, ayye, ayyā sundarīnandā”ti? Evaṃ [T 0.0003] vutte sundarīnandāya bhikkhuniyā antevāsinī bhikkhunī sāḷhaṃ migāranattāraṃ etadavoca – “gilānāvuso; piṇḍapātaṃ nīharissāmī”ti. Atha kho sāḷho migāranattā – “yampāhaṃ atthāya yaṃpāhaṃ (syā.) bhikkhunisaṅghassa bhattaṃ akāsiṃ ayyāya sundarīnandāya kāraṇā”ti manusse āṇāpetvā – “bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ bhattena parivisathā”ti vatvā yena bhikkhunupassayo tenupasaṅkami. Tena kho pana samayena sundarīnandā bhikkhunī bahārāmakoṭṭhake ṭhitā hoti sāḷhaṃ migāranattāraṃ patimānentī. Addasā kho sundarīnandā bhikkhunī sāḷhaṃ migāranattāraṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna upassayaṃ pavisitvā sasīsaṃ pārupitvā mañcake nipajji. Atha kho sāḷho migāranattā yena sundarīnandā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā sundarīnandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ te, ayye, aphāsu, kissa nipannāsī”ti? “Evañhetaṃ, āvuso, hoti yā anicchantaṃ icchatī”ti. “Kyāhaṃ taṃ, ayye[V 0.0286], na icchissāmi? Api cāhaṃ okāsaṃ na labhāmi taṃ dūsetu”nti. Avassuto avassutāya sundarīnandāya bhikkhuniyā kāyasaṃsaggaṃ samāpajji.

At that time Sāḷha, Migāra's grandson, was standing at the outer gatehouse, repeatedly inquiring about the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā: “Where, venerable ladies, is the venerable Sundarīnandā? Where, venerable ladies, is the venerable Sundarīnandā?” When this was said, the bhikkhunī who was Sundarīnandā’s resident pupil said to Sāḷha, Migāra's grandson: “She is ill, friend; I will bring out her alms-food.” Then Sāḷha, Migāra's grandson, thinking, “The meal I prepared for the community of bhikkhunīs was for the sake of the venerable Sundarīnandā,” ordered his people, saying, “Serve the community of bhikkhunīs with the meal,” and went to the bhikkhunīs’ dwelling. At that time the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā was standing in the outer park gatehouse, waiting for Sāḷha, Migāra's grandson. The bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā saw Sāḷha, Migāra's grandson, coming from afar. Having seen him, she entered the dwelling, covered herself including her head, and lay down on the bed. Then Sāḷha, Migāra's grandson, approached the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā. Having approached, he said to the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā: “What troubles you, venerable lady? Why are you lying down?” “This is what happens, friend, to one who desires the unwilling.” “Why would I not desire you, venerable lady? But I do not get the opportunity to corrupt you.” Overcome by lust, he engaged in physical contact with the lustful bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā.

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī jarādubbalā caraṇagilānā sundarīnandāya bhikkhuniyā avidūre nipannā hoti. Addasā kho sā bhikkhunī [M 0.0275] sāḷhaṃ migāranattāraṃ avassutaṃ avassutāya sundarīnandāya bhikkhuniyā kāyasaṃsaggaṃ [T 0.0004] samāpajjantaṃ. Disvāna ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā sundarīnandā avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyissatī”ti[P 4.0213]! Atha kho sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā santuṭṭhā lajjiniyo kukkuccikā sikkhākāmā tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā sundarīnandā avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyissatī”ti! Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā santuṭṭhā lajjino kukkuccakā sikkhākāmā te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma sundarīnandā bhikkhunī avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyissatī”ti!

At that time a certain bhikkhunī, weak from old age and afflicted with a foot disease, was lying down not far from the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā. That bhikkhunī saw Sāḷha, the grandson of Migāra, who was lustful, engaging in physical contact with the lustful bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā. Having seen this, she complained, criticized, and spoke disapprovingly: “How could the venerable Sundarīnandā, being lustful, consent to physical contact with a lustful man?” Then that bhikkhunī reported the matter to the bhikkhunīs. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes, content, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training complained, criticized, and spoke disapprovingly: “How could the venerable Sundarīnandā, being lustful, consent to physical contact with a lustful man?” Then those bhikkhunīs reported the matter to the bhikkhus. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes, content, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training complained, criticized, and spoke disapprovingly: “How could the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, being lustful, consent to physical contact with a lustful man?”

Atha kho te bhikkhū sundarīnandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, sundarīnandā bhikkhunī avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyatī”ti sādiyīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ, bhikkhave, sundarīnandāya bhikkhuniyā ananulomikaṃ appatirūpaṃ assāmaṇakaṃ akappiyaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, sundarīnandā bhikkhunī avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya pasannānaṃ vā bhiyyobhāvāya. Atha khvetaṃ, bhikkhave[T 0.0005], appasannānañceva appasādāya pasannānañca ekaccānaṃ aññathattāyā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā sundarīnandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā dubbharatāya dupposatāya mahicchatāya asantuṭṭhitāya asantuṭṭhatāya (syā.), asantuṭṭhiyā (ka.) saṅgaṇikāya kosajjassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsitvā, anekapariyāyena subharatāya suposatāya appicchassa santuṭṭhassa santuṭṭhiyā (ka.) sallekhassa dhutassa pāsādikassa apacayassa vīriyārambhassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsitvā, bhikkhūnaṃ tadanucchavikaṃ tadanulomikaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññapessāmi dasa atthavase [V 0.0287] paṭicca – saṅghasuṭṭhutāya, saṅghaphāsutāya, dummaṅkūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ niggahāya[M 0.0276], pesalānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ phāsuvihārāya, diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ āsavānaṃ saṃvarāya, samparāyikānaṃ āsavānaṃ paṭighātāya, appasannānaṃ pasādāya, pasannānaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya, saddhammaṭṭhitiyā vinayānuggahāya. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

Then those bhikkhus, having rebuked the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā in many ways, reported the matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on that occasion and in that connection, convened the Sangha of bhikkhus and questioned the bhikkhus: “Is it true, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, being lustful, consents to physical contact with a lustful male person?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her: “This is improper for the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, bhikkhus, unseemly, unsuitable, unworthy of an ascetic, unbecoming, and not to be done. How could the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, being lustful, consent to physical contact with a lustful male person? This, bhikkhus, does not lead to inspiring confidence in the unconfident, nor to the increase of confidence in the confident. Rather, bhikkhus, it leads to a lack of confidence in the unconfident and to causing some of the confident to change.” Then the Blessed One, having rebuked the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā in many ways, spoke in dispraise of being difficult to support, difficult to maintain, of having great desires, of being discontent, of fondness for company, and of laziness. He spoke in many ways in praise of being easy to support, easy to maintain, of having few desires, of being content, of effacement, of ascetic practice, of being inspiring, of non-accumulation, and of energetic exertion. Having given a Dhamma talk that was befitting and suitable for the bhikkhus, he addressed them: “Therefore, bhikkhus, I will lay down a training rule for the bhikkhunīs for ten reasons: for the excellence of the Sangha, for the comfort of the Sangha, for the restraint of ill-behaved bhikkhunīs, for the comfortable living of well-behaved bhikkhunīs, for the restraint of the taints in the present life, for the warding off of the taints in a future life, for inspiring confidence in the unconfident, for the increase of confidence in the confident, for the establishment of the true Dhamma, and for the support of the discipline. And so, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

657. “Yā pana bhikkhunī avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa adhakkhakaṃ ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ āmasanaṃ vā parāmasanaṃ vā gahaṇaṃ vā chupanaṃ vā paṭipīḷanaṃ vā sādiyeyya, ayampi pārājikā hoti asaṃvāsā ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalikā”ti.

657. “Whatever bhikkhunī, being lustful, should consent to a lustful male person’s stroking, caressing, grasping, touching, or squeezing below the collarbones and above the kneecaps, this bhikkhunī also is defeated and no longer in communion for the offense concerning the area above the knees.”

658. Yā [P 4.0214] panāti yā yādisā yathāyuttā yathājaccā yathānāmā yathāgottā yathāsīlā yathāvihārinī yathāgocarā therā vā navā vā majjhimā vā, esā vuccati yā panāti.

658. “Whatever” means: any whatsoever, of any kind, of any sort, of any birth, of any name, of any clan, of any virtue, of any dwelling, of any resort—whether a senior, a newly ordained, or a middle one—this is what is meant by “whatever”.

Bhikkhunīti bhikkhikāti bhikkhunī; bhikkhācariyaṃ ajjhupagatāti bhikkhunī; bhinnapaṭadharāti bhikkhunī[T 0.0006]; samaññāya bhikkhunī; paṭiññāya bhikkhunī; ehi bhikkhunīti bhikkhunī; tīhi saraṇagamanehi upasampannāti bhikkhunī; bhadrā bhikkhunī; sārā bhikkhunī; sekhā bhikkhunī; asekhā bhikkhunī; samaggena ubhatosaṅghena ñatticatutthena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena upasampannāti bhikkhunī. Tatra yāyaṃ bhikkhunī samaggena ubhatosaṅghena ñatticatutthena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena upasampannā, ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

A bhikkhunī is so-called because she is a beggar; a bhikkhunī is so-called because she has undertaken the practice of alms-gathering; a bhikkhunī is so-called because she wears patched robes; a bhikkhunī by designation; a bhikkhunī by acknowledgement; a bhikkhunī by the words, 'Come, bhikkhunī'; a bhikkhunī ordained by the three goings for refuge; a virtuous bhikkhunī; a bhikkhunī of substance; a bhikkhunī in training; a bhikkhunī beyond training; a bhikkhunī ordained by a unified dual Saṅgha through a formal act with a motion and three announcements, which is unshakeable and appropriate to the occasion. Among these, that bhikkhunī who is ordained by a unified dual Saṅgha through a formal act with a motion and three announcements, which is unshakeable and appropriate to the occasion—this is the bhikkhunī intended in this context.

Avassutā nāma sārattā apekkhavatī paṭibaddhacittā.

Lustful (avassutā) means being impassioned, longing, and having a mind bound by passion.

Avassuto nāma sāratto apekkhavā paṭibaddhacitto.

Lustful (avassuto) means being impassioned, longing, and having a mind bound by passion.

Purisapuggalo nāma manussapuriso na yakkho na peto na tiracchānagato viññū paṭibalo kāyasaṃsaggaṃ samāpajjituṃ.

A male person means a human male—not a yakkha, not a peta, not an animal—who is discerning and capable of engaging in bodily contact.

Adhakkhakanti heṭṭhakkhakaṃ.

Below the collarbones means below the two collarbones.

Ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalanti uparijāṇumaṇḍalaṃ.

Above the kneecaps means above the two kneecaps.

Āmasanaṃ [V 0.0288] nāma āmaṭṭhamattaṃ.

Stroking means merely stroking.

Parāmasanaṃ nāma itocito ca sañcopanaṃ.

Caressing means moving to and fro.

Gahaṇaṃ nāma gahitamattaṃ.

Grasping means merely grasping.

Chupanaṃ nāma phuṭṭhamattaṃ.

Touching means merely touching.

Paṭipīḷanaṃ [M 0.0277] vā sādiyeyyāti aṅgaṃ gahetvā nippīḷanaṃ sādiyati.

Or consents to squeezing means: having taken a limb, she consents to the squeezing.

Ayampīti purimāyo upādāya vuccati.

“This one also” is said with reference to the preceding ones.

Pārājikā hotīti seyyathāpi nāma puriso sīsacchinno abhabbo tena sarīrabandhanena jīvituṃ, evameva bhikkhunī avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa adhakkhakaṃ ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ [T 0.0007] āmasanaṃ vā parāmasanaṃ vā gahaṇaṃ vā chupanaṃ vā paṭipīḷanaṃ vā sādiyantī assamaṇī hoti asakyadhītā. Tena vuccati pārājikā hotīti.

She is defeated means: just as a man whose head has been cut off is incapable of living by that bodily connection, so too a bhikkhunī who, being overcome by lust, consents to a male person who is overcome by lust stroking, caressing, grasping, touching, or squeezing her below the two collarbones and above the two kneecaps, is not a contemplative, not a daughter of the Sakyan. Therefore, it is said, 'she is defeated'.

Asaṃvāsāti saṃvāso nāma ekakammaṃ ekuddeso samasikkhatā, eso saṃvāso nāma. So tāya saddhiṃ natthi, tena vuccati asaṃvāsāti.

Not in communion means: communion is a common formal act, a common recitation, and having the same training. This is called communion. That communion does not exist with her; therefore, it is said, 'not in communion'.

659. Ubhatoavassute adhakkhakaṃ ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ kāyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti pārājikassa. Kāyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti thullaccayassa. Kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti thullaccayassa. Kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

659. When both are overcome by lust, if she strokes body with body below the two collarbones and above the two kneecaps, there is an offense of defeat. If she strokes a body-connected object with her body, there is a grave offense. If she strokes a body with a body-connected object, there is a grave offense. If she strokes a body-connected object with a body-connected object, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Nissaggiyena kāyaṃ āmasati[P 4.0215], āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissaggiyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissaggiyena nissaggiyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If she strokes a body with an object to be forfeited, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body-connected object with an object to be forfeited, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes an object to be forfeited with an object to be forfeited, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Ubbhakkhakaṃ adhojāṇumaṇḍalaṃ kāyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti thullaccayassa. Kāyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ [V 0.0289] āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If she strokes body with body above the two collarbones or below the two kneecaps, there is a grave offense. If she strokes a body-connected object with her body, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body with a body-connected object, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body-connected object with a body-connected object, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Nissaggiyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissaggiyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissaggiyena nissaggiyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If she strokes a body with an object to be forfeited, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body-connected object with an object to be forfeited, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes an object to be forfeited with an object to be forfeited, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

660. Ekatoavassute adhakkhakaṃ ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ kāyena kāyaṃ āmasati[T 0.0008], āpatti thullaccayassa. Kāyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati[M 0.0278], āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

660. When one party is overcome by lust, if she strokes body with body below the two collarbones and above the two kneecaps, there is a grave offense. If she strokes a body-connected object with her body, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body with a body-connected object, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body-connected object with a body-connected object, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Nissaggiyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissaggiyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissaggiyena nissaggiyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If she strokes a body with an object to be forfeited, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body-connected object with an object to be forfeited, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes an object to be forfeited with an object to be forfeited, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Ubbhakkhakaṃ adhojāṇumaṇḍalaṃ kāyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If she strokes body with body above the two collarbones or below the two kneecaps, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body-connected object with her body, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body with a body-connected object, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body-connected object with a body-connected object, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Nissaggiyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissaggiyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissaggiyena nissaggiyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If she strokes a body with an object to be forfeited, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body-connected object with an object to be forfeited, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes an object to be forfeited with an object to be forfeited, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

661. Ubhatoavassute yakkhassa vā petassa vā paṇḍakassa vā tiracchānagatamanussaviggahassa vā adhakkhakaṃ ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ kāyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti thullaccayassa. Kāyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

661. When both are overcome by lust, if she strokes body with body below the two collarbones and above the two kneecaps of a yakkha, a peta, a paṇḍaka, or an animal in human form, there is a grave offense. If she strokes a body-connected object with her body, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body with a body-connected object, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body-connected object with a body-connected object, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Nissaggiyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissaggiyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissaggiyena [T 0.0009] nissaggiyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If she strokes a body with an object to be forfeited, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body-connected object with an object to be forfeited, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes an object to be forfeited with an object to be forfeited, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

If she strokes body with body above the two collarbones or below the two kneecaps, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body-connected object with her body, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body with a body-connected object, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body-connected object with a body-connected object, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

If one strokes the body with an object to be forfeited, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one strokes an object connected to the body with an object to be forfeited, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one strokes an object to be forfeited with an object to be forfeited, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

662. Ekatoavassute [M 0.0279] adhakkhakaṃ ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ kāyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If she strokes a body-connected object with a body-connected object, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

If she strokes a body with a detached object, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body-connected object with a detached object, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a detached object with a detached object, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Ubbhakkhakaṃ adhojāṇumaṇḍalaṃ kāyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If she strokes body with body above the collarbones or below the kneecaps, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body-connected object with her body, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body with a body-connected object, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she strokes a body-connected object with a body-connected object, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Nissaggiyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissaggiyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ [T 0.0010] āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissaggiyena nissaggiyaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

663. Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantiyā, asādiyantiyā, ummattikāya, khittacittāya, vedanāṭṭāya, ādikammikāyāti.

663. There is no offense if it is unintentional, if she is unmindful, if she is unknowing, if she is not consenting, if she is insane, if she is of deranged mind, if she is afflicted by pain, or if she is the first offender.

Paṭhamapārājikaṃ samattaṃ bhikkhunivibhaṅge sikkhāpadagaṇanā bhikkhūhi§asādhāraṇavasena pakāsitāti veditabbā.

The first Pārājika is completed.

2. Dutiyapārājikaṃ

2. The Second Pārājika

664. Tena [T 0.0011][P 4.0216] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sundarīnandā bhikkhunī sāḷhena migāranattunā gabbhinī hoti[V 0.0291]. Yāva gabbho taruṇo ahosi tāva chādesi. Paripakke gabbhe vibbhamitvā vijāyi. Bhikkhuniyo thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavocuṃ – “sundarīnandā kho, ayye, aciravibbhantā vijātā. Kacci no sā bhikkhunīyeva samānā gabbhinī”ti? “Evaṃ, ayye”ti. “Kissa pana tvaṃ, ayye, jānaṃ pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ bhikkhuniṃ nevattanā paṭicodesi na gaṇassa ārocesī”ti? “Yo etissā avaṇṇo mayheso avaṇṇo, yā etissā akitti mayhesā akitti, yo etissā ayaso mayheso ayaso, yo etissā alābho mayheso [M 0.0280] alābho. Kyāhaṃ, ayye, attano avaṇṇaṃ attano akittiṃ attano ayasaṃ attano alābhaṃ paresaṃ ārocessāmī”ti? Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā jānaṃ pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ bhikkhuniṃ nevattanā paṭicodessati na gaṇassa ārocessatī”ti! Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhū ye te bhikkhū…pe… (?) bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā [T 0.0012] bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī jānaṃ pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ bhikkhuniṃ nevattanā paṭicodeti paṭicodesi… ārocesīti (ka.) na gaṇassa ārocetī”ti paṭicodesi… ārocesīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī jānaṃ pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ bhikkhuniṃ nevattanā paṭicodessati na gaṇassa ārocessati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

664. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā was pregnant by Sāḷha, the grandson of Migāra. As long as the embryo was young, she concealed it. When the embryo was mature, she disrobed and gave birth. The bhikkhunīs said this to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā: ‘Venerable lady, Sundarīnandā gave birth not long after disrobing. Could it be that she was pregnant while still a bhikkhunī?’ ‘Yes, venerable ladies.’ ‘But why then, venerable lady, knowing a bhikkhunī had committed an offense of Pārājika, did you neither admonish her yourself nor inform the community?’ ‘Whatever disgrace is hers is my disgrace; whatever ill-repute is hers is my ill-repute; whatever dishonor is hers is my dishonor; whatever loss is hers is my loss. Why, venerable ladies, should I report my own disgrace, my own ill-repute, my own dishonor, my own loss to others?’ Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: ‘How could the venerable Thullanandā, knowing a bhikkhunī had committed an offense of Pārājika, neither admonish her herself nor inform the community?’ Then those bhikkhunīs reported this matter to the bhikkhus. The bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this context, having assembled the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, questioned the bhikkhus: ‘Is it true, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, knowing a bhikkhunī had committed an offense of Pārājika, neither admonishes her herself nor informs the community?’ ‘It is true, Blessed One.’ The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… ‘How, bhikkhus, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, knowing a bhikkhunī had committed an offense of Pārājika, neither admonish her herself nor inform the community? This, bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the faithless… And so, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule thus:

665. “Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṃ pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ bhikkhuniṃ nevattanā paṭicodeyya na gaṇassa āroceyya, yadā ca sā ṭhitā vā assa cutā vā nāsitā vā avassaṭā vā, sā pacchā evaṃ vadeyya – ‘pubbevāhaṃ, ayye, aññāsiṃ etaṃ bhikkhuniṃ evarūpā ca evarūpā ca sā bhaginīti[P 4.0217], no ca kho attanā paṭicodessaṃ na gaṇassa ārocessa’nti, ayampi pārājikā hoti asaṃvāsā vajjappaṭicchādikā”ti.

665. ‘Should any bhikkhunī, knowing a bhikkhunī has committed an offense of Pārājika, neither admonish her herself nor inform the community, and when that bhikkhunī is still in the order, or has died, or has been made to disrobe, or has gone over to another sect, she should later say: “Venerable ladies, I knew from the beginning that this sister was of such and such a nature, but I did not admonish her myself, nor did I inform the community,” this bhikkhunī also, for concealing the fault, is defeated and not in communion.’

666. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

666. ‘Any bhikkhunī’ means: whichever… and so on… ‘bhikkhunī’ means: … and so on… in this context, this is the intended bhikkhunī.

Jānāti nāma sāmaṃ vā jānāti, aññe [T 0.0013] vā tassā ārocenti, sā vā āroceti.

‘Knows’ means: she knows by herself, or others inform her, or the offending bhikkhunī herself informs her.

Pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpannanti aṭṭhannaṃ pārājikānaṃ aññataraṃ pārājikaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ.

‘Has committed an offense of Pārājika’ means: has committed one of the eight Pārājika offenses.

Nevattanā [V 0.0292] paṭicodeyyāti na sayaṃ codeyya.

‘Neither admonish her herself’ means: she should not admonish her by herself.

Na gaṇassa āroceyyāti na aññāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ āroceyya.

‘Nor inform the community’ means: she should not inform other bhikkhunīs.

Yadā [M 0.0281] ca sā ṭhitā vā assa cutā vāti ṭhitā nāma saliṅge ṭhitā vuccati. Cutā nāma kālaṅkatā vuccati. Nāsitā nāma sayaṃ vā vibbhantā hoti aññehi vā nāsitā. Avassaṭā nāma titthāyatanaṃ saṅkantā vuccati. Sā pacchā evaṃ vadeyya – “pubbevāhaṃ, ayye, aññāsiṃ etaṃ bhikkhuniṃ evarūpā ca evarūpā ca sā bhaginī”ti.

Regarding ‘And when that bhikkhunī is still in the order, or has died…’: ‘Still in the order’ refers to one who is established in her own monastic status. ‘Has died’ refers to one who has passed away. ‘Has been made to disrobe’ means she has disrobed by herself or has been made to disrobe by others. ‘Has gone over to another sect’ refers to one who has transferred to the school of heretics. She should later say: ‘Venerable ladies, I knew from the beginning that this sister was of such and such a nature.’

No ca kho attanā paṭicodessanti sayaṃ vā na codessaṃ.

‘But I did not admonish her myself’ means: I did not admonish her by myself.

Na gaṇassa ārocessanti na aññāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ ārocessaṃ.

‘Nor did I inform the community’ means: I did not inform other bhikkhunīs.

Ayampīti purimāyo upādāya vuccati.

‘This one also’ is said with reference to the preceding ones.

Pārājikā hotīti seyyathāpi nāma paṇḍupalāso bandhanā pamutto abhabbo haritatthāya, evameva bhikkhunī jānaṃ pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ bhikkhuniṃ nevattanā paṭicodessāmi na gaṇassa ārocessāmīti dhuraṃ nikkhittamatte assamaṇī hoti asakyadhītā. Tena vuccati pārājikā [T 0.0014] hotīti.

‘She is defeated’ means: just as a yellow leaf, fallen from its stalk, is incapable of becoming green again, so too a bhikkhunī who, knowing a bhikkhunī has committed an offense of Pārājika, at the very moment of laying down the burden by thinking, ‘I will not admonish her myself, nor will I inform the community,’ is no longer a female ascetic, no longer a daughter of the Sakyans. Therefore it is said, ‘she is defeated.’

Asaṃvāsāti saṃvāso nāma ekakammaṃ ekuddeso samasikkhatā. Eso saṃvāso nāma. So tāya saddhiṃ natthi. Tena vuccati asaṃvāsāti.

‘Not in communion’ means: Communion is defined as a common formal act, a common recitation of the Pātimokkha, and equality in training. This is called communion. That communion does not exist with her. Therefore, it is said ‘not in communion’.

667. Anāpatti “saṅghassa bhaṇḍanaṃ vā kalaho vā viggaho vā vivādo vā bhavissatī”ti nāroceti, “saṅghabhedo vā saṅgharāji vā bhavissatī”ti nāroceti, “ayaṃ kakkhaḷā pharusā jīvitantarāyaṃ vā brahmacariyantarāyaṃ vā karissatī”ti nāroceti, aññā patirūpā bhikkhuniyo apassantī nāroceti, nacchādetukāmā nāroceti, paññāyissati sakena kammenāti nāroceti, ummattikāya…pe… ādikammikāyāti.

667. There is no offense if one does not inform, thinking: “There will be quarreling, strife, contention, or debate in the Saṅgha,” or thinking: “There will be a schism in the Saṅgha or a fissure in the Saṅgha,” or thinking: “This bhikkhunī is coarse and harsh; she will create a danger to life or a danger to the holy life,” or not seeing other suitable bhikkhunīs, one does not inform, or not wishing to conceal, one does not inform, or thinking: “She will be known by her own deed,” one does not inform. There is no offense for one who is insane... for the originator of the matter.

Dutiyapārājikaṃ samattaṃ.

The Second Pārājika is concluded.

3. Tatiyapārājikaṃ

3. The Third Pārājika

668. Tena [T 0.0015][P 4.0218][V 0.0293] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṃ ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ anuvattati. Yā [M 0.0282] tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṃ ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ anuvattissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṃ ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ anuvattatīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṃ ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ anuvattissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

668. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time the bhikkhunī Thullanandā followed the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, formerly of a vulture-killing clan, who had been expelled by a united Sangha. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the venerable Thullanandā follow the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, formerly of a vulture-killing clan, who has been expelled by a united Sangha?” … “Is it true, bhikkhus, as has been heard, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā follows the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, formerly of a vulture-killing clan, who has been expelled by a united Sangha?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, bhikkhus, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā follow the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, formerly of a vulture-killing clan, who has been expelled by a united Sangha? This, bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the faithless… And so, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule thus:

669. “Yā pana bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṃ bhikkhuṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anādaraṃ appaṭikāraṃ akatasahāyaṃ tamanuvatteyya, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi evamassa vacanīyā – ‘eso kho, ayye, bhikkhu samaggena saṅghena ukkhitto dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anādaro appaṭikāro akatasahāyo, māyye, etaṃ bhikkhuṃ anuvattī’ti. Evañca sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi vuccamānā tatheva paggaṇheyya, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi yāvatatiyaṃ [T 0.0016] samanubhāsitabbā tassa paṭinissaggāya. Yāvatatiyaṃ ce samanubhāsiyamānā taṃ paṭinissajjeyya, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce paṭinissajjeyya, ayampi pārājikā hoti asaṃvāsā ukkhittānuvattikā”ti.

669. “Whatever bhikkhunī should follow a bhikkhu who has been expelled by a united Sangha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction—one who is disrespectful, unrehabilitated, and without companions—that bhikkhunī should be addressed by the other bhikkhunīs thus: ‘Venerable lady, this bhikkhu has been expelled by a united Sangha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction; he is disrespectful, unrehabilitated, and without companions. Venerable lady, do not follow this bhikkhu.’ And if that bhikkhunī, while being addressed by the other bhikkhunīs, should persist in that same way, that bhikkhunī is to be admonished by the other bhikkhunīs up to the third time for the relinquishment of that matter. If, while being admonished up to the third time, she should relinquish it, that is good. If she should not relinquish it, this bhikkhunī also, being a follower of one who was expelled, is defeated and not in communion.”

670. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

670. Whatever: of whatever sort… Bhikkhunī… in this sense, this bhikkhunī is intended.

Samaggo nāma saṅgho samānasaṃvāsako samānasīmāyaṃ ṭhito.

What is called a united Sangha is one of the same communion, established within the same boundary.

Ukkhitto nāma āpattiyā adassane vā appaṭikamme vā appaṭinissagge vā adassanena vā appaṭikammena vā appaṭinissaggena vā (ka.), adassane vā appaṭikamme vā pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge vā (?) ukkhitto.

What is called expelled is a person expelled for not seeing an offense, for not remedying it, or for not relinquishing it.

Dhammena vinayenāti yena dhammena yena vinayena.

In accordance with the Dhamma and the Vinaya: by whichever Dhamma, by whichever Vinaya.

Satthusāsanenāti [V 0.0294] jinasāsanena buddhasāsanena.

By the Teacher’s instruction: by the Conqueror’s instruction, by the Buddha’s instruction.

Anādaro nāma saṅghaṃ vā gaṇaṃ vā puggalaṃ vā kammaṃ vā nādiyati.

What is called disrespectful is one who does not respect the Sangha, a group, an individual, or a formal act.

Appaṭikāro nāma ukkhitto anosārito.

What is called unrehabilitated is one who is expelled and not reinstated.

Akatasahāyo [P 4.0219] nāma samānasaṃvāsakā bhikkhū vuccanti sahāyā. So tehi saddhiṃ natthi, tena vuccati akatasahāyoti.

What is called ‘one without companions’ is as follows: Bhikkhus who are in the same communion are called companions. That same communion does not exist for him with them; therefore, he is called ‘one without companions’.

Tamanuvatteyyāti [M 0.0283] yaṃdiṭṭhiko so hoti yaṃkhantiko yaṃruciko, sāpi taṃdiṭṭhikā hoti taṃkhantikā taṃrucikā.

She would follow him: whatever view he holds, whatever he approves of, and whatever he prefers, she too holds that same view, approves of that, and prefers that.

Sā bhikkhunīti yā sā ukkhittānuvattikā bhikkhunī.

That bhikkhunī: whichever bhikkhunī is the follower of the expelled one.
