Bhikkhunīhīti aññāhi bhikkhunīhi. Yā passanti yā suṇanti tāhi vattabbā – “eso kho, ayye, bhikkhu samaggena saṅghena ukkhitto dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anādaro appaṭikāro akatasahāyo. Māyye, etaṃ bhikkhuṃ [T 0.0017] anuvattī”ti. Dutiyampi vattabbā. Tatiyampi vattabbā. Sace paṭinissajjati, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ; no ce paṭinissajjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sutvā na vadanti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sā bhikkhunī saṅghamajjhampi ākaḍḍhitvā vattabbā – “eso kho, ayye, bhikkhu samaggena saṅghena ukkhitto dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anādaro appaṭikāro akatasahāyo. Māyye, etaṃ bhikkhuṃ anuvattī”ti. Dutiyampi vattabbā. Tatiyampi vattabbā. Sace paṭinissajjati, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce paṭinissajjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sā bhikkhunī samanubhāsitabbā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, samanubhāsitabbā. Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

By the bhikkhunīs: by other bhikkhunīs. Those who see, those who hear, by them she should be told: ‘Venerable lady, this bhikkhu has been expelled by a united Sangha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction; he is disrespectful, unrehabilitated, and without companions. Venerable lady, do not follow this bhikkhu.’ She should be told a second time. She should be told a third time. If she relinquishes it, that is good; if she does not relinquish it, an offense of wrong-doing is incurred. Those who, having heard, do not speak, incur an offense of wrong-doing. That bhikkhunī, having been brought into the midst of the Sangha, should also be told: ‘Venerable lady, this bhikkhu has been expelled by a united Sangha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction; he is disrespectful, unrehabilitated, and without companions. Venerable lady, do not follow this bhikkhu.’ She should be told a second time. She should be told a third time. If she relinquishes it, that is good. If she does not relinquish it, an offense of wrong-doing is incurred. That bhikkhunī is to be formally admonished. And, bhikkhus, she is to be formally admonished in this way. The Sangha is to be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhunī:

671. “Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṃ bhikkhuṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anādaraṃ appaṭikāraṃ akatasahāyaṃ tamanuvattati, sā taṃ vatthuṃ na paṭinissajjati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuniṃ samanubhāseyya tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya. Esā ñatti.

671. ‘Venerable ladies, may the Sangha hear me. This bhikkhunī, so-and-so by name, follows a bhikkhu who has been expelled by a united Sangha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction—one who is disrespectful, unrehabilitated, and without companions. She does not relinquish that matter. If the time is right for the Sangha, let the Sangha formally admonish the bhikkhunī, so-and-so by name, for the relinquishment of that matter. This is the motion.’

“Suṇātu [V 0.0295] me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṃ bhikkhuṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anādaraṃ appaṭikāraṃ akatasahāyaṃ tamanuvattati. Sā taṃ vatthuṃ na paṭinissajjati. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuniṃ samanubhāsati tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā samanubhāsanā tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya, sā tuṇhassa; yassā [T 0.0018] nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.

‘Venerable ladies, may the Sangha hear me. This bhikkhunī, so-and-so by name, follows a bhikkhu who has been expelled by a united Sangha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction—one who is disrespectful, unrehabilitated, and without companions. She does not relinquish that matter. The Sangha formally admonishes the bhikkhunī, so-and-so by name, for the relinquishment of that matter. To whichever venerable lady the formal admonishment of the bhikkhunī, so-and-so by name, for the relinquishment of that matter is agreeable, she should remain silent. To whomever it is not agreeable, she should speak.’

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

‘For a second time I state this matter… For a third time I state this matter…’

“Samanubhaṭṭhā saṅghena itthannāmā bhikkhunī tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

‘The bhikkhunī, so-and-so by name, has been formally admonished by the Sangha for the relinquishment of that matter. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold this.’

Ñattiyā [M 0.0284] dukkaṭaṃ, dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā, kammavācā pariyosāne āpatti pārājikassa.

For the motion, there is an offense of wrong-doing. For the two proclamations, there are grave offenses. At the conclusion of the proclamation, there is the offense of defeat.

Ayampīti purimāyo upādāya vuccati.

‘This one also’ is said with reference to the preceding bhikkhunīs.

Pārājikā hotīti seyyathāpi nāma puthusilā dvedhā bhinnā appaṭisandhikā hoti, evameva bhikkhunī yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya [P 4.0220] na paṭinissajjantī assamaṇī hoti asakyadhītā. Tena vuccati pārājikā hotīti.

‘She is defeated’ means: just as a broad stone slab, split in two, cannot be rejoined, even so a bhikkhunī who, being admonished up to the third time, does not relinquish the view, is not a recluse, not a daughter of the Sakyan. For that reason it is said, ‘she is defeated’.

Asaṃvāsāti saṃvāso nāma ekakammaṃ ekuddeso samasikkhatā. Eso saṃvāso nāma. So tāya saddhiṃ natthi. Tena vuccati asaṃvāsāti.

‘Not in communion’ means: communion, namely, is a single formal act, a single recitation, and equality in training. All this is called communion. That communion does not exist with her. For that reason it is said, ‘not in communion’.

672. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññā na paṭinissajjati, āpatti pārājikassa. Dhammakamme vematikā na paṭinissajjati, āpatti pārājikassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññā na paṭinissajjati, āpatti pārājikassa.

672. In a lawful formal act, perceiving it as a lawful formal act, she does not relinquish it: there is an offense of defeat. In a lawful formal act, being doubtful, she does not relinquish it: there is an offense of defeat. In a lawful formal act, perceiving it as an unlawful formal act, she does not relinquish it: there is an offense of defeat.

Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In an unlawful formal act, perceiving it as a lawful formal act, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In an unlawful formal act, being doubtful, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In an unlawful formal act, perceiving it as an unlawful formal act, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

673. Anāpatti [V 0.0296] asamanubhāsantiyā, paṭinissajjantiyā, ummattikāya…pe… ādikammikāyāti.

673. There is no offense for one who is not admonished, for one who relinquishes, for one who is insane... (and so on)... for the first offender.

Tatiyapārājikaṃ samattaṃ.

The third Pārājika is concluded.

4. Catutthapārājikaṃ

4. The Fourth Pārājika Training Rule

674. Tena [T 0.0019] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa hatthaggahaṇampi sādiyanti, saṅghāṭikaṇṇaggahaṇampi sādiyanti, santiṭṭhantipi, sallapantipi, saṅketampi gacchanti, purisassapi abbhāgamanaṃ sādiyanti, channampi anupavisanti, kāyampi tadatthāya upasaṃharanti etassa asaddhammassa paṭisevanatthāya. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi [M 0.0285] nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa hatthaggahaṇampi sādiyissanti, saṅghāṭikaṇṇaggahaṇampi sādiyissanti, santiṭṭhissantipi, sallapissantipi, saṅketampi gacchissanti, purisassapi abbhāgamanaṃ sādiyissanti, channampi anupavisissanti, kāyampi tadatthāya upasaṃharissanti etassa asaddhammassa paṭisevanatthāyā”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa hatthaggahaṇampi sādiyanti, saṅghāṭikaṇṇaggahaṇampi sādiyanti, santiṭṭhantipi, sallapantipi, saṅketampi gacchanti, purisassapi abbhāgamanaṃ sādiyanti, channampi anupavisanti, kāyampi tadatthāya upasaṃharanti etassa asaddhammassa paṭisevanatthāyāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi [T 0.0020] buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa hatthaggahaṇampi sādiyissanti, saṅghāṭikaṇṇaggahaṇampi sādiyissanti, santiṭṭhissantipi, sallapissantipi, saṅketampi gacchissanti, purisassapi abbhāgamanaṃ sādiyissanti, channampi anupavisissanti, kāyampi tadatthāya upasaṃharissanti etassa asaddhammassa paṭisevanatthāya! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

674. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs of the group of six, being lustful, consented to the grasping of the hand by a lustful man, consented to the grasping of the corner of the outer robe, stood together with him, conversed with him, went to a rendezvous, consented to the man’s approaching them, entered a concealed place, and offered their bodies for the purpose of engaging in this improper conduct. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six, being lustful, consent to the grasping of the hand by a lustful man, consent to the grasping of the corner of the outer robe, stand together with him, converse with him, go to a rendezvous, consent to the man’s approaching them, enter a concealed place, and offer their bodies for the purpose of engaging in this improper conduct?”… “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunīs of the group of six, being lustful, consent to the grasping of the hand by a lustful man, consent to the grasping of the corner of the outer robe, stand together with him, converse with him, go to a rendezvous, consent to the man’s approaching them, enter a concealed place, and offer their bodies for the purpose of engaging in this improper conduct?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six, being lustful, consent to the grasping of the hand by a lustful man, consent to the grasping of the corner of the outer robe, stand together with him, converse with him, go to a rendezvous, consent to the man’s approaching them, enter a concealed place, and offer their bodies for the purpose of engaging in this improper conduct? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And thus, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

675. “Yā pana bhikkhunī avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa hatthaggahaṇaṃ vā sādiyeyya, saṅghāṭikaṇṇaggahaṇaṃ vā sādiyeyya, santiṭṭheyya vā, sallapeyya vā, saṅketaṃ vā [P 4.0221] gaccheyya[V 0.0297], purisassa vā abbhāgamanaṃ sādiyeyya, channaṃ vā anupaviseyya, kāyaṃ vā tadatthāya upasaṃhareyya etassa asaddhammassa paṭisevanatthāya, ayampi pārājikā hoti asaṃvāsā aṭṭhavatthukā”ti.

675. “Whatever bhikkhunī, being lustful, should consent to the grasping of the hand by a lustful man, or should consent to the grasping of the corner of the outer robe, or should stand with him, or should converse with him, or should go to a rendezvous, or should consent to the man’s approach, or should enter a concealed place, or should offer her body for that purpose, for the sake of engaging in this improper conduct, this bhikkhunī also, on account of the eight grounds, is defeated and not in communion.”

676. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

676. ‘Whatever’ means: of whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… this is the bhikkhunī who is intended in this sense.

Avassutā nāma sārattā apekkhavatī paṭibaddhacittā.

‘Lustful’ (feminine) means: impassioned, longing, with an attached mind.

Avassuto nāma sāratto apekkhavā paṭibaddhacitto.

‘Lustful’ (masculine) means: impassioned, longing, with an attached mind.

Purisapuggalo nāma manussapuriso, na yakkho na peto na tiracchānagato viññū paṭibalo kāyasaṃsaggaṃ samāpajjituṃ.

A ‘male person’ means: a human male, not a yakkha, not a peta, not an animal, who is discerning and capable of engaging in bodily contact.

Hatthaggahaṇaṃ [T 0.0021][M 0.0286] vā sādiyeyyāti hattho nāma kapparaṃ upādāya yāva agganakhā. Etassa asaddhammassa paṭisevanatthāya ubbhakkhakaṃ adhojāṇumaṇḍalaṃ gahaṇaṃ sādiyati, āpatti thullaccayassa.

‘Should consent to the grasping of the hand’: ‘Hand’ means from the elbow up to the tips of the nails. For the purpose of engaging in this improper conduct, if she consents to the grasping of the body above the collarbone and below the kneecap, there is an offense of grave transgression.

Saṅghāṭikaṇṇaggahaṇaṃ vā sādiyeyyāti etassa asaddhammassa paṭisevanatthāya nivatthaṃ vā pārutaṃ vā gahaṇaṃ sādiyati, āpatti thullaccayassa.

‘Or should consent to the grasping of the corner of the outer robe’: For the purpose of engaging in this improper conduct, if she consents to the grasping of a lower garment or an upper garment, there is an offense of grave transgression.

Santiṭṭheyya vāti etassa asaddhammassa paṭisevanatthāya purisassa hatthapāse tiṭṭhati, āpatti thullaccayassa.

‘Or should stand with him’: For the purpose of engaging in this improper conduct, if she stands within arm’s reach of a man, there is an offense of grave transgression.

Sallapeyya vāti etassa asaddhammassa paṭisevanatthāya purisassa hatthapāse ṭhitā sallapati, āpatti thullaccayassa.

‘Or should converse with him’: For the purpose of engaging in this improper conduct, standing within arm’s reach of a man, she converses, there is an offense of grave transgression.

Saṅketaṃ vā gaccheyyāti etassa asaddhammassa paṭisevanatthāya purisena – “itthannāmaṃ okāsaṃ idaṃ padaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ na dissati āgacchā”ti – vuttā gacchati. Pade pade āpatti dukkaṭassa. Purisassa hatthapāsaṃ okkantamatte āpatti thullaccayassa.

‘Or should go to a rendezvous’: For the purpose of engaging in this improper conduct, having been told by a man, “Come to such and such a place,” she goes. For every step, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Upon the moment of entering the man’s arm’s reach, there is an offense of grave transgression.

Purisassa [V 0.0298] vā abbhāgamanaṃ sādiyeyyāti etassa asaddhammassa paṭisevanatthāya purisassa abbhāgamanaṃ sādiyati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Hatthapāsaṃ okkantamatte āpatti thullaccayassa.

“Or should consent to the man’s approach”: For the purpose of engaging in this improper conduct, she consents to a man’s approach; there is an offense of wrongdoing. Upon the moment of his entering her arm’s reach, there is an offense of grave transgression.

Channaṃ vā anupaviseyyāti etassa asaddhammassa paṭisevanatthāya yena kenaci paṭicchannaṃ okāsaṃ paviṭṭhamatte āpatti thullaccayassa.

“Or should enter a concealed place”: For the purpose of engaging in this improper conduct, upon the moment of entering any concealed place whatsoever, there is an offense of grave transgression.

Kāyaṃ vā tadatthāya upasaṃhareyyāti etassa asaddhammassa paṭisevanatthāya purisassa hatthapāse ṭhitā kāyaṃ upasaṃharati, āpatti thullaccayassa.

“Or should offer her body for that purpose”: For the purpose of engaging in this improper conduct, standing within arm’s reach of a man, she offers her body; there is an offense of grave transgression.

Ayampīti purimāyo upādāya vuccati.

“This one also”: This is said with reference to the preceding bhikkhunīs.

Pārājikā hotīti seyyathāpi [T 0.0022] nāma tālo matthakacchinno abhabbo puna viruḷhiyā evameva bhikkhunī aṭṭhamaṃ vatthuṃ [P 4.0222] paripūrentī assamaṇī hoti asakyadhītā. Tena vuccati pārājikā hotīti.

“Is defeated”: Just as a palm tree with its top cut off is incapable of further growth, even so a bhikkhunī, having fulfilled the eighth ground, is not a recluse, not a daughter of the Sakyan. Therefore, it is said, “she is defeated.”

Asaṃvāsāti [M 0.0287] saṃvāso nāma ekakammaṃ ekuddeso samasikkhatā. Eso saṃvāso nāma. So tāya saddhiṃ natthi. Tena vuccati asaṃvāsāti.

“Not in communion”: “Communion” means a common act, a common recitation, and the state of having equal training. This is called “communion.” That communion does not exist with her. Therefore, it is said, “not in communion.”

677. Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantiyā, asādiyantiyā, ummattikāya, khittacittāya, vedanāṭṭāya, ādikammikāyāti.

677. There is no offense if it is unintentional, for one who is unmindful, for one who is unknowing, for one who does not consent, for one who is insane, for one whose mind is deranged, for one who is afflicted by pain, or for the first offender.

Catutthapārājikaṃ samattaṃ.

The Fourth Pārājika is concluded.

Uddiṭṭhā kho, ayyāyo, aṭṭha pārājikā dhammā. Yesaṃ bhikkhunī aññataraṃ vā aññataraṃ vā āpajjitvā na labhati bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ saṃvāsaṃ, yathā pure tathā pacchā, pārājikā hoti asaṃvāsā. Tatthāyyāyo pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Dutiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Tatiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Parisuddhetthāyyāyo, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti.

Venerable ladies, the eight pārājika rules have been recited. Whichever bhikkhunī, having committed any one of these, does not receive communion with the bhikkhunīs—just as before, so afterwards—she is defeated, not in communion. In this matter, I ask the venerable ladies: “Are you pure?” A second time I ask: “Are you pure?” A third time I ask: “Are you pure?” The venerable ladies are pure in this matter; therefore, they are silent. Thus I take it.

Bhikkhunivibhaṅge pārājikakaṇḍaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

In the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, the Chapter on Pārājikas is finished.

2. Saṅghādisesakaṇḍaṃ (bhikkhunīvibhaṅgo)

2. The Chapter on Saṅghādisesa

1. Paṭhamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The First Saṅghādisesa Training Rule

Ime kho panāyyāyo sattarasa saṅghādisesā

Venerable ladies, there are these seventeen Saṅghādisesa rules

Dhammā uddesaṃ āgacchanti.

that come up for recitation.

678. Tena [T 0.0023][P 4.0223][M 0.0288][V 0.0299] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro upāsako bhikkhunisaṅghassa udositaṃ uddositaṃ (sī. syā.) datvā kālaṅkato hoti. Tassa dve puttā honti – eko assaddho appasanno, eko saddho pasanno. Te pettikaṃ sāpateyyaṃ vibhajiṃsu. Atha kho so assaddho appasanno taṃ saddhaṃ pasannaṃ etadavoca – “amhākaṃ udosito, taṃ bhājemā”ti. Evaṃ vutte so saddho pasanno taṃ assaddhaṃ appasannaṃ etadavoca – “māyyo, evaṃ avaca. Amhākaṃ pitunā bhikkhunisaṅghassa dinno”ti. Dutiyampi kho so assaddho appasanno taṃ saddhaṃ pasannaṃ etadavoca – “amhākaṃ udosito, taṃ bhājemā”ti. Atha kho so saddho pasanno taṃ assaddhaṃ appasannaṃ etadavoca – “māyyo, evaṃ avaca. Amhākaṃ pitunā bhikkhunisaṅghassa dinno”ti. Tatiyampi kho so assaddho appasanno taṃ saddhaṃ pasannaṃ etadavoca – “amhākaṃ udosito, taṃ bhājemā”ti. Atha kho so saddho pasanno – “sace mayhaṃ [T 0.0024] bhavissati, ahampi bhikkhunisaṅghassa dassāmī”ti – taṃ assaddhaṃ appasannaṃ etadavoca – “bhājemā”ti. Atha kho so udosito tehi bhājīyamāno tassa assaddhassa appasannassa pāpuṇāti pāpuṇi (syā.). Atha kho so assaddho appasanno bhikkhuniyo upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – “nikkhamathāyye, amhākaṃ udosito”ti.

678. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, a certain lay follower had passed away after giving a storehouse to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha. He had two sons—one without faith and displeased, the other with faith and pleased. They divided their father's inheritance. Then the one without faith and displeased said to the one with faith and pleased: “We have a storehouse; let us divide it.” When this was said, the one with faith and pleased said to the one without faith and displeased: “Friend, do not say so. It was given to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha by our father.” A second time, the one without faith and displeased said to the one with faith and pleased: “We have a storehouse; let us divide it.” Then the one with faith and pleased said to the one without faith and displeased: “Friend, do not say so. It was given to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha by our father.” A third time, the one without faith and displeased said to the one with faith and pleased: “We have a storehouse; let us divide it.” Then the one with faith and pleased, thinking, “If it becomes mine, I too will give it to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha,” said to the one without faith and displeased: “Let us divide it.” Then, as that storehouse was being divided by them, it went to the one without faith and displeased. Then the one without faith and displeased approached the bhikkhunīs and said: “Leave, venerable ladies, this is our storehouse.”

Evaṃ [V 0.0300] vutte thullanandā bhikkhunī taṃ purisaṃ etadavoca – “māyyo, evaṃ avaca, tumhākaṃ pitunā bhikkhunisaṅghassa dinno”ti. “Dinno na dinno”ti vohārike mahāmatte pucchiṃsu. Mahāmattā evamāhaṃsu – “ko, ayye, jānāti bhikkhunisaṅghassa dinno”ti? Evaṃ vutte thullanandā bhikkhunī te mahāmatte etadavoca [P 4.0224] – “api nāyyo api nvayyā (syā.), api nāyyo (ka.) tumhehi diṭṭhaṃ vā sutaṃ vā sakkhiṃ ṭhapayitvā dānaṃ diyyamāna”nti[M 0.0289]? Atha kho te mahāmattā – “saccaṃ kho ayyā āhā”ti taṃ udositaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghassa akaṃsu. Atha kho so puriso parājito ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “assamaṇiyo imā muṇḍā bandhakiniyo. Kathañhi nāma amhākaṃ udositaṃ acchindāpessantī”ti! Thullanandā bhikkhunī mahāmattānaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Mahāmattā taṃ purisaṃ daṇḍāpesuṃ. Atha kho so puriso daṇḍito bhikkhunūpassayassa avidūre ājīvakaseyyaṃ kārāpetvā ājīvake uyyojesi – “etā bhikkhuniyo accāvadathā”ti.

When this was said, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā said to that man: “Friend, do not say so; it was given to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha by your father.” Regarding “given or not given,” they asked the ministers in charge of legal matters. The ministers said: “Venerable lady, who knows that it was given to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha?” When this was said, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā said to those ministers: “Good sirs, have you ever seen or heard of a gift being given after establishing a witness?” Then those ministers, thinking, “The venerable lady speaks the truth,” made that storehouse the property of the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha. Then that man, being defeated, complained, disparaged, and spread criticism, saying: “These shaven-headed ones are not true ascetics, these wretched women! How could they have our storehouse seized?” The bhikkhunī Thullanandā reported this matter to the ministers. The ministers had that man punished. Then that man, having been punished, had a dwelling for Ājīvakas built not far from the bhikkhunīs’ residence and incited the Ājīvakas, saying: “Go and revile these bhikkhunīs excessively!”

Thullanandā bhikkhunī mahāmattānaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Mahāmattā taṃ purisaṃ bandhāpesuṃ. Manussā ujjhāyanti [T 0.0025] khiyyanti vipācenti – “paṭhamaṃ bhikkhuniyo udositaṃ acchindāpesuṃ, dutiyaṃ daṇḍāpesuṃ, tatiyaṃ bandhāpesuṃ. Idāni ghātāpessantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā ussayavādikā viharissatī”ti! Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī ussayavādikā viharatīti. “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī ussayavādikā viharissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

The bhikkhunī Thullanandā reported this matter to the ministers. The ministers had that man bound. People complained, disparaged, and spread criticism: “First, the bhikkhunīs had the storehouse seized; second, they had him punished; third, they had him bound. Now they will have him killed!” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, disparaging, and spreading criticism. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they complained, disparaged, and spread criticism, saying: “How could the venerable Thullanandā live being litigious?” Then those bhikkhunīs reported this matter to the bhikkhus… “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā is living as one who is litigious?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How, Bhikkhus, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā live being litigious? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

679. “Yā pana bhikkhunī ussayavādikā vihareyya gahapatinā vā gahapatiputtena vā dāsena vā kammakārena kammakarena (sī. syā.) vā antamaso samaṇaparibbājakenāpi, ayaṃ bhikkhunī paṭhamāpattikaṃ dhammaṃ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṃ saṅghādisesa”nti.

679. “Whatever bhikkhunī should live being litigious with a householder, a householder’s son, a slave, a workman, or even at the very least with an ascetic or wanderer, this bhikkhunī has, at the first instance of the offense, committed a Saṅghādisesa offense that requires being sent away.”

680. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

680. Whatever means: of whatever sort… A bhikkhunī means: …a bhikkhunī is to be understood in this sense.

Ussayavādikā nāma aḍḍakārikā vuccati.

One who is litigious is said to be one who makes a legal case.

Gahapati [V 0.0301] nāma yo koci agāraṃ ajjhāvasati.

A householder is any person who lives in and presides over a house.

Gahapatiputto [M 0.0290] nāma ye keci puttabhātaro.

A householder’s son means any sons or brothers.

Dāso nāma antojāto dhanakkīto karamarānīto[T 0.0026].

A slave is one born in the house, one bought with wealth, or one brought as a captive of war.

Kammakāro nāma bhaṭako āhatako.

A worker is one who is a wage-earner or one who is permanently employed.

Samaṇaparibbājako nāma bhikkhuñca bhikkhuniñca sikkhamānañca sāmaṇerañca sāmaṇeriñca ṭhapetvā yo koci paribbājakasamāpanno.

A wandering ascetic is any person who has attained the state of a wanderer, setting aside a bhikkhu, a bhikkhunī, a female probationary novice, a male novice, and a female novice.

Aḍḍaṃ [P 4.0225] karissāmīti dutiyaṃ vā pariyesati gacchati vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ekassa āroceti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Dutiyassa āroceti, āpatti thullaccayassa. Aḍḍapariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

Thinking, 'I will initiate a legal action,' if she seeks a companion or goes, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she informs one person, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she informs a second person, there is an offense of a grave transgression. At the conclusion of the legal action, there is a Saṅghādisesa offense.

Paṭhamāpattikanti saha vatthujjhācārā āpajjati asamanubhāsanāya.

‘An offense at the first transgression’ means that it is incurred together with the transgression concerning the object, without admonition.

Nissāraṇīyanti saṅghamhā nissārīyati.

‘Requiring expulsion’ means one is expelled from the Saṅgha.

Saṅghādisesanti saṅghova tassā āpattiyā mānattaṃ deti mūlāya paṭikassati abbheti, na sambahulā na ekā bhikkhunī. Tena vuccati “saṅghādiseso”ti. Tasseva āpattinikāyassa nāmakammaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Tenapi vuccati “saṅghādiseso”ti.

‘Saṅghādisesa’ means that the Saṅgha alone gives the penance (mānatta) for that offense, recalls to the beginning, and reinstates—not many bhikkhunīs, nor a single bhikkhunī. Therefore, it is called ‘Saṅghādisesa.’ It is a name, a designation, for that very group of offenses. For that reason too, it is called ‘Saṅghādisesa.’

681. Anāpatti manussehi ākaḍḍhīyamānā gacchati, ārakkhaṃ yācati, anodissa ācikkhati, ummattikāya…pe… ādikammikāyāti.

681. There is no offense if she goes while being dragged by people, if she asks for protection, if she reports without specifying, for one who is insane... or for the first offender.

Paṭhamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The First Saṅghādisesa Training Rule is concluded.

2. Dutiyasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Second Saṅghādisesa Training Rule

682. Tena [V 0.0302] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena vesāliyaṃ aññatarassa licchavissa pajāpati aticārinī hoti. Atha kho so licchavi [T 0.0027] taṃ itthiṃ etadavoca – “sādhu viramāhi, anatthaṃ kho te karissāmī”ti. Evampi sā vuccamānā nādiyi. Tena kho pana samayena vesāliyaṃ licchavigaṇo sannipatito hoti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho so licchavi te licchavayo etadavoca – “ekaṃ me, ayyo[M 0.0291], itthiṃ anujānāthā”ti. “Kā nāma sā”ti? “Mayhaṃ pajāpati aticarati, taṃ ghātessāmī”ti. “Jānāhī”ti. Assosi kho sā itthī – “sāmiko kira maṃ ghātetukāmo”ti. Varabhaṇḍaṃ ādāya sāvatthiṃ gantvā titthiye upasaṅkamitvā pabbajjaṃ yāci. Titthiyā na icchiṃsu pabbājetuṃ. Bhikkhuniyo upasaṅkamitvā pabbajjaṃ yāci. Bhikkhuniyopi na icchiṃsu pabbājetuṃ. Thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ upasaṅkamitvā bhaṇḍakaṃ dassetvā pabbajjaṃ yāci. Thullanandā bhikkhunī bhaṇḍakaṃ gahetvā pabbājesi.

682. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, in Vesālī, the wife of a certain Licchavi was committing adultery. Then that Licchavi said this to that woman: “It would be good for you to desist, or I will bring about your ruin.” Even when spoken to thus, she did not pay heed. Now at that time, the assembly of Licchavis had gathered in Vesālī for some business. Then that Licchavi said this to those Licchavis: “Sirs, grant me permission concerning one woman.” “Who is she?” “My wife is committing adultery; I will kill her.” “Do as you know best,” they said. That woman heard: “It seems my husband wishes to kill me.” Taking her valuable goods, she went to Sāvatthī and approached the sectarians, requesting ordination. The sectarians did not wish to ordain her. She approached the bhikkhunīs and requested ordination. The bhikkhunīs also did not wish to ordain her. She approached the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, showed her the bundle of goods, and requested ordination. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā took the bundle of goods and ordained her.

Atha kho so licchavi taṃ itthiṃ gavesanto sāvatthiṃ gantvā bhikkhunīsu pabbajitaṃ disvāna yena rājā pasenadi kosalo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā [P 4.0226] rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ etadavoca – “pajāpati me, deva, varabhaṇḍaṃ ādāya sāvatthiṃ anuppattā. Taṃ devo anujānātū”ti. “Tena hi, bhaṇe, vicinitvā ācikkhā”ti. “Diṭṭhā, deva, bhikkhunīsu pabbajitā”ti. “Sace, bhaṇe, bhikkhunīsu pabbajitā, na sā labbhā kiñci kātuṃ. Svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, caratu brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Atha kho so licchavi ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti [T 0.0028] – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo coriṃ pabbājessantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tassa licchavissa ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā coriṃ pabbājessatī”ti! Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī coriṃ pabbājetīti pabbājesīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī coriṃ pabbājessati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

Then that Licchavi, searching for that woman, went to Sāvatthī and, having seen her ordained among the bhikkhunīs, he approached King Pasenadi of Kosala. Having approached, he said this to King Pasenadi of Kosala: “Your Majesty, my wife has taken valuable goods and arrived in Sāvatthī. May Your Majesty grant permission concerning her.” “In that case, my good man, investigate and inform me.” “Your Majesty, she has been seen ordained among the bhikkhunīs.” “My good man, if she has been ordained among the bhikkhunīs, it is not possible to do anything to her. The Dhamma has been well-proclaimed by the Blessed One; let her practice the holy life for the right ending of suffering.” Then that Licchavi complained, scorned, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed could the bhikkhunīs ordain a female thief!” The bhikkhunīs heard that Licchavi complaining, scorning, and speaking disparagingly. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… complained, scorned, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed could the venerable Thullanandā ordain a female thief!” Then those bhikkhunīs reported this matter to the bhikkhus… “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā ordained a female thief?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā ordain a female thief! This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

683. “Yā [V 0.0303] pana bhikkhunī jānaṃ coriṃ vajjhaṃ viditaṃ anapaloketvā rājānaṃ vā saṅghaṃ vā gaṇaṃ vā pūgaṃ vā seṇiṃ vā aññatra kappā vuṭṭhāpeyya, ayampi bhikkhunī paṭhamāpattikaṃ dhammaṃ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṃ saṅghādisesa”nti.

683. “Whatever bhikkhunī, knowingly, should give the higher ordination to a female thief who is subject to punishment and is known as such, without having informed the king, or the Saṅgha, or a group, or an association, or a guild—except in the case of one who has been previously ordained—this bhikkhunī too has fallen into a Saṅghādisesa offense, which is incurred at the first transgression and requires expulsion.”

684. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

684. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever sort… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… in this sense, ‘bhikkhunī’ is intended.

Jānāti [M 0.0292] nāma sāmaṃ vā jānāti aññe vā tassā ārocenti, sā vā āroceti.

‘Knows’ means: one knows oneself, or others inform her, or she (the thief) herself informs.

Corī nāma yā pañcamāsakaṃ vā atirekapañcamāsakaṃ vā agghanakaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyati, esā corī nāma.

A ‘female thief’ is a woman who takes, with the intention described as theft, what is not given that is worth five māsakas or more than five māsakas. This is called a ‘female thief’.

Vajjhā nāma yaṃ katvā vajjhappattā hoti.

‘Subject to punishment’ is one who, having committed a certain act, has become subject to punishment.

Viditā nāma aññehi manussehi ñātā hoti [T 0.0029] “vajjhā esā”ti.

‘Known’ means she is known by other people as, “This one is subject to punishment.”

Anapaloketvāti anāpucchā.

‘Without having informed’ means without having informed.

Rājā nāma yattha rājā anusāsati, rājā apaloketabbo.

‘King’ means: where a king governs, the king should be informed.

Saṅgho nāma bhikkhunisaṅgho vuccati, bhikkhunisaṅgho apaloketabbo.

‘Saṅgha’ means the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs; the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs should be informed.

Gaṇo nāma yattha gaṇo anusāsati, gaṇo apaloketabbo.

‘Group’ means: where a group governs, the group should be informed.

Pūgo nāma yattha pūgo anusāsati, pūgo apaloketabbo.

‘Association’ means: where an association governs, the association should be informed.

Seṇi nāma yattha seṇi anusāsati, seṇi apaloketabbo.

‘Guild’ means: where a guild governs, the guild should be informed.

Aññatra [P 4.0227] kappāti ṭhapetvā kappaṃ. Kappaṃ nāma dve kappāni – titthiyesu vā pabbajitā hoti aññāsu vā bhikkhunīsu pabbajitā. Aññatra kappā “vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti gaṇaṃ vā ācariniṃ [V 0.0304] vā pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā. Kammavācāpariyosāne upajjhāyāya āpatti saṅghādisesassa. Gaṇassa ca ācariniyā ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

‘Except for one previously ordained’ means setting aside one who has been previously ordained. ‘One previously ordained’ refers to two types: she has been ordained among heretics, or she has been ordained among other bhikkhunīs. If, setting aside one who has been previously ordained, one thinks, “I will give ordination,” and seeks a group, or a female teacher, or a bowl, or robes, or establishes a boundary, it is an offense of wrong conduct. With the motion, it is an offense of wrong conduct. With the two formal declarations, there are grave offenses. At the conclusion of the formal declaration, the preceptor incurs a Saṅghādisesa offense. The group and the female teacher incur an offense of wrong conduct.

Ayampīti purimaṃ upādāya vuccati.

‘This one too’ is said with reference to the preceding one.

Paṭhamāpattikanti saha vatthujjhācārā āpajjati asamanubhāsanāya.

‘Incurred at the first transgression’ means one incurs an offense together with the transgression of the object, without requiring admonition.

Nissāraṇīyanti saṅghamhā nissārīyati.

‘Requiring expulsion’ means one is to be expelled from the Saṅgha.

Saṅghādisesanti…pe… tenapi vuccati saṅghādisesoti.

‘Saṅghādisesa’… and therefore it is called Saṅghādisesa.

685. Coriyā corisaññā aññatra kappā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti saṅghādisesassa. Coriyā vematikā aññatra kappā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti [M 0.0293] dukkaṭassa. Coriyā acorisaññā aññatra kappā [T 0.0030] vuṭṭhāpeti, anāpatti. Acoriyā corisaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Acoriyā vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Acoriyā acorisaññā, anāpatti.

685. Regarding a thief, if one perceives her as a thief and gives ordination—excepting one previously ordained—it is a Saṅghādisesa offense. Regarding a thief, if one is doubtful and gives ordination—excepting one previously ordained—it is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding a thief, if one perceives her as not a thief and gives ordination—excepting one previously ordained—there is no offense. Regarding a non-thief, if one perceives her as a thief, it is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding a non-thief, if one is doubtful, it is an offense of wrong conduct. Regarding a non-thief, if one perceives her as not a thief, there is no offense.

686. Anāpatti ajānantī vuṭṭhāpeti, apaloketvā vuṭṭhāpeti, kappakataṃ vuṭṭhāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

686. There is no offense if one gives ordination unknowingly; if one gives ordination after having informed; if one gives ordination to one who has been previously ordained; for one who is insane; and for the first offender.

Dutiyasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Second Saṅghādisesa Training Rule is concluded.

3. Tatiyasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Third Saṅghādisesa Training Rule

687. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhaddāya kāpilāniyā antevāsinī bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ bhaṇḍitvā gāmakaṃ gāmake (syā.) ñātikulaṃ agamāsi. Bhaddā kāpilānī taṃ bhikkhuniṃ apassantī bhikkhuniyo pucchi – “kahaṃ itthannāmā, na dissatī”ti! “Bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ, ayye, bhaṇḍitvā na dissatī”ti. “Ammā, amukasmiṃ gāmake etissā ñātikulaṃ. Tattha gantvā vicinathā”ti. Bhikkhuniyo tattha gantvā taṃ bhikkhuniṃ passitvā etadavocuṃ – “kissa tvaṃ, ayye[V 0.0305], ekikā āgatā, kaccisi appadhaṃsitā”ti? “Appadhaṃsitāmhi, ayye”ti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī ekā gāmantaraṃ gacchissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī ekā gāmantaraṃ gacchatīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi [T 0.0031] buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave[P 4.0228], bhikkhunī ekā gāmantaraṃ gacchissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

687. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, at Jeta’s Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, a bhikkhunī who was a pupil of Bhaddā Kāpilānī, having quarreled with the bhikkhunīs, went to a small village, to her relatives’ home. Bhaddā Kāpilānī, not seeing that bhikkhunī, asked the other bhikkhunīs, “Where is the bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name? She is not to be seen!” “Venerable lady, having quarreled with the bhikkhunīs, she is not to be seen.” “My dears, in such-and-such a small village is her relatives’ home. Go there and search.” The bhikkhunīs went there, and upon seeing that bhikkhunī, they said this: “Venerable lady, why have you come alone? Surely you have not been violated?” “I have not been violated, venerable ladies.” Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they criticized, scorned, and spread it about, saying, “How indeed can a bhikkhunī go to another village alone?”… “Is it true, monks, that a bhikkhunī goes to another village alone?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, monks, can a bhikkhunī go to another village alone? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the faithless… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

“Yā pana bhikkhunī ekā gāmantaraṃ gaccheyya, ayampi bhikkhunī paṭhamāpattikaṃ dhammaṃ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṃ saṅghādisesa”nti.

“Whatever bhikkhunī should go alone to another village, this bhikkhunī too has committed a Saṅghādisesa offense, incurred at the first instance and requiring expulsion.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule for the bhikkhunīs was laid down by the Blessed One.

688. Tena [M 0.0294] kho pana samayena dve bhikkhuniyo sāketā sāvatthiṃ addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti. Antarāmagge nadī taritabbā hoti. Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo nāvike upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – “sādhu no, āvuso, tārethā”ti. “Nāyye, sakkā ubho sakiṃ tāretu”nti. Eko ekaṃ uttāresi. Uttiṇṇo uttiṇṇaṃ dūsesi. Anuttiṇṇo anuttiṇṇaṃ dūsesi. Tā pacchā samāgantvā pucchiṃsu – “kaccisi, ayye, appadhaṃsitā”ti? “Padhaṃsitāmhi, ayye! Tvaṃ pana, ayye, appadhaṃsitā”ti? “Padhaṃsitāmhi, ayye”ti. Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo sāvatthiṃ gantvā bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī ekā nadīpāraṃ gacchissatī”ti! Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī ekā nadīpāraṃ gacchatī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī ekā nadīpāraṃ gacchissati! Netaṃ[T 0.0032], bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

688. Now at that time, two bhikkhunīs were traveling on a long journey from Sāketa to Sāvatthī. On the way, there was a river to be crossed. Then those bhikkhunīs approached the boatmen and said this, “Friends, please ferry us across.” “Venerable ladies, it is not possible to ferry both at once.” One ferried one across. The boatman who had crossed violated the bhikkhunī who had been crossed over. The boatman who had not yet crossed violated the bhikkhunī who had not yet been crossed over. Later, when they met, they asked each other, “Venerable, I hope you were unharmed?” “I was violated, venerable lady! And you, venerable lady, were you unharmed?” “I was violated, venerable lady.” Then those bhikkhunīs, having gone to Sāvatthī, reported this matter to the bhikkhunīs. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they criticized, scorned, and spread it about, saying, “How indeed can a bhikkhunī go alone to the other side of a river!” Then those bhikkhunīs reported this matter to the bhikkhus. The bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, monks, that a bhikkhunī goes alone to the other side of a river?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, monks, can a bhikkhunī go alone to the other side of a river! This, monks, is not for the confidence of the faithless… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

“Yā pana bhikkhunī ekā vā gāmantaraṃ gaccheyya, ekā vā nadīpāraṃ gaccheyya, ayampi bhikkhunī paṭhamāpattikaṃ dhammaṃ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṃ saṅghādisesa”nti.

“Whatever bhikkhunī should go alone to another village, or should go alone to the other side of a river, this bhikkhunī too has committed a Saṅghādisesa offense, incurred at the first instance and requiring expulsion.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And so this training rule for the bhikkhunīs was laid down by the Blessed One.

689. Tena [V 0.0306] kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhuniyo kosalesu janapade sāvatthiṃ gacchantā gantvā (ka.) sāyaṃ aññataraṃ gāmaṃ upagacchiṃsu. Tattha aññatarā bhikkhunī abhirūpā hoti dassanīyā pāsādikā. Aññataro puriso tassā bhikkhuniyā saha dassanena paṭibaddhacitto hoti. Atha kho so puriso tāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ seyyaṃ paññapento tassā bhikkhuniyā seyyaṃ [P 4.0229] ekamantaṃ paññāpesi. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī sallakkhetvā – “pariyuṭṭhito ayaṃ puriso; sace rattiṃ āgacchissati, vissaro me bhavissatī”ti, bhikkhuniyo anāpucchā aññataraṃ kulaṃ gantvā seyyaṃ kappesi. Atha kho so puriso rattiṃ [M 0.0295] āgantvā taṃ bhikkhuniṃ gavesanto bhikkhuniyo ghaṭṭesi. Bhikkhuniyo taṃ bhikkhuniṃ apassantiyo evamāhaṃsu – “nissaṃsayaṃ kho sā bhikkhunī purisena saddhiṃ nikkhantā”ti.

689. Now at that time, many bhikkhunīs were traveling through the country of the Kosalans toward Sāvatthī. In the evening, they approached a certain village. There, a certain bhikkhunī was very beautiful, lovely to see, and inspiring. A certain man became infatuated with that bhikkhunī upon seeing her. Then that man, while preparing the lodging for those bhikkhunīs, prepared the bed for that bhikkhunī in a secluded place. Then that bhikkhunī, having noted this, thought: “This man is afflicted with passion; if he comes at night, I will make a cry of distress.” Without asking the other bhikkhunīs, she went to a certain family's house and made her bed. Then that man, having come at night and searching for that bhikkhunī, disturbed the other bhikkhunīs. The bhikkhunīs, not seeing that bhikkhunī, said thus: “Without a doubt, that bhikkhunī has gone out with a man.”

Atha kho sā bhikkhunī tassā rattiyā accayena yena tā bhikkhuniyo tenupasaṅkami. Bhikkhuniyo taṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavocuṃ – “kissa tvaṃ, ayye, purisena saddhiṃ nikkhantā”ti? “Nāhaṃ, ayye, purisena saddhiṃ nikkhantā”ti. Bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ [T 0.0033] ārocesi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī ekā rattiṃ vippavasissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī ekā rattiṃ vippavasīti vippavasīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī ekā rattiṃ vippavasissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

Then, after that night had passed, that bhikkhunī approached those bhikkhunīs. The bhikkhunīs said this to that bhikkhunī: “Venerable lady, why did you go out with a man?” “Venerable ladies, I did not go out with a man.” She told this matter to the bhikkhunīs. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… criticized, scorned, and spread the word, saying: “How indeed could a bhikkhunī stay away alone for a night?”… “Monks, is it true that a bhikkhunī stayed away alone for a night?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “Monks, how indeed could a bhikkhunī stay away alone for a night! Monks, this does not lead to the faith of the faithless… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

“Yā pana bhikkhunī ekā vā gāmantaraṃ gaccheyya, ekā vā nadīpāraṃ gaccheyya, ekā vā rattiṃ vippavaseyya, ayampi bhikkhunī paṭhamāpattikaṃ dhammaṃ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṃ saṅghādisesa”nti.

Whatever bhikkhunī should go alone to another village, or should go alone to the other side of a river, or should stay alone for a night, this bhikkhunī has also committed a Saṅghādisesa offense, which is incurred at the first transgression and requires expulsion.

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

Thus, this training rule for the bhikkhunīs was laid down by the Blessed One.

690. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhuniyo kosalesu janapade sāvatthiṃ addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti. Tattha aññatarā bhikkhunī vaccena pīḷitā ekikā ohīyitvā ohiyitvā (ka.) pacchā agamāsi. Manussā taṃ bhikkhuniṃ passitvā dūsesuṃ. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī yena tā bhikkhuniyo tenupasaṅkami. Bhikkhuniyo taṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavocuṃ – “kissa tvaṃ, ayye, ekikā ohīnā, kaccisi appadhaṃsitā”ti? “Padhaṃsitāmhi, ayye”ti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – kathañhi [V 0.0307] nāma bhikkhunī ekā gaṇamhā ohīyissatīti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī ekā gaṇamhā ohīyatīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti[T 0.0034]. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī ekā gaṇamhā ohīyissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

690. Now at that time, many bhikkhunīs were proceeding on a long journey in the country of the Kosalans to Sāvatthī. There, a certain bhikkhunī, being afflicted by the need to defecate, was left behind alone and went on afterwards. Men, seeing that bhikkhunī, violated her. Then that bhikkhunī approached those bhikkhunīs. The bhikkhunīs said this to her: “Venerable lady, why were you left behind alone? I hope you were not violated?” “I was violated, venerable ladies.” Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… criticized, scorned, and spread the word, saying: “How indeed could a bhikkhunī be left behind alone from the group?”… “Monks, is it true, as has been heard, that a bhikkhunī was left behind alone from the group?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “Monks, how indeed could a bhikkhunī be left behind alone from the group! Monks, this does not lead to the faith of the faithless… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

691. “Yā [M 0.0296] pana bhikkhunī ekā vā gāmantaraṃ gaccheyya, ekā vā nadīpāraṃ gaccheyya, ekā vā rattiṃ vippavaseyya, ekā vā gaṇamhā ohīyeyya, ayampi bhikkhunī paṭhamāpattikaṃ [P 4.0230] dhammaṃ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṃ saṅghādisesa”nti.

691. Whatever bhikkhunī should go alone to another village, or should go alone to the other side of a river, or should stay alone for a night, or should be left behind alone from the group, this bhikkhunī has also committed a Saṅghādisesa offense, which is incurred at the first transgression and requires expulsion.

692. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

692. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Ekā vā gāmantaraṃ gaccheyyāti parikkhittassa gāmassa parikkhepaṃ paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmentiyā āpatti thullaccayassa, dutiyaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmentiyā āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

‘Should go alone to another village’ means: for a bhikkhunī who crosses the enclosure of an enclosed village with the first footstep, there is an offense of grave transgression; for one who crosses with the second footstep, there is an offense of Saṅghādisesa.

Aparikkhittassa gāmassa upacāraṃ paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmentiyā āpatti thullaccayassa. Dutiyaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmentiyā āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

For a bhikkhunī who crosses the precincts of an unenclosed village with the first footstep, there is an offense of grave transgression. For one who crosses with the second footstep, there is an offense of Saṅghādisesa.

Ekā vā nadīpāraṃ gaccheyyāti nadī nāma timaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādetvā yattha katthaci uttarantiyā bhikkhuniyā antaravāsako temiyati. Paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ uttarantiyā āpatti thullaccayassa. Dutiyaṃ pādaṃ uttarantiyā āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

‘Should go alone to the other side of a river’ means: a river is defined as that which, upon being crossed anywhere, wets the under-robe of a bhikkhunī. For a bhikkhunī crossing with the first footstep, there is an offense of grave transgression. For one crossing with the second footstep, there is an offense of Saṅghādisesa.

Ekā vā rattiṃ vippavaseyyāti saha aruṇuggamanā dutiyikāya bhikkhuniyā hatthapāsaṃ vijahantiyā āpatti thullaccayassa. Vijahite āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

‘Should stay alone for a night’ means: for a bhikkhunī who is in the process of leaving the hand’s reach of a companion bhikkhunī at the rising of the dawn, there is an offense of grave transgression. When she has left it, there is an offense of Saṅghādisesa.

Ekā vā gaṇamhā ohīyeyyāti agāmake araññe dutiyikāya bhikkhuniyā dassanūpacāraṃ vā [T 0.0035] savanūpacāraṃ vā vijahantiyā āpatti thullaccayassa. Vijahite āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

‘Should be left behind alone from the group’ means: in a forest where there is no village, for a bhikkhunī who is in the process of leaving either the range of sight or the range of hearing of a companion bhikkhunī, there is an offense of grave transgression. When she has left it, there is an offense of Saṅghādisesa.

Ayampīti [V 0.0308] purimāyo upādāya vuccati.

‘This also’ means: this is said in reference to the preceding bhikkhunīs.

Paṭhamāpattikanti saha vatthujjhācārā āpajjati asamanubhāsanāya.

‘Incurred at the first transgression’ means: one commits the offense at the same time as the transgression itself, not because of a formal admonishment.

Nissāraṇīyanti saṅghamhā nissārīyati.

‘Requiring expulsion’ means: one is to be expelled from the Saṅgha.

Saṅghādisesoti…pe… tenapi vuccati saṅghādisesoti.

‘Saṅghādisesa’ means: … for that reason also it is called ‘Saṅghādisesa’.

693. Anāpatti dutiyikā bhikkhunī pakkantā vā hoti vibbhantā vā kālaṅkatā vā pakkhasaṅkantā vā, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

693. There is no offense if the companion bhikkhunī has departed, or has disrobed, or has died, or has gone over to another sect; in times of danger; for an insane bhikkhunī; for the first offender.

Tatiyasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The third Saṅghādisesa training rule is finished.

4. Catutthasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Fourth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule.

694. Tena [M 0.0297] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī bhaṇḍanakārikā hoti kalahakārikā vivādakārikā bhassakārikā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārikā. Thullanandā bhikkhunī tassā kamme karīyamāne paṭikkosati. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī gāmakaṃ agamāsi kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho bhikkhunisaṅgho – “thullanandā bhikkhunī pakkantā”ti[P 4.0231], caṇḍakāḷiṃ bhikkhuniṃ āpattiyā adassane adassanena (ka.) ukkhipi. Thullanandā bhikkhunī gāmake taṃ karaṇīyaṃ tīretvā punadeva sāvatthiṃ paccāgacchi. Caṇḍakāḷī [T 0.0036] bhikkhunī thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā āgacchantiyā neva āsanaṃ paññapesi na pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakaṭhalikaṃ upanikkhipi na paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahesi na pānīyena āpucchi. Thullanandā bhikkhunī caṇḍakāḷiṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “kissa tvaṃ, ayye, mayi āgacchantiyā neva āsanaṃ paññapesi na pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakaṭhalikaṃ upanikkhipi na paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahesi na pānīyena āpucchī”ti? “Evañhetaṃ, ayye, hoti yathā taṃ anāthāyā”ti. “Kissa pana tvaṃ, ayye, anāthā”ti? “Imā maṃ, ayye, bhikkhuniyo – “ayaṃ anāthā appaññātā, natthi imissā kāci paṭivattā”ti, āpattiyā adassane adassanena (ka.) ukkhipiṃsū”ti.

694. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī was prone to quarreling, prone to arguing, prone to disputing, prone to being contentious, and prone to creating legal issues in the Saṅgha. When a formal act was being carried out against her, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā protested. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā had gone to a small village on some business. Then the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, thinking, “The bhikkhunī Thullanandā has departed,” suspended the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī for not seeing her offense. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having concluded that business in the small village, returned again to Sāvatthī. The bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī neither prepared a seat for the arriving bhikkhunī Thullanandā, nor placed nearby water for the feet, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet, nor went to meet her and receive her bowl and robe, nor asked about drinking water. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā said this to the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī: “Venerable, why is it that when I was arriving, you neither prepared a seat, nor placed nearby water for the feet, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet, nor went to meet me and receive my bowl and robe, nor asked if I wanted drinking water?” “Venerable, this is how it is for one who is without a protector.” “But venerable, why are you without a protector?” “Venerable, these bhikkhunīs suspended me for not seeing an offense, saying, ‘This one is without a protector, she is unknown, there is no one to restrain on her behalf.’”

Thullanandā [V 0.0309] bhikkhunī – “bālā etā abyattā etā, neva jānanti kammaṃ vā kammadosaṃ vā kammavipattiṃ vā kammasampattiṃ vā. Mayaṃ kho jānāma kammampi kammadosampi kammavipattimpi kammasampattimpi. Mayaṃ kho akataṃ vā kammaṃ kāreyyāma kataṃ vā kammaṃ kopeyyāmā”ti, lahuṃ lahuṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ sannipātetvā caṇḍakāḷiṃ bhikkhuniṃ osāresi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṃ bhikkhuniṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anapaloketvā kārakasaṅghaṃ anaññāya gaṇassa chandaṃ osāressatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṃ bhikkhuniṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anapaloketvā [T 0.0037] kārakasaṅghaṃ anaññāya gaṇassa chandaṃ osāretīti osāresīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ[M 0.0298], bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṃ bhikkhuniṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anapaloketvā kārakasaṅghaṃ anaññāya gaṇassa chandaṃ osāressati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

The bhikkhunī Thullanandā said, “These are foolish, these are incompetent; they do not know what is a formal act, the fault of a formal act, the failure of a formal act, or the completion of a formal act. But we know what is a formal act, the fault of a formal act, the failure of a formal act, and the completion of a formal act. We could cause an unperformed formal act to be performed, or we could invalidate a performed formal act.” Then, having hastily assembled the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, she reinstated the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… criticized, censured, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the venerable Thullanandā reinstate a bhikkhunī who had been suspended by a unified Saṅgha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction, without informing the Saṅgha that performed the act and without having ascertained the consent of the group?”… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā reinstated a bhikkhunī who had been suspended by a unified Saṅgha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction, without informing the Saṅgha that performed the act and without having ascertained the consent of the group?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, bhikkhus, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā reinstate a bhikkhunī who had been suspended by a unified Saṅgha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction, without informing the Saṅgha that performed the act and without having ascertained the consent of the group! This, bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the faithless… And so, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule in this way:

695. “Yā pana bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṃ bhikkhuniṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anapaloketvā kārakasaṅghaṃ anaññāya gaṇassa chandaṃ osāreyya, ayampi bhikkhunī paṭhamāpattikaṃ dhammaṃ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṃ saṅghādisesa”nti.

695. “Whatever bhikkhunī should reinstate a bhikkhunī suspended by a unified Saṅgha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction, without informing the Saṅgha that performed the act and without having ascertained the consent of the group, this bhikkhunī too has committed an offense at the first instance, entailing expulsion, a Saṅghādisesa.”

696. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

696. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind... ‘Bhikkhunī’ means... this is the bhikkhunī who is meant in this context.

Samaggo nāma saṅgho samānasaṃvāsako samānasīmāyaṃ ṭhito.

A unified Saṅgha, it is said, is a Saṅgha of the same communion, established within the same boundary.

Ukkhittā [P 4.0232] nāma āpattiyā adassane vā appaṭikamme vā appaṭinissagge vā adassanena vā appaṭikammena vā appaṭinissaggena vā (ka.), adassane vā appaṭikamme vā pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge vā (?) ukkhittā.

‘Suspended,’ it is said, means suspended for not seeing an offense, for not making amends for it, or for not relinquishing a wrong view.

Dhammena vinayenāti yena dhammena yena vinayena.

‘In accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya’ means: by that Dhamma, by that Vinaya.

Satthusāsanenāti jinasāsanena buddhasāsanena.

‘By the Teacher’s instruction’ means: by the Conqueror’s instruction, by the Buddha’s instruction.

Anapaloketvā [V 0.0310] kārakasaṅghanti kammakārakasaṅghaṃ anāpucchā.

‘Without informing the Saṅgha that performed the act’ means: without asking the Saṅgha that performed the formal act.

Anaññāya gaṇassa chandanti gaṇassa chandaṃ ajānitvā.

‘Without having ascertained the consent of the group’ means: not having known the consent of the group.

“Osāressāmī”ti gaṇaṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati[T 0.0038], āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ, dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā, kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

If, thinking, “I will reinstate her,” she seeks a group or designates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong conduct. For the motion, there is an offense of wrong conduct. For the two formal announcements, there are grave offenses. At the conclusion of the formal announcements, there is an offense of Saṅghādisesa.

Ayampīti purimāyo upādāya vuccati.

‘This one too’ is said in reference to the preceding bhikkhunīs.

Paṭhamāpattikanti saha vatthujjhācārā āpajjati asamanubhāsanāya.

‘An offense at the first instance’ means: one commits it at the same time as the transgression concerning the object, without a formal admonition.

Nissāraṇīyanti saṅghamhā nissārīyati.

‘Entailing expulsion’ means: one is expelled from the Saṅgha.

Saṅghādisesoti…pe… tenapi vuccati saṅghādisesoti.

‘Saṅghādisesa’ means... for that reason also it is called Saṅghādisesa.

697. Dhammakamme [M 0.0299] dhammakammasaññā osāreti, āpatti saṅghādisesassa. Dhammakamme vematikā osāreti āpatti saṅghādisesassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññā osāreti, āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

697. In the case of a formal act done according to the Dhamma, if she reinstates, perceiving it as a formal act done according to the Dhamma, there is an offense of Saṅghādisesa. In the case of a formal act done according to the Dhamma, if she reinstates while being uncertain, there is an offense of Saṅghādisesa. In the case of a formal act done according to the Dhamma, if she reinstates, perceiving it as a formal act not done according to the Dhamma, there is an offense of Saṅghādisesa.

Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In the case of a formal act not done according to the Dhamma, if she perceives it as a formal act done according to the Dhamma, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of a formal act not done according to the Dhamma, if she is uncertain, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of a formal act not done according to the Dhamma, if she perceives it as a formal act not done according to the Dhamma, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

698. Anāpatti kammakārakasaṅghaṃ apaloketvā osāreti, gaṇassa chandaṃ jānitvā osāreti, vatte vattantiṃ osāreti, asante kammakārakasaṅghe osāreti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

698. There is no offense: if she reinstates after informing the Saṅgha that performed the formal act; if she reinstates after having known the consent of the group; if she reinstates one who is observing the proper conduct; if she reinstates when the Saṅgha that performed the formal act is not present; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Catutthasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fourth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule is concluded.

5. Pañcamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Fifth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule

699. Tena [V 0.0311] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sundarīnandā bhikkhunī abhirūpā hoti dassanīyā pāsādikā. Manussā bhattagge sundarīnandaṃ [T 0.0039] bhikkhuniṃ passitvā avassutā avassutāya sundarīnandāya bhikkhuniyā aggamaggāni bhojanāni denti. Sundarīnandā bhikkhunī yāvadatthaṃ bhuñjati; aññā bhikkhuniyo na cittarūpaṃ labhanti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā sundarīnandā avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa hatthato khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ [P 4.0233] vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādissati bhuñjissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, sundarīnandā bhikkhunī avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa hatthato khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādati bhuñjatīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, sundarīnandā bhikkhunī avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa hatthato khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādissati bhuñjissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

699. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, in the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā was exceedingly beautiful, lovely to see, and inspiring. People at the alms-hall, seeing the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, being lustful themselves, gave the choicest foods to the lustful bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā. The bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā ate as much as she desired; the other bhikkhunīs did not get as much as they wished. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they criticized, scorned, and spread it about: “How indeed could the venerable Sundarīnandā, being lustful, having received with her own hand hard food or soft food from the hand of a lustful man, eat or consume it?” … “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, being lustful, having received with her own hand hard food or soft food from the hand of a lustful man, eats and consumes it?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, could the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, being lustful, having received with her own hand hard food or soft food from the hand of a lustful man, eat or consume it? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

700. “Yā [M 0.0300] pana bhikkhunī avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa hatthato khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā, ayampi bhikkhunī paṭhamāpattikaṃ dhammaṃ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṃ saṅghādisesa”nti.

700. “Whatever bhikkhunī, being lustful, having received with her own hand hard food or soft food from the hand of a lustful man, should eat or should consume it, this bhikkhunī too has committed an offense at the first instance, entailing expulsion, a Saṅghādisesa.”

701. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

701. `Yā pana` means: whatever, of whatever sort… `Bhikkhunī` means… this bhikkhunī is intended in this context.

Avassutā nāma sārattā apekkhavatī paṭibaddhacittā.

`Avassutā` means: impassioned, longing, with an attached mind.

Avassuto nāma sāratto apekkhavā paṭibaddhacitto.

`Avassuto` means: impassioned, longing, with an attached mind.

Purisapuggalo [T 0.0040] nāma manussapuriso, na yakkho na peto na tiracchānagato, viññū paṭibalo sārajjituṃ.

`Purisapuggala` means a human male, not a male yakkha, not a male peta, not a male animal; one who is discerning and capable of becoming impassioned.

Khādanīyaṃ [V 0.0312] nāma pañca bhojanāni – udakadantaponaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ khādanīyaṃ nāma.

`Khādanīya` means: setting aside the five staple foods and water and tooth-cleaners, the remainder is called `khādanīya`.

Bhojanīyaṃ nāma pañca bhojanāni – odano, kummāso, sattu, maccho, maṃsaṃ.

`Bhojanīya` means the five staple foods: cooked rice, barley-meal, parched grain flour, fish, and meat.

“Khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti thullaccayassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

If one accepts it thinking, ‘I will eat, I will consume,’ there is an offense of thullaccaya. For every mouthful, there is an offense of saṅghādisesa.

Ayampīti purimāyo upādāya vuccati.

`Ayampi` is said with reference to the preceding bhikkhunīs.

Paṭhamāpattikanti saha vatthujjhācārā āpajjati asamanubhāsanāya.

`Paṭhamāpattikaṃ` means: one falls into the offense at the same time as the transgression concerning the object, not because of a formal admonition.

Nissāraṇīyanti saṅghamhā nissārīyati.

`Nissāraṇīyaṃ` means: one is expelled from the Saṅgha.

Saṅghādisesoti…pe… tenapi vuccati saṅghādisesoti.

`Saṅghādiseso`… for that reason also it is called `saṅghādiseso`.

Udakadantaponaṃ paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ekatoavassute “khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one accepts water and a tooth-cleaner, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. When one party is lustful, if one accepts thinking, ‘I will eat, I will consume,’ there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

702. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti thullaccayassa. Udakadantaponaṃ paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ubhatoavassute yakkhassa vā petassa vā paṇḍakassa vā tiracchānagatamanussaviggahassa vā hatthato “khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre [M 0.0301] āpatti thullaccayassa. Udakadantaponaṃ paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ekatoavassute “khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti dukkaṭassa. Udakadantaponaṃ paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

702. For every mouthful, there is an offense of thullaccaya. If one accepts water and a tooth-cleaner, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. When both parties are lustful, if one accepts from the hand of a male yakkha, a male peta, a paṇḍaka, or a male animal in human form, thinking, ‘I will eat, I will consume,’ there is an offense of dukkaṭa. For every mouthful, there is an offense of thullaccaya. If one accepts water and a tooth-cleaner, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. When one party is lustful, if one accepts thinking, ‘I will eat, I will consume,’ there is an offense of dukkaṭa. For every mouthful, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If one accepts water and a tooth-cleaner, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

703. Anāpatti [T 0.0041][P 4.0234] ubhatoanavassutā honti, “anavassuto”ti jānantī paṭiggaṇhāti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

703. There is no offense if both parties are not lustful; if she accepts it knowing, ‘He is not lustful;’ for an insane bhikkhunī; for the first offender.

Pañcamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fifth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule is finished.

6. Chaṭṭhasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Sixth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule

704. Tena [V 0.0313] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sundarīnandā bhikkhunī abhirūpā hoti dassanīyā pāsādikā. Manussā bhattagge sundarīnandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ passitvā avassutā sundarīnandāya bhikkhuniyā aggamaggāni bhojanāni denti. Sundarīnandā bhikkhunī kukkuccāyantī na paṭiggaṇhāti. Anantarikā bhikkhunī sundarīnandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “kissa tvaṃ, ayye, na paṭiggaṇhāsī”ti? “Avassutā, ayye”ti. “Tvaṃ pana, ayye, avassutā”ti? “Nāhaṃ, ayye, avassutā”ti. “Kiṃ te, ayye, eso purisapuggalo karissati avassuto vā anavassuto vā, yato tvaṃ anavassutā. Iṅghaṃ, ayye, yaṃ te eso purisapuggalo deti khādanīyaṃ vā [T 0.0042] bhojanīyaṃ vā taṃ tvaṃ sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khāda vā, bhuñja vā”ti.

704. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī named Sundarīnandā was very beautiful, lovely to see, and inspiring. People at the refectory, having seen the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, being stained by lust, give choice foods to the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā. The bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, feeling scrupulous, does not accept. A nearby bhikkhunī said this to the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā: “Venerable lady, for what reason do you not accept?” “Venerable lady, they are stained by lust.” “But you, venerable lady, are you stained by lust?” “Venerable lady, I am not stained by lust.” “Venerable lady, what will this male person do to you, whether he is stained by lust or not stained by lust, since you are not stained by lust? Come, venerable lady, whatever hard food or staple food this male person gives you, that you, having accepted with your own hand, should either eat or consume.”

Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī evaṃ vakkhati – ‘kiṃ te, ayye, eso purisapuggalo karissati avassuto vā anavassuto vā, yato tvaṃ anavassutā. Iṅgha, ayye, yaṃ te eso purisapuggalo deti khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā taṃ tvaṃ sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khāda vā bhuñja vā”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī evaṃ vadeti – “kiṃ te, ayye, eso purisapuggalo karissati avassuto vā anavassuto vā yato tvaṃ anavassutā! Iṅgha, ayye, yaṃ te eso purisapuggalo deti khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā taṃ tvaṃ sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khāda vā bhuñja vā”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi [M 0.0302] buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī evaṃ vakkhati – “kiṃ te, ayye, eso purisapuggalo karissati avassuto vā anavassuto vā yato tvaṃ anavassutā; iṅgha, ayye, yaṃ te eso purisapuggalo deti khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā taṃ tvaṃ sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khāda vā bhuñja vā”. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they criticized, scorned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could a bhikkhunī say thus: ‘Venerable lady, what will this male person do to you, whether he is stained by lust or not stained by lust, since you are not stained by lust? Come, venerable lady, whatever hard food or staple food this male person gives you, that you, having accepted with your own hand, should either eat or consume’?” … “Is it true, it is said, Bhikkhus, that a bhikkhunī says thus: ‘Venerable lady, what will this male person do to you, whether he is stained by lust or not stained by lust, since you are not stained by lust? Come, venerable lady, whatever hard food or staple food this male person gives you, that you, having accepted with your own hand, should either eat or consume’?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, could a bhikkhunī say thus: ‘Venerable lady, what will this male person do to you, whether he is stained by lust or not stained by lust, since you are not stained by lust? Come, venerable lady, whatever hard food or staple food this male person gives you, that you, having accepted with your own hand, should either eat or consume’? Bhikkhus, this is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule thus:

705. “Yā pana bhikkhunī evaṃ vadeyya – ‘kiṃ te, ayye, eso purisapuggalo karissati avassuto vā anavassuto vā, yato tvaṃ anavassutā. Iṅgha, ayye, yaṃ te eso purisapuggalo deti khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā taṃ tvaṃ sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khāda vā bhuñja vā’ti, ayampi bhikkhunī paṭhamāpattikaṃ dhammaṃ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṃ saṅghādisesa”nti.

705. “Whatever bhikkhunī should say thus: ‘Venerable lady, what will this male person do to you, whether he is stained by lust or not stained by lust, since you are not stained by lust? Come, venerable lady, whatever hard food or staple food this male person gives you, that you, having accepted with your own hand, should either eat or consume,’ this bhikkhunī also has fallen into an offense named Saṅghādisesa, which is incurred at the first transgression and requires expulsion.”

706. Yā [V 0.0314] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

706. `Yā pana` means: whatever, of whatever sort… `Bhikkhunī` means… this bhikkhunī is intended in this context.

Evaṃ vadeyyāti – “kiṃ te, ayye, eso purisapuggalo karissati avassuto vā anavassuto vā, yato tvaṃ [T 0.0043] anavassutā. Iṅgha, ayye, yaṃ te eso purisapuggalo deti khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā taṃ tvaṃ sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khāda vā bhuñja vā”ti uyyojeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Tassā vacanena “khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre [P 4.0235] āpatti thullaccayassa. Bhojanapariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

Should speak thus: if she urges, saying, ‘Venerable lady, what will this male person do to you, whether he is stained by lust or not, since you are not stained by lust? Come now, venerable lady, whatever hard food or soft food this male person gives you, accept it with your own hand and either eat or consume it,’ she commits an offense of wrong conduct. If, at her word, the other accepts, thinking, ‘I will eat, I will consume,’ she commits an offense of wrong conduct. For every mouthful, she commits a grave offense. At the end of the meal, she commits an offense requiring an initial and subsequent meeting of the Sangha.

Ayampīti purimāyo upādāya vuccati.

This one also: this is said with reference to the preceding bhikkhunīs.

Paṭhamāpattikanti saha vatthujjhācārā āpajjati asamanubhāsanāya.

Incurred at the first transgression: one falls into the offense together with the transgression concerning the object, without a formal admonition.

Nissāraṇīyanti saṅghamhā nissārīyati.

Requiring expulsion: one is expelled from the Sangha.

Saṅghādisesoti…pe… tenapi vuccati saṅghādisesoti.

An offense requiring an initial and subsequent meeting of the Sangha: …for that reason also, it is called an offense requiring an initial and subsequent meeting of the Sangha.

Udakadantaponaṃ “paṭiggaṇhā”ti uyyojeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Tassā vacanena khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If she urges, saying, “Accept water and a tooth-stick,” she commits an offense of wrong conduct. If, at her word, the other accepts, thinking, ‘I will eat, I will consume,’ she commits an offense of wrong conduct.

707. Ekatoavassute [M 0.0303] yakkhassa vā petassa vā paṇḍakassa vā tiracchānagatamanussaviggahassa vā hatthato khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā “khāda vā bhuñja vā”ti uyyojeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Tassā vacanena “khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti dukkaṭassa. Bhojanapariyosāne āpatti thullaccayassa. Udakadantaponaṃ paṭiggaṇhāti uyyojeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Tassā vacanena “khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

707. When one of the two is stained by lust, if she urges another to eat or consume hard food or soft food from the hand of a yakkha, a peta, a paṇḍaka, or an animal in the form of a human male, she commits an offense of wrong conduct. If, at her word, the other accepts, thinking, ‘I will eat, I will consume,’ she commits an offense of wrong conduct. For every mouthful, she commits an offense of wrong conduct. At the end of the meal, she commits a grave offense. If she urges another to accept water and a tooth-stick, she commits an offense of wrong conduct. If, at her word, the other accepts, thinking, ‘I will eat, I will consume,’ she commits an offense of wrong conduct.

708. Anāpatti “anavassuto”ti jānantī uyyojeti, “kupitā na [T 0.0044] paṭiggaṇhātī”ti [V 0.0315] uyyojeti, “kulānuddayatāya na paṭiggaṇhātī”ti uyyojeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.
