708. There is no offense: if she urges, knowing, “He is not stained by lust”; if she urges, thinking, “She is angry and will not accept”; if she urges, thinking, “Out of compassion for the family, she will not accept”; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Chaṭṭhasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Sixth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule is finished.

7. Sattamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Seventh Saṅghādisesa Training Rule

709. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ bhaṇḍitvā kupitā anattamanā evaṃ vadeti – “buddhaṃ paccācikkhāmi, dhammaṃ paccācikkhāmi, saṅghaṃ paccācikkhāmi, sikkhaṃ paccācikkhāmi. Kinnumāva samaṇiyo yā samaṇiyo sakyadhītaro, santaññāpi samaṇiyo lajjiniyo kukkuccikā sikkhākāmā tāsāhaṃ santike brahmacariyaṃ carissāmī”ti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā caṇḍakāḷī caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī (ka.) kupitā anattamanā evaṃ vakkhati – buddhaṃ paccācikkhāmi…pe… sikkhaṃ paccācikkhāmi. Kinnumāva samaṇiyo yā samaṇiyo sakyadhītaro, santaññāpi samaṇiyo lajjiniyo kukkuccikā sikkhākāmā tāsāhaṃ santike brahmacariyaṃ carissāmī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī kupitā anattamanā evaṃ vadeti – “buddhaṃ paccācikkhāmi…pe… sikkhaṃ paccācikkhāmi. Kinnumāva samaṇiyo yā samaṇiyo sakyadhītaro, santaññāpi samaṇiyo lajjiniyo kukkuccikā [M 0.0304] sikkhākāmā, tāsāhaṃ santike brahmacariyaṃ carissāmī”ti[T 0.0045]? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī kupitā anattamanā evaṃ [P 4.0236] vakkhati – “buddhaṃ paccācikkhāmi…pe… sikkhaṃ paccācikkhāmi. Kinnumāva samaṇiyo yā samaṇiyo sakyadhītaro, santaññāpi samaṇiyo lajjiniyo kukkuccikā sikkhākāmā, tāsāhaṃ santike brahmacariyaṃ carissāmī”ti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

709. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī, after quarreling with the bhikkhunīs, being angry and displeased, spoke thus: “I renounce the Buddha, I renounce the Dhamma, I renounce the Sangha, I renounce the training. Are only these daughters of the Sakyans nuns? There are other nuns who are conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training—I will practice the holy life in their presence.” Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… they criticized, scorned, and spread it about, saying: “How can the venerable Caṇḍakāḷī, being angry and displeased, speak thus: ‘I renounce the Buddha… I renounce the training. Are only these daughters of the Sakyans nuns? There are other nuns who are conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training—I will practice the holy life in their presence’?”… “Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī, being angry and displeased, speaks thus: ‘I renounce the Buddha… I renounce the training. Are only these daughters of the Sakyans nuns? There are other nuns who are conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training—I will practice the holy life in their presence’?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Blessed One, the Buddha, rebuked her… “How, monks, can the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī, being angry and displeased, speak thus: ‘I renounce the Buddha… I renounce the training. Are only these daughters of the Sakyans nuns? There are other nuns who are conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training—I will practice the holy life in their presence’? This, monks, is not for the faith of the faithless… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

710. “Yā pana bhikkhunī kupitā anattamanā evaṃ vadeyya – ‘buddhaṃ paccācikkhāmi, dhammaṃ paccācikkhāmi, saṅghaṃ paccācikkhāmi, sikkhaṃ paccācikkhāmi. Kinnumāva samaṇiyo yā samaṇiyo sakyadhītaro! Santaññāpi samaṇiyo lajjiniyo kukkuccikā sikkhākāmā, tāsāhaṃ santike [V 0.0316] brahmacariyaṃ carissāmī’ti, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi evamassa vacanīyā – ‘māyye, kupitā anattamanā evaṃ avaca – buddhaṃ paccācikkhāmi, dhammaṃ paccācikkhāmi, saṅghaṃ paccācikkhāmi, sikkhaṃ paccācikkhāmi. Kinnumāva samaṇiyo yā samaṇiyo sakyadhītaro! Santaññāpi samaṇiyo lajjiniyo kukkuccikā sikkhākāmā, tāsāhaṃ santike brahmacariyaṃ carissāmīti, abhiramāyye, svākkhāto dhammo; cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā’ti. Evañca sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi vuccamānā tatheva paggaṇheyya, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsitabbā tassa paṭinissaggāya. Yāvatatiyañce samanubhāsīyamānā taṃ paṭinissajjeyya iccetaṃ kusalaṃ; no ce paṭinissajjeyya[T 0.0046], ayampi bhikkhunī yāvatatiyakaṃ dhammaṃ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṃ saṅghādisesa”nti.

710. “Whatever bhikkhunī, being angry and displeased, should speak thus: ‘I renounce the Buddha, I renounce the Dhamma, I renounce the Sangha, I renounce the training. Are only these daughters of the Sakyans nuns? There are other nuns who are conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training—I will practice the holy life in their presence,’ that bhikkhunī should be spoken to by the bhikkhunīs thus: ‘Venerable one, being angry and displeased, do not speak thus: “I renounce the Buddha, I renounce the Dhamma, I renounce the Sangha, I renounce the training. Are only these daughters of the Sakyans nuns? There are other nuns who are conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training—I will practice the holy life in their presence.” Venerable one, take delight; the Dhamma is well-proclaimed. Practice the holy life for the right ending of suffering.’ And if that bhikkhunī, being spoken to thus by the bhikkhunīs, should persist in that very way, that bhikkhunī should be admonished by the bhikkhunīs up to the third time for the abandoning of that view. If, being admonished up to the third time, she should abandon it, that is good; if she should not abandon it, this bhikkhunī too, at the conclusion of the third formal admonition, has committed an offense requiring an initial and subsequent meeting of the Sangha, which requires expulsion.”

711. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

711. “Whatever” means whatever sort of… “bhikkhunī” means… this bhikkhunī is intended in this context as ‘bhikkhunī’.

Kupitā anattamanāti anabhiraddhā āhatacittā khilajātā.

“Angry, displeased” means not delighting, with an afflicted mind, with a mind that has become obstinate.

Evaṃ vadeyyāti – “buddhaṃ paccācikkhāmi…pe… sikkhaṃ paccācikkhāmi. Kinnumāva samaṇiyo yā samaṇiyo sakyadhītaro! Santaññāpi samaṇiyo lajjiniyo kukkuccikā sikkhākāmā, tāsāhaṃ santike brahmacariyaṃ carissāmī”ti.

“She might speak thus” means: “I renounce the Buddha… I renounce the training. Are only these daughters of the Sakyans nuns? There are other nuns who are conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training—I will practice the holy life in their presence.”

Sā [M 0.0305] bhikkhunīti yā sā evaṃvādinī bhikkhunī. Bhikkhunīhīti aññāhi bhikkhunīhi.

“That bhikkhunī” means the bhikkhunī who is accustomed to speaking thus. “By the bhikkhunīs” means by other bhikkhunīs.

Yā passanti yā suṇanti tāhi vattabbā – “māyye, kupitā anattamanā evaṃ avaca – ‘buddhaṃ paccācikkhāmi…pe… sikkhaṃ paccācikkhāmi. Kinnumāva samaṇiyo yā samaṇiyo sakyadhītaro! Santaññāpi samaṇiyo lajjiniyo kukkuccikā sikkhākāmā, tāsāhaṃ santike brahmacariyaṃ carissāmī’ti. Abhiramāyye, svākkhāto dhammo; cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Dutiyampi vattabbā. Tatiyampi vattabbā. Sace paṭinissajjati iccetaṃ kusalaṃ, no ce paṭinissajjati āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sutvā na vadanti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sā bhikkhunī saṅghamajjhampi ākaḍḍhitvā vattabbā – “māyye, kupitā anattamanā evaṃ avaca – ‘buddhaṃ paccācikkhāmi…pe… sikkhaṃ paccācikkhāmi[T 0.0047]. Kinnumāva [V 0.0317] samaṇiyo yā samaṇiyo sakyadhītaro! Santaññāpi samaṇiyo lajjiniyo kukkuccikā sikkhākāmā, tāsāhaṃ santike brahmacariyaṃ carissāmī’ti. Abhiramāyye, svākkhāto dhammo; cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Dutiyampi vattabbā. Tatiyampi vattabbā. Sace paṭinissajjati iccetaṃ kusalaṃ, no ce paṭinissajjati āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sā bhikkhunī samanubhāsitabbā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, samanubhāsitabbā. Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Those bhikkhunīs who see or hear should say to her: “Venerable lady, being angry and displeased, do not speak thus: ‘I renounce the Buddha… I renounce the training. Are only these Sakyan daughters bhikkhunīs? There are other bhikkhunīs who are conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of the training; in their presence I will practice the holy life.’ Venerable lady, take delight; the Dhamma is well-proclaimed. Practice the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.” A second time it should be said. A third time it should be said. If she relinquishes it, that is good. If she does not relinquish it, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Having heard, if they do not speak, there is an offense of wrong-doing. That bhikkhunī should be brought into the midst of the Saṅgha and told: “Venerable lady, being angry and displeased, do not speak thus: ‘I renounce the Buddha… I renounce the training. Are only these Sakyan daughters bhikkhunīs? There are other bhikkhunīs who are conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of the training; in their presence I will practice the holy life.’ Venerable lady, take delight; the Dhamma is well-proclaimed. Practice the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.” A second time it should be said. A third time it should be said. If she relinquishes it, that is good. If she does not relinquish it, there is an offense of wrong-doing. That bhikkhunī should be formally admonished. And thus, Bhikkhus, should she be formally admonished. A competent and capable bhikkhunī should inform the Saṅgha:

712. “Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā bhikkhunī kupitā anattamanā evaṃ vadeti – ‘buddhaṃ paccācikkhāmi, dhammaṃ paccācikkhāmi, saṅghaṃ paccācikkhāmi, sikkhaṃ paccācikkhāmi. Kinnumāva samaṇiyo yā samaṇiyo sakyadhītaro! Santaññāpi samaṇiyo lajjiniyo kukkuccikā sikkhākāmā tāsāhaṃ santike brahmacariyaṃ carissāmī’ti. Sā taṃ vatthuṃ na paṭinissajjati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuniṃ [P 4.0237] samanubhāseyya tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya. Esā ñatti.

712. “Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhunī named so-and-so, being angry and displeased, speaks thus: ‘I renounce the Buddha, I renounce the Dhamma, I renounce the Saṅgha, I renounce the training. Are only these Sakyan daughters bhikkhunīs? There are other bhikkhunīs who are conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of the training; in their presence I will practice the holy life.’ She does not relinquish this matter. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should formally admonish the bhikkhunī so-and-so for the relinquishment of this matter. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā bhikkhunī kupitā anattamanā evaṃ vadeti – ‘buddhaṃ paccācikkhāmi…pe… sikkhaṃ paccācikkhāmi. Kinnumāva samaṇiyo yā samaṇiyo sakyadhītaro! Santaññāpi samaṇiyo lajjiniyo kukkuccikā sikkhākāmā, tāsāhaṃ [T 0.0048] santike brahmacariyaṃ carissāmī’ti[M 0.0306]. Sā taṃ vatthuṃ na paṭinissajjati. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuniṃ samanubhāsati tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā samanubhāsanā tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati sā, bhāseyya.

“Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhunī named so-and-so, being angry and displeased, speaks thus: ‘I renounce the Buddha… I renounce the training. Are only these Sakyan daughters bhikkhunīs? There are other bhikkhunīs who are conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of the training; in their presence I will practice the holy life.’ She does not relinquish this matter. The Saṅgha formally admonishes the bhikkhunī so-and-so for the relinquishment of this matter. Whichever venerable lady approves of the formal admonition of the bhikkhunī so-and-so for the relinquishment of this matter, she should remain silent; whichever does not approve, she should speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

“For the second time I state this matter… For the third time I state this matter…”

“Samanubhaṭṭhā saṅghena itthannāmā bhikkhunī tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The bhikkhunī named so-and-so has been formally admonished by the Saṅgha for the relinquishment of this matter. It is approved by the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.”

Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā. Kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa. Saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpajjantiyā ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ, dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā paṭippassambhanti.

With the motion, there is an offense of wrong-doing. With the two formal acts, there are grave offenses. At the conclusion of the formal act, there is a Saṅghādisesa offense. For one incurring a Saṅghādisesa, the offense of wrong-doing from the motion and the grave offenses from the two formal acts are pacified.

Ayampīti [V 0.0318] purimāyo upādāya vuccati.

“This one also” is said with reference to the preceding bhikkhunīs.

Yāvatatiyakanti yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya āpajjati, na saha vatthujjhācārā.

“Up to the third time” means that the offense is incurred by the third formal admonition, not together with the initial transgression of the matter.

Nissāraṇīyanti saṅghamhā nissārīyati.

“Entailing expulsion” means she is expelled from the Saṅgha.

Saṅghādisesoti…pe… tenapi vuccati saṅghādisesoti.

“Saṅghādisesa”… therefore it is called a Saṅghādisesa.

713. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññā na paṭinissajjati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa. Dhammakamme vematikā na paṭinissajjati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññā na paṭinissajjati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

713. In a lawful act, perceiving it as a lawful act, if she does not relinquish it, there is a Saṅghādisesa offense. In a lawful act, being in doubt, if she does not relinquish it, there is a Saṅghādisesa offense. In a lawful act, perceiving it as an unlawful act, if she does not relinquish it, there is a Saṅghādisesa offense.

Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa[T 0.0049]. Adhammakamme vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In an unlawful act, perceiving it as a lawful act, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In an unlawful act, being in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In an unlawful act, perceiving it as an unlawful act, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

714. Anāpatti asamanubhāsantiyā, paṭinissajjantiyā, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

714. There is no offense for one who is not being formally admonished, for one who relinquishes it, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Sattamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The seventh Saṅghādisesa training rule is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Eighth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule

715. Tena [M 0.0307] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī kismiñcideva adhikaraṇe paccākatā kupitā anattamanā evaṃ vadeti – “chandagāminiyo ca [P 4.0238] bhikkhuniyo, dosagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo, mohagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo, bhayagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo”ti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā caṇḍakāḷī kismiñcideva adhikaraṇe paccākatā kupitā anattamanā evaṃ vakkhati – chandagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo…pe… bhayagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī kismiñcideva adhikaraṇe paccākatā kupitā anattamanā [V 0.0319] evaṃ vadeti – “chandagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo…pe… bhayagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī kismiñcideva [T 0.0050] adhikaraṇe paccākatā kupitā anattamanā evaṃ vakkhati – “chandagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo…pe… bhayagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo”ti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

715. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, at the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī, having been defeated in some legal matter, being angry and displeased, spoke thus: “The bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of desire, the bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of hatred, the bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of delusion, and the bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of fear.” Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the venerable Caṇḍakāḷī, having been defeated in some legal matter, being angry and displeased, speak thus: ‘The bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of desire… and the bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of fear’?”… “Is it true, monks, as is said, that the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī, having been defeated in some legal matter, being angry and displeased, spoke thus: ‘The bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of desire… and the bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of fear’?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, monks, could the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī, having been defeated in some legal matter, being angry and displeased, speak thus: ‘The bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of desire… and the bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of fear’? This, monks, is not for the faith of the faithless… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

716. “Yā pana bhikkhunī kismiñcideva adhikaraṇe paccākatā kupitā anattamanā evaṃ vadeyya – ‘chandagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo, dosagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo, mohagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo, bhayagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo’ti, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi evamassa vacanīyā – ‘māyye, kismiñcideva adhikaraṇe paccākatā kupitā anattamanā evaṃ avaca – chandagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo dosagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo mohagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo bhayagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyoti. Ayyā kho chandāpi gaccheyya, dosāpi gaccheyya, mohāpi gaccheyya, bhayāpi gaccheyyā’ti. Evañca sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi vuccamānā tatheva paggaṇheyya, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsitabbā tassa paṭinissaggāya. Yāvatatiyañce samanubhāsīyamānā taṃ paṭinissajjeyya, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ; no ce paṭinissajjeyya, ayampi bhikkhunī yāvatatiyakaṃ dhammaṃ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṃ saṅghādisesa”nti.

716. “Whatever bhikkhunī, having been defeated in some legal matter, being angry and displeased, should speak thus: ‘The bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of desire, the bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of hatred, the bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of delusion, and the bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of fear,’ that bhikkhunī should be spoken to by the other bhikkhunīs thus: ‘Venerable lady, having been defeated in some legal matter, being angry and displeased, do not speak thus: “The bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of desire, the bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of hatred, the bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of delusion, and the bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of fear.” Indeed, venerable lady, you yourself might also go on a wrong course out of desire, might go on a wrong course out of hatred, might go on a wrong course out of delusion, and might go on a wrong course out of fear.’ And if that bhikkhunī, being spoken to thus by the bhikkhunīs, should persist in that very same way, that bhikkhunī should be admonished by the bhikkhunīs up to the third time for the abandoning of that. If, being admonished up to the third time, she should abandon it, this is good. If she should not abandon it, this bhikkhunī also has committed a Saṅghādisesa offense, requiring sending away, that is established at the third admonition.”

717. Yā [M 0.0308] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

717. Whatever means: whatever, of whatever kind… A bhikkhunī means: … this is the bhikkhunī who is intended in this matter.

Kismiñcideva adhikaraṇeti adhikaraṇaṃ nāma cattāri adhikaraṇāni – vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, kiccādhikaraṇaṃ.

In some legal matter whatsoever: A legal matter means the four legal matters: legal matters arising from disputes, legal matters arising from accusations, legal matters arising from offenses, and legal matters arising from duties.

Paccākatā nāma parājitā vuccati.

Defeated means 'overcome'.

Kupitā anattamanāti [T 0.0051] anabhiraddhā āhatacittā khilajātā.

Angry and displeased means discontented, with an afflicted mind, having become obdurate.

Evaṃ vadeyyāti – “chandagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo…pe… bhayagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo”ti.

Should speak thus means: ‘The bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of desire… and the bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of fear.’

Sā [V 0.0320] bhikkhunīti yā sā evaṃvādinī bhikkhunī.

That bhikkhunī means: the bhikkhunī who speaks thus.

Bhikkhunīhīti aññāhi bhikkhunīhi.

By the bhikkhunīs means: by other bhikkhunīs.

Yā passanti yā suṇanti tāhi vattabbā – “māyye, kismiñcideva adhikaraṇe paccākatā kupitā anattamanā evaṃ avaca – ‘chandagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo…pe… bhayagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo’ti. Ayyā kho chandāpi gaccheyya…pe… bhayāpi gaccheyyā”ti. Dutiyampi vattabbā. Tatiyampi vattabbā. Sace paṭinissajjati, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ; no ce paṭinissajjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sutvā na vadanti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sā bhikkhunī saṅghamajjhampi ākaḍḍhitvā vattabbā – “māyye, kismiñcideva adhikaraṇe paccākatā kupitā anattamanā evaṃ avaca – ‘chandagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo…pe… bhayagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo’ti. Ayyā kho chandāpi gaccheyya…pe… bhayāpi gaccheyyā”ti. Dutiyampi vattabbā. Tatiyampi vattabbā. Sace paṭinissajjati, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ; no ce paṭinissajjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sā bhikkhunī samanubhāsitabbā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, samanubhāsitabbā. Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

She should be spoken to by those who see or by those who hear, thus: ‘Venerable lady, having been defeated in some legal matter, being angry and displeased, do not speak thus: “The bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of desire… and the bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of fear.” Indeed, venerable lady, you yourself might also go on a wrong course out of desire… and might go on a wrong course out of fear.’ She should be spoken to a second time. She should be spoken to a third time. If she abandons it, this is good. If she does not abandon it, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If, having heard, they do not speak, there is an offense of wrong-doing. That bhikkhunī, having been drawn into the midst of the Saṅgha, should also be spoken to thus: ‘Venerable lady, having been defeated in some legal matter, being angry and displeased, do not speak thus: “The bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of desire… and the bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of fear.” Indeed, venerable lady, you yourself might also go on a wrong course out of desire… and might go on a wrong course out of fear.’ She should be spoken to a second time. She should be spoken to a third time. If she abandons it, this is good. If she does not abandon it, there is an offense of wrong-doing. That bhikkhunī should be formally admonished. And, monks, she should be formally admonished thus. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhunī:

718. “Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā bhikkhunī kismiñcideva adhikaraṇe paccākatā kupitā anattamanā evaṃ vadeti – ‘chandagāminiyo [T 0.0052] ca bhikkhuniyo…pe… bhayagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo’ti. Sā taṃ vatthuṃ na paṭinissajjati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuniṃ samanubhāseyya tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya. Esā ñatti.

718. “Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name, having been defeated in some legal matter, being angry and displeased, speaks thus: ‘The bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of desire… and the bhikkhunīs follow a wrong course out of fear.’ She does not abandon that view. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should formally admonish the bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name for the abandoning of that view. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu [M 0.0309] me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā bhikkhunī kismiñcideva adhikaraṇe paccākatā kupitā anattamanā evaṃ vadeti – ‘chandagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo…pe… bhayagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo’ti. Sā taṃ vatthuṃ na paṭinissajjati. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuniṃ samanubhāsati tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā samanubhāsanā tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.

“Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhunī named so-and-so, having been defeated in some legal issue, being angry and displeased, speaks thus: ‘The bhikkhunīs follow a path of desire… the bhikkhunīs follow a path of fear.’ She does not relinquish that view. The Saṅgha formally admonishes the bhikkhunī named so-and-so for the relinquishment of that view. Whichever venerable lady approves of the formal admonition of the bhikkhunī named so-and-so for the relinquishment of that view, she should be silent; whichever does not approve, she should speak.

“Dutiyampi [V 0.0321] etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

“A second time I speak on this matter… A third time I speak on this matter….

“Samanubhaṭṭhā saṅghena itthannāmā bhikkhunī tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The bhikkhunī named so-and-so has been formally admonished by the Saṅgha for the relinquishment of that view. It is approved by the Saṅgha; therefore, it is silent. Thus I hold it.”

Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā. Kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa. Saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpajjantiyā ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā paṭippassambhanti.

For the motion, there is an offense of wrong-doing. For the two formal acts, there are grave offenses. At the conclusion of the formal act, a Saṅghādisesa offense is incurred. For one who incurs the Saṅghādisesa, the offense of wrong-doing from the motion and the grave offenses from the two formal acts are allayed.

Ayampīti purimāyo upādāya vuccati.

‘This too’ (ayampi) is said with reference to the preceding bhikkhunīs.

Yāvatatiyakanti yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya āpajjati, na saha vatthujjhācārā.

‘Entailing a third formal admonition’ (yāvatatiyakaṃ) means that the offense is incurred upon the third formal admonition, not together with the initial transgression of the matter.

Nissāraṇīyanti saṅghamhā nissārīyati.

‘Liable to expulsion’ (nissāraṇīyaṃ) means that one is expelled from the Saṅgha.

Saṅghādisesoti…pe… tenapi vuccati [T 0.0053] saṅghādisesoti.

‘Saṅghādisesa’… therefore it is also called a Saṅghādisesa.

719. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññā na paṭinissajjati, āpatti saṅghādisessa. Dhammakamme vematikā na paṭinissajjati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññā na paṭinissajjati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

719. In a lawful act, if she perceives it as a lawful act and does not relinquish it, there is an offense of Saṅghādisesa. In a lawful act, if she is in doubt and does not relinquish it, there is an offense of Saṅghādisesa. In a lawful act, if she perceives it as an unlawful act and does not relinquish it, there is an offense of Saṅghādisesa.

Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññā āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In an unlawful act, if she perceives it as a lawful act and does not relinquish it, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In an unlawful act, if she is in doubt and does not relinquish it, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In an unlawful act, if she perceives it as an unlawful act and does not relinquish it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

720. Anāpatti asamanubhāsantiyā, paṭinissajjantiyā, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti[P 4.0239].

720. There is no offense for one who is not being formally admonished, for one who relinquishes it, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Aṭṭhamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The eighth Saṅghādisesa training rule is concluded.

9. Navamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Ninth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule

721. Tena [M 0.0310][V 0.0322] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā antevāsikā bhikkhuniyo saṃsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo saṃsaṭṭhā viharissanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā [T 0.0054] aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo saṃsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikāti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo saṃsaṭṭhā viharissanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

721. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the resident pupils of the bhikkhunī Thullanandā dwelt associating with laypeople, being of corrupt conduct, of evil repute, of corrupt livelihood, being vexatious to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, and being concealers of one another's faults. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… they looked down upon, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs dwell associating with laypeople, being of corrupt conduct, of evil repute, of corrupt livelihood, being vexatious to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, and being concealers of one another's faults?”… “Is it true, it is said, Bhikkhus, that bhikkhunīs dwell associating with laypeople, being of corrupt conduct, of evil repute, of corrupt livelihood, being vexatious to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, and being concealers of one another's faults?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, can bhikkhunīs dwell associating with laypeople, being of corrupt conduct, of evil repute, of corrupt livelihood, being vexatious to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, and being concealers of one another's faults! This, Bhikkhus, is not for the faith of the faithless… And thus, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

722. “Bhikkhuniyo paneva saṃsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Tā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhunīhi evamassu vacanīyā – ‘bhaginiyo kho saṃsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Viviccathāyye. Vivekaññeva bhaginīnaṃ saṅgho vaṇṇetī’ti. Evañca tā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhunīhi vuccamānā tatheva paggaṇheyyuṃ, tā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhunīhi yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsitabbā tassa paṭinissaggāya. Yāvatatiyañce samanubhāsīyamānā taṃ paṭinissajjeyyuṃ, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ; no ce paṭinissajjeyyuṃ, imāpi bhikkhuniyo yāvatatiyakaṃ dhammaṃ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṃ saṅghādisesa”nti.

722. “If bhikkhunīs dwell associating with laypeople, being of corrupt conduct, of evil repute, of corrupt livelihood, being vexatious to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, and being concealers of one another's faults, those bhikkhunīs should be spoken to by other bhikkhunīs thus: ‘Indeed, sisters, you dwell associating with laypeople, being of corrupt conduct, of evil repute, of corrupt livelihood, being vexatious to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, and being concealers of one another's faults. Venerable ladies, be secluded. The Saṅgha praises only seclusion for the sisters.’ And if those bhikkhunīs, being spoken to by other bhikkhunīs, should persist in that very same way, those bhikkhunīs are to be admonished by other bhikkhunīs up to the third time for the abandoning of that matter. If, being admonished up to the third time, they should abandon it, that is good. If they should not abandon it, these bhikkhunīs too have fallen into an offense named Saṅghādisesa, which requires sending away and is determined at the third time.”

723. Bhikkhuniyo panevāti upasampannāyo vuccanti.

723. As for ‘If bhikkhunīs,’ it is said of those who are fully ordained.

Saṃsaṭṭhā viharantīti saṃsaṭṭhā nāma ananulomikena kāyikavācasikena saṃsaṭṭhā viharanti.

In ‘They dwell associating,’ ‘associating’ means: they dwell associating through bodily and verbal actions that are improper for monastics.

Pāpācārāti [T 0.0055][M 0.0311] pāpakena ācārena samannāgatā.

‘Of corrupt conduct’ means: they are endowed with corrupt conduct.

Pāpasaddāti [V 0.0323] pāpakena kittisaddena abbhuggatā.

‘Of evil repute’ means: they are renowned for an evil reputation.

Pāpasilokāti pāpakena micchājīvena jīvitaṃ kappenti.

‘Of corrupt livelihood’ means: they make their living by means of a corrupt, wrong livelihood.

Bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikāti aññamaññissā kamme [P 4.0240] karīyamāne paṭikkosanti.

‘Vexatious to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs’ means: when a formal act is being performed for one another, they object.

Aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikāti aññamaññaṃ vajjaṃ paṭicchādenti.

‘Concealers of one another's faults’ means: they conceal one another's faults.

Tā bhikkhuniyoti yā tā saṃsaṭṭhā bhikkhuniyo.

‘Those bhikkhunīs’ means: those bhikkhunīs who associate.

Bhikkhunīhīti aññāhi bhikkhunīhi.

‘By bhikkhunīs’ means: by other bhikkhunīs.

Yā passanti yā suṇanti tāhi vattabbā – “bhaginiyo kho saṃsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Viviccathāyye. Vivekaññeva bhaginīnaṃ saṅgho vaṇṇetī”ti. Dutiyampi vattabbā. Tatiyampi vattabbā. Sace paṭinissajjanti, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ; no ce paṭinissajjanti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sutvā na vadanti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Tā bhikkhuniyo saṅghamajjhampi ākaḍḍhitvā vattabbā – “bhaginiyo kho saṃsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Viviccathāyye. Vivekaññeva bhaginīnaṃ saṅgho vaṇṇetī”ti. Dutiyampi vattabbā. Tatiyampi vattabbā. Sace paṭinissajjanti, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ; no ce paṭinissajjanti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Tā bhikkhuniyo samanubhāsitabbā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, samanubhāsitabbā. Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Those who see, those who hear, by them it should be said: ‘Indeed, sisters, you dwell associating with laypeople, being of corrupt conduct, of evil repute, of corrupt livelihood, being vexatious to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, and being concealers of one another's faults. Venerable ladies, be secluded. The Saṅgha praises only seclusion for the sisters.’ It should be said a second time. It should be said a third time. If they abandon it, that is good. If they do not abandon it, it is an offense of wrongdoing. Having heard, if they do not speak, it is an offense of wrongdoing. Those bhikkhunīs, having been drawn into the midst of the Saṅgha, should also be spoken to: ‘Indeed, sisters, you dwell associating with laypeople, being of corrupt conduct, of evil repute, of corrupt livelihood, being vexatious to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, and being concealers of one another's faults. Venerable ladies, be secluded. The Saṅgha praises only seclusion for the sisters.’ It should be said a second time. It should be said a third time. If they abandon it, that is good. If they do not abandon it, it is an offense of wrongdoing. Those bhikkhunīs are to be formally admonished. And thus, bhikkhus, they are to be formally admonished. The Saṅgha is to be informed by a competent, capable bhikkhunī:

724. “Suṇātu [T 0.0056] me, ayye, saṅgho. Itthannāmā ca itthannāmā ca bhikkhuniyo saṃsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Tā taṃ vatthuṃ na paṭinissajjanti. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmañca itthannāmañca bhikkhuniyo samanubhāseyya tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya. Esā ñatti.

724. “Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. The bhikkhunīs of such-and-such a name and of such-and-such a name dwell associating with laypeople, being of corrupt conduct, of evil repute, of corrupt livelihood, being vexatious to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, and being concealers of one another's faults. They do not abandon that matter. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should formally admonish the bhikkhunīs of such-and-such a name and of such-and-such a name for the abandoning of that matter. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu [V 0.0324] me, ayye, saṅgho. Itthannāmā ca itthannāmā ca bhikkhuniyo saṃsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Tā taṃ vatthuṃ na paṭinissajjanti. Saṅgho [M 0.0312] itthannāmañca itthannāmañca bhikkhuniyo samanubhāsati tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya ca itthannāmāya ca bhikkhunīnaṃ samanubhāsanā tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.

“Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. The bhikkhunīs of such-and-such a name and of such-and-such a name dwell associating with laypeople, being of corrupt conduct, of evil repute, of corrupt livelihood, being vexatious to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, and being concealers of one another's faults. They do not abandon that matter. The Saṅgha formally admonishes the bhikkhunīs of such-and-such a name and of such-and-such a name for the abandoning of that matter. To whichever venerable lady the formal admonition of the bhikkhunīs of such-and-such a name and of such-and-such a name for the abandoning of that matter is agreeable, she should be silent. To whom it is not agreeable, she should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

“A second time, too, I speak on this matter… A third time, too, I speak on this matter….”

“Samanubhaṭṭhā saṅghena, itthannāmā ca itthannāmā ca bhikkhuniyo tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The bhikkhunīs of such-and-such a name and of such-and-such a name have been formally admonished by the Saṅgha for the abandoning of that matter. It is approved by the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold this.”

Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ, dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā, kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa. Saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpajjantīnaṃ ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā paṭippassambhanti. Dve tisso ekato samanubhāsitabbā. Tatuttari na [T 0.0057] samanubhāsitabbā.

For the motion, an offense of wrongdoing is incurred. For the two formal announcements, grave offenses are incurred. At the conclusion of the formal act, an offense of Saṅghādisesa is incurred. For those incurring the Saṅghādisesa offense, the offense of wrongdoing for the motion and the grave offenses for the two formal announcements subside. Two or three bhikkhunīs are to be formally admonished together. Beyond that, they are not to be formally admonished.

Imāpi bhikkhuniyoti purimāyo upādāya vuccanti.

The phrase 'these bhikkhunīs too' is said with reference to the former bhikkhunīs.

Yāvatatiyakanti yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya āpajjanti, na saha vatthujjhācārā.

‘Up to the third time’ means they incur the offense by means of the formal admonition up to the third time, not together with the transgression of the matter.

Nissāraṇīyanti saṅghamhā nissārīyati.

‘Subject to expulsion’ means one is expelled from the Saṅgha.

Saṅghādisesoti…pe… tenapi vuccati saṅghādisesoti.

‘Saṅghādisesa’… and for that reason also it is called ‘Saṅghādisesa’.

725. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññā na paṭinissajjanti, āpatti saṅghādisesassa. Dhammakamme vematikā na paṭinissajjanti, āpatti saṅghādisesassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññā na paṭinissajjanti, āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

725. In a legitimate formal act, perceiving it as a legitimate formal act, if they do not abandon it, there is an offense of Saṅghādisesa. In a legitimate formal act, being uncertain, if they do not abandon it, there is an offense of Saṅghādisesa. In a legitimate formal act, perceiving it as an illegitimate formal act, if they do not abandon it, there is an offense of Saṅghādisesa.

Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In an illegitimate formal act, perceiving it as a legitimate formal act, there is an offense of wrongdoing. In an illegitimate formal act, being uncertain, there is an offense of wrongdoing. In an illegitimate formal act, perceiving it as an illegitimate formal act, there is an offense of wrongdoing.

726. Anāpatti [V 0.0325] asamanubhāsantīnaṃ, paṭinissajjantīnaṃ, ummattikānaṃ, ādikammikānanti.

726. There is no offense for those not being formally admonished, for those who abandon it, for the insane, and for the first offenders.

Navamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The ninth Saṅghādisesa training rule is concluded.

10. Dasamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Tenth Saṅghādisesa Training Rule

727. Tena [M 0.0313] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunīsaṅghena samanubhaṭṭhā bhikkhuniyo evaṃ vadeti – “saṃsaṭṭhāva ayye, tumhe viharatha. Mā tumhe nānā viharittha. Santi saṅghe aññāpi bhikkhuniyo evācārā evaṃsaddā evaṃsilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa [T 0.0058][P 4.0241] vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Tā saṅgho na kiñci āha. Tumhaññeva tumheyeva (syā.) saṅgho uññāya paribhavena akkhantiyā vebhassiyā vebhassā (sī. syā.) dubbalyā evamāha – ‘bhaginiyo kho saṃsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Viviccathāyye. Vivekaññeva bhaginīnaṃ saṅgho vaṇṇetī’”ti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā bhikkhunī saṅghena samanubhaṭṭhā bhikkhuniyo evaṃ vakkhati – saṃsaṭṭhāva ayye, tumhe viharatha. Mā tumhe nānā viharittha. Santi saṅghe aññāpi bhikkhuniyo…pe… viviccathāyye. Vivekaññeva bhaginīnaṃ saṅgho vaṇṇetīti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī saṅghena samanubhaṭṭhā bhikkhuniyo evaṃ vadeti – saṃsaṭṭhāva ayye tumhe viharatha. Mā tumhe nānā viharittha. Santi saṅghe aññāpi bhikkhuniyo evācārā evaṃsaddā evaṃsilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Tā saṅgho na kiñci āha. Tumhaññeva saṅgho uññāya paribhavena akkhantiyā vebhassiyā dubbalyā evamāha – bhaginiyo kho saṃsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Viviccathāyye. Vivekaññeva bhaginīnaṃ saṅgho vaṇṇetīti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī saṅghena samanubhaṭṭhā bhikkhuniyo evaṃ vakkhati – saṃsaṭṭhāva ayye, tumhe viharatha. Mā tumhe nānā viharittha. Santi saṅghe aññāpi bhikkhuniyo…pe… viviccathāyye. Vivekaññeva bhaginīnaṃ saṅgho vaṇṇetīti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

727. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā said this to the bhikkhunīs who had been admonished by the Saṅgha: “Venerable ones, you should live associated with laypeople. Do not live separately. There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha of such evil conduct, of such evil reputation, of such evil livelihood, who are harassers of the Bhikkhunīsaṅgha, and who conceal each other’s faults. The Saṅgha says nothing to them. It is only to you that the Saṅgha speaks thus out of contempt, out of scorn, out of intolerance, because of their powerful speech, and because of your weakness, saying: ‘Sisters, you live associated with laypeople, with evil conduct, evil reputation, evil livelihood, being harassers of the Bhikkhunīsaṅgha, and concealing each other’s faults. Live apart, venerable ones. The Saṅgha praises only seclusion for the sisters.’” Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes…pe… they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can the venerable Thullanandā say this to the bhikkhunīs who have been admonished by the Saṅgha: ‘Venerable ones, you should live associated with laypeople. Do not live separately. There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha…pe… Live apart, venerable ones. The Saṅgha praises only seclusion for the sisters’?” …pe… “Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā says this to the bhikkhunīs who have been admonished by the Saṅgha: ‘Venerable ones, you should live associated with laypeople. Do not live separately. There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha of such evil conduct, of such evil reputation, of such evil livelihood, who are harassers of the Bhikkhunīsaṅgha, and who conceal each other’s faults. The Saṅgha says nothing to them. It is only to you that the Saṅgha speaks thus out of contempt, out of scorn, out of intolerance, because of their powerful speech, and because of your weakness, saying: ‘Sisters, you live associated with laypeople, with evil conduct, evil reputation, evil livelihood, being harassers of the Bhikkhunīsaṅgha, and concealing each other’s faults. Live apart, venerable ones. The Saṅgha praises only seclusion for the sisters’’?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her…pe… “How, monks, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā say this to the bhikkhunīs who have been admonished by the Saṅgha: ‘Venerable ones, you should live associated with laypeople. Do not live separately. There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha…pe… Live apart, venerable ones. The Saṅgha praises only seclusion for the sisters’? This, monks, is not for the faith of the faithless…pe… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule in this way:

728. “Yā [M 0.0314][V 0.0326] pana bhikkhunī evaṃ vadeyya [T 0.0059] – ‘saṃsaṭṭhāva ayye, tumhe viharatha. Mā tumhe nānā viharittha. Santi saṅghe aññāpi bhikkhuniyo evācārā evaṃsaddā evaṃsilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Tā saṅgho na kiñci āha. Tumhaññeva saṅgho uññāya paribhavena akkhantiyā vebhassiyā dubbalyā evamāha – bhaginiyo kho saṃsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Viviccathāyye. Vivekaññeva bhaginīnaṃ saṅgho vaṇṇetī’ti. Sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi evamassa vacanīyā – ‘mā, ayye, evaṃ avaca – saṃsaṭṭhāva ayye, tumhe viharatha. Mā tumhe nānā viharittha. Santi saṅghe aññāpi bhikkhuniyo evācārā evaṃsaddā evaṃsilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Tā saṅgho na kiñci āha. Tumhaññeva saṅgho uññāya paribhavena akkhantiyā vebhassiyā dubbalyā evamāha – bhaginiyo kho saṃsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Viviccathāyye. Vivekaññeva bhaginīnaṃ saṅgho vaṇṇetī’ti. Evañca sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi vuccamānā tatheva paggaṇheyya, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsitabbā tassa paṭinissaggāya. Yāvatatiyañce samanubhāsīyamānā taṃ paṭinissajjeyya, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ; no ce paṭinissajjeyya, ayampi bhikkhunī yāvatatiyakaṃ dhammaṃ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṃ saṅghādisesa”nti.

728. “Whatever bhikkhunī should speak thus: ‘Venerable ones, you should live associated with laypeople. You should not live separately. There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha of such evil conduct, such evil reputation, and such evil livelihood, who are harassers of the Bhikkhunīsaṅgha and conceal one another's faults. The Saṅgha says nothing to them. It is only to you that the Saṅgha speaks thus out of contempt, scorn, intolerance, because of their powerful speech, and because of your weakness, saying: “Indeed, sisters, they live associated with laypeople, being of evil conduct, evil reputation, and evil livelihood, being harassers of the Bhikkhunīsaṅgha, and concealing one another's faults. Venerable ones, you should be secluded. The Saṅgha praises only seclusion for the sisters.”’ That bhikkhunī should be spoken to by the bhikkhunīs thus: ‘Venerable one, do not speak thus, saying: “Venerable ones, you should live associated with laypeople. You should not live separately. There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha of such evil conduct, such evil reputation, and such evil livelihood, who are harassers of the Bhikkhunīsaṅgha and conceal one another's faults. The Saṅgha says nothing to them. It is only to you that the Saṅgha speaks thus out of contempt, scorn, intolerance, because of their powerful speech, and because of your weakness, saying: ‘Indeed, sisters, they live associated with laypeople, being of evil conduct, evil reputation, and evil livelihood, being harassers of the Bhikkhunīsaṅgha, and concealing one another's faults. Venerable ones, you should be secluded. The Saṅgha praises only seclusion for the sisters.’”’ And if that bhikkhunī, being spoken to by the bhikkhunīs, should persist in that very same way, that bhikkhunī should be formally admonished by the bhikkhunīs up to the third time for the relinquishment of that view. If, being formally admonished up to the third time, she should relinquish it, this is good. If she should not relinquish it, this bhikkhunī also has fallen into a Saṅghādisesa offense requiring expulsion, which is determined on the third admonition.”

729. Yā [T 0.0060] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

729. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever, of whatever sort…pe… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means…pe… in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Evaṃ vadeyyāti – “saṃsaṭṭhāva ayye, tumhe viharatha. Mā tumhe nānā viharittha. Santi saṅghe aññāpi bhikkhuniyo evācārā evaṃsaddā evaṃsilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Tā saṅgho na kiñci āha”.

‘Should speak thus’ means: ‘Venerable ones, you should live associated with laypeople. You should not live separately. There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha of such evil conduct, such evil reputation, and such evil livelihood, who are harassers of the Bhikkhunīsaṅgha and conceal one another's faults. The Saṅgha says nothing to them.’

Tumhaññeva saṅgho uññāyāti avaññāya.

‘The Saṅgha… only to you… out of contempt’ means: out of disregard.

Paribhavenāti pāribhabyatā.

‘Out of scorn’ means: by way of disparagement.

Akkhantiyāti kopena.

‘Out of intolerance’ means: with anger.

Vebhassiyāti [V 0.0327][M 0.0315] vibhassīkatā vibhassikatāya (sī.).

‘Because of their powerful speech’ means: because of being made powerful in speech.

Dubbalyāti [P 4.0242] apakkhatā.

‘Because of weakness’ means: because of being without a faction.

Evamāha – “bhaginiyo kho saṃsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Viciccathāyye. Vivekaññeva bhaginīnaṃ saṅgho vaṇṇetī”ti.

Speaks thus: ‘Indeed, sisters, they live associated with laypeople, being of evil conduct, evil reputation, and evil livelihood, being harassers of the Bhikkhunīsaṅgha, and concealing one another's faults. Venerable ones, you should be secluded. The Saṅgha praises only seclusion for the sisters.’

Sā bhikkhunīti yā sā evaṃvādinī bhikkhunī.

‘That bhikkhunī’ means: that bhikkhunī who is accustomed to speaking thus.

Bhikkhunīhīti aññāhi bhikkhunīhi.

‘By the bhikkhunīs’ means: by other bhikkhunīs.

Yā passanti yā suṇanti tāhi vattabbā – “māyye, evaṃ avaca – ‘saṃsaṭṭhāva ayye, tumhe viharatha. Mā tumhe nānā viharittha. Santi saṅghe aññāpi bhikkhuniyo…pe… viviccathāyye. Vivekaññeva bhaginīnaṃ saṅgho vaṇṇetī”ti. Dutiyampi [T 0.0061] vattabbā. Tatiyampi vattabbā. Sace paṭinissajjati, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ; no ce paṭinissajjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sutvā na vadanti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sā bhikkhunī saṅghamajjhampi ākaḍḍhitvā vattabbā – “māyye, evaṃ avaca – ‘saṃsaṭṭhāva ayye, tumhe viharatha. Mā tumhe nānā viharittha. Santi saṅghe aññāpi bhikkhuniyo…pe… viviccathāyye. Vivekaññeva bhaginīnaṃ saṅgho vaṇṇetī’”ti. Dutiyampi vattabbā. Tatiyampi vattabbā. Sace paṭinissajjati, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ; no ce paṭinissajjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sā bhikkhunī samanubhāsitabbā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, samanubhāsitabbā. Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

She should be spoken to by those who see or hear: ‘Venerable one, do not speak thus: “Venerable ones, you should live associated with laypeople. You should not live separately. There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha… and so on… Venerable ones, you should be secluded. The Saṅgha praises only seclusion for the sisters.”’ She should be spoken to a second time. She should be spoken to a third time. If she relinquishes it, this is good; if she does not relinquish it, an offense of wrong-doing is incurred. If, having heard, they do not speak, an offense of wrong-doing is incurred. That bhikkhunī, having been drawn into the midst of the Saṅgha, should be spoken to: ‘Venerable one, do not speak thus: “Venerable ones, you should live associated with laypeople. You should not live separately. There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha… and so on… Venerable ones, you should be secluded. The Saṅgha praises only seclusion for the sisters.”’ She should be spoken to a second time. She should be spoken to a third time. If she relinquishes it, this is good; if she does not relinquish it, an offense of wrong-doing is incurred. That bhikkhunī should be formally admonished. And thus, O monks, she should be formally admonished. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhunī:

730. “Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā bhikkhunī saṅghena samanubhaṭṭhā bhikkhuniyo evaṃ vadeti – ‘saṃsaṭṭhāva ayye, tumhe viharatha. Mā tumhe nānā viharittha. Santi saṅghe aññāpi bhikkhuniyo evācārā evaṃsaddā evaṃsilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Tā saṅgho na kiñci āha. Tumhaññeva saṅgho uññāya paribhavena akkhantiyā vebhassiyā dubbalyā evamāha – bhaginiyo kho saṃsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā [T 0.0062] pāpasaddā pāpasilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā[V 0.0328]. Viviccathāyye. Vivekaññeva bhaginīnaṃ saṅgho vaṇṇetī’ti. Sā taṃ vatthuṃ na paṭinissajjati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuniṃ samanubhāseyya tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya. Esā ñatti.

730. “Venerable ones, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name speaks thus to the bhikkhunīs who have been formally admonished by the Saṅgha: ‘Venerable ones, you should live associated with laypeople. You should not live separately. There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha of such bad conduct, such bad reputation, and such bad livelihood, who are vexatious to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and conceal one another's faults. The Saṅgha says nothing to them. It is only to you that the Saṅgha speaks thus out of contempt, scorn, intolerance, through domineering speech, and because of your weakness, saying: “Indeed, sisters, they live associated with laypeople, being of bad conduct, bad reputation, and bad livelihood, being vexatious to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha, and concealing one another's faults. Venerable ones, you should be secluded. The Saṅgha praises only seclusion for the sisters.”’ She does not relinquish that view. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should formally admonish the bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name for the relinquishment of that view. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu [M 0.0316] me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā bhikkhunī saṅghena samanubhaṭṭhā bhikkhuniyo evaṃ vadeti – ‘saṃsaṭṭhāva ayye, tumhe viharatha. Mā tumhe nānā viharittha. Santi saṅghe aññāpi bhikkhuniyo evācārā evaṃsaddā evaṃsilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Tā saṅgho na kiñci āha. Tumhaññeva saṅgho uññāya paribhavena akkhantiyā vebhassiyā dubbalyā evamāha – bhaginiyo kho saṃsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā. Viviccathāyye. Vivekaññeva bhaginīnaṃ saṅgho vaṇṇetī’ti. Sā taṃ vatthuṃ na paṭinissajjati. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuniṃ samanubhāsati tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā samanubhāsanā tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.

“Venerable ones, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name speaks thus to the bhikkhunīs who have been formally admonished by the Saṅgha: ‘Venerable ones, you should live associated with laypeople. You should not live separately. There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha of such bad conduct, such bad reputation, and such bad livelihood, who are vexatious to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and conceal one another's faults. The Saṅgha says nothing to them. It is only to you that the Saṅgha speaks thus out of contempt, scorn, intolerance, through domineering speech, and because of your weakness, saying: “Indeed, sisters, they live associated with laypeople, being of bad conduct, bad reputation, and bad livelihood, being vexatious to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha, and concealing one another's faults. Venerable ones, you should be secluded. The Saṅgha praises only seclusion for the sisters.”’ She does not relinquish that view. The Saṅgha formally admonishes the bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name for the relinquishment of that view. To whichever venerable one the formal admonishment of the bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name for the relinquishment of that view is agreeable, she should be silent; to whom it is not agreeable, she should speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

“For a second time I state this matter… and so on… For a third time I state this matter… and so on…”

“Samanubhaṭṭhā saṅghena itthannāmā bhikkhunī tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name has been formally admonished by the Saṅgha for the relinquishment of that view. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold this.”

Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ, dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā, kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa. Saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpajjantiyā ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ, dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā paṭippassambhanti.

For the motion, there is an offense of wrong-doing. For the two formal announcements, there are grave offenses. At the conclusion of the formal announcements, a saṅghādisesa offense is incurred. For the bhikkhunī who incurs the saṅghādisesa offense, the offense of wrong-doing that arose from the motion is pacified, and the grave offenses that arose from the two formal announcements are pacified.

Ayampīti purimāyo upādāya vuccati.

‘This one also’ is said with reference to the preceding bhikkhunīs.

Yāvatatiyakanti yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya āpajjati, na sahavatthujjhācārā.

‘Up to the third time’ means that one incurs an offense by the formal admonishment up to the third time; one does not incur it simultaneously with the transgression of the matter.

Nissāraṇīyanti saṅghamhā nissārīyati.

‘Requiring expulsion’ means one is expelled from the Saṅgha.

Saṅghādisesoti [V 0.0329] saṅghova tassā āpattiyā mānattaṃ deti, mūlāya paṭikassati, abbheti, na sambahulā na ekā bhikkhunī. Tena vuccati “saṅghādiseso”ti. Tasseva āpattinikāyassa nāmakammaṃ adhivacanaṃ, tenapi vuccati “saṅghādiseso”ti.

‘Saṅghādisesa’ means that only the Saṅgha gives mānatta for that offense, sends her back to the beginning, and rehabilitates her; not many bhikkhunīs, nor one bhikkhunī. Therefore, it is called ‘saṅghādisesa’. It is the name and designation of that very class of offenses; for that reason also, it is called ‘saṅghādisesa’.

731. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññā na paṭinissajjati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa[T 0.0063]. Dhammakamme vematikā na paṭinissajjati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññā na paṭinissajjati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

731. In a formal procedure according to the Dhamma, being perceptive that it is a formal procedure according to the Dhamma, if she does not relinquish it, a saṅghādisesa offense is incurred. In a formal procedure according to the Dhamma, being doubtful, if she does not relinquish it, a saṅghādisesa offense is incurred. In a formal procedure according to the Dhamma, being perceptive that it is not a formal procedure according to the Dhamma, if she does not relinquish it, a saṅghādisesa offense is incurred.

Adhammakamme [M 0.0317] dhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In what is not a formal procedure according to the Dhamma, being perceptive that it is a formal procedure according to the Dhamma, an offense of wrong-doing is incurred. In what is not a formal procedure according to the Dhamma, being doubtful, an offense of wrong-doing is incurred. In what is not a formal procedure according to the Dhamma, being perceptive that it is not a formal procedure according to the Dhamma, an offense of wrong-doing is incurred.

732. Anāpatti asamanubhāsantiyā, paṭinissajjantiyā, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

732. There is no offense for a bhikkhunī who is not formally admonished, for one who relinquishes it, for one who is insane, and for the first offender.

Dasamasaṅghādisesasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The tenth saṅghādisesa training rule is finished.

Uddiṭṭhā kho, ayyāyo, sattarasa saṅghādisesā dhammā – nava paṭhamāpattikā, aṭṭha yāvatatiyakā. Yesaṃ bhikkhunī aññataraṃ vā aññataraṃ vā āpajjati, tāya bhikkhuniyā ubhatosaṅghe pakkhamānattaṃ caritabbaṃ. Ciṇṇamānattā bhikkhunī yattha siyā vīsatigaṇo bhikkhunisaṅgho tattha (sā bhikkhunī) ( ) (katthapi natthi) abbhetabbā. Ekāyapi ce ūno vīsatigaṇo bhikkhunisaṅgho taṃ bhikkhuniṃ abbheyya. Sā ca bhikkhunī anabbhitā, tā ca bhikkhuniyo gārayhā, ayaṃ tattha sāmīci.

Venerable ladies, the seventeen rules called saṅghādisesa have indeed been recited: nine are incurred at the first transgression, eight are incurred at the end of the third formal act. Whichever bhikkhunī incurs any one of these, that bhikkhunī must practice pakkhamānatta in both Saṅghas. The bhikkhunī who has completed mānatta must be rehabilitated where there is a Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs numbering twenty. If a Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs numbering twenty less even one should rehabilitate that bhikkhunī, that bhikkhunī is not rehabilitated, and those bhikkhunīs are blameworthy. This is the proper procedure therein.

Tatthāyyāyo pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Dutiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Tatiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Parisuddhetthāyyāyo, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti.

Herein, venerable ladies, I ask you: ‘Are you pure?’ For the second time, I ask you: ‘Are you pure?’ For the third time, I ask you: ‘Are you pure?’ The venerable ladies are pure in this matter, therefore they are silent. Thus I hold this.

Sattarasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section of seventeen is finished.

Bhikkhunivibhaṅge saṅghādisesakaṇḍaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

In the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga, the Saṅghādisesa chapter is finished.

3. Nissaggiyakaṇḍaṃ (bhikkhunīvibhaṅgo)

3. The Chapter on Forfeiture (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga)

1. Pattavaggo

1. The Bowl Chapter

1. Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The First Training Rule

Ime kho panāyyāyo tiṃsa nissaggiyā pācittiyā

Venerable ladies, these are the thirty rules entailing forfeiture and confession.

Dhammā uddesaṃ āgacchanti.

These rules come up for recitation.

733. Tena [T 0.0064][P 4.0243][M 0.0318][V 0.0330] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo bahū patte sannicayaṃ karonti. Manussā vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo bahū patte sannicayaṃ karissanti, pattavāṇijjaṃ vā bhikkhuniyo karissanti, āmattikāpaṇaṃ vā pasāressantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo pattasannicayaṃ karissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo pattasannicayaṃ karontīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo pattasannicayaṃ karissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

733. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs were accumulating many bowls. People wandering about the monastery saw this and complained, criticized, and spread it about: ‘How can these bhikkhunīs accumulate so many bowls? Are the bhikkhunīs engaged in bowl trade, or setting up a pottery shop?’ The bhikkhunīs heard the complaints, criticism, and spreading of rumors by those people. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about: ‘How can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs accumulate bowls?’… ‘Is it true, bhikkhus, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs are accumulating bowls?’ ‘It is true, Blessed One.’ The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… ‘How, bhikkhus, can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs accumulate bowls? This, bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule—

734. “Yā pana bhikkhunī pattasannicayaṃ kareyya[T 0.0065], nissaggiyaṃ pācittiya”nti.

734. ‘Whatever bhikkhunī should accumulate a bowl, it is an offense of forfeiture with confession.’

735. Yā [V 0.0331] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

735. ‘Whatever’ means whichever, of whatever kind… ‘bhikkhunī’… in this sense, this bhikkhunī is intended.

Patto nāma dve pattā – ayopatto, mattikāpatto. Tayo pattassa vaṇṇā – ukkaṭṭho patto, majjhimo patto, omako patto. Ukkaṭṭho nāma patto aḍḍhāḷhakodanaṃ gaṇhāti catubhāgaṃ khādanaṃ tadupiyaṃ byañjanaṃ. Majjhimo nāma patto nāḷikodanaṃ gaṇhāti catubhāgaṃ khādanaṃ tadupiyaṃ byañjanaṃ. Omako [P 4.0244] nāma patto patthodanaṃ gaṇhāti catubhāgaṃ khādanaṃ tadupiyaṃ byañjanaṃ. Tato ukkaṭṭho apatto omako apatto.

A bowl, namely, is of two kinds: an iron bowl and a clay bowl. There are three sizes of bowls: a superior bowl, a medium bowl, and an inferior bowl. A superior bowl, namely, holds half an āḷhaka of cooked rice, a quarter portion of solid food, and a corresponding amount of curry. A medium bowl, namely, holds a nāḷika of cooked rice, a quarter portion of solid food, and a corresponding amount of curry. An inferior bowl, namely, holds a pattha of cooked rice, a quarter portion of solid food, and a corresponding amount of curry. One larger than the superior is not a bowl; one smaller than the inferior is not a bowl.

Sannicayaṃ kareyyāti anadhiṭṭhito avikappito.

‘Should accumulate’ means to do so with a bowl that is undetermined and unshared.

Nissaggiyo [M 0.0319] hotīti saha aruṇuggamanā nissaggiyo hoti. Nissajjitabbo saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā ekabhikkhuniyā vā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, nissajjitabbo. Tāya bhikkhuniyā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – “ayaṃ me, ayye, patto rattātikkanto nissaggiyo, imāhaṃ saṅghassa nissajjāmī”ti. Nissajjitvā [T 0.0066] āpatti desetabbā. Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya āpatti paṭiggahetabbā. Nissaṭṭhapatto dātabbo –

‘It is to be forfeited’ means it is to be forfeited at the rising of dawn. It should be relinquished to the Saṅgha, to a group, or to a single bhikkhunī. And this, bhikkhus, is how it should be relinquished. That bhikkhunī, having approached the Saṅgha, arranging her upper robe over one shoulder, paying homage at the feet of the senior bhikkhunīs, squatting, raising her joined hands, should say this: ‘Venerable ladies, this bowl of mine, having been kept overnight, is to be forfeited; I relinquish it to the Saṅgha.’ Having relinquished it, the offense should be confessed. A competent and capable bhikkhunī should accept the confession of the offense. The relinquished bowl should be given back—

“Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ patto itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā nissaggiyo saṅghassa nissaṭṭho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho imaṃ pattaṃ itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā dadeyyā”ti.

‘May the Saṅgha, venerable ladies, listen to me. This bowl of the bhikkhunī named so-and-so is to be forfeited and has been relinquished to the Saṅgha. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should give this bowl to the bhikkhunī named so-and-so.’

Tāya bhikkhuniyā sambahulā bhikkhuniyo upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassu vacanīyā – “ayaṃ me, ayyāyo, patto rattātikkanto nissaggiyo, imāhaṃ ayyānaṃ nissajjāmī”ti. Nissajjitvā āpatti desetabbā. Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya āpatti paṭiggahetabbā. Nissaṭṭhapatto dātabbo –

That bhikkhunī, having approached several bhikkhunīs, arranging her upper robe over one shoulder, paying homage at the feet of the senior bhikkhunīs, squatting, raising her joined hands, should say this: ‘Venerable ladies, this bowl of mine, having been kept overnight, is to be forfeited; I relinquish it to the venerable ladies.’ Having relinquished it, the offense should be confessed. A competent and capable bhikkhunī should accept the confession of the offense. The relinquished bowl should be given back—

“Suṇantu me ayyāyo. Ayaṃ patto itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā nissaggiyo ayyānaṃ nissaṭṭho. Yadi ayyānaṃ pattakallaṃ, ayyāyo imaṃ pattaṃ itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā dadeyyu”nti.

‘May the venerable ladies listen to me. This bowl of the bhikkhunī named so-and-so is to be forfeited and has been relinquished to the venerable ladies. If it is the proper time for the venerable ladies, the venerable ladies should give this bowl to the bhikkhunī named so-and-so.’

Tāya [V 0.0332] bhikkhuniyā ekaṃ bhikkhuniṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyā – “ayaṃ me, ayye, patto rattātikkanto nissaggiyo. Imāhaṃ ayyāya nissajjāmī”ti. Nissajjitvā āpatti desetabbā. Tāya bhikkhuniyā āpatti paṭiggahetabbā. Nissaṭṭhapatto dātabbo – “imaṃ pattaṃ ayyāya dammī”ti.

That bhikkhunī, having approached a single bhikkhunī, arranging her upper robe over one shoulder, squatting, raising her joined hands, should say this: ‘Venerable sister, this bowl of mine, having been kept overnight, is to be forfeited; I relinquish it to you, venerable sister.’ Having relinquished it, the offense should be confessed. That bhikkhunī should accept the confession of the offense. The relinquished bowl should be given back, saying: ‘I give this bowl to you, venerable sister.’

736. Rattātikkante [T 0.0067] atikkantasaññā, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Rattātikkante vematikā, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Rattātikkante anatikkantasaññā, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Anadhiṭṭhite adhiṭṭhitasaññā, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Avikappite vikappitasaññā, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Avissajjite [M 0.0320] vissajjitasaññā[P 4.0245], nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Anaṭṭhe naṭṭhasaññā… avinaṭṭhe vinaṭṭhasaññā… abhinne bhinnasaññā… avilutte viluttasaññā, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

736. If, when the night has passed, one perceives it as having passed and stores the bowl, it is an offense entailing forfeiture and requiring confession. If, when the night has passed, one is uncertain and stores the bowl, it is an offense entailing forfeiture and requiring confession. If, when the night has passed, one perceives it as not having passed and stores the bowl, it is an offense entailing forfeiture and requiring confession. If a bowl is undetermined, but one perceives it as determined and stores it, it is an offense entailing forfeiture and requiring confession. If a bowl is unshared, but one perceives it as shared and stores it, it is an offense entailing forfeiture and requiring confession. If a bowl has not been relinquished, but one perceives it as relinquished and stores it, it is an offense entailing forfeiture and requiring confession. If it is not lost, but one perceives it as lost and stores it… if it is not destroyed, but one perceives it as destroyed and stores it… if it is not broken, but one perceives it as broken and stores it… if it has not been stolen, but one perceives it as stolen and stores it, it is an offense entailing forfeiture and requiring confession.

Nissaggiyaṃ pattaṃ anissajjitvā paribhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Rattānatikkante atikkantasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Rattānatikkante vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Rattānatikkante anatikkantasaññā anāpatti.

If one uses a bowl that is to be forfeited without having relinquished it, there is an offense of wrongdoing. If, when the night has not passed, one perceives that it has passed, there is an offense of wrongdoing. If, when the night has not passed, one is in doubt, there is an offense of wrongdoing. If, when the night has not passed, one perceives that it has not passed, there is no offense.

737. Anāpatti antoaruṇe adhiṭṭheti, vikappeti, vissajjeti, nassati, vinassati, bhijjati, acchinditvā gaṇhanti, vissāsaṃ gaṇhanti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

737. There is no offense if, before dawn, one determines it, shares it, or gives it away; or if it is lost, destroyed, or broken; or if it is forcibly taken or taken on trust; or for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo nissaṭṭhapattaṃ na denti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, nissaṭṭhapatto na dātabbo. Yā na dadeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, the bhikkhunīs of the group of six did not return a forfeited bowl. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. [The Blessed One said:] 'O bhikkhus, it is not that a forfeited bowl is not to be given; it must indeed be given. Whatever bhikkhunī should not give it, she incurs an offense of wrongdoing.'

Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The first training rule is finished.

2. Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Second Training Rule

738. Tena [T 0.0068] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme[V 0.0333]. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhuniyo gāmakāvāse vassaṃvuṭṭhā vassaṃvutthā (sī. syā.) sāvatthiṃ agamaṃsu vattasampannā iriyāpathasampannā duccoḷā lūkhacīvarā. Upāsakā tā bhikkhuniyo passitvā – “imā bhikkhuniyo vattasampannā iriyāpathasampannā duccoḷā lūkhacīvarā, imā bhikkhuniyo acchinnā bhavissantī”ti bhikkhunisaṅghassa akālacīvaraṃ adaṃsu. Thullanandā bhikkhunī – “amhākaṃ kathinaṃ atthataṃ kālacīvara”nti adhiṭṭhahitvā bhājāpesi. Upāsakā tā bhikkhuniyo passitvā etadavocuṃ – “apayyāhi cīvaraṃ laddha”nti? “Na mayaṃ, āvuso, cīvaraṃ labhāma. Ayyā thullanandā – ‘amhākaṃ kathinaṃ atthataṃ kālacīvara’nti adhiṭṭhahitvā bhājāpesī”ti. Upāsakā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā akālacīvaraṃ ‘kālacīvara’nti adhiṭṭhahitvā bhājāpessatī”ti! Assosuṃ [M 0.0321] kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ upāsakānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā akālacīvaraṃ ‘kālacīvara’nti adhiṭṭhahitvā bhājāpessatī”ti! Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ [P 4.0246] …pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave[T 0.0069], thullanandā bhikkhunī akālacīvaraṃ “kālacīvara”nti adhiṭṭhahitvā bhājāpetīti bhājāpesīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī akālacīvaraṃ “kālacīvara”nti adhiṭṭhahitvā bhājāpessati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

738. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. At that time, many bhikkhunīs who had completed the rains-residence in a village monastery went to Sāvatthī—accomplished in their duties, accomplished in their deportment, with soiled lower garments and coarse robes. Lay devotees, upon seeing these bhikkhunīs, thought, 'These bhikkhunīs are accomplished in their duties and accomplished in their deportment, with soiled lower garments and coarse robes. These bhikkhunīs must have been robbed of their robes.' So they gave out-of-season robes to the Sangha of bhikkhunīs. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having determined, 'For us, the kathina is spread; this is an in-season robe,' had them distributed. The lay devotees, seeing those bhikkhunīs, said, 'Venerable ladies, have you received robes?' 'We have not received robes, friends. The venerable Thullanandā, having determined, "For us, the kathina is spread; this is an in-season robe," had it distributed.' The lay devotees complained, criticized, and grumbled: 'How indeed could the venerable Thullanandā, having determined an out-of-season robe to be an "in-season robe," have it distributed!' The bhikkhunīs heard these lay devotees complaining, criticizing, and grumbling. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and grumbled: 'How indeed could the venerable Thullanandā, having determined an out-of-season robe to be an "in-season robe," have it distributed!' Then those bhikkhunīs informed the bhikkhus about this matter. The bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One… 'Is it true, O bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having determined an out-of-season robe to be an "in-season robe," had it distributed?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… 'How indeed, O bhikkhus, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having determined an out-of-season robe to be an "in-season robe," have it distributed! This, O bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, O bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule as follows—'

739. “Yā pana bhikkhunī akālacīvaraṃ ‘kālacīvara’nti adhiṭṭhahitvā bhājāpeyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiya”nti.

739. “Whatever bhikkhunī, having determined an out-of-season robe to be an ‘in-season robe,’ should have it distributed, it is an offense entailing forfeiture and requiring confession.”

740. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

740. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever sort… and so on. ‘Bhikkhunī’ means: … and so on. In this context, ‘bhikkhunī’ is intended to mean this particular kind of bhikkhunī.

Akālacīvaraṃ nāma anatthate kathine ekādasamāse uppannaṃ, atthate kathine sattamāse uppannaṃ, kālepi ādissa dinnaṃ, etaṃ akālacīvaraṃ nāma.

An 'out-of-season robe' means: when the kathina is not spread, a robe that has arisen during the eleven months; when the kathina is spread, a robe that has arisen during the seven months; and also a robe given with a specific designation during the robe-season. This is called an 'out-of-season robe'.

Akālacīvaraṃ “kālacīvara”nti adhiṭṭhahitvā bhājāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Nissajjitabbaṃ saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā ekabhikkhuniyā vā. Evañca pana[V 0.0334], bhikkhave, nissajjitabbaṃ…pe… idaṃ me, ayye, akālacīvaraṃ “kālacīvara’nti adhiṭṭhahitvā bhājāpitaṃ nissaggiyaṃ, imāhaṃ saṅghassa nissajjāmī”ti…pe… dadeyyāti…pe… dadeyyunti…pe… ayyāya dammīti.

If she, having determined an out-of-season robe to be 'an in-season robe', has it distributed, there is an offense of wrongdoing for the effort. Upon receiving it, it becomes subject to forfeiture. It is to be forfeited to the Sangha, or to a group, or to a single bhikkhunī. And so, O bhikkhus, it is to be forfeited… 'Venerable ladies, this out-of-season robe of mine, having been distributed after being determined as an "in-season robe," is to be forfeited. I forfeit this out-of-season robe to the Sangha.'… It should be given… They should give… 'I give this to the venerable lady.'

741. Akālacīvare akālacīvarasaññā “kālacīvara”nti adhiṭṭhahitvā bhājāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Akālacīvare vematikā “kālacīvara”nti [T 0.0070] adhiṭṭhahitvā bhājāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.
