Akālacīvare kālacīvarasaññā “kālacīvara”nti adhiṭṭhahitvā bhājāpeti[M 0.0322], anāpatti. Kālacīvare akālacīvarasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kālacīvare vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kālacīvare kālacīvarasaññā, anāpatti.

741. If she perceives an out-of-season robe as an out-of-season robe and, having determined it as an 'in-season robe', has it distributed, it is an offense entailing forfeiture and requiring confession. If she is in doubt about an out-of-season robe and, having determined it as an 'in-season robe', has it distributed, there is an offense of wrongdoing. If she perceives an out-of-season robe as an in-season robe and, having determined it as an 'in-season robe', has it distributed, there is no offense. If she perceives an in-season robe as an out-of-season robe and has it distributed, there is an offense of wrongdoing. If she is in doubt about an in-season robe and has it distributed, there is an offense of wrongdoing. If she perceives an in-season robe as an in-season robe and has it distributed, there is no offense.

742. Anāpatti akālacīvaraṃ kālacīvarasaññā bhājāpeti, kālacīvaraṃ kālacīvarasaññā bhājāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

742. There is no offense if she has an out-of-season robe distributed while perceiving it as an in-season robe; if she has an in-season robe distributed while perceiving it as an in-season robe; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The second training rule is finished.

3. Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Third Training Rule

743. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī aññatarāya bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ cīvaraṃ parivattetvā paribhuñji. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī taṃ cīvaraṃ saṅgharitvā saṃharitvā (ka.) nikkhipi. Thullanandā bhikkhunī taṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “yaṃ te, ayye, mayā [P 4.0247] saddhiṃ cīvaraṃ parivattitaṃ, kahaṃ taṃ cīvara”nti? Atha kho sā bhikkhunī taṃ cīvaraṃ nīharitvā thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā dassesi. Thullanandā bhikkhunī [T 0.0071] taṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “handāyye, tuyhaṃ cīvaraṃ, āhara me’taṃ cīvaraṃ, yaṃ tuyhaṃ tuyhamevetaṃ, yaṃ mayhaṃ mayhamevetaṃ, āhara me’taṃ, sakaṃ paccāharā”ti acchindi. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ cīvaraṃ parivattetvā acchindissatī”ti! Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārācesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ cīvaraṃ parivattetvā acchindatīti acchindīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī [V 0.0335] bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ cīvaraṃ parivattetvā acchindissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

743. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having exchanged a robe with a certain bhikkhunī, used it. Then that bhikkhunī, having folded that robe, put it away. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā said this to that bhikkhunī: “Venerable lady, where is that robe that was exchanged with me by you?” Then that bhikkhunī, having taken out that robe, showed it to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā said this to that bhikkhunī: “Here, venerable lady, take your robe. Bring me that robe of mine. What is your robe, let that be yours alone. What is my robe, let that be mine alone. Bring me that robe of mine. Take back what is yours.” And she seized it. Then that bhikkhunī told this matter to the bhikkhunīs. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… and so on… they criticized, found fault, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the venerable lady Thullanandā, having exchanged a robe with a bhikkhunī, seize it?” Then those bhikkhunīs told this matter to the bhikkhus. The bhikkhus told this matter to the Blessed One… and so on… “Is it true, monks, as is said, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having exchanged a robe with a bhikkhunī, seizes it?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… and so on… “How indeed, monks, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having exchanged a robe with a bhikkhunī, seize it? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… and so on… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

744. “Yā [M 0.0323] pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ cīvaraṃ parivattetvā sā pacchā evaṃ vadeyya – ‘handāyye, tuyhaṃ cīvaraṃ āhara, metaṃ cīvaraṃ, yaṃ tuyhaṃ tuyhamevetaṃ, yaṃ mayhaṃ mayhamevetaṃ, āhara metaṃ, sakaṃ paccāharā’ti acchindeyya vā acchindāpeyya vā, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiya”nti.

744. “Whatever bhikkhunī, having exchanged a robe with a bhikkhunī, should afterwards speak thus: ‘Here, venerable lady, take your robe; bring me that robe of mine. What is your robe, let that be yours alone. What is my robe, let that be mine alone. Bring me that robe of mine. Take back what is yours,’ and should seize it or cause it to be seized, it is a pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture.”

745. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

745. ‘Whatever’ means: whichever, of whatever sort… and so on… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… and so on… in this sense, this bhikkhunī is intended.

Bhikkhuniyā saddhinti aññāya bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ.

‘With a bhikkhunī’ means: with another bhikkhunī.

Cīvaraṃ nāma channaṃ cīvarānaṃ aññataraṃ cīvaraṃ vikappanupagaṃ [T 0.0072] pacchimaṃ.

What is called a robe is any one of the six kinds of robes, at the very least, one that is suitable for determination.

Parivattetvāti parittena vā vipulaṃ, vipulena vā parittaṃ.

‘Having exchanged’ means: a valuable one for a less valuable one, or a less valuable one for a valuable one.

Acchindeyyāti sayaṃ acchindati nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

‘Should seize it’ means: she seizes it herself; it is a pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture.

Acchindāpeyyāti aññaṃ āṇāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sakiṃ āṇattā bahukampi acchindati, nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Nissajjitabbaṃ saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā ekabhikkhuniyā vā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, nissajjitabbaṃ…pe… “idaṃ me ayye cīvaraṃ bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ parivattetvā acchinnaṃ nissaggiyaṃ, imāhaṃ saṅghassa nissajjāmī”ti…pe… dadeyyāti…pe… dadeyyunti…pe… ayyāya dammīti.

‘Should cause it to be seized’ means: she orders another; there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one who was ordered once seizes it even many times, it becomes subject to forfeiture. It should be forfeited to the Sangha, or to a group, or to a single bhikkhunī. And so, monks, it should be forfeited… and so on… ‘Venerable ladies, this robe of mine, seized after having been exchanged with a bhikkhunī, is to be forfeited. I forfeit this to the Sangha.’… and so on… ‘Should give.’… and so on… ‘They should give.’… and so on… ‘I give to the venerable lady.’

746. Upasampannāya upasampannasaññā cīvaraṃ parivattetvā acchindati vā acchindāpeti vā, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Upasampannāya [P 4.0248] vematikā cīvaraṃ parivattetvā acchindati vā acchindāpeti vā, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Upasampannāya anupasampannasaññā cīvaraṃ parivattetvā acchindati vā acchindāpeti vā, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

746. If the other is a fully ordained bhikkhunī and one perceives her as such, and having exchanged a robe, one seizes it or causes it to be seized, it is a pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture. If the other is a fully ordained bhikkhunī and one is in doubt, and having exchanged a robe, one seizes it or causes it to be seized, it is a pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture. If the other is a fully ordained bhikkhunī and one perceives her as not fully ordained, and having exchanged a robe, one seizes it or causes it to be seized, it is a pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture.

Aññaṃ [V 0.0336] parikkhāraṃ parivattetvā acchindati vā acchindāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya saddhiṃ cīvaraṃ vā aññaṃ vā parikkhāraṃ parivattetvā acchindati vā acchindāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya upasampannasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya vematikā, āpatti [T 0.0073] dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya anupasampannasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Having exchanged another requisite, if one seizes it or causes it to be seized, there is an offense of wrong-doing. With one who is not fully ordained, having exchanged a robe or another requisite, if one seizes it or causes it to be seized, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of one who is not fully ordained, if one perceives her as fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of one who is not fully ordained, if one is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of one who is not fully ordained, if one perceives her as not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

747. Anāpatti sā vā deti, tassā vā vissasantī gaṇhāti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

747. There is no offense: if the other gives it; or if one takes it based on familiarity; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Third Training Rule is concluded.

4. Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Fourth Training Rule

748. Tena [M 0.0324] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī gilānā hoti. Atha kho aññataro upāsako yena thullanandā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ te, ayye, aphāsu, kiṃ āharīyatū”ti? “Sappinā me, āvuso, attho”ti. Atha kho so upāsako aññatarassa āpaṇikassa gharā kahāpaṇassa sappiṃ āharitvā thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā adāsi. Thullanandā bhikkhunī evamāha – “na me, āvuso, sappinā attho; telena me attho”ti. Atha kho so upāsako yena so āpaṇiko tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ āpaṇikaṃ etadavoca – “na kirāyyo ayyāya sappinā attho, telena attho. Handa te sappiṃ, telaṃ me dehī”ti. “Sace mayaṃ ayyo vikkītaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ [T 0.0074] puna ādiyissāma āharissāma (ka.), kadā amhākaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ vikkāyissati vikkīyissati (?); sappissa kayena sappi haṭaṃ, telassa kayaṃ āhara, telaṃ harissasī”ti. Atha kho so upāsako ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā aññaṃ viññāpetvā aññaṃ viññāpessatī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tassa upāsakassa ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti…pe… atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī aññaṃ viññāpetvā aññaṃ viññāpetīti viññāpesīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā [P 4.0249]…pe… kathañhi [V 0.0337] nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī aññaṃ viññāpetvā aññaṃ viññāpessati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

748. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time the bhikkhunī Thullanandā was sick. Then a certain lay follower approached the bhikkhunī Thullanandā; having approached, he said to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā: “Are you unwell, venerable one? What should be brought?” “I have need of ghee, friend.” Then that lay follower brought ghee worth a kahāpaṇa from a certain shopkeeper’s house and gave it to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā said: “I have no need of ghee, friend; I have need of oil.” Then that lay follower approached that shopkeeper; having approached, he said to the shopkeeper: “It seems the venerable one has no need of ghee; she has need of oil. Come, take your ghee; give me oil.” “If we, sir, were to take back goods already sold, when would our goods be sold? Ghee has been taken for the price of ghee; bring the price of oil, and you shall take oil.” Then that lay follower complained, grumbled, and protested: “How indeed could the venerable Thullanandā, having requested one thing, then request another?” The bhikkhunīs heard that lay follower complaining, grumbling, and protesting. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they complained, grumbled, and protested… Then those bhikkhunīs informed the bhikkhus of this matter. The bhikkhus informed the Blessed One of this matter… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having requested one thing, then requested another?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, bhikkhus, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having requested one thing, then request another? This, bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the faithless… And thus, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

749. “Yā pana bhikkhunī aññaṃ viññāpetvā aññaṃ viññāpeyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiya”nti.

749. “Whatever bhikkhunī, having requested one thing, should request another, it is a Pācittiya offense that entails forfeiture.”

750. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

750. Whatever: whatever, of whatever kind… bhikkhunī… this is the bhikkhunī intended in this context.

Aññaṃ [M 0.0325] viññāpetvāti yaṃ kiñci viññāpetvā.

Having requested one thing: having requested anything whatsoever.

Aññaṃ viññāpeyyāti taṃ ṭhapetvā aññaṃ viññāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Nissajjitabbaṃ saṅghassa [T 0.0075] vā gaṇassa vā ekabhikkhuniyā vā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, nissajjitabbaṃ…pe… “idaṃ me ayye aññaṃ viññāpetvā aññaṃ viññāpitaṃ nissaggiyaṃ, imāhaṃ saṅghassa nissajjāmīti…pe… dadeyyāti…pe… dadeyyunti…pe… ayyāya dammī”ti.

Should request another: setting aside that first item, she requests another. In the attempt, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Upon obtaining it, it becomes subject to forfeiture. It should be forfeited to the Saṅgha, or to a group, or to a single bhikkhunī. And thus, bhikkhus, it should be forfeited… “Venerable ladies, this item of mine, requested after having requested another, is to be forfeited. I forfeit this to the Saṅgha.”… should give… should give… “I give it to the venerable one.”

751. Aññe aññasaññā aññaṃ viññāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Aññe vematikā aññaṃ viññāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Aññe anaññasaññā aññaṃ viññāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

751. Regarding a different thing, perceiving it as different, she requests a different thing: it is a Pācittiya offense that entails forfeiture. Regarding a different thing, being doubtful, she requests a different thing: it is a Pācittiya offense that entails forfeiture. Regarding a different thing, perceiving it as not different, she requests a different thing: it is a Pācittiya offense that entails forfeiture.

Anaññe aññasaññā anaññaṃ viññāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anaññe vematikā anaññaṃ viññāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anaññe anaññasaññā, anāpatti.

Regarding a thing that is not different, perceiving it as different, she requests a thing that is not different: there is an offense of wrong-doing. Regarding a thing that is not different, being doubtful, she requests a thing that is not different: there is an offense of wrong-doing. Regarding a thing that is not different, perceiving it as not different, there is no offense.

752. Anāpatti taññeva tañceva (syā.) viññāpeti, aññañca viññāpeti, ānisaṃsaṃ dassetvā viññāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

752. There is no offense if she requests that very same thing; if she also requests another thing; if she requests after showing the benefit; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fourth Training Rule is concluded.

5. Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Fifth Training Rule

753. Tena [V 0.0338] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī gilānā hoti. Atha kho aññataro upāsako yena thullanandā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “kacci, ayye, khamanīyaṃ kacci yāpanīya”nti? “Na me, āvuso, khamanīyaṃ, na yāpanīya”nti. “Amukassa, ayye, āpaṇikassa ghare kahāpaṇaṃ [T 0.0076] nikkhipissāmi, tato yaṃ iccheyyāsi taṃ āharāpeyyāsī”ti. Thullanandā bhikkhunī aññataraṃ sikkhamānaṃ āṇāpesi – “gaccha, sikkhamāne, amukassa āpaṇikassa gharā kahāpaṇassa telaṃ āharā”ti. Atha kho sā sikkhamānā tassa [P 4.0250] āpaṇikassa gharā kahāpaṇassa telaṃ [M 0.0326] āharitvā thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā adāsi. Thullanandā bhikkhunī evamāha – “na me, sikkhamāne, telena attho, sappinā me attho”ti. Atha kho sā sikkhamānā yena so āpaṇiko tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ āpaṇikaṃ etadavoca – “na kira, āvuso, ayyāya telena attho, sappinā attho, handa te telaṃ, sappiṃ me dehī”ti. “Sace mayaṃ, ayye, vikkītaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ puna ādiyissāma, kadā amhākaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ vikkāyissati! Telassa kayena telaṃ haṭaṃ, sappissa kayaṃ āhara, sappiṃ harissasī”ti. Atha kho sā sikkhamānā rodantī aṭṭhāsi. Bhikkhuniyo taṃ sikkhamānaṃ etadavocuṃ – “kissa tvaṃ, sikkhamāne, rodasī”ti? Atha kho sā sikkhamānā bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā aññaṃ cetāpetvā aññaṃ cetāpessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī aññaṃ cetāpetvā aññaṃ cetāpetīti cetāpesīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī aññaṃ cetāpetvā [T 0.0077] aññaṃ cetāpessati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

753. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta’s Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā was ill. Then a certain lay follower approached the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, and having approached, said this to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā: “Venerable lady, are you keeping well? Are you getting by?” “Friend, I am not keeping well, I am not getting by.” “Venerable lady, I will deposit a kahāpaṇa at the house of such-and-such a shopkeeper. From there, you may have whatever you wish brought.” The bhikkhunī Thullanandā instructed a certain female probationer: “Go, probationer, and bring oil from the house of such-and-such a shopkeeper with the kahāpaṇa.” Then that female probationer, having brought oil from that shopkeeper’s house with the kahāpaṇa, gave it to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā said this: “Probationer, I have no need for oil; I need ghee.” Then that female probationer approached that shopkeeper, and having approached, said this to that shopkeeper: “Friend, it seems the venerable lady has no need for oil; she needs ghee. Here, take your oil and give me ghee.” “Venerable lady, if we were to take back goods that have been sold, when would our goods be sold? Oil was taken for the price of oil. Bring the price for ghee, and you shall take the ghee.” Then that female probationer stood there crying. The bhikkhunīs said this to that female probationer: “Probationer, why are you crying?” Then that female probationer related this matter to the bhikkhunīs. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... were critical, scornful, and contemptuous: “How indeed could the venerable lady Thullanandā, having had one thing acquired, then have another thing acquired?” ... “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having had one thing acquired, then has another thing acquired?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her... “How indeed, Bhikkhus, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having had one thing acquired, then have another thing acquired? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the faithless... And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

754. “Yā pana bhikkhunī aññaṃ cetāpetvā aññaṃ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiya”nti.

754. “Whatever bhikkhunī, having had one thing acquired, should then have another thing acquired, it is an offense of forfeiture and expiation.”

755. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

755. ‘Whatever’: whichever, of whatever kind... ‘bhikkhunī’: ... the bhikkhunī who is intended in this sense is meant.

Aññaṃ [V 0.0339] cetāpetvāti yaṃ kiñci cetāpetvā.

‘Having had one thing acquired’: having had anything whatsoever acquired.

Aññaṃ cetāpeyyāti taṃ ṭhapetvā aññaṃ cetāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Nissajjitabbaṃ saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā ekabhikkhuniyā vā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, nissajjitabbaṃ…pe… “idaṃ me, ayye, aññaṃ cetāpetvā aññaṃ cetāpitaṃ nissaggiyaṃ, imāhaṃ saṅghassa nissajjāmī”ti…pe… dadeyyāti…pe… dadeyyunti…pe… ayyāya dammīti.

‘Should have another thing acquired’: setting that aside, she has another thing acquired. In the effort, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Upon acquisition, it becomes subject to forfeiture. It should be forfeited to the Saṅgha, or to a group, or to a single bhikkhunī. And it should be forfeited in this way, Bhikkhus: ... ‘Venerable ladies, this item of mine, acquired by having one thing acquired after arranging for another, is to be forfeited. I forfeit this to the Saṅgha.’ ... should give ... they should give ... ‘I give it to the venerable lady.’

756. Aññe [M 0.0327] aññasaññā aññaṃ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Aññe vematikā aññaṃ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Aññe anaññasaññā aññaṃ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

756. If she has a different item acquired, perceiving it as different, it is an offense of forfeiture and expiation. If she has a different item acquired, while being uncertain, it is an offense of forfeiture and expiation. If she has a different item acquired, perceiving it as not different, it is an offense of forfeiture and expiation.

Anaññe aññasaññā anaññaṃ cetāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anaññe vematikā anaññaṃ cetāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anaññe anaññasaññā anāpatti.

If she has the same item acquired, but perceives it as different, she commits an offense of wrong conduct. If she has the same item acquired, while being uncertain, she commits an offense of wrong conduct. If she has the same item acquired, perceiving it as the same, there is no offense.

757. Anāpatti taññeva tañceva (syā.) cetāpeti, aññañca cetāpeti, ānisaṃsaṃ dassetvā cetāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

757. There is no offense if one has that very same thing acquired; if one has another thing acquired in a new transaction; if one has something acquired after pointing out its benefits; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fifth Training Rule is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Sixth Training Rule

758. Tena [T 0.0078] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena upāsakā bhikkhunisaṅghassa cīvaratthāya chandakaṃ saṅgharitvā aññatarassa pāvārikassa ghare parikkhāraṃ nikkhipitvā bhikkhuniyo upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – “amukassa, ayye, pāvārikassa ghare cīvaratthāya parikkhāro nikkhitto, tato cīvaraṃ āharāpetvā bhājethā”ti. Bhikkhuniyo tena parikkhārena bhesajjaṃ cetāpetvā paribhuñjiṃsu. Upāsakā jānitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena saṅghikena aññaṃ cetāpessantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ upāsakānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo [V 0.0340] appicchā [P 4.0251]…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena saṅghikena aññaṃ cetāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena saṅghikena aññaṃ cetāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo aññadatthikena [M 0.0328] parikkhārena aññuddisikena saṅghikena aññaṃ cetāpessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… [T 0.0079] evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

758. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, in the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, lay devotees had collected contributions for the purpose of robes for the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, and having deposited the requisites in the house of a certain cloth merchant, they approached the bhikkhunīs and said this: “Venerable ladies, requisites for the purpose of robes have been deposited in the house of such-and-such a cloth merchant. From there, having had robes brought, you should distribute them.” The bhikkhunīs had medicine acquired with those requisites and used it. The lay devotees found out and were critical, scornful, and contemptuous, saying, “How indeed can the bhikkhunīs have something else acquired with requisites given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, and belonging to the Saṅgha?” The bhikkhunīs heard those lay devotees being critical, scornful, and contemptuous. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires … were critical, scornful, and contemptuous, saying, “How indeed can the bhikkhunīs have something else acquired with requisites given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, and belonging to the Saṅgha?” … “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunīs are having something else acquired with requisites given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, and belonging to the Saṅgha?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … “How indeed, Bhikkhus, can the bhikkhunīs have something else acquired with requisites given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, and belonging to the Saṅgha? Bhikkhus, this is not for the confidence of the faithless … And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

759. “Yā pana bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena saṅghikena aññaṃ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiya”nti.

759. “Whatever bhikkhunī, with a Saṅghika requisite given for another purpose and designated for another purpose, should have another thing procured, it is a Pācittiya offense entailing forfeiture.”

760. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

760. ‘Whatever’: whichever, of whatever kind … ‘bhikkhunī’: … this is the bhikkhunī intended in this sense.

Aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikenāti aññassatthāya dinnena.

‘With a requisite given for another purpose, designated for another purpose’: means given for the purpose of another thing.

Saṅghikenāti saṅghassa, na gaṇassa, na ekabhikkhuniyā.

‘Belonging to the Saṅgha’: means relinquished to the Saṅgha, not to a group, not to a single bhikkhunī.

Aññaṃ cetāpeyyāti yaṃatthāya dinnaṃ, taṃ ṭhapetvā aññaṃ cetāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Nissajjitabbaṃ saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā ekabhikkhuniyā vā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, nissajjitabbaṃ…pe… “idaṃ me, ayye, aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena saṅghikena aññaṃ cetāpitaṃ nissaggiyaṃ, imāhaṃ saṅghassa nissajjāmī”ti.…Pe… dadeyyāti…pe… dadeyyunti…pe… ayyāya dammīti.

‘Should have another thing procured’: setting aside that for the purpose of which it was given, one has another thing procured; in the effort, there is a Dukkaṭa offense. Upon its acquisition, it becomes subject to forfeiture. It is to be forfeited to the Saṅgha, or to a group, or to a single bhikkhunī. And thus, monks, it is to be forfeited: … “Venerable ladies, this of mine, having been procured as another thing with a Saṅghika requisite given for another purpose and designated for another purpose, is subject to forfeiture. I forfeit this to the Saṅgha.” … One should give … They should give … “I give it to the venerable lady.”

761. Aññadatthike aññadatthikasaññā aññaṃ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Aññadatthike vematikā aññaṃ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Aññadatthike anaññadatthikasaññā aññaṃ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Nissaṭṭhaṃ paṭilabhitvā yathādāne upanetabbaṃ.

761. In the case of a requisite given for another purpose, if she is perceptive that it was given for another purpose and has another thing procured, it is a Pācittiya offense entailing forfeiture. In the case of a requisite given for another purpose, if she is in doubt and has another thing procured, it is a Pācittiya offense entailing forfeiture. In the case of a requisite given for another purpose, if she is perceptive that it was not given for another purpose and has another thing procured, it is a Pācittiya offense entailing forfeiture. Having received back what was forfeited, it should be applied in accordance with the original donation.

Anaññadatthike [V 0.0341] aññadatthikasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anaññadatthike vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anaññadatthike anaññadatthikasaññā, anāpatti.

In the case of a requisite not given for another purpose, if she is perceptive that it was given for another purpose, there is a Dukkaṭa offense. In the case of a requisite not given for another purpose, if she is in doubt, there is a Dukkaṭa offense. In the case of a requisite not given for another purpose, if she is perceptive that it was not given for another purpose, there is no offense.

762. Anāpatti [T 0.0080] sesakaṃ upaneti, sāmike apaloketvā upaneti, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

762. There is no offense if one applies the remainder; if one applies it after informing the owners; in times of calamity; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Sixth Training Rule is concluded.

7. Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Seventh Training Rule

763. Tena [M 0.0329] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena upāsakā bhikkhunisaṅghassa cīvaratthāya chandakaṃ saṅgharitvā aññatarassa pāvārikassa ghare parikkhāraṃ nikkhipitvā [P 4.0252] bhikkhuniyo upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – “amukassa, ayye, pāvārikassa ghare cīvaratthāya parikkhāro nikkhitto, tato cīvaraṃ āharāpetvā bhājethā”ti. Bhikkhuniyo tena ca parikkhārena sayampi yācitvā bhesajjaṃ cetāpetvā paribhuñjiṃsu. Upāsakā jānitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena saṅghikena saññācikena aññaṃ cetāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena saṅghikena saññācikena aññaṃ cetāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi [T 0.0081] buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena saṅghikena saññācikena aññaṃ cetāpessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

763. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, at the Jeta Grove, in the park of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, lay followers, having collected contributions for the purpose of robes for the community of bhikkhunīs and having deposited the allowable funds in the house of a certain cloth-weaver, approached the bhikkhunīs and said this: ‘Venerable ladies, allowable funds for the purpose of robes have been deposited in the house of the cloth-weaver of such-and-such a name. From there, having had robes brought, please distribute them.’ The bhikkhunīs, with those allowable funds and also with funds they had requested themselves, had medicine procured and used it. The lay followers, having learned of this, criticized, censured, and spread it about, saying: ‘How indeed can the bhikkhunīs, with allowable funds given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, and belonging to the Saṅgha, and with funds requested by oneself, have another thing procured?’ … ‘Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunīs, with allowable funds given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, and belonging to the Saṅgha, and with funds requested by oneself, have another thing procured?’ ‘It is true, Blessed One.’ The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… ‘How indeed, monks, can the bhikkhunīs, with allowable funds given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, and belonging to the Saṅgha, and with funds requested by oneself, have another thing procured? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule in this way:

764. “Yā pana bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena saṅghikena saññācikena aññaṃ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiya”nti.

764. “Whatever bhikkhunī, with allowable funds given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, and belonging to the Saṅgha, and with funds requested by oneself, should have another thing procured, it is a Pācittiya offense entailing forfeiture.”

765. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

765. ‘Whatever’: whichever, of whatever kind… ‘bhikkhunī’: … this is the bhikkhunī intended in this sense.

Aññadatthikena [V 0.0342] parikkhārena aññuddisikenāti aññassatthāya dinnena.

‘With allowable funds given for another purpose, designated for another purpose’: means given for the purpose of another thing.

Saṅghikenāti saṅghassa, na gaṇassa, na ekabhikkhuniyā.

‘Belonging to the Saṅgha’: means relinquished to the Saṅgha, not to a group, not to a single bhikkhunī.

Saññācikenāti sayaṃ yācitvā.

‘Requested by oneself’: means having requested it oneself.

Aññaṃ cetāpeyyāti yaṃatthāya dinnaṃ taṃ ṭhapetvā aññaṃ cetāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Nissajjitabbaṃ saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā ekabhikkhuniyā vā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, nissajjitabbaṃ…pe… “idaṃ me, ayye, aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena [M 0.0330] saṅghikena saññācikena aññaṃ cetāpitaṃ nissaggiyaṃ, imāhaṃ saṅghassa nissajjāmī”ti…pe… dadeyyāti…pe… dadeyyunti…pe… ayyāya dammīti.

‘Should have another thing procured’: means, setting aside that for the purpose of which it was given, one has another thing procured. In the effort, there is a Dukkaṭa offense. Upon acquisition, it becomes subject to forfeiture. It is to be forfeited to the Saṅgha, or to a group, or to a single bhikkhunī. And so, monks, it should be forfeited in this way... ‘Venerable ladies, this item of mine, having been procured as another thing with allowable funds given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, and belonging to the Saṅgha, and with funds requested by oneself, is subject to forfeiture. I forfeit this to the Saṅgha.’ ... It should be given... They should be given... ‘I give it to the venerable lady.’

766. Aññadatthike aññadatthikasaññā aññaṃ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Aññadatthike vematikā aññaṃ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Aññadatthike anaññadatthikasaññā aññaṃ cetāpeti[T 0.0082], nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Nissaṭṭhaṃ paṭilabhitvā yathādāne upanetabbaṃ.

766. In the case of a requisite given for another purpose, if she is perceptive that it was given for another purpose and has another thing procured, it is a Pācittiya offense entailing forfeiture. In the case of a requisite given for another purpose, if she is in doubt and has another thing procured, it is a Pācittiya offense entailing forfeiture. In the case of a requisite given for another purpose, if she is perceptive that it was not given for another purpose and has another thing procured, it is a Pācittiya offense entailing forfeiture. Having received back what was forfeited, it should be applied in accordance with the original donation.

Anaññadatthike aññadatthikasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anaññadatthike vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anaññadatthike anaññadatthikasaññā, anāpatti.

In the case of a requisite not given for another purpose, if she is perceptive that it was given for another purpose, there is a Dukkaṭa offense. In the case of a requisite not given for another purpose, if she is in doubt, there is a Dukkaṭa offense. In the case of a requisite not given for another purpose, if she is perceptive that it was not given for another purpose, there is no offense.

767. Anāpatti sesakaṃ upaneti, sāmike apaloketvā upaneti, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

767. There is no offense if she applies the remainder; if she applies it after informing the owners; in times of danger; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Seventh Training Rule is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Eighth Training Rule

768. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa pūgassa pariveṇavāsikā bhikkhuniyo yāguyā kilamanti. Atha kho so pūgo bhikkhunīnaṃ yāguatthāya chandakaṃ saṅgharitvā aññatarassa āpaṇikassa [V 0.0343] ghare parikkhāraṃ nikkhipitvā bhikkhuniyo upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – “amukassa, ayye, āpaṇikassa ghare yāguatthāya parikkhāro nikkhitto, tato taṇḍulaṃ āharāpetvā yāguṃ pacāpetvā paribhuñjathā”ti. Bhikkhuniyo tena parikkhārena bhesajjaṃ cetāpetvā paribhuñjiṃsu. So pūgo jānitvā ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena mahājanikena aññaṃ cetāpessantī”ti…pe… [T 0.0083] saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena mahājanikena [M 0.0331] aññaṃ cetāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti[P 4.0253]. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena mahājanikena aññaṃ cetāpessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

768. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs residing in the monastic compound of a certain association were in distress for want of rice-gruel. Then that association, having collected contributions for the purpose of rice-gruel for the bhikkhunīs and having deposited the allowable articles at the house of a certain shopkeeper, approached the bhikkhunīs and said this: 'Venerable Ladies, at the house of such-and-such a shopkeeper, allowable articles for the purpose of rice-gruel have been deposited. From there, having had rice brought and having had rice-gruel cooked, you should partake of it.' The bhikkhunīs, with those allowable articles, had medicine procured in exchange and partook of it. That association, having learned of this, complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: 'How indeed could the bhikkhunīs have another thing procured in exchange with allowable articles given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, and belonging to a group?' … 'Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunīs have another thing procured in exchange with allowable articles given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, and belonging to a group?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… 'How indeed, Bhikkhus, could the bhikkhunīs have another thing procured in exchange with allowable articles given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, and belonging to a group? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced…' 'And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:'

769. “Yā pana bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena mahājanikena aññaṃ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiya”nti.

769. Whatever bhikkhunī should have another thing procured in exchange with allowable articles given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, and belonging to a group, it is a Pācittiya offense that entails forfeiture.

770. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

770. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever, of whatever kind... ‘Bhikkhunī’ means... in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikenāti aññassatthāya dinnena.

‘With allowable articles given for another purpose, designated for another purpose’ means: given for the purpose of another thing.

Mahājanikenāti gaṇassa, na saṅghassa, na ekabhikkhuniyā.

‘Belonging to a group’ means: for a group, not for the Saṅgha, not for a single bhikkhunī.

Aññaṃ cetāpeyyāti yaṃatthāya dinnaṃ taṃ ṭhapetvā aññaṃ cetāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Nissajjitabbaṃ saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā ekabhikkhuniyā vā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, nissajjitabbaṃ…pe… “idaṃ me, ayye, aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena mahājanikena aññaṃ cetāpitaṃ nissaggiyaṃ imāhaṃ saṅghassa nissajjāmī”ti…pe… dadeyyāti…pe… dadeyyunti…pe… ayyāya dammīti.

‘Has another thing procured in exchange’ means: setting aside that for the purpose of which it was given, one has another thing procured in exchange; in the effort, there is a Dukkaṭa offense. Upon acquisition, it becomes subject to forfeiture. It is to be forfeited to the Saṅgha, or to a group, or to a single bhikkhunī. And so, Bhikkhus, it is to be forfeited thus… ‘Venerable Ladies, this item of mine, procured with allowable articles that were given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, and belonging to a group, is to be forfeited. I forfeit this to the Saṅgha.’ … It should be given… They should give… ‘I give it to the Venerable Lady.’

771. Aññadatthike [T 0.0084] aññadatthikasaññā aññaṃ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Aññadatthike vematikā aññaṃ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Aññadatthike anaññadatthikasaññā [V 0.0344] aññaṃ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Nissaṭṭhaṃ paṭilabhitvā yathādāne upanetabbaṃ.

771. In the case of an article given for another purpose, if one is perceptive that it was given for another purpose and has another thing procured in exchange, it is a Pācittiya offense that entails forfeiture. In the case of an article given for another purpose, if one is doubtful and has another thing procured in exchange, it is a Pācittiya offense that entails forfeiture. In the case of an article given for another purpose, if one is perceptive that it was not given for another purpose and has another thing procured in exchange, it is a Pācittiya offense that entails forfeiture. Having received back the forfeited item, it should be applied according to the original donation.

Anaññadatthike aññadatthikasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anaññadatthike vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anaññadatthike anaññadatthikasaññā, anāpatti.

In the case of an article not given for another purpose, if one is perceptive that it was given for another purpose, there is an offense of Dukkaṭa. In the case of an article not given for another purpose, if one is doubtful, there is an offense of Dukkaṭa. In the case of an article not given for another purpose, if one is perceptive that it was not given for another purpose, there is no offense.

772. Anāpatti sesakaṃ upaneti, sāmike apaloketvā upaneti, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

772. There is no offense if one applies the remainder; if one applies it after informing the owners; in times of adversity; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Eighth Training Rule is concluded.

9. Navamasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Ninth Training Rule

773. Tena [M 0.0332] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa pūgassa pariveṇavāsikā bhikkhuniyo yāguyā kilamanti. Atha kho so pūgo bhikkhunīnaṃ yāguatthāya chandakaṃ saṅgharitvā aññatarassa āpaṇikassa ghare parikkhāraṃ nikkhipitvā bhikkhuniyo upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – “amukassa, ayye, āpaṇikassa ghare yāguatthāya parikkhāro nikkhitto. Tato taṇḍule āharāpetvā yāguṃ pacāpetvā paribhuñjathā”ti. Bhikkhuniyo tena ca parikkhārena sayampi yācitvā bhesajjaṃ cetāpetvā paribhuñjiṃsu. So pūgo jānitvā ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi [T 0.0085] nāma bhikkhuniyo aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena mahājanikena saññācikena aññaṃ cetāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena mahājanikena saññācikena aññaṃ cetāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena mahājanikena saññācikena aññaṃ cetāpessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

773. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs residing in the monastic compound of a certain association were having difficulty on account of rice-gruel. Then that association, having collected contributions for the purpose of rice-gruel for the bhikkhunīs and having deposited the allowable articles at the house of a certain shopkeeper, approached the bhikkhunīs and said this: 'Venerable ladies, at the house of such-and-such a shopkeeper, allowable articles for the purpose of rice-gruel have been deposited. From there, having caused rice to be brought and having caused rice-gruel to be cooked, you should consume it.' The bhikkhunīs, using those allowable articles and also others obtained by their own request, had medicine procured in exchange and partook of it. That association, having learned of this, complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: 'How indeed could the bhikkhunīs, with allowable articles given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, belonging to a group, and obtained by personal request, have another thing procured in exchange?' … 'Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunīs, with allowable articles given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, belonging to a group, and obtained by personal request, are having another thing procured in exchange?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… 'How indeed, monks, could the bhikkhunīs, with allowable articles given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, belonging to a group, and obtained by personal request, have another thing procured in exchange? Monks, this is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

774. “Yā pana bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena mahājanikena saññācikena aññaṃ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiya”nti.

774. ‘Whatever bhikkhunī, with allowable articles given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, belonging to a group, or obtained by personal request, should have another thing procured in exchange, it is a Pācittiya offense entailing forfeiture.’

775. Yā [V 0.0345] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

775. ‘Whatever’ means: whichever, of whatever sort… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikenāti aññassatthāya dinnena.

‘With allowable articles given for another purpose, designated for another purpose’ means: given for the purpose of another thing.

Mahājanikenāti gaṇassa, na saṅghassa, na ekabhikkhuniyā.

‘Belonging to a group’ means: for a group, not for the Saṅgha, and not for a single bhikkhunī.

Saññācikenāti sayaṃ yācitvā.

‘Obtained by personal request’ means: having requested it oneself.

Aññaṃ cetāpeyyāti yaṃatthāya dinnaṃ taṃ ṭhapetvā aññaṃ cetāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Nissajjitabbaṃ [T 0.0086] saṅghassa vā [M 0.0333] gaṇassa vā ekabhikkhuniyā vā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, nissajjitabbaṃ…pe… “idaṃ me, ayye, aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena mahājanikena saññācikena aññaṃ cetāpitaṃ nissaggiyaṃ. Imāhaṃ saṅghassa nissajjāmī”ti…pe… dadeyyāti…pe… dadeyyunti…pe… ayyāya dammīti.

‘Should have another thing exchanged’ means: setting aside that for the purpose of which it was given, one has another thing exchanged. In the effort, there is a dukkaṭa offense. Upon acquisition, it becomes subject to forfeiture. It is to be forfeited to the Saṅgha, or to a group, or to a single bhikkhunī. And so, Bhikkhus, it should be forfeited thus… ‘Venerable ladies, this item of mine, having been acquired by exchange using requisites given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, belonging to a group, or obtained by personal request, is subject to forfeiture. I forfeit this to the Saṅgha.’ … One should give… They should give… ‘I give to the venerable lady.’

776. Aññadatthike aññadatthikasaññā aññaṃ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Aññadatthike vematikā aññaṃ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Aññadatthike anaññadatthikasaññā aññaṃ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Nissaṭṭhaṃ paṭilabhitvā yathādāne upanetabbaṃ.

776. In the case of something given for another purpose, if one, perceiving it as given for another purpose, has another thing exchanged for it, it is a pācittiya offense entailing forfeiture. In the case of something given for another purpose, if one, being uncertain, has another thing exchanged for it, it is a pācittiya offense entailing forfeiture. In the case of something given for another purpose, if one, perceiving it as not given for another purpose, has another thing exchanged for it, it is a pācittiya offense entailing forfeiture. Having received back what was forfeited, it should be applied as originally given.

Anaññadatthike aññadatthikasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anaññadatthike vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anaññadatthike anaññadatthikasaññā anāpatti.

In the case of something not given for another purpose, if one perceives it as given for another purpose, there is a dukkaṭa offense. In the case of something not given for another purpose, if one is uncertain, there is a dukkaṭa offense. In the case of something not given for another purpose, if one perceives it as not given for another purpose, there is no offense.

777. Anāpatti sesakaṃ upaneti, sāmike apaloketvā upaneti, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

777. There is no offense if one uses the remainder; if one uses it after informing the owners; in times of adversity; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Navamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Ninth Training Rule is concluded.

10. Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Tenth Training Rule

778. Tena [P 4.0254][V 0.0346] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī bahussutā hoti bhāṇikā visāradā paṭṭā dhammiṃ kathaṃ kātuṃ. Bahū manussā thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ payirupāsanti. Tena kho pana samayena [T 0.0087] thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā pariveṇaṃ undriyati udrīyati (syā.). Manussā thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavocuṃ – “kissidaṃ te, ayye, pariveṇaṃ undriyatī”ti? “Natthāvuso, dāyakā, natthi kārakā”ti. Atha kho te manussā thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā pariveṇatthāya chandakaṃ saṅgharitvā thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā parikkhāraṃ adaṃsu. Thullanandā bhikkhunī tena ca parikkhārena sayampi yācitvā bhesajjaṃ cetāpetvā paribhuñji. Manussā jānitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena puggalikena saññācikena aññaṃ cetāpessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ [M 0.0334] kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena puggalikena saññācikena aññaṃ cetāpetīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena puggalikena saññācikena aññaṃ cetāpessati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

778. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā was learned, a reciter, confident, and skilled in giving a Dhamma talk. Many people attended upon the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. At that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā’s dwelling was in disrepair. People said this to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā: “Venerable lady, why is this dwelling of yours in disrepair?” “Friends, there are no donors, there are no workers.” Then those people, having collected contributions for the bhikkhunī Thullanandā’s dwelling, gave requisites to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, using those requisites and also what she had requested herself, had medicine obtained by exchange and used it. People, having found out, complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed could the venerable lady Thullanandā have something else exchanged with requisites that were given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, given to an individual, and obtained by request?” … “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā had something else exchanged with requisites that were given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, given to an individual, and obtained by request?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā have something else exchanged with requisites that were given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, given to an individual, and obtained by request? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

779. “Yā pana bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena puggalikena saññācikena aññaṃ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiya”nti.

779. “Whatever bhikkhunī should have something else exchanged with requisites that were given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, given to an individual, or obtained by request, it is a pācittiya offense entailing forfeiture.”

780. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

780. ‘Whatever’ means: whichever of whatever kind…pe… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means…pe… in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikenāti [T 0.0088] aññassatthāya dinnena.

‘With requisites given for another purpose, designated for another purpose’ means: given for the sake of another thing.

Puggalikenāti ekāya bhikkhuniyā, na saṅghassa, na gaṇassa.

‘Given to an individual’ means: given to one bhikkhunī, not to the Saṅgha, not to a group.

Saññācikenāti sayaṃ yācitvā.

‘Obtained by request’ means: having requested it oneself.

Aññaṃ [V 0.0347] cetāpeyyāti yaṃatthāya dinnaṃ taṃ ṭhapetvā aññaṃ cetāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Nissajjitabbaṃ saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā ekabhikkhuniyā vā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, nissajjitabbaṃ…pe… “idaṃ me, ayye, aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena puggalikena saññācikena aññaṃ cetāpitaṃ nissaggiyaṃ, imāhaṃ saṅghassa nissajjāmī”ti…pe… dadeyyāti…pe… dadeyyunti…pe… ayyāya dammīti.

‘Should have something else exchanged’ means: setting aside that for the sake of which it was given, she has something else exchanged. In the effort, there is a dukkaṭa offense. Upon acquisition, it becomes subject to forfeiture. It is to be forfeited to the Saṅgha, or to a group, or to a single bhikkhunī. And so, Bhikkhus, it is to be forfeited thus... ‘Venerable ladies, this item of mine, acquired by exchange using requisites that were given for another purpose, designated for another purpose, given to an individual, or obtained by request, is subject to forfeiture. I forfeit this to the Saṅgha.’ ... (The Saṅgha) should give... (They) should give... ‘I give it to the venerable lady.’

781. Aññadatthike aññadatthikasaññā aññaṃ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Aññadatthike vematikā aññaṃ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Aññadatthike anaññadatthikasaññā aññaṃ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Nissaṭṭhaṃ paṭilabhitvā yathādāne upanetabbaṃ.

781. Regarding an item given for another purpose, if she perceives it as given for another purpose and has something else exchanged, it is a pācittiya offense entailing forfeiture. Regarding an item given for another purpose, if she is in doubt and has something else exchanged, it is a pācittiya offense entailing forfeiture. Regarding an item given for another purpose, if she perceives it as not given for another purpose and has something else exchanged, it is a pācittiya offense entailing forfeiture. Having received back what was forfeited, it should be applied according to the original donation.

Anaññadatthike aññadatthikasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anaññadatthike vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anaññadatthike anaññadatthikasaññā, anāpatti.

Regarding an item not given for another purpose, if she perceives it as given for another purpose and has it exchanged, there is a dukkaṭa offense. Regarding an item not given for another purpose, if she is in doubt and has it exchanged, there is a dukkaṭa offense. Regarding an item not given for another purpose, if she perceives it as not given for another purpose and has it exchanged, there is no offense.

782. Anāpatti sesakaṃ upaneti, sāmike apaloketvā upaneti, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

782. There is no offense: if she uses the remainder; if she uses it after informing the owners; in times of adversity; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Tenth Training Rule is concluded.

11. Ekādasamasikkhāpadaṃ

11. The Eleventh Training Rule

783. Tena [T 0.0089][P 4.0255][M 0.0335] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī bahussutā hoti bhāṇikā visāradā paṭṭā dhammiṃ kathaṃ kātuṃ. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo sītakāle mahagghaṃ kambalaṃ pārupitvā yena thullanandā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ thullanandā bhikkhunī dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “vadeyyāsi, ayye, yena attho”ti? “Sace me tvaṃ, mahārāja, dātukāmosi, imaṃ kambalaṃ dehī”ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi [V 0.0348] kosalo thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā kambalaṃ datvā uṭṭhāyāsanā thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “mahicchā imā bhikkhuniyo asantuṭṭhā. Kathañhi nāma rājānaṃ kambalaṃ viññāpessantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā [T 0.0090] rājānaṃ kambalaṃ viññāpessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī rājānaṃ kambalaṃ viññāpetīti viññāpesīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī rājānaṃ kambalaṃ viññāpessati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

783. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time the bhikkhunī Thullanandā was learned, a good speaker, confident, and proficient in giving a Dhamma talk. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala, wearing an expensive blanket in the cold season, approached the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. Having approached, he paid homage to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā and sat down to one side. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā then instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened King Pasenadi of Kosala with a Dhamma talk as he sat to one side. Then, having been instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened by the bhikkhunī Thullanandā’s Dhamma talk, King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā: “Venerable lady, please say what you need.” “Great king, if you wish to give me something, then give me this blanket.” Then King Pasenadi of Kosala gave the blanket to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, rose from his seat, paid homage to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, circumambulated her respectfully, and departed. People complained, criticized, and found fault, saying: “These bhikkhunīs have great desires and are discontented. How can they ask the king for a blanket?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and finding fault. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires … complained, criticized, and found fault, saying: “How can the venerable Thullanandā ask the king for a blanket?” … “Is it true, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā asked the king for a blanket?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her … “How can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā ask the king for a blanket? This will not lead to confidence in those who are unconvinced …” … “And so, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

784. “Garupāvuraṇaṃ pāpuraṇaṃ (sī. syā.) pana bhikkhuniyā cetāpentiyā catukkaṃsaparamaṃ cetāpetabbaṃ. Tato ce uttari cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiya”nti.

784. “A bhikkhunī procuring a heavy covering may procure one worth four kaṃsas at most. If she procures one exceeding that, it is an offense of pācittiya entailing forfeiture.”

785. Garupāvuraṇaṃ [M 0.0336] nāma yaṃ kiñci sītakāle pāvuraṇaṃ.

785. A heavy covering: any covering for the cold season.

Cetāpentiyāti viññāpentiyā.

‘Procuring’ means ‘requesting’.

Catukkaṃsaparamaṃ [P 4.0256] cetāpetabbanti soḷasakahāpaṇagghanakaṃ cetāpetabbaṃ.

‘One worth four kaṃsas at most may be procured’ means one worth sixteen kahāpaṇas may be procured.

Tato ce uttari cetāpeyyāti tatuttari viññāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Nissajjitabbaṃ saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā ekabhikkhuniyā vā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, nissajjitabbaṃ…pe… “idaṃ me, ayye, garupāvuraṇaṃ atirekacatukkaṃsaparamaṃ cetāpitaṃ nissaggiyaṃ, imāhaṃ saṅghassa nissajjāmī”ti…pe… dadeyyāti…pe… dadeyyunti…pe… ayyāya dammīti.

‘If she should procure one exceeding that’: if she requests one exceeding that, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the effort. Upon receiving it, it becomes subject to forfeiture. It is to be forfeited to the Saṅgha, to a group, or to a single bhikkhunī. And, bhikkhus, it should be forfeited thus: … “Venerable ladies, this heavy covering of mine, procured in excess of the four-kaṃsa limit, is subject to forfeiture. I forfeit this to the Saṅgha.” … it should be given … they should give … “I give it to the venerable lady.”

786. Atirekacatukkaṃse atirekasaññā cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Atirekacatukkaṃse vematikā cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ[T 0.0091]. Atirekacatukkaṃse ūnakasaññā cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

786. If she procures one worth more than four kaṃsas, perceiving it as worth more, it is an offense of pācittiya entailing forfeiture. If she procures one worth more than four kaṃsas, being in doubt, it is an offense of pācittiya entailing forfeiture. If she procures one worth more than four kaṃsas, perceiving it as worth less, it is an offense of pācittiya entailing forfeiture.

Ūnakacatukkaṃse [V 0.0349] atirekasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ūnakacatukkaṃse vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ūnakacatukkaṃse ūnakasaññā, anāpatti.

If she procures one worth less than four kaṃsas, perceiving it as worth more, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she procures one worth less than four kaṃsas, being in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she procures one worth less than four kaṃsas, perceiving it as worth less, there is no offense.

787. Anāpatti catukkaṃsaparamaṃ cetāpeti, ūnakacatukkaṃsaparamaṃ cetāpeti, ñātakānaṃ, pavāritānaṃ, aññassatthāya, attano dhanena, mahagghaṃ cetāpetukāmassa appagghaṃ cetāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

787. There is no offense: if one procures one worth up to four kaṃsas; if one procures one worth less than four kaṃsas; if it is from relatives; from those who have made an invitation; for the sake of another; with one’s own wealth; if, when a donor wishes to give an expensive one, she requests an inexpensive one; if one is insane; or if one is the first offender.

Ekādasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Eleventh Training Rule is concluded.

12. Dvādasamasikkhāpadaṃ

12. The Twelfth Training Rule

788. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī bahussutā hoti bhāṇikā visāradā paṭṭā dhammiṃ kathaṃ kātuṃ. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo uṇhakāle mahagghaṃ khomaṃ pārupitvā yena thullanandā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā thullanandaṃ [M 0.0337] bhikkhuniṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ thullanandā bhikkhunī dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “vadeyyāsi, ayye, yena attho”ti[T 0.0092]. “Sace me tvaṃ, mahārāja, dātukāmosi, imaṃ khomaṃ dehī”ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā khomaṃ datvā uṭṭhāyāsanā thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “mahicchā imā bhikkhuniyo asantuṭṭhā. Kathañhi nāma rājānaṃ khomaṃ viññāpessantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā rājānaṃ khomaṃ viññāpessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī rājānaṃ khomaṃ viññāpetīti viññāpesīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavāti”. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī rājānaṃ khomaṃ viññāpessati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

788. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā was learned, a skilled speaker, self-assured, and adept at giving a Dhamma talk. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala, wearing an expensive linen cloak in the hot season, approached the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. Having approached, he paid homage to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā and sat down to one side. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā instructed, roused, encouraged, and gladdened King Pasenadi of Kosala, who was seated to one side, with a Dhamma talk. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala, having been instructed, roused, encouraged, and gladdened by the bhikkhunī Thullanandā’s Dhamma talk, said to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā: “Venerable lady, please say what you need.” “Great king, if you wish to give to me, give me this linen cloak.” Then King Pasenadi of Kosala gave the linen cloak to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, rose from his seat, paid homage to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, circumambulated her keeping her to his right, and departed. People complained, criticized, and spread it about: “These bhikkhunīs have great desires and are not content. How could they ask the king for a linen cloak?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How could the venerable Thullanandā ask the king for a linen cloak?”… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā asked the king for a linen cloak?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Blessed One, the Buddha, rebuked her… “How, bhikkhus, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā ask the king for a linen cloak? This, bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

789. “Lahupāvuraṇaṃ [V 0.0350] pana bhikkhuniyā cetāpentiyā aḍḍhateyyakaṃsaparamaṃ cetāpetabbaṃ. Tato ce uttari cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiya”nti.

789. “A bhikkhunī asking for a light cloak may ask for one worth at most two and a half kaṃsas. If she asks for more than that, it is an offense of pācittiya that entails forfeiture.”

790. Lahupāvuraṇaṃ nāma yaṃ kiñci uṇhakāle pāvuraṇaṃ.

790. A light cloak means any cloak for the hot season.

Cetāpentiyāti viññāpentiyā.

‘Asking for’ means making one’s need known.

Aḍḍhateyyakaṃsaparamaṃ cetāpetabbanti dasakahāpaṇagghanakaṃ cetāpetabbaṃ.

‘May be asked for with a maximum value of two and a half kaṃsas’ means one worth ten kahāpaṇas may be asked for.

Tato ce uttari cetāpeyyāti tatuttari viññāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Nissajjitabbaṃ [T 0.0093] saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā ekabhikkhuniyā vā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, nissajjitabbaṃ…pe… idaṃ me, ayye, lahupāvuraṇaṃ atirekaaḍḍhateyyakaṃsaparamaṃ cetāpitaṃ nissaggiyaṃ, imāhaṃ [M 0.0338] saṅghassa nissajjāmīti…pe… dadeyyāti…pe… dadeyyunti…pe… ayyāya dammīti.

‘If she asks for more than that’ means if she makes known her wish for more than that, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the effort. Upon obtaining it, it is to be forfeited. It should be forfeited to the Saṅgha, to a group, or to a single bhikkhunī. And so, bhikkhus, it should be forfeited… “Venerable ladies, this light cloak of mine, having been asked for in excess of two and a half kaṃsas, is to be forfeited. I forfeit this to the Saṅgha.”… “should give”… “they should give”… “I give this to the venerable lady.”

791. Atirekaaḍḍhateyyakaṃse atirekasaññā cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Atirekaaḍḍhateyyakaṃse vematikā cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Atirekaaḍḍhateyyakaṃse ūnakasaññā cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

791. If she asks for something exceeding two and a half kaṃsas, perceiving it as exceeding, it is an offense of pācittiya that entails forfeiture. If she asks for something exceeding two and a half kaṃsas, being in doubt, it is an offense of pācittiya that entails forfeiture. If she asks for something exceeding two and a half kaṃsas, perceiving it as less, it is an offense of pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Ūnakaaḍḍhateyyakaṃse atirekasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ūnakaaḍḍhateyyakaṃse vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ūnakaaḍḍhateyyakaṃse ūnakasaññā[P 4.0257], anāpatti.

If she asks for something less than two and a half kaṃsas, perceiving it as exceeding, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she asks for something less than two and a half kaṃsas, being in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she asks for something less than two and a half kaṃsas, perceiving it as less, there is no offense.

792. Anāpatti aḍḍhateyyakaṃsaparamaṃ cetāpeti, ūnakaaḍḍhateyyakaṃsaparamaṃ cetāpeti, ñātakānaṃ, pavāritānaṃ, aññassatthāya, attano dhanena, mahagghaṃ cetāpetukāmassa appagghaṃ cetāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

792. There is no offense: if she asks for one worth at most two and a half kaṃsas; if she asks for one worth less than two and a half kaṃsas; if she asks relatives or those who have invited her; if it is for the sake of another; if it is with her own wealth; if, from someone who wishes to give an expensive item, she asks for an inexpensive one; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Dvādasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Twelfth Training Rule is concluded.

Uddiṭṭhā kho, ayyāyo, tiṃsa nissaggiyā pācittiyā dhammā. Tatthāyyāyo pucchāmi – “kaccittha [V 0.0351] parisuddhā”? Dutiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Tatiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Parisuddhetthāyyāyo, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti.

Venerable ladies, the thirty rules of pācittiya that entail forfeiture have been recited. In that regard, I ask the venerable ladies: “Are you pure in this?” A second time I ask: “Are you pure in this?” A third time I ask: “Are you pure in this?” The venerable ladies are pure in this, therefore they are silent. Thus I take it.

Bhikkhunivibhaṅge nissaggiyakaṇḍaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

In the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga, the Nissaggiya Section is concluded.

4. Pācittiyakaṇḍaṃ (bhikkhunīvibhaṅgo)

4. The Section on Pācittiya

1. Lasuṇavaggo

1. The Chapter on Garlic

1. Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The First Training Rule

Ime kho panāyyāyo chasaṭṭhisatā pācittiyā

Venerable ladies, there are these one hundred and sixty-six pācittiya rules

Dhammā uddesaṃ āgacchanti.

which come up for recitation.

793. Tena [T 0.0094][P 4.0258][M 0.0339][V 0.0352] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarena upāsakena bhikkhunisaṅgho lasuṇena pavārito hoti – “yāsaṃ ayyānaṃ lasuṇena attho, ahaṃ lasuṇenā”ti. Khettapālo ca āṇatto hoti – “sace bhikkhuniyo āgacchanti, ekamekāya bhikkhuniyā dvetayo bhaṇḍike dehī”ti. Tena kho pana samayena sāvatthiyaṃ ussavo hoti. Yathābhataṃ lasuṇaṃ parikkhayaṃ agamāsi. Bhikkhuniyo taṃ upāsakaṃ upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – “lasuṇena, āvuso, attho”ti. “Natthāyye. Yathābhataṃ lasuṇaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ. Khettaṃ gacchathā”ti. Thullanandā bhikkhunī khettaṃ gantvā na mattaṃ jānitvā bahuṃ lasuṇaṃ harāpesi. Khettapālo ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo na mattaṃ jānitvā bahuṃ lasuṇaṃ harāpessantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tassa khettapālassa ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti [T 0.0095] vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā na mattaṃ jānitvā bahuṃ lasuṇaṃ harāpessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī na mattaṃ jānitvā bahuṃ lasuṇaṃ harāpetīti harāpesīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī na [V 0.0353] mattaṃ jānitvā bahuṃ lasuṇaṃ harāpessati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

793. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, a certain lay follower had invited the community of bhikkhunīs with an offer of garlic, saying: “Whichever venerable ladies have need of garlic, I invite them with garlic.” And the field-keeper was instructed thus: “If bhikkhunīs come, give two or three bundles to each and every bhikkhunī.” Now at that time, there was a festival in Sāvatthī. The garlic that had been brought was exhausted. The bhikkhunīs, having approached that lay follower, said this: “Friend, garlic is needed.” He said: “There is none, venerable ladies. The garlic that was brought is exhausted. Go to the field.” The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having gone to the field and not knowing the proper measure, had much garlic taken. The field-keeper complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs, not knowing the proper measure, have much garlic taken?” The bhikkhunīs heard that field-keeper complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the venerable Thullanandā, not knowing the proper measure, have much garlic taken?” … “Is it true, it is said, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, not knowing the proper measure, had much garlic taken?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, bhikkhus, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, not knowing the proper measure, have much garlic taken? This, bhikkhus, is not for inspiring confidence in the uninspired… Having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus:

“Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī aññatarassa brāhmaṇassa pajāpati ahosi. Tisso [P 4.0259] ca dhītaro – nandā, nandavatī, sundarīnandā. Atha kho, bhikkhave, so brāhmaṇo kālaṅkatvā aññataraṃ haṃsayoniṃ upapajji. Tassa sabbasovaṇṇamayā pattā ahesuṃ. So tāsaṃ ekekaṃ pattaṃ deti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī “ayaṃ [M 0.0340] haṃso amhākaṃ ekekaṃ pattaṃ detī”ti taṃ haṃsarājaṃ gahetvā nippattaṃ akāsi. Tassa puna jāyamānā pattā setā sampajjiṃsu. Tadāpi, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī atilobhena suvaṇṇā parihīnā. Idāni lasuṇā parihāyissatī”ti.

“Once upon a time, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā was the wife of a certain brahmin. And there were three daughters: Nandā, Nandavatī, and Sundarīnandā. Then, bhikkhus, that brahmin, having passed away, was reborn as a swan. His feathers were made entirely of gold. He would give one feather to each of them. Then, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, thinking, ‘This swan gives us one feather each,’ seized that swan-king and made him featherless. The feathers that grew on him again were white. At that time also, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, through excessive greed, was deprived of gold. Now she will be deprived of garlic.”

jā. 1.1.136 suvaṇṇahaṃsajātakepi “Yaṃ [T 0.0096] laddhaṃ tena tuṭṭhabbaṃ, atilobho hi pāpako;

Haṃsarājaṃ gahetvāna, suvaṇṇā parihāyathā”ti.

“One should be content with what is obtained, for excessive greed is indeed evil. Having seized the swan-king, you were deprived of gold.”

Atha kho bhagavā thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā dubbharatāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

Then the Blessed One, having rebuked the bhikkhunī Thullanandā in many ways for being difficult to support… said: “And so, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

794. “Yā pana bhikkhunī lasuṇaṃ khādeyya pācittiya”nti.

794. “Whatever bhikkhunī should eat garlic, it is an offense entailing confession.”

795. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

795. Whatever means: whichever, of whatever kind… Bhikkhunī means: …in this sense, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Lasuṇaṃ nāma māgadhakaṃ vuccati.

Garlic means that of Magadha.

“Khādissāmīti paṭiggaṇhā”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

If she accepts it thinking, “I will eat it,” it is an offense of wrong-doing. With every swallow, it is an offense entailing confession.

796. Lasuṇe lasuṇasaññā khādati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Lasuṇe vematikā khādati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Lasuṇe alasuṇasaññā khādati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

796. If she eats garlic, perceiving it as garlic, it is an offense entailing confession. If she eats garlic while being uncertain, it is an offense entailing confession. If she eats garlic, perceiving it as not garlic, it is an offense entailing confession.

Alasuṇe [V 0.0354] lasuṇasaññā khādati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Alasuṇe vematikā khādati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Alasuṇe alasuṇasaññā khādati, anāpatti.

If she eats what is not garlic, perceiving it as garlic, it is an offense of wrong-doing. If she eats what is not garlic while being uncertain, it is an offense of wrong-doing. If she eats what is not garlic, perceiving it as not garlic, there is no offense.

797. Anāpatti palaṇḍuke, bhañjanake, harītake, cāpalasuṇe, sūpasampāke, maṃsasampāke, telasampāke, sāḷave, uttaribhaṅge, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

797. There is no offense for palaṇḍuka, bhañjanaka, harītaka, or cāpalasuṇa; nor for garlic used in preparing soup, in preparing meat, in preparing oil, in sāḷava, or in uttaribhaṅga; nor for one who is insane, nor for the first offender.

Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The First Training Rule is finished.

2. Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Second Training Rule

798. Tena [T 0.0097][M 0.0341] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo sambādhe lomaṃ saṃharāpetvā aciravatiyā nadiyā vesiyāhi saddhiṃ naggā ekatitthe [P 4.0260] nahāyanti. Vesiyā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo sambādhe lomaṃ saṃharāpessanti, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tāsaṃ vesiyānaṃ ujjhāyantīnaṃ khiyyantīnaṃ vipācentīnaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo sambādhe lomaṃ saṃharāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo sambādhe lomaṃ saṃharāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo sambādhe lomaṃ saṃharāpessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

798. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs of the group-of-six, having had hair removed from a confined place, were bathing naked together with prostitutes at a single ford in the river Aciravatī. The prostitutes complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs have hair removed from a confined place, just like female householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” The bhikkhunīs heard those prostitutes complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about.
