Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the bhikkhunīs of the group-of-six have hair removed from a confined place?”… “Is it true, it is said, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunīs of the group-of-six have hair removed from a confined place?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, bhikkhus, can the bhikkhunīs of the group-of-six have hair removed from a confined place? This, bhikkhus, is not for inspiring confidence in the uninspired, nor for the increase of confidence in the inspired… And thus, bhikkhus, let the bhikkhunīs set forth this training rule:

799. “Yā pana bhikkhunī sambādhe lomaṃ saṃharāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

799. “Should any bhikkhunī have hair removed from a confined place, it is an offense entailing confession.”

800. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

800. Whatever means: whichever… Bhikkhunī means: …in this sense, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Sambādho nāma ubho upakacchakā, muttakaraṇaṃ.

A confined place means: both armpits and the urinary organ.

Saṃharāpeyyāti [V 0.0355] ekampi lomaṃ saṃharāpeti, āpatti [T 0.0098] pācittiyassa. Bahukepi lome saṃharāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

Should have removed: if she has even a single hair removed, it is an offense of pācittiya. If she has many hairs removed, it is an offense of pācittiya.

801. Anāpatti ābādhapaccayā, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

801. There is no offense on account of illness, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Second Training Rule is concluded.

3. Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Third Training Rule

802. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena dve bhikkhuniyo anabhiratiyā [M 0.0342] pīḷitā ovarakaṃ pavisitvā talaghātakaṃ karonti. Bhikkhuniyo tena saddena upadhāvitvā tā bhikkhuniyo etadavocuṃ – “kissa tumhe, ayye, purisena saddhiṃ sampadussathā”ti? “Na mayaṃ, ayye, purisena saddhiṃ sampadussāmā”ti. Bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo talaghātakaṃ karissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo talaghātakaṃ karontīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo talaghātakaṃ karissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

802. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, two bhikkhunīs, being oppressed by discontent, entered a private chamber and performed the act of striking the exterior of the urinary passage. The bhikkhunīs, hearing that sound, ran up and said to those bhikkhunīs, “Why, Noble Ladies, are you corrupting yourselves with a man?” “We are not, Noble Ladies, corrupting ourselves with a man.” They reported this matter to the bhikkhunīs. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs perform the act of striking the exterior of the urinary passage?”… “Is it true, it is said, Bhikkhus, that bhikkhunīs perform the act of striking the exterior of the urinary passage?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, can bhikkhunīs perform the act of striking the exterior of the urinary passage? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced or for the increase of confidence in the convinced… And thus, Bhikkhus, let the bhikkhunīs set forth this training rule:

803. “Talaghātake pācittiya”nti.

803. “For striking the exterior of the urinary passage, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

804. Talaghātakaṃ [T 0.0099][P 4.0261] nāma samphassaṃ sādiyantī antamaso uppalapattenapi muttakaraṇe pahāraṃ deti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

804. The act of striking means: delighting in the contact, should she deliver a strike to the urinary passage even with, at the very least, a lotus leaf, it is an offense of pācittiya.

805. Anāpatti ābādhapaccayā, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

805. There is no offense on account of illness, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Third Training Rule is concluded.

4. Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Fourth Training Rule

806. Tena [V 0.0356] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā purāṇarājorodhā bhikkhunīsu pabbajitā aññataro purāṇarājorodho bhikkhunīsu pabbajito (syā.) hoti. Aññatarā bhikkhunī anabhiratiyā pīḷitā yena sā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “rājā kho, ayye, tumhe cirāciraṃ gacchati. Kathaṃ tumhe dhārethā”ti? “Jatumaṭṭhakena, ayye”ti. “Kiṃ etaṃ, ayye, jatumaṭṭhaka”nti? Atha kho sā bhikkhunī tassā bhikkhuniyā jatumaṭṭhakaṃ ācikkhi. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī jatumaṭṭhakaṃ ādiyitvā dhovituṃ vissaritvā ekamantaṃ chaḍḍesi. Bhikkhuniyo makkhikāhi samparikiṇṇaṃ passitvā [M 0.0343] evamāhaṃsu – “kassidaṃ kamma”nti? Sā evamāha – “mayhidaṃ kamma”nti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī jatumaṭṭhakaṃ ādiyissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī jatumaṭṭhakaṃ ādiyatīti ādiyīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi [T 0.0100] buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī jatumaṭṭhakaṃ ādiyissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

806. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, in the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, a certain former royal consort had gone forth among the bhikkhunīs. A certain bhikkhunī, oppressed by discontent, approached that bhikkhunī; having approached, she said this to that bhikkhunī: “Venerable lady, the king goes away for a very long time. How do you endure?” “With a lacquered rod, venerable lady.” “What is this lacquered rod, venerable lady?” Then that bhikkhunī told that other bhikkhunī about the lacquered rod. Then that bhikkhunī, having taken the lacquered rod, forgot to wash it and discarded it in a suitable place. The bhikkhunīs, seeing it covered all around with flies, said this: “Whose work is this?” She said this: “This is my work.” Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they criticized, scorned, and spread the word disparagingly: “How indeed could a bhikkhunī take a lacquered rod?” … “Is it true, it is said, monks, that a bhikkhunī takes a lacquered rod?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked… “How indeed, monks, could a bhikkhunī take a lacquered rod? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

807. “Jatumaṭṭhake jatumaṭṭake (sī.) pācittiya”nti.

807. “In the matter of a lacquered rod, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

808. Jatumaṭṭhakaṃ nāma jatumayaṃ kaṭṭhamayaṃ piṭṭhamayaṃ mattikāmayaṃ.

808. A lacquered rod, by name, is one made of lac, one made of wood, one made of flour, or one made of fine clay.

Ādiyeyyāti samphassaṃ sādiyantī antamaso uppalapattampi muttakaraṇaṃ paveseti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should take’ means: delighting in the contact, if she inserts even so much as a lotus petal into the urinary passage, it is an offense of pācittiya.

809. Anāpatti ābādhapaccayā, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

809. There is no offense on account of illness, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fourth Training Rule is concluded.

5. Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Fifth Training Rule

810. Tena [P 4.0262] samayena buddho bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Atha [V 0.0357] kho mahāpajāpati gotamī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā adhovāte aṭṭhāsi – “duggandho, bhagavā, mātugāmo”ti. Atha kho bhagavā – “ādiyantu kho bhikkhuniyo udakasuddhika”nti, mahāpajāpatiṃ gotamiṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho mahāpajāpati gotamī bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi [T 0.0101] – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīnaṃ udakasuddhika”nti. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī – “bhagavatā [M 0.0344] udakasuddhikā anuññātā”ti atigambhīraṃ udakasuddhikaṃ ādiyantī muttakaraṇe vaṇaṃ akāsi. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ āroceti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī atigambhīraṃ udakasuddhikaṃ ādiyissatīti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī atigambhīraṃ udakasuddhikaṃ ādiyatī”ti ādiyīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī atigambhīraṃ udakasuddhikaṃ ādiyissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

810. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling among the Sakyans in Kapilavatthu, in the Nigrodha monastery. Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, she stood downwind and said: “Blessed One, a woman has a bad odor.” Then the Blessed One instructed, caused to undertake, roused, and gladdened Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī with a talk on the Dhamma, saying: “Let the bhikkhunīs indeed undertake water cleansing.” Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, having been instructed, caused to undertake, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a talk on the Dhamma, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him to the right, and departed. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow water cleansing for the bhikkhunīs.” Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī, thinking, “Water cleansing has been allowed by the Blessed One,” undertook water cleansing too deeply and made a wound in her urinary passage. Then that bhikkhunī informed the other bhikkhunīs of this matter. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they criticized, scorned, and spread the word disparagingly: “How indeed could a bhikkhunī undertake water cleansing too deeply?” … “Is it true, it is said, monks, that a bhikkhunī undertakes water cleansing too deeply?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked… “How indeed, monks, could a bhikkhunī undertake water cleansing too deeply? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

811. “Udakasuddhikaṃ pana bhikkhuniyā ādiyamānāya dvaṅgulapabbaparamaṃ ādātabbaṃ. Taṃ atikkāmentiyā pācittiya”nti.

811. “Now, for a bhikkhunī undertaking water cleansing, the maximum to be taken is two finger-joints. For one who exceeds that, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

812. Udakasuddhikaṃ nāma muttakaraṇassa dhovanā vuccati.

812. Water cleansing, by name, is called the washing of the urinary passage.

Ādiyamānāyāti dhovantiyā.

‘For one undertaking’ means: for one washing.

Dvaṅgulapabbaparamaṃ ādātabbanti dvīsu aṅgulesu dve pabbaparamā ādātabbā.

‘The maximum to be taken is two finger-joints’ means: on two fingers, the maximum of two joints are to be taken.

Taṃ atikkāmentiyāti samphassaṃ sādiyantī antamaso kesaggamattampi atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘For one who exceeds that’ means: delighting in the contact, if she exceeds by even so much as a hair's tip, it is an offense of pācittiya.

813. Atirekadvaṅgulapabbe atirekasaññā ādiyati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Atirekadvaṅgulapabbe [V 0.0358] vematikā ādiyati, āpatti pācittiyassa[T 0.0102]. Atirekadvaṅgulapabbe ūnakasaññā ādiyati, āpatti pācittiyassa[P 4.0263].

813. When it exceeds two finger-joints, if she takes it perceiving it as exceeding, it is an offense of pācittiya. When it exceeds two finger-joints, if she takes it while being doubtful, it is an offense of pācittiya. When it exceeds two finger-joints, if she takes it perceiving it as less, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Ūnakadvaṅgulapabbe atirekasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ūnakadvaṅgulapabbe vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ūnakadvaṅgulapabbe ūnakasaññā, anāpatti.

When it is less than two finger-joints, if she perceives it as exceeding, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. When it is less than two finger-joints, if she is doubtful, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. When it is less than two finger-joints, if she perceives it as less, there is no offense.

814. Anāpatti dvaṅgulapabbaparamaṃ ādiyati, ūnakadvaṅgulapabbaparamaṃ ādiyati, ābādhapaccayā, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

814. There is no offense if one takes it to the maximum of two finger-joints, if one takes it to less than the maximum of two finger-joints, on account of illness, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fifth Training Rule is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Sixth Training Rule

815. Tena [M 0.0345] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena ārohanto nāma mahāmatto bhikkhūsu pabbajito hoti. Tassa purāṇadutiyikā bhikkhunīsu pabbajitā hoti. Tena kho pana samayena so bhikkhu tassā bhikkhuniyā santike bhattavissaggaṃ karoti. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī tassa bhikkhuno bhuñjantassa pānīyena ca vidhūpanena ca upatiṭṭhitvā accāvadati. Atha kho so bhikkhu taṃ bhikkhuniṃ apasādeti – “mā, bhagini, evarūpaṃ akāsi. Netaṃ kappatī”ti. “Pubbe maṃ tvaṃ evañca evañca karosi, idāni ettakaṃ na sahasī”ti – pānīyathālakaṃ matthake āsumbhitvā vidhūpanena pahāraṃ adāsi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi [T 0.0103] nāma bhikkhunī bhikkhussa pahāraṃ dassatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī bhikkhussa pahāraṃ adāsīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī bhikkhussa pahāraṃ dassati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

815. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. At that time, a great minister named Ārohanta had gone forth among the monks. His former wife had gone forth among the bhikkhunīs. At that time, that monk was taking a meal in the presence of that bhikkhunī. Then, while that monk was eating, that bhikkhunī attended to him with water and a fan, and spoke excessively. Then that monk rebuked that bhikkhunī, saying, “Sister, do not do such a thing. This is not suitable.” “Formerly, you did this and that to me, and now you cannot endure this much?”—she poured the water bowl over his head and struck him with the fan. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… they complained and criticized, saying, “How indeed could a bhikkhunī strike a monk?”… “Is it true, monks, that a bhikkhunī struck a monk?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, monks, could a bhikkhunī strike a monk! This is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

816. “Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhussa bhuñjantassa pānīyena vā vidhūpanena vā upatiṭṭheyya, pācittiya”nti.

816. “Whatever bhikkhunī should attend upon a monk while he is eating, with water or a fan, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

817. Yā [V 0.0359] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

817. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever kind… ‘A bhikkhunī’ means… the bhikkhunī who is meant in this context.

Bhikkhussāti upasampannassa.

‘A monk’ means: one who is fully ordained.

Bhuñjantassāti pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ aññataraṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjantassa.

‘While he is eating’ means: while eating any of the five kinds of staple food.

Pānīyaṃ nāma yaṃ kiñci pānīyaṃ.

‘Water’ means: any kind of drink.

Vidhūpanaṃ nāma yā kāci bījanī.

‘A fan’ means: any kind of fan.

Upatiṭṭheyyāti hatthapāse tiṭṭhati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should attend upon’ means: if she stands within arm’s reach, there is an offense of pācittiya.

818. Upasampanne [P 4.0264] upasampannasaññā pānīyena vā vidhūpanena vā upatiṭṭhati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne vematikā pānīyena vā vidhūpanena vā upatiṭṭhati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne anupasampannasaññā pānīyena vā vidhūpanena vā upatiṭṭhati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

818. If she attends one who is fully ordained, perceiving him as fully ordained, with water or a fan, there is an offense of pācittiya. If she attends one who is fully ordained, being uncertain, with water or a fan, there is an offense of pācittiya. If she attends one who is fully ordained, perceiving him as not fully ordained, with water or a fan, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Hatthapāsaṃ [M 0.0346] vijahitvā upatiṭṭhati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Khādanīyaṃ khādantassa upatiṭṭhati, āpatti [T 0.0104] dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannassa upatiṭṭhati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne upasampannasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne anupasampannasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If she attends from beyond arm’s reach, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she attends one who is eating non-staple food, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she attends one who is not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she attends one who is not fully ordained, perceiving him as fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she attends one who is not fully ordained, being uncertain, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she attends one who is not fully ordained, perceiving him as not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

819. Anāpatti deti, dāpeti, anupasampannaṃ āṇāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

819. There is no offense if she gives, if she causes to give, if she instructs one who is not fully ordained; for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Sixth Training Rule is concluded.

7. Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Seventh Training Rule

820. Tena [V 0.0360] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo sassakāle āmakadhaññaṃ viññāpetvā nagaraṃ atiharanti dvāraṭṭhāne – “dethāyye, bhāga”nti. Palibundhetvā muñciṃsu. Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo upassayaṃ gantvā bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo āmakadhaññaṃ viññāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo āmakadhaññaṃ viññāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo āmakadhaññaṃ viññāpessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

820. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, during the harvest season, bhikkhunīs, having had raw grain requested, were carrying it back into the city. At the gate, they were obstructed by people saying, 'Venerable ladies, give a share!' and were then released. Then those bhikkhunīs went to their dwelling and reported this matter to the other bhikkhunīs. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: 'How can bhikkhunīs have raw grain requested?'… 'Is it true, monks, that bhikkhunīs have raw grain requested?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… 'How, monks, can bhikkhunīs have raw grain requested? This is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:'

821. “Yā pana bhikkhunī āmakadhaññaṃ viññatvā vā viññāpetvā [T 0.0105] vā bhajjitvā vā bhajjāpetvā vā koṭṭetvā vā koṭṭāpetvā vā pacitvā vā pacāpetvā vā bhuñjeyya, pācittiya”nti.

821. “Whatever bhikkhunī, having requested or had requested raw grain, having roasted or had it roasted, having pounded or had it pounded, having cooked or had it cooked, should eat it, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

822. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

822. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever kind of… ‘A bhikkhunī’ means… the bhikkhunī who is meant in this context.

Āmakadhaññaṃ nāma sāli vīhi yavo godhumo kaṅgu varako kudrusako.

Raw grain means: fine rice, common rice, barley, wheat, millet, varaka, and kudrusaka.

Viññatvāti [M 0.0347] sayaṃ viññatvā. Viññāpetvāti aññaṃ viññāpetvā.

Having requested means: having requested it herself. Having had it requested means: having had another request it.

Bhajjitvāti sayaṃ bhajjitvā. Bhajjāpetvāti aññaṃ bhajjāpetvā.

Having roasted means: having roasted it herself. Having had it roasted means: having had another roast it.

Koṭṭetvāti sayaṃ koṭṭetvā. Koṭṭāpetvāti aññaṃ koṭṭāpetvā.

Having pounded means: having pounded it herself. Having had it pounded means: having had another pound it.

Pacitvāti sayaṃ pacitvā. Pacāpetvāti aññaṃ pacāpetvā.

Having cooked means: having cooked it herself. Having had it cooked means: having had another cook it.

“Bhuñjissāmī”ti [V 0.0361] paṭiggaṇhāti[P 4.0265], āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

If she accepts it, thinking, “I will eat,” there is an offense of wrong-doing. For every mouthful, there is an offense of pācittiya.

823. Anāpatti ābādhapaccayā, aparaṇṇaṃ viññāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

823. There is no offense on account of illness; if one requests pulses; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Seventh Training Rule is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Eighth Training Rule

824. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro brāhmaṇo nibbiṭṭharājabhaṭo “taññeva bhaṭapathaṃ yācissāmī”ti sīsaṃ nahāyitvā [T 0.0106] bhikkhunupassayaṃ nissāya rājakulaṃ gacchati. Aññatarā bhikkhunī kaṭāhe vaccaṃ katvā tirokuṭṭe chaḍḍentī tassa brāhmaṇassa matthake āsumbhi. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “assamaṇiyo imā muṇḍā bandhakiniyo. Kathañhi nāma gūthakaṭāhaṃ matthake āsumbhissanti! Imāsaṃ upassayaṃ jhāpessāmī”ti! Ummukaṃ gahetvā upassayaṃ pavisati. Aññataro upāsako upassayā nikkhamanto addasa taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ ummukaṃ gahetvā upassayaṃ pavisantaṃ. Disvāna taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – “kissa tvaṃ, bho, ummukaṃ gahetvā upassayaṃ pavisasī”ti? “Imā maṃ, bho, muṇḍā bandhakiniyo gūthakaṭāhaṃ matthake āsumbhiṃsu. Imāsaṃ upassayaṃ jhāpessāmī”ti. “Gaccha, bho brāhmaṇa, maṅgalaṃ etaṃ. Sahassaṃ lacchasi tañca bhaṭapatha”nti. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo sīsaṃ nahāyitvā rājakulaṃ gantvā sahassaṃ alattha tañca bhaṭapathaṃ. Atha kho so upāsako upassayaṃ pavisitvā bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ [M 0.0348] ārocetvā paribhāsi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo uccāraṃ tirokuṭṭe chaḍḍessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo uccāraṃ tirokuṭṭe chaḍḍentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo uccāraṃ tirokuṭṭe chaḍḍessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave[T 0.0107], bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

824. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, a certain brahmin who had held a royal office, thinking, 'I will ask for that same office,' bathed his head and went to the royal court, passing by the nuns’ dwelling. A certain bhikkhunī, having defecated in a pot, was throwing it over the wall, and it was poured on that brahmin’s head. Then that brahmin complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: 'These shaven-headed women are not ascetics, they are harlots! How could they pour a pot of excrement on my head! I will burn down their dwelling!' Taking a firebrand, he entered the nuns’ dwelling. A certain lay follower, coming out of the dwelling, saw that brahmin entering with a firebrand. Seeing him, he said to that brahmin: 'Why, sir, are you entering the dwelling with a firebrand?' 'These shaven-headed harlots poured a pot of excrement on my head. I will burn down their dwelling!' 'Go, brahmin, this is an auspicious sign. You will receive a thousand and that office.' Then that brahmin, having bathed his head, went to the royal court and received a thousand and that office. Then that lay follower entered the nuns’ dwelling and, having informed the nuns of the matter, rebuked them. Those nuns who were modest… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: 'How can nuns throw excrement over the wall?'… 'Is it true, bhikkhus, that nuns throw excrement over the wall?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them: 'How, bhikkhus, can nuns throw excrement over the wall? This is not for the confidence of the faithless… And so, bhikkhus, the nuns should recite this training rule:'

825. “Yā [V 0.0362] pana bhikkhunī uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā saṅkāraṃ vā vighāsaṃ vā tirokuṭṭe vā tiropākāre vā chaḍḍeyya vā chaḍḍāpeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

825. “Whatever bhikkhunī should discard, or cause to be discarded, excrement, urine, refuse, or leftovers over a wall or over an enclosure, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

826. Yā [P 4.0266] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

826. Whatever means: whatever kind of… A bhikkhunī means… the bhikkhunī intended in this context.

Uccāro nāma gūtho vuccati. Passāvo nāma muttaṃ vuccati.

Excrement means feces. Urine means urine.

Saṅkāraṃ nāma kacavaraṃ vuccati.

Refuse means rubbish.

Vighāsaṃ nāma calakāni vā aṭṭhikāni vā ucchiṭṭhodakaṃ vā.

Leftovers means morsels, bones, or water with food remains.

Kuṭṭo nāma tayo kuṭṭā – iṭṭhakākuṭṭo, silākuṭṭo, dārukuṭṭo.

A wall means three kinds of walls: a brick wall, a stone wall, and a wooden wall.

Pākāro nāma tayo pākārā – iṭṭhakāpākāro, silāpākāro, dārupākāro.

An enclosure means three kinds of enclosures: a brick enclosure, a stone enclosure, and a wooden enclosure.

Tirokuṭṭeti kuṭṭassa parato. Tiropākāreti pākārassa parato.

Over a wall means beyond the wall. Over an enclosure means beyond the enclosure.

Chaḍḍeyyāti sayaṃ chaḍḍeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

Should discard means: if she discards it herself, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Chaḍḍāpeyyāti aññaṃ āṇāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sakiṃ āṇattā bahukampi chaḍḍeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

“Should cause to be discarded” means: if she orders another, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If the one who was ordered once discards it many times, there is an offense of pācittiya.

827. Anāpatti oloketvā chaḍḍeti, avaḷañje chaḍḍeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

827. There is no offense if she looks before discarding; if she discards it in a place for refuse; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Eighth Training Rule is concluded.

9. Navamasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Ninth Training Rule

828. Tena [M 0.0349][V 0.0363] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa [T 0.0108] ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa brāhmaṇassa bhikkhunūpassayaṃ nissāya yavakhettaṃ hoti. Bhikkhuniyo uccārampi passāvampi saṅkārampi vighāsampi khette chaḍḍenti. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo amhākaṃ yavakhettaṃ dūsessantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tassa brāhmaṇassa ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo uccārampi passāvampi saṅkārampi vighāsampi harite chaḍḍessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo uccārampi passāvampi saṅkārampi vighāsampi harite chaḍḍentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo uccārampi passāvampi saṅkārampi vighāsampi harite chaḍḍessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

828. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, a certain brahmin had a barley field near the bhikkhunīs' monastery. The bhikkhunīs would discard excrement, urine, sweepings, and leftovers in the field. Then that brahmin complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed can the bhikkhunīs spoil our barley field?” The bhikkhunīs heard that brahmin complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs discard excrement, urine, sweepings, and leftovers on green crops?” … “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that bhikkhunīs discard excrement, urine, sweepings, and leftovers on green crops?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, can bhikkhunīs discard excrement, urine, sweepings, and leftovers on green crops? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

829. “Yā pana bhikkhunī uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā saṅkāraṃ vā vighāsaṃ vā harite chaḍḍeyya vā chaḍḍāpeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

829. “Whatever bhikkhunī should discard or cause to be discarded excrement, urine, sweepings, or leftovers on green crops, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

830. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

830. ‘Whatever’ means: whichever, of whatever kind... A ‘bhikkhunī’ means... In this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Uccāro nāma gūtho vuccati. Passāvo nāma muttaṃ vuccati.

‘Excrement’ is called feces. ‘Urine’ is called urine.

Saṅkāraṃ nāma kacavaraṃ vuccati.

‘Sweepings’ is called rubbish.

Vighāsaṃ nāma calakāni vā aṭṭhikāni vā ucchiṭṭhodakaṃ vā.

‘Leftovers’ means either food particles, bones, or water with leftovers.

Haritaṃ [P 4.0267] nāma pubbaṇṇaṃ aparaṇṇaṃ yaṃ manussānaṃ upabhogaparibhogaṃ ropimaṃ[T 0.0109].

‘Greenery’ means grain, pulse, or whatever is planted by humans for their use and consumption.

Chaḍḍeyyāti sayaṃ chaḍḍeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should discard’: one discards it oneself; there is an offense of expiation.

Chaḍḍāpeyyāti [V 0.0364] aññaṃ āṇāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sakiṃ āṇattā bahukampi chaḍḍeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should cause to be discarded’: one orders another; there is an offense of wrong-doing. If, having been ordered once, that person discards many times, there is an offense of expiation.

831. Harite haritasaññā chaḍḍeti vā chaḍḍāpeti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Harite vematikā chaḍḍeti vā chaḍḍāpeti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa[M 0.0350]. Harite aharitasaññā chaḍḍeti vā chaḍḍāpeti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

831. On greenery, perceiving it as greenery, one discards or causes it to be discarded: there is an offense of expiation. On greenery, being in doubt, one discards or causes it to be discarded: there is an offense of expiation. On greenery, perceiving it as not greenery, one discards or causes it to be discarded: there is an offense of expiation.

Aharite haritasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Aharite vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Aharite aharitasaññā, anāpatti.

On what is not greenery, perceiving it as greenery: there is an offense of wrong-doing. On what is not greenery, being in doubt: there is an offense of wrong-doing. On what is not greenery, perceiving it as not greenery: there is no offense.

832. Anāpatti oloketvā chaḍḍeti, khettamariyāde chaḍḍitakhette (?) aṭṭhakathā oloketabbā chaḍḍeti sāmike āpucchitvā apaloketvā chaḍḍeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

832. There is no offense: if one discards after looking; if one discards on the boundary of a field; if one discards after asking and informing the owners; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Navamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Ninth Training Rule is concluded.

10. Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Tenth Training Rule

833. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena rājagahe giraggasamajjo hoti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo giraggasamajjaṃ dassanāya agamaṃsu. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo naccampi gītampi vāditampi dassanāya gacchissanti, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ [T 0.0110] khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo naccampi gītampi vāditampi dassanāya gacchissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo naccampi gītampi vāditampi dassanāya gacchantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo naccampi gītampi vāditampi dassanāya gacchissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

833. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Veḷuvana, the Squirrels' Feeding Place. Now at that time, a mountain-top festival was being held at Rājagaha. The group-of-six bhikkhunīs went for the purpose of seeing the mountain-top festival. People censured, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs go to see dancing, singing, and instrumental music, just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people censuring, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they censured, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs go to see dancing, singing, and instrumental music?”… “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs go to see dancing, singing, and instrumental music?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs go to see dancing, singing, and instrumental music? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And thus, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

834. “Yā [V 0.0365] pana bhikkhunī naccaṃ vā gītaṃ vā vāditaṃ vā dassanāya gaccheyya, pācittiya”nti.

834. “Whatever bhikkhunī should go for the purpose of seeing dancing, or singing, or instrumental music, it is an offense of expiation.”

835. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

835. ‘Whatever’ means: whichever, of whatever kind... A ‘bhikkhunī’ means... In this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Naccaṃ [M 0.0351] nāma yaṃ kiñci naccaṃ. Gītaṃ nāma yaṃ kiñci gītaṃ. Vāditaṃ nāma yaṃ kiñci vāditaṃ.

‘Dancing’ means any dancing whatsoever. ‘Singing’ means any singing whatsoever. ‘Instrumental music’ means any instrumental music whatsoever.

836. Dassanāya [P 4.0268] gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yattha ṭhitā passati vā suṇāti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dassanūpacāraṃ vijahitvā punappunaṃ passati vā suṇāti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ekamekaṃ dassanāya gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yattha ṭhitā passati vā suṇāti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dassanūpacāraṃ vijahitvā punappunaṃ passati vā suṇāti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

836. If she goes for the purpose of seeing, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In whatever place she stands and sees or hears, there is an offense of expiation. Having left the range of seeing, if she sees or hears again and again, there is an offense of expiation. If she goes to see each one, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In whatever place she stands and sees or hears, there is an offense of expiation. Having left the range of seeing, if she sees or hears again and again, there is an offense of expiation.

837. Anāpatti ārāme ṭhitā passati vā suṇāti vā, bhikkhuniyā [T 0.0111] ṭhitokāsaṃ vā nisinnokāsaṃ vā nipannokāsaṃ vā āgantvā naccanti vā gāyanti vā vādenti vā, paṭipathaṃ gacchantī passati vā suṇāti vā, sati karaṇīye gantvā passati vā suṇāti vā, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

837. There is no offense if, standing in the monastery, she sees or hears; if they come to the place where the bhikkhunī is standing, sitting, or lying down and dance, sing, or play music; if, while going along the path, she sees or hears; if, there being some business to be done, she goes and sees or hears; in times of danger; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Tenth Training Rule is concluded.

Lasuṇavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter on Garlic is concluded.

2. Andhakāravaggo

2. The Chapter on Darkness

1. Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The First Training Rule

838. Tena [V 0.0366] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhaddāya kāpilāniyā antevāsiniyā bhikkhuniyā ñātako puriso gāmakā sāvatthiṃ agamāsi kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī tena purisena saddhiṃ rattandhakāre appadīpe ekenekā santiṭṭhatipi sallapatipi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī rattandhakāre appadīpe purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhissatipi sallapissatipī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī rattandhakāre appadīpe purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhatipi sallapatipīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave[M 0.0352], bhikkhunī rattandhakāre appadīpe purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhissatipi sallapissatipi! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ [T 0.0112] vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

838. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time, a male relative of a bhikkhunī who was the pupil of Bhaddā Kāpilānī had come from a village to Sāvatthī on some business. Then that bhikkhunī stood and conversed alone with that man, one to one, in the dark of night without a lamp. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes... censured, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How could a bhikkhunī stand and converse alone with a man, one to one, in the dark of night without a lamp?”... “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that a bhikkhunī stood and conversed alone with a man, one to one, in the dark of night without a lamp?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her... “How, Bhikkhus, could a bhikkhunī stand and converse alone with a man, one to one, in the dark of night without a lamp? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident... And thus, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

839. “Yā pana bhikkhunī rattandhakāre appadīpe purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭheyya vā sallapeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

839. “Whatever bhikkhunī should stand or converse alone with a man, one to one, in the dark of night without a lamp, it is an offense of expiation.”

840. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

840. ‘Whatever’ means: whichever, of whatever kind... A ‘bhikkhunī’ means... In this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Rattandhakāreti oggate sūriye. Appadīpeti anāloke.

‘In the dark of night’ means: when the sun has set. ‘Without a lamp’ means: without light.

Puriso [P 4.0269] nāma manussapuriso na yakkho na peto na tiracchānagato viññū paṭibalo santiṭṭhituṃ sallapituṃ.

‘Man’ means a human male, not a male yakkha, not a male peta, not a male animal. He is discerning and capable of standing and conversing.

Saddhinti ekato. Ekenekāti puriso ceva hoti bhikkhunī ca.

‘With’ means together. ‘One-on-one’ means there is a man and there is a bhikkhunī.

Santiṭṭheyya vāti purisassa hatthapāse tiṭṭhati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should stand’ means: if she stands within a man’s arm’s reach, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Sallapeyya [V 0.0367] vāti purisassa hatthapāse ṭhitā sallapati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should converse’ means: if she stands within a man’s arm’s reach and converses, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā santiṭṭhati vā sallapati vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yakkhena vā petena vā paṇḍakena vā tiracchānagatamanussaviggahena vā saddhiṃ santiṭṭhati vā sallapati vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If, having gone beyond arm’s reach, she stands or converses, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. If she stands or converses with a yakkha, a peta, a paṇḍaka, or an animal in the form of a human male, it is an offense of dukkaṭa.

841. Anāpatti yo koci viññū dutiyo yā kāci viññū dutiyā (syā.) hoti, arahopekkhā, aññavihitā santiṭṭhati vā sallapati vā, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

841. There is no offense if some discerning person is present as a companion, if she is not seeking seclusion, if, being intent on something else, she stands or converses, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The First Training Rule is concluded.

2. Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Second Training Rule

842. Tena [T 0.0113] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhaddāya kāpilāniyā antevāsiniyā bhikkhuniyā ñātako puriso gāmakā sāvatthiṃ [M 0.0353] agamāsi kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī – “bhagavatā paṭikkhittaṃ rattandhakāre appadīpe purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhituṃ sallapitu”nti teneva purisena saddhiṃ paṭicchanne okāse ekenekā santiṭṭhatipi sallapatipi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī paṭicchanne okāse purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhissatipi sallapissatipī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī paṭicchanne okāse purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhatipi sallapatipīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī paṭicchanne okāse purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhissatipi sallapissatipi! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

842. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time a male relative of a bhikkhunī, a pupil of Bhaddā Kāpilānī, went from a village to Sāvatthī on some business. Then that bhikkhunī, thinking, 'It was forbidden by the Blessed One to stand or converse one-on-one with a man in the dark of night without a lamp,' both stood and conversed one-on-one with that man in a secluded place. The bhikkhunīs who were of few desires complained and criticized her: 'How could a bhikkhunī both stand and converse one-on-one with a man in a secluded place?' … 'Is it true, Bhikkhus, that a bhikkhunī both stood and conversed one-on-one with a man in a secluded place?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… 'How could a bhikkhunī both stand and converse one-on-one with a man in a secluded place? This is not for the confidence of those without confidence… And thus, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

843. “Yā pana bhikkhunī paṭicchanne okāse purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭheyya vā sallapeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

843. “Whatever bhikkhunī should stand or converse one-on-one with a man in a secluded place, it is an offense entailing expiation.”

844. Yā [V 0.0368] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ [T 0.0114] atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

844. ‘Whatever’ means: whichever, of whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means: …a bhikkhunī is intended in this sense.

Paṭicchanno nāma okāso kuṭṭena vā kavāṭena vā kilañjena vā sāṇipākārena vā rukkhena vā thambhena vā kotthaḷiyā vā yena kenaci paṭicchanno hoti.

‘A secluded place’ means one concealed by a wall, a door, a mat, a curtain, a tree, a pillar, a large sack, or by anything whatsoever.

Puriso nāma manussapuriso na yakkho na peto na tiracchānagato viññū paṭibalo santiṭṭhituṃ sallapituṃ.

‘A man’ means a human male, not a yakkha, not a peta, not an animal; one who is discerning and capable of standing and conversing.

Saddhinti ekato. Ekenekāti puriso ceva hoti bhikkhunī ca.

‘With’ means together. ‘One-on-one’ means there is a man and there is a bhikkhunī.

Santiṭṭheyya vāti purisassa hatthapāse tiṭṭhati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should stand’ means: if she stands within a man’s arm’s reach, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Sallapeyya vāti purisassa hatthapāse ṭhitā sallapati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should converse’ means: standing within a man’s arm’s reach, she converses; there is an offense entailing expiation.

Hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā santiṭṭhati vā sallapati vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yakkhena vā petena vā paṇḍakena vā tiracchānagatamanussaviggahena vā saddhiṃ santiṭṭhati vā sallapati vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If, having gone beyond arm’s reach, she stands or converses, there is an offense of wrong conduct. If she stands or converses with a yakkha, a peta, a paṇḍaka, or an animal in human form, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

845. Anāpatti [M 0.0354] yo koci viññū dutiyo hoti, arahopekkhā, aññavihitā santiṭṭhati vā sallapati vā, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

845. There is no offense if some discerning person is present as a companion, if she is not seeking seclusion, if she stands or converses while her mind is occupied with something else, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Second Training Rule is concluded.

3. Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Third Training Rule

846. Tena [P 4.0270] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhaddāya kāpilāniyā [T 0.0115] antevāsiniyā bhikkhuniyā ñātako puriso gāmakā sāvatthiṃ agamāsi kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī – “bhagavatā paṭikkhittaṃ paṭicchanne okāse purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhituṃ sallapitu”nti teneva [V 0.0369] purisena saddhiṃ ajjhokāse ekenekā santiṭṭhatipi sallapatipi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī ajjhokāse purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhissatipi sallapissatipī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī ajjhokāse purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhatipi sallapatipīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī ajjhokāse purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhissatipi sallapissatipi! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

846. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, a male relative of a bhikkhunī who was a resident student of Bhaddā Kāpilānī went from a small village to Sāvatthī on some business. Then that bhikkhunī, thinking, “The Blessed One has forbidden standing together or conversing together, one-on-one, with a man in a concealed place,” stood together and also conversed together, one-on-one, with that very man in an open place. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they criticized, scorned, and spread the word: “How indeed could a bhikkhunī stand together and also converse together, one-on-one, with a man in an open place?”… “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that a bhikkhunī stood together and also conversed together, one-on-one, with a man in an open place?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, could a bhikkhunī stand together and also converse together, one-on-one, with a man in an open place? This, Bhikkhus, does not lead to the faith of the faithless… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

847. “Yā pana bhikkhunī ajjhokāse purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭheyya vā sallapeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

847. “Whatever bhikkhunī should stand together or converse together, one-on-one, with a man in an open place, it is a pācittiya offense.”

848. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

848. As for 'whatever': whatever sort… As for 'bhikkhunī': …this bhikkhunī is intended in this context.

Ajjhokāso nāma appaṭicchanno hoti kuṭṭena vā kavāṭena vā kilañjena vā sāṇipākārena vā rukkhena vā thambhena vā kotthaḷiyā vā, yena kenaci appaṭicchanno hoti.

An open place, by name, is that which is not concealed. It is not concealed by a wall, a door-leaf, a mat, a curtain-wall, a tree, a pillar, a large sack, or by anything whatsoever.

Puriso [M 0.0355] nāma manussapuriso, na yakkho na peto na tiracchānagato, viññū paṭibalo santiṭṭhituṃ sallapituṃ.

A man, by name, is a human man; not a yakkha, not a peta, not an animal. He is discerning and capable of standing together and conversing together.

Saddhinti [T 0.0116] ekato. Ekenekāti puriso ceva hoti bhikkhunī ca.

As for 'with': it means together. As for 'one-on-one': there is a man and there is a bhikkhunī.

Santiṭṭheyya vāti purisassa hatthapāse tiṭṭhati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

As for 'should stand together': if she stands within a man’s hand’s reach, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Sallapeyya vāti purisassa hatthapāse ṭhitā sallapati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

As for 'should converse together': standing within a man’s hand’s reach, if she converses, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā santiṭṭhati vā sallapati vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yakkhena vā petena vā paṇḍakena vā tiracchāgatamanussaviggahena vā saddhiṃ santiṭṭhati vā sallapati vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Having gone beyond hand’s reach, if she stands together or converses together, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If she stands together or converses together with a yakkha, or with a peta, or with a paṇḍaka, or with an animal in the form of a human man, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

849. Anāpatti [V 0.0370] yo koci viññū dutiyo hoti, arahopekkhā, aññavihitā santiṭṭhati vā sallapati vā, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

849. There is no offense: if there is some intelligent person as a companion; if she is not concerned with seclusion; if, being preoccupied, she stands together or converses together; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Third Training Rule is concluded.

4. Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Fourth Training Rule

850. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī rathikāyapi byūhepi siṅghāṭakepi purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhatipi sallapatipi nikaṇṇikampi jappeti dutiyikampi bhikkhuniṃ uyyojeti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā rathikāyapi byūhepi siṅghāṭakepi purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhissatipi sallapissatipi nikaṇṇikampi jappissati dutiyikampi bhikkhuniṃ uyyojessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ [T 0.0117] kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī rathikāyapi byūhepi siṅghāṭakepi purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhatipi sallapatipi nikaṇṇikampi jappeti dutiyikampi bhikkhuniṃ uyyojetīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī rathikāyapi byūhepi siṅghāṭakepi purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhissatipi sallapissatipi nikaṇṇikampi jappissati dutiyikampi [M 0.0356] bhikkhuniṃ uyyojessati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

850. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā would stand one-on-one and converse with a man on a carriage road, on a dead-end street, or at a crossroads. She would also speak near his ear and send away her companion bhikkhunī. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes…pe… reproached, complained, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the venerable Thullanandā stand one-on-one, converse, speak near his ear, and send away her companion bhikkhunī with a man on a carriage road, on a dead-end street, or at a crossroads?”…pe… “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā does this?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her…pe… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā stand one-on-one, converse, speak near his ear, and send away her companion bhikkhunī with a man on a carriage road, on a dead-end street, or at a crossroads? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the faithless…pe… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

851. “Yā [P 4.0271] pana bhikkhunī rathikāya vā byūhe vā siṅghāṭake vā purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭheyya vā sallapeyya vā nikaṇṇikaṃ vā jappeyya dutiyikaṃ vā bhikkhuniṃ uyyojeyya, pācittiya”nti.

851. “Whatever bhikkhunī, on a carriage road, on a dead-end street, or at a crossroads, should stand one-on-one with a man, or converse, or speak near his ear, or send away a companion bhikkhunī, it is a pācittiya offense.”

852. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

852. ‘Whatever’ means whatever sort…pe… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means…pe… in this context, this bhikkhunī is intended as ‘bhikkhunī’.

Rathikā nāma racchā vuccati. Byūhaṃ nāma yeneva pavisanti teneva nikkhamanti. Siṅghāṭako nāma caccaraṃ vuccati.

‘Rathikā’ is called a carriage road. ‘Byūha’ is where one enters and exits by the same way. ‘Siṅghāṭaka’ is called a crossroads.

Puriso [V 0.0371] nāma manussapuriso na yakkho na peto na tiracchānagato viññū paṭibalo santiṭṭhituṃ sallapituṃ.

A man means a human male, not a yakkha, not a peta, not an animal; one who is discerning and capable of standing together and conversing together.

Saddhinti ekato. Ekenekāti puriso ceva hoti bhikkhunī ca.

‘With’ means together. ‘One with one’ means it is a man and it is a bhikkhunī.

Santiṭṭheyya vāti purisassa hatthapāse tiṭṭhati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should stand together’: if she stands within a man’s hand’s reach, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Sallapeyya vāti purisassa hatthapāse ṭhitā sallapati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should converse together’: if, standing within a man’s hand’s reach, she converses, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Nikaṇṇikaṃ vā jappeyyāti purisassa upakaṇṇake āroceti[T 0.0118], āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should speak near the ear’: if she speaks near a man’s ear, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Dutiyikaṃ vā bhikkhuniṃ uyyojeyyāti anācāraṃ ācaritukāmā dutiyikampi bhikkhuniṃ uyyojeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Dassanūpacāraṃ vā savanūpacāraṃ vā vijahantiyā āpatti dukkaṭassa. Vijahite āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should send away a companion bhikkhunī’: if, wishing to engage in improper conduct, she sends away a companion bhikkhunī, there is a dukkaṭa offense. For abandoning the range of sight or the range of hearing, there is a dukkaṭa offense. When they have been abandoned, there is a pācittiya offense.

Hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā santiṭṭhati vā sallapati vā āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yakkhena vā petena vā paṇḍakena vā tiracchānagatamanussaviggahena vā saddhiṃ santiṭṭhati vā sallapati vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If she stands or converses having gone beyond hand’s reach, there is a dukkaṭa offense. If she stands or converses with a yakkha, a peta, a paṇḍaka, or an animal in human guise, there is a dukkaṭa offense.

853. Anāpatti yo koci viññū dutiyo hoti, arahopekkhā, aññavihitā santiṭṭhati vā sallapati vā, na anācāraṃ ācaritukāmā, sati karaṇīye dutiyikaṃ bhikkhuniṃ uyyojeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

853. There is no offense: if any discerning person is present as a companion; if she is not seeking seclusion; if she stands or converses while preoccupied; if, not wishing to engage in improper conduct, she sends away a companion bhikkhunī when there is business to be done; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fourth Training Rule is concluded.

5. Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Fifth Training Rule

854. Tena [M 0.0357] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī aññatarassa kulassa kulūpikā hoti niccabhattikā. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena taṃ kulaṃ [V 0.0372] tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āsane nisīditvā sāmike anāpucchā pakkāmi. Tassa kulassa dāsī gharaṃ sammajjantī taṃ [P 4.0272] āsanaṃ bhājanantarikāya pakkhipi. Manussā taṃ āsanaṃ apassantā taṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavocuṃ [T 0.0119] – “kahaṃ taṃ, ayye, āsana”nti? “Nāhaṃ taṃ, āvuso, āsanaṃ passāmī”ti. “Dethāyye, taṃ āsana”nti paribhāsitvā niccabhattaṃ pacchindiṃsu. Atha kho te manussā gharaṃ sodhentā taṃ āsanaṃ bhājanantarikāya passitvā taṃ bhikkhuniṃ khamāpetvā niccabhattaṃ paṭṭhapesuṃ. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī purebhattaṃ kulāni upasaṅkamitvā āsane nisīditvā sāmike anāpucchā pakkamissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī purebhattaṃ kulāni upasaṅkamitvā āsane nisīditvā sāmike anāpucchā pakkamatīti pakkamīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave bhikkhunī purebhattaṃ kulāni upasaṅkamitvā āsane nisīditvā sāmike anāpucchā pakkamissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

854. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī was a frequent visitor to a certain family and received a regular meal. Then that bhikkhunī, having dressed in the morning and taken her bowl and robe, approached that family; having approached, she sat down on a seat and departed without asking the owners for permission. The slave-girl of that family, while sweeping the house, placed that seat among the pots. The people, not seeing that seat, said to that bhikkhunī, “Venerable lady, where is that seat?” “Supporters, I do not see that seat.” “Venerable lady, give us that seat,” and having reproached her, they cut off the regular meal. Then those people, while cleaning the house, saw that seat among the pots and, having asked that bhikkhunī for forgiveness, restored the regular meal. Then that bhikkhunī informed the other bhikkhunīs about this matter. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, “How indeed could a bhikkhunī, having approached families in the morning, having sat down on a seat, depart without asking the owners for permission?”… “Is it true, monks, that a bhikkhunī, having approached families in the morning, having sat down on a seat, departs without asking the owners for permission?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, monks, could a bhikkhunī, having approached families in the morning, having sat down on a seat, depart without asking the owners for permission? This, monks, is not for the inspiring of confidence in the uninspired… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

855. “Yā pana bhikkhunī purebhattaṃ kulāni upasaṅkamitvā āsane nisīditvā sāmike anāpucchā pakkameyya, pācittiya”nti.

855. “Whatever bhikkhunī, having approached families in the morning, having sat down on a seat, should depart without asking the owners for permission, it is a pācittiya offense.”

856. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

856. 'Whatever' means: whichever, of whatever sort... 'Bhikkhunī' means... the bhikkhunī who is intended in this context.

Purebhattaṃ nāma aruṇuggamanaṃ upādāya yāva majjhanhikā.

'Before the meal' means from the rising of the dawn until midday.

Kulaṃ nāma cattāri kulāni – khattiyakulaṃ, brāhmaṇakulaṃ, vessakulaṃ, suddakulaṃ. Upasaṅkamitvāti tattha gantvā.

'Family' means four families: the khattiya family, the brāhmaṇa family, the vessa family, and the sudda family. 'Having approached' means having gone there.

Āsanaṃ [T 0.0120][M 0.0358] nāma pallaṅkassa okāso vuccati. Nisīditvāti tasmiṃ nisīditvā.

'A seat' is said to be a space for sitting cross-legged. 'Having sat down' means having sat down on it.

Sāmike anāpucchā pakkameyyāti yo tasmiṃ kule manusso viññū taṃ anāpucchā anovassakaṃ [V 0.0373] atikkāmentiyā āpatti pācittiyassa. Ajjhokāse upacāraṃ atikkāmentiyā āpatti pācittiyassa.

'Should depart without asking the owners for permission' means: for a bhikkhunī who departs without asking a discerning person in that family and crosses beyond the sheltered area, it is an offense of pācittiya. For crossing beyond the precinct in an open area, it is an offense of pācittiya.

857. Anāpucchite anāpucchitasaññā pakkamati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anāpucchite vematikā pakkamati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anāpucchite āpucchitasaññā pakkamati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

857. When she has not asked for permission, if she departs perceiving that she has not asked, it is an offense of pācittiya. When she has not asked for permission, if she departs while being uncertain, it is an offense of pācittiya. When she has not asked for permission, if she departs perceiving that she has asked, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Pallaṅkassa anokāse āpatti dukkaṭassa. Āpucchite anāpucchitasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Āpucchite vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Āpucchite āpucchitasaññā, anāpatti.

On a seat that is not a space for sitting cross-legged, it is an offense of wrong-doing. When she has asked for permission, if she perceives that she has not asked, it is an offense of wrong-doing. When she has asked for permission, if she is uncertain, it is an offense of wrong-doing. When she has asked for permission, if she perceives that she has asked, there is no offense.

858. Anāpatti āpucchā gacchati, asaṃhārime, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

858. There is no offense if she goes after asking for permission; if the seat is immovable; for one who is sick; in times of danger; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fifth Training Rule is finished.

6. Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Sixth Training Rule

859. Tena [P 4.0273] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī pacchābhattaṃ kulāni upasaṅkamitvā sāmike anāpucchā āsane abhinisīdatipi [T 0.0121] abhinipajjatipi. Manussā thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ hirīyamānā āsane neva abhinisīdanti na abhinipajjanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā pacchābhattaṃ kulāni upasaṅkamitvā sāmike anāpucchā āsane abhinisīdissatipi abhinipajjissatipī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā pacchābhattaṃ kulāni [M 0.0359] upasaṅkamitvā sāmike anāpucchā āsane abhinisīdissatipi abhinipajjissatipī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī pacchābhattaṃ kulāni upasaṅkamitvā sāmike anāpucchā āsane abhinisīdatipi abhinipajjatipīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave[V 0.0374], thullanandā bhikkhunī pacchābhattaṃ kulāni upasaṅkamitvā sāmike anāpucchā āsane abhinisīdissatipi abhinipajjissatipi! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

859. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, after the meal, having approached families, without asking the owners, both sat down and lay down on a seat. People, feeling embarrassed by the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, neither sat down nor lay down on the seat. People complained, criticized, and grumbled: “How indeed could the venerable Thullanandā, after the meal, having approached families, without asking the owners, both sit down and lie down on a seat?” The bhikkhunīs heard the complaining, criticizing, and grumbling of those people. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… they complained, criticized, and grumbled: “How indeed could the venerable Thullanandā, after the meal, having approached families, without asking the owners, both sit down and lie down on a seat?”… “Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, after the meal, having approached families, without asking the owners, both sits down and lies down on a seat?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, monks, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, after the meal, having approached families, without asking the owners, both sit down and lie down on a seat? This, monks, is not for the inspiring of confidence in the uninspired… And so, monks, let the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule:”

860. “Yā pana bhikkhunī pacchābhattaṃ kulāni upasaṅkamitvā sāmike anāpucchā āsane abhinisīdeyya vā abhinipajjeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

860. “Whatever bhikkhunī, after the meal, having approached families, should sit down or lie down on a seat without asking the owners, it is a pācittiya offense.”

861. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

861. 'Whatever' means: whichever, of whatever sort... 'Bhikkhunī' means... the bhikkhunī who is intended in this context.

Pacchābhattaṃ nāma majjhanhike vītivatte yāva atthaṅgate sūriye.

'After the meal' means from when midday has passed until the sun has set.

Kulaṃ nāma cattāri kulāni [T 0.0122] – khattiyakulaṃ, brāhmaṇakulaṃ, vessakulaṃ, suddakulaṃ. Upasaṅkamitvāti tattha gantvā.

By 'a family' is meant the four families: the warrior family, the brahmin family, the merchant family, and the commoner family. 'Having approached' means having gone there.

Sāmike anāpucchāti yo tasmiṃ kule manusso sāmiko dātuṃ, taṃ anāpucchā.

'Without asking the owners' means: without asking the person in that family who is the master with authority to give.

Āsanaṃ nāma pallaṅkassa okāso vuccati.

By 'a seat' is meant a space sufficient for a cross-legged sitting posture.

Abhinisīdeyyāti tasmiṃ abhinisīdati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

'Should sit down' means: if one sits on it, one incurs an offense requiring expiation.

Abhinipajjeyyāti tasmiṃ abhinipajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

'Should lie down' means: if one lies down on it, one incurs an offense requiring expiation.

862. Anāpucchite anāpucchitasaññā āsane abhinisīdati vā abhinipajjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anāpucchite vematikā āsane abhinisīdati vā abhinipajjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anāpucchite āpucchitasaññā āsane abhinisīdati vā abhinipajjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

862. When permission has not been asked, and one perceives it as not having been asked, if one sits or lies down on the seat, one incurs an offense requiring expiation. When permission has not been asked, and one is in doubt, if one sits or lies down on the seat, one incurs an offense requiring expiation. When permission has not been asked, but one perceives it as having been asked, if one sits or lies down on the seat, one incurs an offense requiring expiation.

Pallaṅkassa [M 0.0360] anokāse āpatti dukkaṭassa. Āpucchite anāpucchitasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa[V 0.0375]. Āpucchite vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Āpucchite āpucchitasaññā, anāpatti.

In a space not sufficient for a cross-legged sitting posture, one incurs an offense of wrong-doing. When permission has been asked, but one perceives it as not having been asked, one incurs an offense of wrong-doing. When permission has been asked, and one is in doubt, one incurs an offense of wrong-doing. When permission has been asked, and one perceives it as having been asked, there is no offense.

863. Anāpatti [P 4.0274] āpucchā āsane abhinisīdati vā abhinipajjati vā, dhuvapaññatte, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

863. There is no offense: if one asks permission before sitting or lying down on a seat; in the case of a permanently prepared place; for one who is sick; in times of calamity; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Sixth Training Rule is concluded.

7. Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Seventh Training Rule

864. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa [T 0.0123] ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhuniyo kosalesu janapade sāvatthiṃ gacchantiyo sāyaṃ aññataraṃ gāmaṃ upagantvā aññataraṃ brāhmaṇakulaṃ upasaṅkamitvā okāsaṃ yāciṃsu. Atha kho sā brāhmaṇī tā bhikkhuniyo etadavoca – “āgametha, ayye, yāva brāhmaṇo āgacchatī”ti. Bhikkhuniyo – “yāva brāhmaṇo āgacchatī”ti seyyaṃ santharitvā ekaccā nisīdiṃsu ekaccā nipajjiṃsu. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo rattiṃ āgantvā taṃ brāhmaṇiṃ etadavoca – “kā imā”ti? “Bhikkhuniyo, ayyā”ti. “Nikkaḍḍhatha imā muṇḍā bandhakiniyo”ti, gharato nikkaḍḍhāpesi. Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo sāvatthiṃ gantvā bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo vikāle kulāni upasaṅkamitvā sāmike anāpucchā seyyaṃ santharitvā abhinisīdissantipi abhinipajjissantipī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo vikāle kulāni upasaṅkamitvā sāmike anāpucchā seyyaṃ santharitvā abhinisīdantipi abhinipajjantipīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo vikāle kulāni upasaṅkamitvā sāmike anāpucchā seyyaṃ santharitvā abhinisīdissantipi abhinipajjissantipi! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo [T 0.0124] imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

864. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, many bhikkhunīs, while traveling through the country of the Kosalans to Sāvatthī, approached a certain village in the evening. Having gone up to a certain brahmin's household, they asked for lodging. Then that brahmin woman said this to those bhikkhunīs: “Wait, venerable ladies, until the brahmin comes.” The bhikkhunīs, thinking, “We will wait until the brahmin comes,” spread out bedding; some sat down, and some lay down. Then that brahmin, having come at night, said this to that brahmin woman: “Who are these?” “They are bhikkhunīs, my lord.” “Drive out these shaven-headed wretches!” he said, and had them driven out from the house. Then those bhikkhunīs, having gone to Sāvatthī, related this matter to the other bhikkhunīs. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could bhikkhunīs, having approached families at the wrong time without asking the owners, spread out bedding and then sit down and lie down?” … “Is it true, monks, that bhikkhunīs, having approached families at the wrong time without asking the owners, spread out bedding and then sit down and lie down?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, monks, could bhikkhunīs, having approached families at the wrong time without asking the owners, spread out bedding and then sit down and lie down? This, monks, does not conduce to the faith of the faithless... And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

865. “Yā [M 0.0361] pana bhikkhunī vikāle kulāni upasaṅkamitvā sāmike anāpucchā seyyaṃ santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā abhinisīdeyya vā abhinipajjeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

865. Whatever bhikkhunī, having approached families at the wrong time and without asking the owners, should spread out bedding or have it spread out, and should then sit down or lie down, incurs an offense requiring expiation.

866. Yā [V 0.0376] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

866. 'Whatever' means: whatever kind of… and so on. 'Bhikkhunī' means: … and so on … in this sense, 'bhikkhunī' is intended.

Vikālo nāma atthaṅgate sūriye yāva aruṇuggamanā.

By 'the wrong time' is meant the period from sunset until the appearance of dawn.

Kulaṃ nāma cattāri kulāni – khattiyakulaṃ, brāhmaṇakulaṃ, vessakulaṃ suddakulaṃ. Upasaṅkamitvāti tattha gantvā.

By 'a family' is meant the four families: the warrior family, the brahmin family, the merchant family, and the commoner family. 'Having approached' means having gone there.

Sāmike anāpucchāti yo tasmiṃ kule manusso sāmiko dātuṃ, taṃ anāpucchā.

'Without asking the owners' means: without asking the person in that family who is the master with authority to give.

Seyyaṃ nāma antamaso paṇṇasanthāropi. Santharitvāti sayaṃ santharitvā. Santharāpetvāti [P 4.0275] aññaṃ santharāpetvā. Abhinisīdeyyāti tasmiṃ abhinisīdati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Abhinipajjeyyāti tasmiṃ abhinipajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

By 'bedding' is meant, at the very least, even a spread of leaves. 'Having spread it out' means having spread it out oneself. 'Having had it spread out' means having had another spread it out. 'Should sit down' means: if one sits down on it, one incurs an offense requiring expiation. 'Should lie down' means: if one lies down on it, one incurs an offense requiring expiation.

867. Anāpucchite anāpucchitasaññā seyyaṃ santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā abhinisīdati vā abhinipajjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anāpucchite vematikā seyyaṃ santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā abhinisīdati vā abhinipajjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anāpucchite āpucchitasaññā seyyaṃ santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā abhinisīdati vā abhinipajjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

867. When permission has not been asked, and one perceives it as not having been asked, if one spreads out bedding or has it spread out, and then sits or lies down, one incurs an offense requiring expiation. When permission has not been asked, and one is in doubt, if one spreads out bedding or has it spread out, and then sits or lies down, one incurs an offense requiring expiation. When permission has not been asked, but one perceives it as having been asked, if one spreads out bedding or has it spread out, and then sits or lies down, one incurs an offense requiring expiation.

Āpucchite anāpucchitasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Āpucchite vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Āpucchite āpucchitasaññā, anāpatti.

When permission has been asked, but one perceives it as not having been asked, one incurs an offense of wrong-doing. When permission has been asked, and one is in doubt, one incurs an offense of wrong-doing. When permission has been asked, and one perceives it as having been asked, there is no offense.

868. Anāpatti [T 0.0125] āpucchā seyyaṃ santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā abhinisīdati vā abhinipajjati vā, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

868. There is no offense: if one asks permission before spreading out bedding or having it spread out, and then sitting or lying down; for one who is sick; in times of calamity; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Seventh Training Rule is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Eighth Training Rule

869. Tena [M 0.0362][V 0.0377] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhaddāya kāpilāniyā antevāsinī bhikkhunī bhaddaṃ kāpilāniṃ sakkaccaṃ upaṭṭheti. Bhaddā kāpilānī bhikkhuniyo etadavoca – “ayaṃ maṃ, ayye, bhikkhunī sakkacaṃ upaṭṭheti, imissāhaṃ cīvaraṃ dassāmī”ti. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī duggahitena dūpadhāritena paraṃ ujjhāpesi – “ahaṃ kirāyye, ayyaṃ na sakkaccaṃ upaṭṭhemi, na kira me ayyā cīvaraṃ dassatī”ti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī duggahitena dūpadhāritena paraṃ ujjhāpessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī duggahitena dūpadhāritena paraṃ ujjhāpetīti ujjhāpesīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī duggahitena dūpadhāritena paraṃ ujjhāpessati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

869. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. At that time a nun who was a resident pupil of Bhaddā Kāpilānī attended to Bhaddā Kāpilānī with care. Bhaddā Kāpilānī said to the nuns: “This nun, venerable ladies, attends to me with care; I will give her a robe.” Then that nun, with wrong grasping and bad apprehension, caused another to be disparaged, saying: “It seems, venerable ladies, that I do not attend to the venerable lady with care; it seems the venerable lady will not give me a robe.” Those nuns who were modest … complained, criticized, and were disgusted: “How could a nun, with wrong grasping and bad apprehension, cause another to be disparaged?” … “Is it true, monks, that a nun, with wrong grasping and bad apprehension, caused another to be disparaged?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her … “How could a nun, monks, with wrong grasping and bad apprehension, cause another to be disparaged? This, monks, is not for the inspiration of the uninspired… And so, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule:

870. “Yā pana bhikkhunī duggahitena dūpadhāritena paraṃ ujjhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

870. “Whatever nun, with wrong grasping and bad apprehension, should cause another to be disparaged, it is an offense requiring confession.”

871. Yā [T 0.0126] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

871. Whatever: whoever, of whatever kind… nun: …in this context, this is the nun who is meant.

Duggahitenāti aññathā gahitena uggahitena (ka.).

With wrong grasping: with grasping otherwise.

Dūpadhāritenāti aññathā upadhāritena.

With bad apprehension: with apprehension otherwise.

Paranti upasampannaṃ ujjhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

Another: if she causes a fully ordained person to be disparaged, it is an offense requiring confession.

872. Upasampannāya [P 4.0276] upasampannasaññā ujjhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampannāya vematikā ujjhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampannāya anupasampannasaññā ujjhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

872. If she causes a fully ordained person to be disparaged, while perceiving her as fully ordained, it is an offense requiring confession. If she causes a fully ordained person to be disparaged, while being in doubt, it is an offense requiring confession. If she causes a fully ordained person to be disparaged, while perceiving her as not fully ordained, it is an offense requiring confession.

Anupasampannaṃ [M 0.0363] ujjhāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya upasampannasaññā, āpatti [V 0.0378] dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya anupasampannasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If she causes a non-ordained person to be disparaged, it is an offense of wrong conduct. If she causes a non-ordained person to be disparaged, while perceiving her as fully ordained, it is an offense of wrong conduct. If she causes a non-ordained person to be disparaged, while being in doubt, it is an offense of wrong conduct. If she causes a non-ordained person to be disparaged, while perceiving her as not fully ordained, it is an offense of wrong conduct.

873. Anāpatti ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

873. There is no offense for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Eighth Training Rule is concluded.

9. Navamasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Ninth Training Rule

874. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo attano bhaṇḍakaṃ apassantiyo caṇḍakāḷiṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavocuṃ – “apāyye, amhākaṃ, bhaṇḍakaṃ passeyyāsī”ti? Caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “ahameva nūna corī, ahameva nūna [T 0.0127] alajjinī, yā ayyāyo attano bhaṇḍakaṃ apassantiyo tā maṃ evamāhaṃsu – ‘apāyye, amhākaṃ bhaṇḍakaṃ passeyyāsī’ti? Sacāhaṃ, ayye, tumhākaṃ bhaṇḍakaṃ gaṇhāmi, assamaṇī homi, brahmacariyā cavāmi, nirayaṃ upapajjāmi; yā pana maṃ abhūtena evamāha sāpi assamaṇī hotu, brahmacariyā cavatu, nirayaṃ upapajjatū”ti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā caṇḍakāḷī attānampi parampi nirayenapi brahmacariyenapi abhisapissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī attānampi parampi nirayenapi brahmacariyenapi abhisapatīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti.
