Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī attānampi parampi nirayenapi brahmacariyenapi abhisapissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

874. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, some nuns, not seeing their belongings, said this to the nun Caṇḍakāḷī: “Venerable lady, have you perhaps seen our belongings?” The nun Caṇḍakāḷī complained, criticized, and was disgusted: “Am I then a thief? Am I then shameless, that the venerable ladies, not seeing their own belongings, say this to me: ‘Venerable lady, have you perhaps seen our belongings?’ If I, venerable ladies, take your belongings, may I not be a contemplative, may I fall from the holy life, may I be reborn in hell. And whoever says this to me falsely, may she too not be a contemplative, may she fall from the holy life, may she be reborn in hell.” Those nuns who were of few wants… complained, criticized, and were disgusted: “How indeed could the venerable lady Caṇḍakāḷī curse both herself and another with hell and with the holy life?”… “Is it true, monks, that the nun Caṇḍakāḷī curses both herself and another with hell and with the holy life?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, monks, could the nun Caṇḍakāḷī curse both herself and another with hell and with the holy life? This, monks, is not for the inspiration of the uninspired… And so, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule thus:

875. “Yā pana bhikkhunī attānaṃ vā paraṃ vā nirayena vā brahmacariyena vā abhisapeyya, pācittiyya”nti.

875. “Whatever nun should curse herself or another with hell or with the holy life, it is an offense requiring confession.”

876. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

876. Whatever: whoever of whatever kind… nun: …the nun intended in this context.

Attānanti [M 0.0364][V 0.0379] paccattaṃ. Paranti upasampannaṃ. Nirayena vā brahmacariyena vā abhisapati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

Herself: one’s own person. Another: a fully ordained nun. If she curses with hell or with the holy life, it is an offense requiring confession.

877. Upasampannāya [P 4.0277] upasampannasaññā nirayena vā brahmacariyena [T 0.0128] vā abhisapati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampannāya vematikā nirayena vā brahmacariyena vā abhisapati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampannāya anupasampannasaññā nirayena vā brahmacariyena vā abhisapati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

877. If she curses a fully ordained nun, whom she perceives as fully ordained, with hell or with the holy life, it is an offense requiring confession. If she curses a fully ordained nun, while being in doubt, with hell or with the holy life, it is an offense requiring confession. If she curses a fully ordained nun, whom she perceives as not fully ordained, with hell or with the holy life, it is an offense requiring confession.

Tiracchānayoniyā vā pettivisayena vā manussadobhaggena vā abhisapati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannaṃ abhisapati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya upasampannasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya anupasampannasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If she curses with birth in the animal realm, or in the realm of spirits, or with an unfortunate human state, it is an offense of wrong conduct. If she curses one who is not fully ordained, it is an offense of wrong conduct. If she curses one who is not fully ordained, whom she perceives as fully ordained, it is an offense of wrong conduct. If she curses one who is not fully ordained, while being in doubt, it is an offense of wrong conduct. If she curses one who is not fully ordained, whom she perceives as not fully ordained, it is an offense of wrong conduct.

878. Anāpatti atthapurekkhārāya, dhammapurekkhārāya, anusāsanipurekkhārāya, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

878. There is no offense for one who speaks for the sake of a purpose, for the sake of the Dhamma, or for the sake of instruction; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Navamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Ninth Training Rule is concluded.

10. Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Tenth Training Rule

879. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ bhaṇḍitvā attānaṃ vadhitvā vadhitvā rodati. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā caṇḍakāḷī attānaṃ vadhitvā vadhitvā rodissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī attānaṃ vadhitvā vadhitvā rodatīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… [T 0.0129] kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī attānaṃ vadhitvā vadhitvā rodissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

879. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's park. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī, having quarreled with the bhikkhunīs, struck herself again and again and wept. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes... they criticized, censured, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the venerable Caṇḍakāḷī strike herself again and again and weep?” ... “Is it true, monks, as is said, that the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī strikes herself again and again and weeps?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her... “How indeed, monks, could the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī strike herself again and again and weep? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident... And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

880. “Yā [M 0.0365][V 0.0380] pana bhikkhunī attānaṃ vadhitvā vadhitvā rodeyya, pācittiya”nti.

880. “Whatever bhikkhunī should strike herself again and again and weep, it is a pācittiya offense.”

881. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

881. ‘Whatever’ means: of whatever kind... ‘A bhikkhunī’ means: ...in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Attānanti paccattaṃ. Vadhitvā vadhitvā rodati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Vadhati na rodati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Rodati na vadhati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

‘Herself’ means: one's own person. If she strikes herself again and again and weeps, there is an offense of pācittiya. If she strikes but does not weep, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If she weeps but does not strike, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

882. Anāpatti ñātibyasanena vā bhogabyasanena vā rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhā rodati na vadhati, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

882. There is no offense if, being afflicted by the loss of relatives, the loss of wealth, or the affliction of disease, she weeps but does not strike herself; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Tenth Training Rule is concluded.

Andhakāravaggo dutiyo.

The Second Chapter on Darkness.

3. Naggavaggo

3. The Chapter on Nakedness

1. Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The First Training Rule

883. Tena [P 4.0278] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā mahāva. 350 bhikkhuniyo aciravatiyā nadiyā vesiyāhi saddhiṃ naggā ekatitthe nahāyanti. Vesiyā tā bhikkhuniyo uppaṇḍesuṃ – “kiṃ nu kho nāma tumhākaṃ, ayye, daharānaṃ daharānaṃ daharānaṃ (sī.) brahmacariyaṃ ciṇṇena, nanu nāma kāmā paribhuñjitabbā[T 0.0130]! Yadā jiṇṇā bhavissatha tadā brahmacariyaṃ carissatha. Evaṃ tumhākaṃ ubho atthā pariggahitā bhavissantī”ti. Bhikkhuniyo vesiyāhi uppaṇḍiyamānā maṅkū ahesuṃ. Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo upassayaṃ gantvā bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ [V 0.0381] paññapessāmi dasa atthavase paṭicca – saṅghasuṭṭhutāya…pe… vinayānuggahāya. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

883. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's park. Now at that time, many bhikkhunīs were bathing naked together with courtesans at the same bathing place in the Aciravatī River. The courtesans ridiculed those bhikkhunīs, saying: “Venerable ladies, what benefit is there for you, who are young, in having practiced the holy life? Should not sensual pleasures be enjoyed? When you become old, then you may practice the holy life. In this way, both aims will be secured by you.” The bhikkhunīs, being ridiculed by the courtesans, became disconcerted. Then those bhikkhunīs, having gone to their residence, related this matter to the other bhikkhunīs. The bhikkhunīs related this matter to the bhikkhus. The bhikkhus related this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus: “In that case, monks, I will lay down a training rule for the bhikkhunīs, based on ten benefits: for the well-being of the Saṅgha... for the support of the Vinaya. And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule thus:

884. “Yā [M 0.0366] pana bhikkhunī naggā nahāyeyya, pācittiya”nti.

884. “Whatever bhikkhunī should bathe naked, it is a pācittiya offense.”

885. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

885. ‘Whatever’ means: of whatever kind... ‘A bhikkhunī’ means: ...in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Naggā nahāyeyyāti anivatthā vā apārutā vā nahāyati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Nahānapariyosāne āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should bathe naked’ means: if she bathes without wearing a lower garment or without wearing an upper garment, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the attempt. At the conclusion of bathing, there is an offense of pācittiya.

886. Anāpatti acchinnacīvarikāya vā naṭṭhacīvarikāya vā, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

886. There is no offense for one whose robe has been stolen or whose robe is lost; in times of calamity; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The first training rule is concluded.

2. Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Second Training Rule

887. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavatā bhikkhunīnaṃ mahāva. 351 udakasāṭikā [T 0.0131] anuññātā hoti[P 4.0279]. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo – “bhagavatā udakasāṭikā anuññātā”ti appamāṇikāyo udakasāṭikāyo dhāresuṃ dhārenti (pāci. 531-545). Puratopi pacchatopi ākaḍḍhantā āhiṇḍanti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo appamāṇikāyo udakasāṭikāyo dhāressantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo appamāṇikāyo udakasāṭikāyo dhārentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo appamāṇikāyo udakasāṭikāyo dhāressanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

887. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. At that time, a bathing cloth had been allowed for the bhikkhunīs by the Blessed One. The bhikkhunīs of the group of six, thinking, “A bathing cloth has been allowed by the Blessed One,” wore bathing cloths of excessive size. They wandered about, pulling them from the front and from the back. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six wear bathing cloths of excessive size?”… “Is it true, as is said, monks, that the bhikkhunīs of the group of six wear bathing cloths of excessive size?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, monks, can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six wear bathing cloths of excessive size! This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

888. “Udakasāṭikaṃ pana bhikkhuniyā kārayamānāya pamāṇikā kāretabbā. Tatridaṃ pamāṇaṃ [V 0.0382] – dīghaso catasso vidatthiyo, sugatavidatthiyā; tiriyaṃ dve vidatthiyo. Taṃ atikkāmentiyā chedanakaṃ pācittiya”nti.

888. “A bhikkhunī having a bathing cloth made should have it made to the standard size. Herein, this is the standard size: in length, four spans by the Sugata's span; in width, two spans. For one who exceeds that, it is a pācittiya offense that requires cutting.”

889. Udakasāṭikā [M 0.0367] nāma yāya nivatthā nivatthāya (syā.) nahāyati.

889. A bathing cloth is that which is worn for bathing.

Kārayamānāyāti karontiyā vā kārāpentiyā vā.

‘Having it made’ means making it herself or causing it to be made.

Pamāṇikā kāretabbā. Tatridaṃ pamāṇaṃ – dīghaso catasso vidatthiyo, sugatavidatthiyā; tiriyaṃ dve vidatthiyo. Taṃ atikkāmetvā karoti vā kārāpeti vā, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena chinditvā pācittiyaṃ desetabbaṃ.

It should be made to the standard size. Herein, this is the standard size: in length, four spans by the Sugata's span; in width, two spans. If, having exceeded that, she makes it or has it made, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the attempt. Upon receiving it, it should be cut, and the pācittiya offense is to be confessed.

890. Attanā vippakataṃ attanā pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa[T 0.0132]. Attanā vippakataṃ parehi pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Parehi vippakataṃ attanā pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Parehi vippakataṃ parehi pariyosāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

890. If she herself finishes what she herself has left unfinished, there is a pācittiya offense. If she has others finish what she herself has left unfinished, there is a pācittiya offense. If she herself finishes what others have left unfinished, there is a pācittiya offense. If she has others finish what others have left unfinished, there is a pācittiya offense.

Aññassatthāya karoti vā kārāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Aññena kataṃ paṭilabhitvā paribhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If she makes it or has it made for the sake of another, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If, having received one made by another, she uses it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

891. Anāpatti pamāṇikaṃ karoti, ūnakaṃ karoti, aññena kataṃ pamāṇātikkantaṃ paṭilabhitvā chinditvā paribhuñjati, vitānaṃ vā bhūmattharaṇaṃ vā sāṇipākāraṃ vā bhisiṃ vā bibbohanaṃ vā karoti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

891. There is no offense if she makes it to the standard size; if she makes it smaller; if, having received one made by another that exceeds the standard size, she cuts it and then uses it; if she makes a canopy, a floor-covering, a curtain, a mattress, or a pillow; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The second training rule is concluded.

3. Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Third Training Rule

892. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarissā bhikkhuniyā mahagghe cīvaradusse cīvaraṃ dukkaṭaṃ hoti dussibbitaṃ. Thullanandā bhikkhunī [P 4.0280] taṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “sundaraṃ kho idaṃ [V 0.0383] te, ayye, cīvaradussaṃ; cīvarañca kho dukkaṭaṃ dussibbita”nti. “Visibbemi, ayye, sibbissasī”ti? “Āmāyye, sibbissāmī”ti. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī taṃ cīvaraṃ visibbetvā thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā [M 0.0368] adāsi. Thullanandā bhikkhunī – “sibbissāmi sibbissāmī”ti neva sibbati na sibbāpanāya [T 0.0133] ussukkaṃ karoti. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ visibbāpetvā neva sibbissati na sibbāpanāya ussukkaṃ karissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ visibbāpetvā neva sibbati na sibbāpanāya ussukkaṃ karotīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ visibbāpetvā neva sibbissati na sibbāpanāya ussukkaṃ karissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

892. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī's robe, made from a valuable robe-cloth, was badly made and badly sewn. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā said this to that bhikkhunī: 'Venerable, this robe-cloth of yours is indeed beautiful, but the robe is badly made and badly sewn.' 'Venerable, I shall unsew it. Will you sew it?' 'Yes, Venerable, I will sew it.' Then that bhikkhunī, having unsewn that robe, gave it to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, saying, 'I will sew it, I will sew it,' neither sewed it nor made an effort to have it sewn. Then that bhikkhunī told this matter to the other bhikkhunīs. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes... criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: 'How indeed could the Venerable Thullanandā, having caused a bhikkhunī's robe to be unsewn, neither sew it nor make an effort to have it sewn?' ... 'Is it true, it is said, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having caused a bhikkhunī's robe to be unsewn, neither sews it nor makes an effort to have it sewn?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her... 'How indeed, Bhikkhus, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having caused a bhikkhunī's robe to be unsewn, neither sew it nor make an effort to have it sewn! This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced... And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

893. “Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ visibbetvā vā visibbāpetvā vā sā pacchā anantarāyikinī neva sibbeyya na sibbāpanāya ussukkaṃ kareyya, aññatra catūhapañcāhā, pācittiya”nti.

893. Whatever bhikkhunī, having unsewn a robe of another bhikkhunī herself or having caused it to be unsewn, should later, being without obstacle, neither sew it herself nor make an effort to have it sewn, except for four or five days, it is an offense of pācittiya.

894. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

894. 'Whatever' means: whatever, of whatever sort... and so on... 'A bhikkhunī' means... and so on... this is the bhikkhunī who is intended in this meaning.

Bhikkhuniyāti aññāya bhikkhuniyā.

'Of a bhikkhunī' means: of another bhikkhunī.

Cīvaraṃ nāma channaṃ cīvarānaṃ aññataraṃ cīvaraṃ.

A robe, by name, is any one of the six robes.

Visibbetvāti sayaṃ visibbetvā. Visibbāpetvāti aññaṃ visibbāpetvā.

'Having unsewn' means: having unsewn it herself. 'Having caused to be unsewn' means: having caused another to unsew it.

Sā pacchā anantarāyikinīti asati antarāye.

'She, later, being without obstacle' means: when there is no obstacle.

Neva sibbeyyāti na sayaṃ sibbeyya. Na sibbāpanāya ussukkaṃ kareyyāti na aññaṃ āṇāpeyya.

'Should neither sew' means: should not sew it herself. 'Nor make an effort to have it sewn' means: should not command another.

Aññatra [V 0.0384] catūhapañcāhāti ṭhapetvā [T 0.0134] catūhapañcāhaṃ. “Neva sibbissāmi na sibbāpanāya ussukkaṃ karissāmī”ti dhuraṃ nikkhittamatte āpatti pācittiyassa.

'Except for four or five days' means: setting aside four or five days. At the very moment of laying down the responsibility, thinking, 'I will neither sew it nor make an effort to have it sewn,' there is an offense of pācittiya.

895. Upasampannāya upasampannasaññā cīvaraṃ visibbetvā vā visibbāpetvā vā sā pacchā anantarāyikinī neva sibbati na sibbāpanāya ussukkaṃ karoti, aññatra catūhapañcāhā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampannāya vematikā [M 0.0369] cīvaraṃ visibbetvā vā visibbāpetvā vā sā pacchā anantarāyikinī neva sibbati na sibbāpanāya ussukkaṃ karoti, aññatra catūhapañcāhā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampannāya anupasampannasaññā cīvaraṃ visibbetvā vā visibbāpetvā vā sā pacchā anantarāyikinī neva sibbati na sibbāpanāya ussukkaṃ karoti, aññatra catūhapañcāhā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

895. If, regarding a fully ordained bhikkhunī, one is perceptive that she is fully ordained, and having unsewn or caused a robe to be unsewn, she later, being without obstacle, neither sews it nor makes an effort to have it sewn, except for four or five days, there is an offense of pācittiya. If, regarding a fully ordained bhikkhunī, one is doubtful... there is an offense of pācittiya. If, regarding a fully ordained bhikkhunī, one is perceptive that she is not fully ordained... there is an offense of pācittiya.

Aññaṃ parikkhāraṃ visibbetvā vā visibbāpetvā vā sā pacchā anantarāyikinī neva sibbati na sibbāpanāya ussukkaṃ karoti, aññatra catūhapañcāhā, āpatti dukkaṭassa[P 4.0281]. Anupasampannāya cīvaraṃ vā aññaṃ vā parikkhāraṃ visibbetvā vā visibbāpetvā vā sā pacchā anantarāyikinī neva sibbati na sibbāpanāya ussukkaṃ karoti, aññatra catūhapañcāhā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya upasampannasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya anupasampannasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one unsews or causes to be unsewn another requisite, and later, being without obstacle, neither sews it nor makes an effort to have it sewn, except for four or five days, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If one unsews or causes to be unsewn a robe or another requisite for one who is not fully ordained, and later, being without obstacle, neither sews it nor makes an effort to have it sewn, except for four or five days, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If, regarding one who is not fully ordained, one is perceptive that she is fully ordained, and then neither sews it nor makes an effort to have it sewn, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If, regarding one who is not fully ordained, one is doubtful, and then neither sews it nor makes an effort to have it sewn, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If, regarding one who is not fully ordained, one is perceptive that she is not fully ordained, and then neither sews it nor makes an effort to have it sewn, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

896. Anāpatti [T 0.0135] sati antarāye, pariyesitvā na labhati, karontī catūhapañcāhaṃ atikkāmeti, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

896. There is no offense: if there is an obstacle; if, having searched, she does not obtain it; if, while working on it, she exceeds four or five days; for one who is sick; in times of danger; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The third training rule is concluded.

4. Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Fourth Training Rule

897. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo bhikkhunīnaṃ hatthe cīvaraṃ nikkhipitvā santaruttarena janapadacārikaṃ pakkamanti. Tāni cīvarāni ciraṃ nikkhittāni kaṇṇakitāni honti. Tāni bhikkhuniyo otāpenti. Bhikkhuniyo tā bhikkhuniyo etadavocuṃ – “kassimāni[V 0.0385], ayye, cīvarāni kaṇṇakitānī”ti? Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo bhikkhunīnaṃ hatthe cīvaraṃ nikkhipitvā santaruttarena janapadacārikaṃ [M 0.0370] pakkamissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo bhikkhunīnaṃ hatthe cīvaraṃ nikkhipitvā santaruttarena janapadacārikaṃ pakkamantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo bhikkhunīnaṃ hatthe cīvaraṃ nikkhipitvā santaruttarena janapadacārikaṃ pakkamissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

897. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, in the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, bhikkhunīs, having placed a robe in the hands of other bhikkhunīs, went on a tour of the country with only their lower and upper garments. Those robes, having been put aside for a long time, became moldy. Those bhikkhunīs aired them in the sun. Other bhikkhunīs said to those bhikkhunīs, “Venerable ladies, whose moldy robes are these?” Then those bhikkhunīs reported this matter to the other bhikkhunīs. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, “How indeed can bhikkhunīs, having placed a robe in the hands of other bhikkhunīs, go on a tour of the country with only their lower and upper garments?” ... “Is it true, monks, that bhikkhunīs, having placed a robe in the hands of other bhikkhunīs, go on a tour of the country with only their lower and upper garments?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... “How indeed, monks, can bhikkhunīs, having placed a robe in the hands of other bhikkhunīs, go on a tour of the country with only their lower and upper garments? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the faithless... And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule in this way:

898. “Yā pana [T 0.0136] bhikkhunī pañcāhikaṃ saṅghāṭicāraṃ saṅghāṭivāraṃ (syā.) atikkāmeyya, pācittiya”nti.

898. “Whatever bhikkhunī should exceed the five-day period for the rotation of robes, it is a pācittiya offense.”

899. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

899. ‘Whatever’ means: whichever, of whatever sort... ‘Bhikkhunī’ means... the bhikkhunī who is intended in this context.

Pañcāhikaṃ saṅghāṭicāraṃ atikkāmeyyāti pañcamaṃ divasaṃ pañca cīvarāni neva nivāseti na pārupati na otāpeti, pañcamaṃ divasaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should exceed the five-day period for the rotation of robes’ means: on the fifth day, she neither wears as a lower garment, nor drapes as an upper garment, nor airs the five robes in the sun; if she lets the fifth day pass, she incurs a pācittiya offense.

900. Pañcāhātikkante atikkantasaññā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Pañcāhātikkante vematikā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Pañcāhātikkante anatikkantasaññā[P 4.0282], āpatti pācittiyassa.

900. When the five-day period has passed, with the perception that it has passed, there is a pācittiya offense. When the five-day period has passed, while being in doubt, there is a pācittiya offense. When the five-day period has passed, with the perception that it has not passed, there is a pācittiya offense.

Pañcāhānatikkante atikkantasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Pañcāhānatikkante vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Pañcāhānatikkante anatikkantasaññā, anāpatti.

When the five-day period has not passed, with the perception that it has passed, there is a dukkaṭa offense. When the five-day period has not passed, while being in doubt, there is a dukkaṭa offense. When the five-day period has not passed, with the perception that it has not passed, there is no offense.

901. Anāpatti pañcamaṃ divasaṃ pañca cīvarāni nivāseti vā pārupati vā otāpeti vā, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

901. There is no offense: if on the fifth day she wears as a lower garment, or drapes as an upper garment, or airs the five robes in the sun; for one who is sick; in times of danger; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fourth Training Rule is finished.

5. Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Fifth Training Rule

902. Tena [V 0.0386] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī piṇḍāya caritvā allacīvaraṃ pattharitvā vihāraṃ pāvisi. Aññatarā [T 0.0137] bhikkhunī taṃ [M 0.0371] cīvaraṃ pārupitvā gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Sā nikkhamitvā bhikkhuniyo pucchi – “apāyye, mayhaṃ cīvaraṃ passeyyāthā”ti? Bhikkhuniyo tassā bhikkhuniyā etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī mayhaṃ cīvaraṃ anāpucchā pārupissatī”ti! Atha kho sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ anāpucchā pārupissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ anāpucchā pārupatīti pārupīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ anāpucchā pārupissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

902. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī, having wandered for alms, spread out her wet robe and entered the monastery. Another bhikkhunī, having put on that robe, entered the village for alms. That bhikkhunī, having come out, asked the bhikkhunīs: “Venerable ladies, have you seen my robe?” The bhikkhunīs informed that bhikkhunī of this matter. Then that bhikkhunī complained, scorned, and protested: “How indeed could a bhikkhunī put on my robe without asking?” Then that bhikkhunī informed the bhikkhunīs of this matter. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… complained, scorned, and protested: “How indeed could a bhikkhunī put on another bhikkhunī’s robe without asking?” … “Is it true, monks, that a bhikkhunī put on another bhikkhunī’s robe without asking?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, monks, could a bhikkhunī put on another bhikkhunī’s robe without asking? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

903. “Yā pana bhikkhunī cīvarasaṅkamanīyaṃ dhāreyya, pācittiya”nti.

903. “Whatever bhikkhunī should wear a robe that is to be returned, it is a pācittiya offense.”

904. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

904. ‘Whatever’ means: whichever, of whatever sort… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… the bhikkhunī who is intended in this context.

Cīvarasaṅkamanīyaṃ nāma upasampannāya pañcannaṃ cīvarānaṃ aññataraṃ cīvaraṃ tassā vā adinnaṃ taṃ vā anāpucchā nivāseti vā pārupati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A robe that is to be returned means any one of the five robes of a fully ordained bhikkhunī. If one wears it as a lower garment or as an upper garment when it has not been given by her or without asking her, there is a pācittiya offense.

905. Upasampannāya upasampannasaññā cīvarasaṅkamanīyaṃ dhāreti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampannāya vematikā cīvarasaṅkamanīyaṃ dhāreti[T 0.0138], āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampannāya anupasampannasaññā cīvarasaṅkamanīyaṃ dhāreti, āpatti pācittiyassa[P 4.0283].

905. If she wears the robe to be returned of a fully ordained one, perceiving her as fully ordained, there is a pācittiya offense. If she wears the robe to be returned of a fully ordained one, being in doubt, there is a pācittiya offense. If she wears the robe to be returned of a fully ordained one, perceiving her as not fully ordained, there is a pācittiya offense.

Anupasampannāya cīvarasaṅkamanīyaṃ dhāreti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya upasampannasaññā[V 0.0387], āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya anupasampannasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one wears the robe to be returned of an unordained one, there is a dukkaṭa offense. In the case of an unordained one, if one perceives her as fully ordained, there is a dukkaṭa offense. In the case of an unordained one, if one is in doubt, there is a dukkaṭa offense. In the case of an unordained one, if one perceives her as unordained, there is a dukkaṭa offense.

906. Anāpatti sā vā deti, taṃ vā āpucchā nivāseti vā pārupati vā, acchinnacīvarikāya, naṭṭhacīvarikāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

906. There is no offense: if she (the owner) gives it; if one wears it as a lower or upper garment after asking her; for one whose robe has been snatched; for one whose robe is lost; in times of danger; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fifth Training Rule is finished.

6. Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Sixth Training Rule

907. Tena [M 0.0372] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā upaṭṭhākakulaṃ thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “bhikkhunisaṅghassa, ayye, cīvaraṃ dassāmā”ti. Thullanandā bhikkhunī – “tumhe bahukiccā bahukaraṇīyā”ti antarāyaṃ akāsi. Tena kho pana samayena tassa kulassa gharaṃ ḍayhati. Te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā amhākaṃ deyyadhammaṃ antarāyaṃ karissati! Ubhayenāmha paribāhirā parihīnā (sī.), bhogehi ca puññena cā”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ[T 0.0139]. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā gaṇassa cīvaralābhaṃ antarāyaṃ karissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī gaṇassa cīvaralābhaṃ antarāyaṃ akāsīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī gaṇassa cīvaralābhaṃ antarāyaṃ karissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

907. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time, the supporting family of the bhikkhunī Thullanandā said to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, “Venerable, we will give a robe to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs.” The bhikkhunī Thullanandā created an obstacle, saying, “You have many duties, many things to do.” Then at that time, the house of that family burned down. They complained, grumbled, and spoke disparagingly, “How could the venerable Thullanandā create an obstacle for our offering! We are excluded from both—from wealth and from merit!” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, grumbling, and speaking disparagingly. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… and so on… they too complained, grumbled, and spoke disparagingly, “How could the venerable Thullanandā create an obstacle for the community’s gain of a robe?” … and so on… “Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā created an obstacle for the community’s gain of a robe?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… and so on… “How, monks, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā create an obstacle for the community’s gain of a robe! This is not for the confidence of the unconfident… and so on… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

908. “Yā pana bhikkhunī gaṇassa cīvaralābhaṃ antarāyaṃ kareyya, pācittiya”nti.

908. “Whatever bhikkhunī should create an obstacle for the community’s gain of a robe, it is an offense of expiation.”

909. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

909. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever, of whatever kind… and so on… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… and so on… In this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Gaṇo nāma bhikkhunisaṅgho vuccati.

‘Community’ means the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs.

Cīvaraṃ [V 0.0388] nāma channaṃ cīvarānaṃ aññataraṃ cīvaraṃ vikappanupagaṃ pacchimaṃ.

‘Robe’ means any one of the six robes, at minimum that which is suitable for determination.

Antarāyaṃ [P 4.0284] kareyyāti “kathaṃ ime cīvaraṃ na imaṃ cīvaraṃ (ka.) dadeyyu”nti antarāyaṃ karoti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Aññaṃ parikkhāraṃ antarāyaṃ karoti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sambahulānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ vā ekabhikkhuniyā vā anupasampannāya vā cīvaraṃ vā aññaṃ vā parikkhāraṃ antarāyaṃ karoti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

‘Should create an obstacle’ means she creates an obstacle, thinking, ‘How might these people not give a robe?’—it is an offense of expiation. If she creates an obstacle regarding another requisite, it is an offense of wrong-doing. If she creates an obstacle regarding a robe or another requisite for many bhikkhunīs, for one bhikkhunī, or for an unordained woman, it is an offense of wrong-doing.

910. Anāpatti [M 0.0373] ānisaṃsaṃ dassetvā nivāreti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

910. There is no offense for one who prevents by showing the benefit, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Sixth Training Rule is concluded.

7. Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Seventh Training Rule

911. Tena [T 0.0140] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhunisaṅghassa akālacīvaraṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Atha kho bhikkhunisaṅgho taṃ cīvaraṃ bhājetukāmo sannipati. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā antevāsiniyo bhikkhuniyo pakkantā honti. Thullanandā bhikkhunī tā bhikkhuniyo etadavoca – “ayye, bhikkhuniyo pakkantā, na tāva cīvaraṃ bhājīyissatī”ti. Cīvaravibhaṅgaṃ paṭibāhi. Bhikkhuniyo na tāva cīvaraṃ bhājīyissatīti pakkamiṃsu vipakkamiṃsu (syā.). Thullanandā bhikkhunī antevāsinīsu bhikkhunīsu āgatāsu taṃ cīvaraṃ bhājāpesi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā dhammikaṃ cīvaravibhaṅgaṃ paṭibāhissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī dhammikaṃ cīvaravibhaṅgaṃ paṭibāhatīti paṭibāhīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī dhammikaṃ cīvaravibhaṅgaṃ paṭibāhissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

911. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. At that time, an out-of-season robe had arisen for the community of bhikkhunīs. Then the community of bhikkhunīs, wishing to distribute that robe, assembled. At that time, the resident pupils of the bhikkhunī Thullanandā had gone away. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā said to those bhikkhunīs, “Venerables, the bhikkhunīs have gone away; the robe should not be distributed yet.” She prevented the distribution of the robe. The bhikkhunīs, thinking, “The robe will not be distributed yet,” departed. When the resident pupil bhikkhunīs had returned, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā had that robe distributed. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… and so on… complained and criticized, saying, “How indeed could the venerable Thullanandā prevent a rightful distribution of robes?”… and so on… “Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā prevents a rightful distribution of robes?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… and so on… “How indeed, monks, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā prevent a rightful distribution of robes! This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… and so on… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

912. “Yā pana bhikkhunī dhammikaṃ cīvaravibhaṅgaṃ [T 0.0141] paṭibāheyya, pācittiya”nti.

912. “Whatever bhikkhunī should prevent a rightful distribution of robes, it is an offense of expiation.”

913. Yā [V 0.0389] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

913. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever, of whatever kind… and so on… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… and so on… In this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Dhammikonāma cīvaravibhaṅgo samaggo bhikkhunisaṅgho sannipatitvā bhājeti.

A rightful distribution of robes, so-called, is when a harmonious Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, having assembled, distributes them.

Paṭibāheyyāti [P 4.0285] kathaṃ imaṃ cīvaraṃ na bhājeyyāti cīvaraṃ bhājeyyāti (ka.) paṭibāhati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should prevent’ means: one prevents, thinking, ‘How might this robe not be distributed?’; it is an offense of expiation.

914. Dhammike [M 0.0374] dhammikasaññā paṭibāhati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammike vematikā paṭibāhati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Dhammike adhammikasaññā paṭibāhati, anāpatti. Adhammike dhammikasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammike vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammike adhammikasaññā, anāpatti.

914. If one prevents a rightful matter, perceiving it as rightful, it is an offense of expiation. If one prevents a rightful matter while being doubtful, it is an offense of wrong-doing. If one prevents a rightful matter, perceiving it as not rightful, there is no offense. If one prevents a not-rightful matter, perceiving it as rightful, it is an offense of wrong-doing. If one prevents a not-rightful matter while being doubtful, it is an offense of wrong-doing. If one prevents a not-rightful matter, perceiving it as not rightful, there is no offense.

915. Anāpatti ānisaṃsaṃ dassetvā paṭibāhati, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

915. There is no offense for one who prevents by showing a benefit, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Seventh Training Rule is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Eighth Training Rule

916. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī naṭānampi naṭakānampi laṅghakānampi sokajjhāyikānampi sokasāyikānampi (sī.) kumbhathūṇikānampi kumbhathuṇikānampi (ka.) samaṇacīvaraṃ deti – “mayhaṃ parisati parisatiṃ (sī.) vaṇṇaṃ bhāsathā”ti. Naṭāpi naṭakāpi laṅghakāpi sokajjhāyikāpi kumbhathūṇikāpi thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā parisati vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti – “ayyā thullanandā bahussutā bhāṇikā [T 0.0142] visāradā paṭṭā dhammiṃ kathaṃ kātuṃ; detha ayyāya, karotha ayyāyā”ti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā, tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā agārikassa samaṇacīvaraṃ dassatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī agārikassa samaṇacīvaraṃ detīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī agārikassa samaṇacīvaraṃ dassati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

916. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā gave a recluse's robe to actors, dancers, acrobats, magicians, and drummers, saying, “Speak of my virtue in the assembly.” And the actors, dancers, acrobats, magicians, and drummers spoke of the virtue of the bhikkhunī Thullanandā in the assembly, saying, “The venerable lady Thullanandā is very learned, a reciter, confident, and skilled in giving a Dhamma talk. Give to the venerable lady, pay respect to the venerable lady!” Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed can the venerable lady Thullanandā give a recluse's robe to a householder?” … “Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā gives a recluse's robe to a householder?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her … “How indeed, monks, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā give a recluse's robe to a householder? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced … And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

917. “Yā [V 0.0390] pana bhikkhunī agārikassa vā paribbājakassa vā paribbājikāya vā samaṇacīvaraṃ dadeyya, pācittiya”nti.

917. “Whatever bhikkhunī should give a recluse's robe to a householder, a male wanderer, or a female wanderer, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

918. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

918. Whatever means: whatever sort of… Bhikkhunī means: … this bhikkhunī is intended in this sense.

Agāriko [M 0.0375] nāma yo koci agāraṃ ajjhāvasati.

A householder means: anyone who lives in a house.

Paribbājako nāma bhikkhuñca sāmaṇerañca ṭhapetvā yo koci paribbājakasamāpanno.

A male wanderer means: excluding a bhikkhu and a sāmaṇera, anyone who has undertaken the life of a wanderer.

Paribbājikā nāma bhikkhuniñca sikkhamānañca sāmaṇeriñca ṭhapetvā yā kāci paribbājikasamāpannā.

A female wanderer means: excluding a bhikkhunī, a sikkhamānā, and a sāmaṇerī, any woman who has undertaken the life of a wanderer.

Samaṇacīvaraṃ [P 4.0286] nāma kappakataṃ vuccati. Deti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A recluse's robe means: what is called a robe that has been made proper. If she gives it, it is an offense of pācittiya.

919. Anāpatti mātāpitūnaṃ deti, tāvakālikaṃ deti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

919. There is no offense if she gives to her parents, if she gives it temporarily, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Eighth Training Rule is finished.

9. Navamasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Ninth Training Rule

920. Tena [T 0.0143] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā upaṭṭhākakulaṃ thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “sace mayaṃ, ayye, sakkoma, bhikkhunisaṅghassa cīvaraṃ dassāmā”ti. Tena kho pana samayena vassaṃvuṭṭhā bhikkhuniyo cīvaraṃ bhājetukāmā sannipatiṃsu. Thullanandā bhikkhunī tā bhikkhuniyo etadavoca – “āgametha, ayye, atthi bhikkhunisaṅghassa cīvarapaccāsā”ti. Bhikkhuniyo thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavocuṃ – “gacchāyye, taṃ cīvaraṃ jānāhī”ti. Thullanandā bhikkhunī yena taṃ kulaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te manusse etadavoca – “dethāvuso, bhikkhunisaṅghassa cīvara”nti. “Na mayaṃ, ayye, sakkoma bhikkhunisaṅghassa cīvaraṃ dātu”nti[V 0.0391]. Thullanandā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā dubbalacīvarapaccāsāya cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī dubbalacīvarapaccāsāya cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmetīti atikkāmesīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī [M 0.0376] dubbalacīvarapaccāsāya cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmessati[T 0.0144]! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

920. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the supporting family of the bhikkhunī Thullanandā said this to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā: “Venerable lady, if we are able, we will offer a robe to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha.” At that time, the bhikkhunīs who had completed the rains-residence assembled, wishing to divide the robes. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā said this to those bhikkhunīs: “Wait, venerable ladies, there is an expectation of a robe for the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha.” The bhikkhunīs said this to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā: “Go, venerable lady, and find out about that robe.” The bhikkhunī Thullanandā went to that family. Having approached, she said this to those people: “Lay supporters, give a robe to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha.” “Venerable lady, we are unable to give a robe to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha.” The bhikkhunī Thullanandā informed the bhikkhunīs of this matter. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed could the venerable Thullanandā cause the robe season to pass on account of a weak expectation of a robe?” … “Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā is causing the robe season to pass on account of a weak expectation of a robe?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, monks, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā cause the robe season to pass on account of a weak expectation of a robe? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

921. “Yā pana bhikkhunī dubbalacīvarapaccāsāya cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmeyya, pācittiya”nti.

921. “Whatever bhikkhunī, on account of a weak expectation of a robe, should cause the robe season to pass, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

922. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

922. Whatever means: whatever sort of… Bhikkhunī means: … this bhikkhunī is intended in this sense.

Dubbalacīvarapaccāsā nāma “sace mayaṃ sakkoma, dassāma karissāmā”ti vācā bhinnā hoti.

A weak expectation of a robe means that the words, “If we are able, we will give, we will make,” have been uttered.

Cīvarakālasamayo nāma anatthate kathine vassānassa pacchimo [P 4.0287] māso, atthate kathine pañca māsā.

The robe season means: when the kathina has not been spread, it is the last month of the rainy season; when the kathina has been spread, it is five months.

Cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmeyyāti anatthate kathine vassānassa pacchimaṃ divasaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Atthate kathine kathinuddhāradivasaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

Should cause the robe season to pass means: when the kathina has not been spread, if she causes the last day of the rainy season to pass, it is an offense of pācittiya. When the kathina has been spread, if she causes the day of the kathina's removal to pass, it is an offense of pācittiya.

923. Dubbalacīvare dubbalacīvarasaññā cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dubbalacīvare vematikā cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Dubbalacīvare adubbalacīvarasaññā cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmeti, anāpatti.

923. In the case of a weak expectation of a robe, if she perceives it as a weak expectation and causes the robe season to pass, it is an offense of pācittiya. In the case of a weak expectation of a robe, if she is in doubt and causes the robe season to pass, it is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of a weak expectation of a robe, if she perceives it as not a weak expectation and causes the robe season to pass, there is no offense.

Adubbalacīvare dubbalacīvarasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adubbalacīvare vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adubbalacīvare adubbalacīvarasaññā, anāpatti.

In the case of what is not a weak expectation of a robe, if she perceives it as a weak expectation and causes the robe season to pass, it is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of what is not a weak expectation of a robe, if she is in doubt and causes the robe season to pass, it is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of what is not a weak expectation of a robe, if she perceives it as not a weak expectation and causes the robe season to pass, there is no offense.

924. Anāpatti [V 0.0392] ānisaṃsaṃ dassetvā nivāreti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

924. There is no offense if she prevents it after pointing out the benefit; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Navamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Ninth Training Rule is finished.

10. Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Tenth Training Rule

925. Tena [T 0.0145][M 0.0377] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarena upāsakena saṅghaṃ uddissa vihāro kārāpito hoti. So tassa vihārassa mahe ubhatosaṅghassa akālacīvaraṃ dātukāmo hoti. Tena kho pana samayena ubhatosaṅghassa kathinaṃ atthataṃ hoti. Atha kho so upāsako saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā kathinuddhāraṃ yāci. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kathinaṃ uddharituṃ. Evañca pana bhikkhave kathinaṃ uddharitabbaṃ. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

925. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, a certain lay follower had a monastery built for the Saṅgha. On the occasion of the dedication of that monastery, he wished to give out-of-season robes to the two-fold Saṅgha. Now at that time, the kathina had been spread for the two-fold Saṅgha. Then that lay follower approached the Saṅgha and requested the withdrawal of the kathina. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow the withdrawal of the kathina. And, bhikkhus, the kathina should be withdrawn in this way. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent, capable bhikkhu:

926. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho kathinaṃ uddhareyya. Esā ñatti.

926. “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should withdraw the kathina. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho kathinaṃ uddharati. Yassāyasmato khamati kathinassa uddhāro, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The Saṅgha withdraws the kathina. Any venerable one who approves of the withdrawal of the kathina should remain silent; any who disapproves should speak.”

“Ubbhataṃ saṅghena kathinaṃ, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The kathina has been withdrawn by the Saṅgha. The Saṅgha approves, therefore it is silent. Thus I record it.”

927. Atha kho so upāsako bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā kathinuddhāraṃ yāci. Thullanandā bhikkhunī – “cīvaraṃ amhākaṃ [P 4.0288] bhavissatī”ti kathinuddhāraṃ paṭibāhi. Atha kho so upāsako ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo amhākaṃ kathinuddhāraṃ na dassantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho [T 0.0146] bhikkhuniyo tassa upāsakassa ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā dhammikaṃ kathinuddhāraṃ paṭibāhissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī dhammikaṃ kathinuddhāraṃ paṭibāhatīti paṭibāhīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, [V 0.0393] thullanandā bhikkhunī dhammikaṃ kathinuddhāraṃ paṭibāhissati[M 0.0378]! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

927. Then that lay follower approached the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and requested the withdrawal of the kathina. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, thinking, “We will get robes,” prevented the withdrawal of the kathina. Then that lay follower complained, grumbled, and spread criticism, saying: “How is it that the bhikkhunīs will not grant us the withdrawal of the kathina?” The bhikkhunīs heard that lay follower complaining, grumbling, and spreading criticism. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… complained, grumbled, and spread criticism, saying: “How is it that the venerable Thullanandā could prevent a lawful withdrawal of the kathina?”… “Is it true, as is said, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā prevents a lawful withdrawal of the kathina?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How is it, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā could prevent a lawful withdrawal of the kathina? This, bhikkhus, does not lead to the faith of the faithless… And so, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

928. “Yā pana bhikkhunī dhammikaṃ kathinuddhāraṃ paṭibāheyya, pācittiya”nti.

928. “Whatever bhikkhunī should prevent a lawful withdrawal of the kathina, it is an offense of expiation.”

929. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

929. ‘Whatever’ means: any whatever… ‘bhikkhunī’ means… this bhikkhunī is intended in this context.

Dhammiko nāma kathinuddhāro samaggo bhikkhunisaṅgho sannipatitvā uddharati.

A lawful withdrawal of the kathina is when the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha, having assembled in harmony, withdraws it.

Paṭibāheyyāti “kathaṃ idaṃ kathinaṃ na uddhareyyā”ti kathinaṃ uddhareyyāti (ka.) paṭibāhati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should prevent’ means: if, thinking, ‘How might this kathina not be withdrawn?’, she prevents it, it is an offense of expiation.

930. Dhammike dhammikasaññā paṭibāhati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammike vematikā paṭibāhati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Dhammike adhammikasaññā paṭibāhati, anāpatti. Adhammike dhammikasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammike vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammike adhammikasaññā, anāpatti.

930. If she prevents a lawful act, perceiving it as lawful, it is an offense of expiation. If she prevents a lawful act, while being in doubt, it is an offense of wrong conduct. If she prevents a lawful act, perceiving it as unlawful, there is no offense. If she prevents an unlawful act, perceiving it as lawful, it is an offense of wrong conduct. If she prevents an unlawful act, while being in doubt, it is an offense of wrong conduct. If she prevents an unlawful act, perceiving it as unlawful, there is no offense.

931. Anāpatti anisaṃsaṃ dassetvā paṭibāhati, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti[T 0.0147].

931. There is no offense if she prevents it by pointing out a benefit; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Tenth Training Rule is finished.

Naggavaggo tatiyo.

The Third Chapter, on Nudity, is finished.

4. Tuvaṭṭavaggo

4. The Chapter on Lying Down Together

1. Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The First Training Rule

932. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme[V 0.0394]. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo dve ekamañce tuvaṭṭenti. Manussā vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti [M 0.0379] khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo dve ekamañce tuvaṭṭessanti, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo dve ekamañce tuvaṭṭessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo dve ekamañce tuvaṭṭentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo dve ekamañce tuvaṭṭessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

932. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, two bhikkhunīs were lying down on a single couch. People, while wandering on a tour of the monastery, saw them and complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How can two bhikkhunīs lie down on a single couch, just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How can two bhikkhunīs lie down on a single couch?”… “Is it true, as is said, bhikkhus, that two bhikkhunīs are lying down on a single couch?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How, bhikkhus, can two bhikkhunīs lie down on a single couch? This, bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

933. “Yā [P 4.0289] pana bhikkhuniyo dve ekamañce tuvaṭṭeyyuṃ, pācittiya”nti.

933. “Should two bhikkhunīs lie down on a single couch, it is an offense of expiation.”

934. Yā [T 0.0148] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhuniyoti upasampannāyo vuccanti.

934. ‘Whatever’ means: any such… ‘bhikkhunīs’ means: fully ordained women are spoken of.

Dve ekamañce tuvaṭṭeyyunti ekāya nipannāya aparā nipajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ubho vā nipajjanti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Uṭṭhahitvā punappunaṃ nipajjanti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Two should lie down on a single couch’ means: when one is lying down, another lies down, it is an offense of expiation. If both lie down, it is an offense of expiation. If, having gotten up, they lie down again and again, it is an offense of expiation.

935. Anāpatti ekāya nipannāya aparā nisīdati, ubho vā nisīdanti, ummattikānaṃ, ādikammikānanti.

935. There is no offense if, when one is lying down, another sits down, or if both sit down; for those who are insane; for the first offenders.

Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The First Training Rule is finished.

2. Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Second Training Rule

936. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo dve ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā tuvaṭṭenti. Manussā vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo dve ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā tuvaṭṭessanti, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ [M 0.0380] khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo [V 0.0395] appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo dve ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā tuvaṭṭessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo dve ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā tuvaṭṭentīti? “Saccaṃ[T 0.0149], bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo dve ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā tuvaṭṭessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

936. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, two nuns were lying down with a single spread and covering. People, while wandering on a tour of the monastery, saw them and complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How can two nuns lie down with a single spread and covering, just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures?” The nuns heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those nuns who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How can two nuns lie down with a single spread and covering?”… “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that two nuns are lying down with a single spread and covering?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How, Bhikkhus, can two nuns lie down with a single spread and covering? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, Bhikkhus, the nuns should recite this training rule:

937. “Yā pana bhikkhuniyo dve ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā tuvaṭṭeyyuṃ, pācittiya”nti.

937. “Whatever two nuns should lie down with a single spread and covering, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

938. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhuniyoti upasampannāyo vuccanti.

938. ‘Whatever’ (yā pana) means: any such… (and so on). ‘Nuns’ (bhikkhuniyo) means: fully ordained nuns are spoken of.

Dve ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā tuvaṭṭeyyunti taññeva attharitvā taññeva pārupanti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Two should lie down with a single spread and covering’ means: if they lie down having spread that very same thing and also covering with that very same thing, it is an offense of pācittiya.

939. Ekattharaṇapāvuraṇe ekattharaṇapāvuraṇasaññā tuvaṭṭenti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ekattharaṇapāvuraṇe vematikā tuvaṭṭenti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ekattharaṇapāvuraṇe nānattharaṇapāvuraṇasaññā tuvaṭṭenti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

939. If they lie down with a single spread and covering, perceiving it as a single spread and covering, it is an offense of pācittiya. If they lie down with a single spread and covering, being in doubt, it is an offense of pācittiya. If they lie down with a single spread and covering, perceiving it as various spreads and coverings, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Ekattharaṇe nānāpāvuraṇe nānāpāvuraṇasaññā (ka.), āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nānattharaṇe ekapāvuraṇe ekapāvuraṇasaññā (ka.), āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nānattharaṇapāvuraṇe ekattharaṇapāvuraṇasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nānattharaṇapāvuraṇe vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nānattharaṇapāvuraṇe nānattharaṇapāvuraṇasaññā, anāpatti.

With a single spread and various coverings, it is an offense of wrongdoing. With various spreads and a single covering, it is an offense of wrongdoing. With various spreads and coverings, but perceiving it as a single spread and covering, it is an offense of wrongdoing. With various spreads and coverings, but being in doubt, it is an offense of wrongdoing. With various spreads and coverings, and perceiving it as various spreads and coverings, there is no offense.

940. Anāpatti vavatthānaṃ dassetvā nipajjanti, ummattikānaṃ, ādikammikānanti.

940. There is no offense if they lie down having indicated a boundary; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The second training rule is finished.

3. Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Third Training Rule

941. Tena [T 0.0150][P 4.0290][M 0.0381] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī bahussutā hoti bhāṇikā visāradā paṭṭā dhammiṃ kathaṃ kātuṃ. Bhaddāpi kāpilānī bahussutā hoti bhāṇikā visāradā paṭṭā [V 0.0396] dhammiṃ kathaṃ kātuṃ uḷārasambhāvitā. Manussā – “ayyā bhaddā kāpilānī bahussutā bhāṇikā visāradā paṭṭā dhammiṃ kathaṃ kātuṃ uḷārasambhāvitā”ti bhaddaṃ kāpilāniṃ paṭhamaṃ payirupāsitvā, pacchā thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ payirupāsanti. Thullanandā bhikkhunī issāpakatā – “imā kira appicchā santuṭṭhā pavivittā asaṃsaṭṭhā yā imā saññattibahulā viññattibahulā viharantī”ti bhaddāya kāpilāniyā purato caṅkamatipi tiṭṭhatipi nisīdatipi seyyampi kappeti uddisatipi uddisāpetipi sajjhāyampi karoti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā ayyāya bhaddāya kāpilāniyā sañcicca aphāsuṃ karissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī bhaddāya kāpilāniyā sañcicca aphāsuṃ karotīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī bhaddāya kāpilāniyā sañcicca aphāsuṃ karissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… [T 0.0151] evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

941. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. At that time, the bhikkhunī named Thullanandā was learned, a reciter of the Nikāyas, confident, and skilled in giving a Dhamma talk. Bhaddā Kāpilānī was also learned, a reciter of the Nikāyas, confident, skilled in giving a Dhamma talk, and was highly esteemed. People, thinking, “The venerable Bhaddā Kāpilānī is learned, a reciter of the Nikāyas, confident, skilled in giving a Dhamma talk, and is highly esteemed,” would first attend upon Bhaddā Kāpilānī, and afterwards they would attend upon the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, being overcome by jealousy, said this in front of Bhaddā Kāpilānī: “Those who live with much hinting and requesting are supposedly of few wishes, content, secluded, and unentangled.” She also walked, stood, sat, and made her bed in front of her; she also taught the Pāli, caused others to teach, and did recitation. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the venerable Thullanandā deliberately cause discomfort to the venerable Bhaddā Kāpilānī?”… “Is it true, as is said, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā deliberately causes discomfort to Bhaddā Kāpilānī?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā deliberately cause discomfort to Bhaddā Kāpilānī? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And thus, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

942. “Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā sañcicca aphāsuṃ kareyya, pācittiya”nti.

942. “Whatever bhikkhunī should deliberately cause discomfort to another bhikkhunī, it is an offense entailing expiation.”

943. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

943. ‘Whatever’ means: of whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… in this sense, this bhikkhunī is intended.

Bhikkhuniyāti aññāya bhikkhuniyā.

‘To a bhikkhunī’ means: to another bhikkhunī.

Sañciccāti jānantī sañjānantī cecca abhivitaritvā vītikkamo.

‘Deliberately’ means: knowing, being fully aware, intending, and acting with resolve; it is a transgression.

Aphāsuṃ kareyyāti – “iminā imissā aphāsu bhavissatī”ti anāpucchā purato caṅkamati vā tiṭṭhati vā nisīdati vā seyyaṃ vā kappeti uddisati vā uddisāpeti vā sajjhāyaṃ vā karoti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should cause discomfort’ means: thinking, ‘By this, she will be uncomfortable,’ without asking permission, one walks, or stands, or sits, or makes one's bed in front of her, or teaches the Pāli, or causes others to teach, or does recitation; it is an offense of pācittiya.

944. Upasampannāya [P 4.0291][M 0.0382] upasampannasaññā sañcicca aphāsuṃ karoti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampannāya vematikā sañcicca aphāsuṃ karoti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampannāya anupasampannasaññā sañcicca aphāsuṃ karoti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

944. If, in the case of a fully ordained bhikkhunī, one perceives her as fully ordained and deliberately causes discomfort, it is an offense of pācittiya. If, in the case of a fully ordained bhikkhunī, one is in doubt and deliberately causes discomfort, it is an offense of pācittiya. If, in the case of a fully ordained bhikkhunī, one perceives her as not fully ordained and deliberately causes discomfort, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Anupasampannāya [V 0.0397] sañcicca aphāsuṃ karoti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya upasampannasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya anupasampannasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If, in the case of one not fully ordained, one deliberately causes discomfort, it is an offense of wrong-doing. If, in the case of one not fully ordained, one perceives her as fully ordained and deliberately causes discomfort, it is an offense of wrong-doing. If, in the case of one not fully ordained, one is in doubt and deliberately causes discomfort, it is an offense of wrong-doing. If, in the case of one not fully ordained, one perceives her as not fully ordained and deliberately causes discomfort, it is an offense of wrong-doing.

945. Anāpatti na aphāsuṃ kattukāmā āpucchā purato caṅkamati vā tiṭṭhati vā nisīdati vā seyyaṃ vā kappeti uddisati vā uddisāpeti vā sajjhāyaṃ vā karoti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

945. There is no offense: if one does not desire to cause discomfort; if, having asked permission, one walks, stands, sits, or prepares a bed in front of her, or teaches, has another teach, or recites; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Third Training Rule is concluded.

4. Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Fourth Training Rule

946. Tena [T 0.0152] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī dukkhitaṃ sahajīviniṃ neva upaṭṭheti na upaṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karoti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā dukkhitaṃ sahajīviniṃ neva upaṭṭhessati na upaṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī dukkhitaṃ sahajīviniṃ neva upaṭṭheti na upaṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karotīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī dukkhitaṃ sahajīviniṃ neva upaṭṭhessati na upaṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

946. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā neither attended to her sick co-resident pupil herself, nor made an effort to have her attended to. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes…pe… criticized, scorned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the venerable Thullanandā neither attend to her sick co-resident pupil herself, nor make an effort to have her attended to?” …pe… “Is it true, as is said, monks, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā neither attends to her sick co-resident pupil herself, nor makes an effort to have her attended to?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her…pe… “How indeed, monks, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā neither attend to her sick co-resident pupil herself, nor make an effort to have her attended to? This, monks, is not for inspiring faith in the unfaithful…pe… And thus, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

947. “Yā pana bhikkhunī dukkhitaṃ sahajīviniṃ neva upaṭṭheyya na upaṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ kareyya, pācittiya”nti.

947. “Whatever bhikkhunī should neither attend to a sick co-resident pupil herself, nor make an effort to have her attended to, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

948. Yā [M 0.0383] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

948. ‘Whatever’ means: of whatever kind…pe… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means:…pe… in this sense, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Dukkhitā nāma gilānā vuccati.

‘Sick’ means ill.

Sahajīvinī [V 0.0398] nāma saddhivihārinī vuccati.

‘Co-resident’ means a co-resident pupil.

Neva upaṭṭheyyāti na sayaṃ upaṭṭheyya.

‘Should not attend to’ means she should not attend to her personally.

Na upaṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ kareyyāti na aññaṃ āṇāpeyya[T 0.0153].

‘Nor make an effort to have her attended to’ means she should not command another.

“Neva upaṭṭhessāmi, na upaṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karissāmī”ti dhuraṃ nikkhittamatte āpatti pācittiyassa. Antevāsiniṃ vā anupasampannaṃ vā neva upaṭṭheti, na upaṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karoti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

At the mere moment of casting off the burden with the thought, ‘I will not attend to her myself, nor will I make an effort to have her attended to,’ there is the falling into a pācittiya offense. If she does not attend to a resident pupil or a female novice, nor makes an effort to have them attended to, there is the falling into a dukkaṭa offense.

949. Anāpatti [P 4.0292] sati antarāye, pariyesitvā na labhati, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

949. There is no offense if there is an obstacle; if, having searched, she does not find an attendant; if she herself is sick; in times of calamity; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fourth Training Rule is finished.

5. Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Fifth Training Rule

950. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhaddā kāpilānī sākete vassaṃ upagatā hoti. Sā kenacideva karaṇīyena ubbāḷhā thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – “sace me ayyā thullanandā upassayaṃ dadeyya āgaccheyyāmahaṃ sāvatthi”nti. Thullanandā bhikkhunī evamāha – “āgacchatu, dassāmī”ti. Atha kho bhaddā kāpilānī sāketā sāvatthiṃ agamāsi. Thullanandā bhikkhunī bhaddāya kāpilāniyā upassayaṃ adāsi. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī bahussutā hoti bhāṇikā visāradā paṭṭā dhammiṃ kathaṃ kātuṃ. Bhaddāpi kāpilānī bahussutā bahussutāyeva (ka.) hoti bhāṇikā visāradā paṭṭā dhammiṃ kathaṃ kātuṃ uḷārasambhāvitā. Manussā – “ayyā bhaddā kāpilānī bahussutā bhāṇikā visāradā paṭṭā dhammiṃ kathaṃ kātuṃ uḷārasambhāvitā”ti bhaddaṃ kāpilāniṃ [T 0.0154] paṭhamaṃ payirupāsitvā pacchā thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ payirupāsanti. Thullanandā bhikkhunī issāpakatā – “imā kira [M 0.0384] appicchā santuṭṭhā pavivittā asaṃsaṭṭhā yā imā saññattibahulā viññattibahulā viharantī”ti kupitā anattamanā bhaddaṃ kāpilāniṃ upassayā nikkaḍḍhi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā [V 0.0399] ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā ayyāya bhaddāya kāpilāniyā upassayaṃ datvā kupitā anattamanā nikkaḍḍhissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī bhaddāya kāpilāniyā upassayaṃ datvā kupitā anattamanā nikkaḍḍhatīti nikkaḍḍhīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī bhaddāya kāpilāniyā upassayaṃ datvā kupitā anattamanā nikkaḍḍhissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

950. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, Bhaddā Kāpilānī had entered the rains-residence at Sāketa. Pressed by some business, she sent a messenger to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, saying: “If the venerable Thullanandā would give me a lodging, I would come to Sāvatthī.” The bhikkhunī Thullanandā replied, “Let her come, I will give it.” Then Bhaddā Kāpilānī went from Sāketa to Sāvatthī. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā gave Bhaddā Kāpilānī a lodging. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā was learned, a reciter, confident, and skilled in giving a Dhamma talk. Bhaddā Kāpilānī too was learned, a reciter, confident, skilled in giving a Dhamma talk, and esteemed as excellent. People said, “The venerable Bhaddā Kāpilānī is learned, a reciter, confident, skilled in giving a Dhamma talk, and esteemed as excellent.” Having first attended upon Bhaddā Kāpilānī, they afterwards attended upon the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, overcome by jealousy, said sarcastically, “‘Those who live abounding in intimations and abounding in requests—these, it seems, are of few wishes, content, secluded, and unassociated!’” Angry and displeased, she evicted Bhaddā Kāpilānī from the lodging. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes…pe… criticized, scorned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the venerable Thullanandā, after giving a lodging to the venerable Bhaddā Kāpilānī, angrily and displeased, evict her?” …pe… “Is it true, as is said, monks, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, after giving a lodging to Bhaddā Kāpilānī, angrily and displeased, evicted her?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her…pe… “How indeed, monks, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, after giving a lodging to Bhaddā Kāpilānī, angrily and displeased, evict her? This, monks, is not for inspiring faith in the unfaithful…pe… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

951. “Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā upassayaṃ datvā kupitā anattamanā nikkaḍḍheyya vā nikkaḍḍhāpeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

951. “Whatever bhikkhunī, having given a lodging to a bhikkhunī, then, being angry and displeased, should evict her or cause her to be evicted, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

952. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

952. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind…pe… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means:…pe… in this context, this bhikkhunī is intended.

Bhikkhuniyāti aññāya bhikkhuniyā. Upassayo nāma kavāṭabaddho vuccati. Datvāti sayaṃ datvā. Kupitā anattamanāti anabhiraddhā āhatacittā khilajātā.

‘To a bhikkhunī’ means: to another bhikkhunī. A ‘lodging’ is said to be a dwelling fitted with a door-leaf. ‘Having given’ means: having given by oneself. ‘Angry and displeased’ means: not delighted, with an afflicted mind, with a hardened heart.

Nikkaḍḍheyyāti gabbhe [T 0.0155] gahetvā pamukhaṃ nikkaḍḍhati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Pamukhe gahetvā bahi nikkaḍḍhati, āpatti [P 4.0293] pācittiyassa. Ekena payogena bahukepi dvāre atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should evict’ means: if, having seized her in the inner chamber, she drags her out to the entrance-way, there is an offense of pācittiya. If, having seized her in the entrance-way, she drags her outside, there is an offense of pācittiya. If, with one effort, she makes her pass through even many doors, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Nikkaḍḍhāpeyyāti aññaṃ āṇāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa ettha “āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti sabbattha dissati, bhikkhuvibhaṅge pana idisesu āṇattisahagatasikkhāpadesu “aññaṃ āṇāpeti āpatti pācittiyassā”ti āgatattā tamanuvattitvā visodhitamidaṃ. Sakiṃ āṇattā bahukepi dvāre atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should cause to be evicted’ means: if she commands another, there is an offense of pācittiya. If the one who was commanded once makes her pass through even many doors, there is an offense of pācittiya.

953. Upasampannāya upasampannasaññā upassayaṃ datvā kupitā anattamanā nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampannāya vematikā upassayaṃ datvā kupitā anattamanā nikkaḍḍhati vā [M 0.0385] nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampannāya anupasampannasaññā upassayaṃ datvā kupitā anattamanā nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

953. Towards a fully ordained bhikkhunī, perceiving her as fully ordained, having given a lodging, being angry and displeased, one evicts her or causes her to be evicted; this is an offense of pācittiya.
