Towards a fully ordained bhikkhunī, being in doubt, having given a lodging, being angry and displeased, one evicts her or causes her to be evicted; this is an offense of pācittiya. Towards a fully ordained bhikkhunī, perceiving her as not fully ordained, having given a lodging, being angry and displeased, one evicts her or causes her to be evicted; this is an offense of pācittiya.

Tassā [V 0.0400] parikkhāraṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Akavāṭabaddhā nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Tassā parikkhāraṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannaṃ kavāṭabaddhā vā akavāṭabaddhā vā nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Tassā parikkhāraṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya upasampannasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya anupasampannasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If one removes or causes to be removed her requisites, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If one evicts or causes to be evicted from a dwelling not secured with a door-leaf, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If one removes or causes to be removed her requisites, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If one evicts or causes to be evicted one who is not fully ordained, whether from a dwelling secured with a door-leaf or not secured with a door-leaf, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If one removes or causes to be removed her requisites, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. Towards one who is not fully ordained, perceiving her as fully ordained, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. Towards one who is not fully ordained, being in doubt, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. Towards one who is not fully ordained, perceiving her as not fully ordained, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

954. Anāpatti [T 0.0156] alajjiniṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, tassā parikkhāraṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, ummattikaṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, tassā parikkhāraṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, bhaṇḍanakārikaṃ kalahakārikaṃ vivādakārikaṃ bhassakārikaṃ saṅghe adhikaraṇakārikaṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, tassā parikkhāraṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, antevāsiniṃ vā saddhivihāriniṃ vā na sammā vattantiṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, tassā parikkhāraṃ nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

954. There is no offense if one evicts or causes to be evicted a shameless bhikkhunī, or removes or causes to be removed her requisites; if one evicts or causes to be evicted an insane bhikkhunī, or removes or causes to be removed her requisites; if one evicts or causes to be evicted one who is quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, garrulous, or who creates legal issues in the Saṅgha, or removes or causes to be removed her requisites; if one evicts or causes to be evicted a pupil or a co-resident who is not behaving properly, or removes or causes to be removed her requisites. There is no offense for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fifth Training Rule is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Sixth Training Rule

955. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī saṃsaṭṭhā viharati gahapatināpi gahapatiputtenapi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā caṇḍakāḷī saṃsaṭṭhā viharissati gahapatināpi gahapatiputtenapī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī saṃsaṭṭhā viharati gahapatināpi gahapatiputtenapīti[M 0.0386]? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave[P 4.0294], caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī saṃsaṭṭhā viharissati gahapatināpi gahapatiputtenapi! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ [T 0.0157] vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

955. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī was dwelling in association with a householder and a householder's son. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… complained, criticized, and spread it about, “How indeed can the venerable Caṇḍakāḷī dwell in association with a householder and a householder's son?”… “Is it true, it is said, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī dwells in association with a householder and a householder's son?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, can the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī dwell in association with a householder and a householder's son? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

956. “Yā [V 0.0401] pana bhikkhunī saṃsaṭṭhā vihareyya gahapatinā vā gahapatiputtena vā sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi evamassa vacanīyā – ‘māyye, saṃsaṭṭhā vihari gahapatināpi gahapatiputtenapi. Viviccāyye; vivekaññeva bhaginiyā saṅgho vaṇṇetī’ti. Evañca evañca pana (ka.) sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi vuccamānā tatheva paggaṇheyya, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsitabbā tassa paṭinissaggāya. Yāvatatiyañce samanubhāsīyamānā taṃ paṭinissajjeyya, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ; no ce paṭinissajjeyya, pācittiya”nti.

956. “Whatever bhikkhunī should dwell in association with a householder or with a householder’s son, that bhikkhunī should be spoken to by the bhikkhunīs thus: ‘Venerable one, do not dwell in association with a householder or with a householder's son. Be secluded, venerable one; the Saṅgha praises only seclusion for a sister.’ And if that bhikkhunī, being spoken to by the bhikkhunīs, should persist in that very same way, that bhikkhunī should be admonished by the bhikkhunīs up to the third time for the abandoning of that. If, being admonished up to the third time, she should abandon it, this is good. If she should not abandon it, it is a pācittiya offense.”

957. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

957. ‘Whatever’ means: whichever, of whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… in this sense, this bhikkhunī is intended.

Saṃsaṭṭhā nāma ananulomikena kāyikavācasikena saṃsaṭṭhā.

‘Associated’ means: associated by means of unsuitable bodily and verbal association.

Gahapati nāma yo koci agāraṃ ajjhāvasati.

‘Householder’ means: whoever lives in and manages a household.

Gahapatiputto nāma ye keci yo koci (ka.) puttabhātaro.

‘Householder’s son’ means: any sons or brothers.

Sā bhikkhunīti yā sā saṃsaṭṭhā bhikkhunī.

‘That bhikkhunī’ means: that bhikkhunī who is associated.

Bhikkhunīhīti aññāhi bhikkhunīhi. Yā passanti yā suṇanti tāhi vattabbā – “māyye, saṃsaṭṭhā vihari gahapatināpi gahapatiputtenapi. Viviccāyye; vivekaññeva bhaginiyā saṅgho vaṇṇetī”ti. Dutiyampi vattabbā. Tatiyampi vattabbā. Sace paṭinissajjati, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ; no ce paṭinissajjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sutvā na vadanti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sā bhikkhunī saṅghamajjhampi ākaḍḍhitvā vattabbā – “māyye[T 0.0158], saṃsaṭṭhā vihari gahapatināpi gahapatiputtenapi. Viviccāyye; vivekaññevabhaginiyā saṅgho vaṇṇetī”ti. Dutiyampi vattabbā. Tatiyampi vattabbā. Sace paṭinissajjati, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ; no ce paṭinissajjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sā bhikkhunī samanubhāsitabbā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, samanubhāsitabbā. Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

‘By the bhikkhunīs’ means: by other bhikkhunīs. Those who see or those who hear, by them she should be spoken to: ‘Venerable one, do not dwell in association with a householder or with a householder's son. Be secluded, venerable one; the Saṅgha praises only seclusion for a sister.’ She should be spoken to a second time. She should be spoken to a third time. If she abandons it, this is good. If she does not abandon it, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. If, having heard, they do not speak, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. That bhikkhunī, having been brought into the midst of the Saṅgha, should be spoken to: ‘Venerable one, do not dwell in association with a householder or with a householder's son. Be secluded, venerable one; the Saṅgha praises only seclusion for a sister.’ She should be spoken to a second time. She should be spoken to a third time. If she abandons it, this is good. If she does not abandon it, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. That bhikkhunī should be admonished. And so, Bhikkhus, she should be admonished. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhunī:

958. “Suṇātu [M 0.0387] me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā bhikkhunī saṃsaṭṭhā viharati gahapatināpi [V 0.0402] gahapatiputtenapi. Sā taṃ vatthuṃ na paṭinissajjati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuniṃ samanubhāseyya tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya. Esā ñatti.

958. “Venerable ones, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name dwells in association with a householder and a householder's son. She does not abandon that matter. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should admonish the bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name for the abandoning of that matter. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā bhikkhunī saṃsaṭṭhā viharati gahapatināpi gahapatiputtenapi. Sā taṃ vatthuṃ na paṭinissajjati. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuniṃ samanubhāsati tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā samanubhāsanā tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.

“Venerable ones, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name dwells in association with a householder and a householder's son. She does not abandon that matter. The Saṅgha admonishes the bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name for the abandoning of that matter. To whichever venerable one the admonishment of the bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name for the abandoning of that matter is agreeable, she should be silent. To whomever it is not agreeable, she should speak.”

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

“A second time, I speak on this matter… A third time, I speak on this matter…”

“Samanubhaṭṭhā saṅghena itthannāmā bhikkhunī tassa vatthussa paṭinissaggāya; khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The bhikkhunī of such-and-such a name has been admonished by the Saṅgha for the abandoning of that matter. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold it.”

Ñattiyā [P 4.0295] dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti pācittiyassa.

For the motion, there is an offense of wrong-doing. For the two formal announcements, there are offenses of wrong-doing. At the conclusion of the formal announcements, there is an offense of expiation.

959. Dhammakamme [T 0.0159] dhammakammasaññā na paṭinissajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme vematikā na paṭinissajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññā na paṭinissajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

959. In a lawful act, if she perceives it as a lawful act and does not abandon it, there is an offense of expiation. In a lawful act, if she is doubtful and does not abandon it, there is an offense of expiation. In a lawful act, if she perceives it as an unlawful act and does not abandon it, there is an offense of expiation.

Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In an unlawful act, perceiving it as a lawful act, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In an unlawful act, being doubtful, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In an unlawful act, perceiving it as an unlawful act, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

960. Anāpatti asamanubhāsantiyā, paṭinissajjantiyā, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

960. There is no offense for one who is not being admonished, for one who abandons it, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Sixth Training Rule is finished.

7. Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Seventh Training Rule

961. Tena [V 0.0403] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo antoraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṃ caranti. Dhuttā [M 0.0388] dūsenti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo antoraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṃ carissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo antoraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṃ carantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo antoraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṃ carissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca [T 0.0160] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

961. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, bhikkhunīs were journeying on tour within the country, in a region reputed to be perilous and dangerous, without a caravan. Rogues molested them. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs journey on tour within the country, in a region reputed to be perilous and dangerous, without a caravan?”… “Bhikkhus, is it true, as is said, that bhikkhunīs are journeying on tour within the country, in a region reputed to be perilous and dangerous, without a caravan?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, can bhikkhunīs journey on tour within the country, in a region reputed to be perilous and dangerous, without a caravan! This, Bhikkhus, does not lead to the faith of the faithless… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

962. “Yā pana bhikkhunī antoraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṃ careyya, pācittiya”nti.

962. “Whatever bhikkhunī should journey on tour within the country, in a region reputed to be perilous and dangerous, without a caravan, there is an offense of expiation.”

963. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

963. ‘Whatever’: whatever, of whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhunī’: …in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Antoraṭṭheti yassa vijite viharati, tassa raṭṭhe.

‘Within the country’: in the country of the one in whose dominion one dwells.

Sāsaṅkaṃ nāma tasmiṃ magge corānaṃ niviṭṭhokāso dissati, bhuttokāso dissati, ṭhitokāso dissati, nisinnokāso dissati, nipannokāso dissati.

‘Perilous’ means: on that path, a place where thieves have hidden is seen, a place where they have eaten is seen, a place where they have stood is seen, a place where they have sat is seen, and a place where they have lain down is seen.

Sappaṭibhayaṃ nāma tasmiṃ magge corehi manussā hatā dissanti, viluttā dissanti, ākoṭitā dissanti.

‘Dangerous’ means: on that path, people are seen who have been killed by thieves, robbed, and beaten.

Asatthikā nāma vinā satthena.

‘Without a caravan’ means being without a caravan.

Cārikaṃ careyyāti kukkuṭasampāte gāme gāmantare gāmantare āpatti pācittiyassa. Agāmake araññe addhayojane addhayojane āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should journey on tour’: For every interval between villages within a cock’s flight, there is an offense of expiation. In a wilderness without a village, for every half-yojana, there is an offense of expiation.

964. Anāpatti [V 0.0404] satthena saha gacchati, kheme appaṭibhaye gacchati, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

964. There is no offense if she goes together with a caravan; if she goes in a safe, non-dangerous place; in calamities; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Seventh Training Rule is finished.

8. Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Eighth Training Rule

965. Tena [P 4.0296][M 0.0389] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo tiroraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṃ caranti. Dhuttā dūsenti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti [T 0.0161] vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo tiroraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṃ carissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo tiroraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṃ carantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo tiroraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṃ carissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

965. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, bhikkhunīs were journeying on tour in another region, one regarded as perilous and fraught with danger, without a caravan. Rogues molested them. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs journey on tour in another region, one regarded as perilous and fraught with danger, without a caravan?”… “Is it true, it is said, O bhikkhus, that bhikkhunīs are journeying on tour in another region, one regarded as perilous and fraught with danger, without a caravan?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, O bhikkhus, can bhikkhunīs journey on tour in another region, one regarded as perilous and fraught with danger, without a caravan! This, O bhikkhus, does not lead to the faith of the faithless… And so, O bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

966. “Yā pana bhikkhunī tiroraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṃ careyya, pācattiya”nti.

966. “Whatever bhikkhunī should journey on tour in another region, one regarded as perilous and fraught with danger, without a caravan, there is an offense of expiation.”

967. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

967. ‘Whatever’: whatever, of whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhunī’: …in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Tiroraṭṭheti yassa vijite viharati, taṃ ṭhapetvā aññassa raṭṭhe.

‘In another region’ means: setting aside the dominion in which one dwells, it is in the region of another.

Sāsaṅkaṃ nāma tasmiṃ magge corānaṃ niviṭṭhokāso dissati, bhuttokāso dissati, ṭhitokāso dissati, nisinnokāso dissati, nipannokāso dissati.

‘Perilous’ means: on that path, a place where thieves have hidden is seen, a place where they have eaten is seen, a place where they have stood is seen, a place where they have sat is seen, and a place where they have lain down is seen.

Sappaṭibhayaṃ nāma tasmiṃ magge corehi manussā hatā dissanti, viluttā dissanti, ākoṭitā dissanti.

‘Fraught with danger’ means: on that path, people are seen who have been killed by thieves, robbed, and beaten.

Asatthikā [V 0.0405] nāma vinā satthena.

‘Without a caravan’ means being without a caravan.

Cārikaṃ careyyāti kukkuṭasampāte gāme gāmantare gāmantare, āpatti pācittiyassa. Agāmake araññe addhayojane addhayojane āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should go on tour’: When travelling between villages that are within a cock's flight of each other, there is an offense of expiation for each interval. In a forest without villages, there is an offense of expiation for every half-yojana.

968. Anāpatti satthena saha gacchati, kheme appaṭibhaye gacchati[T 0.0162], āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

968. There is no offense: if she goes together with a caravan; if she goes when it is safe and the region is without danger; in times of calamity; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Eighth Training Rule is concluded.

9. Navamasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Ninth Training Rule

969. Tena [M 0.0390] samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo antovassaṃ cārikaṃ caranti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo antovassaṃ cārikaṃ carissanti haritāni tiṇāni ca sammaddantā, ekindriyaṃ jīvaṃ viheṭhentā, bahū khuddake pāṇe saṅghātaṃ āpādentā”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo antovassaṃ cārikaṃ carissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo antovassaṃ cārikaṃ carantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo antovassaṃ cārikaṃ carissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

969. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Place. Now at that time, bhikkhunīs were going on tour during the rains-residence. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly, saying: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs go on tour during the rains-residence, trampling on the green grass, harming one-facultied life, and causing the destruction of many small living beings?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and speaking disparagingly. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly, saying: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs go on tour during the rains-residence?” … “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that bhikkhunīs are going on tour during the rains-residence?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, can bhikkhunīs go on tour during the rains-residence? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And thus, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

970. “Yā pana bhikkhunī antovassaṃ cārikaṃ careyya, pācittiya”nti.

970. “Whatever bhikkhunī should go on tour during the rains-residence, it is an offense of expiation.”

971. Yā [P 4.0297] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

971. Whatever one: of whatever sort... A bhikkhunī: ... in this sense, this bhikkhunī is intended as 'bhikkhunī'.

Antovassanti purimaṃ vā temāsaṃ pacchimaṃ vā temāsaṃ avasitvā.

During the rains-residence means: without having resided for either the first three-month period or the latter three-month period.

Cārikaṃ [V 0.0406] careyyāti kukkuṭasampāte gāme [T 0.0163] gāmantare gāmantare āpatti pācittiyassa. Agāmake araññe addhayojane addhayojane āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should go on tour’: When travelling between villages that are within a cock's flight of each other, there is an offense of expiation for each interval. In a forest without villages, there is an offense of expiation for every half-yojana.

972. Anāpatti sattāhakaraṇīyena gacchati, kenaci ubbāḷhā gacchati, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

972. There is no offense: if she goes on account of a seven-day duty; if she goes, being harassed by someone; on account of dangers; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Navamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Ninth Training Rule is concluded.

10. Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Tenth Training Rule

973. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo tattheva rājagahe [M 0.0391] vassaṃ vasanti, tattha hemantaṃ, tattha gimhaṃ. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “āhundarikā bhikkhunīnaṃ disā andhakārā, na imāsaṃ disā pakkhāyantī”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tena hi, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññapessāmi dasa atthavase paṭicca – saṅghasuṭṭhutāya…pe… saddhammaṭṭhitiyā vinayānuggahāya. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

973. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Place. Now at that time, bhikkhunīs were residing right there in Rājagaha for the rainy season, right there for the winter, and right there for the summer. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly, saying: “Are the directions confined for the bhikkhunīs? Are they in darkness? The directions are not apparent to these bhikkhunīs.” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and speaking disparagingly. Then those bhikkhunīs informed the bhikkhus of this matter. The bhikkhus informed the Blessed One of this matter. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus, saying: “In that case, Bhikkhus, I will lay down a training rule for the bhikkhunīs, based on ten benefits: for the excellence of the Saṅgha… for the stability of the good Dhamma, for the support of the Vinaya. And thus, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

974. “Yā pana bhikkhunī vassaṃvuṭṭhā cārikaṃ na pakkameyya antamaso chappañcayojanānipi, pācittiya”nti.

974. “Whatever bhikkhunī, having completed the rains-residence, should not depart on tour, even as far as five or six yojanas, it is an offense of expiation.”

975. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ [T 0.0164] atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

975. Whatever one: of whatever sort... A bhikkhunī: ... in this sense, this bhikkhunī is intended as 'bhikkhunī'.

Vassaṃvuṭṭhā nāma purimaṃ vā temāsaṃ pacchimaṃ vā temāsaṃ vuṭṭhā.

One who has completed the rains-residence means: one who has resided for either the first three-month period or the latter three-month period.

“Cārikaṃ na pakkamissāmi antamaso chappañcayojanānipī”ti dhuraṃ nikkhittamatte āpatti pācittiyassa.

Just on laying down the burden with the thought, “I will not depart on tour, even as far as five or six yojanas,” there is an offense of expiation.

976. Anāpatti [V 0.0407] sati antarāye, pariyesitvā dutiyikaṃ bhikkhuniṃ na labhati, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

976. There is no offense: if there is an obstacle; if, having searched for a companion bhikkhunī, she does not find one; on account of being sick; on account of dangers; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Tenth Training Rule is concluded.

Tuvaṭṭavaggo catuttho.

The Tuvaṭṭa Chapter, the fourth.

5. Cittāgāravaggo

5. The Chapter on the Picture Hall

1. Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The First Training Rule

977. Tena [P 4.0298] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena rañño pasenadissa kosalassa uyyāne cittāgāre paṭibhānacittaṃ kataṃ [M 0.0392] hoti. Bahū manussā cittāgāraṃ dassanāya gacchanti. Chabbaggiyāpi bhikkhuniyo cittāgāraṃ dassanāya agamaṃsu. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo cittāgāraṃ dassanāya gacchissanti, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo cittāgāraṃ dassanāya gacchissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo [T 0.0165] cittāgāraṃ dassanāya gacchantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo cittāgāraṃ dassanāya gacchissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

977. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, in the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, in the park of King Pasenadi of Kosala, in the picture hall, an ingenious picture had been made. Many people went to see the picture hall. The bhikkhunīs of the group of six also went to see the picture hall. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly, saying: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs go to see a picture hall, just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures!” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and speaking disparagingly. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly, saying: “How indeed can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six go to see a picture hall?” … “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunīs of the group of six go to see a picture hall?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six go to see a picture hall? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And thus, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

978. “Yā pana bhikkhunī rājāgāraṃ vā cittāgāraṃ vā ārāmaṃ vā uyyānaṃ vā pokkharaṇiṃ vā dassanāya gaccheyya, pācittiya”nti.

978. “Whatever bhikkhunī should go to see a king's pleasure house, a picture hall, a pleasure park, a pleasure garden, or a pleasure pond, there is an offense of pācittiya.”

979. Yā [V 0.0408] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

979. ‘Whatever’: whatever, of whatever sort… ‘Bhikkhunī’: …in this sense, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Rājāgāraṃ nāma yattha katthaci rañño kīḷituṃ ramituṃ kataṃ hoti.

A king's pleasure house means any place whatsoever made for the king to play and to delight in.

Cittāgāraṃ nāma yattha katthaci manussānaṃ kīḷituṃ ramituṃ kataṃ hoti.

A picture hall means any place whatsoever made for people to play and to delight in.

Ārāmo nāma yattha katthaci manussānaṃ kīḷituṃ ramituṃ kato hoti.

A pleasure park means any place whatsoever made for people to play and to delight in.

Uyyānaṃ nāma yattha katthaci manussānaṃ kīḷituṃ ramituṃ kataṃ hoti.

A pleasure garden means any place whatsoever made for people to play and to delight in.

Pokkharaṇī nāma yattha katthaci manussānaṃ kīḷituṃ ramituṃ katā hoti.

A pleasure pond means any place whatsoever made for people to play and to delight in.

980. Dassanāya gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yattha ṭhitā passati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dassanūpacāraṃ vijahitvā punappunaṃ passati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ekamekaṃ dassanāya gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Yattha ṭhitā passati, āpatti pacittiyassa. Dassanūpacāraṃ vijahitvā punappunaṃ passati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

980. If she goes to see, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Where she stands and sees, there is an offense of pācittiya. Having left the range of sight, if she sees again and again, there is an offense of pācittiya. If she goes to see each one, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Where she stands and sees, there is an offense of pācittiya. Having left the range of sight, if she sees again and again, there is an offense of pācittiya.

981. Anāpatti [P 4.0299][M 0.0393] ārāme ṭhitā passati, gacchantī vā āgacchantī vā [T 0.0166] passati, sati karaṇīye gantvā passati, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

981. There is no offense: if she stands in a park and sees; if she sees while going or coming; if, there being some business, she goes and sees; in calamities; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The First Training Rule is concluded.

2. Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Second Training Rule

982. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo āsandimpi pallaṅkampi paribhuñjanti. Manussā vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo āsandimpi pallaṅkampi paribhuñjissanti, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ[V 0.0409]. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo āsandimpi pallaṅkampi paribhuñjissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo āsandimpi pallaṅkampi paribhuñjantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo āsandimpi pallaṅkampi paribhuñjissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

982. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were using both high chairs and couches. People, wandering on a tour of the monasteries, saw this and criticized, found fault, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the bhikkhunīs use high chairs and couches, just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people criticizing, finding fault, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they also criticized, found fault, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the bhikkhunīs use high chairs and couches?”… “Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunīs are using high chairs and couches?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, monks, can the bhikkhunīs use high chairs and couches? This, monks, is not for the inspiring of confidence in the unconfident… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

983. “Yā pana bhikkhunī āsandiṃ vā pallaṅkaṃ vā paribhuñjeyya, pācittiya”nti.

983. “Whatever bhikkhunī should use a high chair or a couch, it is an offense entailing expiation.”

984. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ [T 0.0167] atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

984. ‘Whatever’: whatever, of whatever sort… ‘Bhikkhunī’: …in this sense, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Āsandī nāma atikkantappamāṇā vuccati.

What is called a high chair is one that exceeds the standard measurement.

Pallaṅko nāma āharimehi “asaṃhārimehi” iti kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyā sameti vāḷehi kato hoti.

What is called a couch is one made with removable animal figures.

Paribhuñjeyyāti tasmiṃ abhinisīdati vā abhinipajjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

The phrase ‘should use’ means: if she sits down on it or lies down on it, she commits an offense entailing expiation.

985. Anāpatti [M 0.0394] āsandiyā pāde chinditvā paribhuñjati, pallaṅkassa vāḷe bhinditvā paribhuñjati, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

985. There is no offense if she uses a high chair after cutting its legs, if she uses a couch after breaking its animal figures, for a bhikkhunī who is insane, or for the first offender.

Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Second Training Rule is concluded.

3. Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Third Training Rule

986. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo suttaṃ kantanti. Manussā [P 4.0300] vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo suttaṃ kantissanti, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā [V 0.0410] …pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo suttaṃ kantissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo suttaṃ kantantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo suttaṃ kantissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā [T 0.0168] pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

986. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs were spinning thread. People, wandering on a tour of the monasteries, saw this and criticized, found fault, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the bhikkhunīs spin thread, just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people criticizing, finding fault, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they also criticized, found fault, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs spin thread?”… “Is it true, monks, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs are spinning thread?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, monks, can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs spin thread? This, monks, is not for the inspiring of confidence in the unconfident… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

987. “Yā pana bhikkhunī suttaṃ kanteyya, pācittiya”nti.

987. “Whatever bhikkhunī should spin thread, it is an offense entailing expiation.”

988. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

988. ‘Whatever’: whatever, of whatever sort… ‘Bhikkhunī’: …in this sense, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Suttaṃ nāma cha suttāni – khomaṃ, kappāsikaṃ, koseyyaṃ, kambalaṃ, sāṇaṃ, bhaṅgaṃ.

What is called thread refers to six kinds of thread: linen, cotton, silk, wool, hemp, and thread made from a mixture of fibers.

Kanteyyāti sayaṃ kantati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Ujjavujjave āpatti pācittiyassa.

The phrase ‘should spin’ means: if she spins it herself, for the effort there is an offense of wrong-doing. For every spinning motion, she commits an offense entailing expiation.

989. Anāpatti kantitasuttaṃ kantati, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

989. There is no offense if she spins thread that has already been spun, for a bhikkhunī who is insane, or for the first offender.

Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Third Training Rule is concluded.

4. Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Fourth Training Rule

990. Tena [M 0.0395] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo gihiveyyāvaccaṃ karonti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo gihiveyyāvaccaṃ karissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo gihiveyyāvaccaṃ karontīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo gihiveyyāvaccaṃ karissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

990. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, in the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, bhikkhunīs were performing services for householders. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes... criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs perform services for householders?”... “Is it true, as has been heard, Bhikkhus, that bhikkhunīs perform services for householders?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... “How indeed, Bhikkhus, can bhikkhunīs perform services for householders? This, Bhikkhus, does not lead to the faith of the faithless... And so, Bhikkhus, let the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule:

991. “Yā pana bhikkhunī gihiveyyāvaccaṃ kareyya, pācittiya”nti.

991. “Whatever bhikkhunī should perform a service for a householder, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

992. Yā [T 0.0169][V 0.0411] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

992. ‘Whatever’ means: whichever, of whatever sort... ‘Bhikkhunī’ means... the bhikkhunī who is intended in this context.

Gihiveyyāvaccaṃ nāma agārikassa yāguṃ vā bhattaṃ vā khādanīyaṃ [P 4.0301] vā pacati, sāṭakaṃ vā veṭhanaṃ vā dhovati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A service for a householder means: for a householder, she cooks rice-gruel, or rice, or hard food; or she washes a cloth or a turban. It is an offense of pācittiya.

993. Anāpatti yāgupāne, saṅghabhatte, cetiyapūjāya, attano veyyāvaccakarassa yāguṃ vā bhattaṃ vā khādanīyaṃ vā pacati, sāṭakaṃ vā veṭhanaṃ vā dhovati, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

993. There is no offense: in the case of a rice-gruel drink; at a meal for the Saṅgha; for an offering to a cetiya; if she cooks rice-gruel, or rice, or hard food for her own attendant, or washes a cloth or a turban for her; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fourth Training Rule is concluded.

5. Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Fifth Training Rule

994. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – “ehāyye, imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamehī”ti. Thullanandā bhikkhunī ‘sādhū’ti paṭissuṇitvā neva vūpasameti na vūpasamāya ussukkaṃ karoti. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī [M 0.0396] bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā bhikkhuniyā – ‘ehāyye’, imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamehī’ti vuccamānā – ‘sādhū’ti paṭissuṇitvā, neva vūpasamessati na vūpasamāya ussukkaṃ karissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā – “ehāyye, imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamehī”ti vuccamānā – “sādhū”ti paṭissuṇitvā, neva [T 0.0170] vūpasameti na vūpasamāya ussukkaṃ karotīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā – “ehāyye, imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamehī”ti vuccamānā – “sādhū”ti paṭissuṇitvā, neva vūpasamessati na vūpasamāya ussukkaṃ karissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

994. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, in the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī, having approached the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, said this: “Come, venerable one, settle this legal issue.” The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having agreed by saying, “Good,” neither settled it nor made an effort to settle it. Then that bhikkhunī told this matter to the other bhikkhunīs. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes... criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the venerable Thullanandā, having been told by a bhikkhunī, ‘Come, venerable one, settle this legal issue,’ and having agreed by saying, ‘Good,’ neither settle it nor make an effort to settle it?”... “Is it true, as has been heard, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having been told by a bhikkhunī, ‘Come, venerable one, settle this legal issue,’ and having agreed by saying, ‘Good,’ neither settles it nor makes an effort to settle it?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her... “How indeed, Bhikkhus, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having been told by a bhikkhunī, ‘Come, venerable one, settle this legal issue,’ and having agreed by saying, ‘Good,’ neither settle it nor make an effort to settle it? This, Bhikkhus, does not lead to the faith of the faithless... And so, Bhikkhus, let the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule:

995. “Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā – ‘ehāyye, imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamehī’ti vuccamānā [V 0.0412] – ‘sādhū’ti paṭissuṇitvā sā pacchā anantarāyikinī neva vūpasameyya na vūpasamāya ussukkaṃ kareyya, pācittiya”nti.

995. “Whatever bhikkhunī, having been told by another bhikkhunī, ‘Come, venerable one, settle this legal issue,’ and having agreed by saying, ‘Good,’ should afterwards, being without hindrance, neither settle it nor make an effort to settle it, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

996. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

996. ‘Whatever’ means: whichever, of whatever sort... ‘Bhikkhunī’ means... the bhikkhunī who is intended in this context.

Bhikkhuniyāti aññāya bhikkhuniyā.

‘By a bhikkhunī’ means: by another bhikkhunī.

Adhikaraṇaṃ nāma cattāri adhikaraṇāni – vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, kiccādhikaraṇaṃ.

A legal issue means: the four legal issues, namely, a legal issue arising from dispute, a legal issue arising from accusation, a legal issue arising from an offense, and a legal issue arising from procedure.

Ehāyye imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamehīti ehāyye imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vinicchehi.

‘Come, venerable one, settle this legal issue’ means: ‘Come, venerable one, decide this legal issue.’

Sā [P 4.0302] pacchā anantarāyikinīti asati antarāye.

‘She afterwards, being without hindrance’ means: when there is no hindrance.

Neva vūpasameyyāti na sayaṃ vūpasameyya.

‘Should not settle it’ means: she should not settle it herself.

Na vūpasamāya ussukkaṃ kareyyāti na aññaṃ āṇāpeyya. “Neva vūpasamessāmi na vūpasamāya ussukkaṃ karissāmī”ti dhuraṃ nikkhittamatte, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should not make an effort to settle it’ means: she should not command another. Just upon laying down the burden, with the thought, ‘I will not settle it, nor will I make an effort to settle it,’ there is an offense of pācittiya.

997. Upasampannāya [M 0.0397] upasampannasaññā adhikaraṇaṃ neva vūpasameti na vūpasamāya ussukkaṃ karoti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampannāya [T 0.0171] vematikā adhikaraṇaṃ neva vūpasameti, na vūpasamāya ussukkaṃ karoti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampannāya anupasampannasaññā adhikaraṇaṃ neva vūpasameti, na vūpasamāya ussukkaṃ karoti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

997. In the case of an ordained one, if she perceives her as ordained and neither settles the legal issue nor makes an effort to settle it, it is an offense of pācittiya. In the case of an ordained one, if she is doubtful and neither settles the legal issue nor makes an effort to settle it, it is an offense of pācittiya. In the case of an ordained one, if she perceives her as unordained and neither settles the legal issue nor makes an effort to settle it, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Anupasampannāya adhikaraṇaṃ neva vūpasameti, na vūpasamāya ussukkaṃ karoti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya upasampannasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampannāya anupasampannasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In the case of an unordained woman, if she neither settles the legal issue nor makes an effort to settle it, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of an unordained woman, if she perceives her as ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of an unordained woman, if she is doubtful, there is an offense of wrong-doing. In the case of an unordained woman, if she perceives her as unordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

998. Anāpatti [V 0.0413] sati antarāye, pariyesitvā na labhati, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

998. There is no offense: if there is a hindrance; if, having searched, she does not find someone; if she is sick; in times of calamity; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fifth Training Rule is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Sixth Training Rule

999. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī naṭānampi naṭakānampi laṅghakānampi sokajjhāyikānampi kumbhathūṇikānampi sahatthā khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ deti – “mayhaṃ parisati vaṇṇaṃ bhāsathā”ti. Naṭāpi naṭakāpi laṅghakāpi sokajjhāyikāpi kumbhathūṇikāpi thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā parisati vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti – “ayyā thullanandā bahussutā bhāṇikā visāradā paṭṭā dhammiṃ kathaṃ kātuṃ; detha ayyāya, karotha ayyāyā”ti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā [T 0.0172] ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā agārikassa sahatthā khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ dassatīti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī agārikassa sahatthā khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ detīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī agārikassa sahatthā khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ dassati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

999. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, in the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā was giving hard food and soft food with her own hand to actors, dancers, acrobats, magicians, and drummers, saying, 'Speak of my virtues in the assembly.' And the actors, dancers, acrobats, magicians, and drummers spoke of the virtues of the bhikkhunī Thullanandā in the assembly, saying, 'The venerable Thullanandā is very learned, a reciter of the texts, confident, and proficient in giving a Dhamma talk. Give to the venerable one, serve the venerable one.' Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: 'How indeed can the venerable Thullanandā give hard food and soft food with her own hand to a householder?'… 'Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā gives hard food and soft food with her own hand to a householder?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… 'How indeed, monks, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā give hard food and soft food with her own hand to a householder! This, monks, is not for the pleasing of the unpleased… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

1000. “Yā [M 0.0398] pana bhikkhunī agārikassa vā paribbājakassa vā paribbājikāya vā sahatthā khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā dadeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1000. Whatever bhikkhunī should give hard food or soft food with her own hand to a householder, a male wanderer, or a female wanderer, it is an offense requiring expiation.

1001. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1001. 'Whatever' means: whatever sort... 'A bhikkhunī' means... the bhikkhunī who is intended in this meaning.

Agāriko nāma yo koci agāraṃ ajjhāvasati.

A householder is one who lives in a house.

Paribbājako nāma bhikkhuñca sāmaṇerañca ṭhapetvā yo koci paribbājakasamāpanno.

A male wanderer is anyone who has undertaken the life of a wanderer, excluding a bhikkhu and a sāmaṇera.

Paribbājikā [V 0.0414] nāma bhikkhuniñca sikkhamānañca sāmaṇeriñca ṭhapetvā yā kāci paribbājikasamāpannā.

A female wanderer is any woman who has undertaken the life of a female wanderer, excluding a bhikkhunī, a sikkhamānā, and a sāmaṇerī.

Khādanīyaṃ nāma pañca bhojanāni – udakadantaponaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ khādanīyaṃ nāma.

Hard food is that which remains, setting aside the five staple foods, water, and tooth-cleaners.

Bhojanīyaṃ nāma pañca bhojanāni – odano, kummāso, sattu, maccho, maṃsaṃ.

Staple food means the five staple foods: rice, barley-meal, parched-grain flour, fish, and meat.

Dadeyyāti kāyena vā kāyapaṭibaddhena vā nissaggiyena vā [P 4.0303] deti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Udakadantaponaṃ deti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

'Should give' means: if one gives with the body, with something attached to the body, or by tossing it, it is an offense requiring expiation. If one gives water or a tooth-cleaner, it is an offense of wrong conduct.

1002. Anāpatti dāpeti na deti, upanikkhipitvā deti, bāhirālepaṃ [T 0.0173] deti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1002. There is no offense if one causes another to give but does not give it oneself; if one gives by placing it nearby; if one gives an external ointment; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Sixth Training Rule is finished.

7. Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Seventh Training Rule

1003. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī āvasathacīvaraṃ anissajjitvā paribhuñjati. Aññā utuniyo bhikkhuniyo na labhanti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā āvasathacīvaraṃ anissajjitvā [M 0.0399] paribhuñjissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī āvasathacīvaraṃ anissajjitvā paribhuñjatīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī āvasathacīvaraṃ anissajjitvā paribhuñjissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1003. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā used the seasonal robe without having relinquished it. Other bhikkhunīs who were having their season did not receive it. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… murmured, were critical, and spread it about: “How indeed could the venerable Thullanandā use the seasonal robe without having relinquished it?”… “Is it true, as is said, monks, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā used the seasonal robe without having relinquished it?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, monks, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā use the seasonal robe without having relinquished it! This, monks, is not for the pleasing of the unpleased… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1004. “Yā pana bhikkhunī āvasathacīvaraṃ anissajjitvā paribhuñjeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1004. Whatever bhikkhunī should use a seasonal robe without having relinquished it, it is an offense requiring expiation.

1005. Yā [V 0.0415] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1005. 'Whatever' means: whatever sort... 'A bhikkhunī' means... in this sense, this bhikkhunī is meant.

Āvasathacīvaraṃ nāma “utuniyo bhikkhuniyo paribhuñjantū”ti dinnaṃ hoti.

A seasonal robe is one that is given with the thought: 'Let the bhikkhunīs who are having their season use it.'

Anissajjitvā paribhuñjeyyāti dvetisso rattiyo paribhuñjitvā catutthadivase dhovitvā bhikkhuniyā vā sikkhamānāya vā sāmaṇeriyā vā anissajjitvā paribhuñjati[T 0.0174], āpatti pācittiyassa.

As to 'should use without having relinquished it': having used it for two or three nights, on the fourth day, after washing it, if she uses it without having relinquished it to a bhikkhunī, a probationer, or a female novice, it is an offense requiring expiation.

1006. Anissajjite anissajjitasaññā paribhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anissajjite vematikā paribhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anissajjite nissajjitasaññā paribhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

1006. If one uses what has not been relinquished, perceiving it as unrelinquished, it is an offense requiring expiation. If one uses what has not been relinquished, while being in doubt, it is an offense requiring expiation. If one uses what has not been relinquished, perceiving it as relinquished, it is an offense requiring expiation.

Nissajjite anissajjitasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissajjite vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissajjite nissajjitasaññā anāpatti.

If it has been relinquished, but she perceives it as not relinquished, it is an offense of wrong conduct. If it has been relinquished, but she is in doubt, it is an offense of wrong conduct. If it has been relinquished, and she perceives it as relinquished, there is no offense.

1007. Anāpatti nissajjitvā paribhuñjati, puna pariyāyena paribhuñjati, aññā utuniyo bhikkhuniyo na honti, acchinnacīvarikāya, naṭṭhacīvarikāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1007. There is no offense if she uses it after having relinquished it; if she uses it again in turn; if there are no other bhikkhunīs who are having their season; for one whose robe has been snatched away; for one whose robe is lost; in times of calamity; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Seventh Training Rule is finished.

8. Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Eighth Training Rule

1008. Tena [P 4.0304][M 0.0400] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī āvasathaṃ anissajjitvā cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā āvasatho ḍayhati. Bhikkhuniyo evamāhaṃsu – “handāyye, bhaṇḍakaṃ nīharāmā”ti. Ekaccā evamāhaṃsu – “na mayaṃ, ayye, nīharissāma. Yaṃ kiñci naṭṭhaṃ sabbaṃ amhe abhiyuñjissatī”ti. Thullanandā bhikkhunī punadeva taṃ āvasathaṃ paccāgantvā bhikkhuniyo pucchi – “apāyye, bhaṇḍakaṃ nīharitthā”ti? “Na [V 0.0416] mayaṃ, ayye, nīharimhā”ti[T 0.0175]. Thullanandā bhikkhunī ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo āvasathe ḍayhamāne bhaṇḍakaṃ na nīharissantī”ti! Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā āvasathaṃ anissajjitvā cārikaṃ pakkamissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī āvasathaṃ anissajjitvā cārikaṃ pakkamatīti pakkamīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī āvasathaṃ anissajjitvā cārikaṃ pakkamissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1008. At one time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā went wandering without having handed over her dwelling. And at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā’s dwelling burned down. The bhikkhunīs said, “Come, venerable ladies, let us remove the goods.” Some said, “No, venerable ladies, we will not remove them. If anything is lost, she will accuse us for all of it.” When the bhikkhunī Thullanandā returned to that dwelling, she asked the bhikkhunīs, “Venerable ladies, did you not remove the goods?” “No, venerable lady, we did not remove them.” The bhikkhunī Thullanandā complained, criticized, and spread it about, “How could the bhikkhunīs not remove the goods when the dwelling was burning?” Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… and so on… complained, criticized, and spread it about, “How could the venerable Thullanandā go wandering without having handed over her dwelling?”… and so on… “Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā went wandering without having handed over her dwelling?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… and so on… “How indeed, monks, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā go wandering without having handed over her dwelling? This, monks, is not for the inspiring of faith in the faithless… and so on… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1009. “Yā pana bhikkhunī āvasathaṃ anissajjitvā cārikaṃ pakkameyya, pācittiya”nti.

1009. “Whatever bhikkhunī should go wandering without having handed over her dwelling, it is a pācittiya offense.”

1010. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1010. Whatever: whichever… and so on… Bhikkhunī: …and so on… the bhikkhunī who is intended in this context.

Āvasatho nāma kavāṭabaddho vuccati.

A dwelling is defined as that which is fastened with a door-leaf.

Anissajjitvā cārikaṃ pakkameyyāti bhikkhuniyā vā sikkhamānāya vā sāmaṇeriyā vā anissajjitvā parikkhittassa āvasathassa parikkhepaṃ atikkāmentiyā āpatti pācittiyassa. Aparikkhittassa āvasathassa upacāraṃ atikkāmentiyā āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should go wandering without having handed over’: if, without having handed it over to a bhikkhunī, a probationer, or a female novice, she crosses the boundary of an enclosed dwelling, it is a pācittiya offense. If she crosses the vicinity of an unenclosed dwelling without having handed it over, it is a pācittiya offense.

1011. Anissajjite anissajjitasaññā pakkamati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anissajjite vematikā pakkamati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anissajjite [T 0.0176] nissajjitasaññā pakkamati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

1011. If it has not been handed over and she perceives it as not handed over when she departs, it is a pācittiya offense. If it has not been handed over and she is in doubt when she departs, it is a pācittiya offense. If it has not been handed over and she perceives it as handed over when she departs, it is a pācittiya offense.

Akavāṭabaddhaṃ [M 0.0401] anissajjitvā pakkamati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissajjite anissajjitasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissajjite vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Nissajjite nissajjitasaññā, anāpatti.

If she departs without having handed over a dwelling that is not fastened with a door-leaf, it is a dukkaṭa offense. If it has been handed over, but she perceives it as not handed over, it is a dukkaṭa offense. If it has been handed over, and she is in doubt, it is a dukkaṭa offense. If it has been handed over, and she perceives it as handed over, there is no offense.

1012. Anāpatti [P 4.0305][V 0.0417] nissajjitvā pakkamati, sati antarāye, pariyesitvā na labhati, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1012. There is no offense if she departs after having handed it over; if there is an obstacle; if she searches but does not find someone to hand it over to; for one who is ill; in times of danger; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Eighth Training Rule is concluded.

9. Navamasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Ninth Training Rule

1013. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo tiracchānavijjaṃ pariyāpuṇanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo tiracchānavijjaṃ pariyāpuṇissanti, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo tiracchānavijjaṃ pariyāpuṇissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo tiracchānavijjaṃ pariyāpuṇantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi [T 0.0177] nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo tiracchānavijjaṃ pariyāpuṇissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1013. At one time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time the bhikkhunīs of the Group of Six were learning worldly arts. People complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How can bhikkhunīs learn worldly arts, just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… and so on… complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How can the bhikkhunīs of the Group of Six learn worldly arts?”… and so on… “Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunīs of the Group of Six are learning worldly arts?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… and so on… “How, monks, can the bhikkhunīs of the Group of Six learn worldly arts? This is not for the inspiring of faith in the faithless… and so on… And thus, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

1014. “Yā pana bhikkhunī tiracchānavijjaṃ pariyāpuṇeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1014. “Whatever bhikkhunī should learn a worldly art, it is a pācittiya offense.”

1015. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1015. Whatever: whichever… and so on… Bhikkhunī: …and so on… the bhikkhunī who is intended in this context.

Tiracchānavijjā tiracchānavijjaṃ (ka.) nāma yaṃ kiñci bāhirakaṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ.

A worldly art is whatever is external and unbeneficial.

Pariyāpuṇeyyāti [M 0.0402] padena pariyāpuṇāti, pade pade āpatti pācittiyassa. Akkharāya pariyāpuṇāti, akkharakkharāya āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should learn’: if she learns by the word, for each word it is a pācittiya offense. If she learns by the letter, for each letter it is a pācittiya offense.

1016. Anāpatti [V 0.0418] lekhaṃ pariyāpuṇāti, dhāraṇaṃ pariyāpuṇāti, guttatthāya parittaṃ pariyāpuṇāti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1016. There is no offense if she learns writing, if she learns for the purpose of memorization, if she learns a protective text for safety; for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Navamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Ninth Training Rule is concluded.

10. Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Tenth Training Rule

1017. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena [P 4.0306] chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo tiracchānavijjaṃ vācenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo tiracchānavijjaṃ vācessanti, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā [T 0.0178] bhikkhuniyo tiracchānavijjaṃ vācessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo tiracchānavijjaṃ vācentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo tiracchānavijjaṃ vācessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1017. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. At that time, the bhikkhunīs of the Group of Six were teaching worldly arts. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can bhikkhunīs teach worldly arts, just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wants... they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can the bhikkhunīs of the Group of Six teach worldly arts?”... “Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunīs of the Group of Six are teaching worldly arts?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... “How can the bhikkhunīs of the Group of Six teach worldly arts? This, monks, is not for the inspiring of faith in the unfaithful... And thus, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

1018. “Yā pana bhikkhunī tiracchānavijjaṃ vāceyya, pācittiya”nti.

1018. “Whatever bhikkhunī should teach worldly arts, it is an offense requiring confession.”

1019. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1019. 'Whatever' means: whichever... 'Bhikkhunī' means... in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Tiracchānavijjā tiracchānavijjaṃ (ka.) nāma yaṃ kiñci bāhirakaṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ.

'Worldly arts' means: whatever is external to the teaching and unbeneficial.

Vāceyyāti padena vāceti, pade pade āpatti pācittiyassa. Akkharāya vāceti, akkharakkharāya āpatti pācittiyassa.

'Should teach' means: if she teaches by the word, for each word there is an offense requiring confession. If she teaches by the syllable, for each syllable there is an offense requiring confession.

1020. Anāpatti [M 0.0403][V 0.0419] lekhaṃ vāceti, dhāraṇaṃ vāceti, guttatthāya parittaṃ vāceti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1020. There is no offense if she teaches writing, if she teaches for memorization, if she teaches a protective text for safety; for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The tenth training rule is concluded.

Cittāgāravaggo pañcamo.

The Cittāgāra Chapter, the fifth.

6. Ārāmavaggo

6. The Chapter on Monasteries

1. Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The first training rule

1021. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū gāmakāvāse ekacīvarā cīvarakammaṃ karonti. Bhikkhuniyo anāpucchā ārāmaṃ pavisitvā yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Bhikkhū ujjhāyanti [T 0.0179] khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo anāpucchā ārāmaṃ pavisissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo anāpucchā ārāmaṃ pavisantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo anāpucchā ārāmaṃ pavisissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1021. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. At that time, a number of monks in a village dwelling, each with a single robe, were doing robe-work. The bhikkhunīs, without asking permission, entered the monastery and approached those monks. The monks complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can bhikkhunīs enter the monastery without asking permission?” … “Is it true, monks, that bhikkhunīs enter the monastery without asking permission?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How can bhikkhunīs enter the monastery without asking permission? This, monks, is not for the inspiring of faith in the unfaithful… And thus, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

“Yā pana bhikkhunī anāpucchā ārāmaṃ paviseyya, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever bhikkhunī should enter a monastery without asking permission, it is an offense requiring confession.”

Evañcidaṃ [T 0.0180] bhagavatā bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And thus this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhunīs.

1022. Tena kho pana samayena te bhikkhū tamhā āvāsā pakkamiṃsu. Bhikkhuniyo – “ayyā pakkantā”ti, ārāmaṃ nāgamaṃsu. Atha kho te bhikkhū punadeva taṃ āvāsaṃ paccāgacchiṃsu. Bhikkhuniyo – “ayyā āgatā”ti, āpucchā ārāmaṃ pavisitvā yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā [P 4.0307] te bhikkhū abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho tā bhikkhuniyo te bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “kissa tumhe, bhaginiyo, ārāmaṃ [V 0.0420] neva sammajjittha na pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpitthāti? Bhagavatā, ayyā, sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ paññattaṃ hoti (ka.) hoti – “na anāpucchā ārāmo pavisitabbo”ti. Tena mayaṃ na āgamimhā”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, santaṃ bhikkhuṃ āpucchā ārāmaṃ [M 0.0404] pavisituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1022. At that time, those monks departed from that dwelling. The bhikkhunīs, thinking, “The venerables have departed,” did not come to the monastery. Then those monks returned again to that dwelling. The bhikkhunīs, thinking, “The venerables have returned,” asked permission, entered the monastery, and approached those monks. Having approached and paid homage to those monks, they stood to one side. While they were standing to one side, those monks said to those bhikkhunīs: “Sisters, why did you not sweep the monastery, nor set out drinking water and water for use?” “Venerables, the Blessed One has laid down a training rule: ‘A monastery is not to be entered without asking permission.’ That is why we did not come.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Monks, I allow entering a monastery after asking a monk who is present. And thus, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

“Yā pana bhikkhunī santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā ārāmaṃ paviseyya, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever bhikkhunī should enter a monastery without asking a monk who is present, it is an offense requiring confession.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And thus this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhunīs.

1023. Tena kho pana samayena te bhikkhū tamhā āvāsā pakkamitvā punadeva taṃ āvāsaṃ paccāgacchiṃsu. Bhikkhuniyo – “ayyā pakkantā”ti anāpucchā ārāmaṃ pavisiṃsu. Tāsaṃ kukkuccaṃ ahosi – “bhagavatā sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ – ‘na santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā ārāmo pavisitabbo’ti. Mayañcamhā santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā ārāmaṃ pavisimhā. Kacci nu kho mayaṃ pācittiyaṃ āpattiṃ āpannā”ti…pe… bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1023. At that time, those monks, having departed from that dwelling, returned again to that dwelling. The bhikkhunīs, thinking, “The venerables have departed,” entered the monastery without asking permission. Remorse arose for them: “The Blessed One has laid down a training rule: ‘A monastery is not to be entered without asking a monk who is present.’ And we have entered the monastery without asking a monk who is present. Could it be that we have committed an offense requiring confession?” … They reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks… “And thus, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

1024. “Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṃ sabhikkhukaṃ ārāmaṃ anāpucchā paviseyya, pācittiya”nti.

1024. “Whatever bhikkhunī, knowing a monastery to have monks, should enter without asking permission, it is an offense requiring confession.”

1025. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1025. 'Whatever' means: whichever... 'Bhikkhunī' means... in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Jānāti nāma sāmaṃ vā jānāti, aññe vā tassā ārocenti, te vā ārocenti.

'Knowing' means: she knows by herself, or others inform her, or those monks inform her.

Sabhikkhuko nāma ārāmo yattha bhikkhū rukkhamūlepi vasanti.

A monastery 'with monks' means a place where monks dwell, even at the foot of a tree.

Anāpucchā ārāmaṃ paviseyyāti bhikkhuṃ vā sāmaṇeraṃ vā ārāmikaṃ vā anāpucchā parikkhittassa [V 0.0421] ārāmassa parikkhepaṃ atikkāmentiyā āpatti pācittiyassa. Aparikkhittassa ārāmassa upacāraṃ okkamantiyā āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should enter a park without asking’ means: for a bhikkhunī who crosses the boundary of an enclosed park without asking a bhikkhu, a sāmaṇera, or a park-keeper, there is an offense of pācittiya. For a bhikkhunī who steps into the vicinity of an unenclosed park, there is an offense of pācittiya.

1026. Sabhikkhuke sabhikkhukasaññā santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā ārāmaṃ pavisati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Sabhikkhuke vematikā santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā [T 0.0181][M 0.0405] ārāmaṃ pavisati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sabhikkhuke abhikkhukasaññā santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā ārāmaṃ pavisati, anāpatti.

1026. When a park has a bhikkhu and she perceives it as such, if she enters without asking a bhikkhu who is present, there is an offense of pācittiya. When a park has a bhikkhu and she is doubtful, if she enters without asking a bhikkhu who is present, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. When a park has a bhikkhu but she perceives it as not having a bhikkhu, if she enters without asking a bhikkhu who is present, there is no offense.

Abhikkhuke sabhikkhukasaññā, āpatti [P 4.0308] dukkaṭassa. Abhikkhuke vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Abhikkhuke abhikkhukasaññā, anāpatti.

When a park has no bhikkhu, if she perceives it as having a bhikkhu, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. When a park has no bhikkhu, if she is doubtful, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. When a park has no bhikkhu, if she perceives it as not having a bhikkhu, there is no offense.

1027. Anāpatti santaṃ bhikkhuṃ āpucchā pavisati, asantaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā pavisati, sīsānulokikā gacchati, yattha bhikkhuniyo sannipatitā honti tattha gacchati, ārāmena maggo hoti, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1027. There is no offense: if she enters after asking a bhikkhu who is present; if she enters without asking when no bhikkhu is present; if she goes following the lead of those in front; if she goes to a place where bhikkhunīs are assembled; if there is a path through the park; for one who is sick; in emergencies; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The First Training Rule is finished.

2. Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Second Training Rule

1028. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato upālissa upajjhāyo āyasmā kappitako susāne viharati. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ mahattarā mahantatarā (sī.) bhikkhunī kālaṅkatā hoti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo taṃ bhikkhuniṃ nīharitvā āyasmato kappitakassa vihārassa avidūre jhāpetvā thūpaṃ katvā gantvā tasmiṃ thūpe rodanti. Atha kho āyasmā kappitako tena saddena ubbāḷho taṃ thūpaṃ bhinditvā pakiresi. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo – “iminā kappitakena amhākaṃ ayyāya thūpo bhinno, handa naṃ ghātemā”ti, mantesuṃ[T 0.0182]. Aññatarā bhikkhunī āyasmato upālissa etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Āyasmā upāli āyasmato kappitakassa etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Atha kho āyasmā kappitako vihārā nikkhamitvā nilīno acchi. Atha kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo yenāyasmato kappitakassa vihāro tenupasaṅkamiṃsu[V 0.0422]; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmato kappitakassa vihāraṃ pāsāṇehi ca leḍḍūhi ca ottharāpetvā, “mato kappitako”ti pakkamiṃsu.

1028. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling at Vesālī in the Great Wood, in the Hall with the Peaked Roof. Now at that time, the preceptor of the Venerable Upāli, the Venerable Kappitaka, was dwelling in a charnel ground. At that time, a very senior nun of the group of six nuns had passed away. The nuns of the group of six carried that nun out, cremated her not far from the Venerable Kappitaka’s dwelling, built a stūpa, and then went to weep at that stūpa. Then the Venerable Kappitaka, being disturbed by that sound, broke that stūpa and scattered it. The nuns of the group of six conspired, saying, “This Kappitaka has destroyed our noble lady’s stūpa—come, let us kill him!” A certain nun informed the Venerable Upāli of this matter. The Venerable Upāli informed the Venerable Kappitaka of this matter. Then the Venerable Kappitaka left his dwelling and remained in hiding. Then the nuns of the group of six went to where the Venerable Kappitaka’s dwelling was. Having approached, they had the Venerable Kappitaka’s dwelling covered with stones and clods of earth, and then departed, thinking, “Kappitaka is dead!”

Atha [M 0.0406] kho āyasmā kappitako tassā rattiyā accayena pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Addasaṃsu kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo āyasmantaṃ kappitakaṃ piṇḍāya carantaṃ. Disvāna evamāhaṃsu – “ayaṃ kappitako jīvati, ko nu kho amhākaṃ mantaṃ saṃharī”ti? Assosuṃ kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo – “ayyena kira upālinā amhākaṃ manto saṃhaṭo”ti. Tā āyasmantaṃ upāliṃ akkosiṃsu – “kathañhi nāma ayaṃ kāsāvaṭo malamajjano nihīnajacco amhākaṃ mantaṃ saṃharissatī”ti! Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti [P 4.0309] – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ayyaṃ upāliṃ akkosissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo upāliṃ akkosantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo upāliṃ akkosissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave[T 0.0183], bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

Then, after that night had passed, in the morning time, the Venerable Kappitaka dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Vesālī for alms-food. The nuns of the group of six saw the Venerable Kappitaka wandering for alms-food. Having seen him, they spoke thus: “This Kappitaka is alive. Who indeed has revealed our plan?” The nuns of the group of six heard: “It is said that our plan was revealed by the noble Upāli.” They reviled the Venerable Upāli, saying: “How indeed could this wearer of the ochre robe, this cleanser of filth, this one of low birth, reveal our plan?” Those nuns who were of few wishes… (etc.)… they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the nuns of the group of six revile the noble Upāli?”… (etc.)… “Is it true, monks, that the nuns of the group of six revile Upāli?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… (etc.)… “How indeed, monks, could the nuns of the group of six revile Upāli? This, monks, is not for the faith of the faithless… (etc.)… And so, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule:”

1029. “Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuṃ akkoseyya vā paribhāseyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

1029. “Whatever nun should revile or threaten a monk, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

1030. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1030. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever sort… (etc.)… ‘nun’ means… (etc.)… in this context, this is the nun who is intended.

Bhikkhunti upasampannaṃ. Akkoseyya vāti dasahi vā akkosavatthūhi akkosati etesaṃ vā aññatarena, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Monk’ means an ordained one. ‘Should revile’ means: if she reviles with the ten grounds for reviling, or with any one of them, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Paribhāseyya vāti bhayaṃ upadaṃseti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should threaten’ means: if she indicates danger, there is an offense of pācittiya.
