1031. Upasampanne upasampannasaññā akkosati vā paribhāsati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne vematikā akkosati vā paribhāsati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Upasampanne anupasampannasaññā akkosati vā paribhāsati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

1031. In the case of an ordained one, if she perceives him as ordained and reviles or threatens him, there is an offense of pācittiya. In the case of an ordained one, if she is in doubt and reviles or threatens him, there is an offense of pācittiya. In the case of an ordained one, if she perceives him as not ordained and reviles or threatens him, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Anupasampannaṃ [V 0.0423] akkosati vā paribhāsati vā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne upasampannasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anupasampanne anupasampannasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If she reviles or threatens a non-ordained person, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. In the case of a non-ordained person, if she perceives him as ordained, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. In the case of a non-ordained person, if she is in doubt, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. In the case of a non-ordained person, if she perceives him as not ordained, it is an offense of dukkaṭa.

1032. Anāpatti [M 0.0407] atthapurekkhārāya, dhammapurekkhārāya, anusāsanipurekkhārāya, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1032. There is no offense for one who has the meaning as her aim, for one who has the Dhamma as her aim, for one who has instruction as her aim; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Second Training Rule is finished.

3. Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Third Training Rule

1033. Tena [T 0.0184] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī bhaṇḍanakārikā hoti kalahakārikā vivādakārikā bhassakārikā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārikā. Thullanandā bhikkhunī tassā kamme karīyamāne paṭikkosati. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī gāmakaṃ agamāsi kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho bhikkhunisaṅgho – “thullanandā bhikkhunī pakkantā”ti caṇḍakāḷiṃ bhikkhuniṃ āpattiyā adassane ukkhipi. Thullanandā bhikkhunī gāmake taṃ karaṇīyaṃ tīretvā punadeva sāvatthiṃ [P 4.0310] paccāgacchi. Caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā āgacchantiyā neva āsanaṃ paññapesi na pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakaṭhalikaṃ upanikkhipi; na paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahesi na pānīyena āpucchi. Thullanandā bhikkhunī caṇḍakāḷiṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “kissa tvaṃ, ayye, mayi āgacchantiyā neva āsanaṃ paññapesi na pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakaṭhalikaṃ upanikkhipi; na paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahesi na pānīyena āpucchī”ti? “Evañhetaṃ, ayye, hoti yathā taṃ anāthāyā”ti. “Kissa pana tvaṃ, ayye, anāthā”ti? “Imā maṃ, ayye, bhikkhuniyo – “ayaṃ anāthā appaññātā, natthi [T 0.0185] imissā kāci pativattā”ti, āpattiyā adassane ukkhipiṃsū”ti. Thullanandā bhikkhunī – “bālā etā abyattā etā netā jānanti kammaṃ vā kammadosaṃ vā kammavipattiṃ vā kammasampattiṃ vā”ti, caṇḍīkatā gaṇaṃ paribhāsi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā caṇḍīkatā gaṇaṃ paribhāsissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī caṇḍīkatā gaṇaṃ paribhāsatīti paribhāsīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā [V 0.0424] …pe…kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī caṇḍīkatā gaṇaṃ [M 0.0408] paribhāsissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1033. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī was quarrelsome, argumentative, contentious, a babbler, and one who created legal issues in the Saṅgha. When a formal act was being carried out against her, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā protested. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā had gone to a small village on some business. Then the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, thinking, “The bhikkhunī Thullanandā has departed,” suspended the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī for not seeing her offense. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having completed that business in the small village, returned again to Sāvatthī. When the bhikkhunī Thullanandā was arriving, the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī neither prepared a seat, nor placed water for the feet, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet nearby; she did not go out to meet her to receive her bowl and robe, nor did she inquire with drinking water. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā said this to the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī: “Why is it, venerable, that when I was arriving, you neither prepared a seat, nor placed water for the feet, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet nearby; you did not go out to meet me to receive my bowl and robe, nor did you inquire with drinking water?” “This is just how it is, venerable, for one who is without a protector.” “But why, venerable, are you without a protector?” “Venerable, these bhikkhunīs suspended me for not seeing an offense, saying, ‘This one is without a protector, she is unknown; there is no one to restrain her.’” The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, being harsh, disparaged the group, saying: “These are foolish, these are incompetent, they do not know a formal act, or the fault of a formal act, or the failure of a formal act, or the completion of a formal act.” Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… they looked down upon, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the venerable Thullanandā, being harsh, disparage the group?”… “Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, being harsh, disparages the group?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, monks, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, being harsh, disparage the group? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1034. “Yā pana bhikkhunī caṇḍīkatā gaṇaṃ paribhāseyya, pācittiya”nti.

1034. “Whatever bhikkhunī, being harsh, should disparage the group, it is an offense entailing confession.”

1035. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1035. ‘Whatever’ means: whichever, of whatever sort... ‘A bhikkhunī’ means: ... this is the bhikkhunī who is intended in this case.

Caṇḍīkatā nāma kodhanā vuccati.

Being harsh is called being wrathful.

Gaṇo nāma bhikkhunisaṅgho vuccati.

A group is called the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs.

Paribhāseyyāti “bālā etā abyattā etā netā jānanti kammaṃ vā kammadosaṃ vā kammavipattiṃ vā kammasampattiṃ vā”ti paribhāsati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo vā ekaṃ bhikkhuniṃ vā anupasampannaṃ vā paribhāsati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

‘Should disparage’ means: if she disparages them, saying, “These are foolish, these are incompetent, they do not know a formal act, or the fault of a formal act, or the failure of a formal act, or the completion of a formal act,” there is an offense entailing confession. If she disparages many bhikkhunīs, or one bhikkhunī, or an unordained woman, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

1036. Anāpatti [T 0.0186] atthapurekkhārāya, dhammapurekkhārāya, anusāsanipurekkhārāya, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1036. There is no offense for one who has the meaning as her aim, for one who has the Dhamma as her aim, for one who has instruction as her aim; for one who is insane; and for the first offender.

Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Third Training Rule is concluded.

4. Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Fourth Training Rule

1037. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro brāhmaṇo bhikkhuniyo nimantetvā bhojesi[P 4.0311]. Bhikkhuniyo bhuttāvī bhuttāvinī (ka.) pavāritā ñātikulāni gantvā ekaccā bhuñjiṃsu ekaccā piṇḍapātaṃ ādāya agamaṃsu. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo paṭivissake etadavoca – “bhikkhuniyo mayā ayyā santappitā, etha tumhepi santappessāmī”ti. Te evamāhaṃsu – “kiṃ tvaṃ, ayyo, amhe santappessasi! Yāpi tayā nimantitā tāpi amhākaṃ gharāni āgantvā ekaccā bhuñjiṃsu ekaccā [V 0.0425] piṇḍapātaṃ [M 0.0409] ādāya agamaṃsū”ti. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo amhākaṃ ghare bhuñjitvā aññatra bhuñjissanti, na cāhaṃ paṭibalo yāvadatthaṃ dātu”nti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tassa brāhmaṇassa ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo bhuttāvī bhuttāvinī (ka.) pavāritā aññatra bhuñjissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo bhuttāvī pavāritā aññatra bhuñjantīti[T 0.0187]? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo bhuttāvī pavāritā aññatra bhuñjissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1037. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. At that time, a certain brahmin, having invited the bhikkhunīs, served them a meal. The bhikkhunīs, having eaten and having refused more food, went to their relatives’ families, where some ate and some, having taken almsfood, went away. Then that brahmin said this to his neighbors: “The venerable bhikkhunīs have been satisfied by me; come, I will satisfy you too.” They said thus: “Sir, how will you satisfy us? Those bhikkhunīs whom you invited, they too, having come to our houses, some ate, and some, having taken almsfood, went away.” Then that brahmin complained, criticized, and spread the word disparagingly: “How indeed could the bhikkhunīs, having eaten in our house, eat elsewhere? Am I not able to give as much as is desired?” The bhikkhunīs heard that brahmin complaining, criticizing, and spreading the word disparagingly. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread the word disparagingly: “How indeed could the bhikkhunīs, having eaten and having refused more food, eat elsewhere?”… “Is it true, Bhikkhus, as has been heard, that bhikkhunīs, having eaten and having refused more food, eat elsewhere?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “Bhikkhus, how indeed could the bhikkhunīs, having eaten and having refused more food, eat elsewhere? This, Bhikkhus, does not lead to the confidence of the unconfident… And thus, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1038. “Yā pana bhikkhunī nimantitā vā pavāritā vā khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

1038. “Whatever bhikkhunī, having been invited or having refused more food, should chew chewable food or eat staple food, it is an offense entailing confession.”

1039. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1039. ‘Whatever’ means: whichever, of whatever sort... ‘A bhikkhunī’ means: ... this is the bhikkhunī who is intended in this case.

Nimantitā nāma pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ aññatarena bhojanena nimantitā.

Invited means: invited with one or another of the five kinds of staple food.

Pavāritā nāma asanaṃ paññāyati, bhojanaṃ paññāyati, hatthapāse ṭhitā abhiharati, paṭikkhepo paññāyati.

Refused more food means: the act of eating is apparent, the staple food is apparent, one standing within hand's reach brings it forward, and a refusal is apparent.

Khādanīyaṃ nāma pañca bhojanāni – yāguṃ yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ khādanīyaṃ nāma.

That which is called 'chewable food' is the remainder, after setting aside the five staple foods, rice-gruel, time-limited items, seven-day items, and life-long items.

Bhojanīyaṃ nāma pañca bhojanāni – odano, kummāso, sattu, maccho, maṃsaṃ.

That which is called 'staple food' refers to the five staple foods: cooked rice, barley-meal, flour of parched grain, fish, and meat.

“Khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

If one accepts it with the thought, 'I will chew, I will eat,' an offense of wrong-doing is incurred. With every swallow, a pācittiya offense is incurred.

1040. Nimantite [V 0.0426] nimantitasaññā khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Nimantite vematikā khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ [M 0.0410] vā khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa. Nimantite animantitasaññā khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā khādati vā bhuñjati vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

1040. When invited, being aware of the invitation, if one chews chewable food or eats staple food, a pācittiya offense is incurred. When invited, being in doubt about the invitation, if one chews chewable food or eats staple food, a pācittiya offense is incurred. When invited, being unaware of the invitation, if one chews chewable food or eats staple food, a pācittiya offense is incurred.

Yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ [T 0.0188] yāvajīvikaṃ āhāratthāya paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti dukkaṭassa…pe….

If one accepts a time-limited item, a seven-day item, or a life-long item for the purpose of food, an offense of wrong-doing is incurred. With every swallow, an offense of wrong-doing is incurred... (and so on).

1041. Anāpatti nimantitā appavāritā, yāguṃ pivati, sāmike apaloketvā bhuñjati, yāmakālikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ sati paccaye paribhuñjati, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1041. There is no offense for one who, having been invited, has not yet refused more food; if one drinks rice-gruel; if one eats after having informed the owners; if, there being a reason, one consumes a time-limited item, a seven-day item, or a life-long item; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fourth Training Rule is concluded.

5. Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Fifth Training Rule

1042. Tena [P 4.0312] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī sāvatthiyaṃ aññatarissā visikhāya piṇḍāya caramānā yena aññataraṃ kulaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho te manussā taṃ bhikkhuniṃ bhojetvā etadavocuṃ – “aññāpi, ayye, bhikkhuniyo āgacchantū”ti. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī, “kathañhi nāma kathaṃ aññā (syā.) bhikkhuniyo nāgaccheyyu”nti, bhikkhuniyo upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – “amukasmiṃ, ayye, okāse vāḷā sunakhā caṇḍo balibaddo cikkhallo okāso. Mā kho tattha agamitthā”ti. Aññatarāpi bhikkhunī tassā visikhāya piṇḍāya caramānā yena taṃ kulaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho te manussā taṃ bhikkhuniṃ bhojetvā etadavocuṃ – “kissa, ayye, bhikkhuniyo na āgacchantī”ti? Atha kho sā bhikkhunī tesaṃ manussānaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Manussā [T 0.0189] ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī kulaṃ maccharāyissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī kulaṃ [M 0.0411] maccharāyatīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī kulaṃ [V 0.0427] maccharāyissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1042. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī, while walking for alms-food in a certain street in Sāvatthī, approached a certain family. Having approached, she sat down on the prepared seat. Then those people, having fed that bhikkhunī, said this: “Venerable lady, let other bhikkhunīs also come.” Then that bhikkhunī, thinking, “How indeed might the bhikkhunīs not come?” having approached the bhikkhunīs, said this: “Venerable ladies, in such-and-such a place there are fierce dogs, a savage bull, and it is a muddy place. Do not go there.” Another bhikkhunī, while walking for alms-food in that street, approached that family. Having approached, she sat down on the prepared seat. Then those people, having fed that bhikkhunī, said this: “Venerable lady, why do the bhikkhunīs not come?” Then that bhikkhunī told this matter to those people. The people complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed could a bhikkhunī be possessive of a family?”… (and so on) … “Is it true, monks, as is said, that a bhikkhunī is possessive of a family?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… (and so on) … “How indeed, monks, could a bhikkhunī be possessive of a family! This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… (and so on) … And thus, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

1043. “Yā pana bhikkhunī kulamaccharinī assa, pācittiya”nti.

1043. Whatever bhikkhunī should be possessive of a family, it is a pācittiya offense.

1044. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1044. 'Whatever' means: whatever, of whatever kind… (and so on). 'Bhikkhunī' means… (and so on)… in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Kulaṃ nāma cattāri kulāni – khattiyakulaṃ, brāhmaṇakulaṃ, vessakulaṃ, suddakulaṃ.

That which is called a 'family' refers to four kinds of families: the noble family, the brahmin family, the merchant family, and the commoner family.

Maccharinī assāti “kathaṃ bhikkhuniyo nāgaccheyyu”nti bhikkhunīnaṃ santike kulassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Kulassa vā santike bhikkhunīnaṃ avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

'Should be possessive' means: if, thinking, “How might the bhikkhunīs not come?” she speaks dispraise of the family in the presence of the bhikkhunīs, a pācittiya offense is incurred. Or, if she speaks dispraise of the bhikkhunīs in the presence of the family, a pācittiya offense is incurred.

1045. Anāpatti kulaṃ na maccharāyantī santaṃyeva ādīnavaṃ ācikkhati, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1045. There is no offense if, not being possessive of the family, she points out an actual drawback; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fifth Training Rule is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Sixth Training Rule

1046. Tena [P 4.0313] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhuniyo gāmakāvāse vassaṃvuṭṭhā sāvatthiṃ agamaṃsu. Bhikkhuniyo tā [T 0.0190] bhikkhuniyo etadavocuṃ – “katthāyyāyo vassaṃvuṭṭhā? Kacci ovādo iddho ahosī”ti? “Natthayye, tattha bhikkhū; kuto ovādo iddho bhavissatī”ti! Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo abhikkhuke āvāse vassaṃ vasissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo abhikkhuke āvāse vassaṃ vasantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave[M 0.0412], bhikkhuniyo abhikkhuke āvāse vassaṃ [V 0.0428] vasissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1046. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, in the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, many bhikkhunīs who had completed the rains-residence in a village dwelling went to Sāvatthī. The bhikkhunīs said this to those bhikkhunīs: “Venerable ladies, where did you complete the rains-residence? Was the instruction abundant?” “Venerable ladies, there are no bhikkhus there; how could the instruction be abundant?” Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… (and so on) … criticized, scorned, and disparaged them: “How indeed could bhikkhunīs reside for the rains-residence in a dwelling without bhikkhus?”… (and so on) … “Is it true, monks, as has been heard, that bhikkhunīs are residing for the rains-residence in a dwelling without bhikkhus?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… (and so on) … “How indeed, monks, could bhikkhunīs reside for the rains-residence in a dwelling without bhikkhus! This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… (and so on) … And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1047. “Yā pana bhikkhunī abhikkhuke āvāse vassaṃ vaseyya, pācittiya”nti.

1047. Whatever bhikkhunī should reside for the rains-residence in a dwelling without bhikkhus, it is a pācittiya offense.

1048. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1048. 'Whatever' means: whatever, of whatever kind… (and so on). 'Bhikkhunī' means… (and so on)… in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Abhikkhuko nāma āvāso na sakkā hoti ovādāya vā saṃvāsāya vā gantuṃ. “Vassaṃ vasissāmī”ti senāsanaṃ paññapeti pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhapeti pariveṇaṃ sammajjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Saha aruṇuggamanā āpatti pācittiyassa.

A dwelling called 'without bhikkhus' is one from which it is not possible to go for instruction or for communion. If, thinking, 'I will reside for the rains-residence,' she prepares a lodging, sets out drinking water and water for use, or sweeps the compound, an offense of wrong-doing is incurred. At the rising of the dawn, a pācittiya offense is incurred.

1049. Anāpatti vassupagatā bhikkhū pakkantā vā honti vibbhantā vā kālaṅkatā vā pakkhasaṅkantā vā, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1049. There is no offense if, after she has entered the rains-residence, the bhikkhus have departed, or have disrobed, or have died, or have gone over to another sect; in times of calamity; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Sixth Training Rule is concluded.

7. Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Seventh Training Rule

1050. Tena [T 0.0191] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhuniyo gāmakāvāse vassaṃvuṭṭhā sāvatthiṃ agamaṃsu. Bhikkhuniyo tā bhikkhuniyo etadavocuṃ – “katthāyyāyo vassaṃvuṭṭhā; kattha kacci (syā.) bhikkhusaṅgho pavārito”ti[P 4.0314]? “Na mayaṃ, ayye, bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pavāremā”ti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo vassaṃvuṭṭhā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ na pavāressantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo vassaṃvuṭṭhā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ na pavārentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo vassaṃvuṭṭhā [M 0.0413] bhikkhusaṅghaṃ na pavāressanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1050. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, in the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, many bhikkhunīs who had completed the rains-residence in a village dwelling went to Sāvatthī. The bhikkhunīs said this to those bhikkhunīs: “Venerable ladies, where did you complete the rains-residence? Have you invited the Saṅgha of bhikkhus?” “Venerable ladies, we did not invite the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.” Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… criticized, scorned, and disparaged them: “How indeed could bhikkhunīs, having completed the rains-residence, not invite the Saṅgha of bhikkhus?”… “Is it true, Bhikkhus, as has been heard, that bhikkhunīs, having completed the rains-residence, do not invite the Saṅgha of bhikkhus?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, could bhikkhunīs, having completed the rains-residence, not invite the Saṅgha of bhikkhus! This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1051. “Yā [V 0.0429] pana bhikkhunī vassaṃvuṭṭhā ubhatosaṅghe tīhi ṭhānehi na pavāreyya diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā, pācittiya”nti.

1051. “Whatever bhikkhunī, having completed the rains-residence, should not invite before both Saṅghas on three grounds—by what is seen, by what is heard, or by what is suspected—it is an offense of pācittiya.”

1052. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1052. As to 'whatever': whatever, of whatever sort... As to 'bhikkhunī': ... in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Vassaṃvuṭṭhā nāma purimaṃ vā temāsaṃ pacchimaṃ vā temāsaṃ vuṭṭhā. Ubhatosaṅghe tīhi ṭhānehi na pavāressāmi diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā”ti dhuraṃ nikkhittamatte [T 0.0192] āpatti pācittiyassa.

One called 'having completed the rains-residence' is a bhikkhunī who has completed either the first three-month period or the last three-month period. At the mere laying down of the burden with the thought, 'I will not invite before both Saṅghas on three grounds—by what is seen, by what is heard, or by what is suspected,' there is an offense of pācittiya.

1053. Anāpatti sati antarāye, pariyesitvā na labhati, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1053. There is no offense if there is an obstacle; if, having searched, she does not find one; for one who is sick; in calamities; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Seventh Training Rule is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Eighth Training Rule

1054. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhunupassayaṃ upasaṅkamitvā chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ovadanti. Bhikkhuniyo chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo etadavocuṃ – “ethāyye ovādaṃ gamissāmā”ti. “Yampi mayaṃ, ayye, gaccheyyāma ovādassa kāraṇā, ayyā chabbaggiyā idheva āgantvā amhe ovadantī”ti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ovādaṃ na gacchissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ovādaṃ na gacchantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ovādaṃ [P 4.0315] na gacchissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1054. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Nigrodha monastery. Now at that time, the monks of the group-of-six, having approached the nuns' quarters, exhorted the nuns of the group-of-six. The other nuns said this to the nuns of the group-of-six, 'Come, venerable ladies, let us go for the exhortation.' They replied, 'Venerable ladies, to whatever place we might go for the sake of exhortation, the venerable ones of the group-of-six come right here and exhort us.' Those nuns who were of few wishes... criticized, scorned, and disparaged them, saying, 'How indeed could the nuns of the group-of-six not go for the exhortation?' ... 'Is it true, monks, that the nuns of the group-of-six do not go for the exhortation?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... 'How indeed, monks, could the nuns of the group-of-six not go for the exhortation? This, monks, is not for inspiring confidence in the unconfident... And so, monks, the nuns should set forth this training rule:

1055. “Yā [M 0.0414] pana bhikkhunī ovādāya vā saṃvāsāya vā na gaccheyya, pācittiya”nti.

1055. “Whatever bhikkhunī should not go for exhortation or for communion, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

1056. Yā [V 0.0430] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ [T 0.0193] atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1056. As to 'whatever': whatever, of whatever sort... As to 'bhikkhunī': ... in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Ovādo nāma aṭṭha garudhammā.

Exhortation means the eight weighty rules.

Saṃvāso nāma ekakammaṃ ekuddeso samasikkhatā. Ovādāya vā saṃvāsāya vā na gacchissāmīti dhuraṃ nikkhittamatte āpatti pācittiyassa.

Communion means a common formal act, a common recitation, and equal training. 'I will not go for exhortation or for communion.' Merely upon laying down this burden, she incurs an offense of pācittiya.

1057. Anāpatti sati antarāye, pariyesitvā dutiyikaṃ bhikkhuniṃ na labhati, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1057. There is no offense if there is an obstacle; if, after searching, she does not find a companion bhikkhunī; for one who is sick; in times of danger; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Eighth Training Rule is concluded.

9. Navamasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Ninth Training Rule

1058. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo uposathampi na pucchanti ovādampi na yācanti. Bhikkhū ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo uposathampi na pucchissanti ovādampi na yācissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo “uposathampi na pucchanti ovādampi na yācantī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo uposathampi na pucchissanti ovādampi na yācissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1058. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the nuns neither asked about the Uposatha day nor requested the exhortation. The monks criticized, scorned, and disparaged them, saying, 'How indeed could the nuns neither ask about the Uposatha day nor request the exhortation?' ... 'Is it true, monks, that the nuns neither ask about the Uposatha day nor request the exhortation?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... 'How indeed, monks, could the nuns neither ask about the Uposatha day nor request the exhortation? This, monks, is not for inspiring confidence in the unconfident... And so, monks, the nuns should set forth this training rule:

1059. “Anvaddhamāsaṃ bhikkhuniyā bhikkhusaṅghato dve dhammā paccāsīsitabbā [T 0.0194] – uposathapucchakañca ovādūpasaṅkamanañca. Taṃ atikkāmentiyā pācittiya”nti.

1059. “Every half-month, a bhikkhunī should expect two things from the Saṅgha of monks: the asking of the Uposatha day and the approaching for exhortation. For a bhikkhunī who transgresses this, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

1060. Anvaddhamāsanti [M 0.0415] anuposathikaṃ. Uposatho nāma dve uposathā – cātuddasiko ca pannarasiko ca.

1060. Every half-month: on every Uposatha day. Uposatha means two Uposathas: that of the fourteenth day and that of the fifteenth day.

Ovādo [V 0.0431] nāma aṭṭha garudhammā. “Uposathampi na pucchissāmi ovādampi na yācissāmī”ti dhuraṃ nikkhittamatte āpatti pācittiyassa.

Exhortation means the eight weighty rules. 'I will not ask about the Uposatha day, nor will I request the exhortation.' Merely upon laying down this burden, she incurs an offense of pācittiya.

1061. Anāpatti sati antarāye, pariyesitvā dutiyikaṃ bhikkhuniṃ na labhati, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1061. There is no offense if there is an obstacle; if, after searching, she does not find a companion bhikkhunī; for one who is sick; in times of danger; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Navamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Ninth Training Rule is concluded.

10. Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Tenth Training Rule

1062. Tena [P 4.0316] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī pasākhe jātaṃ gaṇḍaṃ purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā bhedāpesi. Atha kho so puriso taṃ bhikkhuniṃ dūsetuṃ upakkami. Sā vissaramakāsi. Bhikkhuniyo upadhāvitvā taṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavocuṃ – “kissa tvaṃ, ayye, vissaramakāsī”ti? Atha kho sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī pasākhe jātaṃ gaṇḍaṃ purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā bhedāpessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī pasākhe jātaṃ gaṇḍaṃ purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā bhedāpetīti [T 0.0195] bhedāpesīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī pasākhe jātaṃ gaṇḍaṃ purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā bhedāpessati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1062. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. At that time, a certain bhikkhunī had a boil that had arisen in the fork of her thighs lanced by a man, one on one with him. Then that man attempted to violate that bhikkhunī. She cried out. The bhikkhunīs ran up and asked that bhikkhunī, “Venerable, why did you cry out?” Then that bhikkhunī told the bhikkhunīs what had happened. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed could a bhikkhunī have a boil that has arisen in the fork of her thighs lanced by a man, one on one with him?” … “Is it true, it is said, Bhikkhus, that a bhikkhunī had a boil that has arisen in the fork of her thighs lanced by a man, one on one with him?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her … “How indeed, Bhikkhus, could a bhikkhunī have a boil that has arisen in the fork of her thighs lanced by a man, one on one with him? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule in this way:

1063. “Yā pana bhikkhunī pasākhe jātaṃ gaṇḍaṃ vā rudhitaṃ vā anapaloketvā saṅghaṃ vā gaṇaṃ vā purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā bhedāpeyya vā phālāpeyya vā dhovāpeyya vā ālimpāpeyya vā bandhāpeyya vā mocāpeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

1063. “Whatever bhikkhunī, without having informed the Saṅgha or a group, should have a boil or a sore that has arisen in the fork of her thighs cut, or lanced, or washed, or anointed, or bandaged, or unbandaged by a man, one on one with him, it is an offense of expiation.”

1064. Yā [M 0.0416] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1064. Whatever means: whoever, of whatever sort… A bhikkhunī means… the bhikkhunī who is meant in this context.

Pasākhaṃ nāma adhonābhi ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ. Jātanti tattha jātaṃ. Gaṇḍo nāma yo koci [V 0.0432] gaṇḍo. Rudhitaṃ nāma yaṃ kiñci vaṇaṃ. Anapaloketvāti anāpucchā. Saṅgho nāma bhikkhunisaṅgho vuccati. Gaṇo nāma sambahulā bhikkhuniyo vuccanti. Puriso nāma manussapuriso, na yakkho, na peto, na tiracchānagato, viññū paṭibalo dūsetuṃ. Saddhinti ekato. Ekenekāti puriso ceva hoti bhikkhunī ca.

The fork of the thighs means the area from below the navel to above the kneecap. That has arisen means that which has arisen there. A boil means any kind of boil. A sore means any kind of wound. Without having informed means without asking. The Saṅgha is said to be the community of bhikkhunīs. A group is said to be several bhikkhunīs. A man means a human male, not a yakkha, not a peta, not an animal—one who is intelligent and capable of violating. With means together. One on one means there is a man and there is a bhikkhunī.

1065. “Bhindā”ti āṇāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Bhinne āpatti pācittiyassa. “Phālehī”ti āṇāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Phālite āpatti [T 0.0196] pācittiyassa. “Dhovā”ti āṇāpeti[P 4.0317], āpatti dukkaṭassa. Dhovite dhote (syā.) āpatti pācittiyassa. “Ālimpā”ti āṇāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Litte ālitte (syā.) āpatti pācittiyassa. “Bandhāhī”ti āṇāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Baddhe āpatti pācittiyassa. “Mocehī”ti āṇāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Mutte āpatti pācittiyassa.

1065. If she commands, “Cut,” there is an offense of wrong conduct. When it is cut, there is an offense of expiation. If she commands, “Lance,” there is an offense of wrong conduct. When it is lanced, there is an offense of expiation. If she commands, “Wash,” there is an offense of wrong conduct. When it is washed, there is an offense of expiation. If she commands, “Anoint,” there is an offense of wrong conduct. When it is anointed, there is an offense of expiation. If she commands, “Bandage,” there is an offense of wrong conduct. When it is bandaged, there is an offense of expiation. If she commands, “Untie,” there is an offense of wrong conduct. When it is untied, there is an offense of expiation.

1066. Anāpatti apaloketvā bhedāpeti vā phālāpeti vā dhovāpeti vā ālimpāpeti vā bandhāpeti vā mocāpeti vā, yā kāci viññū dutiyikā yā kāci viññū dutiyā (syā.), yo koci viññū dutiyo (ka.) hoti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1066. There is no offense if, having informed, she has it cut, or lanced, or washed, or anointed, or bandaged, or unbandaged; if there is any discerning companion present; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Tenth Training Rule is finished.

Ārāmavaggo chaṭṭho.

The Park Chapter, the sixth, is finished.

7. Gabbhinīvaggo

7. The Chapter on Pregnant Women

1. Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The First Training Rule

1067. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo gabbhiniṃ vuṭṭhāpenti. Sā piṇḍāya carati. Manussā evamāhaṃsu – “dethāyyāya bhikkhaṃ[M 0.0417], garubhārā garugabbhā (syā.) ayyā”ti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo gabbhiniṃ vuṭṭhāpessantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo [V 0.0433] appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo gabbhiniṃ vuṭṭhāpessantī”ti…pe… [T 0.0197] saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo gabbhiniṃ vuṭṭhāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo gabbhiniṃ vuṭṭhāpessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1067. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were giving the higher ordination to a pregnant woman. She went about for alms. People said thus: ‘Give alms to the venerable lady; the venerable lady is heavy with child.’ People complained, criticized, and spread it about: ‘How indeed can the bhikkhunīs give the higher ordination to a pregnant woman?’ The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread it about: ‘How indeed can the bhikkhunīs give the higher ordination to a pregnant woman?’… ‘Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunīs are giving the higher ordination to a pregnant woman?’ ‘It is true, Blessed One.’ The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… ‘How indeed, Bhikkhus, can the bhikkhunīs give the higher ordination to a pregnant woman! This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

1068. “Yā pana bhikkhunī gabbhiniṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1068. “Whatever bhikkhunī should give the higher ordination to a pregnant woman, it is an offense of expiation.”

1069. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1069. Whatever means: whoever, of whatever sort... A bhikkhunī means... the bhikkhunī who is meant in this context.

Gabbhinī nāma āpannasattā vuccati. Vuṭṭhāpeyyāti upasampādeyya.

A pregnant woman means one who has conceived a being. Should give the higher ordination means should give the full ordination.

“Vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti gaṇaṃ vā ācariniṃ vā pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne upajjhāyāya āpatti pācittiyassa. Gaṇassa ca ācariniyā ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

With the thought, ‘I will give the higher ordination,’ if she searches for a group, a teacher, a bowl, or a robe, or establishes a boundary, there is an offense of wrong conduct. With the motion, it is an offense of wrong conduct. With the two formal acts, they are offenses of wrong conduct. At the conclusion of the formal act, for the preceptor there is an offense of expiation. For the group and for the teacher, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

1070. Gabbhiniyā gabbhinisaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Gabbhiniyā vematikā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Gabbhiniyā agabbhinisaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, anāpatti. Agabbhiniyā gabbhinisaññā[P 4.0318], āpatti dukkaṭassa. Agabbhiniyā vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Agabbhiniyā agabbhinisaññā, anāpatti.

1070. If she gives the higher ordination to a pregnant woman, perceiving her as pregnant, it is an offense of expiation. If she gives the higher ordination to a pregnant woman while being doubtful, it is an offense of wrong conduct. If she gives the higher ordination to a pregnant woman, perceiving her as not pregnant, there is no offense. In the case of a non-pregnant woman, if she perceives her as pregnant, it is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of a non-pregnant woman, if she is doubtful, it is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of a non-pregnant woman, if she perceives her as not pregnant, there is no offense.

1071. Anāpatti gabbhiniṃ agabbhinisaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, agabbhiniṃ agabbhinisaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1071. There is no offense if she gives the higher ordination to a pregnant woman while perceiving her as not pregnant; if she gives the higher ordination to a non-pregnant woman while perceiving her as not pregnant; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The First Training Rule is finished.

2. Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Second Training Rule

1072. Tena [T 0.0198][M 0.0418][V 0.0434] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo pāyantiṃ vuṭṭhāpenti. Sā piṇḍāya carati. Manussā evamāhaṃsu – “dethāyyāya bhikkhaṃ, sadutiyikā ayyā”ti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo pāyantiṃ vuṭṭhāpessantī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo pāyantiṃ vuṭṭhāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo pāyantiṃ vuṭṭhāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo pāyantiṃ vuṭṭhāpessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1072. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were ordaining a woman with a suckling child. She went about for alms. People said thus, “Give alms to the venerable lady; the venerable lady has a young companion.” People complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed can the bhikkhunīs ordain a woman with a suckling child?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed can the bhikkhunīs ordain a woman with a suckling child?”… “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunīs are ordaining a woman with a suckling child?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, can the bhikkhunīs ordain a woman with a suckling child! This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

1073. “Yā pana bhikkhunī pāyantiṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1073. “Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain a woman with a suckling child, it is an offense of expiation.”

1074. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1074. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… in this sense, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Pāyantī nāma mātā vā hoti hotu (ka.) dhāti dhātī (sī. syā.) vā.

A ‘nursing woman’ means either a mother or a wet nurse.

Vuṭṭhāpeyyāti upasampādeyya.

‘Should ordain’ means: should give the higher ordination.

“Vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti gaṇaṃ vā ācariniṃ vā pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne [T 0.0199] upajjhāyāya āpatti pācittiyassa. Gaṇassa ca ācariniyā ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Thinking, ‘I will ordain,’ if she searches for a group, a teacher, a bowl, or a robe, or establishes a boundary, there is an offense of wrong conduct. With the motion, it is an offense of wrong conduct. With the two formal acts, they are offenses of wrong conduct. At the conclusion of the formal act, for the preceptor there is an offense of expiation. For the group and for the teacher, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

1075. Pāyantiyā pāyantisaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Pāyantiyā vematikā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Pāyantiyā apāyantisaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, anāpatti. Apāyantiyā [V 0.0435] pāyantisaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Apāyantiyā vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Apāyantiyā apāyantisaññā, anāpatti.

1075. In the case of a nursing woman, if she ordains her while perceiving her as a nursing woman, there is an offense of expiation. In the case of a nursing woman, if she ordains her while being doubtful, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of a nursing woman, if she ordains her while perceiving her as not a nursing woman, there is no offense. In the case of a non-nursing woman, if she ordains her while perceiving her as a nursing woman, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of a non-nursing woman, if she ordains her while being doubtful, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of a non-nursing woman, if she ordains her while perceiving her as not a nursing woman, there is no offense.

1076. Anāpatti [M 0.0419] pāyantiṃ apāyantisaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, apāyantiṃ apāyantisaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1076. There is no offense if one ordains a nursing woman while perceiving her as not a nursing woman; if one ordains a non-nursing woman while perceiving her as not a nursing woman; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Second Training Rule is concluded.

3. Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Third Training Rule

1077. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpenti. Tā bālā honti abyattā na jānanti kappiyaṃ vā akappiyaṃ vā. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpentī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi [T 0.0200] nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpessanti! Netaṃ[P 4.0319], bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sikkhamānāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbā. Tāya sikkhamānāya saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā bhikkhunīnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ahaṃ, ayye, itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya sikkhamānā. Saṅghaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṃ yācāmī”ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbā. Tatiyampi yācitabbā. Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

1077. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. At that time, the bhikkhunīs were giving the higher ordination to a probationer who had not trained in the six rules for two years. They were foolish and incompetent, not knowing what was allowable or unallowable. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about: “How indeed can the bhikkhunīs give the higher ordination to a probationer who has not trained in the six rules for two years?”… “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunīs are giving the higher ordination to a probationer who has not trained in the six rules for two years?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, can the bhikkhunīs give the higher ordination to a probationer who has not trained in the six rules for two years? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident…” Having rebuked them… he gave a Dhamma talk and addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow the giving of the training agreement in the six rules for two years to a probationer. And it should be given thus. That probationer should approach the Saṅgha, arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the bhikkhunīs, sit down in the squatting position, raise her joined palms, and she should speak thus: ‘Venerable ladies, I, so-and-so by name, am a probationer of the venerable lady so-and-so by name. I ask the Saṅgha for the training agreement in the six rules for two years.’ She should ask a second time. She should ask a third time. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent, capable bhikkhunī:

1078. “Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya sikkhamānā saṅghaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ saṅgho [V 0.0436] itthannāmāya sikkhamānāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

1078. “Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. This probationer, so-and-so by name, of the venerable lady so-and-so by name, asks the Saṅgha for the training agreement in the six rules for two years. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should give the training agreement in the six rules for two years to the probationer so-and-so by name. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu [M 0.0420] me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya sikkhamānā saṅghaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmāya sikkhamānāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṃ deti. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya sikkhamānāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiyā dānaṃ, sā tuṇhassa; yassā [T 0.0201] nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.

“Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. This probationer, so-and-so by name, of the venerable lady so-and-so by name, asks the Saṅgha for the training agreement in the six rules for two years. The Saṅgha gives the training agreement in the six rules for two years to the probationer so-and-so by name. Whichever venerable lady approves of the giving of the training agreement in the six rules for two years to the probationer so-and-so by name, she should be silent; whichever does not approve, she should speak.”

“Dinnā saṅghena itthannāmāya sikkhamānāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammuti. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The training agreement in the six rules for two years has been given by the Saṅgha to the probationer so-and-so by name. The Saṅgha approves, therefore it is silent. Thus do I record it.”

1079. Sā sikkhamānā “evaṃ vadehī”ti vattabbā – “pāṇātipātā veramaṇiṃ dve vassāni avītikkamma samādānaṃ samādiyāmi. Adinnādānā veramaṇiṃ dve vassāni avītikkamma samādānaṃ samādiyāmi. Abrahmacariyā veramaṇiṃ dve vassāni avītikkamma samādānaṃ samādiyāmi. Musāvādā veramaṇiṃ dve vassāni avītikkamma samādānaṃ samādiyāmi. Surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇiṃ dve vassāni avītikkamma samādānaṃ samādiyāmi. Vikālabhojanā veramaṇiṃ dve vassāni avītikkamma samādānaṃ samādiyāmī”ti.

1079. That probationer should be told, 'Speak thus: “I undertake the training rule to abstain from the destruction of life for two years without transgression. I undertake the training rule to abstain from taking what is not given for two years without transgression. I undertake the training rule to abstain from unchastity for two years without transgression. I undertake the training rule to abstain from false speech for two years without transgression. I undertake the training rule to abstain from distilled and fermented intoxicants which are the basis for heedlessness for two years without transgression. I undertake the training rule to abstain from eating at the wrong time for two years without transgression.”'

Atha kho bhagavā tā bhikkhuniyo anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā dubbharatāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

Then the Blessed One, having rebuked those bhikkhunīs in many ways for being difficult to support… and so on… “And thus, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1080. “Yā pana bhikkhunī dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1080. “Whatever bhikkhunī should give the higher ordination to a probationer who has not trained in the six rules for two years, it is an offense of expiation.”

1081. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1081. Whatever means: whichever, of whatever kind… and so on… bhikkhunī means… and so on… this bhikkhunī is intended in this sense.

Dve [V 0.0437] vassānīti dve saṃvaccharāni. Asikkhitasikkhā [P 4.0320] nāma sikkhā vā na dinnā hoti, dinnā vā sikkhā kupitā. Vuṭṭhāpeyyāti upasampādeyya.

Two years means: two years. Untrained in the training means: either the training has not been given, or the given training has been broken. Should give the higher ordination means: should give the full ordination.

“Vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti gaṇaṃ vā ācariniṃ vā pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi [T 0.0202] dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne upajjhāyāya āpatti pācittiyassa. Gaṇassa ca ācariniyā ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If, thinking, “I will give the higher ordination,” she seeks a group, a teacher, a bowl, or a robe, or she designates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong conduct. With the motion, there is an offense of wrong conduct. With the two formal procedures, there are offenses of wrong conduct. At the conclusion of the formal procedure, for the preceptor, there is an offense of expiation. For the group and for the teacher, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

1082. Dhammakamme [M 0.0421] dhammakammasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme vematikā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

1082. In a valid procedure, perceiving it as a valid procedure, she gives the higher ordination; there is an offense of expiation. In a valid procedure, being in doubt, she gives the higher ordination; there is an offense of expiation. In a valid procedure, perceiving it as not a valid procedure, she gives the higher ordination; there is an offense of expiation.

Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In what is not a valid procedure, perceiving it as a valid procedure, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In what is not a valid procedure, being in doubt, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In what is not a valid procedure, perceiving it as not a valid procedure, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

1083. Anāpatti dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1083. There is no offense if she gives the higher ordination to a probationer who has trained in the six rules for two years; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Third Training Rule is finished.

4. Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Fourth Training Rule

1084. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ sikkhamānaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpenti. Bhikkhuniyo evamāhaṃsu – “etha, sikkhamānā, imaṃ jānātha, imaṃ detha, imaṃ āharatha, iminā attho, imaṃ kappiyaṃ karothā”ti. Tā evamāhaṃsu – “na mayaṃ, ayye, sikkhamānā. Bhikkhuniyo maya”nti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo dve vassāni chasu dhammesu [T 0.0203] sikkhitasikkhaṃ sikkhamānaṃ saṅghena [V 0.0438] asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ sikkhamānaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ sikkhamānaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya sikkhamānāya vuṭṭhānasammutiṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbā. Tāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya sikkhamānāya saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā bhikkhunīnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ [M 0.0422] nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – “ahaṃ[P 4.0321], ayye, itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā sikkhamānā saṅghaṃ vuṭṭhānasammutiṃ yācāmī”ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbā. Tatiyampi yācitabbā. Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

1084. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. At that time, the bhikkhunīs were giving higher ordination to a probationer who had trained in the six rules for two years, who was not approved by the Saṅgha. The bhikkhunīs said, “Come, probationers, know this, give this, bring this, this is needed, make this allowable.” They replied, “Venerables, we are not probationers; we are bhikkhunīs.” Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… and so on… criticized, complained, and spread it about, saying, “How indeed can bhikkhunīs give higher ordination to a probationer who has trained in the six rules for two years, who has not been approved by the Saṅgha?” … and so on… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunīs are giving higher ordination to a probationer who has trained in the six rules for two years, who has not been approved by the Saṅgha?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… and so on… “How indeed, bhikkhus, can bhikkhunīs give higher ordination to a probationer who has trained in the six rules for two years, who has not been approved by the Saṅgha? This, bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident…” and so on… After rebuking them… and so on… he gave a talk on the Dhamma and addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow the giving of the approval for higher ordination to a probationer who has trained in the six rules for two years. And it should be given thus: That probationer, having trained in the six rules for two years, should approach the Saṅgha, arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the bhikkhunīs, sit in the squatting position, raise her joined palms, and should speak thus: ‘Venerables, I, so-and-so, a probationer of the venerable so-and-so, having trained for two years in the six rules, request from the Saṅgha the approval for higher ordination.’ She should request a second time. She should request a third time. A competent, capable bhikkhunī should inform the Saṅgha:

1085. “Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā sikkhamānā saṅghaṃ vuṭṭhānasammutiṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya sikkhamānāya vuṭṭhānasammutiṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

1085. “Venerables, may the Saṅgha hear me. This so-and-so, a probationer of the venerable so-and-so, having trained for two years in the six rules, requests from the Saṅgha the approval for higher ordination. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should give the approval for higher ordination to so-and-so, a probationer who has trained for two years in the six rules. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me[T 0.0204], ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā sikkhamānā saṅghaṃ vuṭṭhānasammutiṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya sikkhamānāya vuṭṭhānasammutiṃ deti. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya sikkhamānāya vuṭṭhānasammutiyā dānaṃ, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.

“Venerables, may the Saṅgha hear me. This so-and-so, a probationer of the venerable so-and-so, having trained for two years in the six rules, requests from the Saṅgha the approval for higher ordination. The Saṅgha gives the approval for higher ordination to so-and-so, a probationer who has trained for two years in the six rules. If the giving of the approval for higher ordination to so-and-so, a probationer who has trained for two years in the six rules, is agreeable to any venerable, she should be silent; if it is not agreeable, she should speak.”

“Dinnā saṅghena itthannāmāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya sikkhamānāya vuṭṭhānasammuti; khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The agreement for ordination has been given by the Saṅgha to the probationer named so-and-so, who has trained for two years in the six rules. This is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it remains silent. Thus do I understand this.”

Atha kho bhagavā tā bhikkhuniyo anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā dubbharatāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

Then the Blessed One, having rebuked those bhikkhunīs in many ways for being difficult to support... and so on... “And thus, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:”

1086. “Yā [V 0.0439] pana bhikkhunī dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ sikkhamānaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1086. “Whatever bhikkhunī should give higher ordination to a probationer who has trained in the six rules for two years and has not been approved by the Saṅgha, it is an offense requiring confession.”

1087. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1087. Whatever means: whatever, of whatever kind…pe… Bhikkhunī means…pe… In this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is meant.

Dve [M 0.0423] vassānīti dve saṃvaccharāni. Sikkhitasikkhā nāma chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā. Asammatā nāma ñattidutiyena kammena vuṭṭhānasammuti na dinnāhoti. Vuṭṭhāpeyyāti upasampādeyya.

Two years means two years. Trained in the training means trained in the six rules. Not approved means that the approval for higher ordination has not been given by a formal act consisting of a motion and one announcement. Should give higher ordination means should give full ordination.

“Vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti gaṇaṃ vā ācariniṃ vā pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne upajjhāyāya [T 0.0205] āpatti pācittiyassa. Gaṇassa ca ācariniyā ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If, with the thought, “I will give higher ordination,” she seeks a group, or a teacher, or a bowl, or a robe, or establishes a boundary, there is an offense of wrongdoing. For the motion, there is an offense of wrongdoing. For the two announcements, there are offenses of wrongdoing. At the conclusion of the announcements, for the preceptor, there is an offense requiring confession. For the group and for the teacher, there is an offense of wrongdoing.

1088. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme vematikā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

1088. In a proper formal act, if she gives higher ordination perceiving it as proper, it is an offense requiring confession. In a proper formal act, if she gives higher ordination while being uncertain, it is an offense requiring confession. In a proper formal act, if she gives higher ordination perceiving it as improper, it is an offense requiring confession.

Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In an improper formal act, if she perceives it as proper, it is an offense of wrongdoing. In an improper formal act, if she is uncertain, it is an offense of wrongdoing. In an improper formal act, if she perceives it as improper, it is an offense of wrongdoing.

1089. Anāpatti dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ sikkhamānaṃ saṅghena sammataṃ vuṭṭhāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1089. There is no offense if she gives higher ordination to a probationer who has trained for two years in the six rules and has been approved by the Saṅgha; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fourth Training Rule is concluded.

5. Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Fifth Training Rule

1090. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme[V 0.0440]. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo ūnadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ vuṭṭhāpenti. Tā akkhamā honti sītassa uṇhassa jighacchāya pipāsāya ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṃ duruttānaṃ durāgatānaṃ vacanapathānaṃ. Uppannānaṃ sārīrikānaṃ vedanānaṃ dukkhānaṃ tibbānaṃ kharānaṃ kaṭukānaṃ asātānaṃ amanāpānaṃ pāṇaharānaṃ anadhivāsakajātikā honti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo ūnadvādasavassaṃ [T 0.0206] gihigataṃ vuṭṭhāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo ūnadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ vuṭṭhāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi [M 0.0424] buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi [P 4.0322] nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo ūnadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ vuṭṭhāpessanti! Ūnadvādasavassā ūnadvādasavassāhi (ka.), bhikkhave, gihigatā akkhamā hoti sītassa uṇhassa jighacchāya pipāsāya ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṃ duruttānaṃ durāgatānaṃ vacanapathānaṃ. Uppannānaṃ sārīrikānaṃ vedanānaṃ dukkhānaṃ tibbānaṃ kharānaṃ kaṭukānaṃ asātānaṃ amanāpānaṃ pāṇaharānaṃ anadhivāsakajātikā hoti. Dvādasavassāva dvādasavassā ca (syā. ka.) kho, bhikkhave, gihigatā khamā hoti sītassa uṇhassa jighacchāya pipāsāya ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṃ duruttānaṃ durāgatānaṃ vacanapathānaṃ. Uppannānaṃ sārīrikānaṃ vedanānaṃ dukkhānaṃ tibbānaṃ kharānaṃ kaṭukānaṃ asātānaṃ amanāpānaṃ pāṇaharānaṃ adhivāsakajātikā hoti. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1090. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were giving higher ordination to a girl under twelve years of age who had cohabited with a man. They were unable to endure cold, heat, hunger, thirst, the touch of gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping things, nor ill-spoken, unwelcome words. They were of a nature unable to endure arisen bodily feelings that are painful, sharp, harsh, pungent, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes…pe… they criticized, scorned, and spread it about, saying: “How can the bhikkhunīs give higher ordination to a girl under twelve years of age who has cohabited with a man?”…pe… “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunīs are giving higher ordination to a girl under twelve years of age who has cohabited with a man?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them…pe… “How can the bhikkhunīs give higher ordination to a girl under twelve years of age who has cohabited with a man? Bhikkhus, a girl under twelve years of age who has cohabited with a man is unable to endure cold, heat, hunger, thirst, the touch of gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping things, nor ill-spoken, unwelcome words. She is of a nature unable to endure arisen bodily feelings that are painful, sharp, harsh, pungent, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening. A girl of twelve years of age who has cohabited with a man, however, is able to endure cold, heat, hunger, thirst, the touch of gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping things, and ill-spoken, unwelcome words. She is of a nature able to endure arisen bodily feelings that are painful, sharp, harsh, pungent, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening. This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the faithless…pe… And thus, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

1091. “Yā pana bhikkhunī ūnadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1091. “Whatever bhikkhunī should give higher ordination to a girl under twelve years of age who has cohabited with a man, it is an offense requiring confession.”

1092. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1092. Whatever means: whatever, of whatever kind…pe… Bhikkhunī means…pe… In this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is meant.

Ūnadvādasavassā nāma appattadvādasavassā. Gihigatā nāma purisantaragatā vuccati. Vuṭṭhāpeyyāti upasampādeyya.

Under twelve years of age means not having reached twelve years of age. Cohabited with a man means one who has associated with a man. Should give higher ordination means should give full ordination.

“Vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti gaṇaṃ vā ācariniṃ vā pattaṃ [T 0.0207] vā cīvaraṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne upajjhāyāya āpatti pācittiyassa. Gaṇassa ca ācariniyā ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If, with the thought, “I will give higher ordination,” she seeks a group, or a teacher, or a bowl, or a robe, or establishes a boundary, there is an offense of wrongdoing. For the motion, there is an offense of wrongdoing. For the two announcements, there are offenses of wrongdoing. At the conclusion of the announcements, for the preceptor, there is an offense requiring confession. For the group and for the teacher, there is an offense of wrongdoing.

1093. Ūnadvādasavassāya [V 0.0441] ūnadvādasavassasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ūnadvādasavassāya vematikā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ūnadvādasavassāya paripuṇṇasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, anāpatti.

1093. If she gives higher ordination to one who is under twelve years of age, perceiving her as under twelve, there is an offense requiring confession. If she gives higher ordination to one who is under twelve years of age, while being uncertain, there is an offense of wrongdoing. If she gives higher ordination to one who is under twelve years of age, perceiving her as of full age, there is no offense.

Paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya [M 0.0425] ūnadvādasavassasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya paripuṇṇasaññā, anāpatti.

If she gives higher ordination to one who is of full twelve years of age, perceiving her as under twelve, there is an offense of wrongdoing. If she gives higher ordination to one who is of full twelve years of age, while being uncertain, there is an offense of wrongdoing. If she gives higher ordination to one who is of full twelve years of age, perceiving her as of full age, there is no offense.

1094. Anāpatti ūnadvādasavassaṃ paripuṇṇasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṃ paripuṇṇasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1094. There is no offense if one gives higher ordination to a person under twelve years of age perceiving her as of full age; if one gives higher ordination to a person of full twelve years of age perceiving her as of full age; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fifth Training Rule is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Sixth Training Rule

1095. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ vuṭṭhāpenti. Tā bālā honti abyattā na jānanti kappiyaṃ vā akappiyaṃ vā. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti [T 0.0208] khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ vuṭṭhāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ vuṭṭhāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ vuṭṭhāpessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā dhammiṃ [P 4.0323] kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya gihigatāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbā. Tāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya gihigatāya saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā bhikkhunīnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ahaṃ, ayye, itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassā gihigatā saṅghaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṃ [V 0.0442] yācāmī”ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbā. Tatiyampi yācitabbā. Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

1095. At one time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. At that time, the bhikkhunīs were giving the higher ordination to a woman who had gone to a man, who had completed twelve years, but who had not trained for two years in the six rules. They were foolish and incompetent, not knowing what was allowable or unallowable. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they criticized, found fault, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs give the higher ordination to a woman who has gone to a man, who has completed twelve years, but who has not trained for two years in the six rules?” … “Is it true, as is said, monks, that bhikkhunīs are giving the higher ordination to a woman who has gone to a man, who has completed twelve years, but who has not trained for two years in the six rules?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, monks, can bhikkhunīs give the higher ordination to a woman who has gone to a man, who has completed twelve years, but who has not trained for two years in the six rules? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the faithless…” Having rebuked them and given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow the giving of the training agreement for two years in the six rules to a woman who has gone to a man and has completed twelve years. And thus, monks, it should be given. That woman who has gone to a man and completed twelve years should approach the Saṅgha, arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, venerate the feet of the bhikkhunīs, sit down squatting, raise her joined palms, and should speak thus: ‘Venerable ladies, I, so-and-so, a woman who has gone to a man and completed twelve years, a dependant of the venerable lady so-and-so, ask the Saṅgha for the training agreement for two years in the six rules.’ She should ask a second time. She should ask a third time. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent, capable bhikkhunī:

1096. “Suṇātu [M 0.0426] me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassā gihigatā saṅghaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ saṅgho itthannāmāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya gihigatāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu [T 0.0209] sikkhāsammutiṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

1096. “Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. This so-and-so, a woman who has gone to a man and completed twelve years, a dependant of the venerable lady so-and-so, asks the Saṅgha for the training agreement for two years in the six rules. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should give the training agreement for two years in the six rules to so-and-so, a woman who has gone to a man and completed twelve years. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassā gihigatā saṅghaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya gihigatāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṃ deti. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya gihigatāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiyā dānaṃ, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.

“Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. This so-and-so, a woman who has gone to a man and completed twelve years, a dependant of the venerable lady so-and-so, asks the Saṅgha for the training agreement for two years in the six rules. The Saṅgha gives the training agreement for two years in the six rules to so-and-so, a woman who has gone to a man and completed twelve years. Let the venerable one who approves of the giving of the training agreement for two years in the six rules to so-and-so, a woman who has gone to a man and completed twelve years, be silent. Let the one who does not approve, speak.”

“Dinnā saṅghena itthannāmāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya gihigatāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammuti. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The training agreement for two years in the six rules has been given by the Saṅgha to so-and-so, a woman who has gone to a man and completed twelve years. The Saṅgha approves; therefore, it is silent. Thus I take note of it.”

Sā paripuṇṇadvādasavassā gihigatā evaṃ vadehīti vattabbā – “pāṇātipātā veramaṇiṃ dve vassāni avītikkamma samādānaṃ samādiyāmi…pe… vikālabhojanā veramaṇiṃ dve vassāni avītikkamma samādānaṃ samādiyāmī”ti.

That woman who has gone to a man and completed twelve years should be told to say this: “For two years, without transgressing, I undertake the observance of abstinence from the destruction of living beings… For two years, without transgressing, I undertake the observance of abstinence from eating at the wrong time.”

Atha kho bhagavā tā bhikkhuniyo anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā dubbharatāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

Then the Blessed One, having rebuked those bhikkhunīs in many ways for being difficult to support… said, “And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1097. “Yā pana bhikkhunī paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1097. “Whatever bhikkhunī should give the higher ordination to a woman who has gone to a man, who has completed twelve years, but who has not trained for two years in the six rules, it is an offense of expiation.”

1098. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1098. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… the bhikkhunī who is intended in this sense is meant.

Paripuṇṇadvādasavassā [V 0.0443] nāma pattadvādasavassā. Gihigatā nāma purisantaragatā vuccati. Dve vassānīti [T 0.0210] dve saṃvaccharāni. Asikkhitasikkhā nāma sikkhā vā na dinnā hoti, dinnā vā sikkhā kupitā. Vuṭṭhāpeyyāti upasampādeyya.

‘One who has completed twelve years’ means: one who has reached twelve years. ‘One who has gone to a man’ is said to be: one who has gone to another man. ‘Two years’ means: two full years. ‘One who has not trained’ means: either the training has not been given, or the training that was given has been invalidated. ‘Should give the higher ordination’ means: should give the full admission.

“Vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti [M 0.0427] gaṇaṃ vā ācariniṃ vā pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne upajjhāyāya āpatti pācittiyassa. Gaṇassa ca ācariniyā ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If, thinking, “I will give the higher ordination,” she seeks a group, a teacher, a bowl, or a robe, or if she designates a boundary, it is an offense of wrong conduct. For the motion, it is an offense of wrong conduct. For the two formal proclamations, they are offenses of wrong conduct. At the conclusion of the formal proclamation, for the preceptor, it is an offense of expiation. For the group and for the teacher, it is an offense of wrong conduct.

1099. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme vematikā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

1099. In a formally correct act, perceiving it as a lawful act, she gives the higher ordination: it is an offense of expiation.
