In a formally correct act, being in doubt, she gives the higher ordination: it is an offense of expiation. In a formally correct act, perceiving it as an unlawful act, she gives the higher ordination: it is an offense of expiation.

Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematikā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In a formally incorrect act, perceiving it as a lawful act, she gives the higher ordination: it is an offense of wrong conduct. In a formally incorrect act, being in doubt, she gives the higher ordination: it is an offense of wrong conduct. In a formally incorrect act, perceiving it as an unlawful act, she gives the higher ordination: it is an offense of wrong conduct.

1100. Anāpatti paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ vuṭṭhāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1100. There is no offense if one gives the higher ordination to a woman who has gone to a man, who has completed twelve years, and who has trained for two years in the six rules; there is no offense for one who is insane, nor for the first offender.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Sixth Training Rule is concluded.

7. Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Seventh Training Rule

1101. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṃ [T 0.0211] gihigataṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpenti. Bhikkhuniyo evamāhaṃsu – “etha sikkhamānā, imaṃ jānātha, imaṃ detha, imaṃ āharatha, iminā attho, imaṃ kappiyaṃ karothā”ti. Tā evamāhaṃsu – “na mayaṃ, ayye, sikkhamānā, bhikkhuniyo maya”nti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ [V 0.0444] vuṭṭhāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ saṅghena asammattaṃ vuṭṭhāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma bhikkhave bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ saṅghena [M 0.0428] asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya gihigatāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya vuṭṭhānasammutiṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbā. Tāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya [P 4.0324] gihigatāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā bhikkhunīnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ahaṃ, ayye, itthannāmā itthannāmāya [T 0.0212] ayyāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassā gihigatā dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā, saṅghaṃ vuṭṭhānasammutiṃ yācāmī”ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbā. Tatiyampi yācitabbā. Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo.

1101. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, nuns were giving the higher ordination to a married woman who had completed twelve years, who had trained for two years in the six rules, but who had not been approved by the Sangha. The nuns said thus: 'Come, trainee, know this, give this, bring this, this is needed, make this allowable.' They replied thus: 'Venerables, we are not trainees, we are nuns.' Those nuns who were of few desires… complained and criticized them, saying: 'How can nuns give the higher ordination to a married woman who has completed twelve years, who has trained for two years in the six rules, but who has not been approved by the Sangha?' … 'Is it true, monks, that nuns are doing this?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… 'How can nuns give the higher ordination to a married woman who has completed twelve years, who has trained for two years in the six rules, but who has not been approved by the Sangha? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced…' After rebuking them… and having given a discourse on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: 'Monks, I allow the giving of approval for the higher ordination to a married woman who has completed twelve years and has trained for two years in the six rules. And it should be given like this. That married woman who has completed twelve years and has trained for two years in the six rules should approach the Sangha of nuns, arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, pay respect at the feet of the nuns, squat on her heels, raise her joined palms, and say, ‘Venerables, I, so-and-so, a married woman who has completed twelve years, who has trained for two years in the six rules under Venerable so-and-so, ask the Sangha for approval for the higher ordination.’ She should ask a second time. She should ask a third time. The Sangha should be informed by a competent and capable nun:

1102. “Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassā gihigatā dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā saṅghaṃ vuṭṭhānasammutiṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya gihigatāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya vuṭṭhānasammutiṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

1102. “Venerables, may the Sangha hear me. This so-and-so, a married woman who has completed twelve years, who has trained for two years in the six rules under the venerable so-and-so, asks the Sangha for approval for the higher ordination. If the time is right for the Sangha, the Sangha should give approval for the higher ordination to so-and-so, a married woman who has completed twelve years and has trained for two years in the six rules. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassā gihigatā dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā saṅghaṃ vuṭṭhānasammutiṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya gihigatāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya vuṭṭhānasammutiṃ deti. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya gihigatāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya vuṭṭhānasammutiyā dānaṃ, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.

“Venerables, may the Sangha hear me. This so-and-so, a married woman who has completed twelve years, who has trained for two years in the six rules under the venerable so-and-so, asks the Sangha for approval for the higher ordination. The Sangha gives approval for the higher ordination to so-and-so, a married woman who has completed twelve years and has trained for two years in the six rules. To whichever venerable the giving of approval for the higher ordination to so-and-so, a married woman who has completed twelve years and has trained for two years in the six rules, is agreeable, she should remain silent. To whom it is not agreeable, she should speak.”

“Dinnā saṅghena itthannāmāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya gihigatāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya vuṭṭhānasammuti. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“Approval for the higher ordination has been given by the Sangha to so-and-so, a married woman who has completed twelve years and has trained for two years in the six rules. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus I take it.”

Atha [V 0.0445] kho bhagavā tā bhikkhuniyo anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā dubbharatāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo [T 0.0213] imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

Then the Blessed One, having rebuked those nuns in many ways for being difficult to support… and so on… said: 'And so, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule:'

1103. “Yā [M 0.0429] pana bhikkhunī paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1103. “Whatever nun should give the higher ordination to a married woman who has completed twelve years, who has trained for two years in the six rules, but who has not been approved by the Sangha, it is a pācittiya offense.”

1104. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1104. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever kind… and so on… ‘Nun’ means… and so on… in this sense, this nun is intended.

Paripuṇṇadvādasavassā nāma pattadvādasavassā. Gihigatā nāma purisantaragatā vuccati. Dve vassānīti dve saṃvaccharāni. Sikkhitasikkhā nāma chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā. Asammatā nāma ñattidutiyena kammena vuṭṭhānasammuti na dinnā hoti. Vuṭṭhāpeyyāti upasampādeyya.

‘Having completed twelve years’ means having reached twelve years. ‘A married woman’ is called one who has gone to another man. ‘Two years’ means two years. ‘Trained in the training’ means trained in the six rules. ‘Not approved’ means approval for the higher ordination has not been given by a formal act with a motion as the second part. ‘Should give the higher ordination’ means should give the higher ordination.

“Vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti gaṇaṃ vā ācariniṃ vā pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne upajjhāyāya āpatti pācittiyassa. Gaṇassa ca ācariniyā ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Thinking, 'I will give the higher ordination,' if she searches for a group, a teacher, a bowl, or a robe, or designates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong conduct. With the motion, there is an offense of wrong conduct. With the two announcements, there are offenses of wrong conduct. At the conclusion of the announcements, for the preceptor there is a pācittiya offense. For the group and for the teacher, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

1105. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme vematikā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

1105. In a lawful act, perceiving it as a lawful act, she gives the higher ordination: there is a pācittiya offense. In a lawful act, being in doubt, she gives the higher ordination: there is a pācittiya offense. In a lawful act, perceiving it as an unlawful act, she gives the higher ordination: there is a pācittiya offense.

Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In an unlawful act, perceiving it as a lawful act: there is an offense of wrong conduct. In an unlawful act, being in doubt: there is an offense of wrong conduct. In an unlawful act, perceiving it as an unlawful act: there is an offense of wrong conduct.

1106. Anāpatti paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ dve vassāni chasu [T 0.0214] dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ saṅghena sammataṃ vuṭṭhāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1106. There is no offense if one ordains a woman who has completed twelve years, has gone to a man, has trained for two years in the six rules, and is approved by the Sangha; there is no offense for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The seventh training rule is completed.

8. Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Eighth Training Rule.

1107. Tena [V 0.0446] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī sahajīviniṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā dve vassāni neva anuggaṇhāti na anuggaṇhāpeti. Tā [M 0.0430] bālā honti abyattā; na jānanti kappiyaṃ vā akappiyaṃ vā. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā sahajīviniṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā dve vassāni neva anuggaṇhissati [P 4.0325] na anuggaṇhāpessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī sahajīviniṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā dve vassāni neva anuggaṇhāti na anuggaṇhāpetīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī sahajīviniṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā dve vassāni neva anuggaṇhissati na anuggaṇhāpessati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1107. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having ordained her co-resident, for two years neither supported her nor had her supported. They were foolish and incompetent; they did not know what was allowable or not allowable. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes... complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How is it that the venerable Thullanandā, having ordained her co-resident, for two years will neither support her nor have her supported?”... “Is it true, Bhikkhus, as is said, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having ordained her co-resident, for two years neither supports her nor has her supported?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her... “How is it, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having ordained her co-resident, for two years will neither support her nor have her supported? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident... And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

1108. “Yā pana bhikkhunī sahajīviniṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā dve vassāni neva anuggaṇheyya na anuggaṇhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1108. “Whatever bhikkhunī, having ordained her co-resident, should for two years neither support her nor cause her to be supported, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

1109. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ [T 0.0215] atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1109. ‘Whatever’ means: of whatever kind... ‘Bhikkhunī’ means: ... in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Sahajīvinī nāma saddhivihārinī vuccati. Vuṭṭhāpetvāti upasampādetvā. Dve vassānīti dve saṃvaccharāni.

‘Co-resident’ means what is called a co-resident disciple. ‘Having ordained’ means having given the higher ordination. ‘Two years’ means two years.

Neva anuggaṇheyyāti na sayaṃ anuggaṇheyya uddesena paripucchāya ovādena anusāsaniyā.

‘Should not support’ means: she herself should not support her by way of recitation, by way of questioning, by way of admonition, or by way of instruction.

Na anuggaṇhāpeyyāti na aññaṃ āṇāpeyya “dve vassāni neva anuggaṇhissāmi na anuggaṇhāpessāmī”ti dhuraṃ nikkhittamatte āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should not cause her to be supported’ means: she should not command another. At the mere moment of laying down the responsibility with the thought, ‘For two years I will neither support her nor cause her to be supported,’ an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

1110. Anāpatti [V 0.0447] sati antarāye, pariyesitvā na labhati, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1110. There is no offense if there is an obstacle; if, having searched, she does not find one; if she is sick; in times of calamity; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The eighth training rule is completed.

9. Navamasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Ninth Training Rule.

1111. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo vuṭṭhāpitaṃ [M 0.0431] pavattiniṃ dve vassāni nānubandhanti. Tā bālā honti abyattā; na jānanti kappiyaṃ vā akappiyaṃ vā. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo vuṭṭhāpitaṃ pavattiniṃ dve vassāni nānubandhissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo vuṭṭhāpitaṃ pavattiniṃ dve vassāni nānubandhantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo vuṭṭhāpitaṃ pavattiniṃ dve vassāni nānubandhissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca [T 0.0216] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1111. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time, bhikkhunīs did not attend for two years on the preceptress who had given them ordination. They were foolish and inexperienced; they did not know what was allowable or unallowable. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes... complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could bhikkhunīs not attend for two years on the preceptress who gave them ordination?”... “Is it true, Bhikkhus, as is said, that bhikkhunīs do not attend for two years on the preceptress who gave them ordination?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... “How indeed, Bhikkhus, could bhikkhunīs not attend for two years on the preceptress who gave them ordination? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident... And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1112. “Yā [P 4.0326] pana bhikkhunī vuṭṭhāpitaṃ pavattiniṃ dve vassāni nānubandheyya, pācittiya”nti.

1112. “Whatever bhikkhunī should not attend for two years on the preceptress who gave the ordination, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

1113. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1113. ‘Whatever’ means: of whatever kind... ‘Bhikkhunī’ means: ... in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Vuṭṭhāpitanti upasampāditaṃ. Pavattinī nāma upajjhāyā vuccati. Dve vassānīti dve saṃvaccharāni. Nānubandheyyāti na sayaṃ upaṭṭhaheyya. Dve vassāni nānubandhissāmīti dhuraṃ nikkhittamatte āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Who has ordained’ means who has given the higher ordination. What is called a `pavattinī` refers to the preceptress. ‘Two years’ means two years. ‘Should not attend on’ means she herself should not attend on. At the mere moment of laying down the responsibility, thinking, ‘I will not attend for two years,’ an offense of pācittiya is incurred.

1114. Anāpatti upajjhāyā bālā vā hoti alajjinī vā, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1114. There is no offense if the preceptress is foolish or shameless; if the bhikkhunī is sick; in times of danger; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Navamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The ninth training rule is completed.

10. Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Tenth Training Rule.

1115. Tena [V 0.0448] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī sahajīviniṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā neva vūpakāseti na vūpakāsāpeti. Sāmiko aggahesi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā sahajīviniṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā neva vūpakāsessati na vūpakāsāpessati, sāmiko aggahesi[M 0.0432]! Sacāyaṃ bhikkhunī pakkantā assa, na ca sāmiko [T 0.0217] gaṇheyyā”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī sahajīviniṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā neva vūpakāseti na vūpakāsāpeti …si (ka.), sāmiko aggahesīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī sahajīviniṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā neva vūpakāsessati na vūpakāsāpessati, sāmiko aggahesi! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1115. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having given ordination to her co-resident, neither led her away herself nor had her led away by another, and her husband seized her. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes... complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the venerable Thullanandā, having given ordination to her co-resident, neither lead her away herself nor have her led away by another, so that her husband seized her? If this bhikkhunī had departed, her husband would not have seized her.”... “Is it true, Bhikkhus, as is said, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having given ordination to her co-resident, neither led her away herself nor had her led away by another, and her husband seized her?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her... “How indeed, Bhikkhus, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having given ordination to her co-resident, neither lead her away herself nor have her led away by another, so that her husband seized her? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident... And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1116. “Yā pana bhikkhunī sahajīviniṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā neva vūpakāseyya na vūpakāsāpeyya antamaso chappañcayojanānipi, pācittiya”nti.

1116. “Whatever bhikkhunī, having given ordination to a co-resident, should neither lead her away herself nor have her led away by another, even for at least six or five leagues, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

1117. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1117. ‘Whatever’ means: of whatever kind... ‘Bhikkhunī’ means: ... in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Sahajīvinī nāma saddhivihārinī vuccati. Vuṭṭhāpetvāti upasampādetvā. Neva [P 4.0327] vūpakāseyyāti na sayaṃ vūpakāseyya. Na vūpakāsāpeyyāti na aññaṃ āṇāpeyya. “Neva vūpakāsessāmi na vūpakāsāpessāmi antamaso chappañcayojanānipī”ti dhuraṃ nikkhittamatte āpatti pācittiyassa.

A co-resident means a fellow-resident pupil. Having given ordination means having conferred full ordination. Should not lead her away herself means she herself should not lead her away. Should not have her led away by another means she should not command another to do so. An offense of expiation is incurred at the mere moment of laying down the responsibility, thinking, ‘I will neither lead her away myself nor have her led away by another, even for at least six or five leagues.’

1118. Anāpatti sati antarāye, pariyesitvā dutiyikaṃ bhikkhuniṃ na labhati, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1118. There is no offense if there is an obstacle; if, after searching, she does not find a companion bhikkhunī; if she is sick; in times of danger; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Tenth Training Rule is concluded.

Gabbhinivaggo sattamo.

The Seventh Chapter on Pregnant Women is concluded.

8. Kumārībhūtavaggo

8. The Chapter on Maidens

1. Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The First Training Rule

1119. Tena [T 0.0218][V 0.0449] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo ūnavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ vuṭṭhāpenti. Tā akkhamā honti sītassa uṇhassa [M 0.0433] jighacchāya pipāsāya ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṃ duruttānaṃ durāgatānaṃ vacanapathānaṃ. Uppannānaṃ sārīrikānaṃ vedanānaṃ dukkhānaṃ tibbānaṃ kharānaṃ kaṭukānaṃ asātānaṃ amanāpānaṃ pāṇaharānaṃ anadhivāsakajātikā honti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo ūnavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ vuṭṭhāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo ūnavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ vuṭṭhāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo ūnavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ vuṭṭhāpessanti! Ūnavīsativassā, bhikkhave, kumāribhūtā akkhamā hoti sītassa uṇhassa…pe… pāṇaharānaṃ anadhivāsakajātikā hoti. Vīsativassāva kho, bhikkhave, kumāribhūtā khamā hoti sītassa uṇhassa…pe… pāṇaharānaṃ adhivāsakajātikā hoti. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1119. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. At that time, bhikkhunīs were giving the higher ordination to maidens under twenty years of age. Those maidens were unable to endure cold and heat; hunger and thirst; the touch of gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping things; badly spoken, ill-come paths of speech; and arisen bodily feelings that were painful, sharp, harsh, acute, disagreeable, unpleasant, and life-threatening. They were of a nature unable to endure them. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they criticized, found fault, and spread it about: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs give the higher ordination to a maiden under twenty years of age?”… “Is it true, monks, that bhikkhunīs are giving the higher ordination to a maiden under twenty years of age?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, monks, can bhikkhunīs give the higher ordination to a maiden under twenty years of age? A maiden under twenty years of age, monks, is unable to endure cold and heat… she is of a nature unable to endure life-threatening feelings. A maiden of twenty years, monks, is indeed able to endure cold and heat… she is of a nature able to endure life-threatening feelings. This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

1120. “Yā pana bhikkhunī ūnavīsativassaṃ [T 0.0219] kumāribhūtaṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1120. “Whatever bhikkhunī should give the higher ordination to a maiden who is under twenty years of age, it is an offense entailing expiation.”

1121. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1121. ‘Whatever’ means: whichever, of whatever sort… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… the bhikkhunī who is intended in this sense is called a ‘bhikkhunī’.

Ūnavīsativassā nāma appattavīsativassā. Kumāribhūtā nāma sāmaṇerī vuccati. Vuṭṭhāpeyyāti upasampādeyya.

‘Under twenty years of age’ means: not having reached twenty years. ‘Maiden’ is said of a female novice. ‘Should give the higher ordination’ means: should give the higher ordination.

“Vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti gaṇaṃ vā ācariniṃ vā pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne [V 0.0450] upajjhāyāya āpatti pācittiyassa. Gaṇassa ca ācariniyā ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Thinking, ‘I will give the higher ordination,’ she searches for a group, a female teacher, a bowl, or a robe, or she authorizes a boundary; this is an offense of wrong conduct. At the end of the motion, there is an offense of wrong conduct. At the end of each of the two formal acts, there is an offense of wrong conduct. At the conclusion of the formal acts, the preceptress incurs an offense of expiation. The group and the female teacher incur an offense of wrong conduct.

1122. Ūnavīsativassāya ūnavīsativassasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ūnavīsativassāya vematikā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ūnavīsativassāya paripuṇṇasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, anāpatti. Paripuṇṇavīsativassāya ūnavīsativassasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Paripuṇṇavīsativassāya [M 0.0434] vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Paripuṇṇavīsativassāya paripuṇṇasaññā, anāpatti.

1122. In the case of one under twenty years of age, if she perceives her as under twenty and gives the higher ordination, it is an offense of expiation. In the case of one under twenty years of age, if she is uncertain and gives the higher ordination, it is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of one under twenty years of age, if she perceives her as having completed the years and gives the higher ordination, there is no offense. In the case of one who has completed twenty years, if she perceives her as under twenty, it is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of one who has completed twenty years, if she is uncertain, it is an offense of wrong conduct. In the case of one who has completed twenty years, if she perceives her as having completed the years, there is no offense.

1123. Anāpatti ūnavīsativassaṃ paripuṇṇasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ paripuṇṇasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1123. There is no offense if she gives the higher ordination to one under twenty years of age while perceiving her as having completed the years; if she gives the higher ordination to one who has completed twenty years while perceiving her as having completed the years; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The First Training Rule is concluded.

2. Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Second Training Rule

1124. Tena [T 0.0220] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ vuṭṭhāpenti. Tā [P 4.0328] bālā honti abyattā; na jānanti kappiyaṃ vā akappiyaṃ vā. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ vuṭṭhāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ vuṭṭhāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ vuṭṭhāpessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhārasavassāya kumāribhūtāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana bhikkhave dātabbā. Tāya aṭṭhārasavassāya kumāribhūtāya saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā bhikkhunīnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ahaṃ, ayye[T 0.0221], itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya [V 0.0451] aṭṭhārasavassā kumāribhūtā saṅghaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṃ yācāmī”ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbā. Tatiyampi yācitabbā. Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

1124. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were giving the higher ordination to a female novice who was a maiden of twenty full years, without her having trained for two years in the six rules. They were foolish and incompetent; they did not know what was allowable and what was not. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they criticized, scorned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could bhikkhunīs give the higher ordination to a female novice who was a maiden of twenty full years, without her having trained for two years in the six rules?” … “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that bhikkhunīs are giving the higher ordination to a female novice who was a maiden of twenty full years, without her having trained for two years in the six rules?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, could bhikkhunīs give the higher ordination to a female novice who was a maiden of twenty full years, without her having trained for two years in the six rules? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the pleasing of the unpleased…” Having rebuked them… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow the giving of the training agreement in the six rules for two years to a female novice who is a maiden of eighteen years. And, Bhikkhus, it should be given in this way. That female novice who is a maiden of eighteen years should approach the Saṅgha, arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, venerate the feet of the bhikkhunīs, sit down squatting, raise her hands in reverence, and should speak thus: ‘Venerables, I, so-and-so, a female novice who is a maiden of eighteen years, of the venerable lady so-and-so, ask the Saṅgha for the training agreement in the six rules for two years.’ She should ask a second time. She should ask a third time. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent, capable bhikkhunī:

1125. “Suṇātu [M 0.0435] me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya aṭṭhārasavassā kumāribhūtā saṅghaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmāya aṭṭhārasavassāya kumāribhūtāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

1125. “Venerables, may the Saṅgha hear me. This so-and-so, a female novice who is a maiden of eighteen years, of the venerable lady so-and-so, asks the Saṅgha for the training agreement in the six rules for two years. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should give to so-and-so, a female novice who is a maiden of eighteen years, the training agreement in the six rules for two years. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya aṭṭhārasavassā kumāribhūtā saṅghaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmāya aṭṭhārasavassāya kumāribhūtāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṃ deti. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya aṭṭhārasavassāya kumāribhūtāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiyā dānaṃ, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.

“Venerables, may the Saṅgha hear me. This so-and-so, a female novice who is a maiden of eighteen years, of the venerable lady so-and-so, asks the Saṅgha for the training agreement in the six rules for two years. The Saṅgha gives to so-and-so, a female novice who is a maiden of eighteen years, the training agreement in the six rules for two years. Whichever venerable lady approves of the giving of the training agreement in the six rules for two years to so-and-so, a female novice who is a maiden of eighteen years, she should be silent. Whichever does not approve, she should speak.

“Dinnā saṅghena itthannāmāya aṭṭhārasavassāya kumāribhūtāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammuti. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The training agreement in the six rules for two years has been given by the Saṅgha to so-and-so, a female novice who is a maiden of eighteen years. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.”

Sā aṭṭhārasavassā kumāribhūtā evaṃ vadehīti vattabbā – “pāṇātipātā veramaṇiṃ dve vassāni avītikkamma samādānaṃ samādiyāmi…pe… [T 0.0222] vikālabhojanā veramaṇiṃ dve vassāni avītikkamma samādānaṃ samādiyāmī”ti.

That female novice who is a maiden of eighteen years should be told to speak thus: ‘For two years, without transgressing, I undertake the undertaking of abstinence from the destruction of life… for two years, without transgressing, I undertake the undertaking of abstinence from eating at the wrong time.’

Atha kho bhagavā tā bhikkhuniyo anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā dubbharatāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

Then the Blessed One, having rebuked those bhikkhunīs in many ways for being difficult to support… and so on… said: “And in this way, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1126. “Yā pana bhikkhunī paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1126. “Whatever bhikkhunī should give the higher ordination to a female novice who is a maiden of twenty full years, without her having trained for two years in the six rules, it is a pācittiya offense.”

1127. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1127. Whatever means: whoever, of whatever sort… A bhikkhunī means… in this sense, this bhikkhunī is intended.

Paripuṇṇavīsativassā [V 0.0452] nāma pattavīsativassā. Kumāribhūtā nāma sāmaṇerī vuccati. Dve vassānīti dve saṃvaccharāni. Asikkhitasikkhā nāma sikkhā vā na dinnā hoti, dinnā vā sikkhā kupitā. Vuṭṭhāpeyyāti upasampādeyya.

Of twenty full years means having reached twenty years. A maiden is said of a female novice. Two years means two years. Untrained in the training means either the training has not been given, or the given training has become invalid. Should give the higher ordination means should confer the higher ordination.

“Vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti [M 0.0436] gaṇaṃ vā ācariniṃ vā pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne upajjhāyāya āpatti pācittiyassa. Gaṇassa ca ācariniyā ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If, with the thought, ‘I will give the higher ordination,’ she seeks a group, or a teacher, or a bowl, or a robe, or establishes a boundary, there is an offense of wrong conduct. For the motion, there is an offense of wrong conduct. For the two formal acts, there are offenses of wrong conduct. At the conclusion of the formal act, for the preceptor there is a pācittiya offense. And for the group and for the teacher, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

1128. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa[T 0.0223]. Dhammakamme vematikā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

1128. In a lawful act, perceiving it as a lawful act, she gives the higher ordination: there is a pācittiya offense. In a lawful act, being uncertain, she gives the higher ordination: there is a pācittiya offense. In a lawful act, perceiving it as an unlawful act, she gives the higher ordination: there is a pācittiya offense.

Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In an unlawful act, perceiving it as a lawful act, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In an unlawful act, being uncertain, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In an unlawful act, perceiving it as an unlawful act, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

1129. Anāpatti paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ vuṭṭhāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1129. There is no offense if she gives the higher ordination to a female novice who is a maiden of twenty full years who has trained for two years in the six rules; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The second training rule is concluded.

3. Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Third Training Rule

1130. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpenti. Bhikkhuniyo evamāhaṃsu – “etha sikkhamānā, imaṃ jānātha, imaṃ detha, imaṃ āharatha, iminā attho, imaṃ kappiyaṃ karothā”ti. Tā evamāhaṃsu – “na mayaṃ, ayye, sikkhamānā; bhikkhuniyo maya”nti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ saṅghena [V 0.0453] asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo [T 0.0224] paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave[M 0.0437], appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paripuṇṇavīsativassāya kumāribhūtāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya vuṭṭhānasammutiṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbā. Tāya paripuṇṇavīsativassāya kumāribhūtāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā bhikkhunīnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ahaṃ, ayye, itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya paripuṇṇavīsativassā kumāribhūtā dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā saṅghaṃ vuṭṭhānasammutiṃ yācāmī”ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbā. Tatiyampi yācitabbā. Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

1130. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time, bhikkhunīs were giving the higher ordination to one who had completed twenty years, who had been a maiden, who had trained for two years in the six rules, but who had not been authorized by the Saṅgha. The bhikkhunīs said thus: 'Come, probationers, know this, give this, bring this, there is a need for this, make this allowable.' They replied thus: 'Venerable ladies, we are not probationers; we are bhikkhunīs.' Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… complained, grumbled, and criticized, 'How indeed can bhikkhunīs give the higher ordination to one who has completed twenty years, who has been a maiden, who had trained for two years in the six rules, but who had not been authorized by the Saṅgha?'… 'Is it true, as is said, monks, that bhikkhunīs are giving the higher ordination to one who has completed twenty years, who has been a maiden, who had trained for two years in the six rules, but who has not been authorized by the Saṅgha?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… 'How indeed, monks, can bhikkhunīs give the higher ordination to one who has completed twenty years, who has been a maiden, who had trained for two years in the six rules, but who has not been authorized by the Saṅgha? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the faithless...' Having rebuked them… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: 'Monks, I allow the giving of the authorization for higher ordination to one who has completed twenty years, who has been a maiden, who has trained for two years in the six rules. And, monks, it should be given in this way. That one who has completed twenty years, who has been a maiden, who has trained for two years in the six rules, should approach the Saṅgha, arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the bhikkhunīs, squat down, raise her joined palms, and should speak thus: "Venerable ladies, I, so-and-so, a pupil of the venerable lady so-and-so, having completed twenty years, having been a maiden, having trained for two years in the six rules, ask the Saṅgha for the authorization for higher ordination." She should ask a second time. She should ask a third time. A competent and capable bhikkhunī should then inform the Saṅgha:'

1131. “Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya paripuṇṇavīsativassā kumāribhūtā dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā saṅghaṃ vuṭṭhānasammutiṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ saṅgho itthannāmāya paripuṇṇavīsativassāya kumāribhūtāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu [T 0.0225] sikkhitasikkhāya vuṭṭhānasammutiṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

1131. “Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. This so-and-so, a pupil of the venerable lady so-and-so, who has completed twenty years, who has been a maiden, and has trained for two years in the six rules, asks the Saṅgha for the authorization for higher ordination. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha grant to so-and-so, who has completed twenty years, who has been a maiden, and has trained for two years in the six rules, the authorization for higher ordination. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya paripuṇṇavīsativassā kumāribhūtā dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā saṅghaṃ vuṭṭhānasammutiṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmāya paripuṇṇavīsativassāya kumāribhūtāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya vuṭṭhānasammutiṃ deti. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya paripuṇṇavīsativassāya kumāribhūtāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya vuṭṭhānasammutiyā dānaṃ, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.

“Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. This so-and-so, a pupil of the venerable lady so-and-so, who has completed twenty years, who has been a maiden, and has trained for two years in the six rules, asks the Saṅgha for the authorization for higher ordination. The Saṅgha grants to so-and-so, who has completed twenty years, who has been a maiden, and has trained for two years in the six rules, the authorization for higher ordination. To whichever venerable lady the granting of the authorization for higher ordination to so-and-so, who has completed twenty years, who has been a maiden, and has trained for two years in the six rules, is agreeable, she should remain silent; to whichever it is not agreeable, she should speak.”

“Dinnā [V 0.0454] saṅghena itthannāmāya paripuṇṇavīsativassāya kumāribhūtāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya vuṭṭhānasammuti. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The authorization for higher ordination has been granted by the Saṅgha to so-and-so, who has completed twenty years, who has been a maiden, and has trained for two years in the six rules. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I record it.”

Atha kho bhagavā tā bhikkhuniyo anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā dubbharatāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

Then the Blessed One, having rebuked those bhikkhunīs in many ways for being difficult to support… and so on… And thus, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

1132. “Yā [M 0.0438] pana bhikkhunī paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1132. “Whatever bhikkhunī should give the higher ordination to one who has completed twenty years, who has been a maiden, who has trained for two years in the six rules, but who has not been authorized by the Saṅgha, it is an offense entailing confession.”

1133. Yā [P 4.0329] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1133. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever, of whatever kind… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… in this sense, ‘bhikkhunī’ is intended.

Paripuṇṇavīsativassā nāma pattavīsativassā. Kumāribhūtā nāma sāmaṇerī vuccati. Dve vassānīti dve saṃvaccharāni. Sikkhitasikkhā nāma chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā[T 0.0226]. Asammatā nāma ñattidutiyena kammena vuṭṭhānasammuti na dinnā hoti. Vuṭṭhāpeyyāti upasampādeyya.

‘Having completed twenty years’ means having reached twenty years. ‘Having been a maiden’ is said of a female novice. ‘Two years’ means two years. ‘Trained in the training’ means trained in the training in the six rules. ‘Not authorized’ means that the authorization for higher ordination has not been given by an act with a motion as its second part. ‘Should give the higher ordination’ means should confer the higher ordination.

“Vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti gaṇaṃ vā ācariniṃ vā pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne upajjhāyāya āpatti pācittiyassa. Gaṇassa ca ācariniyā ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If, with the thought, 'I will give the higher ordination,' she searches for a chapter, a teacher, a bowl, or a robe, or establishes a boundary, there is an offense of wrong conduct. For the motion, there is an offense of wrong conduct. For the two formal proclamations, there are offenses of wrong conduct. At the conclusion of the formal proclamations, for the preceptor there is an offense entailing confession. For the chapter and the teacher, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

1134. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme vematikā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

1134. In a procedurally correct act, perceiving it as a procedurally correct act, she gives the higher ordination: there is an offense entailing confession. In a procedurally correct act, being in doubt, she gives the higher ordination: there is an offense entailing confession. In a procedurally correct act, perceiving it as a procedurally incorrect act, she gives the higher ordination: there is an offense entailing confession.

Adhammakamme dhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In a procedurally incorrect act, with the perception of a procedurally correct act, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In a procedurally incorrect act, with doubt, there is an offense of wrong conduct. In a procedurally incorrect act, with the perception of a procedurally incorrect act, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

1135. Anāpatti [V 0.0455] paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ saṅghena sammataṃ vuṭṭhāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1135. There is no offense if one gives higher ordination to a candidate who has completed twenty years of age, has been a maiden, has trained for two years in the six rules, and has been approved by the Saṅgha; there is no offense for one who is insane, nor for the first offender.

Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The third training rule is completed.

4. Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Fourth Training Rule

1136. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo ūnadvādasavassā vuṭṭhāpenti. Tā bālā honti abyattā na jānanti [T 0.0227] kappiyaṃ [M 0.0439] vā akappiyaṃ vā. Saddhivihāriniyopi bālā honti abyattā; na jānanti kappiyaṃ vā akappiyaṃ vā. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo ūnadvādasavassā vuṭṭhāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo ūnadvādasavassā vuṭṭhāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo ūnadvādasavassā vuṭṭhāpessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1136. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. At that time, bhikkhunīs of less than twelve vassas were giving higher ordination. They were foolish and unskilled; they did not know what was allowable or not allowable. Their co-residents were also foolish and unskilled; they did not know what was allowable or not allowable. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes... they complained, criticized, and disparaged, saying: 'How indeed can bhikkhunīs of less than twelve vassas give higher ordination?'... 'Is it true, monks, that bhikkhunīs of less than twelve vassas are giving higher ordination?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... 'How indeed, monks, can bhikkhunīs of less than twelve vassas give higher ordination? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident...' And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1137. “Yā pana bhikkhunī ūnadvādasavassā vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1137. Whatever bhikkhunī, being of less than twelve vassas, should give higher ordination, it is a pācittiya offense.

1138. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1138. ‘Whatever’ means: whichever, of whatever sort... ‘Bhikkhunī’ means... a bhikkhunī is intended in this sense.

Ūnadvādasavassā nāma appattadvādasavassā.

‘Of less than twelve vassas’ means: one who has not reached twelve vassas.

Vuṭṭhāpeyyāti upasampādeyya.

‘Should give higher ordination’ means: should give higher ordination.

“Vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti gaṇaṃ vā ācariniṃ vā pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne upajjhāyāya āpatti pācittiyassa. Gaṇassa ca ācariniyā ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Thinking, 'I will give higher ordination,' if one searches for a group, a teacher, a bowl, or a robe, or designates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong conduct. For the motion, there is an offense of wrong conduct. For the two formal acts, there are offenses of wrong conduct. At the conclusion of the formal act, for the preceptor, there is a pācittiya offense. For the group and for the teacher, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

1139. Anāpatti [V 0.0456] paripuṇṇadvādasavassā vuṭṭhāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1139. There is no offense if one who has completed twelve vassas gives higher ordination; there is no offense for one who is insane, nor for the first offender.

Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fourth training rule is completed.

5. Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Fifth Training Rule

1140. Tena [T 0.0228][P 4.0330] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇadvādasavassā saṅghena asammatā vuṭṭhāpenti. Tā bālā honti abyattā; na jānanti kappiyaṃ vā akappiyaṃ vā. Saddhivihāriniyopi bālā honti [M 0.0440] abyattā; na jānanti kappiyaṃ vā akappiyaṃ vā. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇadvādasavassā saṅghena asammatā vuṭṭhāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇadvādasavassā saṅghena asammatā vuṭṭhāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇadvādasavassā saṅghena asammatā vuṭṭhāpessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya bhikkhuniyā vuṭṭhāpanasammutiṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbā. Tāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya bhikkhuniyā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ahaṃ, ayye, itthannāmā paripuṇṇadvādasavassā bhikkhunī saṅghaṃ vuṭṭhāpanasammutiṃ [T 0.0229] yācāmī”ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbā. Tatiyampi yācitabbā. Sā bhikkhunī saṅghena paricchinditabbā – “byattāyaṃ bhikkhunī lajjinī”ti. Sace bālā ca hoti alajjinī ca, na dātabbā. Sace bālā hoti lajjinī, na dātabbā. Sace byattā hoti alajjinī, na dātabbā. Sace byattā ca hoti lajjinī ca, dātabbā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbā. Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

1140. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. At that time, bhikkhunīs who had completed twelve vassas were giving higher ordination without being authorized by the Saṅgha. They were foolish and unskilled; they did not know what was allowable or not allowable. Their co-residents were also foolish and unskilled; they did not know what was allowable or not allowable. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes... they complained, criticized, and disparaged, saying: 'How indeed can bhikkhunīs who have completed twelve vassas give higher ordination without being authorized by the Saṅgha?'... 'Is it true, monks, that bhikkhunīs who have completed twelve vassas are giving higher ordination without being authorized by the Saṅgha?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... 'How indeed, monks, can bhikkhunīs who have completed twelve vassas give higher ordination without being authorized by the Saṅgha? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident...' Having rebuked them... and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: 'Monks, I allow the authorization for giving higher ordination to be given to a bhikkhunī who has completed twelve vassas. And it should be given in this way. That bhikkhunī who has completed twelve vassas should approach the Saṅgha, arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior bhikkhunīs, squat down, raise her joined palms, and should speak thus: “Venerable ladies, I, the bhikkhunī so-and-so, who has completed twelve vassas, ask the Saṅgha for the authorization for giving higher ordination.” She should ask a second time. She should ask a third time. That bhikkhunī should be examined by the Saṅgha: “Is this bhikkhunī competent and conscientious?” If she is foolish and shameless, it should not be given. If she is foolish but conscientious, it should not be given. If she is competent but shameless, it should not be given. If she is both competent and conscientious, it should be given. And, monks, it should be given in this way. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhunī:'

1141. “Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā paripuṇṇadvādasavassā bhikkhunī saṅghaṃ vuṭṭhāpanasammutiṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya bhikkhuniyā vuṭṭhāpanasammutiṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

1141. Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhunī, named so-and-so, who has completed twelve vassas, requests from the Saṅgha the authorization for giving higher ordination. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should give to the bhikkhunī named so-and-so, who has completed twelve vassas, the authorization for giving higher ordination. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu [V 0.0457] me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmā paripuṇṇadvādasavassā bhikkhunī saṅghaṃ vuṭṭhāpanasammutiṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya bhikkhuniyā vuṭṭhāpanasammutiṃ deti. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya bhikkhuniyā vuṭṭhāpanasammutiyā dānaṃ, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.

Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha hear me. This bhikkhunī, named so-and-so, who has completed twelve vassas, requests from the Saṅgha the authorization for giving higher ordination. The Saṅgha gives to the bhikkhunī named so-and-so, who has completed twelve vassas, the authorization for giving higher ordination. Whichever venerable lady approves of the giving of the authorization for giving higher ordination to the bhikkhunī named so-and-so, who has completed twelve vassas, she should be silent. Whichever does not approve, she should speak.

“Dinnā saṅghena itthannāmāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya bhikkhuniyā vuṭṭhāpanasammuti. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The authorization for giving higher ordination has been given by the Saṅgha to the bhikkhunī named so-and-so, who has completed twelve vassas. It is approved by the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I take it.

Atha [M 0.0441] kho bhagavā tā bhikkhuniyo anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā dubbharatāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

Then the Blessed One, having rebuked those bhikkhunīs in many ways for being difficult to support... said, 'And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:'

1142. “Yā pana bhikkhunī paripuṇṇadvādasavassā saṅghena asammatā vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti[T 0.0230].

1142. Whatever bhikkhunī, having completed twelve vassas, should give higher ordination without being authorized by the Saṅgha, it is a pācittiya offense.

1143. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1143. Whatever means: whichever... and so on. Bhikkhunī means: ...and so on... in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is meant.

Paripuṇṇadvādasavassā nāma pattadvādasavassā.

‘Having completed twelve years’ means having attained twelve years.

Asammatā nāma ñattidutiyena kammena vuṭṭhāpanasammuti na dinnā hoti. Vuṭṭhāpeyyāti [P 4.0331] upasampādeyya.

‘Not authorized’ means that the authorization to give higher ordination has not been granted by an act consisting of a motion and one announcement. ‘Should give higher ordination’ means should confer higher ordination.

“Vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti gaṇaṃ vā ācariniṃ vā pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne upajjhāyāya āpatti pācittiyassa. Gaṇassa ca ācariniyā ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If, intending, ‘I will give higher ordination,’ she searches for a group, a teacher, a bowl, or a robe, or she designates a boundary, it is an offense of wrong conduct. At the motion, it is an offense of wrong conduct. At the two announcements, they are offenses of wrong conduct. At the conclusion of the formal announcements, for the preceptress, it is an offense of expiation. For the group and for the teacher, it is an offense of wrong conduct.

1144. Dhammakamme dhammakammasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme vematikā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Dhammakamme adhammakammasaññā vuṭṭhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

1144. In a legitimate act, perceiving it as a legitimate act, she gives higher ordination: it is an offense of expiation. In a legitimate act, being in doubt, she gives higher ordination: it is an offense of expiation. In a legitimate act, perceiving it as an illegitimate act, she gives higher ordination: it is an offense of expiation.

Adhammakamme [V 0.0458] dhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In an illegitimate act, perceiving it as a legitimate act: it is an offense of wrong conduct. In an illegitimate act, being in doubt: it is an offense of wrong conduct. In an illegitimate act, perceiving it as an illegitimate act: it is an offense of wrong conduct.

1145. Anāpatti paripuṇṇadvādasavassā saṅghena sammatā vuṭṭhāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1145. There is no offense if a bhikkhunī who has completed twelve years and has been authorized by the Saṅgha gives higher ordination; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fifth training rule is finished.

6. Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Sixth Training Rule

1146. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa [T 0.0231] ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī [M 0.0442] bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā vuṭṭhāpanasammutiṃ yācati. Atha kho bhikkhunisaṅgho caṇḍakāḷiṃ bhikkhuniṃ paricchinditvā – “alaṃ tāva te, ayye, vuṭṭhāpitenā”ti, vuṭṭhāpanasammutiṃ na adāsi. Caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī ‘sādhū’ti paṭissuṇi. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhunisaṅgho aññāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ vuṭṭhāpanasammutiṃ deti. Caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “ahameva nūna bālā, ahameva nūna alajjinī; yaṃ saṅgho aññāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ vuṭṭhāpanasammutiṃ deti, mayhameva na detī”ti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā caṇḍakāḷī – ‘alaṃ tāva te, ayye, vuṭṭhāpitenā’ti vuccamānā ‘sādhū’ti paṭissuṇitvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ āpajjissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, ‘caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī alaṃ tāva te ayye vuṭṭhāpitenā’ti vuccamānā “sādhū”ti paṭissuṇitvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ āpajjatīti āpajjīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī – “alaṃ tāva te, ayye, vuṭṭhāpitenā”ti vuccamānā ‘sādhū’ti paṭissuṇitvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ āpajjissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1146. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. On that occasion, the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī approached the bhikkhunī Saṅgha and requested authorization to give higher ordination. The bhikkhunī Saṅgha, having investigated the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī, said, “Venerable, it is not yet suitable for you to give higher ordination,” and did not grant her the authorization to give higher ordination. The bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī consented, saying, “Very well.” On that occasion, the bhikkhunī Saṅgha granted other bhikkhunīs the authorization to give higher ordination. The bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī complained, criticized, and found fault, saying: “Surely I am foolish, surely I am shameless, that the Saṅgha grants other bhikkhunīs the authorization to give higher ordination, but not me.” Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wants… complained, criticized, and found fault, saying: “How could the venerable Caṇḍakāḷī, on being told, ‘Venerable, it is not yet suitable for you to give higher ordination,’ consent by saying, ‘Very well,’ and later engage in criticism?”… “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī, on being told, ‘Venerable, it is not yet suitable for you to give higher ordination,’ consented by saying, ‘Very well,’ and later engaged in criticism?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How could the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī, Bhikkhus, on being told, ‘Venerable, it is not yet suitable for you to give higher ordination,’ consent by saying, ‘Very well,’ and later engage in criticism? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the faithless… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule in this way:

1147. “Yā pana bhikkhunī – ‘alaṃ tāva te, ayye, vuṭṭhāpitenā’ti vuccamānā ‘sādhū’ti [T 0.0232] paṭissuṇitvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ āpajjeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1147. “Whatever bhikkhunī, on being told, ‘Venerable, it is not yet suitable for you to give higher ordination,’ and having consented, saying, ‘Very well,’ should later engage in criticism, it is an offense of expiation.”

1148. Yā [V 0.0459] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1148. Whatever means: whichever... and so on. Bhikkhunī means: ...and so on... in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is meant.

Alaṃ tāva te ayye vuṭṭhāpitenāti alaṃ tāva te, ayye, upasampāditena. ‘Sādhū’ti paṭissuṇitvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ āpajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘It is not yet suitable for you, venerable, to give higher ordination’ means: it is not yet suitable for you, venerable, to confer higher ordination. Having consented, ‘Very well,’ she later engages in criticism; it is an offense of expiation.

1149. Anāpatti pakatiyā chandā dosā mohā bhayā karontaṃ khiyyati, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1149. There is no offense if she criticizes one who acts according to their nature, or out of desire, aversion, delusion, or fear; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The sixth training rule is finished.

7. Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Seventh Training Rule

1150. Tena [P 4.0332][M 0.0443] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā sikkhamānā thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ upasaṅkamitvā upasampadaṃ yāci. Thullanandā bhikkhunī taṃ sikkhamānaṃ – “sace me tvaṃ, ayye, cīvaraṃ dassasi evāhaṃ taṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti vatvā, neva vuṭṭhāpeti na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karoti. Atha kho sā sikkhamānā bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā sikkhamānaṃ – ‘sace me tvaṃ, ayye, cīvaraṃ dassasi evāhaṃ taṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmī’ti vatvā, neva vuṭṭhāpessati na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī sikkhamānaṃ – “sace me tvaṃ, ayye[T 0.0233], cīvaraṃ dassasi evāhaṃ taṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti vatvā, neva vuṭṭhāpeti na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karotīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī sikkhamānaṃ – “sace me tvaṃ, ayye, cīvaraṃ dassasi evāhaṃ taṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti vatvā, neva vuṭṭhāpessati na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1150. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, a certain probationary nun, having approached the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, requested higher ordination. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having said to that probationary nun, “Venerable, if you give me a robe, then I will have you ordained,” neither had her ordained nor made an effort for her ordination. Then that probationary nun reported this matter to the bhikkhunīs. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wants… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the venerable Thullanandā, having said to a probationary nun, ‘Venerable, if you give me a robe, then I will have you ordained,’ neither have her ordained nor make an effort for her ordination?”… “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having said to a probationary nun, ‘Venerable, if you give me a robe, then I will have you ordained,’ neither has her ordained nor makes an effort for her ordination?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having said to a probationary nun, ‘Venerable, if you give me a robe, then I will have you ordained,’ neither have her ordained nor make an effort for her ordination? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the faithless… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

1151. “Yā pana bhikkhunī sikkhamānaṃ – ‘sace me tvaṃ, ayye, cīvaraṃ dassasi, evāhaṃ [V 0.0460] taṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmī’ti vatvā, sā pacchā anantarāyikinī neva vuṭṭhāpeyya na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ kareyya, pācittiya”nti.

1151. “Whatever bhikkhunī who, having said to a probationary nun, ‘Venerable lady, if you give me a robe, then I will ordain you,’ should afterwards, being without obstruction, neither ordain her nor make an effort for her ordination, it is an offense of expiation.”

1152. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1152. Whatever: of whatever sort… and so on. Bhikkhunī: …and so on. In this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is meant.

Sikkhamānā nāma dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā.

A probationary nun is one who has trained for two years in the six rules.

Sace me tvaṃ ayye cīvaraṃ dassasi evāhaṃ taṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmīti evāhaṃ taṃ upasampādessāmi.

‘Venerable lady, if you give me a robe, then I will ordain you’ means: then I will give you full ordination.

Sā pacchā anantarāyikinīti asati antarāye.

‘She afterwards, being without obstruction’ means: in the absence of an obstruction.

Neva vuṭṭhāpeyyāti na sayaṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya.

‘Should not ordain her’ means: she herself should not ordain her.

Na [M 0.0444] vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ kareyyāti na aññaṃ āṇāpeyya. “Neva vuṭṭhāpessāmi na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karissāmī”ti dhuraṃ nikkhittamatte āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Nor make an effort for her ordination’ means: she should not command another. At the very moment of casting off the responsibility with the thought, ‘I will neither ordain her nor will I make an effort for her ordination,’ an offense of expiation is incurred.

1153. Anāpatti sati antarāye, pariyesitvā na labhati, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1153. There is no offense: if there is an obstruction; if, having searched, she does not find what is needed; if she is sick; in times of danger; if she is insane; for the first offender.

Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Seventh Training Rule is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Eighth Training Rule

1154. Tena [T 0.0234][P 4.0333] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā sikkhamānā thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ upasaṅkamitvā upasampadaṃ yāci. Thullanandā bhikkhunī taṃ sikkhamānaṃ “sace maṃ tvaṃ, ayye, dve vassāni anubandhissasi evāhaṃ taṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti vatvā, neva vuṭṭhāpeti na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karoti. Atha kho sā sikkhamānā bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā sikkhamānaṃ [V 0.0461] – sace maṃ tvaṃ, ayye, dve vassāni anubandhissasi evāhaṃ taṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmīti vatvā, neva vuṭṭhāpessati na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī sikkhamānaṃ – “sace maṃ tvaṃ ayye dve vassāni anubandhissasi evāhaṃ taṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti vatvā, neva vuṭṭhāpeti na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karotīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī sikkhamānaṃ – “sace maṃ tvaṃ, ayye, dve vassāni anubandhissasi evāhaṃ taṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti vatvā, neva vuṭṭhāpessati na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ [T 0.0235] sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1154. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, a certain probationary nun approached the bhikkhunī Thullanandā and requested full ordination. The bhikkhunī Thullanandā said to that probationary nun, “Venerable lady, if you attend upon me for two years, then I will ordain you.” Having said this, she neither ordained her nor made an effort for her ordination. Then that probationary nun informed the bhikkhunīs about this matter. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How could the venerable Thullanandā, having said to a probationary nun, ‘Venerable lady, if you attend upon me for two years, then I will ordain you,’ neither ordain her nor make an effort for her ordination?” … “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having said to a probationary nun, ‘Venerable lady, if you attend upon me for two years, then I will ordain you,’ neither ordains her nor makes an effort for her ordination?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having said to a probationary nun, ‘Venerable lady, if you attend upon me for two years, then I will ordain you,’ neither ordain her nor make an effort for her ordination? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the faithless… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

1155. “Yā pana bhikkhunī sikkhamānaṃ – ‘sace maṃ tvaṃ ayye dve vassāni anubandhissasi evāhaṃ taṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmī’ti vatvā, sā pacchā anantarāyikinī [M 0.0445] neva vuṭṭhāpeyya na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ kareyya, pācittiya”nti.

1155. “Whatever bhikkhunī who, having said to a probationary nun, ‘Venerable lady, if you attend upon me for two years, then I will ordain you,’ should afterwards, being without obstruction, neither ordain her nor make an effort for her ordination, it is an offense of expiation.”

1156. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1156. Whatever: of whatever sort… and so on. Bhikkhunī: …and so on. In this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is meant.

Sikkhamānā nāma dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā.

A probationary nun is one who has trained for two years in the six rules.

Sace maṃ tvaṃ ayye dve vassāni anubandhissasīti dve saṃvaccharāni upaṭṭhahissasi.

‘Venerable lady, if you attend upon me for two years’ means: if you serve me for two years.

Evāhaṃ taṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmīti evāhaṃ taṃ upasampādessāmi.

‘Then I will ordain you’ means: ‘Then I will give you full ordination.’

Sā pacchā anantarāyikinīti asati antarāye.

‘She afterwards, being without obstruction’ means: in the absence of an obstruction.

Neva vuṭṭhāpeyyāti na sayaṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya.

‘Should not ordain her’ means: she herself should not ordain her.

Na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ kareyyāti na aññaṃ āṇāpeyya. “Neva vuṭṭhāpessāmi na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karissāmī”ti dhuraṃ nikkhittamatte āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Nor make an effort for her ordination’ means: she should not command another. At the very moment of casting off the responsibility with the thought, ‘I will neither ordain her nor will I make an effort for her ordination,’ an offense of expiation is incurred.

1157. Anāpatti [V 0.0462] sati antarāye, pariyesitvā na labhati, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1157. There is no offense: if there is an obstruction; if, having searched, she does not find what is needed; if she is sick; in times of danger; if she is insane; for the first offender.

Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Eighth Training Rule is concluded.

9. Navamasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Ninth Training Rule

1158. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī purisasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ kumārakasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ caṇḍiṃ sokāvāsaṃ sokavassaṃ (sī.) sokāvassaṃ (syā.) caṇḍakāḷiṃ sikkhamānaṃ [T 0.0236] vuṭṭhāpeti. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā purisasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ kumārakasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ caṇḍiṃ sokāvāsaṃ sokavassaṃ (sī.) sokāvassaṃ (syā.) caṇḍakāḷiṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī purisasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ kumārakasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ caṇḍiṃ sokāvāsaṃ sokavassaṃ (sī.) sokāvassaṃ (syā.) caṇḍakāḷiṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpetīti vuṭṭhāpesīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho [M 0.0446] bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī purisasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ kumārakasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ [P 4.0334] caṇḍiṃ sokāvāsaṃ caṇḍakāḷiṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpessati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1158. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā ordained a probationary nun named Caṇḍakāḷī, who was associated with men, associated with boys, was harsh, and caused sorrow. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How could the venerable Thullanandā ordain a probationary nun like Caṇḍakāḷī, who is associated with men, associated with boys, is harsh, and causes sorrow?”… “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā ordained a probationary nun named Caṇḍakāḷī, who was associated with men, associated with boys, is harsh, and causes sorrow?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā ordain a probationary nun like Caṇḍakāḷī, who is associated with men, associated with boys, is harsh, and causes sorrow? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the faithless… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

1159. “Yā pana bhikkhunī purisasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ kumārakasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ caṇḍiṃ sokāvāsaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1159. “Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain a probationary nun who is associated with men, associated with boys, is harsh, and causes sorrow, it is an offense of expiation.”

1160. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1160. Whatever: of whatever sort… and so on. Bhikkhunī: …and so on. In this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is meant.

Puriso nāma pattavīsativasso. Kumārako nāma appattavīsativasso. Saṃsaṭṭhā nāma ananulomikena kāyikavācasikena saṃsaṭṭhā. Caṇḍī nāma kodhanā vuccati.

A man is one who has reached twenty years of age. A boy is one who has not reached twenty years of age. Associated means associated by means of unsuitable bodily and verbal interaction. A harsh woman is said to be one who is prone to anger.

Sokāvāsā nāma paresaṃ dukkhaṃ uppādeti, sokaṃ āvisati. Sikkhamānā nāma dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā. Vuṭṭhāpeyyāti upasampādeyya.

One who dwells in sorrow is one who causes suffering for others and enters into sorrow. A probationer is a woman who has trained for two years in the six rules. To give ordination means to give the higher ordination.

“Vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti [V 0.0463] gaṇaṃ vā ācariniṃ vā pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ [T 0.0237] vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne upajjhāyāya āpatti pācittiyassa; gaṇassa ca ācariniyā ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

With the thought, ‘I will give ordination,’ if she seeks a quorum, an instructor, a bowl, or a robe, or if she establishes a boundary, she commits an offense of wrong-doing. For the motion, it is an offense of wrong-doing. For the two announcements, they are offenses of wrong-doing. At the conclusion of the formal act, the preceptor commits an offense of expiation; for the quorum and the instructor, they commit an offense of wrong-doing.

1161. Anāpatti ajānantī vuṭṭhāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1161. There is no offense if she gives ordination not knowing; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Navamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Ninth Training Rule is concluded.

10. Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Tenth Training Rule

1162. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī mātāpitūhipi sāmikenapi ananuññātaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpeti. Mātāpitaropi sāmikopi ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma [M 0.0447] ayyā thullanandā amhehi ananuññātaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpessatī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo mātāpitūnampi sāmikassapi ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā mātāpitūhipi sāmikenapi ananuññātaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī, mātāpitūhipi [T 0.0238] sāmikenapi ananuññātaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpetīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti.
