Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī mātāpitūhipi sāmikenapi ananuññātaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpessati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1162. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time the bhikkhunī Thullanandā gave higher ordination to a probationer who was not permitted by her parents and her husband. Her parents and husband complained, grumbled, and criticized, saying, “How indeed can the venerable Thullanandā give higher ordination to a probationer not permitted by us?” The bhikkhunīs heard the complaints, grumbling, and criticism of the parents and the husband. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… they complained, grumbled, and criticized, saying, “How indeed can the venerable Thullanandā give higher ordination to a probationer who is not permitted by her parents and her husband?”… “Is it true, monks, as is said, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā gave higher ordination to a probationer who is not permitted by her parents and her husband?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, monks, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā give higher ordination to a probationer who is not permitted by her parents and her husband? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And thus, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1163. “Yā [P 4.0335] pana bhikkhunī mātāpitūhi vā sāmikena vā ananuññātaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1163. “Whatever bhikkhunī should give higher ordination to a probationer not permitted by her parents or by her husband, it is an offense of expiation.”

1164. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1164. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever kind of… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Mātāpitaro [V 0.0464] nāma janakā vuccanti. Sāmiko nāma yena pariggahitā hoti. Ananuññātāti anāpucchā. Sikkhamānā nāma dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā. Vuṭṭhāpeyyāti upasampādeyya.

‘Parents’ means those who are called begetters. ‘Husband’ means the one by whom she has been taken. ‘Not permitted’ means without having been asked. ‘Probationer’ means a woman who has trained in the six rules for two years. ‘Should give higher ordination’ means should confer the higher ordination.

Vuṭṭhāpessāmīti gaṇaṃ vā ācariniṃ vā pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne upajjhāyāya āpatti pācittiyassa. Gaṇassa ca ācariniyā ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

With the thought, ‘I will give higher ordination,’ if she seeks a quorum, an instructor, a bowl, or a robe, or if she establishes a boundary, she commits an offense of wrong-doing. For the motion, it is an offense of wrong-doing. For the two announcements, they are offenses of wrong-doing. At the conclusion of the formal act, the preceptor commits an offense of expiation. For the quorum and the instructor, they commit an offense of wrong-doing.

1165. Anāpatti ajānantī vuṭṭhāpeti, apaloketvā vuṭṭhāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1165. There is no offense if she gives higher ordination without knowing that permission was not given; if she gives higher ordination after having obtained consent; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Tenth Training Rule is concluded.

11. Ekādasamasikkhāpadaṃ

11. The Eleventh Training Rule

1166. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī – “sikkhamānaṃ [T 0.0239] vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti [M 0.0448] there bhikkhū sannipātetvā pahūtaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ passitvā – “na tāvāhaṃ, ayyā, sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti there bhikkhū uyyojetvā devadattaṃ kokālikaṃ kaṭamodakatissakaṃ khaṇḍadeviyā puttaṃ samuddadattaṃ sannipātetvā sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpesi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā pārivāsikachandadānena sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpessatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī pārivāsikachandadānena sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpetīti vuṭṭhāpesīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī pārivāsikachandadānena sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpessati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1166. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrel Sanctuary. Now at that time the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, intending to give higher ordination to a probationer, assembled the senior bhikkhus and, after seeing abundant fresh and cooked food, dismissed them, saying, “Venerables, I will not give higher ordination to the probationer just yet.” She then assembled Devadatta, Kokālika, Kaṭamodakatissaka, the son of Khaṇḍadevī, and Samuddadatta, and gave higher ordination to the probationer. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… they complained, grumbled, and criticized, saying, “How can the venerable Thullanandā give higher ordination to a probationer by means of stale consent?”… “Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā gave higher ordination to a probationer by means of stale consent?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How, monks, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā give higher ordination to a probationer by means of stale consent? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… And thus, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1167. “Yā pana bhikkhunī pārivāsikachandadānena sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1167. “Whatever bhikkhunī should give higher ordination to a probationer by means of stale consent, it is an offense of expiation.”

1168. Yā [V 0.0465] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1168. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever kind of… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Pārivāsikachandadānenāti [P 4.0336] vuṭṭhitāya parisāya. Sikkhamānā nāma dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā. Vuṭṭhāpeyyāti upasampādeyya.

‘By means of stale consent’ means: after the assembly has dispersed. ‘Probationer’ means: a woman who has trained in the six rules for two years. ‘Should give higher ordination’ means: should confer the higher ordination.

“Vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti gaṇaṃ vā ācariniṃ vā pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne upajjhāyāya āpatti pācittiyassa[T 0.0240]. Gaṇassa ca ācariniyā ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

With the thought, ‘I will give higher ordination,’ if she seeks a quorum, an instructor, a bowl, or a robe, or if she establishes a boundary, she commits an offense of wrong-doing. For the motion, it is an offense of wrong-doing. For the two announcements, they are offenses of wrong-doing. At the conclusion of the formal act, the preceptor commits an offense of expiation. For the quorum and the instructor, they commit an offense of wrong-doing.

1169. Anāpatti avuṭṭhitāya parisāya vuṭṭhāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1169. There is no offense if she gives higher ordination before the assembly has dispersed; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Ekādasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Eleventh Training Rule is concluded.

12. Dvādasamasikkhāpadaṃ

12. The Twelfth Training Rule

1170. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo anuvassaṃ [M 0.0449] vuṭṭhāpenti, upassayo na sammati. Manussā manussā vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā (sī.) ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo anuvassaṃ vuṭṭhāpessanti, upassayo na sammatī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo anuvassaṃ vuṭṭhāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo anuvassaṃ vuṭṭhāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo anuvassaṃ vuṭṭhāpessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1170. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were giving ordination annually, and the dwelling was not sufficient. People complained, criticized, and spread disparaging remarks: “How indeed can the bhikkhunīs give ordination annually when the dwelling is not sufficient?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading disparaging remarks. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread disparaging remarks: “How indeed can the bhikkhunīs give ordination annually?”… “Is it true, Bhikkhus, as has been heard, that the bhikkhunīs are giving ordination annually?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, can the bhikkhunīs give ordination annually? This, Bhikkhus, does not lead to the confidence of the unconfident… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1171. “Yā pana bhikkhunī anuvassaṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1171. “Whatever bhikkhunī should give ordination annually, it is a pācittiya offense.”

1172. Yā [V 0.0466] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1172. ‘Whatever bhikkhunī’ means: whichever, of whatever kind… ‘A bhikkhunī’: … in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Anuvassanti anusaṃvaccharaṃ. Vuṭṭhāpeyyāti [T 0.0241] upasampādeyya.

‘Annually’ means every year. ‘Should give ordination’ means should give higher ordination.

“Vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti gaṇaṃ vā ācariniṃ vā pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne upajjhāyāya āpatti pācittiyassa. Gaṇassa ca ācariniyā ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If, with the thought, “I will give ordination,” she seeks a group, a teacher, a bowl, or a robe, or she designates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong conduct. For the motion, it is an offense of wrong conduct. For the two formal acts, they are offenses of wrong conduct. At the conclusion of the formal act, for the preceptor, there is a pācittiya offense. For the group and for the teacher, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

1173. Anāpatti ekantarikaṃ vuṭṭhāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1173. There is no offense if she gives ordination in an alternate year, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Dvādasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Twelfth Training Rule is concluded.

13. Terasamasikkhāpadaṃ

13. The Thirteenth Training Rule

1174. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo ekaṃ vassaṃ dve vuṭṭhāpenti. Upassayo tatheva na sammati. Manussā manussā vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā (sī.) tatheva ujjhāyanti [M 0.0450] khiyyanti vipācenti [P 4.0337] – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo ekaṃ vassaṃ dve vuṭṭhāpessanti! Upassayo tatheva na sammatī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo ekaṃ vassaṃ dve vuṭṭhāpessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo ekaṃ vassaṃ dve vuṭṭhāpentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi [T 0.0242] nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo ekaṃ vassaṃ dve vuṭṭhāpessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1174. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were giving ordination to two in one year. The dwelling was likewise not sufficient. People complained, criticized, and spread disparaging remarks: “How indeed can the bhikkhunīs give ordination to two in one year? The dwelling was likewise not sufficient!” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading disparaging remarks. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread disparaging remarks: “How indeed can the bhikkhunīs give ordination to two in one year?”… “Is it true, Bhikkhus, as has been heard, that the bhikkhunīs are giving ordination to two in one year?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, can the bhikkhunīs give ordination to two in one year? This, Bhikkhus, does not lead to the confidence of the unconfident… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1175. “Yā pana bhikkhunī ekaṃ vassaṃ dve vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1175. “Whatever bhikkhunī should give ordination to two in one year, it is a pācittiya offense.”

1176. Yā [V 0.0467] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1176. ‘Whatever bhikkhunī’ means: whichever, of whatever kind… ‘A bhikkhunī’: … in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Ekaṃ vassanti ekaṃ saṃvaccharaṃ. Dve vuṭṭhāpeyyāti dve upasampādeyya.

‘In one year’ means in a single year. ‘Should give ordination to two’ means should give higher ordination to two.

“Dve vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti gaṇaṃ vā ācariniṃ vā pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā pariyesati, sīmaṃ vā sammannati, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ. Dvīhi kammavācāhi dukkaṭā. Kammavācāpariyosāne upajjhāyāya āpatti pācittiyassa. Gaṇassa ca ācariniyā ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

If, with the thought, “I will give ordination to two,” she seeks a group, a teacher, a bowl, or a robe, or she designates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong conduct. For the motion, it is an offense of wrong conduct. For the two formal acts, they are offenses of wrong conduct. At the conclusion of the formal act, for the preceptor, there is a pācittiya offense. For the group and for the teacher, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

1177. Anāpatti ekantarikaṃ ekaṃ vuṭṭhāpeti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1177. There is no offense if she gives ordination to one in an alternate year, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Terasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Thirteenth Training Rule is concluded.

Kumārībhūtavaggo aṭṭhamo.

The Eighth Chapter, the Kumārībhūta, is concluded.

9. Chattupāhanavaggo

9. The Chapter on the Umbrella and Footwear

1. Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The First Training Rule

1178. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo chattupāhanaṃ dhārenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi [T 0.0243][M 0.0451] nāma bhikkhuniyo chattupāhanaṃ dhāressanti, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo chattupāhanaṃ dhāressantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo chattupāhanaṃ dhārentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā [V 0.0468] bhikkhuniyo chattupāhanaṃ dhāressanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1178. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs were using an umbrella and footwear. People complained, criticized, and spread disparaging remarks: 'How can bhikkhunīs use an umbrella and footwear, just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures?' The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading disparaging remarks. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread disparaging remarks: 'How can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs use an umbrella and footwear?'… 'Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs are using an umbrella and footwear?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… 'How can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs use an umbrella and footwear! This is not, Bhikkhus, for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

“Yā pana bhikkhunī chattupāhanaṃ dhāreyya, pācittiya”nti.

“Should any bhikkhunī use an umbrella and footwear, it is an offense of expiation.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

Thus this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhunīs.

1179. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī gilānā hoti. Tassā [P 4.0338] vinā chattupāhanaṃ na phāsu hoti…pe… bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānāya bhikkhuniyā chattupāhanaṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1179. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī was ill. Without an umbrella and footwear, she was not comfortable… They reported this matter to the Blessed One… 'I allow, Bhikkhus, an umbrella and footwear for a sick bhikkhunī. And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:'

1180. “Yā pana bhikkhunī agilānā chattupāhanaṃ dhāreyya, pācittiya”nti.

1180. “Whatever bhikkhunī, not being ill, should use an umbrella and footwear, it is an offense of expiation.”

1181. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1181. ‘Whatever’ means: of whatever kind… and so on… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… and so on… in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Agilānā nāma yassā vinā chattupāhanaṃ phāsu hoti.

‘Not ill’ means one who is comfortable without an umbrella and footwear.

Gilānā nāma yassā vinā chattupāhanaṃ [T 0.0244] na phāsu hoti.

‘Ill’ means one who is not comfortable without an umbrella and footwear.

Chattaṃ nāma tīṇi chattāni – setacchattaṃ, kilañjacchattaṃ, paṇṇacchattaṃ maṇḍalabaddhaṃ salākabaddhaṃ. Dhāreyyāti sakimpi dhāreti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Umbrella’ means: there are three kinds of umbrellas—a white umbrella, a mat umbrella, and a leaf umbrella—that are bound in a circle and bound with ribs. ‘Should use’ means: if one uses it even once, one commits an offense of expiation.

1182. Agilānā agilānasaññā chattupāhanaṃ dhāreti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Agilānā vematikā chattupāhanaṃ dhāreti, āpatti pācittiyassa. Agilānā gilānasaññā chattupāhanaṃ dhāreti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

1182. If she is not ill and perceives herself as not ill while using an umbrella and footwear, she commits an offense of expiation. If she is not ill but is in doubt while using an umbrella and footwear, she commits an offense of expiation. If she is not ill but perceives herself as ill while using an umbrella and footwear, she commits an offense of expiation.

Chattaṃ [M 0.0452] dhāreti na upāhanaṃ, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Upāhanaṃ dhāreti na chattaṃ, āpatti dukkaṭassa[V 0.0469]. Gilānā agilānasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Gilānā vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Gilānā gilānasaññā, anāpatti.

She uses an umbrella but not footwear: it is an offense of wrong conduct. She uses footwear but not an umbrella: it is an offense of wrong conduct. She is ill but perceives herself as not ill: it is an offense of wrong conduct. She is ill but is in doubt: it is an offense of wrong conduct. She is ill and perceives herself as ill: there is no offense.

1183. Anāpatti gilānāya, ārāme ārāmūpacāre dhāreti, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1183. There is no offense for a bhikkhunī who is ill; for one who uses them in a monastery or its precincts; in times of danger; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Paṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The First Training Rule is finished.

2. Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Second Training Rule

1184. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo yānena yāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo yānena yāyissanti, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe. [T 0.0245]… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo yānena yāyissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo yānena yāyantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo yānena yāyissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1184. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs were traveling by vehicle. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can bhikkhunīs travel by vehicle, just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… and so on… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs travel by vehicle?”… and so on… “Is it true, monks, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs travel by vehicle?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… and so on… “How can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs travel by vehicle! This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… and so on… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:”

“Yā [P 4.0339] pana bhikkhunī yānena yāyeyya, pācittiya”nti.

“Whatever bhikkhunī should travel by vehicle, it is an offense of expiation.”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

Thus this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhunīs.

1185. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī gilānā hoti, na sakkoti padasā gantuṃ…pe… bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānāya bhikkhuniyā yānaṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1185. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī was ill; she was not able to go on foot… and so on… They reported this matter to the Blessed One… and so on… “I allow, monks, a vehicle for an ill bhikkhunī. And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:”

1186. “Yā [M 0.0453] pana bhikkhunī agilānā yānena yāyeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1186. “Whatever bhikkhunī, not being ill, should travel by vehicle, it is an offense of expiation.”

1187. Yā [V 0.0470] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1187. ‘Whatever’ means: of whatever kind… and so on… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… and so on… in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Agilānā nāma sakkoti padasā gantuṃ.

‘Not ill’ means: one is able to go on foot.

Gilānā nāma na sakkoti padasā gantuṃ.

‘Ill’ means: one is not able to go on foot.

Yānaṃ nāma vayhaṃ ratho sakaṭaṃ sandamānikā sivikā pāṭaṅkī.

‘Vehicle’ means: a litter, a chariot, a cart, a sedan chair, a palanquin, or a cloth litter.

Yāyeyyāti sakimpi yānena yāyati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should travel’ means: if one travels by vehicle even once, one commits an offense of expiation.

1188. Agilānā agilānasaññā yānena yāyati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Agilānā vematikā yānena yāyati, āpatti pācittiyassa[T 0.0246]. Agilānā gilānasaññā yānena yāyati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

1188. If she is not ill and perceives herself as not ill while traveling by vehicle, she commits an offense of expiation. If she is not ill but is in doubt while traveling by vehicle, she commits an offense of expiation. If she is not ill but perceives herself as ill while traveling by vehicle, she commits an offense of expiation.

Gilānā agilānasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Gilānā vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Gilānā gilānasaññā, anāpatti.

If she is ill but perceives herself as not ill, she commits an offense of wrong conduct. If she is ill but is in doubt, she commits an offense of wrong conduct. If she is ill and perceives herself as ill, there is no offense.

1189. Anāpatti gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1189. There is no offense for one who is ill; in times of danger; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Second Training Rule is finished.

3. Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Third Training Rule

1190. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī aññatarissā itthiyā kulūpikā hoti. Atha kho sā itthī taṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “handāyye, imaṃ saṅghāṇiṃ amukāya nāma itthiyā dehī”ti. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī – “sacāhaṃ pattena ādāya gacchāmi vissaro me bhavissatī”ti paṭimuñcitvā agamāsi. Tassā rathikāya suttake chinne vippakiriyiṃsu. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi [M 0.0454] nāma bhikkhuniyo saṅghāṇiṃ [V 0.0471] dhāressanti, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe. [P 4.0340]… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī saṅghāṇiṃ dhāressatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī [T 0.0247] saṅghāṇiṃ dhāretī”ti dhāresīti (ka.)? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī saṅghāṇiṃ dhāressati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1190. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī was a frequent visitor to the house of a certain woman. Then that woman said to that bhikkhunī, “Come, venerable lady, give this girdle to the woman named so-and-so.” Then that bhikkhunī, thinking, “If I go carrying it in my bowl, it will make a discordant sound,” put it on and went. On the carriage road, its thread broke and its parts scattered. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can bhikkhunīs wear a girdle, just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures!” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… and so on… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can a bhikkhunī wear a girdle?”… and so on… “Is it true, monks, that a bhikkhunī wore a girdle?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… and so on… “How can a bhikkhunī wear a girdle! This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced… and so on… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:”

1191. “Yā pana bhikkhunī saṅghāṇiṃ dhāreyya, pācittiya”nti.

1191. “Whatever bhikkhunī should wear a girdle, it is an offense of expiation.”

1192. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1192. ‘Whatever’ means: of whatever kind… and so on… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means… and so on… in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Saṅghāṇi nāma yā kāci kaṭūpagā.

‘Girdle’ means any kind of waist-ornament.

Dhāreyyāti sakimpi dhāreti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should wear’ means: if she wears it even once, she commits an offense of expiation.

1193. Anāpatti ābādhappaccayā, kaṭisuttakaṃ dhāreti, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1193. There is no offense: on account of illness; if she wears a waist-string; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Third Training Rule is concluded.

4. Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Fourth Training Rule

1194. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo itthālaṅkāraṃ dhārenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo itthālaṅkāraṃ dhāressanti, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo itthālaṅkāraṃ dhāressantī”ti [V 0.0472] …pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo itthālaṅkāraṃ dhārentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi [T 0.0248] nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo itthālaṅkāraṃ [M 0.0455] dhāressanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1194. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs of the group of six were wearing women’s ornaments. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, “How indeed can bhikkhunīs wear women’s ornaments, just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures!” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, “How indeed can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six wear women’s ornaments?” … “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunīs of the group of six wear women’s ornaments?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, Bhikkhus, can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six wear women’s ornaments? This, Bhikkhus, is not for the faith of the faithless… And thus, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1195. “Yā pana bhikkhunī itthālaṅkāraṃ dhāreyya, pācittiya”nti.

1195. “Whatever bhikkhunī should wear a woman’s ornament, it is an offense entailing expiation.”

1196. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1196. Whatever means: whatever sort… A bhikkhunī means:… in this context, this is the intended bhikkhunī.

Itthālaṅkāro nāma sīsūpago gīvūpago hatthūpago pādūpago kaṭūpago. Dhāreyyāti sakimpi dhāreti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A woman’s ornament means a head-adornment, a neck-adornment, a hand-adornment, a foot-adornment, or a waist-adornment. ‘Should wear’ means: if she wears it even once, she commits an offense entailing expiation.

1197. Anāpatti ābādhapaccayā, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1197. There is no offense on account of illness; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fourth Training Rule is concluded.

5. Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Fifth Training Rule

1198. Tena [P 4.0341] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo gandhavaṇṇakena nahāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo gandhavaṇṇakena nahāyissanti, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ [T 0.0249] ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo gandhavaṇṇakena nahāyissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo gandhavaṇṇakena nahāyantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo gandhavaṇṇakena nahāyissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1198. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta’s Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs of the group of six were bathing with fragrant and colored powders. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, “How can bhikkhunīs bathe with fragrant and colored powders, just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wants… they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, “How can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six bathe with fragrant and colored powders?” … “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunīs of the group of six bathe with fragrant and colored powders?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six bathe with fragrant and colored powders? This is not, Bhikkhus, for the faith of the faithless… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1199. “Yā [V 0.0473] pana bhikkhunī gandhavaṇṇakena nahāyeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1199. “Whatever bhikkhunī should bathe with fragrant and colored powders, it is an offense entailing expiation.”

1200. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1200. Whatever means: whatever sort… A bhikkhunī means:… in this context, this is the intended bhikkhunī.

Gandho [M 0.0456] nāma yo koci gandho. Vaṇṇakaṃ nāma yaṃ kiñci vaṇṇakaṃ. Nahāyeyyāti nahāyati. Payoge dukkaṭaṃ, nahānapariyosāne āpatti pācittiyassa.

Scent means any scent. Colored powder means any colored bathing powder. ‘Should bathe’ means she bathes. In the effort, there is an offense of wrong conduct; at the conclusion of the bathing, there is an offense entailing expiation.

1201. Anāpatti ābādhappaccayā, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1201. There is no offense on account of illness; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fifth Training Rule is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Sixth Training Rule

1202. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo vāsitakena piññākena nahāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti [T 0.0250] vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo vāsitakena piññākena nahāyissanti, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo vāsitakena piññākena nahāyissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo vāsitakena piññākena nahāyantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo vāsitakena piññākena nahāyissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1202. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta’s Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs of the group of six were bathing with perfumed sesame powder. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, “How can bhikkhunīs bathe with perfumed sesame powder, just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wants… they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, “How can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six bathe with perfumed sesame powder?” … “Is it true, Bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunīs of the group of six bathe with perfumed sesame powder?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six bathe with perfumed sesame powder? This is not, Bhikkhus, for the faith of the faithless… And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1203. “Yā pana bhikkhunī vāsitakena piññākena nahāyeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1203. “Whatever bhikkhunī should bathe with perfumed sesame powder, it is an offense entailing expiation.”

1204. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1204. Whatever means: whatever sort… A bhikkhunī means:… in this context, this is the intended bhikkhunī.

Vāsitakaṃ [V 0.0474] nāma yaṃ kiñci gandhavāsitakaṃ. Piññākaṃ nāma tilapiṭṭhaṃ vuccati. Nahāyeyyāti nahāyati. Payoge dukkaṭaṃ, nahānapariyosāne āpatti pācittiyassa.

Perfumed means anything perfumed with scent. Sesame powder is said to be sesame flour. ‘Should bathe’ means she bathes. In the effort, there is an offense of wrong conduct; at the conclusion of the bathing, there is an offense entailing expiation.

1205. Anāpatti [M 0.0457] ābādhappaccayā, pakatipiññākena nahāyati, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1205. There is no offense: on account of illness; if she bathes with ordinary sesame powder; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Sixth Training Rule is concluded.

7. Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Seventh Training Rule

1206. Tena [P 4.0342] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa [T 0.0251] ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo bhikkhuniyā ummaddāpentipi parimaddāpentipi. Manussā vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo bhikkhuniyā ummaddāpessantipi parimaddāpessantipi seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo bhikkhuniyā ummaddāpessantipi parimaddāpessantipī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo bhikkhuniyā ummaddāpentipi parimaddāpentipīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo bhikkhuniyā ummaddāpessantipi parimaddāpessantipi! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1206. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, bhikkhunīs were having another bhikkhunī massaged and rubbed. People wandering on a tour of the monastery saw this and criticized, scorned, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs have a bhikkhunī massaged and rubbed, just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people criticizing, scorning, and speaking disparagingly. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wants… criticized, scorned, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs have a bhikkhunī massaged and rubbed?”… “Is it true, monks, as is said, that bhikkhunīs are having another bhikkhunī massaged and rubbed?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, monks, can bhikkhunīs have another bhikkhunī massaged and rubbed? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1207. “Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā ummaddāpeyya vā parimaddāpeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

1207. “Whatever bhikkhunī should have another bhikkhunī massaged or rubbed, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

1208. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1208. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever bhikkhunī, of whatever sort… ‘Bhikkhunī’… this is the bhikkhunī intended in this context.

Bhikkhuniyāti [V 0.0475] aññāya bhikkhuniyā. Ummaddāpeyya vāti ummaddāpeti ubbaṭṭāpeti (sī.), āpatti pācittiyassa. Parimaddāpeyya vāti sambāhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘By a bhikkhunī’ means by another bhikkhunī. ‘Should have massaged’: if she has one massaged, she commits an offense of pācittiya. ‘Should have rubbed’: if she has one rubbed, she commits an offense of pācittiya.

1209. Anāpatti [M 0.0458] gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1209. There is no offense for one who is ill, in times of danger, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Seventh Training Rule is concluded.

8-9-10. Aṭṭhama-navama-dasamasikkhāpadaṃ

The Eighth, Ninth, and Tenth Training Rules.

1210. Tena [T 0.0252] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo sikkhamānāya ummaddāpentipi parimaddāpentipi…pe… sāmaṇeriyā ummaddāpentipi parimaddāpentipi…pe… gihiniyā ummaddāpentipi parimaddāpentipi. Manussā vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma [P 4.0343] bhikkhuniyo gihiniyā ummaddāpessantipi parimaddāpessantipi, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo gihiniyā ummaddāpessantipi parimaddāpessantipīti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo gihiniyā ummaddāpentipi parimaddāpentipīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo gihiniyā ummaddāpessantipi parimaddāpessantipi! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1210. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, bhikkhunīs were having a probationer massaged and rubbed… having a female novice massaged and rubbed… having a laywoman massaged and rubbed. People wandering on a tour of the monastery saw this and criticized, scorned, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs have a laywoman massaged and rubbed, just like laywomen who enjoy sensual pleasures?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people criticizing, scorning, and speaking disparagingly. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wants… criticized, scorned, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs have a laywoman massaged and rubbed?”… “Is it true, monks, as is said, that bhikkhunīs are having a laywoman massaged and rubbed?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, monks, can bhikkhunīs have a laywoman massaged and rubbed? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1211. “Yā pana bhikkhunī (sikkhamānāya…pe… sāmaṇeriyā…pe…) gihiniyā ummaddāpeyya vā parimaddāpeyya vā, pācittiya”nti.

1211. “Whatever bhikkhunī should have a probationer… a female novice… or a laywoman massaged or rubbed, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

1212. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ [T 0.0253] atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1212. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever bhikkhunī, of whatever sort… ‘Bhikkhunī’… this is the bhikkhunī intended in this context.

Sikkhamānā nāma dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā.

A ‘probationer’ is a woman who has trained for two years in the six principles.

Sāmaṇerī [V 0.0476] nāma dasasikkhāpadikā.

A ‘female novice’ is a woman who holds the ten training rules.

Gihinī nāma agārinī vuccati.

A ‘laywoman’ is said to be one who lives in a house.

Ummaddāpeyya [M 0.0459] vāti ummaddāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should have massaged’: if she has one massaged, she commits an offense of pācittiya.

Parimaddāpeyya vāti sambāhāpeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should have rubbed’: if she has one rubbed, she commits an offense of pācittiya.

1213. Anāpatti gilānāya ābādhappaccayā (ka.), āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1213. There is no offense for one who is ill, in times of danger, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Aṭṭhama navama dasamasikkhāpadāni niṭṭhitāni.

The Eighth, Ninth, and Tenth Training Rules are concluded.

11. Ekādasamasikkhāpadaṃ

11. The Eleventh Training Rule.

1214. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo bhikkhussa purato anāpucchā āsane nisīdanti. Bhikkhū ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo bhikkhussa purato anāpucchā āsane nisīdissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo bhikkhussa purato anāpucchā āsane nisīdantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo bhikkhussa purato anāpucchā āsane nisīdissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1214. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, bhikkhunīs were sitting on a seat in front of a bhikkhu without asking permission. The bhikkhus criticized, scorned, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs sit on a seat in front of a bhikkhu without asking permission?” … “Is it true, monks, as is said, that bhikkhunīs are sitting on a seat in front of a bhikkhu without asking permission?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, monks, can bhikkhunīs sit on a seat in front of a bhikkhu without asking permission! This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1215. “Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhussa purato anāpucchā āsane nisīdeyya, pācittiya”nti.

1215. “Whatever bhikkhunī should sit on a seat in front of a bhikkhu without asking permission, it is an offense of pācittiya.”

1216. Yā [T 0.0254] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1216. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever, of whatever sort… ‘Bhikkhunī’… in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Bhikkhussa [V 0.0477] puratoti upasampannassa purato. Anāpucchāti anapaloketvā. Āsane nisīdeyyāti antamaso chamāyapi nisīdati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘In front of a bhikkhu’ means in front of one who is fully ordained. ‘Without asking’ means without having asked permission. ‘Should sit on a seat’: if she sits even on the ground, she commits an offense of pācittiya.

1217. Anāpucchite anāpucchitasaññā āsane nisīdati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anāpucchite vematikā āsane nisīdati, āpatti pācittiyassa[M 0.0460]. Anāpucchite āpucchitasaññā [P 4.0344] āsane nisīdati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

1217. When she has not asked permission, and she perceives it as not having been asked, if she sits on a seat, she commits an offense of pācittiya. When she has not asked permission, and she is in doubt, if she sits on a seat, she commits an offense of pācittiya. When she has not asked permission, but she perceives it as having been asked, if she sits on a seat, she commits an offense of pācittiya.

Āpucchite anāpucchitasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Āpucchite vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Āpucchite āpucchitasaññā, anāpatti.

When she has asked permission, but she perceives it as not having asked, it is an offense of wrongdoing. When she has asked permission, and she is in doubt, it is an offense of wrongdoing. When she has asked permission, and she perceives it as having asked, there is no offense.

1218. Anāpatti āpucchā āsane nisīdati, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1218. There is no offense if she sits on a seat after asking permission; for one who is sick; in times of danger; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Ekādasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Eleventh Training Rule is concluded.

12. Dvādasamasikkhāpadaṃ

12. The Twelfth Training Rule

1219. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo anokāsakataṃ bhikkhuṃ pañhaṃ pucchanti. Bhikkhū ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo anokāsakataṃ bhikkhuṃ pañhaṃ pucchissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo anokāsakataṃ bhikkhuṃ pañhaṃ [T 0.0255] pucchantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo anokāsakataṃ bhikkhuṃ pañhaṃ pucchissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1219. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, bhikkhunīs were asking a question of a bhikkhu who had not granted permission. The bhikkhus complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs ask a question of a bhikkhu who has not granted permission?” … “Is it true, bhikkhus, as has been heard, that bhikkhunīs are asking a question of a bhikkhu who has not granted permission?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, bhikkhus, can bhikkhunīs ask a question of a bhikkhu who has not granted permission! This, bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1220. “Yā pana bhikkhunī anokāsakataṃ bhikkhuṃ pañhaṃ puccheyya, pācittiya”nti.

1220. “Whatever bhikkhunī should ask a question of a bhikkhu who has not granted permission, it is an offense entailing expiation.”

1221. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1221. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever, of whatever sort... ‘Bhikkhunī’ means: ... in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Anokāsakatanti [V 0.0478] anāpucchā. Bhikkhunti upasampannaṃ. Pañhaṃ puccheyyāti suttante okāsaṃ kārāpetvā vinayaṃ vā abhidhammaṃ vā pucchati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Vinaye okāsaṃ kārāpetvā suttantaṃ vā abhidhammaṃ vā pucchati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Abhidhamme okāsaṃ kārāpetvā suttantaṃ vā vinayaṃ vā pucchati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘One who has not granted permission’ means: without having been asked. ‘A bhikkhu’ means: one who is fully ordained. ‘Should ask a question’ means: having had permission granted regarding the Suttanta, if she asks about the Vinaya or the Abhidhamma, it is an offense entailing expiation. Having had permission granted regarding the Vinaya, if she asks about the Suttanta or the Abhidhamma, it is an offense entailing expiation. Having had permission granted regarding the Abhidhamma, if she asks about the Suttanta or the Vinaya, it is an offense entailing expiation.

1222. Anāpucchite [M 0.0461] anāpucchitasaññā pañhaṃ pucchati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anāpucchite vematikā pañhaṃ pucchati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Anāpucchite āpucchitasaññā pañhaṃ pucchati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

1222. When she has not asked permission, and she perceives it as not having asked, if she asks a question, it is an offense entailing expiation. When she has not asked permission, and she is in doubt, if she asks a question, it is an offense entailing expiation. When she has not asked permission, but she perceives it as having asked, if she asks a question, it is an offense entailing expiation.

Āpucchite anāpucchitasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Āpucchite vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Āpucchite āpucchitasaññā, anāpatti.

When she has asked permission, but she perceives it as not having asked, it is an offense of wrongdoing. When she has asked permission, and she is in doubt, it is an offense of wrongdoing. When she has asked permission, and she perceives it as having asked, there is no offense.

1223. Anāpatti okāsaṃ kārāpetvā pucchati, anodissa okāsaṃ kārāpetvā yattha katthaci pucchati, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1223. There is no offense if she asks after having had permission granted; if, after having had permission granted without specifying a topic, she asks about any topic whatsoever; for one who is insane; or for the first offender.

Dvādasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Twelfth Training Rule is concluded.

13. Terasamasikkhāpadaṃ

13. The Thirteenth Training Rule

1224. Tena [T 0.0256] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena [P 4.0345] aññatarā bhikkhunī asaṅkaccikā asaṅkacchikā (syā.) gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Tassā rathikāya vātamaṇḍalikā saṅghāṭiyo ukkhipiṃsu. Manussā ukkuṭṭhiṃ akaṃsu – “sundarā ayyāya thanudarā”ti. Sā bhikkhunī tehi manussehi uppaṇḍiyamānā maṅku ahosi. Atha kho sā bhikkhunī upassayaṃ gantvā bhikkhunīnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī asaṅkaccikā gāmaṃ pavisissatī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī asaṅkaccikā gāmaṃ pāvisīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī asaṅkaccikā gāmaṃ pavisissati! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1224. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, in the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī entered a village for alms without a breast-band. On the carriage road, a whirlwind lifted up her outer robes. People made a clamor, saying, “The venerable lady’s breasts are beautiful!” That bhikkhunī, being mocked by those people, became troubled. Then that bhikkhunī, having gone to the residence, related this matter to the bhikkhunīs. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… criticized, found fault, and spread it about, saying, “How indeed could a bhikkhunī enter a village without a breast-band?” … “Is it true, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhunī entered a village without a breast-band?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her… “How indeed, bhikkhus, could a bhikkhunī enter a village without a breast-band? This, bhikkhus, is not for the inspiration of faith in the uninspired… And thus, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should set forth this training rule:

1225. “Yā [V 0.0479] pana bhikkhunī asaṅkaccikā asaṅkacchikā (syā.) gāmaṃ paviseyya, pācittiya”nti.

1225. “Whatever bhikkhunī should enter a village without a breast-band, it is an offense entailing expiation.”

1226. Yā [M 0.0462] panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1226. ‘Whatever’ means: whatever, of whatever sort… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means: …the bhikkhunī who is intended in this sense.

Asaṅkaccikāti vinā saṅkaccikaṃ.

‘Without a breast-band’ means: without the breast-band.

Saṅkaccikaṃ [T 0.0257] nāma adhakkhakaṃ ubbhanābhi, tassa paṭicchādanatthāya.

A ‘breast-band’ is for the purpose of covering the area below the collarbone and above the navel.

Gāmaṃ paviseyyāti parikkhittassa gāmassa parikkhepaṃ atikkāmentiyā āpatti pācittiyassa. Aparikkhittassa gāmassa upacāraṃ okkamantiyā āpatti pācittiyassa.

‘Should enter a village’ means: upon crossing the enclosure of an enclosed village, there is an offense entailing expiation. Upon entering the precincts of an unenclosed village, there is an offense entailing expiation.

1227. Anāpatti acchinnacīvarikāya, naṭṭhacīvarikāya, gilānāya, assatiyā, ajānantiyā, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1227. There is no offense: if her robe has been stolen, if her robe is lost, if she is ill, if she is unmindful, if she is unknowing, in times of calamity, for one who is insane, or for the first offender.

Terasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Thirteenth Training Rule is concluded.

Chattupāhanavaggo navamo.

The Ninth, the Chapter on the Umbrella and Sandals, is concluded.

Uddiṭṭhā kho, ayyāyo, chasaṭṭhisatā pācittiyā dhammā. Tatthāyyāyo pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Dutiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Tatiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Parisuddhetthāyyāyo, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti.

Venerable ladies, the one hundred and sixty-six rules entailing expiation have been set forth. Therein, I ask the venerable ladies, ‘Are you pure in this matter?’ A second time I ask, ‘Are you pure in this matter?’ A third time I ask, ‘Are you pure in this matter?’ The venerable ladies are pure in this matter; therefore, they are silent. Thus do I take it.

Khuddakaṃ samattaṃ.

The Minor Section is concluded.

Bhikkhunivibhaṅge pācittiyakaṇḍaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

In the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga, the Chapter on Offenses Entailing Expiation is concluded.

5. Pāṭidesanīyakaṇḍaṃ (bhikkhunīvibhaṅgo)

5. The Section on Offenses to be Confessed (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga)

1. Paṭhamapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadaṃ

1. The First Training Rule on an Offense to be Confessed

Ime kho panāyyāyo aṭṭha pāṭidesanīyā

Venerable ladies, these eight rules concerning matters to be confessed

Dhammā uddesaṃ āgacchanti.

come up for recitation.

1228. Tena [T 0.0258][M 0.0463][P 4.0346][V 0.0480] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo sappiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo sappiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjissanti! Kassa sampannaṃ na manāpaṃ, kassa sāduṃ na ruccatī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo sappiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā, bhikkhuniyo sappiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo sappiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1228. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, at Jeta's Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs, having requested ghee, ate it. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, “How indeed can bhikkhunīs, having requested ghee, eat it? To whom is something rich not pleasing? Who does not enjoy what is delicious?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, “How indeed can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs, having requested ghee, eat it?”… “Is it true, monks, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs, having requested ghee, eat it?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, monks, can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs, having requested ghee, eat it? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

“Yā pana bhikkhunī sappiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjeyya, paṭidesetabbaṃ tāya bhikkhuniyā – ‘gārayhaṃ, ayye, dhammaṃ āpajjiṃ asappāyaṃ pāṭidesanīyaṃ, taṃ paṭidesemī’”ti.

“Whatever bhikkhunī, having requested ghee, should eat it, it is to be confessed by that bhikkhunī: ‘Venerable ladies, I have committed a blameworthy, unsuitable act that is to be confessed; I confess it.’”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā [T 0.0259] bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

In this way, this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhunīs.

1229. Tena [V 0.0481] kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo gilānā honti. Gilānapucchikā bhikkhuniyo gilānā bhikkhuniyo etadavocuṃ – “kacci, ayye, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīya”nti? “Pubbe mayaṃ, ayye, sappiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjāma, [M 0.0464] tena no phāsu hoti; idāni pana “bhagavatā paṭikkhitta”nti kukkuccāyantā na viññāpema, tena no na phāsu hotī”ti…pe… bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānāya bhikkhuniyā sappiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjituṃ[P 4.0347]. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1229. Now at that time, some bhikkhunīs were ill. Bhikkhunīs who went to inquire after the sick said this to the sick bhikkhunīs: “Venerable ladies, are you getting by? Are you keeping well?” “Formerly, venerable ladies, we would request ghee and eat, and because of that, we were comfortable. But now, being scrupulous that ‘it has been forbidden by the Blessed One,’ we do not request it, and because of that, we are not comfortable.”… They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Monks, I allow a sick bhikkhunī to request ghee and eat it. And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

1230. “Yā pana bhikkhunī agilānā sappiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjeyya, paṭidesetabbaṃ tāya bhikkhuniyā – ‘gārayhaṃ, ayye, dhammaṃ āpajjiṃ asappāyaṃ pāṭidesanīyaṃ taṃ paṭidesemī’”ti.

1230. “Whatever bhikkhunī, not being ill, having requested ghee, should eat it, it is to be confessed by that bhikkhunī: ‘Venerable ladies, I have committed a blameworthy, unsuitable act that is to be confessed; I confess it.’”

1231. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1231. ‘Whatever’ means: of whatever sort… ‘Bhikkhunī’ means: … in this context, this is the bhikkhunī who is intended.

Agilānā nāma yassā vinā sappinā phāsu hoti.

‘Not ill’ means: one for whom it is comfortable without ghee.

Gilānā nāma yassā vinā sappinā na phāsu hoti.

‘Ill’ means: one for whom it is not comfortable without ghee.

Sappi nāma gosappi vā ajikāsappi vā mahiṃsasappi vā. Yesaṃ maṃsaṃ kappati tesaṃ sappi.

‘Ghee’ means: cow's ghee, goat's ghee, or buffalo's ghee. The ghee of those animals whose meat is allowable.

Agilānā attano atthāya viññāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena “bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre [T 0.0260] āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

One who is not ill requests for her own sake; in the effort, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Upon receiving it, if she accepts it thinking, ‘I will eat it,’ there is an offense of wrong conduct. For every mouthful, there is an offense to be confessed.

1232. Agilānā agilānasaññā sappiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjati, āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa. Agilānā vematikā sappiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjati, āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa. Agilānā gilānasaññā sappiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjati, āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

1232. One who is not ill, perceiving herself as not ill, requests ghee and eats it: there is an offense to be confessed. One who is not ill, being uncertain, requests ghee and eats it: there is an offense to be confessed. One who is not ill, perceiving herself as ill, requests ghee and eats it: there is an offense to be confessed.

Gilānā [V 0.0482] agilānasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Gilānā vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Gilānā gilānasaññā, anāpatti.

One who is ill, perceiving herself as not ill: there is an offense of wrong conduct. One who is ill, being uncertain: there is an offense of wrong conduct. One who is ill, perceiving herself as ill: there is no offense.

1233. Anāpatti [M 0.0465] gilānāya, gilānā hutvā viññāpetvā agilānā bhuñjati, gilānāya sesakaṃ bhuñjati, ñātakānaṃ pavāritānaṃ, aññassatthāya, attano dhanena, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1233. There is no offense for one who is ill; for one who, having been ill, requests it, and then eats it when no longer ill; for one who eats the leftovers of a sick person; for requesting from relatives or from those who have made an invitation; for the sake of another; with one's own funds; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Paṭhamapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The First Training Rule on an Offense to be Confessed is finished.

2. Dutiyādipāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadāni

2. The Second and Subsequent Training Rules on an Offense to be Confessed

1234. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo telaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanti…pe… madhuṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanti…pe… phāṇitaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanti…pe… macchaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanti…pe… maṃsaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanti…pe… khīraṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanti…pe… dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjissanti! Kassa sampannaṃ na manāpaṃ, kassa sāduṃ [T 0.0261] na ruccatī”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjissantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1234. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta’s Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs, having requested oil, ate it... having requested honey, ate it... having requested molasses, ate it... having requested fish, ate it... having requested meat, ate it... having requested milk, ate it... having requested curd, ate it. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can bhikkhunīs, having requested curd, eat it! To whom is something rich not pleasing? Who does not enjoy what is delicious?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs, having requested curd, eat it?”... “Is it true, monks, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs, having requested curd, eat it?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... “How indeed, monks, can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs, having requested curd, eat it? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident...”... “And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

“Yā pana bhikkhunī dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjeyya, paṭidesetabbaṃ tāya bhikkhuniyā – ‘gārayhaṃ, ayye, dhammaṃ āpajjiṃ asappāyaṃ pāṭidesanīyaṃ, taṃ paṭidesemī’”ti.

“Whatever bhikkhunī, having requested curd, should eat it, it is to be confessed by that bhikkhunī: ‘Venerable ladies, I have committed a blameworthy, unsuitable act that is to be confessed; I confess it.’”

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

And thus this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhunīs.

1235. Tena [V 0.0483] kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo gilānā honti. Gilānapucchikā bhikkhuniyo gilānā bhikkhuniyo etadavocuṃ – “kacci, ayye, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīya”nti? “Pubbe mayaṃ, ayye, dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjimhā, [M 0.0466] tena no phāsu hoti, idāni pana “bhagavatā paṭikkhitta”nti kukkuccāyantā na viññāpema, tena no na phāsu hotī”ti…pe… bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānāya bhikkhuniyā dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1235. Now at that time, some bhikkhunīs were sick. The bhikkhunīs inquiring after the sick approached the sick bhikkhunīs and said this: “Venerable ladies, are you enduring? Are you managing?” “Formerly, venerable ladies, we requested curd and ate it, and because of that, we were comfortable. But now, being scrupulous that ‘it has been forbidden by the Blessed One,’ we do not request it, and because of that, we are not comfortable.”... They reported this matter to the Blessed One... “Bhikkhus, I allow a sick bhikkhunī to request curd and eat it. And so, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:

1236. “Yā pana bhikkhunī agilānā (telaṃ…pe… madhuṃ…pe… phāṇitaṃ…pe… macchaṃ…pe… maṃsaṃ…pe… khīraṃ…pe…) dadhiṃ [T 0.0262] viññāpetvā bhuñjeyya [P 4.0348], paṭidesetabbaṃ tāya bhikkhuniyā – ‘gārayhaṃ, ayye, dhammaṃ āpajjiṃ asappāyaṃ pāṭidesanīyaṃ, taṃ paṭidesemī’”ti.

1236. “Whatever bhikkhunī, not being sick, having requested (oil... honey... molasses... fish... meat... milk...) curd, should eat it, it is to be confessed by that bhikkhunī thus: ‘Venerable ladies, I have committed a blameworthy, unsuitable act that is to be confessed, a Pāṭidesanīya offense. I confess it.’”

1237. Yā panāti yā yādisā…pe… bhikkhunīti…pe… ayaṃ imasmiṃ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.

1237. ‘Whatever’ means: whoever, of whatever kind... ‘Bhikkhunī’ means... in this sense, ‘bhikkhunī’ is intended.

Agilānā nāma yassā vinā dadhinā phāsu hoti.

‘Not sick’ means: one for whom it is comfortable without curd.

Gilānā nāma yassā vinā dadhinā na phāsu hoti.

‘Sick’ means: one for whom it is not comfortable without curd.

Telaṃ nāma tilatelaṃ sāsapatelaṃ madhukatelaṃ eraṇḍatelaṃ vasātelaṃ.

‘Oil’ means: sesame oil, mustard oil, licorice-tree oil, castor oil, and tallow.

Madhu nāma makkhikāmadhu. Phāṇitaṃ nāma ucchumhā nibbattaṃ. Maccho nāma odako vuccati. Maṃsaṃ nāma yesaṃ maṃsaṃ kappati tesaṃ maṃsaṃ. Khīraṃ nāma gokhīraṃ vā ajikākhīraṃ vā mahiṃsakhīraṃ vā yesaṃ maṃsaṃ kappati tesaṃ khīraṃ. Dadhi nāma tesaññeva dadhi.

‘Honey’ means: the honey of bees. ‘Molasses’ means: that which is produced from sugarcane. ‘Fish’ is said to be an aquatic being. ‘Meat’ means: the meat of those animals whose meat is allowable. ‘Milk’ means: cow’s milk, goat’s milk, buffalo’s milk, or the milk of those animals whose meat is allowable. ‘Curd’ means: the curd from those same animals.

Agilānā attano atthāya viññāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Paṭilābhena bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

If, not being sick, she requests for her own sake, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the effort. Upon receiving it, if she accepts it thinking, ‘I will eat it,’ there is an offense of wrong-doing. For every mouthful, there is a Pāṭidesanīya offense.

1238. Agilānā agilānasaññā dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjati, āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa[V 0.0484]. Agilānā vematikā dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjati, āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa. Agilānā gilānasaññā dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjati, āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

1238. If she is not sick and perceives herself as not sick, and having requested curd, eats it, there is a Pāṭidesanīya offense. If she is not sick and is doubtful, and having requested curd, eats it, there is a Pāṭidesanīya offense. If she is not sick and perceives herself as sick, and having requested curd, eats it, there is a Pāṭidesanīya offense.

Gilānā [M 0.0467] agilānasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Gilānā vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Gilānā gilānasaññā anāpatti.

If she is sick but perceives herself as not sick, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she is sick and is doubtful, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she is sick and perceives herself as sick, there is no offense.

1239. Anāpatti [T 0.0263] gilānāya, gilānā hutvā viññāpetvā agilānā bhuñjati, gilānāya sesakaṃ bhuñjati, ñātakānaṃ pavāritānaṃ, aññassatthāya, attano dhanena, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti.

1239. There is no offense: for one who is sick; if, having been sick, she requests it and then eats it when she is no longer sick; if she eats the leftovers of a sick bhikkhunī; if she requests from relatives or from those who have given an invitation; if she requests for the sake of another; if it is with her own wealth; for one who is insane; for the first offender.

Aṭṭhamapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Eighth Pāṭidesanīya Training Rule is concluded.

Uddiṭṭhā kho, ayyāyo, aṭṭha pāṭidesanīyā dhammā. Tatthāyyāyo pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Dutiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Tatiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Parisuddhetthāyyāyo, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti.

Venerable ladies, the eight Pāṭidesanīya rules have been recited. In this matter, I ask the venerable ladies: ‘Are you pure in this?’ A second time I ask: ‘Are you pure in this?’ A third time I ask: ‘Are you pure in this?’ The venerable ladies are pure in this, therefore they are silent. Thus do I take it.

Bhikkhunivibhaṅge pāṭidesanīyakaṇḍaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

In the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, the Pāṭidesanīya Section is concluded.

6. Sekhiyakaṇḍaṃ (bhikkhunīvibhaṅgo)

6. The Section on Training Rules (The Bhikkhunīs' Analysis)

1. Parimaṇḍalavaggo

1. The Chapter on Wearing Robes Evenly

Ime kho panāyyāyo sekhiyā

These, venerable ladies, are the training rules.

Dhammā uddesaṃ āgacchanti.

The rules come up for recitation.

1240. Tena [T 0.0264][M 0.0468][P 4.0349][V 0.0485] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo puratopi pacchatopi olambentī nivāsenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo puratopi pacchatopi olambentī nivāsessanti, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā…pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo puratopi pacchatopi olambentī nivāsessantī”ti…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo puratopi pacchatopi olambentī nivāsentīti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo puratopi pacchatopi olambentī nivāsessanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1240. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs wore their lower robes hanging down both in front and behind. People complained, grumbled, and criticized: “How can these bhikkhunīs wear their lower robes hanging down both in front and behind, just like laywomen who indulge in sensual pleasures?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, grumbling, and criticizing. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… complained, grumbled, and criticized: “How can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs wear their lower robes hanging down both in front and behind?”… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs wear their lower robes hanging down both in front and behind?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs wear their lower robes hanging down both in front and behind! This, bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of those who are not yet confident… And thus, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

“Parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“I will wear the lower robe evenly all around”—this is a training to be observed.

Parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsetabbaṃ nābhimaṇḍalaṃ jāṇumaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādentiyā. Yā anādariyaṃ paṭicca purato vā pacchato vā olambentī [T 0.0265] nivāseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The lower robe is to be worn evenly all around, covering the navel and the knees. Whichever bhikkhunī, on account of disrespect, wears it hanging down in front or behind, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti [V 0.0486] asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantiyā, gilānāya, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, ādikammikāyāti…pe… (saṃkhittaṃ).

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, if one does not know, if one is sick, in times of danger, if one is insane, or for the first offender. (This is summarized.)

7. Pādukavaggo

7. The Chapter on Footwear

1241. Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo udake uccārampi passāvampi kheḷampi karonti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo udake uccārampi [M 0.0469] passāvampi kheḷampi karissanti, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti! Assosuṃ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā, tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo [P 4.0350] udake uccārampi passāvampi kheḷampi karissantī”ti! Atha kho bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhū ye te bhikkhū…pe… (?) bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā…pe… bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo udake uccārampi passāvampi kheḷampi karontī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo udake uccārampi passāvampi kheḷampi karissanti! Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

1241. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's park. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs were defecating, urinating, and spitting in the water. People complained, grumbled, and criticized: “How can these bhikkhunīs defecate, urinate, and spit in the water, just like laywomen who indulge in sensual pleasures?” The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, grumbling, and criticizing. Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires complained, grumbled, and criticized: “How can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs defecate, urinate, and spit in the water?” Then the bhikkhunīs informed the bhikkhus of this matter. The bhikkhus informed the Blessed One of this matter. Then the Blessed One… asked the bhikkhus: “Is it true, bhikkhus, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs defecate, urinate, and spit in the water?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them: “… How can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs defecate, urinate, and spit in the water! This, bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of those who are not yet confident… And thus, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

“Na udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti[T 0.0266].

“I will not defecate, urinate, or spit in water”—this is a training to be observed.

Evañcidaṃ bhagavatā bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti.

Thus, this training rule was laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhunīs.

Tena kho pana samayena gilānā bhikkhuniyo udake uccārampi passāvampi kheḷampi kātuṃ kukkuccāyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānāya bhikkhuniyā udake uccārampi passāvampi kheḷampi kātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddisantu –

Now at that time, sick bhikkhunīs felt scruples about defecating, urinating, or spitting in the water. They informed the Blessed One of this matter… “I allow, bhikkhus, a sick bhikkhunī to defecate, urinate, or spit in the water. And thus, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

“Na udake agilānā uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.

“When not ill, I will not defecate, urinate, or spit in water”—this is a training to be observed.

Na [V 0.0487] udake agilānāya uccāro vā passāvo vā kheḷo vā kātabbo. Yā anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake agilānā uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karoti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One who is not ill should not defecate, urinate, or spit in water. Whichever bhikkhunī, on account of disrespect, when not ill, defecates, urinates, or spits in water, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Anāpatti asañcicca, assatiyā, ajānantiyā, gilānāya, thale kato udakaṃ ottharati, āpadāsu, ummattikāya, khittacittāya, vedanāṭṭāya, ādikammikāyāti.

There is no offense if it is unintentional, if one is unmindful, if one does not know, if one is sick, if it is done on dry ground and water flows over it, in times of danger, if one is insane, if one has a scattered mind, if one is afflicted by pain, or for the first offender.

Pannarasamasikkhāpadaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fifteenth training rule is concluded.

Pādukavaggo sattamo.

The seventh chapter, on footwear, is concluded.

Uddiṭṭhā [M 0.0470] kho, ayyāyo, sekhiyā dhammā. Tatthāyyāyo pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Dutiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Tatiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Parisuddhetthāyyāyo, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti.

Venerable ladies, the training rules have been recited. Concerning them, I ask you, venerable ladies: “Are you pure in this?” A second time I ask: “Are you pure in this?” A third time I ask: “Are you pure in this?” The venerable ladies are pure in this, therefore they are silent. Thus I hold it.

Sekhiyakaṇḍaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section on Training is concluded.

7. Adhikaraṇasamathā (bhikkhunīvibhaṅgo)

7. The Settlement of Legal Issues

Ime kho panāyyāyo satta adhikaraṇasamathā

Venerable ladies, there are these seven principles for the settlement of legal issues,

Dhammā uddesaṃ āgacchanti.

which come up for recitation.

1242. Uppannuppannānaṃ [T 0.0267][P 4.0351][V 0.0488] adhikaraṇānaṃ samathāya vūpasamāya sammukhāvinayo dātabbo, sativinayo dātabbo, amūḷhavinayo dātabbo, paṭiññāya kāretabbaṃ, yebhuyyasikā, tassapāpiyasikā, tiṇavatthārakoti.

1242. For the settlement and pacification of legal issues as they arise, the following should be applied: the procedure in the presence of, the procedure of recollection, the procedure for one who is no longer confused, deciding on admission, the decision by a majority, the verdict for one's bad character, and the covering with grass.

Uddiṭṭhā kho, ayyāyo, satta adhikaraṇasamathā dhammā. Tatthāyyāyo pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Dutiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Tatiyampi pucchāmi – “kaccittha parisuddhā”? Parisuddhetthāyyāyo, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti.

Venerable ladies, the seven principles for the settlement of legal issues have been recited. In this regard, I ask you, venerable ladies: 'Are you pure in this?' A second time I ask: 'Are you pure in this?' A third time I ask: 'Are you pure in this?' The venerable ladies are pure in this, and thus are silent. Thus I hold it.

Adhikaraṇasamathā niṭṭhitā.

The Settlement of Legal Issues is concluded.

Uddiṭṭhaṃ kho, ayyāyo, nidānaṃ. Uddiṭṭhā aṭṭha pārājikā dhammā. Uddiṭṭhā sattarasa saṅghādisesā dhammā. Uddiṭṭhā tiṃsa nissaggiyā pācittiyā dhammā. Uddiṭṭhā chasaṭṭhisatā pācittiyā dhammā. Uddiṭṭhā aṭṭha pāṭidesanīyā dhammā. Uddiṭṭhā sekhiyā dhammā. Uddiṭṭhā satta adhikaraṇasamathā dhammā. Ettakaṃ tassa bhagavato suttāgataṃ suttapariyāpannaṃ anvaddhamāsaṃ uddesaṃ āgacchati. Tattha sabbāheva samaggāhi sammodamānāhi avivadamānāhi sikkhitabbanti.

Venerable ladies, the introduction has been recited. The eight rules entailing defeat have been recited. The seventeen Saṅghādisesa rules have been recited. The thirty Nissaggiya Pācittiya rules have been recited. The one hundred and sixty-six Pācittiya rules have been recited. The eight Pāṭidesanīya rules have been recited. The training rules have been recited. The seven principles for the settlement of legal issues have been recited. This much of the Blessed One’s teaching, which has come down in the discourse and is included in the discourse, comes up for recitation every half-month. Herein, all should train together in concord, with mutual appreciation, and without dispute.

Bhikkhunivibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of the Bhikkhunīs' Rules is concluded.

Pācittiyapāḷi niṭṭhitā.

The Pācittiya Pāḷi is concluded.
